points.name: Sereact
points.description: German robotics startup deploying vision-language AI models to enable warehouse robots to pick and sort items autonomously.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose vision-language-action models and manipulation software enable robots to perform autonomous picking, sorting and returns processing in warehouses without retraining for new objects.
1. An AI model developer whose robotic foundation models and manipulation software run on other companies' robots.
2. Vision-language-action models combined with a learned world model that links visual, linguistic and physical information to plan movements before a robot acts.
3. Zero-shot grasping and manipulation of unseen objects, real-time perception and reasoning, and autonomous pick-and-place task generation.
4. AI models and picking software that run on customers' existing robotic hardware, and autonomous pick robots deployed directly into warehouse operations.
5. Warehouses, fulfillment centers, industrial supply chains and intralogistics operations.
6. Automakers, e-commerce retailers, logistics operators and warehouse automation integrators.
7. Its models and software are integrated into robotic systems and warehouse automation built by logistics operators and automation integrators.
8. A proprietary data flywheel where every deployed robot contributes operational data to continuously improve its foundation models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Customers and partners include BMW Group, Daimler Truck, Mercedes-Benz, IKEA, Zalando, Active Ants, Körber, AutoStore and AWL, with investors including Creandum, Earlybird, Coatue and Air Street Capital.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, AI model integration contracts and direct deployment of autonomous pick robots.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2021 with over 200 robotic systems deployed and over $145 million in venture funding.
Geography: Based in Stuttgart, Germany with deployments and partnerships across Europe and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and robotic automation for warehouse and logistics applications is its entire focus.

points.name: Wandelbots
points.description: German robotics software company building no-code platforms that let manufacturers program industrial robots without specialized coding knowledge.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company whose no-code robotics platform enables industrial manufacturers to program and deploy heterogeneous robots without writing lines of code. It builds a hardware-agnostic operating system, cloud data backbone, and teaching tools that unify robot programming, sensor data collection, simulation, and AI model deployment across factory shop floors.
1. A developer tools and platform company that builds a no-code robot programming OS and cloud platform sold as licensed software and developer tools.
2. A hardware-agnostic operating system and cloud platform that abstracts low-level robot motion control and uses hand-guided demonstration with an input device, combined with digital twin simulation, to train and execute robot tasks.
3. Intuitive no-code robot teaching, runtime policy execution, low-level motion abstraction across heterogeneous robots, and large-scale data collection for reinforcement learning.
4. Licensed software, cloud platforms, software development kits, and physical teaching input devices.
5. Industrial factory automation and human-robot collaboration.
6. Industrial manufacturers and robotics developers.
7. Its software platform is installed on factory shop floors to orchestrate and program industrial robots built by various robot makers.
8. It abstracts vendor-specific robot programming languages to provide hardware-agnostic, no-code teaching with continuity between digital twin simulation and live production deployment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with simulation platforms built by NVIDIA and realvirtual.io, and partners with robot makers like Yaskawa.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, cloud subscriptions, and developer tool sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, has raised over $123 million, and serves major industrial manufacturers.
Geography: Based in Germany with a United States headquarters in Chicago and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and industrial automation comprise the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Inbolt
points.description: French AI vision startup deploying real-time 3D perception systems on industrial robots for dynamic manufacturing tasks.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds real-time 3D vision and AI guidance software for industrial robots. It licenses a hardware-agnostic platform that trains from CAD models and integrates with existing robot arms to enable dynamic part localization and trajectory adjustment, reducing setup time and integration costs for manufacturers.
1. An AI model developer that builds 3D vision and robot guidance software licensed as a platform to manufacturers.
2. Real-time workpiece localization AI uses 3D camera input to track workpieces and provide continuous offsets to a robot's trajectory, trained directly from CAD models.
3. 3D perception, dynamic part localization, and real-time trajectory adjustment for industrial robots in unstructured or moving environments.
4. Licensed software and vision systems integrated with existing industrial robots and 3D cameras.
5. Industrial robot arms in factories, assembly lines, automotive manufacturing, and consumer appliance production.
6. Large-scale manufacturers and factories in the automotive, consumer electronics, and appliance sectors.
7. Its software is integrated onto existing industrial robot arms from major manufacturers to retrofit them with vision-guided capabilities.
8. It replaces traditional sensors and fixtures with real-time vision-based part localization, enabling rapid 24-hour installation and commissioning without custom engineering.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and customers include Fanuc, ABB, Kuka, Universal Robots, Zivid, Stellantis, Toyota, Ford, General Motors, Beko, Renault, and Volkswagen.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and platform integration services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019, backed by $17 million in Series A funding, with deployments on over 200 robots across more than 100 factories on three continents.
Geography: Based in Paris, France, operating across Europe with an expanding presence in the United States and Japan.
Beyond physical AI: The company is entirely focused on AI vision-guided industrial robot automation and does not operate in other business domains.

points.name: Enchanted Tools
points.description: French humanoid robotics startup building embodied AI systems for deployment in healthcare, hospitality, and retail environments.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs, manufactures, and deploys wheeled social humanoid robots for human-facing environments, combining edge AI inference, sensors, actuators, and language models into complete systems for enterprises.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells wheeled social humanoid robots.
2. A wheeled humanoid robot platform with an emotive display face, multimodal sensors, actuators, and integrated language models for social interaction.
3. Social multimodal interaction, real-time spatial understanding, environmental perception, gesture-based communication, navigation in human spaces, and load carrying.
4. Complete robots delivered as ready-to-deploy embodied agent systems.
5. Hospitals, hospitality venues, retail locations, and other human-facing service environments.
6. Enterprises and service providers in healthcare, hospitality, and retail sectors.
7. It consumes AI models and edge inference hardware from partners and delivers fully embodied robot solutions to end operators.
8. It distinguishes itself through character-driven design focused on warmth and natural social interaction via an emotive display face.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is an NVIDIA customer or partner and a trusted tester for the Gemini Robotics model family.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robotic systems.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company demonstrating product integration with major AI infrastructure providers at industry conferences like CES 2026.
Geography: Based in France, targeting deployment across North American and global markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI-powered humanoid robotics and embodied AI systems are its entire focus.

points.name: Generative Bionics
points.description: Italian robotics startup building humanoid robots with onboard AI for industrial manufacturing and warehouse automation tasks.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that designs and builds full-body tactile humanoids for physically demanding industrial tasks. The company develops complete robotic platforms integrating onboard AI, distributed tactile sensing, and actuation for industrial automation, operating as an OEM and platform provider for downstream developers.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds complete humanoid robots for industrial use.
2. The core technology is a body-as-compute architecture using embedded processors, GPUs, and FPGAs running a custom robotics OS for low-latency on-device inference, integrated with full-body distributed multimodal tactile skin perceiving touch, proximity, force, and temperature.
3. It delivers on-device inference, tactile perception, safe human-robot collaboration, and force-based task learning for physically demanding industrial labor.
4. Customers get complete humanoid robots and a source-available developer model with an open-source digital twin.
5. Its humanoids are used in manufacturing, shipbuilding, logistics, public safety and inspection, and healthcare settings, with initial deployment as a welding humanoid in shipyards.
6. It sells to industrial manufacturers, logistics operators, and healthcare providers.
7. It designs and builds complete humanoid robots and integrates them into industrial operations.
8. It distinguishes its approach through full-body distributed tactile sensing combined with a body-as-compute architecture that embeds intelligence throughout the physical structure, releasing the robot's digital twin as open source.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with Fincantieri for shipyard welding applications, Synapticon for a sovereign EU-protected actuation stack, and AMD for compute hardware, and was selected for the Google DeepMind Accelerator.
Organization type: It is a privately held deep tech startup spun out of the Italian Institute of Technology in 2024.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of complete humanoid robots.
Scale and maturity: The pre-revenue or early-revenue stage startup has approximately 100 employees, with a functional prototype completed and commercial production scheduled for late 2026 at a $50,000 USD price point per unit.
Geography: It is based in Italy and operates with a focus on a sovereign European supply chain, with intentions to scale globally.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and humanoid robotics constitute its entire focus.

points.name: mimic robotics
points.description: Swiss robotics startup building AI-controlled dexterous hands that learn from human demonstrations to automate complex manual tasks.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds vertically integrated dexterous manipulation systems, combining tendon-driven robotic hands with Video-Action Models to automate complex manual tasks for industrial manufacturers.
1. A robot maker and physical AI company that designs and sells dexterous robotic hands, paired wearable exoskeletons, and integrated manipulation software as complete deployed robotic stations.
2. Tendon-driven robotic hands with tactile sensors and wrist-mounted cameras, custom low-latency communication middleware, and inverse-dynamics World-Action Models using a video diffusion backbone for action decoding.
3. Dexterous manipulation of complex industrial tasks, high-payload fine-motor control, demonstration-based learning from human operators, and on-device AI inference for robot control.
4. Complete robotic stations integrating proprietary hardware with edge-deployed AI software, installed directly in industrial environments.
5. Factory assembly lines, logistics sorting operations, packaging facilities, and laboratory automation.
6. Manufacturing assembly operations, logistics operators, and laboratory automation facilities.
7. The organization designs and builds its own proprietary robotic hands and models, integrating them into deployed stations installed directly in industrial customer facilities.
8. A morphology-matching passive exoskeleton enables human demonstration of manipulation tasks, while its Video-Action Models trained on video generation backbones run on single GPUs at the edge with minimal task-specific fine-tuning.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Audi, NVIDIA, Black Forest Labs, and ETH Zürich.
Organization type: A privately held startup and university spin-off.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic hands and integrated systems, combined with deployed industrial automation solutions.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company less than two years old that has raised a $16 million seed funding round and is actively deploying systems in live manufacturing environments.
Geography: Based in Switzerland with deployments across European manufacturing sites and a focus on the German automotive sector.
Beyond physical AI: Dexterous robotic manipulation and edge AI for industrial automation constitute the entire focus of the organization's business model and technical strategy.

points.name: RLWRLD
points.description: South Korean robotics startup building foundation models that teach robots precise hand manipulation in real factories.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose robotics foundation models enable robots to perform complex five-finger dexterous manipulation in real-world industrial environments. It trains multimodal models on real-world sensor data, robotic systems, and industrial workflows to automate manual processes for industrial conglomerates and large-scale operations in logistics, retail, and service sectors.
1. An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on other companies' robots.
2. Vision-language-action models that fuse vision-language understanding with proprioceptive, tactile, and torque sensing to control diverse robot embodiments.
3. Dexterous manipulation, five-finger hand movements, logical reasoning, quick movements, and generalizable robot control across single-arm, dual-arm, and humanoid embodiments.
4. AI models and training data licensed to robot manufacturers.
5. Factories, warehouses, logistics operations, retail stores, and hotel service environments.
6. Industrial conglomerates, logistics operators, retail operators, hotel operators, and robot manufacturers.
7. Its models are integrated by robot manufacturers and humanoid makers into their robots.
8. It trains its dexterity models exclusively on hundreds of terabytes of real-world industrial data rather than simulation, achieving comparable performance with approximately twenty percent less training compute than frontier models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with AWS, NVIDIA, CJ Logistics, Lawson, Lotte Hotel, WIRobotics, KAIST, Seoul National University, POSTECH, Rainbow Robotics, Wonik Robotics, Robotis, and is backed by Hashed Ventures, Headline Asia, Z Venture Capital, Kakao Investment, Lotte Ventures, Hanwha Asset Management, and Mirae Asset–Emart Investment Fund.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, per-robot royalties, and strategic data partnerships.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2024, it has raised forty-two point three million dollars across two seed rounds and is progressing from memoranda of understanding to joint validation phases with major industrial customers.
Geography: It is based in Seoul, South Korea, operates primarily in Japan and South Korea, and is expanding into the United States and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and robotics comprise its complete business strategy and value proposition.

points.name: Galexea Dynamics
points.description: Chinese robotics startup building full-stack humanoid robots and arms with on-device AI for autonomous manipulation tasks.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker and component supplier that builds full-stack wheeled dual-arm humanoids, modular force-controlled arms, and grippers running on-device vision-language-action models for embodied-AI researchers and industrial automation customers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells wheeled dual-arm humanoid robots and modular manipulators, while also supplying components to other builders.
2. Vision-language-action models and diffusion policies run directly on-device using edge inference processors, integrated with force-controlled actuators, tactile sensing, and a simulation and teleoperation data pipeline for imitation learning.
3. Mobile manipulation, bin picking, vertical workspace reach, real-time task execution, complex reasoning, and safe human-environment interaction.
4. Complete wheeled humanoid robots, modular arms and grippers as components, and an open software stack used for research and industrial deployment.
5. Humanoids, laboratories, warehouses, logistics workflows, and educational institutions.
6. Embodied-AI researchers, industrial automation operators, laboratory automation operators, and educational institutions.
7. Its complete robots are deployed by industrial and research users, while its modular arms and grippers are designed into other machines by component buyers.
8. A three-tier product ladder sharing common hardware and software combines genuine floor-to-two-meter vertical workspace reach, integrated force sensing, and a research-native open stack including teleoperation as a data pipeline.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its robots run on edge inference processors from a named GPU maker.
Organization type: A privately held robotics startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robots and modular components, alongside research and industrial deployment contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established startup with multiple shipping product lines and a Series B unicorn valuation having raised approximately $434M.
Geography: Based and operating primarily in Asia across embodied AI research hubs and industrial automation markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation comprise the organization's entire focus and business model.

points.name: Spirit AI
points.description: Chinese robotics startup developing vision-language-action models that teach humanoid robots to perform complex physical tasks autonomously.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and AI model developer that builds general-purpose humanoid robots and the vision-language-action foundation models that run on them for industrial and commercial use.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells humanoid robots and an AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on them.
2. Vision-language-action models trained on low-cost, open-ended, real-world interaction data, and force-controlled humanoid robots with high-power-density integrated joints.
3. Visual perception, language understanding, action execution, high-precision manipulation, and legged or wheeled locomotion in unstructured environments.
4. Complete humanoid robots and embodied AI models running on them.
5. Humanoids, factories, logistics, warehouses, retail, hotels, and office buildings.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, retailers, and commercial service operators.
7. It builds its own AI models and integrates them into humanoid robots it designs and manufactures itself.
8. It uses a "dirty data" strategy of over 200,000 hours of open-ended, goal-driven real-world interaction data collected through proprietary wearable devices at a tenth of traditional data collection costs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with Bosch, CATL, JD.com, and Shanghai HiSilicon, with backing from Yunfeng Capital, Chaos Investment, Sequoia China, and Shunwei Capital.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Robot hardware sales and model licensing.
Scale and maturity: A 2024-founded unicorn company that raised $435 million and has live deployments on battery production lines.
Geography: Based in Hangzhou, China, and operates across Chinese industrial and commercial sectors.
Beyond physical AI: Embodied AI and robotics represent the entire focus, with no diversified business activities outside this domain.

points.name: Astribot
points.description: Chinese humanoid robotics startup building dexterous dual-arm robots for industrial logistics and household task automation.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that builds and sells cable-driven humanoid robots with integrated imitation learning software for consumer and industrial markets.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells humanoid robots.
2. Cable-driven electric actuation with 52 degrees of freedom, embedded cameras and depth sensors for on-device perception, and transformer-based imitation learning algorithms that model coordinated whole-body actions from RGB observations.
3. Dexterous upper-body manipulation, coordinated dual-arm task execution, whole-body teleoperation, and imitation learning from human demonstrations.
4. Complete humanoid robots.
5. Humanoids used in homes, logistics operations, service industries, assisted living facilities, and industrial settings.
6. Industrial operators, service providers, consumers, and research organizations.
7. It builds its own humanoid robots and sells them directly to industrial and consumer customers.
8. It pursues a precision-first design approach offering high end-effector speeds up to 10 m/s with a sophisticated whole-body teleoperation infrastructure for scalable imitation learning.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It has alliances with Thundersoft and Seer Robotics and operates as a subsidiary of Stardust Intelligence.
Organization type: A privately held startup and subsidiary.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete humanoid robots.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2022, it has secured thousand-unit volume orders for industrial deployment.
Geography: Based in Shenzhen, China, it focuses on Asia-Pacific markets while pursuing expanding global distribution channels.
Beyond physical AI: It is entirely dedicated to humanoid robotics development and deployment.

points.name: Linkerbot
points.description: Chinese robotics startup manufacturing high-dexterity robotic hands and cloud software for precision manipulation tasks.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that designs and mass-manufactures high-degree-of-freedom dexterous robotic hands and end-effectors for humanoid robots and industrial automation, alongside a cloud platform for training manipulation skills. It builds subsystems used by robot makers, industrial companies, and research institutions.
1. A component supplier that builds dexterous robotic hands and end-effectors for robot makers and industrial users.
2. Linkage transmission, tendon drive, and direct drive architectures incorporating joint modules, motors, reducers, and piezoresistive sensors to achieve sub-millimetre precision.
3. Dexterous manipulation, high load-bearing grasping, complex assembly, irregular object handling, and standardized manipulation skills for industrial and research applications.
4. Components and end-effector hardware supplied to robot makers and industrial users, paired with a cloud-based dataset and training platform.
5. Humanoid robots, industrial flexible automation, robotic assembly, surgical assistance, research, education, and household assistance.
6. Humanoid robot makers, industrial companies, technology manufacturers, universities, and research institutions.
7. Its end-effectors and joint modules are integrated into complete robotic systems by robot manufacturers and used as standalone tools by researchers.
8. It achieves price-performance leverage at roughly one-twentieth the cost of competing high-dexterity platforms while mass-producing hands across a broad span of degrees of freedom.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by Ant Group, HongShan Group, Bank of China Asset Management, Fosun Capital, and state-backed investment funds, with clients including Samsung Electronics, Cambridge University, Stanford University, Peking University, Tsinghua University, and the University of Hong Kong.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of dexterous robotic hands and joint modules.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023, the company holds over 80% global market share in high-degree-of-freedom dexterous hands, has delivered over 10,000 units, and targets a $6 billion valuation while operating five factories.
Geography: Based in China with manufacturing operations in Beijing and Shenzhen, shipping to clients globally across multiple continents.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent 100% of its business strategy and revenue model.

points.name: RobotEra
points.description: Chinese robotics company building full-stack humanoid robots with AI perception for logistics and manufacturing automation.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that builds full-stack bipedal robots, wheeled platforms, and dexterous hands for enterprise logistics and manufacturing, supplying complete machines as well as robotic manipulators to external developers.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete humanoid robots and dexterous hands.
2. Bipedal and wheeled locomotion platforms, gear-driven five-fingered dexterous hands with tactile sensing, and vision-language-action architectures running on self-developed direct-drive actuators.
3. Legged and wheeled mobility, dexterous manipulation, material verification, visual inspection, and exception handling guided by real-time business context.
4. Complete humanoid robots, wheeled platforms, and dexterous hand components.
5. Logistics centers, manufacturing facilities, exhibition environments, retail settings, and research institutions.
6. Logistics operators, manufacturing facilities, research institutions, and other robotics developers.
7. Its complete robots and dexterous manipulators are deployed directly in enterprise warehouse workflows and integrated into machines built by other robotics companies.
8. It combines full-stack humanoid hardware with enterprise software integration to execute end-to-end warehouse workflows within enterprise resource planning systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It runs deployments with China Post and SF Express, integrates with SAP Extended Warehouse Management, supplies developers including Skild AI, Humanoid AI, and Extend Robotics, and is backed by SF Group, HSG, IDG Capital, Alibaba, Crystal Stream, Vision Plus Capital, and Lenovo Capital.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and components.
Scale and maturity: Having delivered over 600 units globally, the organization holds a valuation exceeding $1.4 billion and is scaling thousands-of-units deployments across more than ten logistics centers.
Geography: Based in Shenzhen, China, it operates globally with deployments across exhibition, retail, and logistics environments.
Beyond physical AI: Embodied AI robotics and hardware development constitute the entire focus and business of the organization.

points.name: Genesis AI
points.description: Robotics startup building physics simulation and foundation models for training embodied AI systems.
points.bullets:
A full-stack robotics and AI model developer that builds general-purpose wheeled robots, dexterous robotic hands, and a universal robotics foundation model trained using a proprietary physics simulation engine that generates synthetic data.
1. A vertically integrated robot maker and AI model developer that designs and sells complete robots and dexterous hands, and licenses a robotics foundation model intended to run on robots made by other companies.
2. A universal robotics foundation model and a multi-physics simulation engine paired with a photo-realistic renderer and a cross-platform compiler that lowers Python code to run on GPUs, mobile processors, and specialized hardware.
3. General-purpose physical manipulation, dexterous tasks like chopping and solving puzzles, cross-platform robot adaptability, and synthetic training data generation.
4. Complete wheeled robots, dexterous hands, sensor gloves for data capture, and a horizontal robotics platform for other developers.
5. Logistics, manufacturing, hospitality, healthcare, consumer sectors, factories, and laboratories.
6. Robotics researchers, AI developers, manufacturing facilities, laboratories, hospitals, and robot makers.
7. It operates across the entire stack, designing its own hardware and AI models while providing a foundation model and simulation platform for other robot developers to build upon.
8. It co-designs hardware and AI, using a proprietary physics engine that generates synthetic training data orders of magnitude faster than real time to solve data scarcity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by Khosla Ventures, Eclipse Ventures, Y Combinator, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, and Bpifrance.
Organization type: A privately held startup and full-stack robotics company.
Business model: Robot and hardware sales, paired with foundation model licensing and platform provision.
Scale and maturity: Founded in late 2024, emerged from stealth in 2025 with a $105 million seed round, and employs over 20 researchers.
Geography: Based in Paris, France, targeting deployments across North America and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and robotics development constitute the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Persona AI
points.description: Robotics startup building rugged humanoid robots for industrial welding, assembly, and material handling in confined spaces.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and deploys rugged industrial humanoid robots for heavy welding, inspection, and material handling in maritime shipyards and other harsh environments.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete humanoid robots for industrial applications.
2. Bipedal humanoid platforms integrating environmental awareness perception, manipulation, and tendon-driven dexterous hands with 12 degrees of freedom licensed from NASA.
3. Legged locomotion, dexterous manipulation, confined-space navigation, and autonomous industrial welding using standard human tools.
4. Complete humanoid robots provided through a robotics-as-a-service leasing model and pilot deployment programs.
5. Shipyards, defense logistics, energy facilities, and heavy construction sites.
6. Commercial shipbuilders, naval defense agencies, and heavy industrial manufacturers.
7. Its complete humanoid robots are leased to and operated within industrial shipyard facilities.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Has secured deployments and pilot programs with HD Hyundai and Louisiana Shipyards, and licensed dexterous hand technology from NASA.
Organization type: A privately held robotics startup founded by NASA robotics veterans.
Business model: Robotics-as-a-service leasing contracts and pilot deployment agreements.
Scale and maturity: A young company launched in 2024 that has raised over $27 million and secured active pilot deployments across the United States and Asia.
Geography: Based in Houston, Texas, with operational deployments in South Korea, Vietnam, the Philippines, and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the organization's complete business focus.

points.name: Collaborative Robotics
points.description: Robotics startup building autonomous mobile manipulators with on-device AI for warehouse and logistics material handling tasks.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile manipulator robots for material handling, combining mobility, dual-arm manipulation and on-device AI for human-shared environments.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete autonomous mobile manipulator robots.
2. Mobile manipulator hardware with self-swapping batteries, dual-arm manipulation and adaptive grippers, running local task inference on edge compute modules with cloud-based fleet management.
3. Autonomous navigation, mobile manipulation, autonomous task identification without warehouse management system integration, and fleet orchestration.
4. Complete robots sold as integrated hardware and software platforms.
5. Warehouses, manufacturing facilities, hospitals, logistics operations and supply chain environments.
6. Logistics operators, manufacturers, healthcare systems and pharmaceutical companies.
7. Its robots are deployed as complete systems directly into customer facilities.
8. Autonomous task identification software allows robots to self-identify and initiate work without human dispatchers or warehouse management system integration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Runs on NVIDIA Jetson modules and uses NVIDIA Isaac Sim, with cloud infrastructure from AWS, and venture investment from General Catalyst, Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Calibrate Ventures and Mayo Clinic.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robot platforms.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2022 that has raised $100 million in Series B funding and logged over 12,627 operating hours across deployed systems.
Geography: Based in Santa Clara, California, and Seattle, Washington, with deployments in North America and international supply chain operations.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play robotics company whose entire business is autonomous mobile manipulation for material handling.

points.name: Dyna Robotics
points.description: US robotics startup developing foundation models that enable robot arms to learn and perform complex manipulation tasks autonomously.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds embodied foundation models for robotic dexterity and manipulation, enabling autonomous control of robotic arms in production environments.
1. An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on robotic arms to automate repetitive industrial tasks.
2. Vision-language-action models combined with proprietary engineered reward models that provide feedback on robot interactions to train and refine manipulation policies.
3. Dexterous manipulation, natural language and visual instruction following, sustained autonomous operation, and zero-shot environment generalization.
4. AI models integrated into complete robotic manipulation systems and deployed directly in production environments.
5. Industrial automation, logistics, food packaging, and stationary manipulation tasks such as napkin and laundry folding.
6. Industrial manipulation and logistics operators, as well as businesses of all sizes seeking workflow automation.
7. Its foundation models are integrated into robotic arms to perform manipulation tasks for end operators.
8. Its engineered reward models enable sustained autonomous operation with high accuracy and zero-shot generalization across diverse physical conditions without environment-specific tuning.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by CRV, First Round, Umami Capital, Samsung Next, and the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and held within the RoboStrategy portfolio.
Organization type: Privately held early-stage startup.
Business model: Software licensing and systems integration contracts for deploying embodied AI models in production environments.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup based in Redwood City that has raised $120 million in Series A funding and demonstrated public commercial deployments.
Geography: Based in Redwood City, operating within North America with demonstrations at major international robotics conferences.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the entire focus of the organization's business and research mission.

points.name: The Bot Company
points.description: Home robotics startup building autonomous humanoid robots with on-device AI for domestic task automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells wheeled home robots for domestic tasks like tidying and food preparation, integrating on-device AI and foundation models for autonomous operation in household environments.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete wheeled home robots.
2. Wheeled mobile robots with on-device large language models, vision systems, and tendon-driven actuators.
3. Domestic task execution, tidying, and food preparation in unstructured home environments.
4. Complete robots sold as consumer products, priced per unit or via monthly subscription.
5. Homes and household environments.
6. Consumers and early-adopter households.
7. It designs and manufactures complete robots and sells them directly to consumers.
8. A safety-first design for unstructured home environments with on-device processing that minimizes cloud dependency and a continuous learning model from customer feedback.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, Nabeel Hyatt, and Greenoaks, with Eclipse Ventures holding a portfolio stake.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales and consumer subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A Series B startup that has raised over $300 million, operating at a pre-revenue stage with first consumer deliveries planned from a Hayward, California manufacturing facility.
Geography: Based in Hayward, California, targeting the North American market.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is entirely focused on home robotics and consumer embodied AI systems, with no business activities outside this domain.

points.name: Viam
points.description: Robotics infrastructure startup building cloud-connected software to help teams deploy and manage fleets of robots at the edge.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds a modular, cloud-connected robot operating system for developing, deploying, and managing physical AI and robotics applications, serving systems integrators and automation practices.
1. A developer tools company whose software platform and edge runtime robotics engineers use to build and manage machines.
2. A local-first architecture with an on-device binary that handles motion control, SLAM, vision services, and data management while syncing with managed cloud services for fleet management and machine learning.
3. Hardware abstraction, data pipelines, on-device inference, SLAM, vision, motion control, fleet orchestration, and machine learning.
4. Licensed software, open-source modular components, Python SDKs, and managed cloud services that install on edge hardware.
5. Robots and IoT applications across agriculture, food service, medicine, climate, factories, and warehouses.
6. Systems integrators, automation practices modernizing existing equipment, and robotics startups.
7. Its software installs onto existing and newly deployed edge hardware, acting as a horizontal infrastructure layer for systems integrators.
8. Enabling organizations to add robotics and automation capabilities through software-only installation onto deployed hardware to reduce capital expenditure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A founding member of the Robots for America coalition and backed by NEA.
Organization type: A privately held technology company founded by enterprise cloud infrastructure leaders.
Business model: Software licenses, subscriptions, and managed cloud services.
Scale and maturity: A growth-stage company founded in 2021 that has raised $45 million and supports over 100 compatible hardware libraries.
Geography: Based in New York, USA, and serving a global market.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on edge AI, robotics, and physical automation infrastructure, with no diversification into unrelated business domains.

points.name: Bedrock Robotics
points.description: Austin-based robotics startup retrofitting heavy construction equipment with autonomous control systems for continuous on-site operations.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds retrofit autonomy kits and workflow software to convert existing heavy construction equipment like excavators and graders into unmanned machines for general contractors.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses and installs retrofit autonomy kits for existing construction equipment.
2. End-to-end machine learning models trained on entire trajectories and real jobsite data, integrated with onboard compute and sensors to enable autonomous earthmoving.
3. Autonomous excavation, mass earthmoving, site preparation, and multi-machine fleet orchestration with centimeter-level accuracy.
4. A reversible hardware and software autonomy kit mounted onto a customer's existing fleet, paired with workflow and fleet supervision software.
5. Heavy construction equipment, including excavators, bulldozers, and loaders, operating on live job sites.
6. Heavy civil construction companies and site preparation contractors.
7. Its autonomy kits and software are integrated into existing heavy machinery fleets operated by construction contractors.
8. It applies end-to-end multimodal machine learning trained on real jobsite data rather than hand-crafted heuristics to navigate unpredictable construction environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include CapitalG, Valor Atreides AI Fund, NVentures, Eclipse Ventures, and 8VC, while Sundt Construction, Zachry Construction, Champion Site Prep, and Capitol Aggregates deploy the technology, using Anyscale and Ray for compute and being an NVIDIA Inception member.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware and software kit sales combined with deployment contracts for autonomous construction equipment.
Scale and maturity: A growth-stage startup founded in 2024 that has raised a $270 million Series B at a $1.75 billion valuation and has active commercial deployments.
Geography: Based and operating across the United States, with active deployments in California, Arizona, Texas, and Arkansas.
Beyond physical AI: Autonomous construction equipment retrofitting and operation is the organization's entire focus and core business.

points.name: Machina Labs
points.description: Manufacturing robotics startup building AI-powered robotic cells for autonomous metal fabrication and aerospace parts production.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator and manufacturing technology company that builds and operates software-defined robotic factories for metal forming and assembly, combining dual-arm industrial robots, edge AI, and real-time sensor feedback to produce complex sheet metal parts without custom tooling for aerospace, defense, and automotive customers.
1. A systems integrator that builds and operates containerized robotic manufacturing cells and deployable elastic factories for on-demand metal fabrication.
2. Dual industrial robot arms perform incremental sheet metal forming layer-by-layer from CAD models, guided by edge inference and force, torque, and displacement sensors in a real-time closed-loop control system that uses machine learning to refine manufacturing parameters.
3. Robotic metal forming, trimming, scanning, and heat treating of large complex curved sheet metal parts without geometry-specific dies or molds, enabling rapid production switching.
4. Complete robotic manufacturing cells, intelligent factory systems, portable deployable factories, and on-demand manufacturing services operated by the company itself.
5. Aerospace structures, missile bodies, hypersonic structures, airframes, toroidal tanks, low-volume high-variation automotive panels, and heavy machinery.
6. Defense primes, aerospace contractors, automotive manufacturers, government agencies, and space agencies.
7. It integrates industrial robotics hardware, sensors, and edge AI into complete deployed manufacturing systems that it operates to produce parts for end-use customers.
8. It eliminates custom tooling and dies to deliver production-grade metal components in days rather than months, enabling rapid iteration and qualification.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Toyota, Lockheed Martin, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, Woven Capital, Lockheed Martin Ventures, and Balerion Space Ventures.
Organization type: Privately held advanced manufacturing startup.
Business model: Manufacturing contracts, on-demand part production services, and deployable factory operations.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019, raised $124 million in Series C funding, and building a 200,000-square-foot factory to operate up to 50 robotic cells.
Geography: Based in Los Angeles, California, USA, with a focus on domestic deployment for U.S. defense and aerospace customers.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and advanced physical automation are central to the entire business model and mission, representing the core technological and operational foundation of all products and services.

points.name: Rokae
points.description: Chinese robotics company building industrial and collaborative robots with integrated on-device AI for manufacturing automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that designs and manufactures industrial, collaborative, and humanoid robots integrated with on-device artificial intelligence for autonomous physical task execution, primarily for industrial manufacturing sectors.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells industrial, collaborative, and humanoid robots, force-controlled joint modules, and integrated automation systems.
2. A full-stack robotics architecture spanning core hardware components, force-controlled joint modules, sensors, and hierarchical embodied intelligence models optimized for on-device edge execution.
3. Autonomous physical task execution, real-time manufacturing automation, force-controlled manipulation, and near-complete production line automation.
4. Complete robots, joint modules, and end-to-end integrated automation systems deployed in manufacturing facilities.
5. Industrial manufacturing, automotive production lines, electronics assembly, new energy vehicle factories, home appliance manufacturing, food and dairy processing, welding facilities, and medical technology settings.
6. Automotive manufacturers, electronics producers, new energy vehicle makers, home appliance factories, food and dairy producers, welding automation facilities, and medical technology companies.
7. It designs and builds its own proprietary robots and hardware while also integrating end-to-end automation systems directly into customer production lines.
8. Vertical integration of proprietary hardware and edge AI models optimized for real-time manufacturing, with a demonstrated track record of achieving near-complete automation on production lines for major consumer brands.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and joint modules combined with contracts for integrated automation systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, headquartered in Shandong, China, operating at industrial scale with deployed systems across multiple major manufacturing facilities and expanding European operations.
Geography: Based in Shandong, China, with operations focused on Chinese manufacturing sectors and expanding European industrial deployments.
Beyond physical AI: Physical robotics and artificial intelligence form the entire focus of its business activities.

points.name: 1X Technologies
points.description: Norwegian robotics company building humanoid home robots that run vision and language AI models directly on-device for household tasks.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that designs and builds bipedal and wheeled robots for home and light-commercial use, integrating proprietary tendon-driven actuators, dexterous hands and AI models into complete systems for consumers and enterprises.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete humanoid robots and teleoperation services.
2. Bipedal humanoids with gearless tendon-driven actuators, 25-degree-of-freedom hands with tactile sensing, and video-pretrained world models trained on teleoperation and internet-scale data.
3. Bipedal locomotion, dexterous manipulation, safe human interaction, household chore execution and simulated environment prediction.
4. Complete humanoid robots sold through upfront purchase or monthly subscription, paired with teleoperation and cloud-based AI services.
5. Homes, warehouses, factories, logistics operations and healthcare facilities.
6. Consumers, private equity portfolio companies, security firms and logistics operators.
7. It designs and builds its own complete robots and operates the teleoperation and AI infrastructure that supports them.
8. It uses soft, compliant materials and lightweight tendon-driven actuation for inherently safe human interaction, paired with a hybrid autonomy model combining remote teleoperation with video-pretrained world models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by OpenAI Startup Fund, EQT Ventures and Samsung NEXT, with development collaborations with NVIDIA and a commercial deployment partnership with EQT.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales through upfront purchase or monthly rental subscriptions, augmented by teleoperation services.
Scale and maturity: Raised over $136 million in total funding, targeting a $10 billion valuation, with plans to mass-produce 10,000 robots from a California factory.
Geography: Based in Norway and California, operating and targeting initial consumer deployments in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on physical AI and humanoid robotics, with no diversification outside of developing, manufacturing and operating home and commercial robots.

points.name: Agility
points.description: Robotics company building bipedal humanoid robots for warehouse and logistics automation tasks.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that designs and manufactures bipedal robots for material handling and logistics automation. It builds complete robots, integrating sensors, onboard computers, arms, and fleet orchestration software, and deploys them in industrial environments for logistics providers and manufacturers.
1. A robot maker that designs and manufactures complete humanoid robots for industrial material handling.
2. Bipedal humanoid robots integrating onboard computers, sensors, modular end effectors, and autonomy software built and validated using GPU physics simulation and world models.
3. Bipedal locomotion, material handling, tote transfers, and fleet orchestration alongside warehouse management and autonomous mobile robot systems.
4. Complete humanoid robots and orchestration software, delivered through robotics-as-a-service and direct sales.
5. Warehouses, factories, distribution centers, and logistics operations.
6. Third-party logistics providers, e-commerce fulfillment centers, automotive manufacturers, and consumer goods companies.
7. It designs and builds its own complete humanoid robots and operates them at customer facilities under service contracts.
8. It focuses on narrow, repeatable logistics workflows and has achieved early commercial deployments with published throughput metrics rather than pursuing general-purpose autonomy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with NVIDIA to integrate IGX Thor and Halos Core into its robots, and counts GXO, Amazon, Toyota, Spanx, Mercado Libre, and Schaeffler as customers.
Organization type: A privately held robotics company.
Business model: It makes money through robotics-as-a-service contracts and direct robot sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, it operates a production facility with annual capacity for up to 10,000 units and has secured revenue-generating customer contracts.
Geography: It is based in Oregon and deploys robots at customer facilities across the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Humanoid robotics and physical AI for warehouse automation is its entire focus and mission.

points.name: Apptronik
points.description: US robotics startup building general-purpose humanoid robots for industrial automation and physical labor tasks.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that designs and manufactures general-purpose bipedal and wheeled robots for industrial and logistics tasks, building complete machines with proprietary actuators and swappable batteries for continuous operation.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete humanoid robots.
2. General-purpose humanoid platforms using high-reduction strain wave gears and planetary roller screws in a rotary-linear split actuator architecture, paired with hot-swappable battery systems and modular end-effectors.
3. General-purpose manipulation, case-picking, palletizing, tote delivery, and legged or wheeled locomotion in human-centric environments.
4. Complete humanoid robots delivered through pilot deployments and manufacturing partnerships, with plans for commercial fleet sales and robots-as-a-service models.
5. Warehouses, factories, automotive manufacturing, logistics, and material handling operations.
6. Manufacturers, automotive OEMs, third-party logistics operators, and electronics contract manufacturers.
7. Its complete humanoid robots are piloted and operated by industrial end-users in their own facilities, with contract manufacturing partners handling scaled production.
8. Hot-swappable battery systems allowing continuous operation without charging breaks and a heritage translating NASA legged robotics research into modular workforce humanoids.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Google DeepMind to run Gemini Robotics foundation models, collaborates with NVIDIA on Project GR00T, uses Texas Instruments motor control components, and counts Mercedes-Benz, GXO Logistics, Jabil, Amazon, and NASA as deployment, investment, or research partners.
Organization type: A privately held startup spun out of a university robotics lab.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete humanoid robots, with stated intentions to pursue robots-as-a-service models focused on return on investment.
Scale and maturity: Has raised over $935 million in Series A funding extensions at a valuation of roughly $5 billion, employs around 300 people, and operates a 90,000 sq ft training facility while moving from pilots to commercial deployments.
Geography: Based in Austin, Texas, USA, with pilot deployments and manufacturing partnerships across North America and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and humanoid robotics are the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: DJI
points.description: Chinese drone manufacturer building edge AI capabilities into commercial and industrial aerial platforms.
points.bullets:
A drone and aerial robotics manufacturer that builds complete, vertically integrated unmanned aerial vehicles, onboard edge computing units, cameras, and software development kits for consumer, enterprise, and industrial applications.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that designs and sells complete unmanned aerial vehicles, alongside onboard compute modules, gimbal cameras, and docking stations.
2. The core technology centers on fully integrated aircraft designs combining proprietary flight controllers, electronic speed controllers, computer vision algorithms, and edge inference silicon running within onboard computing units.
3. Specific capabilities include autonomous aerial flight, precision spraying, obstacle avoidance, 3D surveying and digital twin generation, automated docking, and onboard AI inference for real-time perception and decision-making.
4. Customers get it as complete drones, onboard compute modules, gimbal payloads, automated docking stations, licensed processing software, and software development kits.
5. The machines are used in agriculture, construction, public safety, infrastructure inspection, industrial logistics, wildlife conservation, and filmmaking.
6. The types of customer it sells to include consumers, farmers, logistics operators, infrastructure inspectors, public safety agencies, and software developers.
7. Its complete platforms and payloads are deployed directly by end-users, integrated into automated workflows by software developers, and operated via cloud platforms by enterprise customers.
8. Its approach is distinguished by massive manufacturing scale, aggressive pricing, and deep vertical integration of the electro-mechanical and software stack, dominating the civilian market.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It operates with Microsoft Azure as its preferred cloud computing partner, counts HongShan as an investor, and integrates with third-party software platforms like IMGING and Spexi.
Organization type: It is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of drones, payloads, and docks, alongside licensed software and cloud platform subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: It is a large, mature, well-capitalized organization holding a dominant majority share of the commercial drone market and maintaining a massive global installed base.
Geography: It is headquartered in Shenzhen, China, and operates globally across the Americas, Europe, and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on aerial robotics, edge computing hardware, and physical AI.

points.name: Figure AI
points.description: US robotics startup building general-purpose humanoid robots for manufacturing and logistics automation using vision-language models.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and builds general-purpose humanoid robots paired with proprietary vision-language-action models for autonomous physical labor in human environments.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells general-purpose humanoid robots integrated with in-house AI control software.
2. Bipedal humanoid platforms with rotary-linear actuator architectures, strain wave gearing and liquid cooling, controlled by a closed-source vision-language-action model using a hierarchical dual-system architecture trained on retargeted human motion data.
3. Dynamic whole-body coordination, dexterous manipulation, conversational human-machine interaction, autonomous navigation and task execution in cluttered industrial environments.
4. Complete autonomous humanoid robots deployed through commercial pilot programs and paid operational leases on customer production lines.
5. Automotive manufacturing plants, logistics warehouses and distribution centers, with development targeting domestic home environments.
6. Automakers, logistics operators and retail distribution companies.
7. It builds complete robots internally and deploys them directly into the operations of manufacturing and logistics customers.
8. It vertically integrates proprietary robot hardware with a custom vision-language-action model controlled via a hierarchical dual-system architecture, using a global mobile app to crowdsource human task video for training.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and investors include BMW Group, Amazon, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Intel Capital and individual investor Jeff Bezos.
Organization type: A privately held robotics startup.
Business model: It makes money through paid commercial robot deployments, charging customers an hourly rate per robot-operating-hour.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2022, it has raised over $1 billion in Series C funding at a $39 billion valuation, operating a manufacturing facility tooled for 12,000 units annually with roughly 150 robots delivered to date.
Geography: Based in California, United States, with primary operational deployments at customer facilities in South Carolina.
Beyond physical AI: It is a pure-play physical AI and humanoid robotics company with its entire focus on designing, manufacturing and deploying autonomous labor.

points.name: Unitree
points.description: Chinese robotics company building affordable humanoid robots for on-device AI vision and manipulation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and builds cost-efficient quadruped and humanoid robots and their core components, selling complete machines to researchers, educators, and industrial users.

2. Electric-motor-powered bipedal and quadrupedal robots featuring in-house quasi-direct-drive actuators, joint motors, precision reducers, sensors, and dexterous hands integrated with edge AI computing modules.
3. High-dynamic legged locomotion, dynamic balancing, whole-body control, acrobatic movement, and dexterous manipulation.
4. Complete robots and robotic arms, alongside individual actuators, motors, and sensors.
5. Humanoids, quadrupeds, warehouses, factories, power inspection facilities, research institutions, and education.
6. Research institutions, universities, developers, enterprise software platforms, and industrial manufacturers.
7. Its complete robots are purchased by research labs, educators, and industrial enterprises, while its humanoid chassis serves as the reference body for AI compute platforms.
8. High-volume mass production and vertical integration of core actuation components enable price points drastically below comparable competitors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, RealSense, RoboSense, Hesai, SAP, BYD, Meituan, Tencent, Alibaba, Ant Group, Xiaomi, ByteDance, DeepSeek, and CATL.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.

Geography: Based in Hangzhou, China, deploying robots in over 30 countries with its largest overseas commercial channel in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are its entire focus.

points.name: Waymo
points.description: US autonomous vehicle company deploying self-driving robotaxis and delivery fleets using onboard AI for real-time perception and navigation.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vehicle company and robotaxi operator that designs Level 4 self-driving systems and runs driverless ride-hailing fleets at scale. It develops the complete autonomy stack, including multi-modal sensor fusion and planning software, and integrates it into vehicles manufactured by external automakers to operate commercial transportation services for passengers and logistics clients.
1. An autonomous vehicle operator and autonomy software developer that builds self-driving systems and operates a fleet of robotaxis it upfits itself, selling rides as a service rather than licensing its software to automakers.
2. A modular perceive-predict-plan software architecture using redundant multi-modal sensor fusion across lidar, radar, and cameras, processed on custom edge compute hardware, with neural networks trained on cloud TPUs and tested via proprietary closed-loop simulation.
3. Level 4 autonomous navigation, geofenced urban driving, highway driving, sensor-fusion perception, and real-time motion planning.
4. A robotaxi fleet it operates itself, providing driverless ride-hailing and delivery services via a mobile application to passengers and logistics partners.
5. Robotaxis, autonomous delivery vehicles, and autonomous trucks operated in urban streets, highways, and geofenced commercial ride-hailing zones.
6. Ride-hailing passengers, delivery platforms, logistics operators, and freight brokers.
7. It buys vehicle platforms from automakers, upfits them with its own autonomous hardware and software, and operates the complete fleet itself.
8. A sensor-heavy, redundant hardware approach combined with an extensive proprietary simulation platform and over a decade of real-world driving data to achieve fully driverless Level 4 commercial operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Alphabet, Hyundai, Zeekr, Geely, Jaguar, Toyota, Uber, DoorDash, Daimler Trucks, and Volvo Trucks.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary of a publicly traded technology parent company.
Business model: Per-ride passenger fares, delivery fees, and freight logistics contracts from operating its own autonomous vehicle fleets.
Scale and maturity: A mature, heavily funded corporate subsidiary operating over a thousand vehicles, completing half a million paid rides weekly across more than ten U.S. metropolitan areas, and having accumulated over 100 million autonomous miles.
Geography: Headquartered in Mountain View, California, with commercial robotaxi operations across major U.S. cities and expansion efforts in the United Kingdom and Japan.
Beyond physical AI: Autonomous vehicle operation and physical AI is the sole focus of the organization, though it leverages cloud infrastructure and AI research from its parent company.

points.name: Spanx
points.description: Apparel brand deploying humanoid robots in warehouses to automate tote transfer and order fulfillment for shapewear products.
points.bullets:
An apparel company that operates as an end user and early adopter of humanoid robots in its own warehouse, deploying commercial robotic systems alongside a third-party logistics provider for tote transfer and fulfillment workflows.
1. A retail apparel company that operates third-party humanoid and mobile robots in its own warehouse facilities.
2. Autonomous warehouse tote transfer and logistics workflow automation through deployed humanoid robots.
3. Robots-as-a-service operated in its own facilities.
4. Warehouses and distribution centers.
5. It operates humanoid robots built by robot makers inside its own logistics facilities.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Agility Robotics and GXO Logistics.
Organization type: Privately held apparel company.

points.name: BMW

points.bullets:
A vehicle maker and manufacturing operator that builds premium passenger cars and runs large-scale factories where it deploys third-party humanoid robots, edge AI inspection systems, and autonomous driving stacks in its own production lines and vehicle fleets.
1. An automaker that manufactures passenger vehicles and operates its own manufacturing plants, acting as a deployer and integrator of physical AI systems rather than a producer of robotics hardware or models.
2. Advanced driver assistance systems integrating 4D radar and lidar sensors, neuromorphic monitoring systems for intelligent cockpits, digital twin factory simulations, and edge AI vision running on assembly-line inspection cameras.
3. Autonomous driving up to Level 3 on public roads, in-factory logistics automation, precision assembly using cobots and humanoid robots, predictive maintenance, and 3D quality inspection of vehicle bodies.
4. Complete passenger vehicles sold to consumers, deployed automation run in its own factories, and licensed autonomy software integrated into its cars.
5. Automobiles, factory assembly lines, logistics warehouses, and smart factories.
6. Consumers for its vehicles, and its own manufacturing operations for factory automation.
7. It buys and operates humanoid robots, autonomous systems, and batteries from suppliers to run in its own factories and integrate into the vehicles it sells.
8. It acts as an early enterprise adopter running high-volume production pilots of humanoid robots on active automotive assembly lines rather than developing robotics hardware itself.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Figure AI, Hexagon Robotics, Sereact, Intel, Mobileye, Innoviz, SynSense, Momenta, Applied Intuition, CATL, Qualcomm, Baidu, HERE Technologies, Seoul Robotics, Vicon, and Workswell.
Organization type: Publicly traded automotive manufacturer.

Scale and maturity: A large, mature global manufacturer with massive production volume, running multi-year robotics pilots involving tens of thousands of vehicles and thousands of operational robot hours.
Geography: Headquartered in Germany with manufacturing plants and vehicle deployments globally, including major facilities in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization designs, engineers, and sells premium passenger vehicles globally.

points.name: Physical Intelligence
points.description: US robotics startup developing foundation models that enable different robot platforms to perform diverse physical tasks without retraining.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on other companies' robots. It builds general-purpose vision-language-action models that map visual observations and natural-language instructions to continuous motor commands, enabling diverse robot platforms to perform complex manipulation tasks without task-specific retraining. The company operates in the software and model layer of the robotics stack, licensing its models to manufacturers, logistics operators, and enterprises deploying robots in diverse environments.
1. An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on other companies' robots.
2. Vision-language-action foundation models using flow matching and diffusion-based action generation for high-frequency continuous control of dexterous robotic systems.
3. Cross-embodiment generalization, dexterous manipulation, long-horizon task execution, and zero-shot generalization to unseen environments.
4. Models running on customers' hardware, licensed software, and cloud APIs.
5. Humanoids, robotic arms, and mobile robots used in warehouses, factories, e-commerce fulfillment, and assembly operations.
6. Robot makers, manufacturers, logistics operators, and enterprises deploying robots.
7. Its models are integrated by hardware manufacturers and robot OEMs into their own machines.
8. It trains on over 10,000 hours of cross-embodiment data across seven robot platforms and 68 tasks to achieve generalizable physical intelligence.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Thrive Capital, OpenAI, CapitalG, Lux Capital, Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Jeff Bezos, and the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, while collaborating with Scale, Trossen Robotics, AgiBot, and Robot.com.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions, per-task APIs, and industry-specific vertical bundles.
Scale and maturity: A recently founded unicorn startup with over $1 billion in funding and a valuation exceeding $5.6 billion.
Geography: Based in the United States within a 30-mile radius of San Francisco, serving enterprise customers across North America and international markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is the organization's entire focus, comprising all research, product development, and commercial activities.

points.name: Skild AI
points.description: US robotics startup building a foundation model that controls any robot body type through a unified software platform.

An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on other companies' robots, building a hardware-agnostic "brain" designed to transfer skills across different robot morphologies and environments without extensive retraining for industrial and enterprise customers.
1. An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on other companies' robots.
2. Omni-bodied robot foundation models trained on physics-based simulation, synthetic data, and human videos using GPU simulation frameworks.
3. General-purpose robotic intelligence enabling zero-shot generalization, dexterous manipulation, legged locomotion, autonomous navigation, and rapid in-context adaptation across diverse hardware.
4. Models running on customers' hardware, integrated into industrial robotic arms, mobile robots, and quadrupeds through OEM partnerships.
5. Manufacturing assembly lines, warehouses, construction sites, security patrols, facility inspection, and data center operations.
6. Robot makers, industrial automation providers, contract manufacturers, and systems integrators.
7. Its models are integrated by robot makers into their hardware for deployment across industrial facilities.
8. It trains on over 100,000 distinct robot configurations in physics-based simulation to achieve omni-bodied control and zero-shot generalization across any robot morphology.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include NVIDIA, ABB Robotics, Universal Robots, Foxconn, MiR, SoftBank, Amazon, Samsung, LG, and In-Q-Tel.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and per-robot royalties.
Scale and maturity: Valued at over $14 billion with roughly $1.8 billion in total funding, generating $30 million in revenue in 2025.
Geography: Based in Pittsburgh and the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in India, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and robotics represent the entire focus of the company, which positions itself as foundational infrastructure for scaling intelligent physical systems.

points.name: Wayve
points.description: UK autonomous driving startup building end-to-end AI models that teach vehicles to drive safely from sensor data without maps.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer whose end-to-end AI foundation models and self-driving stack learn to drive from raw camera data without hand-coded rules or HD maps, for automakers and mobility operators.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a mapless, vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving stack to automakers and fleet operators.
2. End-to-end deep learning foundation models, including vision-language-action models and generative world simulators, trained on large-scale driving footage to convert raw sensor inputs into driving actions.
3. Mapless Level 4 autonomous urban navigation, zero-shot generalization to new cities, and language-controllable interpretability of driving decisions.
4. Licensed autonomy software and AI models running on automotive-grade compute platforms in partner vehicles, alongside generative simulation tools for validation.
5. Passenger robotaxis, level 4 autonomous vehicles, and urban mobility fleets.
6. Automakers, mobility platforms, and ride-hailing operators.
7. Its driving software is integrated by automakers and mobility platforms into their vehicles and robotaxi fleets.
8. Replaces modular sense-plan-act architectures and HD-map dependencies with a single end-to-end neural network that learns driving behavior from diverse, real-world visual data.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors and partners include Uber, Nissan, NVIDIA, Microsoft, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Eclipse, and Balderton.
Organization type: A privately held venture-backed startup.
Business model: Software licenses, per-vehicle or per-ride royalties, and autonomous mobility service fees.
Scale and maturity: A well-funded, growth-stage company that has raised $2.5 billion, including a $1.2 billion Series D in February 2026, and is conducting level 4 robotaxi trials in London.
Geography: Headquartered in the United Kingdom with a United States headquarters in Sunnyvale, operating autonomous vehicle trials in the UK and Tokyo.
Beyond physical AI: Autonomous driving and embodied AI for vehicle automation is its entire focus.

points.name: Covariant
points.description: Warehouse robotics company building AI-powered picking systems that operate at scale in global fulfillment centers.

An AI model developer that builds foundation models for robotic manipulation and also deploys complete AI-powered pick-and-place robotic systems in warehouse fulfillment centers. It combines edge inference on local sensors with foundation models so industrial arms can perceive, reason, grasp and handle unfamiliar items in real time for logistics providers.
