2. Foundation models trained on large-scale real-world manipulation data, combining computer vision, reinforcement learning and robotic control on a GPU-accelerated edge platform.
3. On-device inference, object perception, dexterous manipulation, piece picking, sortation induction and palletization of mixed SKUs.
4. Complete robotic picking systems, induction cells and putwall systems integrated into warehouse operations.
5. Warehouses, fulfillment centers and distribution operations handling apparel, health-and-beauty, grocery, pharmaceuticals and parcels.
6. Logistics providers, third-party logistics operators, retailers, e-commerce fulfillment operators and warehouse automation integrators.
7. It builds and operates its own deployed robotic picking systems and licenses its foundation models to integrators and machine makers.
8. A proprietary data flywheel where its large deployed fleet collects massive real-world manipulation trajectories to train its foundation model for generalization across novel SKUs and warehouse environments without retraining.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Amazon holds a non-exclusive license and hired its founding team, while KNAPP and ABB integrate its technology, with investment from Radical Ventures, Index Ventures and notable AI researchers.
Organization type: A privately held startup acquired and acquihired by Amazon.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic systems, software licensing of its AI models and recurring automation-as-a-service contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017 with over $250 million in total funding and an estimated $2.5 billion valuation, deploying nearly 300 robots across 15 countries.
Geography: Headquartered in Berkeley, California, with deployed systems across North America, Europe and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is entirely focused on edge AI-powered warehouse robotics and does not operate in other business domains.

points.name: Overview AI
points.description: Manufacturing AI company deploying edge vision cameras for real-time defect detection on production lines.
points.bullets:
A smart camera maker that builds edge-deployed AI vision systems for real-time defect detection on manufacturing production lines, combining image sensors, embedded GPUs and trained neural networks into integrated hardware for industrial customers.
1. A vision system maker that builds and sells AI-powered smart cameras for factory quality inspection.
2. Embedded NVIDIA Jetson GPUs running computer vision models trained with as few as five example images, performing local inference without cloud connectivity.
3. On-device defect detection, rapid few-shot model training, 3D perception, image segmentation and real-time data logging at the edge.
4. Complete smart cameras with integrated lighting and optics, shipped as standalone hardware units.
5. Factory production lines and manufacturing quality inspection stations.
6. Manufacturers across diverse industrial sectors seeking automated visual inspection.
7. Its smart cameras are installed by manufacturers directly onto production lines and integrated with factory automation infrastructure via industrial protocols.
8. Few-shot model training in under an hour and an all-in-one camera design provide a lower-cost, faster-to-deploy alternative to traditional machine vision systems without requiring cloud subscriptions or per-inspection fees.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Builds embedded NVIDIA Jetson GPUs into its cameras and integrates with Siemens Industrial Edge factory automation infrastructure.
Organization type: A privately held technology startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of integrated smart cameras.
Scale and maturity: An early to growth-stage startup with proven technology deployments across multiple manufacturing applications.
Geography: Based in and operates primarily within North America and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and physical automation through visual inspection systems represent the complete strategic purpose and exclusive business activity of the company.

points.name: DeepSeek
points.description: Chinese AI company developing highly efficient open-source models optimized for on-device inference.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds highly efficient open-weight large language, reasoning and embodied-AI foundation models, including small distilled variants suitable for on-device inference, for robot makers, chip companies and developers.
1. An AI model developer whose foundation and reasoning models run on other companies' silicon and robots, sold as open weights and via inference APIs.
2. Sparse-attention transformer architectures and distilled reasoning models with as few as 1.5 billion parameters, optimized to lower compute and memory costs for inference.
3. Natural language processing, mathematical reasoning, automated software engineering and multimodal embodied reasoning for robot control.
4. Open-weight model releases, inference APIs and distilled models that run on customer hardware.
5. Humanoid robots, on-device edge computing and semiconductor inference platforms.
6. Robot makers, chip companies, developers and downstream model users.
7. Its models are integrated by robot makers into their humanoids and optimized by chip companies onto their processing platforms.
8. It achieves near-frontier reasoning performance at a fraction of training and inference cost, with small distilled variants that run efficiently on edge devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: UBTech, Unitree, Huawei, Qualcomm, SiMa.ai, Tencent, Tsinghua University, Peking University and Nanjing University.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Funded by equity investment, it makes money through inference APIs and strategic investments in robot makers.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023, it has raised tens of billions in equity funding and its models are deployed across global edge and robotics platforms.
Geography: Based in Hangzhou, China, with models deployed globally and banned on U.S. government devices over security concerns.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it develops large language models for general text, mathematical reasoning and software engineering tasks.

points.name: Sequoia
points.description: Venture capital firm funding embodied AI companies, robotics startups, and on-device inference hardware across the physical AI stack.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that funds companies across the edge and physical AI stack, from robot foundation models and inference semiconductors to deployed robotic systems, investing capital in robotics and physical AI startups.
1. A venture capital firm that provides funding to early and growth-stage companies developing physical AI, autonomy software, robotics, and inference semiconductors.
2. The firm sells capital and strategic support to robotics startups, robot makers, AI model developers, and silicon designers.
3. It acts as an institutional capital provider at the top of the physical AI value chain, funding the development of robot models, machine makers, and chip designers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and co-investors include Khosla Ventures and Alumni Ventures, and it has backed organizations including Physical Intelligence, Skild AI, and Etched.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: The firm makes money through fund management, generating returns on capital invested in robotics and AI startups.
Scale and maturity: An established, top-tier institutional investor, it has led or participated in funding rounds amounting to hundreds of millions of dollars, including individual rounds of $300 million and $400 million.
Geography: Based in the United States, it operates globally with an established presence in London and active investments across multiple continents.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the firm invests across diverse technology sectors including decentralized AI platforms, in-space mirrors, mathematical reasoning, and developer infrastructure.

points.name: 1789 Capital
points.description: Venture capital firm investing in AI infrastructure and frontier computing companies including chip makers and language model developers.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that funds late-stage companies across AI, defense technology, and advanced manufacturing, including makers of autonomous drones, brain-computer interfaces, and AI-enabled smart factories. It provides capital and government contracting access to national security-adjacent businesses rather than developing technologies directly. The firm targets institutional and high-net-worth investors seeking exposure to a politically aligned parallel economy of conservative businesses.
1. A venture capital firm that makes equity investments in private U.S. companies.
2. The firm provides equity capital through its fund vehicles.
3. The firm serves institutional and high-net-worth investors seeking exposure to AI, defense technology, and national security-adjacent companies.
4. It acts as an investor and portfolio company selector within the AI, robotics, and defense technology ecosystems rather than as a technology developer or systems integrator.
5. Its strategic positioning at the intersection of venture capital, financial markets, and U.S. defense policymaking provides portfolio companies with policy leverage and government contracting access.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable portfolio companies include autonomous defense drone makers, AI-enabled aerospace factory builders, quantum computing firms, large language model developers, and brain-computer interface companies.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: The firm makes money through fund management and equity investments in private companies.
Scale and maturity: An established late-stage investor with approximately $3 billion in capital under management, making typical investments ranging from $5 million to $50 million.
Geography: The firm is based in Palm Beach, Florida, USA and focuses on companies benefiting from U.S. defense innovation priorities.
Beyond physical AI: The firm's core investment thesis centers on conservative political values and patriotic capitalism, positioning itself as an anti-ESG investor building a parallel economy of conservative businesses.

points.name: Pentagon
points.description: US government agency funding and deploying autonomous weapons systems, drones, and edge AI for military defense applications.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds, procures, integrates and operates unmanned vehicles, drones, robots and autonomous systems for the U.S. military.
1. A government agency that procures and operates drones, unmanned vehicles and robots, and commissions autonomy software, as fielded defense programs.
2. Program management for autonomous weapon swarms, attritable unmanned systems and military AI governance.
3. Deployment of thousands of unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles, AI strike kits and humanoid robots across multiple warfighting domains.
4. Procurement contracts for hardware, autonomy software and strike kits, and approved vendor lists for government drone use.
5. Drones, unmanned ground vehicles, humanoid robots, weapon swarms and decision-support systems across land, air and sea military operations.
6. U.S. military services, allied defense forces and Ukrainian forces.
7. It buys unmanned systems, robots and software from defense contractors and operates them within its own military forces.
8. It holds regulatory and acquisition authority to set governance frameworks for autonomous weapons and approve defense platforms for operational use.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Foundation Future Industries, Auterion, NODA AI, Parrot, OpenAI and Anthropic.
Organization type: Government agency and military headquarters.
Business model: Government funding, procurement contracts and research programs.
Scale and maturity: A massive defense institution with billions in unmanned systems spending and initiatives to field tens of thousands of autonomous platforms.
Geography: Based in the United States, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: It manages the full spectrum of national defense and military operations beyond autonomous systems and physical AI.

points.name: Agility Robotics
points.description: US robotics company deploying bipedal humanoid robots for warehouse material-handling tasks.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that designs and builds a bipedal mobile manipulation robot for warehouse logistics and sells or leases it to logistics operators and manufacturers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells or leases complete bipedal humanoid robots for warehouse tasks.
2. Bipedal legged locomotion using series elastic actuators with springs and cable drives, integrated with depth vision sensors and proprietary AI models for task adaptability.
3. Bipedal locomotion in human-centric environments, tote manipulation, package handling, and fleet management via a cloud automation platform.
4. Complete humanoid robots and cloud-based fleet management software, offered through direct sales and a robots-as-a-service leasing model.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers, fulfillment centers, and automotive manufacturing plants.
6. Logistics operators, contract logistics providers, e-commerce companies, and automotive manufacturers.
7. It builds complete humanoid robots and operates them directly in customer facilities under robots-as-a-service agreements.
8. It uses a distinctive reverse-jointed bipedal design optimized specifically for reliable, high-volume tote handling in existing warehouse infrastructure rather than pursuing general-purpose humanoid flexibility.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and investors include Amazon, GXO Logistics, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, Schaeffler, DCVC, Playground Global, SoftBank, and NVIDIA.
Organization type: Privately held robotics company spun out of a university lab, pursuing a public listing via a SPAC merger.
Business model: Robot hardware sales, multi-year robots-as-a-service leasing contracts, and software platform integration.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, it has raised over $640 million, holds over $300 million in multiyear orders, and operates a dedicated manufacturing facility with a peak annual capacity of 10,000 units.
Geography: Headquartered in Oregon with offices in Pittsburgh and Palo Alto, it deploys robots across customer facilities in North America and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Sanctuary AI
points.description: Canadian humanoid robotics company building general-purpose physical AI robots for industrial automation.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that builds general-purpose humanoid robots and proprietary cognitive AI control software, targeting industrial labor.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete humanoid robots with integrated AI control software.
2. Humanoid robots with wheeled bases and hydraulically actuated dexterous hands, controlled by an AI system that combines large language models, reinforcement learning and symbolic reasoning.
3. General-purpose dexterous manipulation, fine motor control and physical task execution with rapid task learning from teleoperation and simulation.
4. Complete humanoid robots.
5. Automotive factories, manufacturing, logistics, healthcare and retail.
6. Automotive suppliers, manufacturers and industrial enterprises.
7. Its complete humanoid robots are deployed directly into the facilities of industrial operators.
8. An AI-first approach uses a cognitive architecture designed to transfer task knowledge across diverse physical configurations and multi-embodiment hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Magna International, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Amazon, Bell Canada and the Government of Canada.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales and strategic deployment partnerships.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018 with over C$140 million in funding, running commercial pilots.
Geography: Based in Vancouver, Canada, with a subsidiary in China.
Beyond physical AI: The development of physical AI and general-purpose humanoid robots is its sole focus.

points.name: World Labs
points.description: US research organization developing spatial intelligence models that perceive and interact with 3D environments for physical automation.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose Large World Models generate persistent, editable, physics-aware 3D environments for robotics developers and embodied AI researchers.
1. An AI model developer that builds and licenses generative world models and spatial intelligence models via APIs and software products.
2. Multimodal generative world models and 3D Gaussian splatting systems trained to reconstruct, generate, and simulate physical environments including geometry, lighting, and spatial layout.
3. 3D environment generation, spatial reasoning, physics-aware simulation, real-time video generation, and synthetic training data production.
4. Cloud APIs, licensed foundational models, and open-source rendering software.
5. Robotics simulation, autonomous system training, and synthetic data pipelines.
6. Robotics developers, simulation library builders, and embodied AI model developers.
7. Its models and APIs are integrated by robotics developers into simulation platforms and synthetic data generation pipelines.
8. It focuses on frontier-grade generative world models that enable real-to-sim-to-real training workflows by creating photorealistic environments from text and image prompts.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA provides Isaac Sim infrastructure and investment, Autodesk is a major investor, and Black Gibbon and Antioch integrate its models.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, API subscriptions, and foundational model access.
Scale and maturity: Achieved unicorn status in its first four months, having raised approximately $1.23 billion with a roughly $5 billion valuation.
Geography: Based in San Francisco with an office in New York, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Advancing spatial intelligence and building multimodal generative world models is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: FieldAI
points.description: US robotics software startup building edge AI models that let robots navigate and work independently in unmapped, GPS-denied environments without cloud connectivity.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer whose Field Foundation Models give robots an embodiment-agnostic autonomy brain for navigating unstructured, GPS-denied environments. The company builds models for perception, world prediction, motion feasibility, and multi-robot coordination that run as an on-device software stack on other companies' hardware. It targets industrial customers needing safe, continuous operation of diverse robots without prior maps or cloud connectivity.
1. An AI model developer that builds robot foundation models and licenses them as an autonomy stack running on other companies' robots.
2. Field foundation models combining data-driven AI with physics-based reasoning and uncertainty awareness, including a Belief World Model, a Dynamics Foundation Model, and a Multiagent Foundation Model.
3. Autonomous navigation, localization, and task completion in dynamic environments without maps, GPS, or pre-planned routes, plus real-time risk-aware decision-making and fleet coordination at the edge.
4. Licensed software autonomy stacks and on-device runtime packages deployed directly onto customers' existing robot hardware.
5. Quadrupeds, humanoids, wheeled robots, and passenger-scale vehicles operating at construction sites, mines, energy plants, logistics facilities, and federal installations.
6. Construction firms, data center operators, defense companies, and industrial operators.
7. Its models and software stacks are integrated onto robots built by hardware makers for deployment in industrial settings.
8. Hardware-agnostic models validated in DARPA challenges that fuse physics-based reasoning with uncertainty quantification for safe off-road and subterranean autonomy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Built on NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Isaac simulation frameworks, integrates with Microsoft Azure for synthetic data, pairs its software with Boston Dynamics' Spot robot, and is backed by Khosla Ventures, Bezos Expeditions, Intel Capital, Samsung Ventures, NVentures, Temasek, and Hyundai Motor Group.
Organization type: A privately held startup spun out of DARPA-funded research at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Business model: Software licenses and autonomy stack deployments to industrial customers.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2023 with roughly 180 employees by 2026, valued at $2 billion after raising $405 million, with commercial deployments across hundreds of sites on three continents.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating deployments across North America, Europe, and other continents.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and physical autonomy for industrial robotics represent the entire focus of its business model and technical roadmap.

points.name: Generalist AI
points.description: US robotics startup developing foundational AI models that power robot hands for diverse physical tasks.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds hardware-agnostic robot foundation models for dexterous physical manipulation, operating a global data collection network to amass hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world robotic activity for model training. The company develops embodied foundation models designed to run across different robots and environments, from factories and laboratories to homes and space, enabling machines to understand and act in the physical world.
1. An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on other companies' robots.
2. Vision-language-action models trained on hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world robotic activity collected via hand-mimicking gripper devices, featuring cross-embodiment compatibility with 6DoF, 7DoF, and 16+DoF robots.
3. Dexterous manipulation, cross-embodiment control, few-shot learning from short video demonstrations, and simultaneous thinking and acting.
4. Models running on customers' hardware.
5. Factories, warehouses, laboratories, restaurants, farms, homes, and space applications.
6. Robot makers and integrators.
7. Its models are integrated by robot makers into their robots.
8. A single foundational model trained on massive real-world data capable of fast, reliable performance across a broad range of end effectors and robotic hands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Universal Robots, 8VC, Radical Ventures, Union Square Ventures, Bezos Expeditions.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2024, having raised $553 million in total equity funding at a $3 billion valuation.
Geography: Based in San Mateo, California, USA, with a global data collection network.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Nuro
points.description: US autonomous delivery startup developing Level 4 self-driving software and zero-occupant vehicles for goods transportation.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vehicle company that builds purpose-built electric delivery vehicles and licenses a Level 4 self-driving stack to automakers and mobility platforms for robotaxi and last-mile goods delivery.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that builds autonomous delivery vehicles and an autonomy software developer that licenses its self-driving stack to automakers.
2. A sensor-fusion autonomy software stack combining cameras, radar and lidar running on Arm-based compute subsystems and autonomous drive chips for Level 4 driving.
3. Autonomous navigation, urban driving, lane changes, merging, parking and last-mile goods delivery.
4. Complete autonomous delivery vehicles and licensed Level 4 autonomy software integrated on automotive OEM production lines.
5. Robotaxis, last-mile delivery vehicles, grocery and parcel delivery, ride-hailing fleets.
6. Automakers, mobility platforms, ride-hailing networks, logistics operators, grocery chains and quick-service restaurants.
7. Its autonomy stack is integrated by automakers into their production vehicles and its delivery robots carry goods for retail and logistics partners.
8. It builds zero-occupant electric delivery vehicles for goods transport while licensing its universal autonomy platform to automakers for passenger robotaxis.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Uber, Lucid, NVIDIA, Arm, SoftBank, Woven Capital, Kroger, Walmart, Domino's, 7-Eleven, FedEx and CVS.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Vehicle hardware sales, licensed software and autonomous delivery services.
Scale and maturity: A late-stage company with over $5 billion valuation, $2.3 billion raised and over 1.4 million autonomous miles driven.
Geography: Based in Mountain View, California with operational deployments in Texas, Arizona and California.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play physical AI and autonomous vehicle company focused entirely on self-driving technology.

points.name: Dexterity
points.description: Bay Area robotics startup deploying dual-arm mobile robots for warehouse parcel handling and logistics automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds full-stack physical AI robotic systems, including dual-arm mobile manipulators and AI software platforms, for warehouse, logistics, and supply chain automation.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete dual-arm mobile manipulator robots and licensed AI software stacks for logistics automation.
2. Physics-informed AI world models, machine vision, force sensing, and real-time AI decision-making integrated into mobile robotic hardware platforms.
3. Mixed-SKU picking, truck loading and unloading, palletizing, depalletizing, sorting, dexterous manipulation, and autonomous mobile manipulation in unpredictable environments.
4. Complete robots and robotic systems, alongside SaaS-based robotic intelligence platforms and AI software licensed to logistics operators.
5. Warehouses, logistics facilities, parcel handling operations, truck loading bays, and supply chain distribution centers.
6. Logistics operators, third-party logistics companies, parcel delivery services, manufacturers, and supply chain operators.
7. Its robots and AI platforms are deployed directly in customer warehouses and integrated into broader automation solutions by systems integrators.
8. It builds a full-stack physical AI platform combining proprietary hardware like the Mech superhumanoid with the Foresight world model trained on millions of autonomous production actions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA Inception, FedEx, Sagawa Express, GXO Logistics, HIWIN Technologies, Kawasaki Robotics, Sumitomo Corporation, Dematic, Sanmina, and Obvious Ventures.
Organization type: A privately held venture-backed startup and U.S.-based unicorn company.
Business model: Robot and hardware sales, SaaS-based software platform licenses, and joint venture distribution agreements.
Scale and maturity: A commercial-stage unicorn company founded in 2017 with a $1.65 billion valuation and deployed systems across North America, Asia, and Europe.
Geography: Based in Redwood City, California, operating and deploying robotic systems in the United States, Japan, and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire commercial focus and operation is the design, development, and deployment of physical AI and robotic systems for logistics automation.

points.name: Bright Machines
points.description: Software company deploying modular robotic assembly lines for automated electronics manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator and original equipment manufacturer that designs and installs modular robotic assembly lines, combining robotic hardware, edge computing, computer vision, and proprietary software to automate electronics manufacturing for OEMs and electronics manufacturing services.
1. A systems integrator and machine builder that designs and installs modular robotic assembly lines and the proprietary software that runs them for electronics manufacturers.
2. Software-defined manufacturing platforms combining machine learning, computer vision, edge computing, and adaptive robotics into modular production lines with accompanying AI simulation tools for design optimization.
3. Flexible electronics assembly, automated component insertion, computer-vision-guided part handling, production data analytics, and manufacturing process optimization.
4. Complete physical production lines installed on the factory floor, delivered alongside licensed software platforms and simulation design tools.
5. Electronics manufacturing facilities, data center server assembly lines, and automotive electronics factories.
6. Original equipment manufacturers, electronics manufacturing services providers, original design manufacturers, and hyperscalers.
7. It builds and installs complete robotic production lines on the factory floors of electronics manufacturers, integrating third-party and proprietary robotics with its own software.
8. It replaces hard-wired, labor-intensive automation with intelligent, adaptable, software-defined systems that substantially increase units produced per hour and reduce defects.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Eclipse Ventures and BlackRank are investors, while it partners with Nvidia and Microsoft.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Capital equipment sales of physical microfactories, software platform licenses, and systems integration services.
Scale and maturity: A well-established, late-stage company with over $648 million in total funding through a Series C round, serving over 60 global manufacturing customers with deployments across more than 10 countries.
Geography: Based in San Francisco, California, USA, with R&D and field operation centers in Tel Aviv and Guadalajara, and a global deployment footprint.
Beyond physical AI: Factory automation, industrial robotics, and intelligent manufacturing constitute its entire commercial focus and business model.

points.name: Standard Bots
points.description: US robotics startup building AI-native robotic arms for manufacturing automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and manufactures AI-native six-axis robotic arms and industrial humanoids for factory automation, selling complete machines to manufacturers and defense contractors.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells six-axis collaborative robotic arms and industrial humanoids.
2. Six-axis robotic manipulators with integrated machine vision and collision detection, trained through learning-from-demonstration using transformer neural networks and GPU physics simulation.
3. Dexterous manipulation, machining, welding, palletizing, grinding, fastening, dispensing, assembly, inspection, and collision detection.
4. Complete robots sold as hardware, including proprietary software, firmware, electronics, vision systems, and mechanical parts.
5. Factories, machine shops, industrial manufacturing, machining, and defense manufacturing operations.
6. Fortune 500 manufacturers, independent machine shops, defense contractors, government agencies, and logistics operators.
7. Its complete robots are deployed directly by manufacturers and government agencies in their own facilities.
8. Programming by worker demonstration instead of hand-coded movements allows non-specialist workers to deploy and reprogram the robots.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates NVIDIA Isaac Sim for simulation and training, and is backed by investors including RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Andreessen Horowitz, Sequoia Capital, Thrive Capital, and the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic arms.
Scale and maturity: A unicorn company valued at $1 billion that raised $200 million in Series C funding and is expanding its manufacturing facility to 70,000 square feet.
Geography: Based in Glen Cove, New York, with manufacturing and sales operations entirely within the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Designing and assembling collaborative robotic arms for factory tasks constitutes the organization's entire business focus.

points.name: Pickle Robot
points.description: Robotics startup deploying AI-powered mobile manipulators to automate warehouse truck unloading.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile manipulator robots for trailer unloading and package handling in logistics, selling complete physical AI systems to large supply-chain operations.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells autonomous mobile robots and manipulation systems for warehouse automation.
2. Robotic arms integrated with mobile platforms, sensors and an autonomy engine that handles package variability and unpredictable layouts.
3. Autonomous truck unloading, grasping, piece handling, sorting, labeling and packing in existing warehouse environments.
4. Complete robotic systems deployed directly into warehouse operations.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers and supply-chain logistics.
6. Large logistics operators and package delivery firms.
7. It builds and deploys complete robots that integrate into existing warehouse infrastructure and connect downstream to other automation systems.
8. It engineers robots that deploy in existing warehouse infrastructure without facility redesign.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It has integrated with a pallet-building system maker, a package delivery company and a process-intelligence platform.
Organization type: A privately held startup founded in 2018.
Business model: Hardware and system sales, including a large purchase agreement.
Scale and maturity: It has raised approximately $97 million in funding and secured a $120 million purchase agreement.
Geography: It is based in Boston and deploys systems within the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and robotics for warehouse automation represent its entire business focus.

points.name: ANYbotics
points.description: US-based robotics company deploying autonomous legged robots for industrial inspection.
