A robot maker that builds and sells rugged autonomous quadruped robots for industrial inspection in harsh and hazardous environments.
1. A robot maker that builds complete quadruped robots and proprietary actuator modules for industrial inspection.
2. Autonomous legged robots powered by proprietary series elastic actuators and on-device inference software for autonomous navigation and AI-powered anomaly detection.
3. Legged locomotion over rough terrain and stairs, autonomous navigation, industrial inspection, and anomaly detection.
4. Complete deployed robots, fleet management software, and integration services.
5. Industrial inspection in energy, oil and gas, mining, metals, chemicals, offshore platforms, and other hazardous facilities.
6. Energy producers, oil and gas operators, metals processors, mining operators, and industrial facilities.
7. Its robots are deployed as turnkey autonomous inspection solutions by industrial operators.
8. Proprietary series elastic actuator technology and rugged IP67 and ATEX-certified quadruped designs provide superior terrain navigation and hazardous-environment operation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ETH Zurich, SAP, Yokogawa, RealSense, Cognite, AWS, NVIDIA, Siemens Energy, SLB, Equans, Bessemer Venture Partners, Qualcomm Ventures, TDK Ventures, NGP Capital, Walden Catalyst, Swisscom Ventures, Aker BP, BP, Equinor, and Petrobras.
Organization type: Privately held robotics company and university spin-off.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and actuators, software for fleet management, and integration services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016, with over 200 robots shipped and large orders from major energy and industrial companies.
Geography: Based in Zurich, Switzerland, with an office in San Francisco and international deployments.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI are the company's entire focus.

points.name: Ghost Robotics
points.description: US robotics company building autonomous quadruped robots with on-device AI for real-time navigation and perception.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells rugged quadrupedal unmanned ground vehicles and a command interface for defense, security, and industrial customers.
1. A robot maker that builds quadruped robots and an accompanying control platform for defense and industrial applications.
2. Autonomous legged robots with proprietary blind-mode control for locomotion using proprioceptive feedback, modular architectures for sensor integration, and web-based command software.
3. Autonomous navigation, perimeter patrol, reconnaissance, unstructured terrain mobility, sensor deployment, and mission execution.
4. Complete robots, sensors, and components, along with a web-based command interface.
5. Defense bases, military reconnaissance, data centers, construction sites, and perimeter security.
6. Militaries, government agencies, security forces, and industrial enterprises.
7. It sells complete robots directly to defense and industrial customers for autonomous deployment.
8. It uses a proprietary blind-mode control architecture that enables robots to maintain mobility through proprioceptive feedback when visual sensors fail.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company has integrated armed systems with a weapon manufacturer and a remote weapon system maker, and was acquired by a defense company.
Organization type: Privately held company that is a subsidiary of a defense firm.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and payloads.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, it was acquired for a majority stake at a $400 million valuation and has deployed robots with multiple branches of the U.S. military.
Geography: Based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA, with primary operations in U.S. defense markets and deployments with allied militaries.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play robotics and physical AI company.

points.name: Hugging Face
points.description: US AI platform hosting open-source models and datasets for physical robotics and on-device inference.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that hosts models, datasets, and software frameworks for machine learning and robotics engineers, and has expanded into building open-source humanoid robots and robot arms. It provides the infrastructure for sharing open-weight models and collaborative robotics datasets, and develops the LeRobot open-source framework for training vision-language-action models on physical robots.
1. A developer tools company whose model hub, datasets, and robotics frameworks machine learning engineers use, and a robot maker that builds and sells open-source humanoid robots and robotic arms.
2. Open-source Transformer libraries, vision-language-action models trained on community teleoperation datasets, and 3D-printed humanoid robot hardware with actuated degrees of freedom.
3. Model hosting and distribution, dataset sharing, fine-tuning and on-device inference optimization, teleoperation, bipedal locomotion, and dexterous manipulation.
4. Cloud APIs, open-source software libraries, hosted datasets, and complete open-source robots.
5. Humanoids, desktop robotic arms, edge devices, and machine learning research.
6. Machine learning developers, robotics researchers, and open-source hardware communities.
7. Its software libraries and models are used by developers to build and optimize their own robots and edge AI applications, and its own robots are sold directly to the open-source community.
8. It leverages a massive open-source community and permissive licensing to standardize and distribute open-weight models and robotics datasets at scale.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, AWS, AMD Ventures, Lux Capital, and acquired Pollen Robotics.
Organization type: Privately held technology company currently under acquisition by a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Cloud inference endpoints, enterprise subscriptions, and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Hosts over 500,000 models, serves over 5 million users, and is being acquired for $12.9 billion.
Geography: Based in New York, New York, USA, and operates globally as a digital platform.
Beyond physical AI: It is the central hub for hosting machine learning models, datasets, and applications across the entire AI landscape, including natural language processing, code generation, and biology.

points.name: Proception
points.description: Robotics startup building dexterous robotic hands and data-capture gloves for training humanoid manipulation systems.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that builds high-dexterity robotic hands and data-collection gloves for humanoid robots and general-purpose manipulation, selling to robotics companies and research institutions.
1. A component supplier that makes dexterous robotic hands and sensor-laden data gloves sold as hardware to robot developers.
2. Multi-jointed robotic hands with 22 degrees of freedom and sensor-packed wearable gloves that capture human hand interaction data for training.
3. Human-level dexterity, contact-rich manipulation and teleoperation data capture for robotic systems.
4. Components sold as hardware modules to robotics developers.
5. Humanoids and general-purpose robotic manipulation.
6. Robotics companies and research institutions.
7. Its hand hardware and data gloves are integrated into robots built by other developers.
8. It combines human-like kinematic hardware with wearable sensors to overcome training data scarcity for contact-rich manipulation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by First Round Capital, Y Combinator and BoxGroup, and uses Autodesk Fusion for design and simulation.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic hands and data gloves.
Scale and maturity: A seed-stage company that has raised $11 million and begun shipping initial batches.
Geography: Based in Mountain View, California.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is the entire focus of the pure-play organization.

points.name: Zipline
points.description: Drone delivery company operating autonomous aircraft fleets for medical supplies and consumer goods across multiple countries.
points.bullets:
A drone maker and operator that builds autonomous delivery drones and runs a last-mile aerial logistics network, transporting medical supplies, food and retail goods to end customers.
1. A drone maker that builds and operates autonomous delivery drones, sold and delivered as a delivery service.
2. Fixed-wing and hybrid VTOL drones that use NVIDIA Jetson edge AI modules for onboard sensor fusion, autonomous navigation, detection and avoidance, and tethered precision delivery.
3. Autonomous flight, real-time routing, obstacle avoidance, precision package placement via a tethered droid, and fleet operation without cloud dependency.
4. A delivery service it operates itself using its own proprietary drones and charging infrastructure.
5. Drones used in medical delivery, retail, restaurants, groceries and last-mile logistics.
6. Healthcare systems, hospitals, retailers, restaurant chains, e-commerce platforms and governments.
7. It designs, manufactures and operates its own drones to run a delivery service for end customers.
8. It combines proprietary fixed-wing and tethered-droid hardware with an edge AI-first architecture to run fully autonomous delivery operations at nationwide scale without cloud dependency.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Walmart, Sweetgreen, Uber, Cleveland Clinic, Michigan Medicine and the government of Rwanda, running on the NVIDIA Jetson platform with Fidelity as an investor.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Delivery and logistics fees from operating an autonomous drone delivery service.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, it has raised over $2 billion across eight funding rounds, surpassed two million commercial deliveries and flies over 100 million commercial miles across seven countries.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates across seven countries including the US, Rwanda and Ghana.
Beyond physical AI: Autonomous drone delivery is its entire focus.

points.name: RIVR
points.description: Swiss robotics startup building wheeled-legged robots for autonomous last-mile delivery.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous wheeled-legged robots and a full autonomy stack for last-mile delivery. The company designs the complete hardware and software platform, including on-device AI runtimes and continuously learning behavioral models, to automate doorstep parcel and food delivery.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds fully integrated wheeled-legged autonomous delivery robots.
2. Wheeled-legged locomotion mechanisms controlled by neural networks trained through reinforcement learning and large-scale simulation.
3. High-speed driving on flat surfaces, walking locomotion for stair climbing and uneven terrain navigation, and autonomous doorstep delivery.
4. Complete autonomous robots deployed directly into commercial logistics operations.
5. Last-mile parcel and food delivery in urban environments.
6. E-commerce and food delivery companies seeking autonomous logistics solutions.
7. Its complete robotic platforms are deployed directly into commercial delivery operations by logistics providers.
8. Its robots combine high-speed wheeled locomotion with legged walking to actively navigate stairs, curbs, and uneven terrain.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Spun out of ETH Zurich and acquired by Amazon, which previously invested through its Industrial Innovation Fund, with earlier backing from Bezos Expeditions and Linear Capital.
Organization type: A startup spin-out that operated as a privately held company before being acquired.
Business model: Hardware systems deployment and delivery services through commercial logistics pilots and partnerships.
Scale and maturity: Founded in April 2023, raised a $22 million seed round, completed commercial pilots, and was acquired in March 2026.
Geography: Based in Zurich, Switzerland, with commercial delivery pilots conducted in Austin, Texas, and Zurich.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and autonomous delivery robotics constitute the organization's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Moog Inc.
points.description: US motion control manufacturer providing motors and slip rings that convert AI decisions into precise robotic movements.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that builds high-precision electromechanical actuators, frameless torque motors, slip rings, and motion-control hardware for robot makers and aerospace integrators.
1. A component supplier that makes robot actuators, motors, and slip rings, sold as components and subsystems.
2. Electromechanical and hydraulic actuation systems, fractional-horsepower brushless DC motors, and slip rings for power and data transmission across continuous rotational joints.
3. High-torque actuation, high power density, precise motion control, and low-noise operation for dynamic physical movement.
4. Components, motors, and integrated actuator assemblies sold to device manufacturers.
5. Humanoid platforms, medical robotics, laboratory automation, industrial machinery, and aerospace defense systems.
6. Robot OEMs, systems integrators, aerospace manufacturers, and industrial machinery builders.
7. Its actuators and motors are designed into robots and vehicles by device makers.
8. It combines electric, hydraulic, and hybrid actuation technologies derived from aerospace motion-control expertise to deliver high power density and precision.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with Near Earth Autonomy on the MARV-EL program and the RUC-60 Black Hawk conversion, integrating autonomy software into its Genesys Avionics Suite.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of components, motors, and actuator subsystems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1951 with 13,500 employees and extensive global manufacturing infrastructure.
Geography: Based in the United States with global operations.
Beyond physical AI: It is a diversified industrial corporation with historical roots in aerospace and defense motion control.

points.name: Bosch Sensortec
points.description: German sensor manufacturer integrating machine learning directly into microelectromechanical systems for intelligent on-device detection.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that builds MEMS sensors and smart sensor hubs with embedded AI for consumer electronics, wearables, robotics, drones, and IoT applications. It designs and manufactures compact inertial, environmental, and motion sensors with integrated microcontrollers and embedded machine learning algorithms for on-device inference. The company supplies these AI-enabled sensor components to device makers, enabling intelligent perception and continuous monitoring without cloud connectivity.
1. A sensor maker that builds MEMS sensors and smart sensor hubs with integrated AI for on-device inference, sold as hardware components.
2. Micro-electromechanical systems sensors, including accelerometers, gyroscopes, magnetometers, inertial measurement units, and environmental sensors, with integrated microcontrollers running custom movement classification and activity recognition algorithms.
3. On-device inference, motion detection, gesture recognition, indoor navigation, optical image stabilization, voice activity detection, full-body motion tracking, and environmental sensing.
4. Sensors and smart sensor modules sold as hardware components to device manufacturers.
5. Smartphones, wearables, AR/VR headsets, drones, robots, smart home devices, and industrial IoT systems.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, wearable device makers, robotics companies, industrial IoT providers, smart home developers, and drone manufacturers.
7. Its sensors are designed into consumer electronics, wearables, robots, and IoT devices by device makers.
8. It embeds always-on, ultra-low-power edge AI inference directly within compact MEMS sensor packages, enabling continuous monitoring without battery drain.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with third-party tools and platforms, including Qeexo AutoML, and operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH.
Organization type: A wholly owned subsidiary of Robert Bosch GmbH.
Business model: Hardware sales of sensor components and modules.
Scale and maturity: It has shipped over 1 billion MEMS sensors with integrated microcontrollers and software as of 2024, targeting more than 10 billion units sold by 2030.
Geography: It is based in Germany and operates globally, including in India, the United States, China, and Israel.
Beyond physical AI: It is a specialized sensor and embedded AI component manufacturer within the broader Robert Bosch conglomerate, which operates across automotive, industrial, consumer goods, and energy sectors.

points.name: Micron Technology
points.description: US semiconductor company manufacturing memory and storage chips that power on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that supplies industrial-grade memory and storage components for edge AI and physical automation. It manufactures DRAM, NAND flash storage, multichip packages, and specialty memory for neuromorphic computing, providing the memory substrates upon which robotics controllers and autonomous platforms execute their workloads. The organization serves original equipment manufacturers and systems integrators across the industrial automation, automotive, robotics, and drone sectors.
1. A semiconductor company that designs and sells memory chips and solid-state storage for edge computing, automotive, and robotics applications.
2. High-speed DRAM, high-bandwidth memory, NAND flash storage, multichip packages, and resistive RAM and phase-change memory for neuromorphic systems.
3. Low-power, high-bandwidth memory and durable storage for on-device AI inference, real-time decision-making, and AI-enhanced video recording and analytics in constrained edge environments.
4. Chips, multichip packages, and flash storage modules sold to device makers and systems integrators.
5. Drones, automotive cluster applications, industrial automation, robotics, and connected vehicles.
6. Original equipment manufacturers, systems integrators, automotive makers, and semiconductor companies.
7. Its chips and storage modules are designed into embedded systems and autonomous platforms by device manufacturers.
8. A broad portfolio of memory and storage products specifically optimized to minimize power consumption and latency in constrained edge environments, combined with high-bandwidth memory manufacturing scale.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with an embedded processing company on high-bandwidth memory compute architecture for AI accelerators, partners with a microcontroller supplier on automotive cluster platforms, and is a strategic investor in an edge AI chip startup.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor manufacturer.
Business model: Semiconductor and storage component sales.
Scale and maturity: A large, established global entity and one of only three worldwide manufacturers of high-bandwidth memory.
Geography: Headquartered in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is on the design and manufacture of advanced memory and storage technologies.

points.name: 42dot
points.description: South Korean autonomous driving software developer building camera-based perception and Level 4 self-driving systems for vehicles and delivery robots.
points.bullets:
An autonomous driving and mobility platform company that develops Level 4 self-driving software stacks and operates urban autonomous transportation systems for passenger vehicles and logistics applications.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack to automakers and operates an autonomous transportation platform for self-driving vehicles manufactured by other companies.
2. Camera-only perception algorithms without reliance on high-definition maps, sensor-fusion autonomy software, machine learning training platforms, and secure cloud-edge communication architectures.
3. Autonomous navigation, camera-centric 3D perception, fleet orchestration, dataset management, autonomous delivery, and drone flight.
4. Licensed software, an autonomous transportation platform it operates, data software development kits, and large-scale annotated driving datasets.
5. Robotaxis, autonomous delivery robots, drones, passenger vehicles, smart logistics, and urban transportation systems.
6. Automakers, urban transportation operators, and logistics companies.
7. Its autonomy software is integrated into self-driving vehicles manufactured by automakers, and it operates the fleet platform that manages those vehicles.
8. A camera-centric perception approach that eliminates external mapping dependencies, combined with vertical integration across the full software stack from perception through fleet management.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Hyundai Motor Group and Seoul City.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary operating as the global software center of a major automotive conglomerate.
Business model: Software licenses, platform operation contracts, and government transportation operator agreements.
Scale and maturity: Operating at scale within a major automotive conglomerate with an established commercial deployment as a city's certified autonomous transportation system.
Geography: Based in South Korea and operating Seoul's multi-manufacturer autonomous vehicle platform.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is the core vehicle software development entity for a major automotive conglomerate and the primary developer of its production autonomous vehicles.

points.name: Toyota Motor Corporation
points.description: Japanese automotive manufacturer building driver assistance systems, autonomous vehicles, and factory automation powered by edge AI.
points.bullets:
An automotive manufacturer and mobility conglomerate that builds vehicles, service robots and factory automation systems, and operates an internal research division developing robotics foundation models and driver-assistance software.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that builds passenger cars and assistive service robots, and develops autonomy software and robot foundation models for its own machines.
2. Robotic manipulator arms with teleoperation interfaces, open robotics foundation models trained for basic object manipulation, and driver-assistance software for automated highway driving.
3. Human support and elderly care assistance, remote teleoperation of robotic arms, autonomous driving assistance, and synthetic factory automation for metal forging.
4. Complete passenger vehicles and service robots, licensed driver-assistance software stacks, open-source robot foundation models, and automated production lines.
5. Passenger vehicles, factory production lines, home and elderly care settings, and robotic research platforms.
6. Consumers, manufacturing operations, academic research communities, and automotive fleet operators.
7. It designs and builds complete robots and vehicles for end users, manufactures its own automated production lines, and licenses its autonomous driving software to its own automotive brand.
8. It pursues an assistive autonomy philosophy centered on human-machine collaboration and safety rather than fully replacing human drivers or operators.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with an autonomous driving software developer, an eVTOL aircraft maker, an autonomous shuttle operator, and an industrial simulation platform company, and its venture capital arm invests in robotics startups.
Organization type: A publicly traded multinational conglomerate.
Business model: Vehicle and robot hardware sales, automotive software licensing, and venture capital fund management.
Scale and maturity: A large, established global manufacturer with subsidiaries conducting advanced robotics and artificial intelligence research.
Geography: It is based in Japan and operates manufacturing, research and development facilities globally.
Beyond physical AI: It is a diversified global automotive and manufacturing conglomerate whose operations span vehicles, robotics, energy systems and industrial equipment.

points.name: Volkswagen
points.description: German automaker deploying autonomous electric vehicles for commercial robotaxi services.
points.bullets:
An automaker that designs and manufactures passenger and commercial vehicles and integrates third-party physical AI, autonomy software, sensors and robots into its platforms and production operations. It builds electric minivans configured for robotaxi service, embeds ADAS and automated parking systems in its cars, and deploys computer-vision-guided robots and autonomous yard trucks in its factories and logistics. It acts as a customer and integrator of edge and physical AI components built by others, and as an operator of robotaxi fleets, rather than developing foundational AI itself.
1. An automaker that builds and sells passenger cars, commercial vehicles and electric minivans, and integrates third-party autonomy software, sensors and robots into its vehicles and factories.
2. Embedded advanced driver assistance and automated parking systems using surround sensors, data distribution service middleware, sensor fusion, HD mapping, virtual ECU validation in the cloud, and computer vision-aided industrial robots.
3. SAE Level 2 and Level 3 driving automation, autonomous valet parking, robotaxi mobility, autonomous yard truck logistics, and precision assembly automation.
4. Complete vehicles with embedded ADAS, autonomous electric minivans operated for robotaxi service, and integrated third-party robots and autonomous trucks installed in its own production operations.
5. Robotaxis, passenger cars, commercial vehicles, autonomous valet parking, factories and logistics.
6. Consumers for vehicles, ride-hailing passengers for robotaxi service and its own manufacturing operations for industrial automation.
7. It buys sensors, autonomy software, chips and robots from suppliers and integrates them into vehicles it builds and production facilities it operates.
8. It leverages partnerships with ride-hailing platforms and autonomous driving software developers to deploy electric minivans for commercial robotaxi service rather than building the autonomy stack itself.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Mobileye, Aurora, Bosch, Uber, FERNRIDE, Inbolt, XPENG, Amazon Web Services, CATL and Standard Robots.
Organization type: Publicly traded automotive manufacturer.
Business model: Vehicle sales, ride-hailing service fees through partnerships and manufacturing operational efficiencies from integrated automation.
Scale and maturity: A global enterprise that has committed multi-billion-dollar investments to autonomous driving initiatives through joint ventures.
Geography: Based in Germany, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization mass manufactures and sells passenger and commercial vehicles worldwide.

points.name: Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America
points.description: US automotive manufacturing facility deploying humanoid robots and assembling autonomous vehicles for commercial robotaxi services.
points.bullets:
A vehicle manufacturing facility and systems integrator that assembles electric vehicles configured for autonomous operation and deploys humanoid and quadruped robots for internal factory automation, acting as the inaugural deployment site for humanoid robots in factory settings.
1. An operator that runs manufacturing automation and deploys robots in its own factory, and an automaker that builds electric vehicles for autonomous ride-hailing companies.
2. Highly connected, automated, and flexible manufacturing systems integrating autonomous mobile robots, quadruped inspection robots, and planned humanoid automation for industrial sequencing tasks.
3. Electric vehicle and battery manufacturing, exterior quality inspection using quadruped robots, and planned autonomous execution of factory sequencing and manipulation tasks by humanoid robots.
4. Complete electric vehicles assembled for autonomous fleet operators, and internally operated robotic systems deployed directly on the factory floor for manufacturing automation.
5. Automotive factories, electric vehicle production lines, weld shops, and battery manufacturing facilities.
6. Autonomous ride-hailing operators that purchase its assembled vehicles, and the manufacturing facility itself which operates the deployed robots internally.
7. It buys robots from OEMs and runs them in its own factory, while assembling complete electric vehicles for autonomous fleet operators to deploy.
8. A manufacturing-scale strategy that generates operational data flywheel advantages across autonomous vehicles, humanoid robotics, and factory automation while maintaining vertical integration of hardware production.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Waymo, Motional, Boston Dynamics, LG Energy Solution, and the Savannah College of Art and Design.
Organization type: A manufacturing facility and strategic division within a publicly traded multinational automotive conglomerate.
Business model: Vehicle and battery manufacturing sales, and internally funded factory automation for operational cost reduction.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale, recently established manufacturing operation planning to reach 8,500 jobs by 2031 with production targets including 30,000 humanoid units annually by 2028.
Geography: Based in Bryan County, Georgia, USA, operating as part of a South Korean multinational corporation's U.S. expansion strategy.
Beyond physical AI: The broader parent company business encompasses vehicle production, autonomous driving partnerships, robotics development, hydrogen fuel-cell trucks, and factory automation.

points.name: Richard King Mellon Foundation
points.description: Pittsburgh-based philanthropic foundation funding robotics research facilities and physical AI commercialization infrastructure.
points.bullets:
A philanthropic foundation that funds physical AI and robotics infrastructure, providing large capital grants to build research facilities and testbeds for universities rather than developing commercial products itself.
1. A philanthropic foundation that makes capital grants for robotics research centers and testing facilities.
2. Large-scale philanthropic capital deployed to build university research centers and advanced manufacturing testbeds.
3. It finances the physical spaces and testing facilities necessary for developing embodied AI, sensors, and mobile manipulation technologies.
4. Capital grants and gifts awarded to academic institutions and research centers.
5. University robotics research centers, advanced manufacturing facilities, and urban robotics innovation parks.
6. Academic institutions, university research centers, and regional economic development entities.
7. Its grants fund the research facilities where universities and other organizations develop physical automation technologies.
8. A collaborative anchor-investment strategy that connects advanced robotics research parks with surrounding communities and regional economic revitalization initiatives.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Carnegie Mellon University, the University of Pittsburgh, Hellbender, and the Almono Limited Partnership.
Organization type: A privately held philanthropic foundation.
Business model: Philanthropic grantmaking through endowment payouts.
Scale and maturity: A well-established, major foundation capable of making anchor investments, exemplified by a $150 million grant to fund a university robotics facility.
Geography: Based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with investments concentrated on establishing the surrounding region as a global hub for robotics.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond its physical automation grants, the organization is a broad philanthropic entity dedicated to regional economic development, life sciences advancement, and community revitalization.

points.name: Carnegie Mellon University
points.description: US research university developing autonomous systems, robotics, and edge AI through world-class testing facilities and interdisciplinary collaboration.
points.bullets:
A private research university and academic research lab that conducts fundamental and applied research across the physical AI stack, building open datasets, robot learning models, and testing facilities for autonomous systems, and licensing robotics technology to machine makers and startups.
1. A university lab that develops autonomous driving datasets, tactile sensing skins, and imitation learning models, and operates large-scale robotics testing facilities for corporate and academic researchers.
2. Multi-modal sensor fusion datasets, vision-based imitation learning algorithms for mobile manipulation, and open-source tactile sensing skins built through academic research.
3. Synthetic perception training data, in-the-wild robot learning for home tasks, dexterous manipulation research, and physical testing infrastructure for autonomous vehicles, drones, and manipulators.
4. Open-source datasets, licensed robotics technology, joint research collaborations, and physical testing facilities provided to corporate and academic researchers.
5. Autonomous vehicles, home robots, medical robots, mining and construction automation, drones, and automated laboratories.
6. Autonomous vehicle developers, medical robot makers, government agencies, manufacturing institutes, and other academic researchers.
7. Its research outputs and licensed technologies are spun out into commercial robotics companies and integrated by machine makers into their products.
8. It operates a 150,000-square-foot Robotics Innovation Center with indoor and outdoor testing facilities and maintains a multi-decade track record of winning autonomous vehicle competitions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Fujitsu, Meta, Argo AI, the U.S. Army, Caterpillar, the Richard King Mellon Foundation, and the Advanced Robotics for Manufacturing Institute.
Organization type: A private research university operating university labs and government-funded research centers.
Business model: Research grants, corporate partnerships, technology licensing, and institutional funding.
Scale and maturity: A century-old institution with over $500 million in annual research budgets, a 150,000-square-foot robotics center, and a founding role in multiple robotics startups.
Geography: Based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with international research collaborations.
Beyond physical AI: A comprehensive research university with programs spanning science, engineering, business, public policy, humanities, and the arts.

points.name: Advanced Robotics for Manufacturing Institute
points.description: US research institute advancing robotics and AI adoption in manufacturing through demonstrations, assessments, and workforce training.
points.bullets:
A nonprofit consortium and systems integrator that accelerates the adoption of robotics and artificial intelligence in U.S. manufacturing by providing proof-of-concept demonstrations, assessments, and workforce development for small and medium-sized manufacturers and defense contractors.
1. A systems integrator and federally-funded consortium that de-risks and coordinates the implementation of robotics and physical AI technologies for manufacturers.
2. Hands-on demonstrations, modeling and simulation services, and proof-of-concept assessments of robotics and physical AI systems.
3. Robotics implementation assessment, manufacturing process de-risking, and workforce development for physical automation.
4. Integration services, expert assessments, and collaborative demonstrations coordinated across nearly 500 member organizations.
5. Factories and defense manufacturing facilities.
6. Small and medium-sized manufacturers with 500 or fewer employees, defense manufacturers, and workforce development partners.
7. It operates as a neutral broker between robot makers, academic researchers, and manufacturers to install and evaluate automation on factory floors.
8. It functions as a non-commercial, public-private partnership that de-risks robotics adoption for underserved manufacturers through expert assessment rather than selling products for profit.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Carnegie Mellon University, the Department of Defense, the Manufacturing USA network, Ohio State University, and the Air Force Research Laboratory.
Organization type: A nonprofit institute and public-private partnership operating as a federally-funded consortium.
Business model: Federal funding and consortium memberships used to manage robotics adoption programs, demonstrations, and workforce development.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, operating with approximately 35 staff and 400 member organizations from a 90,000-square-foot facility while managing four regional innovation accelerators.
Geography: Based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and operating regionally across southwestern Pennsylvania while serving manufacturers across the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses broadly on workforce development, defense manufacturing support, and research into how artificial intelligence transforms manufacturing careers and work.

points.name: FANUC
points.description: Japanese industrial robotics manufacturer building factory automation systems with embedded AI vision and force sensing for autonomous task execution.
points.bullets:
A robot and factory automation maker that builds and sells industrial robotic arms, collaborative robots, CNC systems, and production machinery, integrating edge AI inference controllers, vision systems, and simulation software for manufacturers.
1. A robot and machine tool maker that builds and sells industrial arms, cobots, CNC systems, and factory automation machinery.
2. Multi-axis articulated robotic arms, collaborative robots, CNC controllers, electric injection molding machines, and wire-cut EDM machines, integrated with edge AI accelerators, robotic vision, and physics-based simulation software.
3. Industrial articulated manipulation, collaborative payload handling, precision machining, bin picking, welding, painting, palletizing, and virtual commissioning of robotic cells.
4. Complete robots, cobots, machine tools, controllers, simulation software, and integrated factory automation systems.
5. Automotive factories, electronics manufacturing, warehouses, food processing, and general industrial assembly.
6. Manufacturers, automotive companies, electronics producers, food processors, logistics operators, and system integrators.
7. Its robots and machine tools are deployed in factories by manufacturers and configured by authorized system integrators.
8. It combines an established industrial robotics install base exceeding 2 million units with edge AI controllers and open-platform ROS 2 support.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Strategic collaborations include NVIDIA, Google, Fujitsu, PTC, and Vention.
Organization type: A publicly traded industrial manufacturing company.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and machine tools, controller and software sales, and factory automation integration contracts.
Scale and maturity: A multinational corporation founded in 1950 with annual revenue of $4.7 billion and a global install base exceeding 2 million robots.
Geography: Headquartered in Japan with a major subsidiary in North America and global operations spanning 100 countries.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's broader business encompasses comprehensive factory automation, CNC systems, and industrial machinery.

points.name: Yaskawa
points.description: Japanese industrial robotics manufacturer deploying AI-powered robotic arms for smart manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and component supplier that builds and sells industrial robotic arms, collaborative robots, servo motors, and pre-engineered automation systems for manufacturers. The company equips its robots with on-device AI inference silicon, vision systems, and simulation frameworks for autonomous welding, assembly, and material handling.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells industrial arms, collaborative robots, and servo motors, along with pre-engineered automation cells.
2. Electrically driven industrial robots, servo motors with high torque and minimal backlash, and AI controllers integrating edge inference modules, machine vision, and ROS 2 compatibility.
3. Arc and spot welding, palletizing, bin picking, machine tending, fenceless collaborative operation, and virtual commissioning of production lines.
4. Complete robots, collaborative robots, servo motors, controllers, and pre-engineered automation cells sold to manufacturers and integrators.
5. Factories, warehouses, automotive assembly lines, semiconductor fabrication, healthcare laboratories, and production facilities.
6. Automotive manufacturers, electronics manufacturers, logistics operators, and industrial systems integrators.
7. Its robots and servo motors are designed into factory automation lines operated by manufacturers and integrated with third-party vision and gripper systems.
8. It combines deep heritage in servo motors and welding robotics with integrated edge AI inference and GPU-accelerated simulation frameworks for virtual commissioning.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Fujitsu, SoftBank, ARM Institute, and Nabtesco.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots, servo motors, and controllers, alongside pre-engineered automation systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1915, with annual revenue around $1.7 billion, over 12,000 employees, and a global installed base exceeding two million robots.
Geography: Based in Japan with major manufacturing expansions in North America and a global operational footprint.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is industrial robotics, motion control systems, and factory automation.

points.name: Midea Group
points.description: Chinese manufacturing company developing multi-arm mobile industrial robots for flexible factory automation.
points.bullets:
An appliance and electronics manufacturer that has expanded into industrial robotics, building multi-arm mobile robots for factory automation and integrating them into its own manufacturing operations and those of external industrial customers.
1. A robot maker and systems integrator that builds multi-arm mobile industrial robots and deploys factory automation systems for manufacturers.
2. Six independent robotic arms mounted on a wheeled mobile base, designed for parallel task execution and dynamic role-shifting in industrial environments.
3. Multi-arm coordination, complex manipulation, parallel task execution and integration into closed-loop manufacturing processes.
4. Complete robotic platforms and factory automation systems installed as integrated manufacturing solutions.
5. Industrial manufacturing and assembly operations in factories.
6. Industrial manufacturers and its own internal manufacturing operations.
7. It builds complete robotic platforms and integrates them into factory environments, both for its own plants and for external manufacturers.
8. It prioritizes functional efficiency over humanoid design by mounting six independent robotic arms on a wheeled mobile base to enable dynamic role-shifting without major hardware reconfiguration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It owns the industrial robotics company KUKA and has partnerships with HONPINE for precision motion solutions.
Organization type: A publicly traded conglomerate listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic platforms, factory automation integration services and consumer appliance sales.
Scale and maturity: A large, established global enterprise founded in 1968, employing about 150,000 people and operating over 100 smart manufacturing plants.
Geography: Based in Foshan, China, it operates a global network of manufacturing plants and partnerships.
Beyond physical AI: It manufactures consumer and commercial appliances, automotive parts and semiconductor ventures alongside its industrial robotics business.

points.name: CMR Surgical
points.description: UK medical device manufacturer building robotic surgical assistants for minimally invasive soft-tissue procedures.
points.bullets:
A medical robot maker that builds and sells portable, modular surgical robotic systems for minimally invasive soft-tissue procedures, using simulation to train and validate the robotic intelligence before clinical deployment.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds complete portable surgical robotic systems and sells them to hospitals.
2. Modular surgical robotic arms on portable carts with integrated visualization instruments and robotic intelligence trained and validated in GPU physics simulation.
3. Minimally invasive soft-tissue manipulation, portable modular operating-room deployment, and fluorescence imaging for real-time surgical visualization.
4. Complete surgical robotic systems and integrated surgical instruments sold to medical facilities under per-procedure leasing and purchase models.
5. Hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and operating rooms for laparoscopic surgery.
6. Public and private hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and healthcare providers.
7. It designs and manufactures its own complete surgical robotic systems and places them directly into hospital operating rooms.
8. It competes on portability, modularity, and cost-effectiveness with a compact form factor designed for ambulatory surgery centers and mid-sized facilities.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Siemens, and Cisco, and its surgical intelligence is trained using NVIDIA Cosmos-H simulation.
