8. A simulation-first reinforcement learning approach generates thousands of hours of daily synthetic training data for rapid sim-to-real transfer, reducing reliance on human teleoperation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is an NVIDIA Inception program member and is backed by Prosus Ventures.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and model licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2024, the company recently secured a $50 million Series A funding round to scale operations and accelerate global commercialization.
Geography: Based with research and development operations in Zurich and a United States headquarters in the Bay Area, planning to scale robot fleets globally.
Beyond physical AI: The company maintains no other business activities, as physical AI software represents its entire operational focus.

points.name: Vention
points.description: Canadian robotics startup providing modular hardware and cloud-based design tools for building custom factory automation systems.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and component supplier that builds a cloud-based manufacturing automation platform combining modular hardware, simulation, and AI-driven programming for designing, simulating, deploying, and operating robotic workcells.
1. A developer tools and component supplier whose cloud-based automation platform and modular hardware are sold to manufacturers and integrators.
2. A cloud-based CAD, digital twin simulation, and AI model pipeline running on edge controllers that integrate modular hardware components like extrusions, motors, and conveyors with third-party robotic arms.
3. Design, simulation, deployment, and operation of robotic workcells, plus zero-shot autonomous bin picking, piece picking, palletizing, welding, and machine tending.
4. The platform is delivered as cloud-based software alongside physical modular hardware components, controllers, and pre-engineered turnkey workcells.
5. The technology is used in factories for robotic palletizing, machine tending, welding, sanding, bin picking, and case packing.
6. The company sells to manufacturers, small and medium-sized businesses, systems integrators, and research laboratories.
7. Its platform bridges component supply and final integration by letting customers design and build their own automated workcells using its hardware and software ecosystem.
8. Its zero-shot automation approach uses composable AI models and natural language interaction to compress robotic deployment timelines from weeks to hours.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with NVIDIA for Isaac Sim, Jetson, and Isaac platform integration, and with FANUC, Universal Robots, and ABB for plug-and-play robot arm compatibility.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through hardware component sales, software platform access, and turnkey automation systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016, the company has raised $110 million in funding and deployed over 25,000 machines globally.
Geography: The company is based in Canada and operates globally with a strong market presence among United States manufacturers.
Beyond physical AI: Designing and deploying custom and turnkey factory automation solutions represents the company's entire business focus.

points.name: Fauna Robotics
points.description: US robotics company developing social humanoid robots for homes, schools, and healthcare facilities.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that builds a small, lightweight bipedal robot designed for social interaction in human-centered spaces, sold as a developer platform for research and entertainment customers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells kid-size humanoid robots.
2. A bipedal humanoid robot with soft exterior panels, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin compute, and an open software development kit for on-device vision, conversation, and embodied decision-making.
3. Bipedal locomotion, light manipulation, socially expressive interaction, and developer-accessible perception and navigation.
4. Complete robots sold as physical developer platforms.
5. Humanoids used in homes, schools, offices, healthcare facilities, and entertainment environments.
6. Academic research laboratories, corporate research divisions, animation corporations, and established robotics makers.
7. Its complete robots are bought by research and entertainment companies for application development and social interaction.
8. It prioritizes physical safety, emotional expressiveness, and developer accessibility over heavy industrial manipulation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: PTC and NVIDIA for design and simulation, with Disney and Boston Dynamics as early customers, and Amazon as its parent company.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a large technology and e-commerce conglomerate, formerly an early-stage startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete humanoid robots.
Scale and maturity: A two-year-old company acquired in 2026 with roughly 50 employees, selling robots priced at around $50,000.
Geography: Based in New York City, operating under a large technology conglomerate.
Beyond physical AI: Developing socially interactive bipedal humanoid robots represents the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Tether
points.description: Financial services firm embedding self-custodial payments and edge AI runtimes into robotic systems.
points.bullets:
An infrastructure provider and lead investor in edge and physical AI that supplies an edge AI runtime and a secure payment SDK for third-party robotic platforms, rather than manufacturing hardware. It makes local on-device AI execution and self-custodial financial transaction capabilities available to developers and operators of autonomous machines. Beyond its physical AI investments, the organization is a financial services and software company that issues a fiat-collateralized stablecoin and operates in the cryptocurrency and blockchain space.
1. A software and financial infrastructure company that builds an edge AI runtime and a wallet development kit, provided as software development kits integrated into other companies' robotics platforms.
2. A local edge AI runtime for on-device machine learning execution and a secure financial software layer that embeds self-custodial payment functionality directly into autonomous systems.
3. Local on-device AI model execution and embedded secure financial transaction capability for autonomous machines.
4. Software development kits integrated into third-party robotic platforms.
5. Manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and household service robotics.
6. Developers and operators of full-stack robotic platforms.
7. Its software kits are integrated into robots built and deployed by other physical AI platform makers.
8. It approaches the machine economy by combining decentralized edge compute with independent financial capabilities, allowing autonomous machines to operate without centralized cloud or financial intermediaries.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It led a Series C funding round for a cognitive robotics maker and participated in a funding round for a robotics company.
Organization type: A privately held financial services and software company that invests in emerging technology sectors.
Business model: It generates revenue through software integration and manages capital through strategic investments in robotics companies.
Scale and maturity: It operates at significant scale, demonstrated by leading a $1.4 billion Series C funding round in 2026.
Geography: It operates globally, anchoring strategic technology partnerships at the intersection of industrial automation and artificial intelligence.
Beyond physical AI: It issues a fiat-collateralized stablecoin and operates a broader cryptocurrency and blockchain business beyond its edge AI and robotics investments.

points.name: Mach Industries
points.description: United States defense robotics startup building autonomous unmanned strike and reconnaissance aircraft.
points.bullets:
A defense contractor and unmanned systems maker that designs, builds and vertically manufactures autonomous military platforms, including VTOL strike drones, glide munitions, high-altitude sensor aircraft and hybrid-electric uncrewed aircraft, for the U.S. armed forces and allied militaries.
1. A defense drone and vehicle maker that builds and sells complete unmanned aerial systems and munitions.
2. Vertically integrated unmanned warfare systems incorporating hybrid-electric propulsion, runway-independent vertical takeoff and landing flight control, high-altitude gliding, energetics and decentralized manufacturing networks.
3. Autonomous strike, long-range munitions delivery, persistent high-altitude sensing and communications, runway-independent heavy-lift operations and adaptable wartime production.
4. Complete unmanned aircraft, munitions and defense systems delivered to government customers, along with physical manufacturing infrastructure.
5. Defense, military strike, contested logistics and distributed weapons manufacturing.
6. U.S. Department of Defense branches including the Army, Air Force and SOCOM, and allied forces.
7. It designs and builds complete unmanned platforms and their underlying propulsion and energetics subsystems in its own facilities, delivering finished defense systems directly to military customers.
8. It combines rapid unmanned hardware development with a decentralized, pop-up manufacturing network designed to enable fast switching of product lines and resilient wartime production.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Whisper Aero for Atlas aircraft propulsion integration, HevenDrones for hydrogen-powered UAV production, Infinite Capital and Ribbit Capital as investors, and the Defense Innovation Unit RIMES program.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Defense contracts, systems integration awards and direct military hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A 2023-founded startup that has raised $300 million in a Series C funding round and operates a 115,000-square-foot manufacturing facility.
Geography: Based in the United States, manufacturing and operating domestically.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization operates energetics engineering and manufacturing subsidiaries, developing explosives, propulsion systems and test infrastructure for defense applications.

points.name: Shifters
points.description: US robotics startup developing AI-native autonomous robot teams for hazardous and GPS-denied ground missions.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that builds AI-native autonomous ground robotic teams for hazardous environments, combining rugged hardware, an AI motion control stack, and multi-robot orchestration software for defense and commercial markets.
1. A robot maker and systems integrator that builds and sells complete rugged ground robotic platforms and the supervised autonomy and orchestration software that runs on them.
2. Rugged ground robotic platforms and an AI motion control stack for autonomous navigation in complex, unseen, GPS-denied environments, with a command layer that translates human intent into robotic tasking and an orchestration layer for coordinated multi-robot execution.
3. Supervised robotic team autonomy, autonomous navigation in complex and unseen environments, multi-robot coordination and synchronized operations, and translation of operator intent into robotic tasking.
4. Complete integrated robotic platforms, licensed autonomy and orchestration software, and end-to-end systems integration.
5. Hazardous environments, defense missions, subterranean navigation, perimeter security, building scanning, and industrial infrastructure inspection.
6. Defense forces and defense agencies, commercial operators in industrial infrastructure, and security organizations.
7. It designs and builds its own rugged ground robots and the autonomy and orchestration software that run on them, delivering complete platforms rather than isolated components.
8. It combines a category-defining AI motion control stack for legged robotics with supervised multi-robot team autonomy and rugged hardware to navigate unseen, GPS-denied environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ace Capital Partners led its seed funding round, and Aurelius Capital is an investment firm whose founding partner commented positively on its capabilities and potential.
Organization type: A privately held deep-tech startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robotic platforms and software licenses or contracts for autonomy and orchestration systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023, it has secured $15 million in total funding, including a $10.2 million seed round, and is developing and unveiling its first products.
Geography: Headquartered in Washington, DC, with research and development operations in Israel, and it operates primarily within the United States and allied defense markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are its entire focus and core business.

points.name: U.S. Department of War
points.description: US government agency funding autonomous robotic systems and edge AI for military operations.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds, procures, integrates and operates autonomous systems and unmanned platforms across the defense autonomy stack, acting simultaneously as a technology developer, systems integrator and primary operator for the U.S. military.
1. A government agency that funds and buys robotic platforms, drone guidance kits and autonomy software, and operates them as fielded defense systems.
2. Machine vision, edge computing and autonomous navigation systems integrated into unmanned ground vehicles, small unmanned aircraft and maritime platforms.
3. Intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, explosive ordnance disposal, autonomous logistics, collaborative swarm operations and combat support.
4. Non-dilutive capital, procurement contracts, fielded defense programs and integrated systems deployed in active military contexts.
5. Unmanned ground vehicles, small unmanned aircraft, drones, tactical ground robots and autonomous maritime platforms.
6. Its own internal military branches, including the Army, Air Force and Special Operations Command.
7. It buys robots, components and software from defense OEMs and operates the integrated systems in its own military operations.
8. Its proposed multi-billion-dollar budget consolidation and push to transition from remotely operated systems to highly autonomous, collaborative swarm platforms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Robotics developers, defense OEMs and AI solution providers, including Mach Industries, Ondas, Roboteam, Havoc and Auterion.
Organization type: A government agency operating under the federal government of the United States.
Business model: Federal defense funding, government contracts and direct government procurement of systems and technologies.
Scale and maturity: A long-established institution with a multi-decade history, recently proposing a budget increase to $53.6 billion for fiscal year 2027 to consolidate unmanned systems development.
Geography: Based in the United States and deploying systems globally through its military operations.
Beyond physical AI: It is responsible for the broader national defense, military readiness and global security operations of the United States.

points.name: Vantor
points.description: US geospatial technology company developing on-device vision software for GPS-denied drone navigation.
points.bullets:
A spatial intelligence software company that develops vision-based positioning software and operates a proprietary satellite constellation to supply 3D terrain maps for autonomous navigation in GPS-denied environments.
1. A software and geospatial data company that builds vision-based positioning software and terrain data products for autonomous platforms.
2. On-device inference algorithms process live camera feeds against a global 3D terrain model built from high-resolution satellite imagery to determine precise geolocation.
3. GPS-denied navigation, visual positioning, georegistration, and 3D terrain mapping for autonomous systems.
4. On-device positioning software, software development kits, cloud data subscriptions, and 3D terrain data accessed through a hub.
5. Drones, ground vehicles, defense autonomy, last-mile delivery, disaster response, and tactical operations.
6. Defense agencies, drone manufacturers, hardware integrators, and European governments.
7. Its software and terrain data are integrated by hardware manufacturers into autonomous platforms for navigation in contested environments.
8. It owns a proprietary high-resolution satellite constellation that supplies updated 3D terrain models within hours to ensure autonomous systems operate on current geographical data.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: BAE Systems, Niantic Spatial, Advent International, and European governments.
Organization type: Privately held company spun out from a former space technology firm.
Business model: Software licenses, data subscriptions, project-based data sales, and change-based refresh subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Operates a six-satellite constellation and covers over 100 million square kilometers at high accuracy.
Geography: Based in the United States with sovereign spatial intelligence collaborations in Germany and other European nations.
Beyond physical AI: It maintains a broad geospatial intelligence focus covering persistent monitoring, Earth observation, and classified AI modeling.

points.name: Ansys
points.description: US software company providing simulation platforms for testing autonomous vehicle perception systems in virtual environments.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds engineering simulation software for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI. The platform provides closed-loop virtual testing and validation infrastructure using physically accurate sensor models and synthetic data. The tools allow engineers to exercise autonomy software stacks and evaluate the safety of AI-based perception systems without physical prototypes.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation platform robotics and automotive engineers use to test autonomous machines in virtual environments.
2. GPU physics simulation, multiphysics modeling, sensor-accurate synthetic data generation, software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing, and model-based systems engineering.
3. Virtual testing of autonomous driving systems, sensor simulation, safety evaluation of AI-based perception, embedded software validation, and digital twin modeling.
4. Licensed software, simulation tools, and cloud-based platforms that integrate with other engineering environments.
5. Autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, automotive lamp design, radar systems, and digital twins for industrial machinery.
6. Automakers, autonomous vehicle startups, automotive Tier-1 suppliers, and semiconductor designers.
7. Its simulation tools are used by automakers and autonomous system developers to validate perception software and sensor hardware before physical deployment.
8. The combination of physics-based simulation fidelity, ISO 26262 functional safety certification capabilities, and the ability to virtualize complex multi-sensor autonomous driving scenarios at scale.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Synopsys, NVIDIA Omniverse, Toyota Customizing & Development, Samsung, Oculii, and Isaac for Healthcare.
Organization type: Subsidiary of Synopsys, formerly a publicly traded company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions for engineering simulation tools.
Scale and maturity: An established, mature company acquired by Synopsys in a $35 billion transaction completed in 2025.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: A broad engineering simulation company whose core business spans multiphysics modeling, optical and electromagnetic simulation, semiconductor power integrity, and simulation data management.

points.name: Hurotics
points.description: South Korean robotics company building wearable exosuits with on-device AI for medical rehabilitation.
points.bullets:
A wearable robot maker that builds and sells soft exosuits for lower-limb medical rehabilitation, integrating on-device AI with physical actuator hardware and sensors into a complete clinical solution for medical institutions.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells wearable rehabilitation robots.
2. Wearable actuation hardware, real-time sensors and embedded AI models for real-time gait analysis and adaptive motor assistance in a soft exosuit.
3. Lower-limb muscle recovery, joint rehabilitation and adaptive motor assistance for patients following stroke, spinal cord injury or Parkinson's disease.
4. Complete robotic rehabilitation suits sold as a Class II combination medical device.
5. Hospitals and clinical rehabilitation settings.
6. Medical institutions, hospital administrators, doctors and medical device distributors.
7. Its rehabilitation robots are deployed directly into hospital clinical settings by medical professionals.
8. A lightweight, clothing-like soft exosuit that integrates with existing hospital equipment without the bulk of rigid-frame designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: KODIT and hospital rehabilitation teams conducting clinical research.
Organization type: Privately held startup focused on the healthcare technology sector.
Business model: Medical device sales.
Scale and maturity: An emerging enterprise recognized by a national credit guarantee fund as a First Penguin Enterprise, with FDA registration and Korean Class II medical device certification.
Geography: Based in South Korea and expanding operations into the United States and European medical device markets.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on medical rehabilitation robotics rather than industrial or military applications, making healthcare its sole business focus.

points.name: FRT Robotics
points.description: South Korean robotics company building wearable exoskeletons that reduce muscle fatigue for industrial workers.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that develops and sells wearable robots, specifically exoskeletons, for industrial, rehabilitation, and emergency response use. It builds lower-body wearable robots that assist muscle strength, correct posture, and reduce physical strain for workers performing repetitive bending and heavy lifting, incorporating on-device AI technology. The company serves government agencies, agricultural workers, and industrial users with affordable, reliable designs and aims to expand into the humanoid robot market.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells wearable exoskeleton robots for industrial and rehabilitation use.
2. Wearable exoskeletons with on-device AI that assist muscle strength, correct posture, and reduce muscle fatigue and injury risk.
3. Physical strain reduction, posture correction, muscle strength assistance, and injury prevention during repetitive bending and heavy lifting.
4. Complete wearable robots and exoskeleton systems.
5. Industrial workplaces, agriculture, fisheries, care facilities, forestry, firefighting, and rescue operations.
6. Government agencies, public sector organizations, older adults, female workers, agricultural and fisheries workers, care workers, and industrial on-site workers.
7. It builds complete wearable robots and supplies them directly to government agencies and industrial users.
8. It targets the industrial wearable market with affordable, reliable exoskeleton designs tailored for specific demographics like older adults and female workers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Korea Forest Service, National Fire Agency, Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute, and Seoul Business Agency.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of wearable robots.
Scale and maturity: Founded in March 2015, with products registered as Innovative Products for public sector deployment and proven reliability in firefighting and rescue operations.
Geography: Based in South Korea, with aims to expand into overseas markets.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and wearable robotics is its entire focus.

points.name: Fourier Rehab
points.description: Chinese robotics company building rehabilitation exoskeletons that run on-device AI for real-time patient therapy.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that builds rehabilitation robots and exoskeletons for clinical therapy, integrating hardware, on-device AI inference, clinical software, and deployment support for healthcare and research institutions.
1. A robot maker that builds upper- and lower-limb rehabilitation robots and exoskeletons, sold as complete deployed clinical systems.
2. Rehabilitation robots and exoskeletons using six-degree-of-freedom motion platforms, force plates, motion capture, immersive VR, and on-device AI inference for adaptive therapy and real-time feedback.
3. Upper- and lower-limb rehabilitation, balance and gait training, biomechanical analysis, intelligent assistance, adaptive therapy modes, real-time performance metrics, and cloud-connected data synchronization.
4. Complete robotic systems and integrated modular rehabilitation platforms installed as turnkey clinical solutions, alongside an open-source development framework for researchers.
5. Hospitals, rehabilitation clinics, and research institutions.
6. Healthcare providers, physical therapy clinics, and research institutions.
7. Its rehabilitation robots and integrated clinical systems are deployed in hospitals and clinics worldwide.
8. An integrated full-stack approach combining hardware, on-device AI inference, clinical software, therapist training, and protocol development in a unified system.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include Shirley Ryan AbilityLab, KITE Research Institute, ETH Zürich, National Healthcare Group, University of Melbourne, COSMED, ProCare, and Brooks' Center for Innovation.
Organization type: Privately held subsidiary of a corporate group.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete clinical systems and robotic platforms.
Scale and maturity: An established subsidiary with approximately 500 team members, serving over 2,000 institutions across more than 40 countries.
Geography: Headquartered in Shanghai, China, with global operations spanning over 40 countries and notable market expansion in Europe and North America.
Beyond physical AI: The parent corporate group also develops general-purpose humanoid robots.

points.name: Edge Medical
points.description: Shenzhen surgical robotics company developing minimally invasive robotic platforms for single and multi-port surgeries.
points.bullets:
A surgical robot maker that designs, develops and manufactures minimally invasive surgical robotic systems, including multi-port, single-port, and natural orifice platforms for hospitals.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete surgical robots.
2. Multi-port, single-port and natural orifice endoscopic robotic platforms incorporating real-time sensor fusion and telesurgery capabilities.
3. Minimally invasive surgical manipulation, real-time teleoperation over distances exceeding 1,200 kilometers, and unified console control of both multi-port and single-port configurations.
4. Complete surgical robotic systems.
5. Hospitals and operating rooms for urology, gynecology, general surgery and thoracic surgery.
6. Hospitals and medical providers.
7. Its complete surgical robots are deployed in hospitals by medical providers.
8. A unified surgical console allows surgeons to operate both multi-port and single-port configurations from a single system.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Boyu, Temasek, HongShan, 3H Health, LYFE Capital, China State-Owned Enterprise Mixed Ownership Reform Fund and OrbiMed.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Surgical robot hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Holds over 736 patent grants and applications globally, has a registered capital of RMB360 million and a valuation exceeding US$1.5 billion.
Geography: Based in Shenzhen, China, and operates in global markets with EU CE Mark approval.
Beyond physical AI: Designing and manufacturing surgical robotics is its entire focus.

points.name: Galbot
points.description: Chinese robotics company building wheeled humanoid robots that use onboard AI and sensors to perform physical tasks without cloud connectivity.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that builds general-purpose wheeled humanoid robots powered by proprietary vision-language-action models for autonomous task execution in semi-structured environments, selling and deploying complete systems for retail, manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete wheeled humanoid robots.
2. General-purpose wheeled humanoid robots featuring edge sensing, dexterous actuators, and proprietary end-to-end vision-language-action models for on-device inference.
3. Autonomous parts sorting, bin handling, medication picking, folding clothes, dexterous grasping, dynamic task replanning, and obstacle adaptation without cloud connectivity.
4. Complete robotic systems offered through purchase, rental, or hire arrangements, alongside open-sourced foundation model algorithms and synthetic manipulation datasets.
5. Humanoid-operated stores, logistics facilities, pharmaceutical chains, battery manufacturing lines, energy, manufacturing, and real estate settings.
6. Retailers, manufacturers, healthcare operators, logistics operators, and energy companies.
7. It designs and builds complete robots and operates its own retail stores, integrating its proprietary models directly into its hardware.
8. An end-to-end embodied AI architecture trained on synthetic data and large-scale dexterous hand datasets enables rapid adaptation to dynamic environments on-device without cloud connectivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors and deployment partners include CATL, SAIC Motor, Sinopec, CITIC Investment Holdings, the national AI industry investment fund, and the Hong Kong Investment Corporation; it uses NVIDIA Jetson compute modules and Isaac simulation and partners with SAP and Daimon Robotics.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Robot hardware sales, rental and hire arrangements, and open-sourced model algorithms.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023 with over 2.5 billion yuan in funding, a valuation exceeding 10 billion yuan, and more than 1,000 robots deployed across over 30 cities.
Geography: Based in Beijing and deploying robotic systems across China and Hong Kong.
Beyond physical AI: The design, development, and commercialization of embodied AI and physical robotics represent the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
points.description: US government agency regulating AI-powered medical devices and physical robotics used in healthcare.
points.bullets:
A government agency that regulates medical devices utilizing edge AI, robotics, and physical automation, evaluating the safety and efficacy of on-device inference software and physical robotic actuators before market authorization. It oversees the total product lifecycle of deployed hardware and on-device AI software, serving healthcare providers, patients, and medical technology manufacturers by authorizing which AI-enabled medical devices can be brought to the physical market.
1. A government agency that reviews and clears medical devices, including robotic surgical systems, exoskeletons, and AI-based diagnostic tools, through regulatory pathways rather than developing these technologies directly.
2. Regulatory frameworks and review processes, including 510(k) clearance, De Novo classification, Predetermined Change Control Plans for AI/ML-based Software as a Medical Device, and breakthrough device designations.
3. Market authorization, total product lifecycle oversight of deployed medical robotics and on-device AI, safety and efficacy evaluation, and clearance of AI-based computer-aided detection devices.
4. Regulatory decisions, clearances, and guidance documents that authorize medical device manufacturers to commercialize their robotic and AI-enabled products in the United States.
5. Surgical robots, neurorehabilitation exoskeletons, endovascular robotic systems, dental surgery robots, and AI-enabled medical diagnostic devices used in hospitals and clinical settings.
6. Medical device manufacturers, robotics companies, and healthcare technology developers seeking regulatory approval to market their physical AI and robotic medical devices.
7. Its regulatory clearances are required by medical robot makers and AI medical device developers before they can commercialize their products for healthcare providers.
8. It develops unique regulatory frameworks, such as Predetermined Change Control Plans, which allow on-device AI and robotic medical systems to safely adapt and learn from real-world data post-deployment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with researchers and institutions, including Atashzar, and works with international regulatory bodies such as Health Canada and the UK’s MHRA.
Organization type: A federal government agency of the United States.
Business model: Federally funded regulatory oversight funded by government appropriations and user fees paid by medical device manufacturers seeking product review.
Scale and maturity: A long-established federal authority that has cleared over 1,000 AI/ML-based medical devices as of 2024, with a mature regulatory infrastructure overseeing rapidly evolving medical technologies.
Geography: Based in the United States, operating domestically while collaborating with international regulatory bodies.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's broader mandate covers the comprehensive regulation of foods, drugs, biologics, cosmetics, veterinary products, and tobacco products to ensure public health and safety.

points.name: Public Procurement Service
points.description: South Korean government agency funding and testing early-stage robotics through public sector pilot deployments.
points.bullets:
A government agency that drives the deployment of physical AI, robotics, and edge silicon across the public sector by designating domestic technologies as innovative procurement products. It acts as a strategic first buyer and market catalyst to bridge the gap between early-stage development and commercialization for domestic suppliers. The organization uses national purchasing power to stimulate demand and validate real-world performance of physical AI and automation in public settings.
1. A government agency that funds and facilitates the deployment of physical AI and robotics technologies through public procurement programs.
2. Market creation, pilot procurement validation, and public-sector deployment of edge AI chips and robotic systems.
3. Public procurement contracts and innovation procurement designations that place edge silicon and robots into public sector operations.
4. Public sector deployments, including healthcare settings where designated robotic and edge AI products are trialed.
5. Domestic robotics and artificial intelligence suppliers, along with public sector buyers.
6. It sits at the top of the value chain as a demand-side buyer, buying edge AI chips and robots from domestic manufacturers to deploy them in public facilities.
7. Its Innovation Procurement program uses government purchasing power to provide an initial first-buyer safety net for early-stage domestic technologies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Engages internationally with organizations including the International Trade Centre and Consip SpA.
Organization type: A government agency.
Business model: Public procurement and government spending.
Scale and maturity: Manages roughly 225 trillion won in annual public spending and has registered multiple robotics and AI chip products for public deployment.
Geography: Based in South Korea and operating domestically with international engagements.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, it is deploying tools for AI transformation of the procurement process itself, including market intelligence, price analysis, and supply chain monitoring.

points.name: Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement
points.description: South Korean government agency accelerating the adoption and commercialization of physical automation technologies across manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and service robotics sectors.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and administers programs to advance South Korea's robot industry, selecting and supporting physical automation technologies for manufacturing, logistics, healthcare and services.
1. A government agency that runs demonstration programs, testing and certification infrastructure, and policy initiatives for robotics manufacturers and startups.
2. It delivers ecosystem support, project funding, testing and certification, standardization, and market-creation pilots.
3. Government programs, demonstration centers, test-beds and policy implementation.
4. Manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, service robotics and wearable robots.
5. Robotics manufacturers, startups, academia and automation firms.
6. It holds the official authority to direct government resources, set industry standards and influence procurement.
points.profile:
Organization type: A government-affiliated agency.
Business model: Government funding programs and contracts.
Scale and maturity: A national-level institute managing established programs and demonstration centers.
Geography: Based and operating entirely in South Korea.
Beyond physical AI: Robotics and physical automation represent its entire focus, guided by national strategic plans to establish the domestic robot industry as a global leader.

points.name: Encord
points.description: California startup providing data annotation and management software to train vision models for autonomous vehicles and robotics.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a data management and annotation platform for training physical AI models, and operates teleoperation labs to manufacture physical training data for robotic manipulation tasks. It supplies the data infrastructure layer—ingestion, curation, annotation, and evaluation of multimodal sensor datasets—to robotics and autonomous vehicle developers.
1. A developer tools company whose data and teleoperation platform robotics and autonomy engineers use to build training datasets.
2. A data platform that processes LiDAR, 3D point clouds, multi-camera setups, and synced video streams, complemented by physical teleoperation rigs and forearm electromyography sensors that generate demonstration data for manipulation models.
3. Data curation, annotation, and evaluation of multimodal datasets, plus teleoperation data collection using leader-follower robotic arms and muscle-sensing wearables to produce manipulation training data.
4. Licensed software platform and data collection services run in dedicated lab facilities.
5. Robotic manipulation, autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, and manufacturing robotics.
6. Robotics firms developing manipulation systems, autonomous vehicle developers, and manufacturing engineering teams.
7. Its platform and teleoperation data feed directly into the model training pipelines of robot makers and autonomy developers.
8. It combines a multimodal data management and annotation platform with in-house physical teleoperation labs to actively manufacture training data, rather than only processing customer-supplied data.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Zander Labs on brain wave measurement trials, and manipulation robotics firms including Pickle Robot.
Organization type: Privately held technology startup.
Business model: Software platform licenses, subscriptions, and teleoperation data collection services.
Geography: Based in San Leandro, California, with teleoperation lab facilities in the Bay Area.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on providing the data management, annotation, and teleoperation infrastructure required for developing physical AI.

points.name: Berkshire Grey
points.description: US robotics company deploying integrated robotic systems to automate warehouse picking, sorting, and fulfillment operations.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and builds vertically integrated automated robotic systems for warehouse, fulfillment, and logistics operations, integrating robotics hardware, machine vision, grasping capabilities, planning software, and controls.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds complete warehouse picking, sorting, packing, and trailer-unloading robots, sold as capital equipment or via robotics-as-a-service.
2. AI-guided perception and manipulation software integrated with automated storage, retrieval, grasping, and sortation hardware.
3. Mixed-SKU piece picking, automated sortation, packing, trailer unloading, order fulfillment, and store replenishment.
4. Complete robotic systems and integrated automation platforms delivered through traditional sales or robotics-as-a-service models.
5. Warehouses, e-commerce fulfillment centers, retail replenishment, distribution centers, and logistics operations.
6. Logistics operators, e-commerce companies, retailers, and distribution firms.
7. Its robotic systems are integrated into fulfillment and distribution centers by systems integrators or installed directly for operators.
8. A vertically integrated full-stack approach built for high-throughput operations and uncontrolled warehouse conditions handling irregular shapes, mixed cartons, and polybags.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partnered with Swisslog as a systems integration partner and FedEx to launch autonomous trailer-unloading robots, acquired by SoftBank.
Organization type: Privately held subsidiary, formerly a publicly traded company before being taken private.
Business model: Hardware and system sales and robotics-as-a-service contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2013 with approximately $500 million in revenue, acquired in 2023 after a prior public listing.
Geography: Based in Bedford, Massachusetts, operating in the American market.
Beyond physical AI: Warehouse and fulfillment automation represents the organization's entire business focus.

points.name: Dassault Systèmes
points.description: French software company providing simulation and digital twin platforms to safely design and validate physical AI systems before deployment.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds simulation, digital twin, and product lifecycle management software for designing, validating, and virtually commissioning robotics and autonomous production systems.
1. A software company that licenses simulation and digital twin platforms to robotics engineers and manufacturers.
2. Cloud-based 3D design, multi-disciplinary simulation, and virtual commissioning software that emulates robot trajectories, sensor perceptions, and PLC control logic.
3. Robot trajectory creation, high-fidelity physics simulation, digital twin experiences, and hardware-in-the-loop virtual commissioning.
4. Licensed software platforms and cloud-based collaborative applications used by engineering teams.
5. Factory and warehouse automation, production lines, and autonomous manufacturing systems.
6. Robot makers, industrial automation integrators, and automotive manufacturers.
7. Its simulation and lifecycle software is used by robotics manufacturers and integrators to design and validate machines before physical deployment.
8. It bridges the sim-to-real gap by combining exact robot controller software emulation with physically accurate 3D digital twins for production systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Neura Robotics, Volkswagen Group, NVIDIA, and CNBM Triumph Robotics.
Organization type: Publicly traded software company.
Business model: Software licenses and cloud-based subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A mature, large-scale global enterprise with long-term industrial partnerships.
Geography: Based in France and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: A comprehensive provider of 3D design, simulation, and product lifecycle management software for a wide range of industries beyond physical AI.

points.name: Hexagon AB
points.description: Swedish technology company providing sensor fusion and perception software for physical AI platforms.
points.bullets:
A technology company that provides sensor fusion, perception software and geospatial measurement systems for industrial and physical-world applications.
1. A sensor and software maker that builds geosystems, metrology sensors and perception software sold as components, instruments and licensed platforms.
2. The core technology combines geospatial measurement hardware, industrial sensors and sensor-fusion perception software.
3. It delivers high-precision spatial measurement, 3D perception and sensor fusion for industrial mapping and autonomy.
4. Customers get it through industrial sensors, metrology instruments and licensed software platforms.
5. The technology is used in surveying, construction, mining, industrial manufacturing and autonomous machine perception.
6. It sells to industrial enterprises, surveyors, construction firms, mining operators and autonomous machine developers.
7. Its approach pairs parent-company geospatial measurement and metrology hardware with advanced sensor-fusion perception software.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its Geosystems division maintains a strategic partnership with LocLab.
Organization type: It is a publicly traded technology company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: It is a large, established global technology company listed among leading players in the physical AI software platform market.
Geography: It is based in Sweden and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Its broader focus includes digital reality solutions, industrial metrology and geospatial information systems beyond edge and physical AI.

points.name: Coppelia Robotics
points.description: Swiss robotics software company creating simulation platforms for prototyping and validating robot control algorithms prior to physical deployment.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds and maintains a cross-platform robot simulation platform for designing, prototyping, and validating robot control algorithms before physical deployment. It provides simulation software and customized engineering solutions for engineers, researchers, and educators working in physical AI. The organization acts as a foundational software provider within the physical AI value chain, enabling other organizations to develop and verify on-device control systems without manufacturing its own inference silicon, actuators, or deployed robotic hardware.
1. A developer tools company whose robot simulation platform robotics engineers use, sold as a software library and platform with customized engineering solutions.
2. A robotics simulator with a distributed control architecture, kinematics engine, and support for multiple physics simulation libraries.
3. Design, prototyping, and validation of robot control algorithms for complex multi-robot scenarios and distributed control architectures.
4. Free educational software versions and paid commercial licenses, complemented by customized model creation, specialized plugin development, and personalized training sessions.
5. Factory automation, mobile manipulation, humanoid robotics, and autonomous aerial vehicles.
6. Engineers, researchers, and educators in industry, academia, and research.
7. Its simulation platform is used by engineers and researchers to develop and verify on-device control systems for factory automation and mobile manipulation.
8. It sets itself apart through its versatility and scalable support for complex multi-robot scenarios and distributed control architectures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The simulator was originally developed within Toshiba R&D and is currently developed and maintained by the organization.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: It makes money through commercial software licenses and customized engineering solutions including model creation, specialized plugin development, and personalized training sessions.
Scale and maturity: A mature software provider that has achieved widespread adoption in academia and industry, highlighted by a flagship publication that became the most-cited paper in its leading conference proceedings for a multi-year period.
Geography: It is based and operates in Switzerland.
Beyond physical AI: It is a pure-play software entity whose entire business is focused on robotics simulation technology.

points.name: Parallel Domain
points.description: US software company generating synthetic data and sensor simulations for testing autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a synthetic data and sensor simulation platform for autonomous systems. It generates photorealistic digital replicas from real-world capture data to train and validate perception models, serving developers of autonomous vehicles, drones, and robotics.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation platform and synthetic data products robotics and autonomy engineers use.
2. A reconstruction pipeline that converts real-world sensor logs into high-fidelity digital environments, generating deterministic camera, lidar, and radar simulations for autonomy stacks.
3. Synthetic training data for perception systems, sim-to-real gap reporting for validation, and API-based integration for closed-loop and open-loop testing in CI/CD pipelines.
4. Cloud APIs and simulation software that plug into existing autonomy stacks.
5. Autonomous vehicles, drones, eVTOL aircraft, and warehouse automation.
6. Automakers, automotive suppliers, and robotics developers.
7. Its simulation and synthetic data tools are used by developers to build and validate their own perception and autonomy stacks.
8. The reconstruction-based simulation approach anchors testing in real data while remaining controllable and scalable, bridging the gap between rigid log replay and fully generated video.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Google, Continental, Woven Planet, and Toyota Research Institute are customers, and it uses NVIDIA Omniverse in its reconstruction pipeline.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, subscriptions, and synthetic data generation services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, with 51 to 200 employees and $30 million in Series B funding.
Geography: Based in San Francisco, Vancouver, and Karlsruhe.
Beyond physical AI: Providing physical AI simulation and synthetic data is the entire focus and business of the company.

points.name: Cognata
points.description: Israeli software company creating photorealistic virtual environments for training and testing autonomous vehicle AI.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a cloud-based simulation platform for testing, training, and validating autonomous vehicle and physical AI systems using digital twins and synthetic data.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation platform robotics and autonomous vehicle engineers use.
2. The platform combines deep learning, computer vision, supervised generative AI, and high-fidelity 3D rendering with precision vehicle physics simulation to generate photorealistic driving scenarios and sensor inputs.
3. It delivers synthetic training data, automatic labeling, safety-critical scenario generation, and off-road terrain simulation for perception and control validation.
4. Customers get the simulation software through cloud-based platforms and digital twin environments.
5. The platform is used for autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, defense ground vehicles, agriculture, mining, warehouses, and smart cities.
6. Customers include automotive OEMs, defense agencies, militaries, and agriculture technology developers.
7. Its simulation software is used by automotive and defense developers to validate algorithms and train autonomy stacks before physical deployment.
8. Its approach uses real-to-real AI technology to transform high-resolution datasets into new sensor inputs, allowing previously collected video data to test cameras in new optical paths.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include ZF Group, LeddarTech, AgJunction, Israel Aerospace Industries, the Israeli Ministry of Defense, and the Israeli Innovation Authority.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: The organization makes money through software licenses and subscriptions for its simulation platform.
Scale and maturity: The company is a mature, established provider with significant industry partnerships and prestigious award recognitions.
Geography: It is based in Israel and conducts local smart city pilot projects while serving international automotive partners.
Beyond physical AI: Developing cloud-based simulation platforms for autonomous systems is the company's entire focus and core business activity.

points.name: Foretellix
points.description: Israeli software company providing simulation platforms to verify the safety of autonomous vehicles.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a safety-focused verification and validation simulation platform for autonomous driving systems. It licenses its toolchain to automakers and autonomous vehicle developers to test ADAS and self-driving software against regulatory requirements in virtual environments.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation and verification platform autonomous driving engineers use.
2. Scenario-based verification and validation software that uses GPU physics simulation and world foundation models to simulate traffic scenarios, weather conditions and pedestrian behaviors.
3. Safety-focused scenario generation, virtual environment simulation and regulatory validation for autonomous driving systems.
4. Licensed software and simulation tools used by autonomous vehicle developers.
5. Autonomous vehicles, ADAS and self-driving systems.
6. Automakers, autonomous vehicle developers and autonomous trucking companies.
7. Its simulation tools are used by autonomous vehicle developers to verify and validate their self-driving stacks.
8. It specializes in safety-focused, scenario-based verification and validation designed to ensure systems meet regulatory requirements.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Torc and Woven Capital.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Geography: Based in Israel.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on edge and physical AI verification and validation tooling.

points.name: Mujin
points.description: Japanese robotics software company developing platform intelligence for autonomous industrial robots.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds a no-code physical AI operating system and fleet management software for industrial robotics, supplying perception, motion planning, and orchestration for warehouse and manufacturing automation.
1. A developer tools and platform company whose robotics control OS and controllers run on third-party industrial robots.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software, real-time deterministic motion planning algorithms, and fleet orchestration middleware running on industrial-grade controllers.
3. Autonomous perception, real-time motion planning, dynamic fleet orchestration, random bin picking, mixed-SKU palletizing and depalletizing, and automated guided vehicle coordination.
4. Licensed software, industrial controllers, operator pendants, and subscription services for its robotics operating system.
5. Warehouses, manufacturing facilities, distribution centers, and industrial automation cells.
6. Logistics operators, manufacturers, retail and grocery distributors, and industrial robotics integrators.
7. Its software platform and controllers are integrated with industrial robot arms and mobile robots from multiple hardware vendors to automate production and logistics operations.
8. A vendor-agnostic approach that dynamically orchestrates diverse third-party industrial robots without pre-programming through a unified no-code platform.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Kawasaki, FANUC, Yaskawa, Geek+, Schmalz, and SICK.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software subscriptions, controller and pendant hardware sales, and licensed robotics applications.
Scale and maturity: Powers over 2,000 deployed robots worldwide, leveraging motion planning algorithms developed over 15 years.
Geography: Headquartered in Japan with operations in the United States, Europe, and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Developing intelligent software for physical automation is the company's entire focus.

points.name: Realtime Robotics
points.description: US startup building motion planning software that enables industrial robots to operate efficiently in dynamic, unstructured environments.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and component company that builds hardware-accelerated motion planning software and specialized processors for industrial robots and autonomous vehicles. It licenses collision-free motion planning and multi-robot coordination software, and sells FPGA-based planning processors, to manufacturers and robotics companies for use in dynamic, unstructured environments.
1. A developer tools and component company that designs hardware-accelerated motion planning software and FPGA-based processors, sold as licensed software suites, cloud services, and hardware modules.
2. FPGA-based motion planning processors and software algorithms that generate collision-free paths in microseconds.
3. Real-time collision-free motion planning, multi-robot coordination, dynamic obstacle avoidance, and cycle-time optimization.
4. Licensed software, cloud-based optimization services, and hardware processors.
5. Industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots, and manufacturing automation.
6. Manufacturers, robotics companies, and engineering firms.
7. Its software and processors are integrated into robotic systems and manufacturing simulations by industrial conglomerates.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Siemens, Mitsubishi, and BotBuilt.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, cloud subscriptions, and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016 and originated from Duke University research.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates within the broader global industrial automation ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Physical artificial intelligence and edge automation are its entire focus.

points.name: XYZ Robotics Inc.
points.description: South Korean AI robotics startup deploying autonomous service robots and robot-operated café franchises.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and operator that builds semi-humanoid robots, robot barista solutions and autonomous delivery robots, develops its own robot intelligence models and teleoperation data-gathering hardware, and runs its own robot-operated retail locations to collect physical AI training data.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete semi-humanoid and service robots and develops robot intelligence models that run on its own machines.
2. Embodied behavior models trained on real-world teleoperation and service data inside a digital twin simulation environment, integrated into semi-humanoid robot hardware with multi-sensory perception.
3. On-device intelligence for shelf organizing, goods transport, cleaning, food and beverage preparation, and autonomous delivery.
4. Complete robots, robotic café solutions, autonomous delivery robots, motion-capture data-gloves for external sale, and robot-operated retail locations.
5. Retail cafés, warehouses, hospitals, offices and homes.
6. Warehouse operators, retailers, food and beverage operators and developers of embodied AI.
7. It builds its own robots and intelligence models, runs its own retail locations to gather training data, and installs its warehouse robots at customer sites.
8. It operates a closed-loop Physical AI Data Flywheel that gathers daily real-world data from its own commercial robot deployments to train and verify improved on-device intelligence in a digital twin.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with NVIDIA on a physical AI training program and with a warehouse retailer for goods receiving automation.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and motion-capture gloves, food and beverage sales from its robot-operated cafés and warehouse automation deployments.
Scale and maturity: A Series B startup with approximately 27 billion KRW in total funding that has fulfilled over one million robot-prepared food and beverage orders.
Geography: Based in Seoul, South Korea with operations expanded into Japan and Singapore.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, robotics and physical automation are the entire focus and central mission of its business strategy.

points.name: LoungeX
points.description: South Korean retail subsidiary operating robotic cafés that gather real-world interaction data to train physical AI models.
points.bullets:
An operator of robotic cafés that functions as a physical AI data collection hub. It runs beverage automation storefronts that combine on-device inference for drink preparation with algorithmic control of physical manipulation and brewing parameters, serving the food service and hospitality sectors while feeding real-world operational data into a closed-loop pipeline for model training and simulation.
1. An operator that runs robotic café locations and franchises a robot-transformation model, deploying robotic baristas it obtains from its parent robotics organization.
2. Robotic baristas programmed with variable drip algorithms that adjust pour pattern, flow rate and brewing duration based on coffee bean characteristics, combined with on-device inference for drink preparation and physical manipulation control.
3. Robotic drink preparation, variable drip brewing, physical manipulation, and high-volume real-world data generation for model training and field verification.
4. Operated cafés and franchise locations, plus a franchise model based on robot transformation that reduces required staff hours.
5. Cafés, food service, hospitality, government buildings, automotive manufacturers and corporate food service providers.
6. Institutional customers in food service and hospitality, including government buildings, automotive manufacturers and corporate food service providers, plus franchise operators.
7. It operates storefronts as deployed physical systems that generate thousands of daily data points feeding its parent company's robot intelligence engine.
8. Its commercial storefronts function as scalable testbeds creating a physical AI data flywheel that continuously trains and refines its parent company's proprietary robot intelligence.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of XYZ Robotics, backed by venture capital firms in a recent $8.73 million Series B round, with its parent organization holding strategic partnerships with global AI computing leaders and government technology ministries.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary.
Business model: Café operations, beverage sales and franchise fees, while generating data for its parent company's physical AI development.
Scale and maturity: An emerging enterprise that has logged over 10,000 hours of continuous robotic operation and collects over 3,000 real-world data points daily, backed by a recent $8.73 million Series B round.
Geography: Based in Seoul, South Korea, operating its robotic café deployments domestically.
Beyond physical AI: Deploying automated café systems and capturing operational data for physical AI training represents its entire operational focus.

points.name: Seoul Business Agency
points.description: South Korean government agency funding real-world testing and commercialization for Seoul-based robotics and edge AI startups.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and administers programs to help local startups commercialize physical AI, robotics, and autonomous systems. It provides grants, proof-of-concept funding, and real-world urban testbeds to move technologies from R&D into deployment. The agency acts as a facilitator and funding intermediary rather than building hardware or software itself.
1. A government agency that funds and administers commercialization programs for physical AI and robotics startups.
2. The agency administers municipal testbed infrastructure and grant programs that allocate public funding to AI-convergent and robotics technologies.
3. It delivers proof-of-concept funding, real-world urban testing infrastructure, mentoring, and public procurement registration for emerging technology firms.
4. Startups receive financial grants, administrative support, pilot program facilitation, and official validation certificates through municipal programs.
5. The supported technologies are deployed in urban environments, public nursing homes, and construction sites.
6. Its beneficiaries are Seoul-based startups and companies developing physical automation, agentic AI, and robotics technologies.
7. It sits outside the technical value chain, using public funds to support the post-R&D demonstration and commercialization phases of robotics companies.
8. It provides official technology validation certificates signed by the city's mayor alongside comprehensive follow-up services like public procurement registration and global exhibition facilitation.
points.profile:
Organization type: A small business support organization and government agency under the Seoul Metropolitan Government.
Business model: It operates through public funding allocation, distributing grants and running municipal innovation programs.
Scale and maturity: Launched in 2018, the program is well-established and has supported 206 projects with a total of ₩68.3 billion in funding.
Geography: It is based in Seoul, South Korea, and operates urban testbeds within the city while expanding international partnerships for local companies.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is on supporting the growth of local businesses and startups through commercialization assistance and public funding.

points.name: Fujitsu
points.description: Japanese technology and IT services company building collaborative control platforms for autonomous industrial robots using large language models and simulation environments.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded information and communications technology company that builds edge AI software and collaborative control platforms, integrating visual intelligence with industrial robots and enterprise systems. It develops integration infrastructure that unifies AI model development and simulation-to-real workflows for robot makers, alongside custom deep learning silicon for inference.
1. A developer tools company that builds a collaborative control platform and edge AI software for robotic systems, sold as licensed software and integration services.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software, visual intelligence for image processing, and custom deep learning units built with proprietary instruction sets for edge inference.
3. Intelligent image processing and data extraction at the edge, automated visual inspection, and unified simulation-to-real robot learning across heterogeneous industrial systems.
4. Licensed software platforms, edge AI models running on customer devices, and systems integration services.
5. Factories, warehouses, healthcare facilities, and enterprise edge environments using industrial robots and cameras.
6. Industrial robot manufacturers, automotive companies, logistics operators, and healthcare providers.
7. It integrates robot makers and enterprise platforms into a unified control infrastructure that bridges digital systems with physical automation.
8. Its sovereign collaborative control platform bridges legacy industrial automation with modern physical AI and simulation workflows across multiple major robot manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Carnegie Mellon University, FANUC, Yaskawa Electric, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Nutanix, and SAP.
Organization type: Publicly traded, established global information and communications technology conglomerate.
Business model: Software licenses, systems integration contracts, and enterprise IT services.
Scale and maturity: A mature, large-scale multinational corporation with a long-standing global presence and significant industrial deployments.
Geography: Based in Japan and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: The broader organization offers comprehensive IT services, telecommunications, enterprise software, and computing hardware solutions.

points.name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries
points.description: Japanese manufacturing conglomerate building and deploying autonomous robotic systems for industrial and healthcare applications.
points.bullets:
A diversified industrial manufacturer and robot maker that builds industrial robots, surgical systems, hospital transport robots, and humanoid platforms, applying edge AI across manufacturing, healthcare, shipbuilding, and energy.
1. A robot and heavy-equipment maker that builds industrial robotic arms, surgical robots, mobile platforms, and humanoid prototypes for factory, medical, and heavy-industry use.
2. Industrial robotics, multi-axis actuators, vision and sensing systems, and physical AI inference platforms integrated into autonomous and teleoperated machines.
3. Surgical assistance, hospital transport, nursing support, parts assembly, logistics handling, heavy-duty machinery operation, and digital shipyard automation.
4. Complete robots, robotic systems, industrial machinery, and integrated automation platforms.
5. Factory floors, semiconductor fabrication lines, hospitals, elder-care facilities, shipyards, mines, and aerospace plants.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, semiconductor equipment makers, hospitals, defense forces, and energy companies.
7. Its robots are installed by industrial manufacturers, hospitals, and heavy-industry operators.
8. It combines a half-century legacy of industrial robotics with edge AI to develop end-to-end physical automation for heavy industry, shipbuilding, healthcare, and manufacturing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with NVIDIA on physical AI, Fujitsu on a collaborative control platform, and Sysmex through the Medicaroid joint venture, and is a customer of Neura Robotics.
Organization type: A publicly traded industrial conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales, robotics systems sales, industrial equipment contracts, and maintenance services.
Scale and maturity: A multinational company with over 50 years of robotics experience and significant global market share in semiconductor-manufacturing robots.
Geography: Based in Japan with a Physical AI Center in Silicon Valley and global operations across heavy industry and manufacturing.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond robotics, it is a diversified industrial powerhouse operating in aerospace, shipbuilding, energy, plant engineering, and motorcycles.

points.name: Hitachi
points.description: Japanese industrial technology and infrastructure company integrating real-time edge AI into physical systems for railways, energy, manufacturing, and buildings.
points.bullets:
A multinational industrial conglomerate that acts as a systems integrator and platform provider, deploying edge AI semiconductors, sensor-fusion software, and multi-agent orchestration platforms to automate critical social and industrial infrastructure for operators and manufacturers.
1. A systems integrator that builds and installs edge AI hardware and orchestration software for physical AI applications, delivered as integrated infrastructure solutions.
2. Edge AI semiconductors with high-density circuitry for low-power processing and sensor fusion, integrated with multi-agent orchestration platforms built on GPU reference architectures and physical AI world models.
3. Real-time on-site inference of diverse sensor data including images, sounds and vibrations, equipment failure diagnostics, multi-factor biometric authentication, and autonomous control of operational environments.
4. Edge AI semiconductors, AI infrastructure, and multi-agent orchestration platforms deployed as integrated solutions and AI agent services for industrial equipment.
5. Smart buildings, rail infrastructure, factories, logistics operations, energy grids, manufacturing sites, railway ticket gates, and in-store payment terminals.
6. Railway operators, renewable energy providers, industrial manufacturers, logistics operators, and building operators.
7. It designs edge AI semiconductors and orchestration platforms, integrating them with third-party edge accelerators and legacy equipment to operate deployed physical AI systems.
8. Its vendor-agnostic platform combines over a century of operational technology heritage with advanced AI orchestration to reduce train maintenance costs and shrink equipment diagnostic times to seconds.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with NVIDIA, Oracle, Microsoft, GlobalLogic, Daikin, and Mitsubishi Chemical.
Organization type: A publicly traded multinational conglomerate.
Business model: Integrated solution contracts, AI infrastructure sales, software subscriptions, and digital engineering services.
Scale and maturity: A global enterprise with approximately 280,000 employees, 618 consolidated subsidiaries, and consolidated revenues of 9,783.3 billion yen for fiscal year 2024.
Geography: Based in Japan with active deployments and strategic partnerships spanning multiple continents including Europe and Asia.

points.name: Shimizu Corporation
points.description: Japanese construction company deploying AI vision systems for worker safety monitoring and developing humanoid robots for building sites.
points.bullets:
A construction company and systems integrator that develops and deploys specialized construction robots and AI-powered site monitoring systems for building projects. It builds autonomous welding and material transport robots for high-rise construction sites and uses computer vision platforms for construction worker safety monitoring.
1. A construction company and systems integrator that builds autonomous welding and material transport robots and installs AI-powered safety monitoring systems for construction sites.
2. Autonomous welding systems, material transport robots, and AI-powered computer vision for construction worker safety monitoring.
3. Autonomous welding, material transport, and construction worker safety monitoring.
4. Complete robots and integration services.
5. High-rise construction sites and construction worker safety monitoring.
6. Construction companies and general contractors.
7. It builds and operates robots and AI monitoring systems for its own construction projects.
8. It integrates physical AI directly into the workflow of large-scale construction projects as a general contractor.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA.
Organization type: A publicly traded construction company.

points.name: AWL
points.description: Japanese industrial and retail technology company embedding on-device video analytics and perception into automated physical workflows.

A systems integrator that builds retail and manufacturing solutions by embedding edge AI video analytics and perception software into physical automation workflows for intralogistics.
1. A systems integrator that designs and installs edge AI and robotics solutions built from other companies' hardware and models.
2. On-device video analytics and perception software built on NVIDIA DeepStream and Jetson-class hardware, integrated with third-party AI models for mobile manipulation.
3. Operational intelligence, real-time decision-making, and sensor-driven perception for physical workflows.
4. Integration services and deployed systems that combine edge AI software with physical automation hardware.
5. Retail, manufacturing, factories, and warehouses.
6. Retail and manufacturing operators requiring sensor-driven perception for physical workflows.
7. It integrates third-party AI models and robotic hardware into deployed physical workflows for end users.
8. It acts as a platform-level integrator with a 30-year heritage in robot integration rather than a component supplier.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Sereact, SiMa.ai, and Tesollo.
Organization type: Privately held company with origins as a certified startup from Hokkaido University.
Business model: Contracts and integration services for deployed physical automation systems.

points.name: Mitsubishi Electric
points.description: Japanese industrial conglomerate building intelligent factory robots and embedding AI directly into manufacturing equipment for real-time automation.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded industrial conglomerate and component supplier that designs and builds factory automation equipment, industrial robots, and edge AI control systems for manufacturers. It integrates AI algorithms directly into servo drives, programmable logic controllers, and vision systems for real-time, on-device automation, and also distributes last-mile delivery robots.
1. A component supplier and robot maker that builds servo motors, programmable logic controllers, variable frequency drives, and industrial robot arms sold to manufacturers.
2. Neural networks and AI algorithms embedded directly into the firmware of low-power industrial controllers, servo drives, and CNC systems for on-device inference.
3. On-device inference for predictive maintenance, real-time production line optimization, anomaly detection, collaborative robot kinematics, and precise motion control.
4. Components, industrial robots, control systems, and licensed factory automation software sold to equipment builders and factory operators.
5. Factories, warehouses, manufacturing lines, food and beverage processing, pharmaceutical production, and automotive assembly.
6. Manufacturers, factory operators, machine builders, logistics operators, and mall operators.
7. Its components and control systems are designed into factory automation lines and robotic cells by machine builders, and it distributes third-party robots for last-mile logistics.
8. It embeds compact AI directly into individual factory automation components like drives and servos for edge processing without relying on the cloud, rather than offering standalone AI modules.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Cartken, Tulip, Renault Group, Google, and a joint venture with Advanced Vision Solutions.
Organization type: Publicly traded industrial conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware and component sales, software licenses, and distribution agreements.
