points.name: Murata Manufacturing
points.description: Japanese electronic components manufacturer supplying sensors and core technologies for physical AI hardware.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that makes electronic components and sensors for edge and physical AI devices, selling parts to device makers and participating in broader AI hardware supply chains.
1. An electronic components manufacturer that builds sensors and other core components sold into other companies' machines.
2. Electronic components and sensors built for integration into AI hardware and edge devices.
3. Sensing and core electronic functions for edge AI hardware supply chains.
4. Components and sensors sold to device makers for integration into their products.
5. Edge and physical AI devices and hardware built by other manufacturers.
6. Device makers, AI hardware supply chain participants and semiconductor consortia.
7. Its components and sensors are designed into edge and physical AI devices built by other manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA and the KyoHA consortium.
Organization type: A publicly traded electronic components manufacturer.
Business model: Component and sensor sales to device makers.
Geography: Based in Japan and participating in global AI hardware supply chains.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI it is a broad electronic components manufacturer supplying a wide range of industries.

points.name: Panasonic
points.description: Japanese technology company manufacturing smart security cameras with built-in AI for on-device video analytics.
points.bullets:
A diversified electronics and component manufacturer that builds edge AI cameras, industrial welding robots, robot gearboxes and motors, AI chips, and solid-state batteries for drones. It acts as a hardware supplier and complete solutions provider for smart factories, physical security, and automotive applications. The organization serves industrial manufacturers, automakers, and security operators with physical automation components and integrated edge AI systems.
1. A component and systems supplier that makes industrial robots, precision gearboxes, edge AI cameras, inference chips, and drone batteries, sold as hardware components, complete machines, and integrated factory systems.
2. In-memory computing chips, memristor arrays, PTZ camera optics, harmonic gearboxes, industrial welding robot arms, and solid-state battery cells.
3. On-device video analytics, robotic arc welding, automated parts feeding, precision motion control, long-range drone power, and SMT production line traceability.
4. Components, complete robotic welding systems, smart cameras, manufacturing software, and fully integrated factory automation lines.
5. Factories, security networks, smart cities, transport hubs, drones, and electric vehicles.
6. Automotive manufacturers, electronics manufacturers, logistics operators, security operators, and drone makers.
7. Its components are designed into robots, drones, and vehicles by machine makers, and its complete robotic systems are installed directly into factory production lines.
8. It combines long-standing hardware manufacturing expertise with an open-systems approach that integrates specialized third-party AI software into its physical edge platforms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Tesla, thyssenkrupp Bilstein, ZF Automotive, NVIDIA, A.I. Tech, and Huiling Technology.
Organization type: A publicly traded multinational conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales, component sales, software licenses, and systems integration services.
Scale and maturity: A century-old global corporation with diverse business units and widespread international factory deployments.
Geography: Based in Japan with a global manufacturing and operational footprint.
Beyond physical AI: The broader corporate entity produces a wide array of consumer electronics, home appliances, avionics, and advanced industrial materials.

points.name: TDK Corporation
points.description: Japanese electronics company developing power-efficient neuromorphic computing components and sensors for robotics.
points.bullets:
An electronics component supplier that builds high-performance sensors and neuromorphic computing memristors for autonomous navigation and on-device AI. It develops physical components and memory technology used by chip platforms and robotics systems to reduce power consumption and provide perception data.
1. A component supplier that makes high-performance sensors and spin-memristors for edge AI and neuromorphic computing.
2. Solid-state sensors for autonomous navigation and spin-memristor devices designed to mimic synaptic behavior for neuromorphic computing.
3. High-performance sensing for autonomous navigation and low-power neuromorphic computing for on-device AI inference.
4. Electronic components and sensors designed into robotics platforms and edge AI hardware.
5. Autonomous navigation, robotics platforms, and low-power edge AI systems.
6. Chip platform providers, robotics system makers, and electronics manufacturers.
7. Its components are designed into robotics platforms and edge AI hardware built by device and chip makers.
8. It develops spin-memristor technology claiming a 99% reduction in AI power consumption for neuromorphic computing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA and Qualcomm.
Organization type: A publicly traded electronics components company.
Business model: Component and sensor sales to electronics and robotics manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A major global electronics supplier founded in 1935 and based in Japan.
Geography: Based in Japan with global operations.
Beyond physical AI: A broad electronics components company that also produces batteries, power supplies, magnetic heads, and other passive electronic components.

points.name: University of Toronto
points.description: Canadian university developing robotic lab assistants and open-source surgical robot training frameworks.
points.bullets:
A university research institution that conducts edge and physical AI research, building robotic assistants for automated chemistry and open-source simulation frameworks for training surgical robots. It operates research labs and partners with robotics component suppliers to study AI-based manipulation, reinforcement learning, teleoperation, and humanoid robotics. The institution collaborates with industry partners on GPU-driven workflows and serves as an academic hub for AI founders and researchers.
1. A university lab that builds research prototypes like robotic assistants and open-source simulation frameworks, and operates them for academic study.
2. Robotic manipulation systems using reinforcement learning, teleoperation, GPU-driven simulation, and AI-based chemistry workflows.
3. Automated chemistry experimentation, surgical robot training through open-source simulation, AI-based manipulation, and teleoperation research.
4. Open-source simulation frameworks and experimental robotic systems developed and operated for academic research.
5. Chemistry laboratories, surgical robotics research, humanoid robotics research, and manipulation research.
6. Academic researchers, surgical robotics engineers, and students.
7. Its research platforms and tools are used directly by its own labs and shared with the broader academic community.
8. It integrates supplied robotic hardware into advanced AI research to build open-source frameworks and automated experimental systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Franka Robotics, Tesollo, and Waabi.
Organization type: A public university and academic research institution.
Business model: Academic research funded through grants, institutional budgets, and industry collaborations.
Scale and maturity: A major Canadian university with multiple research labs and established industry collaborations.
Geography: Based in Toronto, Canada.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it is a comprehensive university active in quantum chemistry, AI theory, and broad academic disciplines.

points.name: Gorilla Technology Group
points.description: Technology company providing edge AI appliances for real-time video analytics and on-device inference.
points.bullets:
An edge AI solutions provider and systems integrator that builds on-device video analytics appliances for enterprises and governments, combining third-party AI silicon and industrial hardware.
1. An AI solutions company that designs edge video analytics appliances and software and sells them as integrated hardware-software systems.
2. Real-time video analytics software running on edge computing appliances powered by third-party neural processing units.
3. On-device inference and real-time video analytics processing across multiple camera channels.
4. Edge AI appliances preloaded with video analytics software, delivered as complete integrated systems to end users.
5. Smart cities, retail, enterprise security, transportation, healthcare and education.
6. Governments and enterprises.
7. It integrates third-party AI silicon and industrial computing hardware into finished edge analytics appliances for end users.
8. It delivers decentralized, privacy-focused on-device processing without cloud connectivity at a high price-to-performance ratio through integration rather than underlying component development.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Hardware platforms from Lanner and AI processors from Hailo.
Organization type: Publicly traded technology company.
Business model: Hardware appliance sales and software licensing.
Scale and maturity: An established provider with over two decades of industry experience.
Geography: Headquartered in London and operating across multiple global sectors.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, intelligent video analytics and IoT technologies represent the company's entire focus.

points.name: Edge Impulse
points.description: United States development platform helping engineers build and deploy machine learning models directly onto edge hardware.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides an end-to-end MLOps platform for building, training, optimizing, and deploying machine learning models on physical edge devices, serving embedded engineering teams across industrial and consumer sectors.
1. A developer tools company whose embedded ML platform engineers use to build TinyML applications for microcontrollers and edge devices.
2. Cloud-based development environment with low-code and no-code workflows, automated optimization, and embedded machine learning algorithms like the FOMO object detection network.
3. Dataset collection, model training, optimization, on-device inference, anomaly detection, object detection, predictive maintenance, and production model monitoring.
4. Licensed software, cloud APIs, platform-as-a-service, C++ SDKs, and Arduino libraries that run on customers' edge hardware.
5. Industrial IoT devices, wearables, hearables, smart manufacturing, consumer electronics, and automotive systems.
6. Embedded engineers, hardware makers, industrial IoT operators, consumer electronics manufacturers, and developers.
7. Its development platform is used by device makers and engineers to build and deploy AI models onto inference silicon from other companies.
8. Democratizes edge AI development by enabling domain experts without specialized machine learning knowledge to create production-grade models using low-code and no-code workflows.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Qualcomm, NVIDIA, Arduino, Silicon Labs, BrainChip, Ambiq, Alif Semiconductor, Eta Compute, Arm, AWS, HP Poly, and Advantech.
Organization type: Privately held startup acquired as a subsidiary.
Business model: Software licenses, platform-as-a-service subscriptions, and solutions engineering services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019 with a global developer community of over 160,000 developers.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California, USA, with a global developer base.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: U.S. Department of Transportation
points.description: US government agency funding and regulating the safe deployment of autonomous vehicles, drones, and intelligent transportation systems.
points.bullets:
A government agency that regulates, funds and coordinates the integration of edge and physical AI into national transportation, setting safety standards for autonomous vehicles and aircraft while supporting robotics research for highway mobility. The agency develops policy frameworks that govern the commercial deployment of automated driving systems, manages testing exemptions for non-compliant autonomous vehicles, and oversees the modernization of air traffic control for advanced air mobility. It serves automakers, autonomous vehicle operators, state and city agencies and the general public by accelerating the safe fielding of on-device inference, edge sensors and autonomous mobility.
1. A government agency that develops federal safety standards and policy frameworks for autonomous vehicles and advanced air mobility, and funds transportation robotics research, rather than building hardware or software itself.
2. Federal regulatory frameworks, performance-based safety standards, testing exemptions and research grants that govern how automated driving systems, edge sensors and autonomous aircraft are deployed.
3. Standardization of autonomous vehicle safety, streamlined testing exemptions for ADS-equipped vehicles, coordination of automated vehicle policy across modal administrations, and funding of robotics research for transportation safety and mobility.
4. Regulatory frameworks, safety standards, policy guidance, deployment exemptions and research grants issued to automakers, operators, state agencies and research institutions.
5. Autonomous passenger vehicles, autonomous commercial motor vehicles, advanced air mobility, air traffic control, traffic management and highway safety systems.
6. Automakers, autonomous vehicle operators, commercial motor vehicle operators, aviation operators, state and city transportation agencies, robotics researchers and the general public.
7. Its standards and policies govern the testing, deployment and commercial operation of autonomous vehicles and aircraft built and run by automakers, operators and technology vendors.
8. It holds unique federal authority to standardize physical AI deployments, grant testing exemptions, fund infrastructure transitions and maintain public safety while accelerating transportation innovation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Houses the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the Federal Aviation Administration, the Federal Highway Administration, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration and the Volpe research center, and partners with Mcity and the National Science Foundation on the NRI-3.0 robotics program.
Organization type: A cabinet-level federal department of the United States government.
Business model: Federal funding and regulatory operations funded by congressional appropriations.
Scale and maturity: A long-established, cabinet-level federal department operating at a massive national scale across all fifty states, with divisions overseeing millions of motor vehicles and the entire national airspace.
Geography: Based and operating entirely within the United States, directing nationwide deployments across states and municipalities.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge AI and physical automation, the broader entity manages all aspects of national transportation policy, infrastructure funding, economic growth and safety regulation across ground, air and marine modes.

points.name: European Commission
points.description: European government agency funding physical AI research and coordinating sovereign computing infrastructure for edge and robotics innovation.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds, regulates and coordinates edge and physical AI innovation across Europe. It finances semiconductor design, robotics research and testing facilities, and sets the legislative framework for AI-enabled machinery and autonomous systems. The agency acts as the public counterpart in public-private partnerships to align research, industrial deployment and infrastructure development for automakers, robot makers and manufacturers.
1. A government agency that funds robotics, edge AI and autonomy research programs and operates regulatory regimes for physical AI systems.
2. Grant funding instruments, regulatory frameworks, conformity assessments and supercomputing facilities dedicated to AI model training and semiconductor development.
3. Research coordination, regulatory compliance for high-risk AI systems, semiconductor design support and physical robot testing infrastructure.
4. Government grants, public procurement contracts, regulatory frameworks, testing facilities and co-financed infrastructure programs.
5. Autonomous vehicles, hospital robots, agricultural robots, exoskeletons, space semiconductors and industrial automation systems.
6. Research institutions, robot makers, automakers, semiconductor developers, logistics operators, hospitals, farmers, and small and medium-sized enterprises.
7. It sits at the top of the value chain, funding and regulating the developers, manufacturers and integrators that build edge AI chips, robots and autonomy software.
8. It combines a continental regulatory mandate over AI and machinery safety with direct funding of physical AI research and AI Gigafactory infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: euRobotics, the European Investment Bank, the Big Data Value Association and the ADRA association.
Organization type: A supranational government agency and the executive body of the European Union.
Business model: Public funding allocation, grant management, public procurement and regulatory enforcement.
Scale and maturity: A large, established governing institution managing a continental portfolio of over 200 AI services and numerous funding programs across multiple member states.
Geography: Based in Brussels, Belgium, operating across all European Union member states.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, it manages general technology policy, digital sovereignty, migration, counter-terrorism and comprehensive regulatory enforcement across the European internal market.

points.name: U.S. Department of Energy
points.description: US government agency advancing autonomous laboratory robotics and physical AI for scientific discovery and national security.
points.bullets:
A federal government agency that funds, coordinates, and operates physical AI and automation initiatives across the U.S. energy and science enterprise, deploying autonomous laboratories and edge AI infrastructure for national laboratories and universities.
1. A government agency that funds robotics and physical AI programs, operates scientific cloud infrastructure for hosting AI models, and sets standards for battery and technology adoption readiness.
2. Autonomous laboratory platforms, self-improving AI models hosted on a scientific cloud, edge AI systems spanning inference silicon and sensors, and frameworks for evaluating advanced architectures.
3. Autonomous experimentation, automated catalyst discovery, robotic synthesis, AI model hosting and distribution for scientific research, and rigorous testing of software porting for advanced architectures.
4. Research grants and funding awards to universities and laboratories, federal prize competitions, and a cloud platform that distributes scientific data and AI models to the research community.
5. Autonomous laboratories, advanced manufacturing, EV technology, solar energy deployment, and scientific experimentation in chemistry and materials science.
6. National laboratories, universities, scientific research organizations, and domestic robotics and energy technology developers.
7. It funds and operates upstream research and infrastructure that feeds physical AI into scientific and industrial deployments by universities and national labs.
8. Access to world-class supercomputing resources, unique scientific datasets from experimental user facilities, and an extensive national laboratory infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Carnegie Mellon University, University of Wisconsin-Madison, Ames National Laboratory, North Carolina State University, ARPA-E, Manufacturing USA institutes, Cosmic Robotics, BrainChip Holdings, Quantum Ventura.
Organization type: A cabinet-level department of the United States federal government.
Business model: Federal funding, research grants, and prize competitions appropriated to external researchers and national laboratories.
Scale and maturity: A long-established federal institution that has committed over $320 million to AI and robotics initiatives, including recent awards of $34 million for autonomous labs and $9 million for EV technology.
Geography: Based in the United States, operating across federal facilities, national laboratories, and university partnerships nationwide.
Beyond physical AI: The broader mandate encompasses national energy policy, energy production, nuclear safety, and foundational scientific discovery.

points.name: Graphcore
points.description: United Kingdom technology company developing specialized AI accelerator processors for machine intelligence workloads.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs specialized AI accelerators and integrated server systems for machine learning training and inference, primarily for data center environments. It develops massively parallel processors, rack-scale compute pods, and a dedicated compiler stack for AI workloads. While it sits within the broader AI hardware ecosystem, its technology targets large-scale computing infrastructure rather than on-device edge, robotics, or physical automation deployments.
1. A chip company that designs AI accelerators and server systems for machine learning training and inference.
2. Intelligence processing units built on a bulk synchronous parallel architecture with abundant on-chip SRAM memory, high-performance interconnects, and a dedicated compiler stack.
3. High-throughput AI model training and inference, sparse matrix computation, and dynamic processor provisioning for multi-tenancy.
4. Processors, PCIe cards, rack-scale compute systems, and a software development kit sold directly or through cloud platforms.
5. Data centers and cloud computing infrastructure for natural language processing, image classification, speech recognition, and quantum computing research.
6. Cloud providers, financial institutions, research universities, and technology companies.
7. Its chips and server systems are integrated into data center infrastructure operated by cloud providers and enterprises.
8. Its architecture utilizes a bulk synchronous parallel model with specialized in-processor memory and proprietary networking fabric to provide high density and throughput for irregular and sparse processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SoftBank Group, Dell, Microsoft Azure, Atos, TSMC, and Cirrascale.
Organization type: A wholly owned subsidiary of a publicly traded holding company.
Business model: Hardware sales of processors and compute systems, plus software licenses.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016, valued at nearly $2 billion before being acquired for over $600 million in 2024.
Geography: Based in Bristol, United Kingdom, with operations in Europe and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Developing high-performance AI compute infrastructure is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Mythic
points.description: Canadian semiconductor startup developing analog compute-in-memory chips for power-efficient AI inference at the edge.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that develops analog compute-in-memory processors for power-efficient AI inference at the edge. It supplies specialized inference chips, associated compilers, and model optimization tools for integration into larger deployed systems for original equipment manufacturers and systems integrators.
1. A chip company that designs analog NPUs and accelerator cards for on-device inference.
2. Analog compute-in-memory architecture that stores AI parameters directly in the processor to perform matrix multiplication in analog within memory, eliminating memory bottlenecks.
3. High-performance, low-power on-device AI inference for edge devices and embedded systems.
4. Chips, M.2 and PCIe accelerator cards, and evaluation kits.
5. Robotics, automotive advanced driver-assistance systems, autonomous defense platforms, smart homes, aerospace, and edge servers.
6. Original equipment manufacturers and systems integrators building robots, vehicles, and defense platforms.
7. Its chips and cards are designed into edge devices and embedded systems by hardware manufacturers.
8. Its analog computing architecture achieves up to 100 times better system-level performance-per-watt-per-dollar compared to traditional digital architectures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Honda, Lockheed Martin, DCVC, NEA, Softbank, Future Ventures, and Atreides.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Chip and accelerator card sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2012, raised approximately $165.5 million in total funding including a $125 million round in late 2025.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates in the global edge AI market.
Beyond physical AI: The development and commercialization of analog compute-in-memory AI processors constitutes the organization's entire business focus.

points.name: ADLINK
points.description: Taiwanese technology company manufacturing rugged edge computing hardware for industrial automation and robotics.
points.bullets:
A hardware manufacturer and systems integrator that builds industrial-grade edge AI computing platforms and embedded boards for physical AI applications. It designs computer-on-modules, single-board computers, industrial motherboards, and rugged edge servers that integrate silicon from major acceleration partners for real-time inference and sensor processing in harsh environments.
1. A computing platform company that builds industrial embedded boards and edge AI inference systems, sold as hardware modules and integrated ruggedized computers.
2. Industrial embedded computing hardware incorporating neural processing units from ecosystem silicon partners, engineered for high-bandwidth multi-camera sensing and extreme environment ruggedization.
3. Real-time reasoning AI, sensor processing, machine vision, and AI inspection for autonomous machines and industrial automation.
4. Computer-on-modules, industrial motherboards, single-board computers, and rugged AI edge servers delivered as integrated hardware.
5. General-purpose robots, industrial automation, smart manufacturing, machine vision, medical imaging, transportation, logistics, retail, and defense.
6. Robotics developers, industrial automation operators, manufacturers, medical imaging providers, and defense contractors.
7. Its embedded computers and edge AI platforms are designed into robots, autonomous machines, and industrial systems by device makers and integrators.
8. Industrial-grade ruggedization with shock and vibration certification paired with high-bandwidth multi-camera sensing tailored for harsh physical environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates silicon from AMD, Ampere, Arm, Intel, MediaTek, NVIDIA, NXP, and Qualcomm, and has a joint development agreement with Noble Machines for general-purpose robot autonomy.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of embedded computing modules, boards, and edge AI platforms.
Scale and maturity: A 30-year-old company with over 1,600 global customers and dual manufacturing centers.
Geography: Based in Taiwan with manufacturing facilities in Taipei and Shanghai, serving a global customer base.
Beyond physical AI: The company also operates as an electronics manufacturer that uses digital twin technologies, automated optical inspection, and AI-driven safety systems in its own production lines.

points.name: BrainChip
points.description: Semiconductor company building neuromorphic processors that mimic the brain for low-power edge AI.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs and licenses neuromorphic processors and AI accelerator IP for ultra-low-power edge inference and on-device learning, serving defense, aerospace, industrial IoT and automotive markets.
1. A chip company that designs neuromorphic processors and licenses the IP for integration into other companies' systems-on-chip.
2. A fully digital, event-based neuromorphic architecture using spiking neural networks to perform inference and local learning at extremely low power.
3. Ultra-low-power on-device inference, object detection, radar and RF signal classification, and edge learning local to the chip.
4. Standalone accelerator chips, licensed processor IP integrated into custom SoCs, reference platforms, and cloud-based developer tools.
5. IoT devices, industrial sensors, aerospace systems, defense electronics, automotive systems, smart wearables, and radar.
6. Defense contractors, government agencies, aerospace microprocessor makers, sensor makers, and edge IoT developers.
7. Its processor IP and standalone chips are designed into SoCs and edge devices built by hardware partners.
8. It is the first commercial producer of a fully digital, event-based neuromorphic processor, achieving commercial deployment while competing efforts remained in research.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Prophesee, Frontgrade Gaisler, Edge Impulse, Arm, VVDN, Raytheon, and the Air Force Research Laboratory.
Organization type: A publicly traded commercial semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip and IP licensing sales, hardware sales, and government contracts.
Scale and maturity: Millions of deployed processors globally, with $25 million raised and next-generation volume production planned for 2026.
Geography: Based in Laguna Hills, California, USA, with deployments and partnerships worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Amazon Web Services
points.description: Cloud provider delivering edge computing runtimes and machine learning chips for on-device inference.
points.bullets:
A cloud computing platform that supplies the infrastructure, developer tools, and edge runtimes used to train machine learning models, run simulations, and deploy physical AI systems. The organization provides cloud compute, storage, and orchestration for AI workloads, alongside edge software and agent-to-device libraries for robotics developers. It serves enterprises, startups, and robotics manufacturers building autonomous machines and industrial automation.
1. A developer tools and platform company whose cloud infrastructure and edge runtimes robotics engineers use to train, simulate, and deploy models.
2. Data center GPUs and custom Arm-based CPUs, alongside an edge runtime that manages containerized applications and orchestrates cloud-based simulation.
3. Large-scale distributed model training, robot simulation, fleet management, edge analytics, and device-to-cloud orchestration.
4. Cloud APIs, managed SaaS tools, and licensed edge runtime software running on customer hardware.
5. Autonomous trucking development, drone logistics, warehouse robotics, manufacturing, industrial automation, and satellite operations.
6. Robot makers, autonomous vehicle developers, drone operators, industrial manufacturers, and software developers.
7. Its cloud and edge platforms are used by developers and systems integrators to build, train, and deploy autonomous machines.
8. It provides a vertically integrated cloud-to-edge architecture that combines custom data center silicon with managed robotics simulation and edge orchestration services.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates infrastructure for NVIDIA, integrates with Boston Dynamics, and partners with automakers and robotics startups.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded e-commerce and technology conglomerate.
Business model: Cloud compute and storage subscriptions, managed software services, and startup accelerator programs.
Scale and maturity: A global hyperscale cloud provider generating tens of billions in quarterly revenue and supporting millions of server instances.
Geography: Based in Seattle, Washington, operating global cloud regions and edge networks worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a comprehensive cloud computing provider offering on-demand IT infrastructure, storage, databases, and enterprise software beyond physical AI.

points.name: Imagination Technologies
points.description: British semiconductor IP company designing graphics processors that accelerate edge AI workloads in automotive, robotics, and consumer devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor IP company that designs and licenses GPU, neural network accelerator, and RISC-V CPU cores for system-on-chip integration in edge AI, automotive, and consumer electronics markets.
1. A semiconductor IP company that designs and licenses GPU and AI accelerator cores for on-device inference and compute in system-on-chip designs.
2. Neural processing units within scalable GPU and neural network accelerator IP cores, paired with RISC-V processors, delivering up to 200 TOPS for mixed graphics and compute workloads.
3. On-device inference, parallel compute acceleration, graphics rendering, and functional safety for embedded systems.
4. Licensed semiconductor IP cores integrated by chip designers into custom system-on-chip designs.
5. Advanced driver assistance systems, autonomous driving, industrial automation, robotics, smartphones, and consumer electronics.
6. System-on-chip designers, semiconductor manufacturers, and automotive processor suppliers.
7. Its IP cores are licensed to and integrated by semiconductor companies that build system-on-chips for device makers.
8. It offers programmable and flexible hardware blocks that handle mixed graphics and compute workloads to reduce chip complexity and cost.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: MulticoreWare, Ambarella, Texas Instruments, RISC-V International, and Fortress Investment Group.
Organization type: A privately held semiconductor intellectual property design company.
Business model: Technology licensing fees and royalties from semiconductor manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: An established company founded in 1985 that secured one hundred million dollars in strategic funding.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and operating globally through partnerships with major system-on-chip designers.
Beyond physical AI: It provides broader graphics processing units and general compute solutions for digital applications.

points.name: Latent AI
points.description: US technology startup optimizing and deploying machine learning models directly on physical devices in low-bandwidth and disconnected environments.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides a modular edge AI software platform for optimizing, deploying, and managing machine learning models on diverse physical hardware, primarily for defense applications. It builds MLOps toolchains, edge runtimes, and data-labeling software that compress models for low-latency, disconnected inference on ruggedized devices and autonomous platforms. The organization serves government and commercial customers seeking to run AI on resource-constrained edge devices without cloud dependency.
1. A developer tools company whose edge AI MLOps and deployment platform robotics and defense engineers use.
2. Model compression, compilation, and deployment toolchains for tinyML and edge inference, combined with data annotation and runtime management software for networked-denied environments.
3. Model optimization, on-device inference, ML lifecycle management, automated data annotation, and real-time field-updatable AI on ruggedized hardware.
4. Licensed software platforms, developer tools, and ruggedized edge runtimes delivered as toolchains, plugins, and tactical server or wearable computing form factors.
5. Defense systems, autonomous unmanned platforms, pan-tilt-zoom cameras, mission-critical systems, and orbital space-based platforms.
6. Defense agencies, militaries, defense systems integrators, and commercial developers building ruggedized edge devices.
7. Its software tools are used by defense integrators and device makers to embed optimized AI models into ruggedized edge hardware and autonomous platforms.
8. It provides an end-to-end, hardware-agnostic platform that reduces reliance on cloud computing and GPU infrastructure by automating optimization and deployment across diverse edge devices in disconnected environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Sigma Defense, Abaco Systems, Wind River, Edge AI Foundation, Vertosoft, Booz Allen Ventures, Voyager Technologies, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Navy, U.S. Army.
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses, platform subscriptions, and government contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018, maintains active contracts with U.S. military branches, winner of a U.S. Army technology grand challenge cohort, backed by strategic venture investments.
Geography: Based in the United States, focused on serving American defense agencies and expanding to orbital space platforms.
Beyond physical AI: Delivering artificial intelligence software for ruggedized, physical edge devices constitutes the company's entire focus and core business operations.

points.name: Advantech
points.description: Taiwanese technology company providing edge AI hardware systems for on-device vision processing and real-time industrial analytics.
points.bullets:
A hardware and embedded systems company that builds industrial edge AI computers, autonomous mobile robot controllers, and developer tools for on-device inference, supplying subsystems and complete platforms to machine makers and industrial operators.
1. An embedded systems and computer company that builds rugged industrial PCs, edge AI servers, robot controller boards, and single-board computers for integration into robots, vehicles, and factory systems.
2. Industrial computing hardware integrating processors, GPUs, and neural processing units from multiple silicon vendors, paired with software development kits for simulating and deploying on-device AI models.
3. On-device AI inference, real-time analytics, robotic vision, sensor fusion, and autonomous mobile robot control.
4. Industrial PCs, embedded modules, controller boards, and licensed software sold to equipment manufacturers for integration into complete machines and automation systems.
5. Autonomous mobile robots, industrial cart robots, smart factories, warehouses, intelligent transportation, medical devices, and surveillance.
6. Robot makers, vehicle manufacturers, industrial automation providers, and systems integrators.
7. Its controller boards and edge computers are designed into autonomous mobile robots and industrial automation systems by equipment manufacturers.
8. It combines proprietary rugged hardware platforms with a chip-agnostic software environment that supports deploying AI models across multiple silicon vendors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with silicon and AI companies including NVIDIA, Intel, AMD, Qualcomm, Hailo, DEEPX, Rockchip, Edge Impulse, and Axelera AI.
Organization type: A publicly traded technology company.
Business model: Hardware sales of embedded modules, controller boards, and industrial PCs, plus software licenses and developer tools.
Scale and maturity: A large, established global technology provider with a broad product portfolio and mature deployments across industrial markets.
Geography: Based in Taiwan with global operations spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it builds broader industrial IoT, networking, cloud, and smart retail systems.

points.name: Dell Technologies
points.description: US technology company providing AI-optimized servers and full-stack computing infrastructure for edge deployment.

A systems manufacturer that builds and sells servers, workstations, and storage infrastructure optimized for AI workloads, from edge environments to centralized data centers. It assembles rack-scale systems integrating GPUs and companion chips for enterprise AI, model training, and inference, primarily for large enterprises and AI developers.
1. A systems manufacturer that builds AI-optimized servers and workstations and sells them as complete hardware platforms.
2. Rack-scale server systems and workstations integrating high-density GPUs, liquid cooling, and object storage platforms designed for edge and enterprise AI infrastructure.
3. High-performance compute for large-parameter model training, edge data storage for unstructured data, and orchestration of computer vision workloads.
4. Complete servers, desktop supercomputers, storage appliances, and edge infrastructure software sold to end customers.

The company fuses radio wave-based subsurface scanning with proprietary spatial reconstruction algorithms to generate three-dimensional imagery of metallic and plastic threats. It serves humanitarian demining and post-conflict reconstruction sectors, supplying defense and government bodies with hardware-agnostic subsystems.
1. A sensor maker that builds airborne radar payloads and sensor fusion systems for integration onto commercial drones.
2. Synthetic-aperture radar, aerial ground-penetrating radar operating in the 1–6 GHz range, and proprietary spatial reconstruction algorithms for volumetric imaging.
3. Subsurface 3D perception, buried object detection and categorization, and high-resolution volumetric imaging of both metallic and plastic-cased threats.
4. Lightweight radar sensors and payloads designed as hardware-agnostic modules for commercial unmanned aerial vehicles.
5. Demining operations, post-conflict land clearance, and border-security missions.
6. Governments, international bodies, and defense organizations involved in humanitarian demining.
7. Its sensors are integrated as payloads onto commercial drones operated by demining and defense organizations.
8. It leverages commercial off-the-shelf components for affordability while using proprietary algorithms to produce 3D subsurface imagery of both metallic and plastic threats.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ScaleWolf and NATO.
Organization type: Privately held defense technology startup.
Business model: Hardware sensor sales and defense contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023 and having raised roughly one million euros including an eight-hundred-thousand-euro Series A in 2024, operating at a mid-technology readiness level without independently validated field deployments.
Geography: Based in Vilnius, Lithuania, focusing operations on European and NATO defense priorities.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Dropla
points.description: Danish defense startup building autonomous robots and drones that use onboard AI to detect and clear landmines.
points.bullets:
A robot and drone maker that builds an integrated demining platform of unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles and onboard AI software for defense and civilian demining operations. The organization supplies its own interconnected hardware, autonomy software and proprietary AI models as an end-to-end solution for explosive hazard detection. It serves government demining agencies and military organizations operating in post-conflict zones.
1. A robot and drone maker that builds unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles and onboard detection software, sold as an integrated demining platform.
2. Onboard edge AI fuses optical, thermal, magnetometric, multispectral and lidar sensor data across unmanned aerial vehicles and ground components.
3. Multi-modal sensor fusion, landmine and unexploded ordnance detection, drone swarm coordination, vegetation removal and safety zone confirmation.
4. Complete unmanned aerial vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles and proprietary software delivered as an end-to-end demining platform.
5. Humanitarian demining, post-conflict remediation, active conflict zones and infrastructure development.
6. Government demining agencies, defense forces and civilian emergency services.
7. It builds its own robots and drones and supplies them directly to government demining organizations for field deployment.
8. It uses a multi-drone swarm methodology to reduce unmanned ground vehicle manufacturing costs from over a million euros to approximately ten thousand euros each.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Selected for a national robotics startup incubator hosted by a Danish technological institute and tested by the Ukrainian government demining organization.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of unmanned vehicles and integrated platform sales for demining contracts.
Scale and maturity: A startup founded in 2023, incubated and testing equipment in active conflict zones.
Geography: Based in Odense, Denmark, operating and testing in Ukraine.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play enterprise entirely focused on developing autonomous physical systems for explosive hazard detection.

points.name: Embodied Inc.
points.description: Pasadena software company developing companion robots that help children build social and emotional skills.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that built a physical companion robot for children, integrating on-device multimodal inference software for natural, social human-machine interaction. The company designed its own hardware and proprietary AI platform in-house to help children build social, emotional, and cognitive skills through play-based learning.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete companion robots.
2. On-device multimodal inference software and hardware combining computer vision, natural language processing, audio direction, and automatic speech recognition.
3. Fluid social interaction, perception of emotional states, and generation of appropriate vocal tones, facial expressions, and body language.
4. Complete robots.
5. Homes.
6. Consumers, specifically children on the autism spectrum and those facing social-emotional challenges.
7. It designs and builds its own complete robots and proprietary AI platform entirely in-house.
8. Its proprietary social interaction platform fuses computer vision, natural language processing, and audio direction to perceive emotional states and respond with expressive vocal tones, facial expressions, and body language.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Intel Capital, Toyota AI Ventures, Amazon Alexa Fund, and Sony Innovation Fund, and it uses automatic speech recognition from Google and engineering services from Lantronix.
Organization type: A privately held startup that ultimately ceased operations.
Business model: Hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: The company raised approximately $80 million in venture funding before going out of business.
Geography: Based in Pasadena, California, with robots designed for in-home use.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation were completely central to the organization's mission, representing the sole foundation of its social and therapeutic robotics business.

points.name: Robbyant
points.description: Chinese AI startup building full-stack embodied AI models and wheeled humanoid robots for service industries.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and AI model developer that builds wheeled humanoid robots for service tasks and develops open-source embodied AI foundation models spanning perception, world modeling, and vision-language-action control for robotics.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells wheeled dual-arm humanoid robots, and an AI model developer whose open-source robot foundation models run on other companies' robots.
2. Neural spatial perception models using masked depth modeling to reconstruct missing depth information, vision-language-action models, and real-time streaming 3D reconstruction running on wheeled humanoid hardware.
3. High-precision depth estimation, real-time 3D mapping, spatial intelligence, dexterous manipulation, autonomous navigation, and physical task execution including cooking, medication sorting, and service delivery.
4. Complete wheeled humanoid robots, open-source foundation models, and training datasets.
5. Humanoids, community centers, restaurants, pharmacies, hospitals, homes, elderly care facilities, and hospitality settings.
6. Service operators, healthcare providers, pharmacy operators, and developers.
7. Its robots are deployed directly in service environments and its open-source models are integrated by other robotics developers into their hardware.
8. It combines complete humanoid robot manufacturing with openly released foundation models and datasets, leveraging its parent corporation's financial technology and local services ecosystem for commercial-scale deployment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ant Group is its parent company and Orbbec supplies its 3D vision sensors.
Organization type: A wholly owned subsidiary of a publicly traded technology company.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and open-source release of AI models and datasets.
Scale and maturity: Founded in late 2024 with substantial registered capital and live deployments in pharmacies, community centers, and restaurants.
Geography: Based in China and operates within its parent corporation's local services infrastructure.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the absolute core of its mission, serving as its exclusive reason for establishment.

points.name: Saronic

A defense robot maker that designs, builds, and operates autonomous surface vessels for the U.S. military, covering the full stack from hull design and autonomy software to its own shipbuilding infrastructure.
1. A robot maker that designs and manufactures complete autonomous surface vessels for government customers.
2. Autonomous maritime platforms integrating edge AI inference, sensor fusion, and cross-platform mission-level autonomy software.
3. Autonomous navigation, multi-asset teaming, long-range maritime operations, and modular payload delivery.
4. Complete unmanned vehicles sold to government customers under defense contracts.
5. Defense, maritime security, and naval surface operations.
6. Militaries, navies, and defense agencies.
7. It designs, builds, and sells the complete machine directly to defense forces.

Organization type: Privately held startup.

points.name: Shihang Intelligent

A robot maker that designs and builds autonomous underwater robotic systems, including the physical hardware and proprietary edge AI models, for maritime industries.

2. Core underwater robot hardware subsystems integrated with a proprietary ocean embodied AI model trained on millions of hours of data.
3. Autonomous underwater navigation, ship hull cleaning, offshore wind farm inspection, and seabed exploration.
4. Complete robotic systems integrated with proprietary intelligent software.

points.name: Mind Robotics

A full-stack industrial robotics platform company that develops purpose-built robots, foundation models, and deployment infrastructure to automate dexterous, variable, and reasoning-intensive manufacturing tasks at scale.

2. Foundation models trained on real production data paired with physical factory robots and deployment infrastructure.
3. Autonomous completion of dexterous, variable, and reasoning-intensive industrial manipulation tasks requiring generalization across environments.
4. Complete deployed robotics systems integrating purpose-built hardware, software models, and deployment infrastructure.

7. Its robots and models are deployed directly into factory environments, utilizing a parent company's manufacturing facilities as its primary launch customer and testing ground.

points.name: Symbotic
points.description: US robotics and automation company deploying AI-driven autonomous warehouse fleets for storage and retrieval.

A robot maker and systems integrator that builds end-to-end warehouse automation platforms, combining proprietary autonomous mobile robots and AI orchestration software to automate supply chain operations for large retailers and wholesalers.

2. Autonomous mobile robots, automated storage and retrieval systems, and self-learning edge AI orchestration software that routes and controls fleets of bots in real time.

points.name: Fox Robotics

points.name: Zebra Technologies
points.description: US technology company deploying autonomous mobile robots for warehouse automation.

An enterprise technology and automation company that builds autonomous mobile robots for material handling, integrating them with its barcode scanning, RFID, and machine vision data-capture systems for warehouse and fulfillment environments, before winding down and divesting its robotics division.
1. A robot maker and systems integrator that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots alongside rugged mobile computers, barcode scanners, and fixed industrial vision systems.

7. Its robots and data-capture hardware are deployed together into the warehouses and fulfillment centers of enterprise operators.
8. It couples autonomous mobile robots with a dense existing ecosystem of enterprise barcode, RFID, and machine-vision data-capture infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: StayLinked, Peak Technologies, Build With Robots, Agility Robotics, OpenAI, and Skild AI.

Business model: Hardware sales of robots, scanners, and mobile computers, alongside software licenses and cloud-based fleet management subscriptions.

points.name: Assured Robot Intelligence

4. AI models and cognitive software intended to power physical actuators, sensors, and complete deployed robotic systems.
5. Humanoid robots and household environments.

7. Its models are integrated into humanoid robots and physical systems developed by other organizations.
8. It pursued physical artificial general intelligence through models that learn directly from human behavior, driven by a leadership team with deep academic robotics expertise.

8. A proprietary sub-threshold power optimized technology platform sets it apart by enabling processors to operate below 1 Volt for 2–5x better power efficiency than traditional semiconductor designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: TSMC for silicon manufacturing, Edge Impulse for edge AI development, and investors including Kleiner Perkins, Arm, Austin Ventures, and Mercury Fund, with chips adopted by top wearable brands including Garmin, Suunto, and Google.
Organization type: Publicly traded semiconductor company listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
Business model: Chip sales and semiconductor component sales to device manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A mature, publicly traded enterprise with over 290 million chips shipped as of early 2026 and $76.1 million in reported 2024 revenue.
Geography: Headquartered in Singapore with a strong and growing global market presence outside mainland China, demonstrated by 94% year-over-year international sales growth in early 2025.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play enterprise where ultra-low-power edge AI semiconductor design is its entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Syntiant
points.description: US semiconductor company designing ultra-low-power neural processor chips for fast local inference on battery-operated devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power neural decision processors for edge AI inference, paired with MEMS microphones and deep learning models, for consumer and industrial device makers.
1. A chip company that designs neural processing units and MEMS microphones for on-device inference.
2. At-memory architecture neural processors built on programmable deep learning cores, delivering INT8 performance in a microwatt-to-milliwatt power envelope alongside analog MEMS microphone technology.
3. On-device inference for always-on voice control, wake-word detection, acoustic event detection, speaker verification, person detection, object classification, motion tracking and occupancy monitoring.
4. Chips, MEMS microphone modules, hardware-agnostic AI software models and TinyML development boards.
5. Earbuds, laptops, smart home devices, wearables, security cameras and automotive cabin monitoring systems.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, automotive electronics suppliers, industrial device makers and other semiconductor companies.
7. Its processors and microphones are designed into battery-powered edge devices by consumer electronics manufacturers, and its deep learning models are licensed to other chip companies.
8. Extreme energy efficiency enables always-on neural computation in the microwatt range, shifting inference from cloud infrastructure to battery-constrained edge devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Intel Capital, Microsoft's M12, Applied Ventures, Robert Bosch Venture Capital and the Amazon Alexa Fund, with models licensed to Qualcomm and Ambarella.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Chip sales, MEMS microphone hardware sales and AI software model licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017 with roughly 155 million dollars in funding and over 100 million processor units deployed.
Geography: Headquartered in Irvine, California, and operating globally within the consumer and industrial electronics markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence hardware is the organization's entire focus, developing low-power inference accelerators and sensors with no involvement in complete robotic or automated systems.

points.name: TTTech Computertechnik AG
points.description: Austrian automotive technology company developing safe real-time computing platforms for industrial edge automation.
points.bullets:
A platform provider and systems integrator that develops safe, deterministic real-time computing platforms and industrial edge computing solutions for autonomous systems. The organization supplies safety-critical control units, application software, and consulting services for functional safety and secure system architectures, utilizing time-triggered Ethernet and deterministic networking to enable secure connectivity and real-time data processing from sensors to control units. It serves original equipment manufacturers, suppliers, and regulators across aerospace, automotive, industrial automation, and energy sectors.
1. A platform provider and systems integrator that builds deterministic real-time computing platforms, safety-critical control units, and application software, sold as embedded hardware, software, and integration services.
2. Time-triggered Ethernet and deterministic networking technologies that enable secure connectivity and real-time data processing from sensors to deployed control units.
3. Deterministic real-time performance, secure connectivity, functional safety, and real-time data processing for autonomous systems.
4. Safety-critical control units, application software, and consulting services delivered through integration projects and lifecycle management.
5. Aerospace, automotive, off-highway machinery, advanced air mobility, industrial automation, and energy sectors.
6. Original equipment manufacturers, suppliers, and regulators in aerospace, automotive, industrial automation, and energy.
7. Its deterministic networking and safety-critical control units are integrated into autonomous systems and control architectures by original equipment manufacturers.
8. Deep cross-industry expertise in deterministic real-time performance, long-term production contracts, and rigorous obsolescence management for safety-critical systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Multi-stakeholder platforms established with major semiconductor firms, NASA's Artemis program, and French nuclear power plants.
Organization type: A privately held company that actively manages joint ventures and strategic partnerships.
Business model: Hardware and software sales, integration services, and long-term production contracts.
Scale and maturity: Over 25 years of industry experience with a mature global presence, specialized application development centers, and high-profile deployments.
Geography: Based in Europe and executes high-profile deployments globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are central to its mission, leveraging its core competency in deterministic networking to enable functional safety and machine learning in autonomous systems.

points.name: X Square Robot
points.description: Chinese embodied AI startup developing general-purpose foundation models and robotic arms for physical manipulation tasks.

X Square Robot Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and AI model developer that builds general-purpose wheeled humanoid robots, dexterous hands, and embodied AI foundation models for real-world manipulation. The organization operates an integrated stack spanning proprietary data collection, world models, and complete robotic hardware for household, industrial, and logistics scenarios.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete humanoid robots and dexterous hands, and an AI model developer whose embodied foundation models run on those robots.
2. Vision-language-action models and world models trained on multimodal teleoperation data within a unified architecture that integrates perception, language, action, and physical prediction.
3. Dexterous manipulation, fine manipulation, long-horizon task planning, fabric deformation assessment, autonomous navigation, and cross-embodiment transfer.
4. Complete robots, robotic hands, open-source models, and data-collection hardware, as well as robot cleaning services operated with partners.
5. Households, hotels, retirement homes, schools, retail, logistics, and automobile manufacturing.
6. Consumers, service operators, schools, hotels, retirement homes, and automakers.
7. Its robots and embedded models are deployed directly into end-user environments, and its open-source models are used by robotics developers.
8. A tightly integrated hardware-software stack uses a unified World Unified Model architecture that trains perception, language, action, and physical prediction together rather than in separate modules.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance, Xiaomi, Meituan, HongShan, IDG, and Source Code Capital, with service partnerships with 58.com and Chery Automobile, and runs its compute on Nvidia chips.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Robot and hardware sales, open-source models, and operated robot cleaning services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023, valued over $2.8 billion, having raised over $423 million across multiple funding rounds through Series D.
Geography: Headquartered in Shenzhen, China, with deployments and operations in Shenzhen and Beijing.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play edge and physical AI company entirely focused on its embodied AI stack, hardware, and commercial physical automation services.

points.name: IDG Capital
points.description: Chinese investment firm funding embodied AI and robotics startups building physical robots.
points.bullets:
A venture capital and private equity firm that provides funding to companies across the physical AI and robotics ecosystem, with a particular focus on complete robotic systems, humanoid platforms, and autonomous operating systems for industrial, commercial, research, and household applications.
1. A venture capital firm that funds robot makers, AI model developers, and autonomy software developers.
2. It deploys capital to accelerate the development, manufacturing, and scaling of embodied AI platforms and full-stack robotic systems.
3. It delivers growth capital, Series A funding, pre-IPO financing, and follow-on investments to robotics startups and established robotics businesses.
4. Its investments target humanoids, quadruped robots, and autonomous robotic systems operating in industrial, commercial, research, and household settings.
5. Its customers are robotics startups, embodied AI developers, and full-stack robotics platform companies seeking capital.
6. It operates at the top of the value chain as a financial backer that funds robot makers and physical AI platform developers.
7. It concentrates its physical AI investments on companies competing at the complete system and platform level rather than companies supplying individual hardware or software components.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It co-invests with GSR Ventures and Matrix Partners China.
Organization type: A privately held global venture capital and private equity firm.
Business model: It generates returns through fund management and equity appreciation from its portfolio investments.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1993, it is a major global investor that leads funding rounds ranging from angel investments to pre-IPO rounds exceeding hundreds of millions of dollars.
Geography: It is headquartered in Hong Kong and targets investments across China, Europe, the Middle East, and North America.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI and robotics, the firm manages a diversified global investment portfolio spanning software, internet, e-commerce, consumer, healthcare, and finance sectors.

points.name: HSG
points.description: Chinese venture capital firm funding early-stage humanoid robotics and embodied AI companies.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that deploys early and growth-stage funding into physical robotics and embodied artificial intelligence companies. The firm builds strategic exposure across the humanoid robotics stack by backing ventures that create everything from open-source foundation models and complete humanoid systems to dexterous manipulation hardware. It primarily serves emerging robotics ventures in the domestic Chinese market.
1. A venture capital firm that invests in robot makers, component suppliers and AI model developers.
2. Investment capital allocated across the physical AI stack, spanning foundation models, complete humanoid systems and dexterous manipulation hardware.
3. Early and growth-stage funding for physical AI startups, including seed and Series B rounds.
4. Financial capital provided through direct equity investments in private robotics and AI ventures.
5. Humanoid robotics, embodied AI and physical automation.
6. Emerging robotics ventures, integrated robot OEMs and specialized component suppliers.
7. Its capital funds both integrated robot OEMs and specialized component suppliers like actuator vendors.
8. It sets itself apart by strategically investing across complementary layers of the humanoid robotics supply chain, capturing value from both proprietary hardware subsystems and end-to-end software platforms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed ventures include Genesis AI, ROBOTERA, TARS Robotics and X Square Robot, and it collaborates with ETH on robotics and AI research.

points.name: Meituan
points.description: Chinese technology company deploying autonomous delivery vehicles and drones for local logistics.

A logistics operator that runs autonomous ground vehicles and aerial drones for food and grocery delivery, and a corporate venture capital firm that backs robotics, autonomy and component startups. 6. Consumers using its food delivery application.
7. It operates autonomous vehicles and drones in its own delivery network and takes equity stakes in robotics and component makers.

Key partners and customers: Backed by Tencent and HongShan; holds a stake in Unitree; invests in X Square Robot, Pudu Technology, Mech-Mind Robotics, Inceptio Technology and Mindverse; sources lidar from Hesai.

points.name: ByteDance
points.description: Chinese technology company funding early-stage robotics startups.

A Chinese internet technology company and venture investor that develops large-scale robot foundation models and builds data-collection robots for its own research, while providing lead-round funding to robotics startups and buying AI compute chips at scale.

points.name: PsiBot
points.description: Shanghai AI startup building embodied AI models and vision-language-action systems that enable robots to perform complex physical tasks.

An AI model developer that builds embodied AI foundation models, world models and vision-language-action architectures for robots and self-driving cars, licensing its intelligence layer to third-party robot makers and verifying its systems in logistics and manufacturing settings.

2. Vision-language-action models and world models built on a hierarchical end-to-end fast/slow brain architecture that pairs a slow reasoning system with a fast execution system, applying reinforcement learning to solve complex manipulation tasks.
3. Embodied intelligence, dexterous grasping and manipulation, long-horizon task planning, physical world understanding, and complex action execution in open environments.
4. AI models and VLA frameworks licensed to third-party robot makers, alongside a 21-DOF dexterous hand designed for dexterous manipulation.

6. Robot makers, logistics operators, manufacturers, and retail enterprises.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its founding team includes a member from a major university artificial intelligence institute, and its funding round is led by an automaker with participation from a consumer electronics component manufacturer.

An automaker and strategic investor that applies physical AI to its vehicles and manufacturing operations while backing external robotics startups, licensing embodied AI software and integrating it into automotive and industrial systems rather than building models from scratch.

A component supplier and sensor maker that mass-produces complete humanoid robots, dexterous hands and harmonic reducers for global partners, while also supplying precision glass and sensors to consumer electronics and automakers, and investing in robotics firms.

A systems integrator and engineering services firm that provides full-lifecycle support for robotics and physical automation, from R&D and hardware development through deployment and live operations, for industrial clients seeking production-grade systems.

points.name: SVRC

A robotics research organization and data services provider that captures multimodal robotic datasets from physical hardware and distributes tactile sensors for AI model training.

points.name: Stanford

A university research lab that develops open-source vision-language-action models, mobile manipulation platforms, and autonomous vehicle architectures, providing foundational software and reference hardware for the robotics community.
