points.description: United States robotics software company developing AI tools to simplify industrial robot programming and deployment.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a robot-agnostic software platform and integrated automation cells for industrial manufacturing. It develops AI, perception, and simulation tools that enable industrial robots from multiple manufacturers to be easily programmed, deployed, and operated without hand-coded instructions.
1. A developer tools company that builds a robotics software platform and productized automation cells, sold as licensed software, development environments, and integrated hardware-software systems.
2. Deep learning algorithms and multi-modal sensor fusion networks combine RGB, infrared, and polarization data with digital twin simulation and ROS 2 middleware to generate robot skills and 3D vision architectures.
3. Robot-agnostic programming, scalable robotic grasping, 3D perception of complex and reflective objects, automated sensor calibration, and sim-to-real deployment.
4. Licensed software platforms, web-based developer environments, and productized automation cells integrating third-party robot arms and cameras.
5. Manufacturing environments, factory automation, electronics assembly, sheet-metal processing, and machine tending.
6. Manufacturers, system integrators, and consumer electronics contract manufacturers.
7. Its software and development tools sit above the hardware layer, integrating third-party robot arms and sensors to enable end-user manufacturing applications.
8. It abstracts complex robot programming into pre-built AI skills, significantly lowering the barrier to entry for adopting factory automation across disparate robot hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Alphabet, Google, NVIDIA, Siemens, FANUC, KUKA, Comau, Cognex, TRUMPF, Foxconn, ETH Zurich Gramazio Kohler Research, and the Open-RMF Project Management Committee.
Organization type: A subsidiary of Alphabet, formerly an independent moonshot project, now integrated into Google.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions, integrated hardware-software cells, and joint venture factory automation contracts.
Scale and maturity: A growth-stage organization founded five years ago, currently expanding field deployments after acquiring Open Source Robotics Corporation and Vicarious.
Geography: Based in the United States with deployments and partnerships extending globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are its entire focus.

points.name: ViDi Systems
points.description: Swiss startup developing deep learning software for AI-powered industrial machine vision inspection.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that built deep learning software for industrial machine vision, providing vision models and inspection tools that manufacturers use for automated quality control.
1. A software company whose deep learning vision models run on industrial inspection systems built by machine vision providers.
2. Convolutional neural networks trained on images of acceptable products and defects to perform visual classification, object detection and segmentation.
3. Defect detection, classification of acceptable variations, and image analysis for automated visual inspection.
4. Licensed software integrated into industrial machine vision platforms.
5. Factories, production lines, automotive electronics, consumer goods and wine production.
6. Manufacturers requiring automated quality control and process automation.
7. Its software is embedded within industrial machine vision platforms sold to manufacturers.
8. It uses AI to distinguish between acceptable product variations and actual defects, overcoming the limitations of traditional hand-coded vision rules and reducing false rejects.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by and integrated into Cognex Corporation, co-founded by the CPA Group.
Organization type: Former privately held startup acquired by a publicly traded company.
Business model: Software licenses for industrial machine vision.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2012, acquired after roughly five years of independent operation.
Geography: Based in Switzerland, supporting global manufacturing customers.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and machine vision were the sole focus of its original business and the core capability it contributed to its parent company.

points.name: Clearpath Robotics
points.description: Canadian robotics company deploying autonomous mobile robots that process computer vision tasks at the edge.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile robots and research platforms for industrial material handling and robotics research. It manufactures high-payload AMRs, outdoor rovers, and base mobile platforms, develops autonomous navigation software, and provides custom hardware integration services.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots, base robotic platforms, and autonomy software for industrial and research use.
2. Autonomous mobile robot platforms with integrated navigation systems using lidar, stereo vision, IMU, GPS, and ROS-based open-source ecosystems.
3. Indoor and outdoor autonomous navigation, high-payload material transport, mobile robot customization, and hardware systems integration.
4. Complete robots, base robotic platforms, autonomous navigation software packages, and custom robotic integration services.
5. Warehouses, factories, agriculture, mining, military, aerospace, academic research, and outdoor environments.
6. Industrial logistics operators, manufacturers, mining companies, military organizations, agricultural operations, and academic research institutions.
7. Its robots and platforms are deployed directly in industrial facilities or used as base units by integrators and researchers for custom applications.
8. It bridges robotics research and industrial deployment by commercializing base mobile platforms alongside high-payload AMRs and custom integration services.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Rockwell Automation, Open Robotics, WiBotic.
Organization type: Subsidiary of a publicly traded industrial automation conglomerate.
Business model: Robot and hardware platform sales, software licenses, and custom engineering and integration services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2009 with over 150 employees, acquired in 2023, with a parent division operating in the warehouse robotics market.
Geography: Based in Canada, operating globally in industrial and research markets.
Beyond physical AI: It focuses entirely on robotics, edge AI, and physical automation across hardware, software, and services.

points.name: Aurora
points.description: US autonomous vehicle startup developing self-driving AI systems for freight trucks.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vehicle company that builds a full-stack Level 4 self-driving system, including hardware and software, for Class 8 trucks and passenger vehicles, and operates its own driverless freight fleet. It designs its system for truck makers and logistics carriers, integrating sensors, computers, and autonomy software directly into commercial vehicle platforms to enable hub-to-hub freight and ride-hailing.
1. An autonomy software developer that builds a Level 4 self-driving stack integrated with its own hardware kit, licensed as a driver-as-a-service product to automakers and fleet operators.
2. A full-stack autonomous driving system combining sensor fusion from cameras, imaging radar, and frequency-modulated continuous-wave lidar with an onboard compute platform running planning, perception, and navigation software.
3. Autonomous highway navigation, dynamic route planning, long-range object detection, intersection navigation, and fleet monitoring.
4. A self-driving system consisting of a hardware kit and licensed software integrated into vehicle manufacturers' production-line trucks, paired with a cloud-based fleet management platform.
5. Autonomous trucking, robotaxis, logistics, and freight operations on public highways.
6. Truck manufacturers, automakers, logistics operators, and fleet operators.
7. Its self-driving system is integrated by truck manufacturers into their Class 8 chassis and operated by logistics carriers in their freight networks.
8. It developed and integrates proprietary frequency-modulated continuous-wave lidar to provide long-range object detection and velocity measurement for high-speed trucking.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include truck manufacturers Volvo and PACCAR, automotive supplier AUMOVIO, technology company NVIDIA, and logistics operators FedEx, Uber Freight, and Werner Enterprises.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Software and hardware system sales and licensing, per-vehicle royalties, and driver-as-a-service fees.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, it has raised billions in funding, went public via SPAC in 2021, and launched commercial driverless freight operations across multiple U.S. Sun Belt routes.
Geography: Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, it operates autonomous freight routes primarily in Texas, Arizona, and the broader U.S. Sun Belt.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and physical autonomy constitute its entire focus.

points.name: Quantum Systems
points.description: German autonomous drones unicorn manufacturing AI-powered eVTOL aircraft for real-time defense and security surveillance.
points.bullets:
A drone maker that builds and sells autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles and multi-domain unmanned systems, along with mission control software, for defense and security forces.
1. A drone and unmanned vehicle maker that designs and manufactures electric vertical-takeoff-and-landing fixed-wing drones, ground and maritime unmanned vehicles, and command-and-control software for military customers.
2. Electric tilt-rotor vertical-takeoff-and-landing fixed-wing unmanned aerial systems integrated with dual NVIDIA Jetson edge computing modules, acoustic payloads, and GPS-denied navigation software.
3. Autonomous real-time intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, GPS-denied navigation, target tracking, acoustic sound source detection, and multi-domain unmanned system command-and-control.
4. Complete unmanned aerial, ground and maritime vehicles, acoustic payloads, and licensed ground control and fleet management software.
5. Defense, security, emergency services, agriculture, mining, and infrastructure mapping.
6. NATO-aligned militaries, defense forces, emergency services, and commercial operators.
7. Its unmanned aerial systems and command software are operated directly by defense forces and emergency services in the field.
8. The unmanned aerial systems are combat-proven with open-architecture designs enabling autonomous navigation in GPS-denied environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by Blackstone, Airbus, Advent and Balderton Capital, with acquired entities including Fernride, AirRobot, Nordic Unmanned and Spleenlab, and partnerships with YellowScan and Hensoldt.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of unmanned systems and licensed software for defense and security operations.
Scale and maturity: Has raised $1.7 billion across funding rounds, employs over 550 people globally, and has executed over 19,000 missions in Ukraine.
Geography: Headquartered near Munich, Germany, with global production facilities and offices in the United States, Australia, Ukraine, Romania, the United Kingdom, and the Baltics.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation constitute the organization's entire focus.

points.name: WeRide
points.description: Chinese autonomous vehicle company deploying L4 robotaxis and driver-assist systems for urban mobility.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vehicle company that builds Level 2 to Level 4 self-driving systems and operates commercial robotaxi fleets, as well as autonomous buses, vans, and street sweepers. It develops a full autonomous driving stack, sensor suites, and computing platforms for its own deployed vehicles and for automotive partners.
1. An autonomous vehicle company that builds and operates self-driving taxis and other autonomous vehicles, and licenses its autonomous driving stack to automakers.
2. Multi-sensor fusion algorithms combining vision-centric and lidar-centric pipelines, high-definition maps, proprietary middleware, and a physical AI foundation model running on high-performance computing platforms.
3. L4 autonomous driving, robotaxi fleet operations, urban navigation, 360-degree perception, and autonomous last-mile logistics and sanitation.
4. Complete robotaxis and autonomous vehicles it operates itself, alongside licensed autonomy stacks for automakers.
5. Robotaxis, autonomous minibuses, autonomous delivery vans, street sweepers, and passenger mobility services.
6. Mobility platform operators, automakers, and municipal transportation operators.
7. It designs its own autonomous driving software and sensor suites, integrates them into vehicle architectures from automotive partners, and operates the resulting robotaxi fleets itself or through ride-hailing platforms.
8. It operates a full-stack physical AI model and autonomous driving platform spanning L2 to L4, running across a diverse matrix of vehicle types from robotaxis to street sweepers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Uber, Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance, Nvidia, Hesai, RoboSense, Horizon Robotics, Grab, GreenMobility, and Farizon.
Organization type: A publicly traded company listed on the Nasdaq and Hong Kong stock exchanges.
Business model: Ride and delivery fares from operated robotaxi and logistics fleets, and licensed autonomous driving systems to automakers.
Scale and maturity: A commercial-stage company with over 800 robotaxis in one fleet, over 13 million kilometers of autonomous driving, operations in over 40 cities across 12 countries, and $1.5 billion in total funding.
Geography: Based in China, operating commercial and pilot autonomous driving services across the Middle East, Europe, North America, and Southeast Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Physical autonomy is the company's entire focus, with all operations and product development dedicated to autonomous mobility.

points.name: Waabi
points.description: Canadian autonomous trucking startup deploying AI systems to operate driverless trucks.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds a Level 4 autonomous driving stack for heavy-duty trucks and robotaxis, combining a generative AI driving model with a proprietary neural simulation platform for automakers and freight operators.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack to automakers and operates it through ride-hailing and freight networks.
2. An end-to-end generative AI foundation model that predicts 3D environments from lidar data, trained on a neural simulator that synthesizes traffic scenarios, weather conditions, and pedestrian behaviors.
3. Autonomous hub-to-hub highway navigation, urban robotaxi driving, sensor fusion, and synthetic training data generation.
4. Licensed autonomy software integrated into commercial truck platforms, alongside a driver-as-a-service model deployed on ride-hailing networks.
5. Autonomous trucks, robotaxis, and commercial freight corridors.
6. Automakers, commercial trucking fleets, ride-hailing platforms, and freight carriers.
7. Its autonomy software and virtual driver are integrated into trucks built by OEMs and operated through third-party logistics and ride-hailing networks.
8. It uses a single end-to-end generative AI foundation model that generalizes across different vehicle types and environments, trained entirely in simulation rather than through extensive real-world fleet testing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Volvo Autonomous Solutions, Peterbilt, Uber, Uber Freight, NVIDIA, Khosla Ventures, G2 Venture Partners, Porsche Automobil Holding SE, BlackRock, Radical Ventures, Scania Invest, and Ingka Investments.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licensing, per-vehicle royalties, and autonomous transport fees collected through its own deployments on partner freight and ride-hailing networks.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2021, it has raised over $1 billion in total funding, including a $750 million Series C, and is running commercial loads with safety drivers between Dallas and Houston while planning deployments of 25,000 robotaxis.
Geography: Based in Toronto, Canada, with autonomous trucking operations in Texas.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play physical AI and autonomous vehicle company, focusing entirely on developing self-driving systems for real-world transportation.

points.name: Stack AV
points.description: US autonomous trucking startup developing self-driving systems for freight transport.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer and autonomous trucking startup building a self-driving stack for on-highway Class 8 trucks for the commercial freight sector.
1. An autonomy software developer that builds a self-driving stack for autonomous freight trucking and operates its own development fleet.
2. An end-to-end autonomous driving platform integrating real-time perception systems, machine learning inference, and data engineering infrastructure.
3. Autonomous navigation, perception, and fleet operations for self-driving trucks.
4. Self-driving trucks operated by the company during development and testing.
5. On-highway Class 8 trucks, freight hauling, and logistics operations.
6. Commercial freight and logistics operators.
7. It develops and operates its own autonomous trucking technology and testing infrastructure.
8. It is founded by autonomous vehicle industry veterans with leadership expertise specifically tailored to addressing trucking industry inefficiencies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by investment holding firm SoftBank Group Corp.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Developing autonomous trucking technology for commercialization.
Scale and maturity: A development-stage company founded in 2023 with 150 employees and $1 billion in funding.
Geography: Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with a testing facility in New Stanton and operations across 15 states including Memphis, Denver, Atlanta, and Phoenix.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: EDGE AI FOUNDATION
points.description: Global foundation advancing edge AI adoption through educational content, industry partnerships, and strategic resources.
points.bullets:
An industry standards and community organization that advances edge and physical AI by uniting developers, academia and technology makers, running working groups, publishing benchmarks and best practices, and providing educational content and datasets for the ecosystem.
1. A non-profit standards and community body that develops industry standards, benchmarks, educational content and open resources for edge AI developers and technology makers.
2. Educational platforms, datasets, models and code for edge AI research, alongside industry working groups focused on energy-efficient machine learning and edge reference architectures.
3. Workforce development and certification, ecosystem benchmarking, cross-industry best practices and open standards development for energy-efficient on-device AI.
4. Community events, global conferences, a video channel, online learning ecosystems and working group publications.
5. Resource-constrained edge devices, defense systems and general edge AI applications.
6. Technology companies, semiconductor suppliers, silicon IP providers, system integrators, academic institutions and edge AI developers.
7. It convenes the ecosystem, publishing resources and standards that device makers, chip companies and software developers use to build and deploy edge AI systems.
8. It is the world's largest community of edge AI developers, evolved from a focus on ultra-low-power tinyML to encompass generative AI, computer vision and natural language processing at the edge.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ST, Google, Arm, AWS, Wind River, Ceva, Alif Semiconductor, Gorilla Technology, Eta Compute, DeepGate and Latent AI.
Organization type: A California-based 501c3 non-profit organization.
Business model: Membership participation, conference organizing and educational content distribution.
Scale and maturity: Established in 2018, it engages over 100 technology companies and over 100,000 individuals worldwide, with a YouTube channel reaching 115,000 subscribers.
Geography: Based in California, operating globally across Europe, the U.S. and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is entirely focused on advancing edge and physical AI technologies and community.

points.name: Edge AI
points.description: Private hardware company building portable pipeline inspection robots with on-device sensor processing.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and service provider that builds portable inspection robots for precision data collection and survey-grade infrastructure assessments, offering them through a subscription model. The company integrates edge computing and on-device AI into its hardware to perform real-time local processing and cloud-based data uploads for pipeline inspection. It serves municipalities, engineering firms, and water authorities with complete field inspection platforms.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells portable pipeline inspection robots.
2. Man-portable robotic systems equipped with live video streaming, precision positioning, and on-device processing units designed for minimally invasive infrastructure assessments.
3. Precision data collection, live video streaming, cloud-based data upload, and survey-grade infrastructure assessment.
4. Portable robotic inspection systems offered through a commercial subscription-based service model.
5. Pipeline and infrastructure inspection operations in municipal and environmental service settings.
6. Municipalities, engineering firms, construction companies, and rural water authorities.
7. It builds complete inspection robots and operates them as a service for municipal and environmental customers.
8. The portability of its inspection robots eliminates the need for specialized heavy vehicles and significantly reduces deployment costs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Tenaya Capital, Innovation Works, M7 Ace Neo, LMNT Ventures, and Organic Growth Fund.
Organization type: A privately held hardware company.
Business model: Hardware sales and a subscription-based robotics-as-a-service model.
Scale and maturity: A commercial-stage company founded in 2020 with 36 employees that is currently generating revenue.
Geography: Based in Homestead, Pennsylvania, USA, and primarily operating across Pennsylvania and neighboring regions.
Beyond physical AI: As a pure-play enterprise, its entire focus is on physical automation and edge AI hardware applied to infrastructure assessment.

points.name: Tenaya Capital
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-growth stage technology companies.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that holds a minority stake in an edge AI company, supplying early-growth stage capital to technology entrepreneurs rather than building physical AI products directly.
1. A venture capital firm that provides early-growth stage funding to technology companies.
2. It sells to early-growth stage technology entrepreneurs building companies in the physical AI space.
3. It supplies capital to businesses across the technology value chain that may build anything from edge inference chips to complete robotic systems.
points.profile:
Organization type: A venture capital firm that invests in privately held technology companies.
Business model: Fund management through venture capital investments.
Scale and maturity: It operates at an established level within the venture capital industry.
Beyond physical AI: It is a broad technology investor with no evidence indicating physical AI, robotics, or automation represents a dedicated focus area.

points.name: Innovation Works
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage edge AI and robotics startups.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that provides funding and mentorship to early-stage startups across the edge and physical AI ecosystem, holding minority equity positions in companies developing components, sensors, vehicles, and warehouse automation. It deploys capital into hardware and robotics startups rather than manufacturing its own products, building a diversified portfolio that spans the entire physical AI stack for technology entrepreneurs.
1. A venture capital firm that funds and holds minority stakes in early-stage startups building edge AI, robotics, and automation technologies.
2. It delivers early-stage capital, mentorship, and strategic support across component-level technologies, autonomous vehicles, and warehouse automation platforms.
3. It acts purely as a financial investor and strategic mentor taking minority equity stakes in startups across the physical AI stack.
4. It leverages Pittsburgh's emergence as a top-ten U.S. market for AI and autonomous vehicle investment, capitalizing on the region's elite robotics research ecosystem.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is part of the Ben Franklin Technology Partners network and counts robotics and AI startups among its portfolio additions.
Organization type: An early-stage venture capital firm.
Business model: The firm makes money through venture capital fund management and equity returns on startup investments.
Scale and maturity: An established investor operating since 1988, it has supported a portfolio exceeding 830 companies and participates in large funding rounds.
Geography: The organization is based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and primarily operates within the Southwestern Pennsylvania technology ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge AI and physical automation, the firm focuses broadly on providing capital and mentorship across a general technology landscape including information technology, healthcare, and biotechnology.

points.name: M7 Ace Neo
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage robotics, agricultural, clean, and artificial intelligence hardware startups.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that deploys minority equity capital into early-stage HardTech startups developing physical artificial intelligence, robotics, agricultural technology, clean technology and deep technology. It provides seed funding and strategic guidance to entrepreneurs building edge inference, sensor and automation technologies. The firm acts as an external financier rather than building, operating or licensing physical AI hardware or software.
1. A venture capital firm that invests minority equity in early-stage robotics, physical AI and deep technology startups.
2. The firm delivers seed capital and strategic guidance to portfolio companies in exchange for minority equity stakes.
3. The firm serves early-stage technology startups and entrepreneurs seeking financial backing.
4. The firm supplies financial capital from the sidelines of the physical AI value chain to startup companies developing hardware and software.
5. The firm pairs early-stage funding with strategic guidance and a cross-continental collaboration network bridging United States and Southeast Asian markets.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held, early-stage venture capital firm and limited liability company affiliated with a parent holding company.
Business model: The organization makes money through venture capital fund management and minority equity returns on startup investments.
Scale and maturity: A moderately established firm with a growing portfolio of more than 40 funded startups and a recent expansion from the United States into Southeast Asia.
Geography: Headquartered in Akron, Ohio, with primary investment operations concentrated in the Midwest and Northeast Ohio and a strategic expansion into Singapore.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, the firm focuses capital allocation on a diversified portfolio of HardTech ventures addressing systemic global challenges across agricultural, clean and deep technology sectors.

points.name: DEEPX
points.description: South Korean technology startup designing ultra-low-power neural processing units for on-device AI inference in physical systems.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs ultra-low-power neural processing units and software for on-device AI inference in edge devices, targeting makers of robots, industrial systems, and smart cameras.
1. A chip company that designs low-power NPUs and accelerator modules for on-device inference.
2. Neural processing units in low-power SoCs, using a proprietary quantization stack that compresses FP32 models to INT8 with minimal accuracy loss and an on-chip compiler that translates ML framework models at runtime.
3. On-device inference, vision processing, and real-time edge AI execution for battery-powered and thermal-constrained machines.
4. Chips, M.2 form-factor modules, and accelerator boards, paired with a software development kit for model optimization and deployment.
5. Robotics, industrial computers, edge gateways, smart cameras, smart mobility, factory automation, and smart city infrastructure.
6. Robot makers, industrial computer and gateway manufacturers, camera makers, embedded hardware vendors, and systems integrators.
7. Its chips and modules are designed into edge devices and accelerator boards built by hardware partners.
8. It delivers up to 25 TOPS at INT8 precision within a sub-5W power envelope, achieving high energy efficiency through on-chip compilation and aggressive model quantization.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Samsung Foundry, Raspberry Pi, Sixfab, Advantech, Hyundai Robotics LAB, Wind River, Baidu PaddlePaddle, and Ultralytics.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Chip and module sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018, with over 140 employees, over 400 patents pending, and more than 50 customer projects in production.
Geography: Based in South Korea, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: The company's entire focus is designing and commercializing ultra-low-power AI semiconductors and associated software for on-device inference.

points.name: UC San Diego
points.description: Public research university advancing secure AI hardware design and humanoid robotics research.
points.bullets:
A public research university that conducts edge and physical AI research across silicon, algorithms, systems and testing infrastructure. It designs neural network accelerators, develops mobile manipulation and dexterous grasping policies, builds verification tools for cyber-physical systems and operates an outdoor UAV testing facility, for academic and industry researchers.
1. A university research lab that develops neural processing hardware, robot autonomy software and verification tools for academic research.
2. Silicon microdisk-based convolutional neural network accelerators combining analog photonics with memristor-based memory, whole-body mobile manipulation policies, and automated reasoning tools for synthesizing and verifying cyber-physical systems.
3. On-device inference acceleration, mobile base navigation with dexterous manipulation, and formal verification of complex cyber-physical systems.
4. Research systems, prototypes and software tools developed for academic and collaborative research.
5. Humanoid robots, mobile manipulators and unmanned aerial vehicles.
6. Academic researchers, robotics engineers and industry collaborators.
7. Its research prototypes and algorithms are adopted and extended by industry and academic researchers into physical machines and systems.
8. It combines analog photonic accelerator design with mobile dexterous manipulation research and formal cyber-physical system verification under one institution.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Brain Corporation.
Organization type: A public research university.
Business model: Federally funded research grants, academic budgets and industry collaborations.
Scale and maturity: A large public research university hosting a dedicated robotics institute and an outdoor UAV testing facility.
Geography: Based in San Diego, California, USA.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a comprehensive university with broad academic, scientific and engineering programs beyond physical AI.

points.name: PepsiCo
points.description: Multinational food and beverage company deploying driverless delivery trucks and digital twin technology across US supply chains.
points.bullets:
A food and beverage manufacturer and logistics operator that deploys autonomous trucks, digital twins, and vision-based warehouse inventory systems in its supply chain and production facilities. It integrates and operates automation technologies and autonomous middle-mile freight services from external vendors rather than building robots or AI itself.
1. A consumer goods manufacturer and logistics operator that deploys autonomous trucks, robotic warehouse systems, and digital twin technology in its own facilities and supply chain.
2. Autonomous middle-mile freight transport, digital twin production line optimization, and high-speed vision-based warehouse inventory reading.
3. Integration services and operated fleets: driverless trucks operated by a vendor in its supply chain, and vision and simulation software deployed in its own facilities.
4. Middle-mile logistics, warehouses, and production lines.
5. Internal supply chain and manufacturing operations.
6. It buys, deploys, and operates automation, robots, and autonomy services from external vendors in its own manufacturing and logistics operations.
7. It applies digital twin technology to identify most potential production issues before physical implementation and achieves double-digit throughput increases.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include autonomous trucking, robotics, simulation, and AI vision vendors.
Organization type: A publicly traded multinational corporation.
Business model: Manufactures and sells food and beverage products, using automation to optimize internal logistics and production.
Scale and maturity: A global enterprise operating a fleet of dozens of driverless trucks across multiple states and deploying automation in major production facilities.
Geography: Based in the United States, with autonomous truck deployments in Texas, Arizona, and Arkansas.
Beyond physical AI: It is one of the world's largest food and beverage companies.

points.name: Fourier
points.description: Chinese robotics company building humanoid robots for medical rehabilitation and industrial automation.
points.bullets:
A humanoid robot maker that builds general-purpose bipedal robots and rehabilitation exoskeletons, integrating on-device AI, multimodal perception and custom actuators into complete hardware-software platforms for healthcare, research and industrial customers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells humanoid robots and rehabilitation robotics platforms.
2. Bipedal humanoid platforms with detachable batteries, tactile sensors and custom actuators, trained using GPU physics simulation and simulation-to-real transfer.
3. General-purpose humanoid locomotion, medical rehabilitation, physical patient interaction and clinical research support.
4. Complete robots and exoskeletons, plus an open development platform for research institutions.
5. Hospitals, rehabilitation centers, warehouses, factories and clinical research settings.
6. Hospitals, research and development institutions, logistics operators and manufacturers.
7. It designs and builds complete robots and exoskeletons that are deployed directly into clinical and industrial facilities.
8. It translates a medical exoskeleton and rehabilitation heritage into general-purpose humanoids with clinical safety features and established institutional distribution.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab for simulation, and included in the NVIDIA GR00T training set; National Instruments and the University of Melbourne for research platforms.
Organization type: Privately held company operating a specialized rehabilitation subsidiary.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robots, exoskeletons and research platforms to institutions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, producing approximately 5,000 robotic units annually and deployed across over 2,000 institutions in 40 countries.
Geography: Headquartered in Shanghai with research and development labs in Singapore and Malaysia, operating primarily across Asia-Pacific and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation are its entire focus.

points.name: Rokid
points.description: Chinese AR glasses manufacturer building smart wearables that run on-device AI for real-time translation and visual assistance.
points.bullets:
A wearable device maker that designs and manufactures AI and augmented reality glasses for consumers and enterprises, building complete systems that integrate third-party inference silicon, camera modules, and cloud-connected AI services.
1. A wearable device maker that designs and manufactures smart glasses and sells them as finished hardware products to consumers and enterprises.
2. A dual-chip architecture using a low-power microcontroller for baseline tasks and a neural processing unit for on-device AI workloads, combined with micro-LED diffraction waveguide optical systems and camera modules.
3. On-device inference for real-time translation, contextual digital overlays, gaze-based payments, hands-free voice control, and remote collaboration.
4. Complete smart glasses and augmented reality wearables.
5. Consumer eyewear, museums and cultural institutions, manufacturing, education, hospitality, and healthcare.
6. Consumers, cultural institutions, enterprises, and a developer ecosystem of registered creators.
7. Its finished wearables are sold directly to end users and enterprises for physical-world task enhancement and digital interaction.
8. It prioritizes lightweight, affordable, fashion-forward designs focused on practical AI assistant capabilities over social media or entertainment features.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It integrates silicon from Qualcomm and NXP, cloud AI models and services from OpenAI, Google and Alibaba, and payment and fitness systems from Alipay and Garmin.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of smart glasses.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, the company has reached a C+ funding stage, reports over 2.5 million users, and maintains a developer ecosystem of over 6,200 creators.
Geography: Based in China, operating across domestic and international consumer and enterprise markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, augmented reality, and physical-world task enhancement represent the organization's entire focus.

points.name: NSF Athena AI Institute
points.description: US government research institute developing foundational AI technologies for networked edge devices.
points.bullets:
A government research institute that conducts foundational research on AI-driven edge computing technologies and algorithmic paradigms for resource-constrained networked devices, funded by national science and security agencies for academic and industrial collaborators.
1. A government agency that funds and operates foundational edge computing and AI research programs.
2. Algorithmic foundations and computing paradigms designed to run AI models efficiently on distributed networked hardware.

Scale and maturity: It is a commercialized startup selected for an accelerator program with established partnerships with major silicon vendors.
Geography: It is based in Montreal, Canada and operates within global technology ecosystems.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and 3D vision technology represent the entire focus of this pure-play organization.

points.name: Google Cloud
points.description: Cloud services division providing edge inference infrastructure, AI security analytics, and robotics software integration.
points.bullets:
A cloud provider that offers enterprise cloud infrastructure, on-device ML benchmarking tools, and edge connectivity for robotics and industrial automation, running models and data pipelines for automakers, manufacturers, and robotics software developers.
1. A cloud provider that builds cloud infrastructure, on-premises distributed cloud appliances, and an on-device ML benchmarking portal delivered as cloud services and managed platforms.
2. Arm-based data center processors, tensor processing units, cloud data warehouses, and edge gateways running over 270 industrial protocols to connect factory floor devices.
3. Cloud-based model training, on-device machine learning model benchmarking, industrial data ingestion and processing, and conversational AI.
4. Cloud APIs, managed SaaS platforms, on-premises distributed cloud hardware appliances, and edge gateways.
5. Factory automation, automotive infotainment, supply chain logistics, autonomous driving development, and robotic operations management.
6. Automakers, manufacturers, logistics operators, robotics software developers, and enterprises.
7. Its cloud infrastructure and AI models are consumed by device makers, automakers, and industrial operators to run their own workloads and connect their physical assets.
8. It provides a hyperscale cloud platform that spans from data center tensor processing units down to edge connectivity gateways for industrial protocols and on-device ML benchmarking.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with robotics software developers, automotive OEMs, industrial automation integrators, and chip design automation tool providers.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded technology company.
Business model: Cloud infrastructure rentals, software subscriptions, managed platform fees, and professional services.
Scale and maturity: A major global hyperscaler involved in multi-billion-dollar international AI infrastructure partnerships and enterprise deployments worldwide.
Geography: Based in the USA and operating globally, including significant infrastructure partnerships in the Middle East.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it provides general-purpose enterprise cloud computing, generative AI models, productivity software, data analytics, and cybersecurity platforms.

points.name: Ampere
points.description: Semiconductor company designing power-efficient Arm-based processors to optimize cloud and edge AI inference workloads.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs Arm-based processors for cloud and edge inference, supplying high-core-count CPUs used in server and module computing for data centers and edge systems.
1. A chip company that designs Arm-based CPUs for cloud and edge inference.
2. Arm-based processors with high core counts optimized for power efficiency and density in inference workloads.
3. Server-class on-device and cloud inference processing with high utilization and low power consumption.
4. Chips and processor modules sold to system integrators and cloud providers.
5. Data centers, edge computing systems and autonomous driving infrastructure.
6. Edge computing module makers and cloud infrastructure operators.
7. Its processors are designed into edge computing modules by embedded system makers and deployed in cloud servers by infrastructure operators.
8. It targets inference workloads with Arm-based architectures that emphasize affordability, power efficiency and high utilization over traditional x86 server CPUs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with edge computing module maker ADLINK and cloud infrastructure operator Uber.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales.
Scale and maturity: It is a established public company supplying processors at cloud scale.
Geography: It is based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Its focus extends to general cloud and data center computing beyond edge and physical AI.

points.name: NIST
points.description: United States government agency developing standards and test methods for manufacturing robotics and physical AI deployment.
aliases: National Institute of Standards and Technology
points.bullets:
A government agency that develops metrics, test methods, and risk frameworks to accelerate the adoption of AI-enhanced robotics and embodied AI in manufacturing environments.
1. A government agency that develops standards, benchmarking methodologies, and cooperative funding programs for advanced manufacturing technologies.
2. Measurement protocols, standardized task benchmark boards, and structured risk management frameworks that evaluate trustworthiness and lifecycle governance in AI systems.
3. Performance validation, physical safety evaluation for human-robot collaboration, calibration standards for sensors, and governance frameworks for AI-enabled robotic systems.
4. Voluntary governance frameworks, public-private partnership programs, cooperative funding agreements, and standardized benchmark datasets.
5. Factories and manufacturing facilities using AI-enhanced robotics, automation equipment, and AI governance processes.
6. Manufacturing industry partners, robotics integrators, academic institutions, equipment makers, and federal contractors.
7. Its frameworks and standards are adopted by equipment makers and integrators to validate and govern the deployment of AI in physical systems.
8. Its federal authority to develop consensus standards and its comprehensive AI Risk Management Framework make it the central validating body for physical AI systems in U.S. manufacturing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The U.S. Department of Commerce, the Manufacturing USA network, and the ARM Institute.
Organization type: A U.S. federal agency under the Department of Commerce.
Business model: Federal funding allocation, cooperative agreements, and government-sponsored research programs.
Scale and maturity: A long-established federal institution that administers national manufacturing programs and releases frameworks adopted across state, federal, and international regulations.
Geography: Based in the United States, focusing its standardization and operational efforts on the U.S. manufacturing sector.
Beyond physical AI: The organization maintains a broader mission of developing measurement science, standards, and technology to promote innovation and industrial competitiveness across all sectors.

points.name: U.S. Department of Energy Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy
points.description: US government agency funding autonomous laboratory robotics and AI-guided systems to accelerate industrial discovery and manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and oversees programs integrating edge AI with autonomous laboratory systems and robotic platforms to accelerate physical experimentation and manufacturing processes for national laboratories, universities, and early-stage startups.
1. A government agency that funds integrated workflows combining machine learning models, AI-guided design, and automated robotic hardware.
2. Machine learning models, AI-guided design, and automated robotic hardware integrated into complete physical experimentation workflows.
3. Autonomous laboratory systems, robotic platforms, and automated physical experimentation and manufacturing processes.
4. Non-dilutive funding and program oversight for integrated automation projects.
5. Laboratory automation, catalyst discovery, fuels, chemicals, biomass conversion, and specialty materials manufacturing.
6. National laboratories, universities, and early-stage startups.
7. It provides non-dilutive capital and early-stage systems integration to validate advanced technological breakthroughs before private venture capital is required.
8. It provides non-dilutive capital that preserves company equity while offering national-level technical validation without typical venture capital constraints.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: United States Department of Energy, American research institutions, and domestic startup ventures.
Organization type: A government agency operating under the United States Department of Energy.
Business model: Government funding of advanced technological programs.
Scale and maturity: A flagship initiative announced in 2026 is backed by $34 million supporting 12 projects, building on prior programs launched in 2019.
Geography: Based in the United States and exclusively funds and operates domestic projects involving American research institutions and startups.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is broadly dedicated to funding and accelerating high-potential, high-impact energy technologies to overcome critical energy and environmental challenges.

points.name: GE HealthCare
points.description: US healthcare company deploying on-device AI in medical imaging machines for automated diagnostic workflows.
points.bullets:
A medical device maker and systems integrator that builds AI-enabled imaging and patient monitoring equipment, embedding edge inference silicon and software platforms from semiconductor partners into finished clinical hardware and diagnostics for healthcare providers.
1. A medical device maker that builds and sells AI-enabled imaging systems, mobile radiography units and patient monitoring devices as integrated clinical hardware and software suites.
2. On-device AI algorithms for medical imaging that run on edge AI chips from semiconductor partners to perform automated image analysis and critical condition triage directly on the equipment.
3. On-device inference for pneumothorax detection in chest X-rays, real-time cardiac imaging analysis, mobile cone-beam computed tomography and continuous patient monitoring with actionable insights.
4. Complete medical devices and imaging systems, licensed clinical software suites and cloud-connected diagnostic platforms sold to healthcare facilities.
5. Hospitals, operating rooms, acute care settings, cardiac care units and mobile radiography environments.
6. Hospitals, healthcare providers and clinicians.
7. The company buys edge AI chips and software platforms from semiconductor and computing partners and integrates them into finished medical imaging equipment it sells to healthcare facilities.
8. The company holds the highest number of AI-enabled medical device authorizations from the Food and Drug Administration, supported by strict adherence to responsible AI principles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Intel, NVIDIA, NXP and the Mayo Clinic.
Organization type: A publicly traded company that operates as a standalone corporate entity.
Business model: Hardware sales of medical imaging systems, software licenses for clinical AI suites and cloud-enabled healthcare subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A mature organization with over 125 years of operation, approximately 53,000 employees and an extensive installed base of medical equipment worldwide.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates globally across the worldwide healthcare industry.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge AI and physical automation, the company provides a comprehensive portfolio of traditional medical technologies, pharmaceutical diagnostics and healthcare IT solutions.

points.name: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)
points.description: US government agency deploying AI systems for real-time air traffic management.
points.bullets:
A government agency that regulates and certifies civil aviation, including drones and autonomous aircraft, while operating and modernizing the national airspace system with edge AI infrastructure.
1. A government agency that regulates and operates national airspace infrastructure, deploying AI-powered air traffic management systems.
2. AI-powered air traffic management systems utilizing on-device inference to process real-time radar and flight data within 50-millisecond latency requirements.
3. Air traffic control modernization, regulatory certification for commercial drone operations, and beyond visual line of sight flight authorization.
4. Regulatory frameworks, airworthiness certifications, and contracted modernized air traffic control infrastructure.
5. National airspace, commercial drone delivery, and autonomous aviation.
6. Aviation operators, commercial drone delivery companies, autonomous aircraft developers, and the traveling public.
7. Its regulations and certifications govern the operation of commercial drones and autonomous aircraft, while its contracted systems integrate edge AI into national air traffic control infrastructure.
8. It serves a unique dual function as both the regulatory authority and the operational operator deploying edge AI to enhance human decision-making.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with the Department of Transportation, Transportation Security Administration, and industry partners including DoorDash, Amazon Prime Air, UPS Flight Forward, Reliable Robotics, Xwing, and Joby.
Organization type: A federal government agency.
Business model: Government funding and legislative appropriations.
Scale and maturity: Manages one of the government's largest edge AI deployments, supported by an initial $12.5 billion in legislative funding and an $875 million AI partnership contract.
Geography: Based and operates entirely within the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization comprehensively regulates and oversees all aspects of civil aviation, including communications, navigation, and surveillance infrastructure.

points.name: DOD
points.description: US government agency deploying ruggedized edge AI hardware and on-device inference to autonomous military platforms for real-time battlefield targeting.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds, procures, deploys and operates autonomous systems, AI software and physical robots for military use, serving its own internal defense forces and combatant commands.
1. A government agency that operates autonomous vehicles, drones and robotic systems and contracts for their underlying silicon, sensors and software.
2. Deployed edge AI inference hardware, autonomous navigation and perception software, and unmanned platforms integrated through joint command and control networks.
3. Autonomous navigation, intelligence surveillance and reconnaissance, drone swarms, robotic combat vehicles, tactical edge inference and battle management.
4. Complete unmanned aircraft, vessels and ground vehicles, licensed autonomy software, edge computing hardware and integration services acquired through procurement contracts and direct deployments.
5. Drones, unmanned surface vessels, robotic combat vehicles, autonomous logistics, defense bases and contested battlefield environments.
6. Military branches, combatant commands and allied defense forces.
7. It buys complete robots, vehicles and software from commercial suppliers and operates them directly within its own military organizations.
8. It imposes Directive 3000.09 requiring human judgment in lethal autonomous engagements while driving rapid fielding of thousands of attritable platforms through its Replicator initiative.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: DARPA, the Defense Innovation Unit, Purdue University, AeroVironment, Anduril, Shield AI, Kratos and Joby Aviation.
Organization type: Federal government agency and military department.
Business model: Congressional funding allocations and defense procurement contracts.
Scale and maturity: A vast military enterprise investing tens of billions of dollars annually in unmanned systems and AI.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating globally across its military commands.
Beyond physical AI: It is the national defense ministry responsible for all military operations, global logistics and national security.

points.name: Untether AI
points.description: Canadian semiconductor startup building energy-efficient inference chips for edge AI applications.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs ultra-efficient inference accelerators and chips for on-device edge AI in autonomous vehicles, agricultural machinery and industrial automation, using at-memory compute architecture.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V-based NPUs and accelerator cards for on-device inference.
2. Neural processing elements and RISC-V processors integrated directly within SRAM memory banks in an at-memory compute architecture that minimizes data movement to reduce energy consumption.
3. Low-power, high-throughput on-device inference for edge applications.
4. Chips, accelerator cards and inference devices sold to system integrators and automakers.
5. Autonomous vehicles, agricultural machinery and industrial automation.
6. Automakers, manufacturers and agricultural equipment builders.
7. Its inference chips are designed into autonomous vehicles and industrial machines by automakers and system integrators.
8. Its at-memory compute architecture places processing elements directly inside SRAM banks to eliminate the energy and latency costs of moving data between memory and processors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its technology was selected by Mercedes-Benz for next-generation autonomous vehicles, it raised funding from Intel Capital and Tracker Capital Management, and its assets were acquired by AMD.
Organization type: A privately held startup whose assets were acquired by a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip and accelerator card sales and hardware licensing.
Scale and maturity: A venture-backed startup that raised $125 million and was acquired in 2025.
Geography: Based in Toronto, Canada.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI inference silicon is its entire focus.

points.name: Natural Resources Canada
points.description: Canadian government agency funding machine learning solutions for natural resource sectors.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and conducts applied research and develops analytical software for the natural resource sectors, documenting the use of AI chipsets and automation in mining and forestry without building physical AI hardware itself.
1. A government agency that develops analytical software, remote sensing tools, and decision-support systems for resource industries.
2. Machine learning proofs of concept, analytical models, and remote sensing systems built by a federal Digital Accelerator.
3. Software, satellite missions, and government-funded research programs delivered to resource operators.
4. Mining, forestry, energy, and environmental monitoring operations.
5. Natural resource operators, government agencies, and academic researchers.
6. The agency funds digital transformation and co-creates technological solutions with industry and academia.
7. Its strategic position as a government-funded platform applies advanced techniques like quantum-AI diffusion models to specialized environmental challenges such as flood risk mapping and lumber pest detection.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Carleton University, Environment and Climate Change Canada, and the Canadian Space Agency.
Organization type: A federal government agency and science-based department.
Business model: Government funding of research, policy development, and technological initiatives.
Scale and maturity: An established federal department managing a $169.9 million satellite mission and operating a dedicated Digital Accelerator.
Geography: Based in Canada, directing its operational focus toward domestic natural resource sectors.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is fundamentally responsible for the stewardship, management, and regulatory oversight of Canada's energy, minerals, forests, and geographic data.

points.name: Google Nest
points.description: Consumer electronics company building smart home devices that process voice commands and sensor data locally on low-power AI chips.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics company that builds smart home devices incorporating low-power edge AI silicon for local voice recognition and activity detection, selling finished hardware directly to consumers.
1. A device maker that builds smart home electronics with embedded inference chips, sold as complete consumer hardware products.
2. Low-power neural processing units and supporting software runtimes run local inference for voice recognition and activity detection directly on consumer devices.
3. On-device inference, local voice recognition and activity detection.
4. Complete consumer electronics devices with embedded edge AI silicon, alongside developer modules for edge computing applications.
5. Smart home devices, consumer electronics and IoT products.
6. Consumers in the smart home market and developers using edge computing tools.
7. Its embedded inference silicon and software are integrated into finished consumer devices it manufactures and sells itself.
8. A vertically integrated approach pairs custom, energy-efficient inference silicon with proprietary software tools to enable fast, privacy-preserving local processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a division of a publicly traded multinational technology conglomerate.
Organization type: A division of a publicly traded multinational technology conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of finished consumer electronics.
Scale and maturity: It operates at a massive global scale leveraging the vast resources of its parent company.
Geography: It is based in North America and focuses its operations and market reach primarily on consumers within that region.
Beyond physical AI: The parent company operates massive global businesses in cloud computing, search, software and digital advertising.

points.name: FuriosaAI
points.description: South Korean fabless AI chip startup building high-efficiency inference accelerators for enterprise edge deployment.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs neural processing units for enterprise and data-center inference, building high-efficiency AI accelerators for computer vision and large language models. It supplies individual accelerator cards and fully integrated inference servers to enterprises, targeting high-performance inference workloads with low power consumption.
1. A fabless semiconductor company that designs neural processing units and inference accelerators, sold as chips, accelerator cards and integrated inference servers.
2. The core technology is a proprietary Tensor Contraction Processor architecture built on a 5nm process node, optimized for parallel processing and reduced memory access latency to maximize compute density and power efficiency.
3. It delivers high-efficiency inference for large language models, multimodal models and computer vision, providing stable multi-user processing and high FP8 and INT8 throughput.
4. Customers receive it as accelerator cards, individual chips and fully integrated multi-accelerator inference servers.
5. The accelerators are used in data centers, edge servers, healthcare, retail, finance, manufacturing, telecommunications and VR/AR settings.
6. It sells to enterprise data center operators, telecommunications companies and technology integrators.
7. Its chips and accelerator cards are designed into inference servers and sovereign AI appliances built by system integrators and telecommunications providers.
8. Its approach distinguishes itself through superior tokens-per-watt performance that enables standard data-center deployment without requiring liquid cooling or specialized facility infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with TSMC for foundry manufacturing, Arm for system-level efficiency, LG Uplus for sovereign AI appliances, Equinix for data center deployment, Rambus for controller IP, Hugging Face for model integration and Broadcom for third-generation accelerator development.
Organization type: It is a privately held fabless semiconductor startup preparing for an IPO.
Business model: It makes money through the sale of inference chips, accelerator cards and integrated inference servers.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, the company has shipped two generations of AI chips, secured over $250 million in Series C bridge funding and aims to grow its workforce to 200.
Geography: It is based in South Korea with offices in Silicon Valley and a compiler-focused R&D lab in Lisbon, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: The development of artificial intelligence hardware and its accompanying software ecosystem represents the entire focus of this pure-play company.

points.name: Samsung Foundry
points.description: South Korean semiconductor foundry manufacturing low-power chips for on-device AI inference and physical-world automation.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor foundry that manufactures advanced inference chips on leading-edge nodes for AI chip developers. It fabricates accelerators and NPUs used for on-device AI and physical-world automation, supplying advanced process silicon, memory integration, and multi-die packaging rather than complete deployed systems.
1. A semiconductor foundry that builds advanced logic process silicon and IP for AI chip designers.
2. Advanced logic process technology including 5nm, 4nm, and 2nm gate-all-around transistors, combined with embedded flash memory IP and multi-die packaging.
3. High-volume silicon manufacturing, logic design, layout, verification, and advanced packaging for edge inference accelerators.
4. Wafers and foundry services delivered to fabless chip companies, including process technology licensing and IP alliances.
5. Edge servers, autonomous vehicles, smart cameras, robotics, and on-device AI hardware.
6. Fabless AI semiconductor startups, accelerator developers, and technology firms.
7. Its fabricated silicon is designed into AI chips that device makers integrate into robots, cameras, and vehicles.
8. A vertically integrated platform that combines advanced process nodes, high-bandwidth memory, and multi-die packaging in a one-stop offering.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: DeepX, Rebellions, Tenstorrent, SEMIBRAIN, ANAFLASH, and Rambus.
Organization type: A division of a publicly traded global conglomerate.
Business model: Wafer manufacturing contracts, foundry services, and IP ecosystem licensing.
Scale and maturity: One of the top five global semiconductor foundries by market share, posting record AI-chip revenue and aggressive capacity allocation.
Geography: Based in South Korea, with a strategic focus on domestic AI customers and global deployment sectors.
Beyond physical AI: A division of a globally diversified technology conglomerate spanning consumer electronics, digital media, and telecommunications equipment.

points.name: Pegatron
points.description: Taiwanese electronics manufacturer integrating edge-AI modules and building robotic systems to digitalize factory operations.
points.bullets:
An electronics manufacturer and systems integrator that builds robotic systems and integrates edge-AI modules into consumer and industrial devices, using digital-twin and simulation platforms to automate its own circuit-board factories.
1. A systems integrator and electronics manufacturer that builds robotic systems and installs factory automation for device makers.
2. Factory digitalization built on simulation, synthetic data generation, and edge-AI module integration for automated electronics assembly.
3. Factory simulation, digital-twin operations, automated circuit-board manufacturing, and edge-AI module integration for consumer and industrial devices.
4. Integration services, manufactured electronic components, and robotic systems installed in production lines.
5. Electronics factories, circuit-board production lines, consumer devices, and industrial devices.
6. Electronics OEMs, consumer device brands, and industrial equipment manufacturers.
7. It designs and operates automation in its own manufacturing facilities and integrates edge-AI hardware for device makers.
8. It combines large-scale electronics manufacturing with digital-twin simulation to automate and optimize its own factory operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with NVIDIA for simulation, Omniverse, Isaac, and Metropolis platforms, DeepX for edge-AI modules, Foxconn for module integration, and MIT CSAIL for robotics research.
Organization type: A publicly traded electronics manufacturer and systems integrator.
Business model: Electronics manufacturing services, systems integration contracts, and produced components and robotic systems.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale global electronics manufacturer operating extensive production facilities.
Geography: Based in Taiwan with global manufacturing operations.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, it is a major contract manufacturer of consumer electronics, computers, and communications devices.

points.name: SiMa.ai
points.description: US AI chip startup designing embedded processors for on-device machine learning inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs power-efficient machine learning system-on-chip platforms and companion software for on-device inference, targeting embedded edge and physical AI applications. The company supplies its unified hardware and software stack to original equipment manufacturers and systems integrators who need to run computer vision and generative AI workloads locally on battery-powered or power-constrained machines.
1. A chip company that designs machine learning system-on-chips for on-device inference.
2. Neural processing units integrated into low-power system-on-chips manufactured on a 6nm process, paired with a proprietary software suite for static scheduling, quantization and compilation.
3. On-device inference, computer vision processing, vision transformer and convolutional neural network acceleration, and local execution of large language and multimodal models.
4. Chips, system-on-modules, PCIe cards and developer kits, along with licensed software development platforms.
5. Industrial automation, automotive advanced driver-assistance systems, aerospace and defense systems, robotics, smart vision and medical devices.
6. Industrial original equipment manufacturers, edge appliance makers, automotive suppliers, defense agencies, robotics builders and medical device manufacturers.
7. Its chips and modules are designed into industrial computers, automotive systems and defense platforms by hardware manufacturers.
8. It combines a software-centric unified platform supporting any framework or sensor with high power efficiency for embedded edge inference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Arm, Synopsys, TSMC, Wind River, Emerson, Advantech, Lanner, Kontron and Supermicro.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Chip and module sales, along with software licenses and developer hardware kit sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018 and has raised $270 million in total funding.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California and operates globally through technology partnerships.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and embedded edge machine learning are the entire focus of the company.

points.name: NEC
points.description: Japanese technology company building on-device AI models that predict human movement and stress to enable safe human-robot collaboration.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded technology company that develops physical AI models, world models, and digital twin software for industrial robotics, providing robot task planning and human-robot collaboration systems for manufacturing customers.
1. An AI model and software developer whose physical AI frameworks, world models, and digital twin planning services are licensed to manufacturing operations.
2. Proprietary AI algorithms and world models that predict human movement and mental states in real time, along with digital twin technology that automatically generates synchronized multi-robot motion plans.
3. Automated robot teaching, coordinated multi-robot operations, human movement and stress prediction, and safe human-robot collaboration in shared workspaces.
4. Licensed software, AI algorithms, and digital twin services integrated with existing robot simulation platforms.
5. Factory automation, warehouse logistics, and spacecraft production facilities.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, and aerospace companies.
7. Its software and AI models are integrated into manufacturing facilities and combined with robot simulation platforms by industrial technology providers.
8. A world model AI framework that predicts human movements and quantitatively estimates human stress levels in real time so robots can autonomously adjust their paths.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Siemens, Lockheed Martin, Sony, Honda, and SoftBank.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Software licenses, AI technology licensing, and integration services.
Scale and maturity: A global corporation established in 1899 with approximately 110,000 employees.
Geography: Based in Japan with operations worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: The company provides broader IT, network, security, communications, facial recognition, and procurement AI technologies across public services, retail, healthcare, and aerospace industries.

points.name: Ceva, Inc.
points.description: Semiconductor IP licensing company designing neural processing units and software for on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor IP company that licenses neural processing unit and digital signal processor architectures, along with software development kits, to chipmakers for on-device inference across smart edge devices.
1. A semiconductor IP company that designs NPUs and DSPs and licenses them to other semiconductor companies.
2. Neural processing units and AI digital signal processors designed for ultra-low-power on-device inference, complemented by sensor fusion processors and wireless connectivity IP.
3. On-device AI inference, voice recognition, always-on sensing, and TinyML execution for battery-powered edge devices.
4. Licensable silicon IP and software toolkits integrated by customers into their systems-on-chip.
5. Smart edge devices spanning consumer electronics, automotive advanced driver assistance systems, industrial IoT, personal computing, and infrastructure.
6. Semiconductor companies, original equipment manufacturers, and microcontroller vendors.
7. Its NPU and DSP IP cores are designed into systems-on-chip by semiconductor companies and device makers.
8. It combines self-contained neural processing units with sensor fusion and wireless connectivity IP to enable independent operation without a host CPU, reducing power consumption and system complexity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Microchip Technology, Nextchip, ALi Corp, Flex Logix, Visionary.ai, ENOT.ai, Texas Instruments, and the EDGE AI FOUNDATION.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Silicon and software IP licensing, generating revenue through licensing fees and royalties.
Scale and maturity: A mature company with technology deployed in over 20 billion devices across more than 400 customers worldwide.
Geography: Based in Rockville, Maryland, USA, with a global customer base.
Beyond physical AI: The company provides broader digital signal processing and wireless connectivity solutions for embedded technologies beyond physical AI.

points.name: ALi Corp
points.description: Semiconductor company integrating neural processing units into video display platforms for on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company and ASIC design services provider that builds multimedia systems-on-chip and video display subsystems integrating licensed neural processing units for edge AI acceleration in consumer electronics and industrial devices.
1. A chip company that designs multimedia SoC platforms and provides ASIC design services for original design manufacturers and original equipment manufacturers.
2. Neural processing units integrated into video display subsystems built on proprietary hardware IP and software for 4K/8K video processing and AI acceleration.
3. On-device inference and video display acceleration for custom high-performance ASICs.
4. Platforms and ASIC design services delivered to semiconductor partners and device makers.
5. Digital signage, automotive, smart devices, consumer electronics, and industrial video platforms.
6. Original design manufacturers, original equipment manufacturers, and semiconductor partners.
7. Its platforms and licensed NPUs are designed into custom ASICs by device and chip makers.
8. Combines deep multimedia and video codec expertise with integrated AI acceleration to offer a complete end-to-end ASIC design service portfolio that simplifies system-on-chip development.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ceva for NPU licensing.
Organization type: Privately held company operating as a platform and semiconductor design services provider.
Business model: Platform licensing and ASIC design services contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established, active semiconductor design organization with a strategic NPU integration agreement established in August 2025.
Geography: Based and operating globally within the semiconductor industry.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization provides comprehensive system planning, RTL design, optimization, fabrication, and testing grounded in broad proprietary hardware and software expertise in video codecs and display systems.

points.name: Nextchip
points.description: Semiconductor company designing system-on-chips for in-vehicle vision processing and on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs automotive system-on-chips integrating neural processing units, GPUs and image signal processors for advanced driver assistance systems. It licenses third-party NPU IP and builds its own domain controllers to enable real-time vision processing and sensor fusion on-device. It sells these chips to automotive Tier 1 suppliers and original equipment manufacturers.
1. A chip company that designs ADAS system-on-chips for automotive perception and inference.
2. Neural processing units, GPUs and image signal processors integrated into automotive domain controllers for sensor fusion and vision processing.
3. On-device inference, sensor fusion, pedestrian automatic emergency braking, thermal sensing and automotive vision processing.
4. Chips sold to automotive Tier 1 suppliers and original equipment manufacturers.
5. Advanced driver assistance systems in passenger vehicles.
6. Automotive Tier 1 suppliers and original equipment manufacturers.
7. Its chips are designed into ADAS modules and vehicle systems by automotive Tier 1 suppliers and original equipment manufacturers.
8. It combines scalable neural processing unit architectures with integrated image signal processing in a single automotive domain controller targeting entry-level ADAS compliance with European safety standards.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It licenses neural processing unit IP from Ceva.
Organization type: A privately held or publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Semiconductor chip sales.
