Scale and maturity: It targets a high-growth ADAS market segment projected to reach $122.8 billion by 2030 and tests its products for compliance with EURO NCAP 5 STAR requirements.
Geography: It demonstrates global ambitions by testing its products for compliance with European safety requirements and targeting international automotive and smart city markets.
Beyond physical AI: Automotive semiconductors and edge AI vision processing constitute the organization's entire focus, as it actively expands from camera-centric automotive safety into broader sensor markets for industrial IoT and smart cities.

points.name: Kneron
points.description: San Diego startup designing neural processing chips for on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs reconfigurable neural processing units and full-stack edge AI software to run large language models and vision algorithms directly on physical devices. The organization provides low-power AI inference silicon, compact edge servers, and developer platforms to device manufacturers for privacy-sensitive, on-premises workloads.
1. A chip company that designs NPUs and edge AI SoCs for on-device inference.
2. Reconfigurable neural processing unit architecture integrated into low-power SoCs, utilizing RISC-V and Arm cores alongside proprietary compression for efficient transformer and convolutional network execution.
3. On-device inference of large language models, vision transformer processing, real-time natural language processing, and intelligent vision for low-power, resource-constrained environments.
4. Chips, AI accelerator modules, developer boards, and rack-scale edge GPT servers.
5. Autonomous driving, smart home devices, security cameras, enterprise edge servers, robotics, and IoT sensors.
6. Device manufacturers, OEMs, system integrators, enterprises, hospitals, universities, and government agencies.
7. Its chips and software are designed into autonomous vehicles, smart home devices, and edge servers by device manufacturers.
8. It delivers high computational capacity at ultra-low power consumption, enabling large language model inference at the edge without additional cooling infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include Qualcomm, Sequoia Capital, and Foxconn, and its edge servers are used by Stanford University.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Chip sales, hardware sales, and developer platform distribution.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, the company has raised $200 million in funding and has over 28,000 developers on its platform.
Geography: Headquartered in San Diego, California, with deployments spanning the Asia-Pacific region and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play edge artificial intelligence provider with no business outside of physical AI and on-device inference.

points.name: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. Ltd.
points.description: Taiwanese electronics manufacturer deploying AI robotics platforms for automated factory assembly and inspection.
aliases: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd.
points.bullets:
A contract electronics manufacturer and systems integrator that develops intelligent factory automation, integrating AI vision models and robotics into full-scale factory orchestration for electronics assembly, and also invests in edge AI silicon.
1. A systems integrator and component supplier that designs and installs AI-driven factory automation for OEMs.
2. Web-based developer environments, AI vision models, and intelligent robotics integrated into factory orchestration systems.
3. Adaptive and flexible electronics assembly, factory automation, and full-scale factory orchestration.
4. Integration services, deployed automation systems, and supplied components and subsystems.
5. Electronics assembly factories and manufacturing facilities.
6. Original equipment manufacturers and the broader electronics manufacturing sector.
7. It integrates AI models and robotics into deployed factory systems and supplies components to OEMs.
8. It combines immense traditional manufacturing expertise with software-first AI robotics platforms through strategic joint ventures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Invested $49 million in Kneron's 2023 funding round.
Organization type: A publicly traded, global contract manufacturing conglomerate and subsidiary of Hon Hai Technology Group.
Business model: Contract manufacturing, component sales, and integration services.
Scale and maturity: A well-established manufacturing giant operating a massive global manufacturing footprint, deploying AI-driven systems in multi-phased factories in the United States.
Geography: Based in Taiwan, with a massive global manufacturing footprint including operations in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, the broader organization is a comprehensive contract electronics manufacturer strategically investing in electric vehicles and digital health.

points.name: TEMPO
points.description: Belgian research consortium developing neuromorphic computing hardware for efficient on-device inference in autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
A research consortium that investigates neuromorphic computing to enable efficient on-device AI for physical automation and autonomous robots, spanning the full stack from neuromorphic hardware acceleration to embodied AI model design for academic and industrial partners.
1. A research consortium that develops neuromorphic computing hardware substrates and foundational models for edge AI, delivering research outputs rather than commercial products.
2. Brain-inspired neuromorphic computing hardware, spike encoding strategies and embodied intelligence models designed for low-power on-device inference.
3. Low-latency, low-power on-device inference and foundational models for autonomous navigation and physical automation under tight memory and energy constraints.
4. Research outcomes and prototypes transferred to embedded platforms through collaborative projects with partner institutions.
5. Warehouse automation, autonomous navigation, industrial inspection, precision agriculture and general-purpose robotics.
6. Academic researchers, microelectronics partner institutions and organizations developing physical AI systems.
7. Its research outputs are integrated into embedded platforms and physical AI systems by partner institutions.
8. It targets the severe latency, power and memory constraints that currently prevent the widespread adoption of intelligent robots in unstructured physical environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A consortium of 19 partner institutions leveraging the infrastructure of a broader European microelectronics research ecosystem.
Organization type: A research consortium of approximately 150 to 250 researchers distributed across 19 partner institutions.
Business model: Research funding and collaborative grants translating foundational academic studies into practical embedded implementations.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019 with approximately 150 to 250 researchers across 19 partner organizations.
Geography: Headquartered and conducting research activities in Leuven, Belgium, within a prominent European microelectronics center.
Beyond physical AI: Developing brain-inspired computational paradigms to power autonomous physical systems is the central mission and sole focus of the organization.

points.name: Sandia National Laboratories
points.description: US government research facility developing neuromorphic computing hardware and software for energy-efficient, on-device inference in defense systems.
points.bullets:
A government research laboratory that develops neuromorphic computing hardware, software, and algorithms for energy-efficient on-device inference at the physical edge, primarily for national security applications.
1. A government laboratory that develops neuromorphic computing architectures and training algorithms for low-power edge inference.
2. Core technology comprises bio-inspired spiking neural networks, reservoir architectures for time-varying data, and training methods that progressively sharpen activation functions for deployment on neuromorphic hardware.
3. Specific capabilities include low-power on-device inference, rapid adaptation for autonomous systems, and robust sensor processing for edge environments.
4. Technology is delivered through research programs, hardware deployments at its own facilities, and computational tools licensed to partners.
5. Applications include edge artificial intelligence for defense infrastructure, autonomous systems, and sensor processing in constrained environments.
6. Primary customers are government agencies within the defense and intelligence communities, specifically the National Nuclear Security Administration.
7. It operates at the foundational research level, developing neuromorphic hardware and software architectures that it tests in its own facilities and transfers to government partners.
8. The approach targets extreme size, weight, and power constraints by leveraging bio-inspired spiking neural networks and local learning rules to achieve massive compute-per-watt improvements over traditional computing systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Intel and SpiNNcloud, with funding from the National Nuclear Security Administration's Advanced Simulation and Computing program.
Organization type: It is a government research laboratory operated for the Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration.
Business model: Operations are funded through federal government appropriations and specific program allocations for advanced computing and national security research.
Scale and maturity: It is a large, well-established national laboratory with decades of research history and multiple major computing deployments.
Geography: It is based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and conducts advanced research and supercomputer deployments locally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical artificial intelligence, the organization maintains a broad mandate for advanced scientific computing, cybersecurity, and nuclear deterrence programs.

points.name: UK Multidisciplinary Centre for Neuromorphic Computing
points.description: UK research center developing brain-inspired, energy-efficient computing hardware for edge AI and autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
A government-funded university research center that develops brain-inspired, energy-efficient neuromorphic computing technologies for edge AI and autonomous systems, spanning materials science, photonic devices, algorithms and proof-of-concept subsystems for multiple sectors.
1. A research lab that builds neuromorphic computing hardware and algorithms and delivers them through published research and proof-of-concept demonstrations.
2. Neuromorphic computing across the full stack, from basic materials and photonic device engineering through novel algorithms to prototype subsystems, informed by human stem cell-derived neuronal data for biological fidelity.
3. Energy-efficient, real-time computing for power-constrained edge environments and autonomous systems.
4. Research outputs, published papers and proof-of-concept subsystems rather than finished commercial products.
5. Healthcare, energy, advanced manufacturing, defence, telecommunications and autonomous systems.
6. Major technology firms, small enterprises and the academic research community.
7. It conducts fundamental and applied research that downstream chip and device makers may translate into commercial neuromorphic products.
8. It uses human stem cell-derived neuronal data to inform hardware and algorithm design with greater biological fidelity than conventional neuromorphic approaches.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Funded by EPSRC, led by the AiPT, with University of Oxford providing researchers and Microsoft Research as an industry partner.
Organization type: A government-funded academic research center and national interdisciplinary consortium drawing researchers from seven universities.
Business model: National research council grants and funding.
Scale and maturity: The first national interdisciplinary hub in its niche, established as a multi-university consortium backed by national research council funding.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom with consortium members distributed across the country and a regional technology-translation focus in the West Midlands.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is neuromorphic computing and physical AI development with no operations outside that field.

points.name: SynSense
points.description: Chinese technology company developing neuromorphic chips and sensors for ultra-low-power on-device inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs neuromorphic processors and event-based vision sensors for ultra-low-power, low-latency on-device inference, targeting edge AI and physical world interaction.
1. A chip and sensor company that designs neuromorphic inference silicon and dynamic vision sensors, sold as chips, IP blocks, development kits and integrated modules.
2. Mixed-signal and fully digital neuromorphic processors and event-driven dynamic vision sensors that use spiking neural networks for asynchronous sensory data processing.
3. Ultra-low-power, sub-millisecond on-device inference for visual, tactile, audio and motion perception, including obstacle avoidance, optical flow analysis and spatial localization.
4. Chips, smart sensors, neuromorphic development kits and IP blocks, alongside full-stack application development services for downstream integrators.
5. Robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, AR/VR glasses, brain-computer interfaces, smart grids, industrial monitoring and smart home devices.
6. Automakers, robotics and drone manufacturers, consumer electronics makers, industrial monitoring operators and ecosystem hardware partners.
7. Its processors and sensors are designed into edge devices and robotic systems by device makers and integrators.
8. Its fundamental neuromorphic architecture cuts power consumption by 100 to 1,000 times and improves latency by 10 to 100 times compared to traditional von Neumann computing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company merged with iniVation and co-develops neuromorphic monitoring systems with an automaker, while its chip is integrated into a smart module by an ecosystem partner.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Chip, sensor and IP sales alongside full-stack application development contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, the company operates multiple research and development centers and recently expanded through an acquisition.
Geography: Headquartered in China with research and development teams in Shanghai and Chengdu, and a subsidiary in Zurich.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation represent the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: ANDANTE-AI
points.description: French neuromorphic chip developer building power-efficient processors for IoT edge devices.
points.bullets:
A neuromorphic chip developer that builds ultra-low-power processors based on spiking neural networks for edge IoT and autonomous systems. It operates as a collaborative R&D consortium supplying foundational silicon and software platforms to downstream partners rather than selling end-user products. The organization targets partners building IoT edge products for indoor positioning, autonomous systems, medical imaging, warehouse automation, and digital farming.
1. A fabless chip developer that designs neuromorphic processors and software platforms for on-device inference at the edge.
2. Neuromorphic integrated circuits combining spiking neural networks with embedded non-volatile memory to enable persistent local learning without cloud connectivity.
3. Ultra-low-power on-device inference and local learning for intelligent physical systems.
4. Chips and software platforms supplied to downstream partners developing edge products.
5. Indoor positioning, autonomous systems, medical imaging, warehouse automation, and digital farming.
6. Semiconductor firms, design houses, sensor suppliers, and system integrators developing IoT edge products.
7. Its chips and software are designed into edge IoT products by downstream device makers and integrators.
8. Integration of embedded non-volatile memory with neuromorphic processors enables persistent, efficient local learning at the edge without cloud connectivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A consortium of 30 partner organizations across 7 European countries, including semiconductor firms, design houses, sensor suppliers, and system integrators.
Organization type: A collaborative research and development consortium.
Business model: Collaborative R&D and ecosystem development funded as a large-scale European project.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale European collaborative project uniting 30 partner organizations across 7 countries.
Geography: Based in Grenoble, France, with partners across seven European Union nations.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play entity whose entire focus is advancing neuromorphic computing hardware and software ecosystems for physical intelligence.

points.name: NimbleAI
points.description: Spanish neuromorphic chip developer building integrated sensors and processors that capture visual changes for low-power edge vision.
points.bullets:
A publicly funded research consortium that develops neuromorphic chips and event-based vision sensors for edge AI and physical automation. It designs 3D stacked silicon that integrates sensing and processing to cut energy and latency for visual perception at the edge. The project builds prototype platforms and EDA tools for robotics, industrial automation and space systems stakeholders.
1. A chip developer that designs neuromorphic sensing-and-processing chips and event-based vision sensors, delivered as prototype hardware and design tools.
2. 3D stacked neuromorphic silicon combining near-memory computing, RISC-V processors and FPGA-based acceleration with light-field dynamic vision sensors that transmit only meaningful visual state changes.
3. Ultra-low latency 3D perception and on-device inference under power constraints.
4. Prototype platforms, sensors, EDA tools and programming tools for testing algorithms.
5. Robotics, industrial automation and space systems.
6. Research institutions, semiconductor companies and industrial partners.
7. Its chips and sensors are designed into edge devices by industrial stakeholders.
8. 3D integrated neuromorphic chips transmit only meaningful visual data changes to achieve 100x energy efficiency and 50x latency reductions over conventional video processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A European consortium of research institutions and semiconductor and industrial partners funded under Horizon Europe.
Organization type: A collaborative, publicly funded research and development project.
Business model: Grant funding with structured exploitation strategies for future commercialization.
Scale and maturity: A recently concluded three-year project under Horizon Europe.
Geography: Based in Europe, advancing the region's technological sovereignty in edge computing.
Beyond physical AI: Advancing neuromorphic sensing and edge AI processing is its entire focus.

points.name: iniVation
points.description: Swiss neuromorphic vision company building bio-inspired event cameras and software for low-latency edge perception.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops neuromorphic event-based vision systems for real-time edge AI and robotics applications. The company builds bio-inspired Dynamic Vision Sensors and event cameras, along with processing software, for robotics, automotive, and aerospace customers. It is a subsidiary operating as part of a larger neuromorphic processing group.
1. A sensor maker that builds neuromorphic event cameras and dynamic vision sensors, sold as hardware modules and stereo vision kits.
2. Dynamic Vision Sensor pixels operate asynchronously, outputting events only when brightness changes, which provides ultra-low latency, high dynamic range, and low power consumption.
3. Ultra-low response latency, low data rates, high dynamic range, ultra-low power consumption, and concurrent event-based and frame-based sensing.
4. Customers get it as event camera modules, stereo vision kits, and software libraries.
5. Used in autonomous robotics, drone navigation, automotive systems, consumer electronics, aerospace, and extreme environments like space and Antarctica.
6. Sells to over 700 organizations across more than 40 countries, including robotics developers, automakers, consumer electronics companies, and aerospace organizations.
7. Its sensors are integrated into machines and platforms by device makers requiring real-time visual processing.
8. Founded by the inventors of event-based vision, it leverages a foundational R&D heritage to provide asynchronous pixel processing that outperforms conventional frame-based machine vision in speed and power efficiency.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates as a subsidiary of SynSense Group and uses Nvidia Jetson SOMs in some stereo vision products.
Organization type: Privately held subsidiary.
Business model: Hardware sales of event camera modules and kits.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2008 with deployments across over 700 organizations globally.
Geography: Based in Zurich, Switzerland, with deployments in over 40 countries.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are the organization's entire focus.

points.name: GSI Technology
points.description: US semiconductor company developing compute-in-memory processors for highly efficient edge AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs compute-in-memory processors for edge AI inference, supplying specialized silicon to defense contractors and robotics developers for power-constrained applications.
1. A chip company that designs compute-in-memory accelerators for edge AI inference.
2. Neuromorphic associative processing units perform computation directly inside memory arrays to avoid the energy cost of moving data in standard computing.
3. On-device inference for search-heavy workloads such as facial recognition and real-time Synthetic Aperture Radar processing.
4. Chips and silicon components designed for integration into larger hardware systems.
5. Drones, satellites, defense systems, robotics and smart city surveillance.
6. Defense contractors, drone manufacturers, robotics developers and smart city operators.
7. Its chips are designed into edge hardware systems by device makers.
8. It delivers GPU-class inference throughput with over 98 percent lower energy consumption than conventional graphics cards.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The U.S. Army selected it for a potential SBIR contract award, and Cornell University independently validated its compute-in-memory architectures.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales and self-funded research and development subsidized by a profitable static random-access memory business.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1995, it has invested $175 million of self-funded research and development into its next-generation processor families.
Geography: Headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, with sales offices in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond its edge AI initiatives, it operates a profitable static random-access memory business.

points.name: Everspin Technologies
points.description: United States semiconductor company manufacturing MRAM memory solutions for on-device inference and embedded AI systems.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs and manufactures Magnetoresistive RAM for non-volatile memory in edge AI accelerators, autonomous systems, and defense applications. It supplies persistent memory chips and IP that enable on-device inference and in-memory compute for industrial, automotive, and aerospace customers, and develops MRAM-based neural accelerators under military contracts.
1. A chip company that designs and sells MRAM memory chips and foundry IP for on-device inference and embedded AI systems.
2. Magnetoresistive RAM uses electron spin to store data, providing non-volatile memory that is immune to radiation and power loss and enables in-memory compute for neural accelerators.
3. Radiation-resistant persistent memory, instant state recovery after power restoration, and low-thermal-signature in-memory compute for edge AI.
4. Discrete memory chips, licensed MRAM IP, and foundry services for defense and research programs.
5. Aerospace systems, defense neural accelerators, industrial IoT, data centers, and embedded autonomous AI systems.
6. Defense agencies, industrial automation firms, automotive suppliers, aerospace manufacturers, and university research programs.
7. Its memory chips and IP are designed into AI accelerators, FPGAs, and embedded systems by defense contractors and industrial device makers.
8. It uses proven MRAM technology with over 700 active patents to deliver radiation-immune, instant-on persistent memory for mission-critical environments where data integrity and survival after power loss are paramount.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It provides MRAM IP and foundry services for Purdue University's ME Commons In-Memory Compute project and supplies the backbone for the CHEETA program developing MRAM-based neural accelerators.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Memory chip sales, licensed IP, foundry services, and government development contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established semiconductor provider holding over 700 active patents and delivering components globally to data center, industrial, and aerospace markets.
Geography: Based in the United States and serving global technology markets.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it supplies general-purpose persistent memory solutions for data centers, gaming, and smart energy markets.

points.name: SkyWater Technology
points.description: US specialty foundry manufacturing custom chips and advanced packaging for edge AI hardware.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor foundry that manufactures custom chips for neuromorphic and radiation-hardened edge AI workloads, operating on a Technology as a Service model. It industrializes advanced 3D system-on-chip platforms using carbon nanotubes and resistive RAM, serving commercial customers and federal defense programs.
1. A semiconductor foundry that manufactures custom silicon wafers and advanced chip packages for defense and AI customers.
2. Three-dimensional system-on-chip fabrication using carbon nanotubes stacked with resistive RAM, alongside a 90nm radiation-hardened process supporting embedded FPGA and non-volatile memory.
3. Custom process flows enabling 50x greater energy efficiency for AI workloads and radiation-hardened inference for satellite and defense applications.
4. Fabricated wafers and advanced chip packages manufactured under a Technology as a Service model.
5. Neuromorphic chips, defense systems, and satellites.
6. Commercial semiconductor designers and federal defense programs.
7. It manufactures custom silicon wafers designed by chip developers and federal agencies.
8. It provides a Technology as a Service model enabling custom process flows as a DMEA-accredited Category 1A Trusted Foundry.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: MIT, DARPA, and IonQ.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded quantum computing company.
Business model: Foundry services and Technology as a Service contracts.
Scale and maturity: The largest exclusively U.S.-based semiconductor foundry with state-of-the-art facilities in Minnesota, Florida, and Texas.
Geography: Based and operating in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Its broader focus includes quantum computing hardware, quantum networking, and specialized microelectronics manufacturing.

points.name: Tower Semiconductor
points.description: Israeli specialty foundry manufacturing low-power analog chips and emerging memory technologies for on-device edge AI processing.
points.bullets:
A specialty foundry that manufactures mixed-signal and analog semiconductors enabling ultra-low-power edge AI and on-device inference for businesses developing silicon for robotics, autonomous systems, industrial automation, and embodied AI applications.
1. A semiconductor foundry that manufactures analog mixed-signal circuits, silicon photonics, and ReRAM integration for chip companies.
2. Mixed-signal analog circuits, silicon photonics, and resistive random-access memory integration that enable compute-in-memory paradigms and analog sensing directly within image sensors.
3. Ultra-low-power edge AI processing and compute-in-memory capabilities that process sensor data before it reaches main processors.
4. Wafer manufacturing and foundry services delivered to fabless semiconductor companies and technology developers.
5. Edge AI accelerators, neuromorphic processors, image sensors, robotics, autonomous systems, industrial automation, and embodied AI applications.
6. Fabless semiconductor companies and technology developers building silicon for robotics, autonomous systems, and industrial automation.
7. Its manufacturing services are designed into edge AI accelerators, neuromorphic processors, and image sensors by chip companies.
8. Specialized expertise in analog mixed-signal manufacturing and ReRAM integration that allows compute-in-memory paradigms to be physically realized at scale.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Intel provides 300mm manufacturing capacity through a 2023 agreement to fulfill large-scale orders.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Wafer manufacturing and foundry service contracts.
Scale and maturity: A major manufacturer in the silicon photonics supply chain that has committed billions to silicon photonics manufacturing capacity in 2026.
Geography: Based in Israel and provides foundry services globally.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire business focus centers on its broader role as a specialty analog foundry for diverse semiconductor applications.

points.name: Prophesee
points.description: French technology company building event-based vision sensors for low-power machine perception.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops and sells neuromorphic event-based vision sensors, cameras, and software for machine perception in autonomous and robotic systems. It partners with semiconductor manufacturers to co-develop and commercialize silicon that captures pixel-level luminance changes asynchronously rather than in frames. The company provides its technology to industrial camera makers, robot developers, and defense integrators for high-speed, low-power perception.
1. A sensor maker that designs neuromorphic event-based vision sensors and evaluation kits, sold as packaged chips, camera modules, and software development kits.
2. Neuromorphic event-based vision sensors where individual pixels fire only when light intensity changes, producing asynchronous time-continuous data streams with high dynamic range and low latency.
3. High-speed motion analysis, object tracking, 3D perception, drone detection, low-light vision, and ultra-low power consumption with temporal resolution equivalent to tens of thousands of frames per second.
4. Packaged sensor chips, USB and embedded evaluation kits, embedded starter kits for FPGA and MCU platforms, and a software development kit with algorithms for event signal processing.
5. Robotic manipulation, industrial machine vision, bin picking, drone detection and tracking, autonomous vehicles, driver monitoring, smart surveillance, space situational awareness, and smartphone photography.
6. Industrial camera makers, robot developers, autonomous vehicle developers, defense integrators, smartphone makers, and research institutions.
7. Its sensors and modules are designed into industrial cameras and embedded vision systems by device makers and integrated into perception stacks by autonomous system developers.
8. Its bio-inspired neuromorphic architecture captures only changes in the scene pixel-by-pixel, reducing data volume and power consumption by up to 100 times compared to conventional frame-based cameras while achieving superior speed and dynamic range.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Sony Semiconductor Solutions co-develops and manufactures its sensors; partners include AMD, STMicroelectronics, Qualcomm, Intel, BrainChip, IDS Imaging Development Systems, LUCID Vision Labs, FRAMOS, and Xiaomi.
Organization type: Privately held deep-tech company.
Business model: Sensor and camera hardware sales, evaluation kit sales, software licensing, and development partnerships.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, has raised approximately €126 million, holds over 50 international patents, and maintains offices in Paris, Grenoble, Shanghai, Tokyo, and Silicon Valley.
Geography: Headquartered in Paris, France with global operations and partnerships across Europe, Asia, and North America.
Beyond physical AI: The development and commercialization of neuromorphic event-based vision technology is its sole business activity.

points.name: Innatera
points.description: Dutch semiconductor company developing ultra-low-power neuromorphic microcontrollers for AI inference directly at the sensor.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that develops ultra-low-power neuromorphic microcontrollers for AI inference directly at the sensor edge. It builds integrated systems-on-chip combining analog and digital spiking neural network cores, a RISC-V CPU, CNN accelerators, and signal processing capabilities. These chips act as a low-power gatekeeper, filtering sensor noise and identifying patterns before waking the main CPU to extend battery life in constrained devices.
1. A chip company that designs neuromorphic microcontrollers and accelerators for on-device inference.
2. Analog-mixed-signal spiking neural network cores integrated with digital RISC-V control processing and conventional CNN accelerators.
3. Ultra-low-power on-device inference, always-on audio scene classification, sub-milliwatt pattern recognition, and low-latency sensory signal processing.
4. Chips and software development kits.
5. Wearables, smart home devices, industrial sensors, consumer electronics, and robotics OEMs requiring real-time sensor processing.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, smart home system makers, industrial monitoring operators, and robotics OEMs.
7. Its chips are designed into sensors and edge devices by original equipment manufacturers.
8. An analog-digital hybrid architecture delivers up to 100x lower energy consumption and reduced latency compared to conventional AI processors, paired with a software development kit that ports standard machine learning models to its neuromorphic platform.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Akeana for RISC-V processor technology, Socionext for radar-based sensor development, and Synopsys for simulation and analysis tools.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Chip sales and software development kits.
Scale and maturity: Incorporated in 2018 as a spin-off from Delft University of Technology, has completed a Series A funding round, and is commercializing its first processor.
Geography: Based in the Netherlands and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Developing specialized neuromorphic processing hardware is the organization's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: CHEETA program
points.description: Defense research program developing energy-efficient memory chips for on-device AI processing in military robots.
points.bullets:
A government-backed university research program that develops in-memory computing silicon and autonomous robotic systems for edge AI in defense applications. It builds specialized MRAM-based neural accelerators and multi-agent robotic platforms, translating academic research into field-ready military capabilities for the United States armed forces.
1. A government agency and university lab that develops MRAM-based neural accelerator chips and autonomous robotic systems, funded by defense grants and delivered as hardware prototypes and tested systems.
2. Magnetoresistive RAM hardware fabrics and shape-shifting AI chips that process data entirely within magnetic memory arrays to reduce power consumption and thermal signatures for edge computing, alongside multi-agent robotic systems.
3. On-device inference with low thermal signatures for military hardware, tactical surveillance, logistics support, and autonomous multi-agent robotic operations.
4. Hardware prototypes, accelerator chips, and complete robotic systems developed and tested in dedicated facilities and transitioned to military applications.
5. Defense hardware, tactical surveillance, military logistics, and soldier-support systems.
6. United States military customers and defense agencies, specifically supporting Army modernization objectives.
7. It develops silicon and robotic systems from foundational research through prototyping, partnering with commercial foundries to translate them into military-grade edge AI hardware.
8. It uses MRAM-based in-memory computing to eliminate data movement between memory and processor, reducing thermal signatures for covert military edge computing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The United States Department of Defense and Purdue University.
Organization type: A collaborative government and university research program.
Business model: Government grants and defense research funding.
Scale and maturity: A well-established program supported by millions of dollars in long-term government grants with a 13,000-square-foot robotics and autonomy testbed.
Geography: Based at a university in Indiana and operates in support of United States defense agencies.
Beyond physical AI: It is part of a comprehensive university that integrates physical AI research with a wider environment of AI theorists, systems engineers, and applied roboticists.

points.name: Purdue University
points.description: Indiana academic institution advancing physical AI and autonomous robotics through interdisciplinary research and industry partnerships.
points.bullets:
A public research university that develops edge AI hardware, autonomous robotic systems, and computing architectures for physical AI, producing prototypes and funded research for government agencies and industry partners.
1. A university lab that builds research prototypes for in-memory computing chips and autonomous air-ground robots, delivered as funded research programs.
2. The core technologies include CMOS+MRAM in-memory computing hardware fabrics for neural accelerators, processing-in-DRAM designs, and AI-enabled air-ground robotic systems capable of GPS-denied navigation.
3. It delivers energy-efficient edge inference, massively parallel multiplication within memory arrays, and autonomous mapping and maneuvering in hostile terrain.
4. It delivers its outputs through funded research projects, prototypes, and collaborative development programs.
5. Its research is applied in neuromorphic accelerators, military drones, autonomous ground robots, and edge computing systems.
6. It serves defense agencies, semiconductor companies, and industry partners collaborating on advanced manufacturing and cybersecurity.
7. Its prototypes and research are integrated and commercialized by industry partners and defense agencies that build on its findings.
8. It combines a highly interdisciplinary approach spanning neuromorphic computing, edge AI, and autonomous robotics with a decade of underlying research informing its hardware projects.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with the Department of Defense, Everspin, TII, StreamCI, SMART USA, CyManII, and Lilly 360.
Organization type: A public research university and academic institution.
Business model: It operates through government and industry research grants and funding contracts.
Scale and maturity: A well-established, mature research institution that has received millions in targeted funding for specific physical AI and hardware projects.
Geography: It is based in West Lafayette, Indiana, USA, and operates primarily as a domestic research hub.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it functions as a comprehensive educational institution offering a wide array of academic programs.

points.name: Cornell University
points.description: New York research university advancing autonomous systems and novel computing architectures for physical AI.
points.bullets:
A university research lab that conducts foundational and applied research across the edge and physical AI ecosystem, spanning compute-in-memory architectures, autonomous systems, agricultural robotics, and urban robot deployment planning.
1. A research university whose labs produce validated silicon architectures, agricultural robotics foundations, and planning metrics for physical AI.
2. Compute-in-memory architectures for low-power AI inference, UV-C light agricultural treatment research, and spatial metrics for robot navigation.
3. Independent validation of edge inference silicon, foundational technology for agricultural robots, and urban robotability scoring for autonomous navigation.
4. Peer-reviewed research papers, validated architectural models, and planning methodologies.
5. Inference hardware, agricultural robots, and urban autonomous navigation.
6. Chip companies, sensor startups, agricultural robotics makers, and urban planners.
7. Its research outputs are adopted and commercialized by silicon developers, sensor makers, and robotics manufacturers.

points.name: onsemi

2. Silicon carbide power devices, high dynamic range and global shutter CMOS image sensors, indirect Time-of-Flight depth sensors, and mixed-signal platforms that integrate analog, digital, and power functions across a wide voltage range.
3. High-fidelity machine perception under challenging lighting, depth sensing, proximity and presence detection, high-resolution angular sensing, and power management for electrified vehicle powertrains.

points.name: IMChip

A fabless chip company developing in-memory processors that use spintronic memristors to physically emulate synaptic behavior for AI inference at the edge, merging storage and computation in the same device to reduce data movement.

points.name: POLYN Technology
points.description: US semiconductor company designing ultra-low-power analog AI chips that process sensor data directly at the edge.

A fabless semiconductor company that develops neuromorphic analog signal processing chips and IP for ultra-low-power AI inference directly at the sensor level, serving manufacturers of always-on edge devices.

points.name: SambaNova Systems

2. The firm finances companies developing perception sensors, autonomous navigation stacks, robot foundation models, fleet management platforms, and voice AI inference engines.
3. Its investments fund the development of physical AI capabilities including autonomous navigation, dexterous manipulation, sensor perception, fleet orchestration, and on-device inference.
4. It provides venture capital funding, board-level strategic guidance, and scaling support to portfolio companies.
5. Its investments target humanoids, drones, autonomous mobile robots, defense autonomy systems, industrial automation, and deskless enterprise workflows.
6. The firm serves technology entrepreneurs and startup founders building robotics, edge AI, and autonomous systems.
7. As an investor, it provides capital to startups that design and manufacture physical AI hardware and software for end-users.
8. The firm specifically targets the engineering and organizational deployment gap, funding infrastructure that helps autonomous systems scale from bounded tasks to reliable operation in unpredictable real-world environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The firm has backed Waymo, ANYbotics, Auterion, Foxglove, DroneDeploy, RocketLab, and co-invests with Alumni Ventures.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: Fund management, generating returns through equity investments in venture-backed startups.
Scale and maturity: The firm manages $19 billion of assets under management and has made numerous investments in the physical AI sector across early and growth stages.
Geography: Based in the USA, the firm operates globally and backs international portfolio companies.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, the firm is a comprehensive venture capital fund that invests broadly across cloud infrastructure, voice AI, cybersecurity, and enterprise software.

points.name: RISC-V International
points.description: Swiss standards organization defining open-source processor specifications used to build custom chips for on-device inference.
points.bullets:
A standards organization that governs and ratifies the open RISC-V instruction set architecture, providing the modular specifications, vector extensions, and matrix extensions that semiconductor companies use to design custom processors for edge AI inference and physical automation without licensing fees.
1. A standards body that codifies and publishes open instruction set architecture specifications and ratified profiles for chip designers.
2. Open, modular instruction set architecture specifications with extensions for vector processing and high-efficiency matrix operations optimized for transformer workloads and deep learning inference.
3. Foundation for custom processor design enabling on-device inference, variable-length vector processing, mixed-precision compute kernels, and low-power code compression for edge AI hardware.
4. Royalty-free architectural specifications, ratified platform profiles, unified databases, and working group forums accessible through tiered membership.
5. Edge inference processors, IoT devices, industrial automation, autonomous vehicles, and space systems.
6. Semiconductor companies, processor IP designers, hardware startups, and established tech companies.
7. Its specifications are implemented by chip companies and IP vendors that design processors for device makers.
8. It provides a royalty-free, open-standard alternative to proprietary instruction set architectures, eliminating licensing barriers to democratize custom silicon design.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Founding and premier members include Andes Technology, SiFive, Intel, Microsoft, Imagination, Tenstorrent, and the European Space Agency.
Organization type: A non-profit industry consortium and standards organization.
Business model: Membership fees from individual and corporate members across tiered levels.
Scale and maturity: Formed in 2015 with over 4,500 members as of 2025, projecting market penetration to grow from 2.5% in 2021 to 33.7% by 2031.
Geography: Based in Switzerland with a global operational footprint.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is entirely dedicated to managing and promoting its open-source instruction set architecture as its sole business focus.

points.name: Beijing Institute of Open-Source Chip
points.description: Chinese research institute developing open-source processors for edge AI devices.
points.bullets:
A research institute that develops open-source RISC-V processor architectures and instruction set extensions for on-device AI inference, building the enabling technology for custom processors rather than complete end-to-end systems.
1. A research institute that designs RISC-V processor architectures and instruction set extensions for edge inference silicon.
2. Open RISC-V instruction set architectures, processor designs, and accelerator integration frameworks for heterogeneous system-on-chip designs.
3. On-device inference, processor architecture design, and instruction set extensions for power-constrained embedded systems.
4. Open-source chip designs, architectures, and frameworks delivered to developers and chipmakers.
5. Industrial automation, smart devices, automotive systems, healthcare applications, robotics, and industrial controllers.
6. Developers and manufacturers building custom processors.
7. Its architectures and designs are used by chipmakers to build processors for edge devices.
8. It leverages open instruction set architectures to establish indigenous edge computing capabilities independent of proprietary processor technologies.
points.profile:
Organization type: A research institute.
Geography: The organization is based in Beijing, China, and operates within the country's open-source chip ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, robotics, and physical automation represent the central focus of the organization's mission to advance open instruction set architectures.

points.name: Andes Technology
points.description: Taiwanese semiconductor company designing RISC-V processor cores and AI accelerators for on-device inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor IP company that designs and licenses RISC-V processor cores and deep learning accelerators for on-device inference, targeting chipmakers building SoCs for edge and physical AI systems.
1. A chip IP company that licenses RISC-V CPU cores and neural processing accelerators to semiconductor designers.
2. RISC-V 32/64-bit processor cores, out-of-order multiprocessor clusters, and deep learning accelerator IP featuring native hardware support for Transformer networks and SIMD/DSP extensions.
3. On-device inference for large language and Transformer models, low-power embedded processing, functional safety, and hardware-level instruction set extensibility for edge devices.
4. Licensed semiconductor IP cores, accelerator IP, and software development kits integrated by chipmakers into their SoCs.
5. Wearables, IoT devices, automotive safety systems, industrial automation, and robotics.
6. Semiconductor designers, IoT chipmakers, and automotive SoC integrators.
7. Its processor and accelerator IP is designed into custom SoCs by semiconductor companies building edge AI hardware.
8. Native hardware-level support for Transformer networks within its deep learning accelerator IP enables large language model inference on resource-constrained edge devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Intel Foundry Services, RISC-V International, BrainChip, Axelera AI, Sequans Communications, Menta, and Deeplite.
Organization type: Publicly traded semiconductor IP company.
Business model: IP licensing fees and software toolchain licenses for semiconductor design.
Scale and maturity: A founding premier member of RISC-V International with over 20 billion powered SoCs deployed globally.
Geography: Based in Taiwan and operating globally through international semiconductor partnerships.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI through on-device inference and functional safety processing is the entirety of its business focus.

points.name: Useful Sensors
points.description: US technology company embedding machine learning into low-cost hardware modules for consumer electronics.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that builds low-cost, integrated hardware modules embedding machine learning models for on-device inference in consumer electronics.
1. A sensor maker that builds ML-enabled sensor modules for object detection, person sensing, gesture recognition and QR code scanning, sold as drop-in hardware components.
2. Camera modules with embedded microcontrollers and neural processing units that run optimized machine learning models entirely on-device.
3. On-device person detection, facial recognition, gesture recognition, QR code scanning and offline speech recognition with privacy-preserving local processing.
4. Low-cost hardware modules, open-source software libraries and standalone offline devices sold through component distributors.
5. Consumer electronics including smart appliances, televisions and laptops, plus standalone offline voice assistant devices.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers building smart appliances and devices, and hobbyists buying modules through distributors.
7. Its modules are designed into consumer electronics products by device makers as drop-in inference subsystems.
8. Running transformer-based architectures on extremely low-cost microcontroller hardware for privacy-first, on-device processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: OKdo for manufacturing, SparkFun for distribution, Synopsys and Arm for processing cores, and RockChip for SoCs.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware module sales and standalone device sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in March 2022 with $5 million in seed funding and fewer than ten employees.
Geography: Based in the United States with global manufacturing and distribution.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI hardware and software for physical devices is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Esperanto Technologies
points.description: US semiconductor company developing energy-efficient RISC-V processors for edge and data center AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs massively parallel RISC-V AI accelerator chips and integrated rack-mount appliances for energy-efficient inference, targeting data center and edge environments.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V-based system-on-chips and integrated hardware-software appliances for AI inference.
2. Massively parallel architecture combining over a thousand RISC-V processor cores with custom machine learning vector and tensor instructions on a single low-power system-on-chip.
3. High-throughput inference for large language models and recommendation systems at ultra-low power consumption.
4. Chips sold to system integrators and a complete rack-mount generative AI appliance integrating hardware and software.
5. Enterprise edge servers, localized data centers, and industries with strict data privacy requirements like healthcare, legal, and finance.
6. Data center operators, enterprise IT departments, researchers, and data science teams in various industries.
7. Its chips and appliances are integrated by enterprises into private data center infrastructure as an alternative to cloud GPU infrastructure.
8. Its use of an open-instruction-set architecture featuring over a thousand cores delivers high inference performance while significantly reducing the power consumption of traditional GPU acceleration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: TSMC for current chip manufacturing, Intel Foundry Services for advanced nodes, Meta for open transformer models, and investors including Atlantic Bridge and Comet Labs.
Organization type: A privately held technology company that closed in 2025.
Business model: Chip sales, integrated appliance sales, and hardware evaluation access for researchers.
Scale and maturity: A venture-backed company that reached Series B funding, maintaining an early-stage market presence focused on establishing developer ecosystems.
Geography: Based in the USA and designing hardware for global deployment in enterprise edge environments and localized data centers.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and data center hardware is the entire focus of this pure-play semiconductor company.

points.name: Embecosm
points.description: Technology company building optimized RISC-V compiler tool chains for edge AI accelerators.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds C/C++ and Rust toolchains based on GCC and LLVM for semiconductor companies designing edge AI accelerators and embedded processors. It provides compiler optimization, custom feature implementation, and software infrastructure to enable efficient on-device inference on RISC-V and other architectures. The organization acts as a specialized systems integrator bridging chip designers and product teams without manufacturing physical silicon or robotic systems itself.
1. A developer tools company whose compiler toolchains and software infrastructure semiconductor and system engineers use to optimize AI inference on edge hardware.
2. C/C++ and Rust compiler toolchains based on GCC and LLVM optimized for RISC-V architectures and AI accelerators.
3. Compiler optimization, custom feature implementation, and software infrastructure for AI-enabled chips and on-device inference.
4. Software toolchains, engineering services, support, and training delivered to hardware developers.
5. Edge AI accelerators, microcontrollers, and stream processors.
6. Semiconductor developers and engineering teams building custom AI accelerators and embedded processors.
7. Its toolchains are used by chip companies to optimize inference performance on their silicon.
8. Deep expertise in modern C/C++ and Rust toolchains based on GCC and LLVM specifically tailored for RISC-V architectures and AI accelerators.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with Southampton University and has participated in Google Summer of Code.
Organization type: Privately held technology consulting and services firm.
Business model: Engineering services, toolchain development contracts, support, and training.
Scale and maturity: An established specialist firm with international collaborations and academic research partnerships.
Geography: Operates and collaborates internationally, with partnerships in the United Kingdom.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and embedded processing are central to its mission, and it is a pure-play technology provider focused entirely on optimized software environments for specialized computing hardware.

points.name: Semidynamics
points.description: European semiconductor company designing custom RISC-V processors and memory subsystems to accelerate large-scale AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs RISC-V-based neural processing units and complete rack-scale inference systems for large-scale AI, selling IP cores, chips, boards, and racks to data centre and cloud operators.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V NPUs and inference SoCs for AI inference, sold as licensed IP cores, fabricated chips, and integrated rack-scale hardware.
2. 64-bit RISC-V processors with unified scalar, vector, and tensor units, featuring on-chip memory and latency-tolerance technology that sustains high compute throughput using commodity LPDDR memory.
3. On-device and data-centre inference acceleration for large-scale AI models with support for ONNX, PyTorch, and standard Linux workloads.
4. Licensed IP cores, fabricated 3nm inference SoCs, inference boards, and liquid-cooled OCP-compliant inference racks, accompanied by a software development kit and orchestrator.
5. Data centres, high-performance computing, and cloud inference platforms.
6. Cloud operators, data centre operators, and high-performance computing system builders.
7. Its IP cores and chips are designed into boards, servers, and rack-scale infrastructures by system builders.
8. Its memory-compute co-design uses commodity LPDDR memory and proprietary latency-tolerance technology to avoid the memory bottlenecks and supply constraints of high-bandwidth memory.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with SiPearl, SK hynix, TSMC, Multiverse Computing, E4 Computer Engineering, MEGWARE, and the EuroHPC JU.
Organization type: Privately held semiconductor company.
Business model: IP licensing fees, chip sales, and hardware system sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016 with over 150 engineers, having taped out a 3nm chip in late 2025.
Geography: Based in Barcelona and participating in European compute initiatives.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and data-centre AI inference is the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Ceremorphic
points.description: AI processor startup building energy-efficient silicon accelerators for edge computing.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs high-performance AI processors combining RISC-V and Arm cores with custom machine-learning accelerators for data centers, automotive, high-performance computing, and robotics.
1. A fabless chip company that designs high-performance computing processors and accelerators for AI training and inference.
2. Heterogeneous processors built on a 5nm process node that integrate RISC-V CPUs, Arm GPUs, custom machine-learning accelerators, and a patented multi-threaded processing architecture.
3. High-performance AI model training and inference for data centers, edge deployments, and autonomous systems.
4. Chips and high-performance computing systems sold to system builders and operators.
5. Data centers, automotive systems, high-performance computing, and robotics.
6. System builders and operators in data center, automotive, high-performance computing, and robotics markets.
7. Its chips are designed into advanced computing systems and edge devices by system builders.
8. A patented quantum-inspired hierarchical learning architecture pairs proprietary multi-threaded processing technology with a combination of RISC-V and Arm cores.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company manufactures its processors on a 5nm process node provided by a named foundry partner.
Organization type: A privately held semiconductor startup.
Business model: Chip and hardware system sales.
Scale and maturity: A startup founded in 2020 that emerged from stealth mode with $50 million in Series A funding.
Geography: Based in San Jose, California, operating in the global semiconductor market.
Beyond physical AI: The organization also develops high-performance computing systems for drug discovery and metaverse workloads.

points.name: Codasip
points.description: Semiconductor design company creating customizable RISC-V processors for on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor IP and design tool provider that develops customizable RISC-V processor cores and processor design automation tools for system-on-chip developers building edge AI, robotics, and physical automation systems.
1. A semiconductor IP company that licenses customizable RISC-V processor cores and design automation tools to chip designers.
2. RISC-V processor architecture implemented with a custom design language, incorporating CHERI memory protection technology and extensible instructions via embedded FPGA cores.
3. Customizable on-device inference processing, enhanced architectural memory security against out-of-bounds vulnerabilities, and application-specific instruction sets for AI/ML workloads.
4. Processor IP cores, architecture description languages, and design automation tools licensed to system-on-chip developers.
5. Industrial robotics, defense, avionics, automotive systems, critical national infrastructure, and IoT edge devices.
6. System-on-chip developers, systems integrators building specialized edge devices, and industrial technology providers.
7. Its processor IP and design tools are licensed to chip developers and integrators that build specialized edge devices for autonomous systems.
8. It provides the first commercial CHERI-enabled 64-bit RISC-V application core, pairing highly customizable instruction sets with hardware-level memory security.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Western Digital, Menta, and the RISC-V Foundation.
Organization type: A privately held, venture-backed company.
Business model: IP licensing fees and design tool software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A mature commercial entity claiming over 2 billion processor cores shipped.
Geography: A European company operating within a global ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on delivering customizable silicon IP and design tools that enable developers to create application-specific processors.

points.name: SpacemiT
points.description: Global semiconductor company designing RISC-V processors for edge computing and on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs RISC-V processors for on-device AI inference, building SoCs that run AI workloads directly on the main CPU for robotics, industrial automation and autonomous systems.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V AI CPUs and SoCs for on-device inference.
2. RISC-V-compatible processor cores and SoCs that integrate general-purpose cores with dedicated AI compute cores to run large language models and inference workloads directly on the main chip without separate neural processing units.
3. On-device inference of up to 30B parameter large language models with 60 TOPS of AI compute, power-efficient edge AI execution, and server-grade AI workloads.
4. Chips and processors sold to system partners for integration into developer boards, single-board computers and laptops.
5. Humanoid robots, AI computing boards, RISC-V laptops and server-grade AI systems.
6. Single-board computer makers, laptop manufacturers and robotics makers.
7. Its processors are designed into developer platforms and single-board computers by hardware partners.
8. It uses a vendor-independent open RISC-V architecture to avoid the proprietary lock-in constraints of traditional ARM and x86 platforms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Banana Pi and Deep Computing.
Organization type: Commercial semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales.
Scale and maturity: A globally operating company with notable commercial maturity, standardized platform certifications and real-world hardware integrations.
Geography: Based globally with real-world hardware deployments and operational validation in Beijing.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is dedicated to the design and commercialization of specialized RISC-V computing processors.

points.name: Canonical
points.description: Global software company optimizing Ubuntu for real-time robotics control and AI inference at the edge.
points.bullets:
A software company that provides the Ubuntu Linux operating system and open-source middleware used as the base platform for edge and physical AI systems, targeting RISC-V developers and industrial robotics applications. It builds and supports a Linux distribution that integrates real-time-capable control, AI inference, and orchestration for developers and machine makers.
1. A software company that builds and distributes the Ubuntu operating system for edge devices and robots, delivered as an open-source platform with long-term support.
2. A Linux-based operating system with long-term support releases that target RISC-V architecture profiles and integrate real-time control and AI inference capabilities.
3. Operating system standardization, real-time control, AI inference execution, and orchestration on edge devices.
4. Open-source operating system distributions and long-term support subscriptions.
5. Industrial controllers, modular robotics, and RISC-V edge development boards.
6. Robotics developers, industrial controller manufacturers, and RISC-V hardware developers.
7. Its operating system is installed as the base software layer on edge controllers and development boards built by hardware manufacturers.
8. It provides a standardized, open-source Linux distribution with long-term enterprise support specifically targeting emerging RISC-V profiles and industrial robotics middleware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Arm, NVIDIA, SiFive, and Small Robot Company.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Operating system distribution and enterprise long-term support subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A global software company with established enterprise adoption across industrial and edge environments.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: It develops open-source software infrastructure and tools for cloud, enterprise data centers, and edge computing environments.

points.name: Akeana
points.description: Semiconductor IP company developing configurable RISC-V processors for robotics and edge AI workloads.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor IP company that designs and licenses RISC-V-based processor cores, system IP, interconnects, and AI accelerators for edge AI and physical automation, providing silicon developers with configurable compute building blocks for on-device inference and control.
1. A semiconductor IP company that designs and licenses RISC-V processor cores, accelerators, and system-on-chip building blocks for chip developers.
2. RISC-V processor cores with vector extensions and systolic arrays for AI acceleration, network-on-chip interconnects, and multi-threaded out-of-order architectures optimized for heterogeneous compute.
3. On-device AI inference acceleration, real-time control processing, multi-core scalability, and low-latency compute for embedded systems.
4. Licensed semiconductor IP cores, system IP, interconnects, and a processor customization platform delivered to silicon designers.
5. Embedded controllers, edge AI devices, industrial automation systems, automotive systems, and robotics.
6. Chip designers, semiconductor companies, and system-on-chip developers in robotics, automotive, and industrial automation.
7. Its processor IP and accelerators are integrated into system-on-chip designs by semiconductor manufacturers serving edge and embedded markets.
8. A configurable single-point-solution approach spanning microcontrollers to high-performance cores with AI vector extensions and systolic arrays under one RISC-V architecture.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with Innatera on edge AI integration and uses Cadence verification tools and Palladium Cloud for IP development.
Organization type: A venture-funded startup that recently emerged from stealth mode.
Business model: Semiconductor IP licensing with configurable processor and system IP offerings.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company with a range of released processor IP products and a demonstrated test chip.
Geography: Based in Santa Clara, California, USA, with a global market focus.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is providing processor and system IP for heterogeneous computing and AI acceleration across embedded and edge applications.

points.name: Cavium/Marvell
points.description: Semiconductor company designing custom data center silicon and optical interconnects for AI infrastructure.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that designs custom silicon, optical interconnects, and switching solutions for large-scale AI model training and deployment in hyperscale data centers, rather than edge inference sensors, actuators, or robotics systems. The organization provides the compute architectures and connectivity fabrics that hyperscale cloud providers use to build centralized AI platforms. Its work is strictly centered on enabling the centralized processing backbone required for large-scale AI systems and is peripheral to edge AI and physical automation.
1. A semiconductor company that designs custom compute silicon, optical digital signal processors, and PCIe switching silicon for hyperscale data centers.
2. The core technology comprises custom accelerator compute architectures, optical digital signal processors, and PCIe switching silicon that form the connectivity fabrics and silicon backbone for AI computing clusters.
3. Customers receive the technology as components and subsystems, including custom silicon, optical interconnects, and switching solutions, integrated into their own centralized AI platforms.
4. The technology is used in hyperscale data centers and next-generation AI computing clusters for large-scale AI model training and deployment.
5. The primary customers are hyperscale cloud providers and major AI infrastructure builders constructing next-generation AI computing clusters.
6. The organization functions as a component and subsystem supplier within the AI value chain, providing silicon and interconnects that hyperscalers use to build their own centralized AI platforms.
7. The approach is distinguished by holding approximately 40% market share in optical DSPs for the emerging 1.6T era and offering specialized custom compute and interconnect solutions.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor and data infrastructure provider.
Business model: The company makes money through component and subsystem sales, with data center revenue representing roughly three-quarters of its total income.
Scale and maturity: The mature-scale company reached its current state following strategic acquisitions over several years, with data center revenue projected to grow 50% year-over-year.
Geography: The organization is based in the United States and operates globally to supply major cloud and AI infrastructure providers.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is on centralized data center infrastructure, providing high-bandwidth memory optimization, data center interconnect modules, and scale-up connectivity standards, with edge AI and physical automation being entirely peripheral to its mission.

points.name: T-Head
points.description: Chinese semiconductor subsidiary developing RISC-V processors for on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs RISC-V processor cores, system-on-chips and AI accelerators for on-device inference and edge computing, licensing the intellectual property and selling silicon to device makers.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V processor cores, system-on-chips with NPUs and AI accelerators for edge devices and cloud clusters.
2. 64-bit RISC-V instruction set processors with out-of-order superscalar pipelines, hardware cache coherency, integrated neural processing units and high-bandwidth interconnects.
3. On-device inference, edge computing, hardware cache coherency and neural network acceleration.
4. Processor intellectual property, system-on-chips, networking switches and software stacks licensed or sold to chip designers and board makers.
5. Edge endpoints, single-board computers, consumer electronics, automotive electronics and industrial IoT devices.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, automotive electronics developers, industrial IoT firms and single-board computer makers.
7. Its processor cores and system-on-chips are designed into chips and boards by device manufacturers.
8. It open-sources its processor core designs to address software fragmentation and enable hardware-software co-optimization.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A wholly owned subsidiary of Alibaba, collaborating with the RISC-V community and powering boards from BeagleBoard.org and chips from Allwinner.
Organization type: A wholly owned semiconductor subsidiary of a large multinational technology conglomerate.
Business model: Chip sales, intellectual property licensing and associated software stack distribution.
Scale and maturity: It has shipped over 560,000 AI accelerator units, reached a production capacity of two billion units and garnered adoption from over 200 firms.
Geography: Based in China with a strategic focus tied to the domestic market.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on edge AI and semiconductor design while its parent conglomerate operates global e-commerce, cloud computing and technology businesses.

points.name: SMIC
points.description: Chinese semiconductor manufacturer fabricating advanced chips for AI accelerators.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor foundry that fabricates advanced-node AI ASICs and NPUs for chip companies serving edge and physical AI applications, producing 7nm-class silicon using DUV lithography. It manufactures processors for AI silicon designers rather than building robots, sensors or autonomy software itself. Its output supplies the foundational inference and computing hardware used in on-device and physical-world AI systems.
1. A semiconductor foundry that manufactures AI ASICs and NPUs as fabricated wafers and chips for fabless chip companies.
2. 14nm and 7nm-class semiconductor fabrication processes using DUV lithography to manufacture high-performance computing silicon.
3. High-volume fabrication of advanced-node processors for AI accelerators and neural processing units.
4. Fabricated wafers and manufactured chips delivered to fabless semiconductor designers.
5. Edge AI inference silicon and autonomous-system processors.
6. Fabless AI chip companies and research institutions.
7. Its fabricated chips are designed by fabless chip companies into NPUs and SoCs for edge AI devices.
8. It achieves 7nm-class fabrication domestically using DUV lithography despite restrictions on importing EUV equipment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The Chinese Academy of Sciences, Cambricon and Horizon Robotics are named customers.
Organization type: A partially state-owned, publicly traded semiconductor foundry.
Business model: Wafer fabrication and chip manufacturing contracts.
Scale and maturity: China's largest semiconductor foundry, producing 7nm chips at scale and expanding advanced-node capacity.
Geography: Based in China, contributing a significant share of global twelve-inch wafer-fab capacity.
Beyond physical AI: Its core business is general semiconductor fabrication and integrated circuit manufacturing for broad industries beyond edge and physical AI.

points.name: Espressif Systems
points.description: Chinese semiconductor company designing microcontrollers and system-on-chip devices for on-device AI inference and IoT applications.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power microcontrollers and systems on a chip for on-device AI inference and IoT applications. It builds RISC-V based silicon and software frameworks used by developers to run machine learning models on connected edge devices.
1. A chip company that designs microcontrollers and systems on a chip for on-device inference.
2. RISC-V compatible processor cores, built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and neural network acceleration in low-power microcontrollers.
3. On-device inference, voice recognition, local object detection and TinyML deployments.
4. Chips and modules, plus software frameworks for model deployment.
5. Smart manufacturing, industrial automation, healthcare monitoring, smart home technology and smart grid systems.
6. Developers and enterprises building connected devices.
7. Its chips are designed into connected devices by device makers.
8. Superior energy efficiency during AI inference tasks, integrated wireless connectivity and low idle power consumption compared to alternative development boards.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Qt Group.
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Chip sales.
Scale and maturity: Globally adopted with a mature hardware and software ecosystem.
Geography: Based in Shanghai, China, operating worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, IoT and physical automation are the entire focus of its business.

points.name: StarFive
points.description: Chinese semiconductor company designing RISC-V processors for edge computing and on-device artificial intelligence.

A fabless chip company that designs RISC-V-based application processors and microcontrollers for on-device inference and embedded control in industrial IoT and edge computing. It builds quad-core SoCs and single-board computers that deliver real-time image and video processing with high power efficiency for physical automation and robotics control applications.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V application processors and single-board computers for embedded edge computing and on-device inference.
