2. RISC-V instruction set architecture implemented in quad-core application processors and single-board computing platforms with integrated image and video processing capabilities.
3. On-device inference, real-time image and video processing, and embedded autonomous control for industrial IoT and edge computing deployments.
4. Processors, system-on-chips, and single-board computers sold to system integrators and developers for embedded deployments.
5. Industrial IoT, smart manufacturing, robotics control, edge computing gateways, and embedded autonomous systems.
6. System integrators, embedded developers, and industrial automation engineers requiring stable edge computing platforms with industrial protocol integration.
7. Its processors and single-board computers are designed into industrial IoT devices and edge computing gateways by system integrators and developers.
8. It uses the open, customizable RISC-V instruction set architecture to deliver cost-effective, power-efficient processors that reduce dependence on traditional proprietary semiconductor architectures.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held technology company operating as a semiconductor and embedded computing vendor.
Business model: Chip and single-board computer hardware sales to system integrators and developers.
Scale and maturity: An established domestic vendor in China with recently launched embedded computing products, actively expanding its footprint in the industrial edge computing market.
Geography: Based in China, operating within a strategic domestic ecosystem focused on locally controlled semiconductor alternatives.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play technology provider whose entire operational focus is dedicated to advancing RISC-V-based embedded computing and single-board hardware.

points.name: European Processor Initiative
points.description: European government initiative developing autonomous microprocessors and accelerators for edge computing and physical AI applications.
points.bullets:
A government initiative that develops sovereign processor and accelerator technologies for high-performance computing, edge computing, and physical artificial intelligence applications. It coordinates the design of custom silicon architectures to enable downstream robotics, autonomous systems, and visual perception for European industrial sectors.
1. A government initiative that coordinates the design of processors and accelerators based on ARM and RISC-V instruction sets for downstream industrial automation and autonomous systems.
2. Custom processor architectures and accelerators built on ARM and RISC-V instruction sets, including general-purpose processors and low-power compute units.
3. On-device inference, secure compute infrastructure, and foundational silicon processing for safety-critical physical AI applications.
4. Processors and proof-of-concept accelerators developed through participating semiconductor companies for integration into compute platforms.
5. Industrial automation, autonomous vehicles, video surveillance, robotics, and defense systems.
6. Industrial automation companies, autonomous vehicle makers, defense agencies, and downstream semiconductor and systems integrators.
7. Its processors and architectures are designed by participating silicon developers for integration into compute platforms used by device makers and system builders.
8. It focuses on European technological sovereignty, ensuring safety-critical and sensitive applications run on domestically controlled supply chains rather than competing on commercial performance alone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SiPearl and Semidynamics participate in the initiative.
Organization type: A government-led strategic initiative.
Business model: Government funding and coordination of semiconductor research and development programs.
Scale and maturity: It has delivered a general-purpose processor and proof-of-concept accelerators, with ongoing work focused on next-generation low-power units.
Geography: It is based in and operates entirely within Europe, aligning with the broader European digital independence strategy.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge computing, the organization is dedicated to building high-performance computing technologies and ensuring data residency and supply chain security for European industrial and defense applications.

points.name: Canaan Inc.
points.description: Chinese semiconductor company designing edge AI chips for smart home devices and formerly operating the Kendryte AI chip division.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs RISC-V-based edge inference chips for image and voice processing, alongside its primary business of Bitcoin mining ASICs. It builds neural processing units and system-on-chips for on-device deployment in robotics, drones, and smart home devices, and also holds minority investments in robotics companies.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V-based edge AI SoCs and NPUs for on-device inference, sold as bare chips and developer boards.
2. Neural processing units built on RISC-V cores with integrated audio and vision accelerators, manufactured on a 28 nm process node.
3. On-device inference for image classification, object detection, and voice processing at low power.
4. Chips and developer boards, accompanied by a MicroPython environment and custom model format for neural network deployment.
5. Smart door locks, access control, UAV aerial photography, robotics, and advanced driver assistance systems.
6. Device makers, robotics developers, and makers.
7. Its chips are designed into edge devices and development boards by electronics manufacturers.
8. It employs a RISC-V architecture with integrated vision and audio accelerators for low-power edge inference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: TSMC manufactures its chips, Sipeed builds developer boards around them, and it is an investor in a medical robot maker.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Chip sales, primarily from Bitcoin mining ASICs and secondarily from edge AI SoCs.
Scale and maturity: A publicly traded company founded in 2013 with approximately 700 employees and roughly $270 million in 2024 revenue, which shut down its AI chip division in June 2025.
Geography: Based in Beijing, China, exporting products worldwide including to Japan, Germany, South Korea, and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The company is a major designer and manufacturer of Bitcoin mining ASICs and blockchain servers.

points.name: Sipeed
points.description: Chinese hardware company producing affordable development boards for entry-level on-device AI inference.
points.bullets:
A hardware company that builds affordable edge AI development boards and system-on-modules that integrate inference silicon, cameras, microphones and displays for hobbyists, educators and developers.
1. A hardware company that designs edge AI development boards and modules and sells them as low-cost physical components to developers.
2. Development boards and modules built around RISC-V and Arm-based inference processors, packaged with integrated vision and audio sensors and supporting Linux and microcontroller software environments.
3. On-device vision and audio inference, face recognition, inventory counting and voice-activated robotics on low-power edge hardware.
4. Physical development boards and AI modules distributed through hardware kit retailers and online model training services.
5. Educational robotics, smart agriculture, industrial IoT, home automation and maker projects.
6. Hobbyists, educators, industrial developers and makers.
7. It packages inference silicon from upstream chip companies into accessible development boards and modules for developers.
8. It drives adoption of edge AI silicon among developers through low-cost, well-documented boards priced between ten and thirty dollars.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses inference and connectivity chips from upstream semiconductor manufacturers and distributes kits through an electronics hardware partner.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of development boards and modules.
Scale and maturity: A company that has put its boards in the hands of a million developers through a broad community project base.
Geography: Based in China, leveraging domestic semiconductor partnerships to build its edge AI hardware ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and physical automation represent the entire focus of the organization, which is dedicated to making on-device vision and audio processing accessible to developers.

points.name: Modular
points.description: AI software startup developing programming tools and inference engines to run AI models efficiently across diverse hardware.
points.bullets:
An AI software startup that develops a programming language and a hardware-agnostic inference engine allowing developers to run artificial intelligence models across diverse processing chips without hardware-specific rewrites.
1. A developer tools company that builds a programming language and an inference serving framework, sold as software and cloud services to developers.
2. A superset programming language and a portable inference serving engine that compile and execute model code across heterogeneous processors.
3. Hardware-agnostic on-device inference, portable model deployment, and cross-vendor execution without code rewrites.
4. Licensed software, inference engines, and cloud platform services.
5. General artificial intelligence inference and edge computing.
6. Software developers.
7. Its inference engine and language are used by developers to deploy models on hardware from multiple semiconductor vendors.
8. It reduces vendor lock-in by enabling the same model code to run across competing hardware platforms without rewrites.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It was acquired by Qualcomm, and its investors include GV, US Innovative Technology fund, DFJ Growth, General Catalyst, and Greylock.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and cloud services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2022 and acquired in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $3.92 billion.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses on developing a specialized programming language and a cross-platform inference engine for general software development.

points.name: Autotalks
points.description: Israeli automotive chip designer making chips that let vehicles communicate directly with each other and infrastructure for safer driving.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication chipsets for automotive safety, serving automakers and transportation platforms with connectivity technology for assisted and autonomous driving.
1. A chip company that designs V2X communication semiconductors and system-on-a-chip technology for automotive edge connectivity.
2. Purpose-built dual-mode V2X chipsets supporting DSRC and C-V2X standards to enable real-time communication between vehicles and roadside infrastructure.
3. Delivers beyond-line-of-sight hazard perception, automatic emergency braking support, and proactive collision avoidance for connected vehicles.
4. Automotive-qualified chips and chipsets supplied to automakers for integration into vehicle platforms.
5. Conventional vehicles, two-wheelers, unmanned vehicles, and autonomous driving platforms.
6. Automakers and automotive Tier 1 suppliers building connected and autonomous vehicles.
7. Its chips are designed into vehicle platforms by automakers to serve as an information-rich sensor for advanced driver assistance systems.
8. Produces production-ready, dual-mode safety solutions compatible with multiple global V2X communication standards within a single chipset.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Now integrated into Qualcomm's Snapdragon Digital Chassis portfolio after its acquisition.
Organization type: Subsidiary of a publicly traded semiconductor conglomerate, formerly an independent fabless chip designer.
Business model: Semiconductor chip sales to automotive customers.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2008, acquired for roughly $350 to $400 million in 2023, with its parent organization holding a $30 billion automotive business pipeline.
Geography: Based in Israel, designing technology to support a worldwide customer base across multiple geographic regions.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and vehicular communication are the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: BOS Semiconductors
points.description: South Korean fabless semiconductor company designing automotive neural processing chips for in-vehicle AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs automotive system-on-chip semiconductors and AI accelerator chiplets for on-device inference in vehicles, built on licensed neural processing unit IP and chiplet architecture for automakers and Tier-1 suppliers.
1. A chip company that designs automotive SoCs and RISC-V AI accelerator chiplets for on-device inference.
2. Neural processing units in low-power automotive system-on-chips and chiplets, incorporating licensed Tensix NPU core technology and RISC-V architecture.
3. On-device inference for advanced driver assistance systems and in-vehicle infotainment, delivering scalable chiplet-based inference performance up to over 2,000 TOPS.
4. Chips and chiplets sold to automotive manufacturers and Tier-1 suppliers.
5. Automobiles, autonomous driving systems and connected vehicle domain computing.
6. Automakers and Tier-1 automotive suppliers.
7. Its chips are designed into automotive computing systems by vehicle manufacturers and automotive part suppliers.
8. It is the first automotive fabless company to adopt chiplet architecture, achieving reported 5× better cost efficiency.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Tenstorrent and is funded by Hyundai Motor Group and Kia.
Organization type: Privately held fabless semiconductor startup.
Business model: Chip sales and semiconductor licensing.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup established within its first year that has secured over 10 billion Korean Won in funding and distributed product samples to global automotive OEMs.
Geography: Based in South Korea and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play automotive semiconductor designer whose entire business is focused on silicon architecture for autonomous and connected vehicle applications.

points.name: Atreides Management
points.description: US hedge fund financing venture-stage artificial intelligence companies.
points.bullets:
A hedge fund and crossover investment firm that finances technology companies across public and private markets, including those building inference silicon, edge processors and physical AI hardware. It acts as a capital provider for venture-stage and growth-stage semiconductor and AI hardware developers, as well as for public market participants seeking exposure to artificial intelligence infrastructure.
1. A venture capital and hedge fund firm that invests in edge AI, robotics and semiconductor companies.
2. It provides growth capital to semiconductor and AI hardware developers that design inference silicon and edge processors.
3. It exploits cross-sectional valuation inefficiencies in AI-related hardware, specifically targeting foundational semiconductor infrastructure rather than end-user applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable investments include companies developing RISC-V processors, wafer-scale AI accelerators and millimeter-wave radar sensors.
Organization type: A privately held hedge fund and registered investment adviser.
Business model: Fund management and investment advisory fees.
Scale and maturity: It manages approximately $7 billion in investments and has led funding rounds exceeding $400 million for individual semiconductor companies.
Geography: It is based in the United States and focuses its venture-stage investments primarily across the United States and Canada.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it manages long and short technology funds and makes privately negotiated investments across the wider technology and consumer sectors.

points.name: Apollo Global Management
points.description: US investment firm funding early-stage AI startups and building AI capabilities within its portfolio companies.
points.bullets:
A global asset management and private equity firm that acts as a strategic investor and operational incubator for artificial intelligence startups and physical automation technologies. It finances large-scale compute capacity and infrastructure, and drives the integration of artificial intelligence into its industrial portfolio companies.
1. An investment firm that provides venture capital funding to physical AI and compute startups.
2. The organization delivers capital through participation in funding rounds and directs strategic integration services across its industrial portfolio companies.
3. The firm sells capital allocation and operational scaling to artificial intelligence startups, compute infrastructure projects, and industrial portfolio companies.
4. Its capital is deployed directly into AI hardware companies and is used to purchase and integrate physical automation technologies within its own industrial holdings.
5. A dedicated data and artificial intelligence team differentiates the firm by identifying specific value pools, conducting detailed due diligence, and guiding portfolio companies from pilot phases to full-scale production.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The firm participated in a $400 million funding round for a RISC-V processor company.
Organization type: A publicly traded global alternative investment management and private equity firm.
Business model: The organization makes money through fund management, private equity, credit, and infrastructure asset management.
Scale and maturity: The organization is a mature, well-established global investment manager that participates in massive multi-billion-dollar infrastructure funds and recently opened an innovation hub in Austin, Texas.
Geography: The firm is headquartered in North America and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical artificial intelligence, the organization's broader profile encompasses global alternative investment management, including private equity, credit, and massive infrastructure financing.

points.name: D1 Capital Partners
points.description: US investment firm funding semiconductor and edge computing companies.
points.bullets:
A growth equity investor that provides late-stage funding to technology companies, including semiconductor developers whose processor architectures are used for edge computing and on-device inference.
1. A venture capital firm that provides growth equity funding to semiconductor and edge AI companies.
2. It provides capital to semiconductor design companies developing processor architectures for edge computing.
3. Its backing of a prominent semiconductor design company focused on open processor architectures distinguishes its edge AI investment portfolio.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held investment firm.
Business model: Fund management and equity investment returns.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge computing and physical artificial intelligence, it is a general investment organization focused on broader financial growth across technology sectors.

points.name: Sutter Hill Ventures
points.description: US venture capital firm funding early-stage silicon and AI technology companies.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that provides financial backing to early-stage technology companies, including those designing inference silicon for edge AI. The organization often incubates companies and actively collaborates with founders rather than passively providing capital. Its role in edge and physical AI is indirect, funding the component designers that build underlying hardware.
1. A venture capital firm that provides early-stage funding to technology companies.
2. The organization funds companies developing semiconductor technology such as RISC-V processors used for on-device inference.
3. Early-stage companies receive investment capital and strategic guidance through equity funding rounds.
4. Technology entrepreneurs and early-stage startups in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, big data, enterprise software, and healthcare.
5. Its capital is used by semiconductor designers to develop inference chips for edge devices.
6. The firm employs an origination model that incubates companies and actively collaborates with founders rather than acting as a passive financial participant.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization is a recurring investor in a RISC-V processor company and has backed cloud computing and data storage firms.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: The firm makes money through fund management and equity returns on its early-stage investments.
Scale and maturity: The organization was established in 1962 and participates in funding rounds ranging from Series B to Series G.
Geography: The firm is based in the USA.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization focuses on funding and building early-stage companies across cloud computing, enterprise software, fintech, and healthcare technology.

points.name: Spark Capital
points.description: US venture capital firm funding edge AI silicon and photonic computing platforms for autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that finances foundational compute hardware and simulation infrastructure enabling edge and physical AI, funding early-stage and growth startups building inference silicon, networking chips and developer tools rather than deployed robotic systems.
1. A venture capital firm that invests in chip designers, computing platform developers and simulation software startups in exchange for equity.
2. The firm deploys financial capital into companies developing photonic processors, AI accelerators, low-power SoCs and sim-to-real software platforms.
3. Its investments provide funding and strategic backing for on-device inference hardware, computing platforms and physical simulation tools.
4. Portfolio companies receive capital through early-stage and growth funding rounds in exchange for equity.
5. Its investments support edge AI silicon, computing platforms and simulation infrastructure used in autonomous systems and robotics.
6. Its portfolio companies include silicon designers, AI simulation platform developers and computing infrastructure startups.
7. The firm operates as an early-stage and growth investor backing component and subsystem developers in the compute and software layers.
8. The firm focuses on financing foundational computing infrastructure required for artificial general intelligence rather than investing in end-to-end deployed robotic systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named portfolio companies include a RISC-V chip designer, a robotic arm maker, a photonic computing startup, an AI silicon developer and an engineering simulation platform.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: The firm generates returns through venture capital fund management and equity appreciation in its portfolio companies.
Scale and maturity: The firm is a well-established investor with a track record that includes leading and participating in funding rounds from 2016 through 2024.
Geography: The firm is based and operates primarily in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge AI and physical automation, the firm invests broadly across various technology sectors including cybersecurity, data infrastructure and consumer electronics.

points.name: IBM Research
points.description: Technology research organization developing architectural frameworks for edge AI deployment and industrial automation.
points.bullets:
A corporate research laboratory that develops analog in-memory computing chips and architectures for on-device AI inference, building hardware and algorithms that run neural networks directly in memory for industrial and edge deployments.
1. A chip research organization that designs analog in-memory computing neural processing units and small AI models for edge inference.
2. Analog in-memory computing using grids of programmable resistors such as phase-change memory to perform matrix vector multiplications directly in memory, combining analog and digital accelerator nodes for mixed-precision inference.
3. On-device inference of neural networks, transformer acceleration and mixture-of-experts execution with reduced latency and full on-chip weight storage.
4. Research-stage chips, architectures and models demonstrated on test hardware.
5. Edge devices and industrial systems requiring efficient on-device AI inference.
6. Industrial, energy, healthcare, manufacturing and logistics sectors seeking edge AI hardware and predictive maintenance platforms.
7. Its chip architectures and algorithms are intended for integration into edge devices and industrial systems by hardware makers.
8. It performs compute directly in memory using phase-change materials and programmable resistors, eliminating the data movement bottleneck of conventional digital processors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The research has been published in Nature Computational Science, Nature Machine Intelligence and presented at the IEEE International Electron Devices Meeting.
Organization type: A corporate research division of a publicly traded technology conglomerate.
Business model: Corporate-funded research and development producing intellectual property, published science and architectural foundations.
Scale and maturity: A long-established global research laboratory with extensive resources, working on near-software-accuracy test chips.
Geography: Based and operates globally as part of a multinational technology corporation.
Beyond physical AI: The broader organization encompasses cloud computing, enterprise software, consulting services and fundamental research across diverse technology domains.

points.name: EnCharge AI
points.description: US startup building energy-efficient AI chips that run models directly on edge devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs analog in-memory computing accelerators for on-device AI inference, providing hardware and full-stack software to enterprises in automation, robotics, aerospace, and defense.
1. A chip company that designs AI accelerators for on-device inference, sold as PCIe cards and M.2 modules.
2. Charge-based analog in-memory computing architecture that performs computation directly in memory to reduce energy-intensive data movement.
3. Low-power on-device inference that enables AI to run locally without cloud dependency.
4. Hardware accelerator chips in M.2 and PCIe form factors alongside an integrated software stack.
5. Laptops, workstations, industrial robotics, warehouse automation, retail, drones, aerospace, and defense systems.
6. Enterprises in automation, robotics, retail, drones, aerospace, defense, and client computing.
7. Its chips are designed into edge devices and deployed systems by equipment manufacturers and integrators.
8. It uses charge-domain analog computation to achieve higher energy efficiency and density than traditional digital AI accelerators.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Spun out of Princeton University, it works with TSMC on manufacturing and is backed by DARPA, the Department of Defense, RTX Ventures, In-Q-Tel, Tiger Global, Anzu Partners, and LAM Research Capital.
Organization type: Privately held startup spun out of university research.
Business model: Chip and hardware sales alongside software stack licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2022, it has raised roughly $164 million across four funding rounds including a $100 million Series B.
Geography: Based in the United States and preparing to serve the broader global market.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is on developing semiconductor solutions to overcome size, weight, and power constraints for deploying AI in physical environments.

points.name: TetraMem Inc.
points.description: California semiconductor startup developing analog memory chips that process AI directly in memory to slash power consumption for edge devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs analog in-memory computing chips for AI inference at the edge, supplying specialized system-on-chips to developers of power-constrained devices.
1. A chip company that designs analog in-memory computing SoCs for on-device AI inference.
2. The core technology is analog in-memory computing based on multi-level memristor (RRAM) technology, integrating memory and compute to perform high-throughput vector-matrix operations directly within memory arrays to reduce data movement and improve energy efficiency.
3. It delivers high-performance, energy-efficient on-device inference for power- and latency-sensitive edge applications, including voice and audio processing, wearable devices, IoT systems, and always-on sensing.
4. Customers get it as chips and evaluation kits.
5. It is used in edge devices such as wearables, IoT systems, and always-on sensing applications.
6. The company sells to developers of edge devices.
7. Its chips are designed into edge devices by device makers.
8. The approach is distinguished by practical multi-level resistive random-access memory devices capable of high-precision analog computing with thousands of conductance levels.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include SK hynix, TSMC, and researchers at USC.
Organization type: It is a privately held startup.
Business model: The organization makes money through chip sales.
Scale and maturity: The company has advanced from an initial 65nm prototype to achieving tape-out and silicon validation of its 22nm platforms, with evaluation kits expected to ship in the second half of 2026.
Geography: It is based in Silicon Valley and operates globally through strategic partnerships.
Beyond physical AI: Designing analog in-memory computing silicon represents the organization's entire focus and core business activity.

points.name: Aspinity
points.description: United States semiconductor company designing fully analog machine learning processors for ultra-low-power always-on edge AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company developing fully analog machine learning processors for ultra-low-power inference at the edge, targeting always-on sensing in battery-operated devices for automotive, industrial, and smart home sectors.
1. A chip company that designs analog AI processors for on-device edge inference.
2. Analog in-memory computing architectures that perform machine learning inference directly on raw analog sensor data to bypass power-intensive digitization.
3. Ultra-low-power always-on inference for acoustics, bio signals, and industrial anomaly detection at under 50 microwatts.
4. Chips and reconfigurable analog compute cores sold to system makers for integration into edge devices.
5. Smart home security, industrial IoT, automotive sensing, healthcare wearables, and consumer battery-operated devices.
6. IoT device manufacturers, sensor makers, automotive electronics suppliers, and industrial systems integrators.
7. Its chips are designed into edge sensing devices and IoT systems by hardware manufacturers.
8. It keeps the entire signal chain in the analog domain to reduce always-on system power by 95 percent, offering broader analog flexibility across signal types than audio-only competitors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Renesas, through the Preferred Partners Program and Quick-Connect IoT platform demonstrations, and the University of Pittsburgh, where its foundational research originated.
Organization type: A privately held commercial-stage semiconductor startup.
Business model: Semiconductor chip sales and licensed analog compute cores.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, transitioning from research and development into volume production with its first-generation processor shipping and a next-generation 22nm chip in development.
Geography: Based in Pittsburgh, United States, with commercial focus across automotive, industrial, and smart home sectors.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play semiconductor company focused exclusively on analog machine learning technology for edge AI.

points.name: Rain Neuromorphics
points.description: US semiconductor company building brain-inspired analog chips for energy-efficient AI training.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs neuromorphic analog processing units for on-device AI training and inference, targeting extreme power efficiency for edge computing environments.
1. A chip company that designs neuromorphic analog processing units for on-device inference and on-chip training.
2. Neural processing units built on resistive RAM and 3D memristor arrays that compute neural network training and inference at extremely low power using equilibrium propagation.
3. On-device inference, on-chip training and extreme energy efficiency for AI workloads.
4. Chips shipped to partners and device makers.
5. Edge computing and power-constrained AI hardware.
6. Technology firms seeking strategic partnerships or acquisitions.
7. Its chips are designed into edge computing hardware by device makers.
8. It eliminates power-hungry analog-to-digital converters and uses an algorithm compatible with backpropagation to enable on-chip training that conventional analog systems lack.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Prosperity 7 Ventures led its Series A funding round and Sam Altman is an angel investor.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Chip sales.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage hardware startup that taped out a test chip and shipped initial units to partners in 2024.
Geography: Based in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Creating specialized neuromorphic processing units is the entire focus of the company.

points.name: General Vision Inc.
points.description: US semiconductor company designing neuromorphic chips for ultra-low-power on-device learning and edge inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company and IP licensor that develops neuromorphic semiconductors and cognitive memory chips for on-device inference and learning, targeting industrial, maritime and defense automation.
1. A chip company that designs neuromorphic inference chips and licenses the associated IP and developer tools for integration into hardware systems.
2. Cognitive memory chips using a neuromorphic architecture that executes k-Nearest Neighbor inference on a million vectors in under ten microseconds while providing explainable decision-making and lifelong on-device learning.
3. Ultra-fast, ultra-low-power on-device inference, pattern recognition and sensory processing.
4. Cognitive memory chips, licensable IP, APIs, developer tools and complete AI cameras for surface inspection.
5. Manufacturing quality control, commercial fishing vessels and regulated defense programs.
6. Industrial manufacturers, maritime operators and defense agencies.
7. Its chips and IP are designed into heterogeneous hardware architectures like low-power FPGAs by partners integrating edge intelligence.
8. A neuromorphic architecture executes k-Nearest Neighbor inference on a million vectors in under ten microseconds while providing natively explainable decision-making and lifelong on-device learning.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Chip sales, IP licensing and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1988, the mature, established enterprise has tens of thousands of its neuromorphic devices deployed in the field since 2007.
Geography: Headquartered in San Francisco, it operates across both United States and international defense sectors.
Beyond physical AI: The pure-play entity dedicates its entire operational focus to advancing neuromorphic components and intellectual property for edge AI applications.

points.name: Huawei HiSilicon
points.description: Chinese semiconductor company designing AI chips for on-device mobile inference and edge computing.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor design company that develops AI-specific processors and mobile SoCs for on-device inference, edge computing, and autonomous physical systems. It operates as the captive silicon design arm of a larger technology parent company, supplying specialized chips for integration into vertically integrated consumer electronics, automotive, and industrial platforms. The organization focuses on enabling real-time, low-latency processing for autonomous machines rather than centralized cloud infrastructure.
1. A chip company that designs neural processing units and mobile SoCs for on-device inference.
2. Neural processing units and AI-specific silicon in mobile SoCs, utilizing a LogicFolding chip architecture that achieves performance via logic gate reuse and stacking rather than advanced lithography process nodes.
3. On-device inference, real-time low-latency processing, and edge computing for autonomous physical systems.
4. Chips and SoCs designed exclusively for integration into its parent company's vertically integrated product platforms.
5. Advanced driver-assistance systems, autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, autonomous mobile robots, industrial vision systems, smart infrastructure, and mobile devices.
6. Its parent company and its parent company's vertically integrated product platforms.
7. Its chips are designed into devices and autonomous machines manufactured by its parent company.
8. It achieves competitive AI performance through a LogicFolding architecture relying on logic gate reuse and stacking instead of restricted advanced lithography process nodes.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A larger technology parent company and third-party foundries.
Organization type: A captive semiconductor design subsidiary of a larger technology company.
Business model: Internal component supply for its parent company's vertically integrated hardware products.
Scale and maturity: A well-established, large-scale semiconductor entity actively pursuing manufacturing independence.
Geography: Based in China, focusing on supporting domestic AI chip industry goals and serving domestic and export markets.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is the design of semiconductor components, including neural network processors for mobile devices and data center applications.

points.name: Azimuth AI
points.description: Indian semiconductor company designing ultra-low-power system-on-chips for on-device edge AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs application-specific integrated circuits for on-device edge AI inference and real-time intelligence in industrial and infrastructure applications.
1. A chip company that designs system-on-chips for on-device edge AI inference.
2. The core technology is a Software-Defined Silicon architecture that integrates multi-core custom computing, analog sensing, memory, and intelligent power management into an ultra-low-power system-on-chip.
3. It delivers intelligent, energy-efficient on-device inference for real-time local processing without cloud connectivity.
4. Customers get it as chips provided through a turnkey solution spanning design through fabrication and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test management.
5. The chips are used in smart utilities, advanced metering, battery management, smart city infrastructure, and industrial automation.
6. The company sells to industrial automation providers and smart infrastructure operators.
7. Its chips are designed into smart utility, metering, and industrial IoT devices by infrastructure and automation equipment makers.
8. A proprietary Software-Defined Silicon architecture enables flexible, future-ready designs combined with exceptionally low power consumption.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A mixed-signal and power ASIC partner co-develops the chips and manages design through fab, OSAT management, and final chip delivery.
Organization type: A privately held startup in the early commercialization phase.
Business model: The organization makes money through chip sales.
Scale and maturity: A newly established firm launched in November 2025 with technology in early commercialization phases.
Geography: The company is based in India and operates entirely within the country, aligning with India's domestic semiconductor value chain objectives.
Beyond physical AI: As a pure-play embedded silicon company, its entire focus is the design and delivery of specialized edge computing chips for local intelligence.

points.name: Cyient
points.description: Indian technology company designing custom low-power silicon chips for smart utility edge devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor design and turnkey services company that builds custom system-on-chip platforms for high-efficiency edge AI and industrial automation. The organization manages the complete silicon lifecycle from architecture and mixed-signal design through fabrication and outsourced assembly, delivering foundational chips for smart utilities, robotics, automotive, and industrial sectors.
1. A chip company that designs custom ASICs and system-on-chip platforms for edge AI inference and industrial applications.
2. Low-power mixed-signal ASICs and intelligent power management systems engineered for edge inference.
3. On-device edge AI inference, intelligent power management, and custom silicon lifecycle management.
4. Chips and custom semiconductor design services.
5. Smart utilities, advanced metering, robotics, automotive, data centers, and industrial automation.
6. Smart utilities, automotive manufacturers, robotics makers, data center operators, and industrial automation companies.
7. Its custom chips are designed into industrial, automotive, and robotic systems by device manufacturers.
8. A true custom ASIC turnkey solution model that accelerates time-to-market for complex systems-on-chip through mixed-signal design and intelligent power management.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A chip design partner that co-developed an edge AI silicon chip with Azimuth AI.
Organization type: A publicly traded commercial technology company aligned with national strategic initiatives.
Business model: Semiconductor design services, custom chip sales, and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test management.
Scale and maturity: An established domestic semiconductor player in India that unveiled a collaborative silicon platform in November 2025.
Geography: Headquartered in Hyderabad, India, operating largely within the domestic Indian market while building a global chip design presence.
Beyond physical AI: A broader engineering and custom semiconductor manufacturing services provider for energy management and industrial intelligence.

points.name: Forschungszentrum Jülich
points.description: German research institution developing energy-efficient silicon chips for real-time AI inference in robotics.
points.bullets:
A research center that develops energy-efficient inference silicon and full-stack edge AI systems for real-time, deterministic decision-making in robotics and industrial applications, serving the energy, chemical, automotive, and advanced materials sectors through research and technology transfer.
1. A research institution that designs edge AI inference accelerators and FPGA demonstrators, delivering them through technology transfer and spinoffs.
2. The core technology is a patented low-bit AI engine using gain-cell crossbar array architectures and analog in-memory computing for LLM attention mechanisms, optimizing inference latency per watt while achieving near-FP32 accuracy.
3. It delivers low-power on-device inference, deterministic real-time decision-making, and AI-powered research and development automation.
4. It provides hardware accelerators, FPGA demonstrators, and PyTorch-compatible software toolchains via technology transfer and spinoff commercialization.
5. The technology is used in robotics, industrial systems, and energy, chemical, and advanced materials research.
6. It serves the energy, chemical, automotive, and advanced materials sectors, and robotics developers seeking technology transfer.
7. Its chips and subsystems are designed into robotics and industrial systems by device makers and industrial developers.
8. Its approach distinguishes itself by optimizing for inference latency per watt rather than raw computational throughput, using proprietary low-bit precision processing to achieve near-FP32 accuracy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It hosts the JARA Institute for Energy-efficient Information Technology (PGI-10) and has spun off ViMi Labs.
Organization type: It is a government research institution and national research center.
Business model: It operates through institutional research funding and technology transfer commercialization.
Scale and maturity: It is a well-established scientific institution that recently launched a dedicated physical AI spinoff platform in 2024.
Geography: The organization is based in Germany and focuses on technological sovereignty within the European market.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond its physical AI initiatives, it operates as a broad scientific research center that transfers wider technological innovations to industrial applications.

points.name: Locai
points.description: Device-first AI infrastructure company building local processing hardware for on-device inference.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds edge AI infrastructure software for orchestrating on-device inference across fleets of physical automation systems, handling device registration, fleet management, model deployment, and cloud fallback routing for operators of distributed edge computing devices.
1. A developer tools company whose edge AI orchestration platform manages model deployment and fleet management for on-device inference.
2. The platform uses a lightweight runtime agent that keeps models warm on-device to eliminate cold start latency, runs models as GGUF files using llama.cpp, and uses a pub/sub protocol designed for distributed low-latency edge workloads.
3. Device registration, fleet management, model deployment, workload routing, and cloud fallback infrastructure for on-device AI inference.
4. Licensed software and runtime agents deployed across customer device fleets.
5. Distributed edge computing devices and physical automation systems.
6. Operators requiring orchestration of distributed edge computing devices and physical AI deployments.
7. Its orchestration platform is integrated by operators into their distributed edge devices and physical automation systems.
8. Its orchestration capabilities bridge local device management with cloud fallback infrastructure while keeping models warm on-device to eliminate cold start latency.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Google for Startups, NVIDIA Inception, and Fuel Ventures.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions for edge AI infrastructure orchestration.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup backed by venture and corporate accelerator programs.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI infrastructure and physical automation orchestration are the complete and entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Fuel Ventures
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage companies developing autonomous AI systems for industrial and critical infrastructure deployments.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that funds early-stage startups developing edge AI, sensor-fusion and autonomous systems for industrial and critical infrastructure applications, providing capital and operational expertise.
1. A venture capital firm that invests in startups building edge AI software and sensor-fusion platforms for industrial autonomy.
2. The firm targets investments in foundational edge AI software and sensor-fusion platforms that enable on-premises autonomy.
3. Its investments support the development of real-time autonomous decision-making platforms for heavy industries.
4. The firm provides funding and operational guidance, along with access to discounted software and infrastructure tools.
5. Its portfolio companies deploy field-level autonomous systems in oil and gas, energy, water, manufacturing, and transport.
6. It serves entrepreneurs and early-stage companies building industrial automation technology.
7. It operates as an early-stage investor providing capital and operational support to physical AI startups.
8. The firm leverages its founder's entrepreneurial experience and network to offer portfolio companies discounted software and infrastructure partnerships alongside capital.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable portfolio investments include Locai and Intelligent Core.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm founded by Mark Pearson.
Business model: The firm generates returns through venture capital investing in early-stage startups.
Scale and maturity: It is an established investor that leads initial funding rounds ranging from £500k to £2m.
Geography: The firm operates within the British venture capital ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are central to its investment thesis and represent its entire focus.

points.name: Ultralytics
points.description: US software company developing real-time computer vision models for edge devices.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and developer tools company that builds the YOLO family of real-time object detection and image segmentation models and provides a Python package for training, testing and deploying them. Its computer vision models are exported to edge inference formats and run on third-party silicon and sensors for physical AI applications like factory defect detection and autonomous driving perception.
1. An AI model developer and developer tools company whose computer vision models and training and deployment software run on other companies' edge hardware.
2. Convolutional neural network architectures for real-time object detection, segmentation, classification, tracking and depth estimation, optimized for low-latency inference and exportable to hardware-specific edge toolchains.
3. Real-time object detection, image segmentation, object tracking, depth estimation and high-throughput multi-stream camera processing.
4. Open-source and packaged computer vision models, a Python package and export toolchains delivering models that run on customers' edge hardware and inference chips.
5. Factory automation, defect detection, quality inspection, object counting and autonomous driving perception.
6. Edge device makers, chip companies, factory automation engineers and developers building computer vision pipelines.
7. Its models and software tools are integrated by device makers and developers into edge hardware and vision systems built around other companies' silicon and sensors.
8. Its YOLO model family pairs state-of-the-art detection precision and low latency with a Python package that exports directly to a wide range of edge inference formats and neural processing units.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with Huawei, Axelera AI, Intel OpenVINO, Sony IMX500, Google LiteRT and DEEPX.
Organization type: Privately held software company.
Business model: Software licenses, platform subscriptions and developer tools.
Geography: Based in the USA and serves a global developer community.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is computer vision model development and deployment software for edge and physical AI.

points.name: Mirai
points.description: London-based software startup building inference engines that run AI models directly on consumer devices without cloud dependency.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds on-device inference infrastructure for consumer edge devices. It makes a proprietary inference engine and software development kit that optimize AI model performance on Apple Silicon, enabling local execution for developers building consumer applications.
1. A developer tools company that builds a Rust-based inference engine and SDK for on-device AI optimization on edge devices.
2. A hardware-aware runtime and inference engine written in Rust that co-designs models and runtime for Apple Silicon to accelerate local generation and prefill.
3. On-device inference, model optimization, hybrid cloud routing, and deployment tooling for local execution.
4. Licensed software and SDKs that developers integrate into their applications.
5. Smartphones, laptops, and other consumer edge devices running on-device assistants, transcribers, translators, and chat tools.
6. Software developers and consumer-facing application builders.
7. Its inference stack is integrated by software developers into apps running on consumer hardware platforms.
8. Its engine co-designs models and runtime specifically for Apple Silicon and delivers faster generation and prefill speeds than alternative runtimes.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Apple Silicon is its key platform, with cloud support from Base10 and seed funding led by Uncork Capital.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A 14-person team that has raised a $10 million seed round.
Geography: Based in London, United Kingdom, with software optimization focused on Apple Silicon and plans to expand to Android.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Uncork Capital
points.location: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage platforms that deploy machine learning models to mobile devices and edge hardware.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that funds seed-stage startups building edge AI and robotics infrastructure, investing in developer tools, machine learning optimization platforms, and inference silicon providers that supply the physical AI ecosystem.
1. A venture capital firm that makes seed and opportunity-fund investments in early-stage startups.
2. Seed-stage financial capital and partnership support targeting edge machine learning, on-device AI deployment tools, and inference silicon startups.
3. Funding for edge AI infrastructure development, including machine learning optimization platforms and developer tools for on-device inference.
4. Equity investments and portfolio support services delivered to early-stage startup founders.
5. Edge devices, robotics, drones, autonomous vehicles, and smart devices used by its portfolio companies' customers.
6. Early-stage software teams and technology startups building AI-native platforms and infrastructure.
7. It provides capital to startups developing the developer tools and silicon that device makers and robotics engineers integrate into their own products.
8. It combines a 20-year seed-stage specialist focus with an explicit investment thesis around bridging infrastructure gaps in emerging frontier technologies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Portfolio companies include an inference silicon developer, an on-device machine learning platform, and a maritime autonomy software developer, with Goodwin Legal and Silicon Valley Bank providing strategic services.
Organization type: Privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: Fund management, generating returns through equity appreciation and exits across its portfolio companies.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2004, it manages a $225 million seed fund and a $75 million opportunity fund, with over 275 portfolio companies and tens of billions in exit enterprise value.
Geography: Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, California, backing companies targeting global software and hardware markets.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it is a general venture capital fund that also invests heavily in developer tools, enterprise software, and other foundational technology sectors.

points.name: Schaeffler
points.description: German industrial company building precision motion systems and actuators for physical AI and robotics.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that manufactures precision motion systems, actuators, planetary roller screws, bearings, and gearboxes for robotics, while operating its own factories using purchased humanoid robots and investing in robot makers. It builds mechanical components that enable the physical deployment of edge AI in robotics and automation, and it operates as a manufacturing customer deploying thousands of humanoids in its own facilities.
1. A component supplier that makes robot actuators, gearboxes, roller screws, and bearings for robot makers, and a manufacturing operator that deploys purchased humanoid robots in its own plants.
2. Precision mechanical components including planetary gear actuators, inverted planetary roller screws, slewing rings, and linear modules designed for continuous-duty joint articulation in robots, alongside solid-state battery technology under development.
3. High-precision joint motion, continuous-duty actuation, minimal-compliance torque transmission for complex robotic movements, and condition monitoring for industrial automation.
4. Components sold to robot manufacturers, integration services and engineering consultation, and complete robots-as-a-service operated in its own manufacturing facilities.
5. Humanoid robots, industrial robot arms, collaborative robots, automotive drivetrains, and factory automation in manufacturing and warehouse environments.
6. Robot makers, automakers, and industrial manufacturers, while also acting as a paying deployment customer for humanoid robot operators.
7. Its actuators, bearings, and gearboxes are designed into humanoid robots and industrial arms by device makers, and it buys complete robots from OEMs to run in its own factories.
8. It combines decades of precision mechanical engineering and automotive-scale manufacturing with strategic venture investments and large-scale deployment commitments in the humanoid robotics companies it supplies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Agility Robotics, Humanoid, Neura Robotics, Hexagon Robotics, and Tesla.
Organization type: Publicly traded industrial manufacturing company that makes strategic venture investments in robotics startups.
Business model: Component sales to robot and automaker OEMs, engineering consultation, and robotics-as-a-service rental fees paid to robot operators for in-factory deployment.
Scale and maturity: A Fortune 500 company with around 120,000 employees and more than 250 locations in 55 countries, expecting a robotics order book reaching hundreds of millions of euros by 2030.
Geography: Based in Germany with a dedicated embodied intelligence robotics unit in Taicang, China, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: A traditional automotive and industrial components manufacturer producing bearings, drivetrain components, and solid-state batteries for the broader mobility and industrial sectors.

points.name: LimX Dynamics
points.description: Chinese robotics company manufacturing full-size humanoid platforms for embodied AI research and commercial deployment.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells general-purpose humanoid and multi-modal robots, paired with its own operating system, embodied AI models and developer tools, for research, commercial and enterprise customers.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells humanoid, bipedal and wheeled quadruped robots along with a proprietary operating system and VLA model training platform.
2. Full-size humanoid hardware with 31 degrees of freedom, reinforcement learning-based motion control, vision-language-action models, and an agentic operating system using large language models and world models for reasoning and planning.
3. Dynamic bipedal locomotion, whole-body motion control, real-time terrain perception, stair climbing, and autonomous reasoning and planning in physical environments.
4. Complete robots, modular robot bases, and a licensed operating system and open-source VLA model training platform.
5. Humanoids, research platforms, entertainment, hospitality, retail, manufacturing, and commercial service settings.
6. Developers, research institutions, systems integrators, and commercial operators.
7. Its robots and operating systems are sold directly to developers, research institutions and commercial operators, with distribution and integration handled by integrators in Europe.
8. It builds the complete embodied AI stack from humanoid hardware and motion foundation models to an agentic operating system, and can synchronize control of up to 200 robots at millisecond-level precision.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: EnduX serves as a distributor and integrator in Europe, and its investors include Alibaba, NIO Capital, IDG Capital, Lens Technology and SAIC Motor-backed Shangqi Capital.
Organization type: A privately held startup preparing for an IPO.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots, software licenses, and developer platform access.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2022, it has raised approximately $200 million in a Series B round and pre-IPO funding, holds 99 patents, and is delivering and taking pre-orders for thousands of humanoid units globally.
Geography: Based in Shenzhen, China, with global pre-order availability and deliveries to customers in South Korea.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation represent the complete and entire focus of the organization's overall mission and business.

points.name: iRobot
points.description: US consumer robotics company manufacturing autonomous home cleaning robots with on-device AI for navigation and mapping.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and builds autonomous home cleaning robots and military explosive ordnance disposal robots, integrating sensors, edge inference silicon, actuators and navigation software into complete consumer and defense robotic platforms.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds complete autonomous floor-cleaning and mopping robots for consumers and tracked manipulator robots for militaries.
2. Visual simultaneous localization and mapping software running on mobile processors, combined with computer vision, smart mapping and underactuated end-effectors.
3. Autonomous navigation, room-specific floor cleaning, multi-robot coordination, map memory and explosive ordnance disposal manipulation.
4. Complete consumer robots and military ground robots sold as physical hardware, alongside companion mobile applications.
5. Homes, lawns and military field operations.
6. Consumers and militaries.
7. Its complete robots are sold directly to consumers and procured under contract by defense agencies, integrating third-party processors and its own proprietary software.
8. It is a pure-play consumer robotics pioneer that has scaled autonomous vacuum deployment to tens of millions of households using on-device mapping and multi-robot coordination.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Qualcomm Technologies provides processors for its consumer robots, Boeing jointly secured Air Force contracts for small unmanned ground systems, Picea Robotics is its parent company and former contract manufacturer, and the U.S. Navy and Air Force are defense customers.
Organization type: A wholly-owned subsidiary of a foreign parent company, previously publicly traded before Chapter 11 bankruptcy restructuring.
Business model: Hardware sales of consumer robots and accessories, alongside defense contracts for military robots.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1990, it has shipped over 50 million consumer robots globally and deployed over 4,500 military robots, with historical peak revenues exceeding $1.5 billion before a severe financial decline.
Geography: Based in the United States, with a newly established domestic subsidiary for data security, operating globally and owned by a Chinese parent company.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and consumer robotics constitute the entirety of its business focus.

points.name: RealSense
points.description: California-based robotics technology company building embedded depth cameras for physical AI perception.
points.bullets:
A depth camera company spun out of a major semiconductor manufacturer that designs and sells 3D vision sensors and embedded perception chips for robots, automation systems and biometrics, serving robot makers and industrial automation providers worldwide.
1. A sensor maker that builds stereo depth cameras and vision system-on-chips for on-device 3D perception in robots.
2. Stereo depth cameras and vision processing SoCs that compute 3D depth maps and six-degree-of-freedom tracking on-device for real-time spatial awareness.
3. 3D perception, obstacle detection, spatial mapping, visual odometry and object recognition for autonomous navigation and manipulation.
4. Depth camera modules and embedded vision chips designed into robots by device makers.
5. Autonomous mobile robots, humanoid robots, robot arms, industrial automation, security, healthcare and biometric identification.
6. Robot makers, industrial automation providers, healthcare providers and retail technology developers.
7. Its sensors and chips are designed into robots and automation systems by robot manufacturers.
8. Its depth cameras are embedded in the majority of the world's autonomous mobile robots and humanoids, giving it dominant market penetration in robotics 3D vision.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its sensors are compatible with NVIDIA's Isaac software suite and Jetson Thor computing platform, and its customers include Unitree Robotics, Boston Dynamics and Agility Robotics.
Organization type: A privately held startup spun out from Intel.
Business model: Hardware sales of depth cameras and vision chips.
Scale and maturity: Spun out with $50 million in Series A funding, holding over 80 patents and serving more than 3,000 customers worldwide.
Geography: Based in California, USA, and operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and physical robotics represent the entire focus of the company.

points.name: Kiva Systems
points.description: US robotics company deploying automated mobile robots to transport inventory pods within fulfillment warehouses.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that built automated guided vehicles and an integrated fleet coordination system to move inventory racks to stationary human workers in e-commerce fulfillment centers, operating originally for outside retailers and now solely for its parent company's logistics network.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells mobile warehouse robots and integrated fulfillment systems.
2. Mobile drive-unit robots that navigate via floor-mounted barcode stickers and cameras and lift storage pods using a corkscrew mechanism, coordinated by centralized fleet orchestration software.
3. Autonomous navigation of warehouse floors, heavy-load lifting and transport of storage pods, adaptive motion control, and distributed fleet coordination for collision avoidance.
4. Complete robots and integrated fulfillment systems installed directly in warehouse facilities, now operated solely within its parent company's network.
5. Warehouses, e-commerce fulfillment centers and retail distribution centers.
6. Retailers, logistics operators and e-commerce companies, now exclusively its parent company.
7. It builds mobile robots and orchestration software and sells or deploys them as integrated warehouse automation systems.
8. Its adaptive motion control and distributed fleet coordination technology allows individual robots to learn warehouse-specific conditions and share that data across the entire fleet.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Bain Capital Ventures was an early investor, Staples was its first flagship customer, and Amazon acquired it in 2012 and rebranded it as Amazon Robotics.
Organization type: Formerly a privately held startup, now a subsidiary of a publicly traded e-commerce conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales and integrated systems deployment for external customers prior to acquisition, now internal automation operations for its parent company.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2003, deployed hundreds of robots for external clients before being acquired for $775 million, and now operates a fleet exceeding one million mobile robots across more than 300 facilities.
Geography: Based in North Reading, Massachusetts, deployed systems across domestic distribution centers, and now operates within its parent company's global warehouse network.
Beyond physical AI: Its parent entity is a global e-commerce and technology conglomerate that has expanded the robotics division to include AI-powered computer vision robotic arms for item sorting.

points.name: Geek+
points.description: Chinese robotics developer deploying autonomous mobile robots for warehouse and supply chain automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile robots and humanoid robots for warehouse and supply chain automation. It designs and manufactures mobile robots, tote-and-shuttle systems, and warehouse-specific humanoids, alongside fleet management and warehouse execution software. It sells complete systems to logistics operators, retailers, and manufacturers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots, tote-to-person shuttles, sortation systems, and warehouse humanoids.
2. Mobile robots using QR-code and SLAM navigation, high-resolution lidar, onboard processors, and cloud-based fleet scheduling software capable of coordinating heterogeneous fleets of thousands of robots.
3. Goods-to-person and tote-to-person fulfillment, autonomous sortation, piece picking, intralogistics transport, and large-scale multi-robot fleet orchestration.
4. Complete robots, shuttles, and integrated systems, sold as capital equipment or offered through robots-as-a-service arrangements.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers, fulfillment centers, and manufacturing production lines.
6. E-commerce companies, retailers, third-party logistics providers, apparel brands, pharmaceutical companies, and manufacturers.
7. Its robots and software are deployed in warehouses operated by logistics companies and retailers, sometimes integrated into broader systems by warehouse automation integrators.
8. Its fleet management software coordinates thousands of heterogeneous mobile robots in a single facility, and it has extended its robot-making into general-purpose warehouse humanoids.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include Microsoft and Intel, and its robots are integrated by supply chain companies like Körber and FORTNA; customers include DHL, Walmart, Nike, Decathlon, and SF Express.
Organization type: Publicly traded company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and systems, software licenses, and robots-as-a-service leasing arrangements.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, it has over 1,500 employees, has deployed over 56,000 robots across 40-plus countries, and holds a leading share of the global goods-to-person market.
Geography: Headquartered in China, it operates globally across Asia-Pacific, the Americas, and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: As a pure-play company, edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are its entire focus.

points.name: Mobile Industrial Robots (MiR)
points.description: Danish manufacturer building autonomous mobile robots that use on-device AI for navigation and warehouse logistics.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that develops and manufactures autonomous mobile robots and fleet management software for internal logistics and material handling. It provides modular, infrastructure-free mobile platforms and mobile manipulators that transport payloads up to 1,350 kg, along with cloud-based fleet orchestration tools.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots, mobile manipulators, and fleet management software for industrial logistics.
2. SLAM navigation, AI-based pallet detection, publish-subscribe data exchange for fleet coordination, and mobile manipulator integration combining its AMRs with external collaborative robot arms.
3. Autonomous navigation, heavy-payload transport, floor-to-floor pallet movement, mobile manipulation, and fleet orchestration of more than 100 AMRs with MES and ERP integration.
4. Complete robots, mobile manipulators, and licensed fleet management software.
5. Factories, warehouses, and logistics environments for internal material transport.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, and enterprises of varying sizes.
7. It sells complete robots to end users and integrators, and supplies mobile manipulator platforms that integrate manipulators from a sister subsidiary.
8. It combines a broad payload range from low to heavy loads under a common fleet management software, with modular hardware requiring no fixed infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Teradyne, Universal Robots, NVIDIA Isaac, RealSense, and Skild AI.
Organization type: Subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of mobile robots and software licenses or subscriptions for fleet management.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2013, acquired in 2018, an established global supplier with nearly 220 distributors and integrators across 60 countries.
Geography: Based in Odense, Denmark, with global operations spanning 60 countries.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, robotics, and physical automation represent the complete and central focus of the organization's overall mission.

points.name: Sunday Robotics
points.description: Robotics company building wheeled semi-humanoid home robots for household automation tasks.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds vertically integrated, dual-armed wheeled mobile manipulation robots for household chores, developing its own hardware, actuators, and vision-language-action foundation models in-house for the consumer market.
1. A robot maker that builds complete wheeled semi-humanoid robots and proprietary teleoperation glove systems for data collection.
2. Wheeled mobile manipulators with dual arms, three-finger grippers, millimeter-precision actuators, and on-device inference running vision-language-action foundation models trained on human demonstration data.
3. General-purpose household manipulation including folding laundry, constructing boxes, and generalizing learned skills to new homes and previously unseen objects.
4. Complete robots placed in homes through beta programs.
5. Domestic homes.
6. Consumers.
7. It builds its own hardware and AI models and places complete robots directly into consumer households.
8. It avoids in-home teleoperation by using off-site human demonstration data from a distributed network of workers using a low-cost kinematic glove system.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by venture capital firms Bain Capital Ventures, Conviction, Benchmark, and Coatue Management.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of consumer robots.
Scale and maturity: A prototype-stage company that raised an $185M Series B funding round and plans a pre-commercial beta deployment across approximately fifty households by 2026.
Geography: Based in Mountain View, California, USA, and operating within domestic environments.
Beyond physical AI: Designing, building, and training physical home robots is the company's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Weave Robotics
points.description: Robotics company building household laundry-folding and wheeled humanoid robots with on-device autonomy and remote teleoperation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells dual-armed mobile manipulation robots for household tasks, designing complete machines that combine on-device autonomy with physical hardware for home use.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells wheeled mobile humanoid robots for domestic chores.
2. The core technology integrates dual-armed manipulation hardware, wheeled mobile bases, autonomous navigation software, edge AI inference for on-device perception, and privacy features like mechanical camera shutters.
3. The specific capabilities delivered include autonomous navigation in home environments, dexterous manipulation for folding laundry, tidying rooms, making beds, and putting away toys.
4. Customers get complete robots.
5. The machines are used in homes, with planned expansion into adjacent commercial settings like hotels, nursing homes, and supermarkets.
6. The types of customer it sells to are mainstream consumers.
7. It designs and manufactures its own complete robots for direct deployment in home environments.
8. A pragmatic, task-focused strategy that prioritizes narrow, high-frequency household chores distinguishes its approach from competitors pursuing general-purpose humanoid platforms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a portfolio company of ALM Ventures Fund I.
Organization type: It is a privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of complete robots.
Scale and maturity: It is an early-stage company that began deliveries of its first stationary robot in early 2024 and launched its second mobile humanoid system later that year.
Geography: It is based in San Francisco, California, and operates deployments across California.
Beyond physical AI: It is a pure-play robotics enterprise where its entire business focus is dedicated to physical automation and edge AI.

points.name: Rethink Robotics
points.description: Robotics manufacturer building collaborative robotic arms equipped with force-sensing joints for safe physical automation alongside factory workers.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that built collaborative robotic arms designed to work safely alongside human workers in factory environments, providing complete deployed systems for small and medium-sized manufacturers.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete collaborative robots with integrated operating systems.
2. Series elastic actuators with joint-level force sensing, integrated vision and sonar, and a proprietary intuitive operating system enabling learning-by-doing programming.
3. Safe human-robot collaboration, force-limited operation, high-precision assembly, machine tending, and task training through physical demonstration.
4. Complete robotic arms with integrated software.
5. Factories, assembly lines, machine tending, electronic assembly, circuit board testing and packaging operations.
6. Small and medium-sized manufacturers.
7. It builds and sells complete robotic arms directly to manufacturers for use on their production lines.
8. Its elastic actuators and learning-by-doing software allowed factory workers to teach tasks through physical demonstration rather than requiring specialized engineering code.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Cognex, GE Lighting, Steelcase, GE Ventures, HAHN Group, United Robotics Group, Corun USA and Génération Robots.
Organization type: Privately held startup before bankruptcy and acquisition.
Business model: Robot hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2008, raised approximately $113.5 million in funding and ceased original operations in 2018.
