Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, with sales and operational focus across North America, Western Europe, China, Japan and Mexico.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and industrial robotics represented the absolute core of its mission.

points.name: HAHN Group
points.description: German holding company integrating collaborative robots and intuitive programming software for industrial automation.
points.bullets:
A holding company and systems integrator that builds and integrates industrial automation and collaborative robots for manufacturers, combining its own acquired cobot technology with integration services and equipment rental offerings.
1. A robot maker and systems integrator that builds collaborative robots and industrial robotic arms, sold as complete machines, integration services and rental offerings.
2. Collaborative manipulation and single-arm industrial robotic tasks, mobile robot deployment and turnkey factory automation.
3. Complete robots, autonomous mobile robots, licensed programming software and integration services.
4. Industrial manufacturing environments and factories.
5. Manufacturers and industrial enterprises.
6. It pairs its own acquired, intuitively programmable collaborative robot technology with German engineering expertise in industrial automation.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held holding company.
Business model: Robot sales, equipment rental offerings, software licensing and integration contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established organization with over 30 years of experience, about 1,100 employees and 19 locations across over a dozen countries.
Geography: Based in Germany with production and integration sites across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and North America.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation constitute the entire core business focus of this industrial automation specialist.

points.name: Johns Hopkins University
points.description: Maryland research institution developing autonomous surgical robots that perform complex procedures with minimal human intervention.
points.bullets:
A university research lab that develops autonomous surgical robotics and AI models, building experimental systems that integrate vision-language models with commercial surgical robots to perform medical procedures with minimal human intervention for the healthcare sector.
1. A university research lab that builds autonomous surgical robotics software and models, validated on existing surgical robot hardware.
2. Vision-language models and transformer-based on-device AI decision-making integrated with real-time computer vision and physical robotic manipulation systems.
3. Autonomous execution of surgical tasks such as gallbladder removal, learning from demonstrations, and responding to real-time voice commands.
4. Research prototypes and open datasets, including surgical robotics demonstration data for temporal action segmentation.
5. Hospitals and surgical settings using robotic surgical systems.
6. Federal research funding agencies, medical institutions, and academic collaborators.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Nomagic, Hai Robotics, and Toyota Industries.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Systems integration, hardware and software sales, and lifecycle services contracts.
Scale and maturity: A mature, globally deployed business with an established installed base at high-volume distribution centers.
Geography: Based in Europe and operating across global logistics hubs.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire business is dedicated to optimizing physical logistics and material handling through intelligent software, automated sorting systems, and predictive maintenance.

points.name: Nomagic
points.description: Robotics company deploying AI-powered picking and packing robots for warehouse fulfillment operations.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds AI-powered robotic arms and software for piece picking and packing in warehouse automation, combining vision-language-action models with its own end-of-arm tooling and integration into existing storage systems.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells robotic picking and packing systems integrated with existing warehouse infrastructure.
2. Vision-language-action models trained on a proprietary dataset of millions of real-world edge cases drive robotic arms with 3D vision and proprietary link technology for autonomous operation.
3. Bin picking, single-item picking, shoebox handling, packing, sorter induction, and adaptation to dynamic environments with high SKU variety.
4. Complete robotic arms and picking cells with integrated AI software, installed and operated in customers' fulfillment centers.
5. Warehouses, fulfillment centers, e-commerce, fashion logistics, and automated storage and retrieval systems.
6. Logistics operators, e-commerce retailers, and system integrators.
7. It builds and supplies its own robotic systems directly to logistics operators for installation in their fulfillment centers.
8. A proprietary dataset of real-world edge cases built from millions of live operational picks enables fast deployment and high accuracy on millions of SKU variations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Customers and partners include Zalando, Brack.Alltron, Komplett, Arvato, Vanderlande, and Khosla Ventures, using 3D cameras from Zivid.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic systems and associated software for warehouse automation.
Scale and maturity: A maturing enterprise that raised a $44M Series B in February 2025, with robots generating millions of successful picks monthly for paying customers.
Geography: Based in Poland with deployments across European fulfillment centers, including Scandinavia and Germany, and an expanded presence in Georgia.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play robotics provider focused entirely on physical artificial intelligence for warehouse automation.

points.name: Neural Magic
points.description: Software company accelerating on-device AI inference on commodity hardware.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops inference optimization and model compression tools enabling efficient execution of sparse large language models on commodity processors and edge hardware for enterprise customers.
1. An AI software company that builds inference engines and model pruning tools delivered as software.
2. A sparsity-aware inference engine and pruning libraries that exploit model sparsity to accelerate neural network execution on standard CPUs.
3. On-device inference acceleration, model pruning, and sparse library optimization for large language models.
4. Licensed software and open-source tools integrated into enterprise and cloud AI infrastructure.
5. Enterprise AI and cloud inference deployments.
6. Enterprises seeking cost-effective AI deployment on commodity hardware.
7. Its inference software is integrated by enterprises into their AI infrastructure to run optimized models on standard processors.
8. It delivers faster inference for sparse models on commodity hardware without specialized AI accelerators while maintaining accuracy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates as a subsidiary of Red Hat and has collaborated with Cerebras.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded enterprise software company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Acquired in January 2025 after reaching maturity as an independent company.
Geography: Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA.
Beyond physical AI: The organization now concentrates on integrating virtual large language model technologies into a broader enterprise AI infrastructure platform.

points.name: MosChip
points.type: AI Engineering and Machine Learning services company
points.description: AI engineering services company accelerating industrial automation through modular edge AI model deployment.
points.bullets:
An AI engineering and embedded systems services company that designs, optimizes and deploys edge AI models, firmware and RISC-V computing solutions for industrial automation and connected product ecosystems, serving enterprises needing real-time, on-device inference.
1. A developer tools and engineering services company that builds pre-trained edge AI model suites, model optimization runtimes and embedded firmware, sold as modular software platforms and engineering services.
2. Hardware-optimized neural network inferencing runtimes and pre-trained edge AI models designed to run across heterogeneous low-power silicon including FPGAs, NPUs, MPSoCs and RISC-V cores.
3. On-device inference, real-time industrial analytics, predictive maintenance, quality control and edge model optimization across constrained hardware architectures.
4. Modular software platforms with reusable AI models and engineering integration services deployed onto customer hardware.
5. Industrial automation, smart manufacturing, industrial IoT, multimedia and connected industrial products.
6. Manufacturers, industrial operators, semiconductor companies and enterprises building connected products.
7. Its software and engineering services are integrated by industrial device makers and enterprises directly onto their edge hardware platforms.
8. Deep semiconductor design and FPGA expertise ensures AI models perform consistently across heterogeneous hardware architectures without manual per-deployment optimization.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: TSMC, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, NXP, AMD-Xilinx, Lattice, Infineon and Google TensorFlow.
Organization type: A privately held engineering services and platform company.
Business model: Software platform licensing and engineering services contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established company with over 25 years of experience, development centers in India and the USA and over 500 products delivered.
Geography: Based in India with a corporate office in Santa Clara, California and global development operations.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization's broader business encompasses foundational semiconductor design, silicon verification and embedded systems engineering.

points.name: Apache TVM
points.description: Open-source compiler framework optimizing machine learning models to run efficiently on diverse edge and physical AI hardware.
points.bullets:
A developer tools project that builds an open-source machine learning compiler framework to optimize and deploy AI models on resource-constrained edge devices and diverse hardware accelerators for developers and manufacturers.
1. A developer tools project that builds an open-source ML compiler framework and runtime, distributed as free open-source software.
2. An end-to-end deep learning compiler stack that provides a unified abstraction across processors and includes a microcontroller runtime extension.
3. Hardware-agnostic model optimization, cross-platform compilation, and low-latency local inference across x86, ARM, and specialized accelerator architectures.
4. Open-source software framework and runtime stack.
5. Robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, industrial automation, and microcontroller-class edge devices.
6. Developers and original equipment manufacturers building robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, and industrial automation systems.
7. Its compiler infrastructure is integrated by developers and manufacturers to bridge AI frameworks with diverse hardware accelerators in their devices.
8. A hardware-agnostic approach enables flexible, cross-platform compilation across diverse architectures, unlike vendor-specific solutions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Woven Planet adopts the framework as its core compiler infrastructure to unify inference across various processors, and it compiles models to run on RISC-V based hardware.
Organization type: An open-source project managed under the Apache Software Foundation.
Business model: Free open-source software maintained through community and industry contributions.
Scale and maturity: An established, widely recognized framework within the artificial intelligence infrastructure landscape.
Geography: Global reach through its open-source nature allowing a worldwide community of developers to utilize and contribute.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is the entire focus of the project, as its core technology exists specifically to solve the computational bottlenecks of local inference in physical systems.

points.name: PrismML
points.description: California startup shrinking large language models to run on smartphones and laptops.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds fully binarized 1-bit large language models designed to run on consumer edge devices and physical AI systems while maintaining performance at a fraction of the memory footprint of traditional models.
1. An AI model developer whose compressed large language models run on consumer devices and edge hardware.
2. A proprietary mathematical framework that quantizes neural network weights to single bits represented as +1 or -1 to compress transformer-based models.
3. On-device large language model inference with significantly reduced memory and energy consumption.
4. Compressed AI models running on customers' hardware.
5. Smartphones, laptops and PCs.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers and mobile developers.
7. Its compressed models are evaluated by device makers for integration into consumer hardware.
8. It uses a purely binarized, end-to-end compression approach that eliminates higher-precision escape hatches to achieve a dramatic increase in intelligence density.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by Khosla Ventures and Cerberus Capital Management, spun out from the California Institute of Technology, in talks with Apple, and compressing models from Alibaba and Google.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Model licensing and software subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup that emerged from stealth with a $16.25 million seed round.
Geography: Based in Silicon Valley, California, USA, targeting global consumer electronics markets.
Beyond physical AI: Enabling on-device AI inference and model compression constitutes its entire focus.

points.name: Google Research
points.description: Technology research division developing on-device machine learning systems and robotics algorithms for physical automation.
points.bullets:
A corporate research division that develops neural processing units, model optimization algorithms, and machine learning frameworks for edge AI and general artificial intelligence. It designs low-power inference silicon and open-source compiler infrastructure, providing hardware IP and software tools for semiconductor companies and developers.
1. A corporate research lab that designs edge NPUs and develops machine learning model frameworks and optimization algorithms.
2. RISC-V-based neural processing engines, ASIC inference accelerators, and compiler infrastructures built on MLIR.
3. On-device inference acceleration, large language model compression, and model compilation for diverse hardware targets.
4. Open-source IP architectures, software frameworks, compact language models, and NPU designs integrated into partner silicon.
5. Edge devices, developer boards, and on-device AI inference systems.
6. Semiconductor companies, software developers, and the scientific research community.
7. Its NPU designs and software frameworks are integrated into processors and development boards by silicon partners.
8. It develops open-source hardware IP and compiler infrastructure backed by the computational resources of a major technology conglomerate.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Synaptics and the University of Cambridge.
Organization type: Corporate research division of a publicly traded multinational technology conglomerate.
Business model: Funded internally by its parent company, providing open-source frameworks and hardware IP through collaborative partnerships.
Scale and maturity: A long-established, globally distributed research organization operating at massive scale.
Geography: Based in Mountain View, California, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: A comprehensive technology research powerhouse dedicated to advancing foundational computing, artificial intelligence, and software engineering.

points.name: MediaPipe
points.description: Google software framework providing optimized on-device models for real-time computer vision and perception tasks.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a software framework for on-device machine learning inference, providing pre-trained models and APIs for real-time vision, text, and audio intelligence on edge hardware.
1. A developer tools company whose cross-platform ML inference framework runs on other companies' edge devices.
2. Optimized machine learning pipelines and pre-trained perception models designed for low-latency execution on resource-constrained edge hardware.
3. On-device inference, real-time computer vision, text intelligence, and audio intelligence.
4. Software frameworks, APIs, and pre-trained models that run on customer hardware.
5. Manufacturing inspection systems, healthcare applications, and retail robotics.
6. Developers building cross-platform edge applications and industries requiring real-time visual perception.
7. Its framework is integrated by developers into edge devices and hardware accelerators.
8. Highly optimized, lightweight models specifically designed for low-latency, local visual processing without cloud dependencies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: General-purpose runtime environments including TensorFlow Lite and ONNX Runtime.
Organization type: Software framework owned and developed by a publicly traded technology conglomerate.
Business model: Open-source software framework.
Scale and maturity: A mature, established platform with widespread adoption across various commercial sectors.
Geography: Developed by a global technology conglomerate and supports edge devices worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: It is part of a vast, global technology conglomerate that offers a wide array of internet services, software, and hardware products.

points.name: ONNX Runtime
points.description: Open-source framework accelerating AI model execution across diverse edge hardware.
points.bullets:
A developer tools project that builds an open-source cross-platform inference engine for executing AI models on edge hardware, enabling on-device deployment for developers and enterprises.
1. A developer tools project that builds an open-source inference engine for executing models on edge hardware, released as open-source software.
2. A cross-platform inference engine with hardware execution providers that accelerates model execution across diverse hardware architectures and operating systems.
3. On-device inference, cross-platform model deployment and hardware acceleration for resource-constrained edge devices.
4. Open-source software that developers integrate into their applications and edge deployment pipelines.
5. Robotics, industrial automation, autonomous vehicles and smart surveillance.
6. Developers and enterprises needing to deploy real-time on-device inference across heterogeneous edge devices.
7. Its inference engine is integrated by developers into edge AI solutions running on hardware from chipmakers.
8. A hardware-agnostic interface provides cross-platform flexibility and framework interoperability for a train-once, deploy-anywhere approach.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is integrated by an AI platform company in its transformers libraries and by a GPU maker in builds for its edge devices.
Organization type: An open-source project.
Business model: Open-source software.
Scale and maturity: An established open-source project with wide adoption as a core component of the edge AI software ecosystem.
Geography: It operates globally within the broader technology ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Providing the open-source inference engine constitutes the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: tinyML
points.description: Global research community developing tools to run machine learning on low-power microcontrollers.
points.bullets:
An open research and engineering community focused on enabling machine learning on resource-constrained microcontroller devices, providing the software frameworks and tools to deploy models on low-power embedded systems.
1. A developer tools and platform community that builds software frameworks and deployment tools for machine learning on microcontrollers.
2. Software frameworks and algorithms optimized to run machine learning inference within the kilobytes of memory available on low-power embedded microcontroller processors.
3. On-device inference for intelligent IoT applications across vision, voice, and vibration domains.
4. Open-source software frameworks and development resources used by embedded engineers.
5. Intelligent IoT devices, low-cost low-power robots, warehouse robots, manufacturing equipment, and service robots.
6. Embedded software developers, hardware engineers, and researchers across manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, and autonomous vehicle industries.
7. Its software frameworks are used by embedded developers to deploy inference models onto microcontrollers manufactured by silicon providers.
8. It brings autonomous decision-making to devices with only kilobytes of memory, reducing processing latency to single-digit milliseconds while maintaining strict data privacy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with hardware leaders including Arm and Google.
Organization type: An open research and engineering community rather than a traditional commercial corporation or government agency.
Business model: Funded through community collaboration and industry partnerships to advance open embedded machine learning technology.
Scale and maturity: An established global network of researchers and industry engineers with a vast ecosystem including major hardware partners and thousands of affiliated developers.
Geography: Operates globally, supporting embedded deployments in diverse environments from localized manufacturing sites to remote industrial operations.
Beyond physical AI: Advancing machine learning capabilities for microcontrollers and resource-constrained embedded systems constitutes its entire focus and primary activity.

points.name: Arduino
points.description: Italian hardware platform enabling machine learning deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers and sensors.
points.bullets:
A microcontroller board and development platform maker that builds low-power hardware for edge AI and TinyML, supplying embedded inference boards, carrier boards, integrated development environments, and libraries to hobbyists, educators, and enterprise engineers.
1. A hardware company that designs and sells open-source microcontroller boards and single-board computers for on-device inference and embedded machine learning.
2. Low-power microcontrollers and dual-core processing boards, frequently embedding ARM-based cores and paired with onboard inertial and environmental sensors.
3. On-device inference for TinyML, sensor data capture, gesture detection, predictive maintenance, environmental monitoring, and control for physical actuation tasks.
4. Microcontroller boards, development boards, and enterprise hardware modules sold alongside the open-source integrated development environment.
5. Edge AI prototyping, embedded IoT devices, TinyML experiments, crop health analysis, mosquito breeding site detection, predictive maintenance, robotics, and actuation projects.
6. Hobbyists, educators, prototyping engineers, industrial IoT developers, and enterprise solution builders.
7. Its development boards are designed into custom electronics and physical AI prototypes by embedded device developers and makers.
8. It pairs open-source accessibility and low-cost hardware with a broad ecosystem of compatible machine learning tools and runtimes.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Qualcomm, Edge Impulse, TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, Qeexo AutoML, and LiteRT.
Organization type: A privately held company that is a subsidiary of a semiconductor company.
Business model: Hardware sales of development boards and modules.
Scale and maturity: A mature, globally recognized manufacturer with an established international footprint.
Geography: Based in Italy and operates internationally.
Beyond physical AI: It also provides the broader open-source electronics platform and integrated development environment for general IoT and digital device prototyping.

points.name: Nordic Semiconductor
points.description: Norwegian semiconductor company designing ultra-low-power wireless chips for battery-operated AI devices.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power wireless system-on-chips with integrated neural processing units and TinyML model support for battery-powered edge devices.
1. A chip company that designs low-power SoCs with integrated NPUs for on-device inference.
2. Ultra-low-power wireless SoCs combining Arm Cortex-M processors, 2.4 GHz multi-protocol transceivers, and an integrated neural processing unit running sub-5 KB machine learning models.
3. On-device inference for anomaly detection, activity recognition, and gesture recognition alongside Bluetooth Low Energy, Thread, and Zigbee wireless connectivity.
4. Chips, system-in-packages, and prototyping boards, accompanied by runtime libraries and automated machine learning developer tools.
5. IoT sensors, wearables, healthcare monitoring devices, industrial predictive maintenance systems, and smart home products.
6. Electronics manufacturers, embedded developers, and procurement teams building battery-operated connected devices.
7. Its chips and software are designed into connected sensors and wearables by original equipment manufacturers.
8. It prioritizes extreme power efficiency over raw computational speed, enabling long-duration deployments on battery-constrained devices through proprietary ultra-tiny models and integrated NPUs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its hardware powers the AkidaTag reference platform and it sponsors the Edge AI Technology Report.
Organization type: A publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip and module sales, supplemented by acquired software and device management platforms.
Scale and maturity: A mature global semiconductor manufacturer founded in 1983, executing strategic acquisitions to expand its artificial intelligence portfolio.
Geography: Based in Norway, maintaining a global operational footprint to serve international electronics manufacturers.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge artificial intelligence, the broader company profile encompasses the design and sale of general wireless connectivity hardware for consumer and industrial electronics.

points.name: OpenMV
points.description: US development platform building low-power microcontroller cameras for on-device machine vision.
points.bullets:
A hardware developer that builds low-power microcontroller camera boards for tinyML computer vision, giving developers, researchers, and hobbyists an easy way to run on-device image classification, object detection, and other vision workloads on embedded hardware.
1. A hardware developer that makes compact machine vision camera boards for building edge AI applications, sold with a companion IDE, firmware, and example projects.
2. Its cameras pair ARM Cortex-M and microcontroller-class processors with image sensors and removable, interchangeable lenses, running TensorFlow Lite models and traditional computer vision algorithms under a MicroPython-based runtime programmable in Python.
3. The boards deliver real-time on-device inference for TinyML image classification, object detection, and image categorization at very low power.
4. Customers get complete camera boards plus a free integrated development environment, documentation, firmware, and example projects for writing and deploying code.
5. Its cameras are used in robotics, drones, industrial automation, educational robotics competitions, and general embedded vision projects.
6. It sells to developers, researchers, hobbyists, and engineers building robotics and edge AI systems.
7. Its camera modules are bought as standard perception subsystems and integrated into robots, drones, and other deployed physical systems built by device makers.
8. Its platform stands out for accessibility, letting users run TensorFlow Lite models and classical computer vision algorithms together in a single Python script on microcontroller-class hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its modules integrate STMicroelectronics and NXP microcontrollers and image sensors, and it has partnered with AWS IoT Core, FLIR, and Prophesee; its co-founder has presented at the Embedded Vision Summit and Edge AI and Vision Alliance Forum.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: It makes money from hardware sales of its camera boards, supported by freely provided development software.
Scale and maturity: An established company with a flagship camera product line spanning multiple hardware iterations and successive board generations.
Geography: Based in the USA, serving a global developer community.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and machine vision are the company's entire focus, spanning both its hardware and software products.

points.name: MathWorks
points.description: US software company providing tools to design, simulate, and deploy AI models onto embedded and edge hardware.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company whose MATLAB and Simulink platforms support the entire tinyML and embedded AI workflow, from model development and simulation to code generation and deployment on physical devices. It builds engineering software used to design, simulate, validate, and deploy AI models and control systems onto embedded microcontrollers, GPUs, and hardware accelerators for engineers across multiple industries.
1. A developer tools company that builds mathematical computing, simulation, and code generation software sold as licensed engineering platforms.
2. A block diagram and high-level programming environment that supports deep learning, sensor fusion, and control system design, featuring automated code generation for embedded C/C++ and GPUs.
3. Edge and tinyML model optimization, system simulation, automated driving perception prototyping, and hardware deployment of AI and control models.
4. Licensed software tools, toolboxes, and support packages.
5. Autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, manufacturing, and embedded intelligence systems.
6. Engineers and scientists at industrial manufacturers, automotive makers, and embedded system developers.
7. Its tools are used by device makers and engineers to design and deploy software onto embedded hardware.
8. It bridges algorithm development and safety-critical deployment through integrated verification, validation, and automated code generation for diverse hardware targets.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with semiconductor companies, NVIDIA, and counts Mercedes-Benz and Coca-Cola among its users.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A mature, established company with a long-standing global presence and broad multinational deployments.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: It develops broader mathematical computing and model-based design software used widely across engineering and scientific disciplines.

points.name: Neuton.AI
points.description: US technology company building no-code machine learning tools that generate tiny AI models for deployment on resource-constrained devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides an automated, no-code TinyML platform generating ultra-compact neural network models for resource-constrained embedded microcontrollers and smart sensors.
1. A developer tools company whose automated machine learning platform outputs compiled C libraries for embedded microcontrollers.
2. A patented neural network framework that grows deep learning models neuron-by-neuron to achieve minimal memory footprints without manual hyperparameter tuning.
3. Automated generation of machine learning models under 5kB for on-device inference on 8, 16, and 32-bit MCUs.
4. A platform-as-a-service that provides compiled C libraries for direct embedding into microcontrollers or sensors.
5. Wearables, health monitoring, industrial predictive maintenance, smart home devices, and IoT sensor systems.
6. Developers and manufacturers requiring on-device intelligence on ultra-low-power hardware.
7. Its automated model generation tools are used by developers to deploy AI onto embedded microcontrollers and smart sensors.
8. Its patented framework produces models under 5KB that are up to 1,000 times smaller than comparable TensorFlow Lite models while maintaining accuracy and running significantly faster.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Part of Arm's AI ecosystem and acquired by Nordic Semiconductor.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Platform-as-a-service offered for free to developers, now integrated into its parent company's hardware ecosystem.
Scale and maturity: Serves a global user base of thousands of free-tier developers following its 2025 acquisition.
Geography: Based in the USA and operates within a global hardware and developer ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and physical automation are entirely central to its mission, as its sole purpose is to enable practical on-device processing where power and memory constraints prohibit traditional AI.

points.name: Silicon Labs
points.description: US semiconductor company manufacturing wireless microcontrollers with hardware acceleration for energy-efficient on-device machine learning.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power wireless microcontroller system-on-chips with integrated hardware acceleration for on-device machine learning inference, targeting resource-constrained Internet of Things devices. It supplies inference silicon, software development kits, and machine learning tools to embedded device developers, enabling TinyML applications like wake word detection, gesture recognition, and people counting at the edge.
1. A chip company that designs low-power microcontrollers and wireless SoCs with integrated NPUs for on-device inference.
2. The core technology centers on ultra-low-power microcontroller and wireless SoC architectures featuring a built-in Matrix Vector Processor for hardware-accelerated machine learning inferencing.
3. It delivers fast, low-power on-device inference for edge vision tasks such as image recognition, human pose detection, people counting, wake word detection, and gesture recognition.
4. Customers get it through packaged silicon chips, development kits, and software development kits integrated into a dedicated integrated development environment.
5. It is used in smart homes, industrial automation, healthcare, agriculture, logistics, and consumer wearables where low-latency, privacy-critical, or connectivity-limited on-device intelligence is required.
6. It sells to embedded device developers, IoT hardware manufacturers, and product engineers.
7. Its chips and software tools are designed into connected edge devices and wearables by hardware manufacturers.
8. Its Matrix Vector Processor hardware accelerator distinguishes its approach by enabling up to eight times faster inferencing at one-sixth the energy consumption of unaccelerated alternatives while bundling wireless connectivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with Edge Impulse, SensiML, Eta Compute, Micro.ai, Sparkfun, and Google.
Organization type: It is a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: It makes money through chip sales, development kit hardware, and software tool licensing.
Scale and maturity: It is a mature, globally deployed semiconductor vendor with commercially available silicon and an established network of third-party design service providers.
Geography: It is based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and on-device machine learning are central to its focus on democratizing intelligence for extremely low-power, resource-constrained connected devices.

points.name: Deeplite
points.description: AI software company shrinking large AI models to run efficiently on small battery-powered devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides automated optimization software to compress and quantize deep learning models for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
1. A software company that builds an AI model compression platform sold to chip designers and original equipment manufacturers.
2. Automated deep neural network compression and quantization software that reduces model size, increases inference speed, and lowers power consumption.
3. Model size reduction up to ten times, inference acceleration up to five times, and power consumption reduction for edge deployment.
4. Software platform and optimization tools licensed to semiconductor and hardware manufacturers.
5. Smartphones, drones, connected vehicles, smart infrastructure, and connected devices.
6. Original equipment manufacturers, chip designers, and semiconductor companies.
7. Its optimization software is used by hardware manufacturers to streamline AI model deployment on inference silicon.
8. It automates model compression to achieve up to ten times size reduction and five times speed increase without sacrificing accuracy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by STMicroelectronics, collaborated with AI researcher Yoshua Bengio, partnered with Arm and Andes Technology.
Organization type: Privately held startup acquired as a wholly owned subsidiary of a publicly traded semiconductor conglomerate.
Business model: Software licenses and platform subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: An early commercial stage startup with a small number of paying enterprise customers, acquired in April 2025.
Geography: Based in Montreal, Canada, serving global semiconductor and technology markets.
Beyond physical AI: The broader parent company is a leading microcontroller supplier, while this division provides the software counterpart for edge AI adoption.

points.name: Imagimob
points.description: Swedish AI software company building development tools for deploying machine learning on resource-constrained embedded devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company whose platform builds and deploys tinyML models for embedded devices, offering an end-to-end software suite and pre-trained models to engineers designing constrained hardware systems for automotive, manufacturing, healthcare and consumer markets.
1. A developer tools company that builds and sells a software platform for developing and deploying machine learning models on embedded devices.
2. Software tools for end-to-end edge AI development, model explainability and deployment optimized for microcontrollers with severe memory constraints.
3. Auditory event detection, voice control, predictive maintenance, gesture recognition and on-device inference on resource-constrained hardware.
4. Licensed software tools, pre-trained models and a hub for reference designs.
5. Smart home devices, wearables, automotive systems, manufacturing equipment, healthcare devices and industrial applications.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, automotive suppliers, industrial device makers and embedded systems developers.
7. Its software sits between microcontroller hardware and end-product developers, integrated into devices designed by hardware makers.
8. It enables machine learning on extremely resource-constrained hardware, allowing models to operate with as little as 3kB of RAM and 15kB of Flash memory.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Infineon Technologies, which acquired it in May 2023.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded semiconductor manufacturer.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions for its development platform and ready-made models.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2013 with established global market presence across consumer and industrial applications.
Geography: Based in Sweden and serves worldwide consumer and industrial markets as part of a global semiconductor parent.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is creating machine learning software tools and pre-trained models optimized for embedded edge devices.

points.name: Neurala
points.description: US technology company developing software frameworks for vision-language-action models in edge computing environments for robotics and physical automation.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops vision-language-action models and visual inspection software for edge devices, selling frameworks and application-specific implementations to manufacturers and robotics builders for on-device inference.
1. A developer tools and software company that builds AI frameworks and vision-language-action models for edge devices, sold as licensed software and platforms.
2. Vision-language-action models and TinyML software optimized for low-power semiconductors and resource-constrained edge hardware.
3. On-device inference, visual defect detection, and model optimization for real-time perception in industrial robotics.
4. Licensed software platforms and AI frameworks that run on customers' edge hardware and semiconductor chips.
5. Manufacturing environments, warehouse automation, industrial robotics, healthcare robotics, autonomous systems, and consumer robotics.
6. Manufacturers, semiconductor firms, robotics builders, and developers of physical automation systems.
7. Its software is integrated by semiconductor firms into their chips and by manufacturers into their inspection lines.
8. It develops application-specific vision-language-action implementations tailored for particular robotic embodiments rather than generic model compression.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Lattice Semiconductor.
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses, platform sales, and technology partnerships.
Scale and maturity: Based in the USA, operating across multiple global manufacturing and robotics application domains.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are the entire focus and primary business of this pure-play company.

points.name: Aizip
points.description: US technology company building efficient AI models for on-device inference across resource-constrained endpoint devices.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds tinyML models for vision, audio, and time-series inference on resource-constrained endpoint devices, serving semiconductor makers and system integrators across diverse industries.
1. An AI model developer whose TinyML models run on other companies' endpoint devices and silicon.
2. Small neural networks built using neural architecture search and quantization-aware training for low-power on-device inference.
3. On-device inference for vision, audio, time-series processing, and anomaly detection.
4. Models and automated design tools delivered as software to customers, and models integrated onto other companies' silicon.

Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on modernizing freight logistics through the development of autonomous, battery-electric rail systems.

points.name: Phiar
points.description: California automotive AI startup developing lightweight spatial perception software for on-device augmented reality navigation in vehicle dashboards.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds a spatial AI perception engine and an augmented reality navigation platform for automotive applications. The software performs on-device computer vision using a single camera to provide real-time road scene understanding and augmented guidance on standard automotive infotainment systems, targeting automakers and tier-one suppliers.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a spatial AI perception and AR navigation stack to automakers.
2. The core technology is an ultra-lightweight deep learning inference engine that processes monocular camera input for 3D localization and real-time perception without requiring custom silicon.
3. The software delivers on-device computer vision, spatial perception, road scene understanding and augmented reality navigation.
4. Customers get it as a licensed software stack integrated into existing automotive cockpit platforms.
5. The software is used in automotive infotainment systems and advanced driver assistance systems.
6. The company sells to automakers, automotive original equipment manufacturers and tier-one suppliers.
7. Its software is integrated by automotive suppliers and device makers into in-vehicle infotainment platforms.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by enabling real-time vehicle perception using a single camera rather than specialized hardware or complex sensor arrays.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company partnered with Qualcomm and Panasonic Automotive, and was acquired by Google.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The business model relies on software licenses and platform integration contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, the company operates with a small team of 2-10 employees and secured $12 million in Series A funding in September 2021.
Geography: The company is based in Redwood City, California, and operates primarily within the global automotive sector.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play software provider whose entire business is focused on spatial AI and augmented reality for automotive applications.

points.name: Asylon
points.description: Security company deploying autonomous ground and aerial robots for automated perimeter and critical infrastructure defense.
points.bullets:
A security services provider and systems integrator that builds and operates full-service robotic perimeter security solutions combining air and ground robots, automated patrols, and a remote monitoring center for enterprises and critical infrastructure.
1. A systems integrator and operator that buys and modifies mobile robots and drones, packages them with sensors and recharging hubs, and sells perimeter security as a managed service.
2. Autonomous ground robots, aerial drones, third-party sensor payloads, secure mesh communications, and a central command-and-control orchestration layer running remote monitoring software.
3. Automated perimeter patrols, threat detection and response, 24/7 remote monitoring, autonomous recharging, and fleet orchestration.
4. A robotic security service comprising integrated hardware and software, managed through a remote operations center with included maintenance and overnight replacements.
5. Warehouse perimeter security, critical infrastructure defense, event security, and enterprise facility monitoring.
6. Logistics operators, automotive manufacturers, critical infrastructure operators, and event organizers.
7. It buys robots from OEMs, modifies them, and operates them as a unified security service for end customers.
8. It integrates heterogeneous sensor payloads and operates effectively in GPS-denied and communication-constrained environments, supported by a 24/7 remote monitoring center.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Boston Dynamics and FedEx.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Managed security service contracts and systems integration.
Scale and maturity: It has completed over 140,000 security drone and robot missions.
Geography: It is based in the United States and operates domestically.
Beyond physical AI: Physical automation, edge AI, and robotics are the company's entire focus.

points.name: Ambi Robotics
points.description: AI robotics startup deploying autonomous robotic stacking and parcel sorting systems for warehouse logistics.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds AI-powered robotic systems for parcel sortation and palletizing in warehouses, combining physical machines with its own operating software and offering them to logistics operators under a robots-as-a-service model.
1. A robotics company that builds and sells parcel sortation, putwall and pallet-building robotic systems delivered as a managed service.
2. AI-powered robotic arm systems for parcel sorting and multipurpose stacking, controlled by a proprietary operating system and a perception platform for item-level intelligence.
3. Parcel sortation, pallet building, package reading, perception of messy variable environments, fleet performance monitoring across facilities and throughput, accuracy and uptime management.
4. Complete robotic systems including sortation, putwall and pallet-building machines, fleet analytics software and integration services, offered as robots-as-a-service.
5. Warehouses, e-commerce fulfillment centers and inbound logistics workflows.
6. Retail and logistics operators including e-commerce fulfillment centers.
7. It designs and builds its own robotic hardware and operating software, integrating its palletizing systems with other vendors' unloading robots to create automated inbound logistics workflows.
8. Its robotic systems are engineered for interoperability with other vendors' equipment to create end-to-end automated workflows without requiring facility redesigns.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A commercial integration with Pickle Robot links trailer-unloading robots to the company's pallet-building system, and it is a UC Berkeley spin-off.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Robots-as-a-service fees tied to throughput, accuracy and uptime KPIs that deliver cost reductions.
Scale and maturity: A pre-Series A startup with 55 employees operating in the United States.
Geography: Based in Silicon Valley, California, operating domestically within the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Developing physical AI for industrial automation is the company's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Chooch
points.description: AI company building computer vision platforms that enable on-device inference for real-time visual monitoring in physical operational environments.
points.bullets:
An AI platform company that builds and licenses computer vision software for real-time visual monitoring and automated decision-making on edge devices, serving enterprises across healthcare, manufacturing, safety, and defense.
1. An AI platform company that builds computer vision software for on-device inference and sells it as a licensed platform with pre-trained models.
2. Large vision models and computer vision models trained for real-time object detection, recognition, and analysis in video streams, managed through a low-code lifecycle platform.
3. Real-time visual perception, object and behavior recognition, inventory tracking, demand forecasting, and automated visual inspection.
4. Licensed software, pre-trained models, and a low-code platform that run on customers' existing cameras and edge compute hardware.
5. Hospital inventory management, workplace safety, manufacturing, physical security, wildfire detection, and geospatial analysis.
6. Hospitals, manufacturers, government and military agencies, and facility operators.
7. Its software is deployed on existing camera and edge compute infrastructure by enterprise customers and integrators.
8. It offers enterprise-focused, vertical-specific vision solutions with managed deployment across large distributed environments rather than developer-first tooling.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Deloitte, NVIDIA, Cisco, EY, Intel, Henry Schein, Vizient, Galliford Try, AWS, and Microsoft Azure.
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A mature technology venture with large-scale enterprise deployments and established partnerships with major hardware and cloud providers.
Geography: Based in the United States and serving enterprise customers across multiple sectors.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, computer vision, and physical automation are its entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Scythe
points.description: US robotics startup deploying autonomous commercial mowers for large-scale outdoor maintenance using edge AI computer vision.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous, electric commercial mowers for off-road environments, integrating custom hardware and autonomy software in-house to perform large-scale outdoor maintenance for the commercial landscaping industry.
1. A robotics company that designs and sells complete autonomous commercial-grade mowing machines.
2. All-electric robotic platforms running edge AI perception, combining multi-sensor fusion, machine learning-based vision, and high-precision RTK positioning for autonomous navigation.
3. Autonomous navigation, obstacle detection and avoidance, and off-road terrain traversal executing on-device inference without requiring site infrastructure.
4. Complete robots and robotic systems sold to commercial operators.
5. Outdoor ground maintenance, commercial landscaping, and unstructured off-road environments.
6. Commercial landscaping operators and property managers.
7. It designs and builds complete robots and sells them to commercial operators.
8. Hardware-software co-design enabling autonomous operation without infrastructure installation at customer sites.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by Inspired Capital, True Ventures, Zigg Capital, and Lemnos.
Organization type: Privately held startup, later acquired by a major industrial vehicle automation company.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete autonomous mowers.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018 with $18.6 million in funding, having maintained nearly 2 billion square feet of terrain across 30 states by 2025.
Geography: Based in Longmont, Colorado, operating primarily across the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and autonomous off-road automation represent the entirety of its mission, with plans to expand into related outdoor tasks like aeration and fertilizer application.

points.name: Cartken
points.description: US platform startup deploying camera-equipped autonomous robots for last-mile delivery and industrial material handling.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and sells autonomous mobile robots for last-mile delivery and industrial material handling, operating them under a robots-as-a-service model for delivery platforms, retailers, and industrial facilities.
1. A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile delivery and utility robots and sells them through robots-as-a-service and direct sales.
2. Camera-first visual navigation using six cameras and wheel odometry processed on NVIDIA Jetson edge AI modules to achieve Level 4 autonomy without lidar.
3. Level 4 autonomous sidewalk navigation, object detection, last-mile delivery, and indoor material transport.
4. Complete robots and fleet management software provided as robots-as-a-service or direct deployments.
5. Sidewalk last-mile delivery, university campuses, retail grocery delivery, factories, warehouses, and laboratories.
6. Food delivery platforms, grocery retailers, universities, and industrial facility operators.
7. It builds its own robots and fleet software, contracting a manufacturing partner to scale production, and operates them for end customers.
8. It achieves profitable autonomous delivery using a low-cost, camera-based perception system instead of lidar arrays.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Uber Eats, Grubhub, Kroger, Mitsubishi Electric, Magna International, NVIDIA, and the Robot Delivery Association.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Robots-as-a-service contracts and direct robot deployments.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019 with deployments across the U.S., Japan, Germany, and the U.K., scaling to mass production of thousands of robots.
Geography: Based in the United States with international operations in Japan, Germany, and the U.K.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the entirety of the organization's mission and business model.

points.name: Moon Surgical
points.description: Medical robotics startup developing an AI-powered surgical assistant platform for laparoscopic procedures.
points.bullets:
A medical robot maker that builds a laparoscopic surgical-assistant system combining two robotic arms, computer vision, and haptics on a single cart for operating rooms. It designs the complete robot and integrates edge AI hardware for on-device sensor processing, providing intraoperative AI capabilities and digital workflow analytics for surgeons and medical facilities.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells surgical-assistant robots for laparoscopic procedures.
2. A dual-arm robotic cart that holds a camera and standard surgical instruments, using edge AI computer vision and haptic feedback for real-time intraoperative assistance.
3. Surgeon-controlled robotic camera and instrument manipulation, AI-enhanced intraoperative scene understanding, and digital workflow data capture for operating room coordination.
4. Complete robotic systems cleared by the FDA and integrated into hospital operating rooms, alongside a digital data analytics platform.
5. Hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and operating rooms performing high-volume laparoscopic and gynecological procedures.
6. Surgeons, hospitals, and ambulatory surgery centers.
7. Its complete robotic systems are deployed directly into operating rooms by medical facilities for surgical assistance.
8. It keeps surgeons in direct control at the patient bedside using standard surgical instruments rather than a separate console-driven system.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA provides the Holoscan and Isaac for Healthcare platforms, Lux Capital holds a stake, and Sofinnova Partners is an investor.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Capital sales of surgical robotic systems, alongside digital platform software.
Scale and maturity: A clinical-stage enterprise that has received FDA clearances, completed first-in-human trials, and treated over 200 patients internationally as of early 2024.
Geography: Based in France and the USA, supporting clinical deployments across Europe and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Advancing surgical robotics and physical AI is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Olis Robotics
points.description: Software company providing edge-based AI monitoring and remote control systems for industrial robots.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds edge-based remote monitoring, diagnostics, and teleoperation software for industrial robotic workcells. It provides framework-agnostic applications and mobile diagnostic tools that use on-device AI agents to analyze video feeds and PLC logs, serving integrators and factory facilities seeking to reduce downtime.
1. A developer tools company whose edge-hosted monitoring and teleoperation software runs on industrial robots it does not manufacture.
2. Edge-hosted on-device AI agents that synchronize and analyze video feeds, PLC logs, and system events directly at the workcell.
3. Remote automation monitoring, real-time diagnostics, error recovery, teleoperation, and fault visibility.
4. Software applications, mobile apps, and edge-hosted products compatible with existing robotic systems.
5. Industrial robotic workcells and sortation systems in factories.
6. Industrial automation customers, smaller systems integrators, and large factory facilities.
7. Its software is installed onto industrial robots and PLCs built by major robot manufacturers.
8. An edge-first architecture keeps sensitive manufacturing data on-premises, enabling secure remote troubleshooting without complex IT infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: U.S. Navy, NASA, the i4.0 Accelerator, and major robot manufacturers.
Organization type: Privately held startup spun out of a university applied physics lab.
Business model: Software application sales and ongoing support services.
Scale and maturity: An emerging venture that recently unveiled a mobile diagnostic app and supports more than 50% of the global installed industrial robot market base.
Geography: Based in the Pacific Northwest and operates within the industrial automation sector.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play software platform business focused entirely on on-device diagnostic and remote control solutions for physical automation.

points.name: Falkonry
points.description: Edge AI startup analyzing time-series manufacturing data to predict equipment failures and reduce downtime.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a predictive operations and machine learning platform for analyzing time-series data to anticipate equipment failures for plant operators.
1. A developer tools company whose AI-based operational platform runs on industrial plant infrastructure.
2. Machine learning for analyzing time-series data to detect and act on events that could negatively impact operations.
3. Predictive operations that anticipate equipment failures to reduce costly downtime.
4. A cloud or on-premise software platform that plant operators use.
5. Manufacturing plants and industrial operations.
6. Plant operators and manufacturers.
7. Its platform is deployed by plant operators within their own facilities.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on predictive operations and machine learning for manufacturing.

points.name: DeepGate
points.description: Edge AI compiler startup translating AI models into optimized software for low-cost microcontrollers and smart devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds an edge AI compiler for deploying neural network models on microcontrollers and embedded AI accelerators. Its compiler turns quantized TensorFlow Lite models into optimized inference binaries with reduced RAM usage and faster execution, sold to developers building smart wearables, audio, vision, and industrial products.
1. A developer tools company whose edge AI compiler robotics and embedded developers use to deploy models on microcontrollers.
2. Neural network compilation that converts quantized TensorFlow Lite models into static inference binaries with hardware-aware kernel optimizations, replacing standard runtime interpreters.
3. On-device inference on microcontrollers and embedded AI accelerators with up to 3× less RAM usage and 45× faster execution while maintaining model accuracy.
4. Licensed compiler software and model optimization technology offered through a vendor-agnostic deployment workflow.
5. Smart wearables, audio devices, vision products, and industrial products running AI on small, low-cost embedded devices.
6. Embedded developers building AI features on microcontroller-based hardware across consumer and industrial products.
7. Its compiler replaces standard runtime interpreters and is used by device developers as the deployment layer between trained models and inference silicon.
8. Static binary compilation and hardware-aware kernel optimizations deliver lower RAM usage and faster inference than interpreted runtime approaches like TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers, as shown in MLPerf Tiny benchmarks against vendor toolchains on their own chips.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A member of the EDGE AI Foundation, with compiler performance validated and benchmarked on microcontrollers and AI toolchains from major semiconductor vendors.
Organization type: A privately held technology startup staffed by scientists and engineers with expertise in machine learning, compiler design, and embedded systems.
Business model: Software licenses for its compiler and model optimization technology.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage, commercially active startup that has released its core compiler at version 0.15.0 and benchmarks it against industry-standard toolchains.
Geography: Operates within a global edge AI ecosystem as a member of an international edge AI foundation.
Beyond physical AI: Building compiler software for on-device AI inference is the company's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Blaize
points.description: US AI chip startup designing low-power programmable processors for edge inference and physical AI deployment.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs low-power, inference-optimized SoCs and embedded accelerator modules for visual AI at the edge, along with the software development kits to program them. It builds graph-streaming processor architecture hardware for system integrators and enterprises deploying smart vision and sensor-fusion applications in power-constrained environments.
1. A chip company that designs programmable AI inference accelerators and system-on-modules for on-device edge computing.
2. Graph-streaming processor architecture in low-power SoCs, using 16-core application processors with integrated RISC-V CPUs to achieve 16-TOPS INT8 performance at 7W.
3. On-device visual AI inference, multi-stream real-time object detection, and sensor fusion processing.
4. Chips, system-on-modules, and embedded AI edge platforms, sold alongside a graph-native software development kit and a code-free visual programming platform.
5. Industrial mobility platforms, patrol vehicles, unmanned systems, smart retail, and field operations.
6. System integrators, rugged computing platform manufacturers, and enterprises in industrial automation and smart cities.
7. Its inference silicon is designed into rugged embedded platforms by industrial system manufacturers.
8. Its graph-streaming processor architecture reduces memory bandwidth consumption by fifty times and lowers latency compared to legacy GPU solutions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its silicon is integrated into rugged platforms by Winmate and paired with lidar sensors from LeiShen, with backing from investors including DENSO, Daimler, Magna, Samsung Catalyst Fund and Temasek.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Chip and hardware module sales, alongside associated software development tools.
Scale and maturity: A late-stage startup that has raised around $155 million in equity funding and has its silicon selected for top-tier industrial integrations.
Geography: Based in the United States with a strong strategic presence and operational focus in the Asia-Pacific market.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical artificial intelligence represent the entire focus of this pure-play semiconductor and software provider.

points.name: SRI International
points.description: Nonprofit research institute developing power-efficient edge inference software and autonomous physical systems for defense and industrial applications.
points.bullets:
An independent nonprofit research institute that develops foundational physical AI technologies, including teleoperation systems, novel actuators, and neuromorphic edge inference software, for government agencies and commercial partners. It acts as an advanced research provider and intellectual property licensor rather than a high-volume manufacturer, creating complete deployed systems for robotic surgery, space exploration, and industrial collaboration.
1. A research institute that develops robotic actuators, teleoperation systems, and neuromorphic edge inference software, licensed to commercial spinouts and government clients.
2. Biomimetic computing frameworks utilizing hyperdimensional computing and saccadic selective attention, novel mechanical actuator drives, and teleoperation control systems for generating AI training data.
3. Power-efficient on-device inference, teleoperated robotic manipulation, and secure memory protection for autonomous systems.
4. Licensed technologies, intellectual property, and contracted research services provided to commercial spinouts and government agencies.
5. Bomb disposal robots, cleanroom automation, robotic surgery platforms, and autonomous vehicle deployments.
6. Government agencies, defense forces, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and commercial robotics spinouts.
7. Its technologies are licensed to spinouts and integrated into commercial robotic platforms by medical and defense device makers.
8. It leverages biomimetic computing approaches to achieve 100 to 1,000 times greater efficiency than standard edge AI configurations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The University of Cambridge, DARPA, IARPA, Ethicon, and its commercial spinout Autonomique.
Organization type: An independent nonprofit research institute established in 1946.
Business model: Government research contracts, commercial research partnerships, and technology licensing fees.
Scale and maturity: An institution founded over 80 years ago with a long-standing legacy in artificial intelligence research and a broad portfolio of deployed physical systems.
Geography: Based in Menlo Park, California, operating across diverse physical environments for government and commercial clients.
Beyond physical AI: The institute solves complex problems across technical disciplines, advancing quantum sensors, semantic forensics, and broad scientific research alongside its physical AI work.

points.name: Tencent
points.description: Chinese technology company operating large-scale AI compute clusters and providing infrastructure for the broader edge and physical AI ecosystem.
points.bullets:
A technology conglomerate that develops on-device and embodied AI models, builds cloud and training infrastructure, and acts as a strategic investor in robotics and autonomous vehicle startups.
1. An AI model developer and cloud infrastructure provider that builds foundation models, on-device language models, and simulation platforms, alongside operating as a venture investor.
2. Mixture-of-experts vision-language-action models, ultra-low precision 1.25-bit quantization for on-device deployment, and multi-agent reinforcement learning frameworks.
3. On-device multilingual translation, robotic perception and manipulation, embodied agent reasoning, and scalable model compression for edge inference.
4. Cloud APIs, open-sourced models, simulation toolkits, and venture capital funding.
5. Humanoid robots, mobile manipulation, industrial edge settings, and consumer mobile devices.
6. Robot makers, autonomous vehicle developers, mobile phone users, and AI developers.
7. Its models are integrated by humanoid makers into their robots, its cloud infrastructure is used by developers, and its capital funds robotics OEMs.
8. It pairs extreme model compression for edge deployment with direct capital deployment into physical AI hardware makers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: XPENG, Pony.ai, Unitree Robotics, UBTECH Robotics, Leju Robotics, Toyota, Apple, OpenRouter.
Organization type: Publicly traded technology conglomerate.
Business model: Cloud computing fees, API and software subscriptions, and venture capital returns.
Scale and maturity: A massive, mature technology conglomerate operating large-scale training clusters.
Geography: Based in China, operating its computational and AI initiatives primarily within the domestic market.
Beyond physical AI: It operates social media, gaming, and fintech services.

points.name: SK Telecom
points.description: Seoul telecommunications company building AI-native networks that distribute computation across edge infrastructure to support physical AI applications.
points.bullets:
A telecommunications operator that orchestrates a national physical AI and robotics ecosystem, combining its AI cloud, data centers, digital twins, and foundation models with startup technologies to commercialize industrial robotics.
1. A telecommunications operator and ecosystem orchestrator that builds AI cloud infrastructure and foundation models, partners with robotics startups, and co-develops robots for industrial applications.
2. The core technology comprises gigawatt-scale AI cloud infrastructure built with GPUs and AI accelerators, AI-RAN wireless networks, digital twin environments replicating industrial sites, and foundation models trained with NVIDIA microservices.
3. It delivers full-stack AI inference infrastructure, digital twin generation for robot learning data, AI-RAN edge orchestration, and foundation models for AI agents.
4. It provides AI cloud services, digital twin platforms, foundation models via APIs, and co-developed complete robots through partnerships.
5. Its technologies are used in semiconductor fabs, manufacturing facilities, logistics operations, retail store operations, and autonomous mobility infrastructure.
6. It sells to industrial manufacturers, semiconductor fabs, retail operators, government agencies, and physical AI startups.
7. It integrates AI cloud and digital twin capabilities with robots and software built by partner startups, deploying the combined solutions into industrial sites.
8. It is differentiated by its vertical integration across the physical AI value chain, combining sovereign telecommunications infrastructure, dedicated AI cloud factories, and proprietary foundation models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with NVIDIA, Ericsson, SK hynix, Doosan Robotics, Gauss Labs, MakinaRocks, CMES Robotics, WIRobotics, Yuil Robotics, Config Intelligence, Holiday Robotics, and RLWRLD.
Organization type: A publicly traded telecommunications company and subsidiary of a major conglomerate.
Business model: It makes money through telecommunications services, AI cloud computing contracts, government infrastructure projects, and joint commercial robotics deployments.
Scale and maturity: It is a major national mobile operator executing large-scale, multi-year demonstration projects with gigawatt-scale AI cloud deployments planned through 2027.
Geography: It is based in Seoul, South Korea, and operates its national initiatives and smart manufacturing deployments locally while extending AI cloud services across Greater Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, it operates a massive traditional mobile telecommunications business that underpins its broader technology and infrastructure initiatives.

points.name: Grinn
points.description: Polish IoT company building voice-controlled robotic arms with integrated camera safety zones.
points.bullets:
An IoT product company that designs and builds edge AI-powered robotic control systems and application-ready System-on-Modules integrating compute, connectivity, and sensor processing for on-device inference.
1. A developer tools and component supplier company that builds application-ready System-on-Modules and single-board computers incorporating edge AI platforms.
2. System-on-Modules and single-board computers integrating neural processing units for on-device inference, sensor processing, and physical actuator control.
3. On-device inference, voice-based robotic arm and gripper control, and low-latency physical automation.
4. The organization provides its technology as application-ready System-on-Modules and integrated control systems for consumer and industrial deployments.
5. The systems are used in robotic arms, grippers, collaborative robotics, and warehouse automation.
6. The company primarily serves the industrial and consumer robotics sectors and industrial automation developers.
7. Its System-on-Modules and control systems are integrated by robotics developers into their physical automation machines.
8. It combines perception, processing, and physical actuation into context-aware systems such as robotic arms with integrated safety zones powered by voice commands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with Synaptics and ENERZAi.
Organization type: It is a privately held IoT product company.
Business model: It makes money by selling hardware products, System-on-Modules, and integrated control systems.
Scale and maturity: It is an established market participant that demonstrates integrated hardware solutions at major industry events.
Geography: It is based in Poland and focuses on the broader industrial robotics and automation ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the core mission and entire business focus of the organization.

points.name: Houmo.AI
points.description: Chinese semiconductor startup designing energy-efficient edge AI inference chips that process data directly within memory.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs compute-in-memory inference accelerators for on-device large language model execution, selling silicon and compiler toolchains to consumer electronics, telecommunications, and robotics device makers.
1. A semiconductor company that designs compute-in-memory inference processing units for on-device AI, sold as chips and licensed intellectual property.
2. Compute-in-memory architecture neural processing units that execute floating-point matrix operations directly within memory cells to eliminate von Neumann data-shuttling bottlenecks.
3. Low-power, low-latency on-device inference for large language models with up to seventy billion parameters entirely offline.
4. Chips and proprietary compiler toolchains compatible with mainstream deep learning frameworks.
5. Personal computers, tablets, smart voice systems, telecommunication edge networks, and robots.
6. Telecommunications operators, consumer electronics manufacturers, and speech recognition system providers.
7. Its chips are designed into personal computers and smart devices by hardware manufacturers and deployed in telecommunication edge computing networks.
8. A compute-in-memory architecture that runs floating-point models natively within memory cells to overcome the energy and bandwidth limits of conventional processors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: China Mobile is an investor and client, Lenovo uses its chips in AI-powered PCs, iFlyrec uses them in smart voice systems, and Zhipu AI language models run on its hardware.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Chip sales and licensed intellectual property.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2021, it has reached early commercialization with marquee customers and strategic investors.
Geography: Based in China, operating within the domestic and global edge AI chip markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI inference silicon is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: China Mobile
points.description: Chinese telecommunications company deploying service robots in retail stores and advancing network infrastructure for physical AI.
points.bullets:
A telecommunications operator and venture investor that deploys physical AI robots in its own service centers, funds robot and AI silicon makers, and converts its nationwide offline network infrastructure into data collection centers for embodied AI.
1. A telecommunications operator and corporate venture investor that runs robots in its own facilities and invests in robotics, AI model, and silicon companies.
