2. Large-scale physical robot deployment across retail service centers and the operation of distributed physical data collection networks for embodied AI.
3. Telecommunications network infrastructure, corporate venture capital investment, and robots it operates itself in its own facilities.
4. Robot service centers, offline telecommunications networks, and data collection centers for embodied intelligence.
5. Robotics and AI ecosystem companies that receive its investment, partnership, and network infrastructure.
6. It buys robots from OEMs and operates them in its own service centers, while investing capital into robotics, silicon, and AI model developers.
7. It leverages its nationwide telecommunications footprint to transform offline network locations into large-scale data collection centers for embodied intelligence.
points.profile:
Organization type: A state-owned telecommunications operator and corporate venture investor.
Business model: Telecommunications services, corporate venture capital, and network infrastructure partnerships.
Scale and maturity: A major nationwide telecommunications operator that deployed robots across 22 cities and holds equity stakes in multiple robotics and AI companies.
Geography: Based in China, operating a nationwide telecommunications and service network.
Beyond physical AI: A major telecommunications company providing nationwide mobile and broadband network infrastructure.

points.name: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
points.description: Chinese government agency setting national policies for humanoid robot and edge AI development.
aliases: China Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT)
China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT)
Chinese Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT)
points.bullets:
A government agency that regulates, plans and funds China's edge and physical AI ecosystem, issuing technical standards, deployment mandates and industrial policy for humanoid robots, autonomous vehicles and semiconductor architectures. It sets national targets for mass production and commercial adoption of embodied intelligence, and establishes safety requirements for self-driving systems. Rather than building hardware or software, it shapes the market through guidelines, standardization committees and state mandates.
1. A government agency that establishes national standards, deployment quotas and innovation frameworks for robotics, autonomous vehicles and edge silicon.
2. Government policy instruments including technical standardization frameworks, five-year industrial plans, safety requirements for SAE Level 3 and Level 4 autonomous driving systems, and mass-production targets for humanoid robots.
3. Market creation through regulation, industrial planning, standard-setting, mandated commercial deployment quotas and national supply chain coordination.
4. Published government guidelines, proposed safety standards, mandated deployment targets and national industrial plans.
5. Humanoid robots, autonomous vehicles, electric vehicles, commercial fleets, manufacturing and broader physical AI industries.
6. Domestic robot makers, automakers, state-owned enterprises, local governments, chipmakers and sensor manufacturers subject to its regulations and targets.
7. Its standards and mandates flow down to robot makers, automakers and component suppliers that must comply with its technical requirements and deployment quotas.
8. It combines centralized regulatory authority with direct deployment mandates, requiring state-owned enterprises and local governments to deploy specific quantities of physical AI machines.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Works jointly with the state-owned asset supervisor to mandate humanoid robot deployment and coordinates with UN regulatory bodies on autonomous driving standards.
Organization type: A government ministry responsible for industrial and information technology policy.
Business model: State allocation of subsidies, regulatory mandates and industrial planning funded by government budgets.
Scale and maturity: A national-level ministry governing an industrial robotics sector that includes over 140 humanoid robot manufacturers and more than 330 product models, with targets for deploying over 10,000 humanoid robots by 2026.
Geography: Based in China, with policies and standards applied across the nation's domestic industrial ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, the organization governs the country's entire industrial and information technology sectors, including digital transformation, IoT adoption and semiconductor architecture policy.

points.name: Google AI Edge
points.description: US product division providing runtimes and on-device models for mobile and embedded machine learning inference.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that provides an integrated software stack for deploying on-device machine learning models and small language models onto mobile, web, and embedded devices. It builds runtimes, compression tools, and visualization software that abstract hardware-specific complexities for developers, enabling AI inference across CPUs, GPUs, and neural processing units.
1. A developer tools company whose on-device AI deployment platform and runtimes are used by mobile and embedded software engineers.
2. The core technology is a cross-platform machine learning inference runtime, complemented by model compression, quantization, and performance visualization tools, optimized through micro-kernels that utilize hardware acceleration architectures.
3. The platform delivers on-device inference, model optimization, automatic hardware acceleration, and deployment of small language, multimodal, and audio generation models.
4. Customers get it through open-source libraries, software development kits, and model hosting on developer platforms.
5. The tools are used in mobile applications, industrial IoT, smart manufacturing, and AI-enhanced consumer electronics.
6. The organization sells to software developers, machine learning engineers, and consumer electronics manufacturers.
7. Its software stack is integrated by application developers into their mobile and embedded products.
8. The approach is distinguished by unified application programming interface abstraction across vendor neural processing unit SDKs and cross-platform support spanning Android, iOS, web browsers, and embedded hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The platform integrates with Arm architecture and is hosted on the Hugging Face platform.
Organization type: A product division within a publicly traded technology conglomerate.
Business model: The division makes money through parent-company ecosystem support, driving adoption of cloud and hardware products.
Scale and maturity: The core runtime framework powers over 100,000 applications serving billions of global users.
Geography: It is based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the broader parent organization operates search engines, cloud computing, mobile operating systems, and consumer hardware.

points.name: OCP SAFE
points.description: Industry standards initiative developing security frameworks for edge computing and AI hardware deployments.
points.bullets:
A standards body that develops security frameworks and software update protocols for edge AI processors and peripherals used in physical automation systems.
1. A standards body that publishes security specifications for edge AI processors and peripherals.
2. Security specifications and frameworks that establish runtime protections and updatable software mechanisms for inference silicon, sensors, and deployed robotic systems.
3. Device-level security and secure software update protocols for distributed on-device intelligence.
4. Open standards and security frameworks adopted by industrial computing manufacturers.
5. Manufacturing, transportation, healthcare, and critical infrastructure settings.
6. Industrial computing, robotics, autonomous vehicle, healthcare, and critical infrastructure sectors.
7. Its standards are implemented by makers of processors and peripherals into their edge AI hardware.
8. It shifts the security burden to hardware makers by assigning responsibility for updatable software to processor and peripheral manufacturers.
points.profile:
Organization type: A standards initiative and collaborative industry body.
Scale and maturity: An established collaborative initiative operating across the global edge AI ecosystem.
Geography: Based and operating worldwide across global edge AI deployments.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI security standards represent the organization's entire focus.

points.name: MLC LLM
points.description: Open-source software framework optimizing large language models to run efficiently on diverse edge hardware.
points.bullets:
A developer tools organization that provides an open-source machine learning compilation framework for deploying large language models across diverse hardware backends for on-device inference. It operates in the inference runtime and compiler layer, bridging foundational models and the specialized silicon used in edge devices. The framework primarily serves software developers, AI engineers, and researchers who need to deploy generative AI models efficiently onto local hardware and consumer devices.
1. A developer tools organization whose open-source machine learning compilation framework for on-device language model inference software developers and AI engineers use.
2. An open-source machine learning compiler and inference runtime that optimizes large language models to run natively across heterogeneous edge computing hardware.
3. On-device language model inference, hardware backend optimization, and local execution of generative AI models without relying on cloud infrastructure.
4. An open-source software framework distributed to developers.
5. Edge devices, consumer devices, local hardware, and autonomous robots requiring efficient native processing.
6. Software developers, AI engineers, and researchers.
7. Its inference runtime and compiler layer are integrated by software developers into edge device software stacks.
8. A universal compilation approach allows developers to deploy models across a wide variety of unsupported or unconventional hardware platforms without waiting for proprietary vendor optimization.
points.profile:
Organization type: An open-source project maintained by a broader academic and industry research community and hosted within a major university computer science laboratory.
Geography: The core development team is based in the United States, and the open-source project sustains a highly distributed network of global contributors and users.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is on advancing machine learning compilation, democratizing access to artificial intelligence, and optimizing model deployment across heterogeneous computing environments.

points.name: Sensory
points.description: Technology company developing on-device AI software for voice, vision, and biometric applications on resource-constrained devices.
points.bullets:
A software company that develops on-device AI software for voice, vision, and biometric applications on resource-constrained edge devices, providing embedded inference software deployable across third-party silicon and complemented by a hybrid cloud infrastructure for consumer electronics and automotive manufacturers.
1. An AI software developer that builds compact voice and vision models and wake word technologies, sold as embedded software libraries and cloud platforms to device makers.
2. Small language models, wake word detection algorithms, and natural language understanding software optimized to run on low-power microcontrollers and edge processors.
3. On-device speech recognition, natural language understanding, computer vision, sound identification, biometric security, and low-power wake word detection.
4. Embedded software licensed to device makers and a hybrid cloud platform that allows customers to deploy custom models.
5. Mobile phones, refrigerators, remote controls, wearables, automotive cockpits, and smart home devices.
6. Consumer electronics manufacturers, automotive companies, and wearable makers.
7. Its software is integrated into the hardware products of consumer electronics and automotive device makers.
8. It differentiates through decades of specialized expertise in low-power, on-device AI inference and a hybrid computing approach that balances local edge processing with selective cloud connectivity for privacy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses tools from NVIDIA and partners with Alif Semiconductor, and its technology is used by LG and Samsung.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses, cloud platform services, and embedded technology licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1994, it is an established provider with technologies shipped in over two billion devices worldwide.
Geography: It is based in Silicon Valley and operates on a global scale across international consumer electronics and IoT markets.
Beyond physical AI: As a pure-play software company, its entire focus is dedicated to delivering practical, deployable on-device intelligence for interactive consumer and enterprise devices.

points.name: LeddarTech
points.description: Technology company developing sensor fusion software that helps autonomous vehicles understand their surroundings.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker and perception software developer that builds automotive-grade solid-state lidar and sensor-fusion platforms for advanced driver-assistance systems and autonomous vehicles. It supplies modular lidar development solutions and middleware that fuses raw data from lidar, radar, and cameras to generate 3D environmental models for automakers and system integrators. Its offerings enable on-device decision-making for Level 1 through Level 5 autonomous driving applications.
1. A sensor maker that builds solid-state lidar sensors and sensor-fusion perception software, sold as hardware components and licensed software platforms.
2. Solid-state flash lidar utilizing proprietary integrated circuits combined with various light sources, alongside sensor-agnostic perception software that fuses multi-modal raw data into 3D environmental models.
3. 3D perception, multi-sensor integration, and low-cost environmental sensing for autonomous navigation and obstacle detection.
4. Lidar components, complete sensor modules, and licensed perception software stacks sold to automotive system integrators and original equipment manufacturers.
5. Autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, robotaxis, autonomous shuttles, commercial trucks, and smart city infrastructure.
6. Tier 1 and Tier 2 automotive system integrators and original equipment manufacturers developing passenger and commercial vehicles.
7. Its lidar components and perception software are integrated into modular sensing systems by automotive suppliers and vehicle manufacturers.
8. Its sensor-agnostic perception software allows rapid integration and cost optimization across multiple hardware types, distinguishing it from hardware-bound sensor suppliers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its ecosystem includes simulation software developer Cognata, perception software company Seoul Robotics, and lighting and photonics company Osram as an investor.
Organization type: A privately held company spun out of the National Optics Institute.
Business model: Hardware component sales, software licenses, and modular lidar development solutions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2007, the company holds over 95 patented technologies and has secured over $101 million in Series C funding.
Geography: Based in Canada, it operates globally with sensor and software solutions deployed in autonomous mobility and industrial environments worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play provider of autonomous driving technology focused entirely on automotive perception software, lidar sensing hardware, and virtual simulation platforms.

points.name: Innoviz
points.description: Israeli LiDAR startup manufacturing automotive-grade sensors and perception software for autonomous vehicles.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops automotive-grade LiDAR sensors and complementary perception software for autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, and smart infrastructure, selling to automakers and industrial developers.
1. A sensor maker that builds LiDAR sensors and perception software, sold as hardware components and licensed software to automakers and machine builders.
2. MEMS-based solid-state LiDAR hardware combined with perception software that runs on edge AI processing modules.
3. High-resolution 3D perception, long-range and short-range object detection, and real-time tracking for autonomous navigation.
4. LiDAR sensors, edge devices, and perception software sold to automakers and industrial developers for integration into their vehicles and machines.
5. Autonomous passenger vehicles, autonomous commercial trucks, aerial robotics, security systems, and smart infrastructure.
6. Automakers, commercial vehicle manufacturers, industrial robotics developers, and smart-city operators.
7. Its sensors and software are designed into autonomous vehicles and robotic systems by automotive and industrial manufacturers.
8. It combines hardware and software co-design with a Tier-1 direct supplier model targeting low-cost, high-performance solid-state LiDAR.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its partners and customers include BMW, Volkswagen, Daimler Truck, Torc Robotics, NVIDIA, Samsung Catalyst, SoftBank Ventures Korea, Magna, and Jabil.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sensor sales and software licensing to automotive and industrial customers.
Scale and maturity: A globally operating Tier-1 supplier with a multi-billion-dollar deal with a major automaker and series production contracts for autonomous commercial trucks starting in 2025.
Geography: Based in Tel Aviv, Israel, operating across the United States, Europe, and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI and physical automation represent the company's entire business focus, centered on LiDAR-based perception technology for autonomous systems.

points.name: Ouster
points.description: US hardware manufacturer producing digital LiDAR sensors that give autonomous systems real-time environmental awareness.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that designs and manufactures digital lidar sensors, industrial stereo cameras, edge AI compute modules, and perception software for autonomous systems. The organization builds hardware components that enable 3D perception and on-device inference for robotics, automotive, and industrial automation applications, selling sensors and software to machine makers and autonomy developers.
1. A sensor maker that builds digital lidar sensors, stereo cameras, and perception software, sold as hardware components and licensed software to robot makers, automakers, and autonomy developers.
2. Digital lidar architecture using single photon avalanche diode detectors on custom CMOS chips, multi-beam flash lidar, and SPAD-based sensors that combine depth and color imagery.
3. High-resolution 3D point cloud generation, native color lidar sensing, sensor fusion, and real-time 3D perception for navigation and collision avoidance in unstructured environments.
4. Digital lidar sensors, stereo cameras, edge AI compute modules, and perception software delivered as hardware components and software licenses.
5. Autonomous vehicles, robotaxis, humanoids, quadruped robots, drones, industrial mobile robots, autonomous yard trucks, mining equipment, and smart infrastructure systems.
6. Automakers, robotaxi operators, robot makers, industrial automation developers, logistics operators, mining equipment manufacturers, defense contractors, and government agencies.
7. Its sensors and compute modules are designed into autonomous machines and infrastructure systems by vehicle makers, robot builders, and integrators.
8. Its digital lidar architecture uses single-chip CMOS with SPAD detectors to combine depth and color imagery in a single sensor while scaling production at lower cost than legacy analog designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners include NVIDIA, Honeywell, Komatsu, Forterra, Serve Robotics, FieldAI, AIM, Constellis, Benchmark Electronics, Fujifilm, DXOMARK, and Stereolabs.
Organization type: A publicly traded company listed on NASDAQ.
Business model: Hardware sensor sales, software licenses, and multimillion-dollar supply agreements with industrial and automotive customers.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, it generated $169 million in revenue in 2025 and has grown through acquisitions including Velodyne and Stereolabs.
Geography: Headquartered in San Francisco, California, with manufacturing in San Jose and Thailand, and customers across North America, Europe, and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI sensing and perception represent the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Trimble
points.description: Technology company supplying high-precision positioning systems and integrated autonomy solutions for field robotics and agricultural vehicles.
points.bullets:
A technology company that provides high-precision GNSS receivers, laser scanners, and autonomy software for field robotics and physical automation. It builds the positioning hardware and agentic AI platforms that original equipment manufacturers and system integrators use to enable autonomous machines in heavy industries.
1. A component and software supplier that makes GNSS receivers, antennas, and 3D laser scanners, sold alongside licensed autonomy and agentic AI software.
2. Centimeter-level GNSS positioning hardware, high-speed 3D laser scanning, and agentic AI software for physical construction workflows.
3. High-precision positioning, 3D reality capture, georeferencing, and autonomous decision-making for field robotics.
4. Components, sensors, and licensed software provided to OEMs and system integrators.
5. Construction, agriculture, transportation, geospatial mapping, and field robotics.
6. Robot makers, automakers, system integrators, construction contractors, and logistics operators.
7. Its sensors and software are integrated into robotic platforms and field workflows by original equipment manufacturers and service providers.
8. It combines precise geospatial positioning hardware with industry-specific agentic AI to connect the physical and digital worlds for heavy industries.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with Microsoft and Boston Dynamics.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales and software subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A large enterprise with 11,500 employees and $2.4 billion in annual recurring revenue.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: The company is fundamentally a provider of advanced location-based positioning, modeling, and workflow solutions for industrial applications.

points.name: RIEGL
points.description: Austrian manufacturer building laser scanners and measurement systems for physical environment mapping.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that builds terrestrial, mobile, airborne and UAV-based laser scanning systems for surveying and mapping applications. It manufactures LiDAR sensors, IMU/GNSS subsystems and integrated drone platforms that capture high-precision 3D digital data for surveyors, researchers and industrial operators.
1. A sensor maker that builds laser scanning systems and LiDAR sensors sold as standalone hardware, integrated payloads and complete unmanned aerial platforms.
2. Pulsed time-of-flight lidar and proprietary smart-waveform technology combined with high-precision IMU/GNSS localization subsystems to capture 3D digital data over ranges up to 6000 meters.
3. 3D perception, high-accuracy topographic mapping, topo-bathymetric underwater surveying, mobile 360-degree laser capture and ultra long-range scanning for snow and ice environments.
4. Customers get hardware as standalone sensors, integrated laser scanners, mobile mapping systems and complete UAV platforms equipped with mounted sensors.
5. Airborne mapping, mobile mapping, terrestrial surveying, forest measurement, powerline corridor mapping, snow and ice monitoring and unmanned aerial vehicle-based surveying.
6. Surveying and mapping professionals, academic and forestry research institutions, geospatial AI companies and industrial operators.
7. Its sensors and integrated scanning platforms are deployed by surveyors and researchers to capture 3D geospatial data in the field.
8. Its proprietary smart-waveform lidar technology enables high-accuracy capture over extreme ranges up to 6000 meters and across diverse environments from topo-bathymetric surfaces to snow and ice.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Wageningen University, the Center for International Forestry Research and the geospatial AI company Enview.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of laser scanners, integrated mapping systems and unmanned aerial platforms.
Scale and maturity: An established manufacturer with over 45 years producing commercial LiDAR systems, operating a global portfolio and a North American headquarters.
Geography: Based in Austria with an international operational footprint including a United States office.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is high-performance laser scanning technology and geospatial hardware.

points.name: Luminar
points.description: Orlando-based autonomous vehicle sensor manufacturer building long-range LiDAR systems that help self-driving cars detect road hazards.
points.bullets:
A lidar maker that builds long-range automotive lidar sensors and integrated perception software for autonomous vehicles and advanced driver-assistance systems. It supplies sensors and software stacks to global automakers, robotaxi operators, and aviation partners for Level 3+ autonomous driving and flight.
1. A sensor maker that builds automotive lidar and perception software.
2. 1550 nm indium-phosphide semiconductor lasers, InGaAs receivers, and application-specific integrated circuits paired with AI-based perception software.
3. Long-range object detection, object classification, and 3D velocity detection for autonomous driving and proactive safety.
4. Lidar sensors, licensed perception software, and integrated sensor-software systems sold to automakers and autonomous vehicle developers.
5. Autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, robotaxis, autonomous trucks, and autonomous flight.
6. Automakers, robotaxi operators, autonomous truck developers, and aviation companies.
7. Its sensors and software are designed into vehicles and autonomous stacks by automakers and technology partners.
8. It uses a 1550 nm infrared wavelength that enables higher resolution and longer detection range than conventional lidar while meeting eye-safety limits at higher power.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Volvo, Mercedes-Benz, Nissan, SAIC Motor, Toyota Research Institute, Toyota Ventures, Daimler, Mobileye, Pony.ai, Airbus subsidiary UpNext, Zenseact, Plus, Peter Thiel, Canvas Ventures, GVA Capital, and 1517 Fund.
Organization type: A publicly traded technology company that filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.
Business model: Hardware sales of lidar sensors and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2012, publicly traded via a SPAC merger with a multi-billion-dollar valuation, with restructuring and bankruptcy filing after major automaker contracts fell apart.
Geography: Based in the United States with partnerships and operations globally.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire business is focused on autonomous vehicle perception hardware and software.

points.name: Quanergy Systems
points.description: Technology company building edge AI LiDAR sensors that process environmental data on-device for autonomous vehicle navigation and collision avoidance.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that builds solid-state lidar and perception software for edge AI applications in physical automation. It designs and sells lidar sensors and companion perception software for autonomous navigation, security, and industrial mapping. It serves customers needing 3D perception and on-device detection across transportation and industrial sectors.
1. A sensor maker that builds solid-state lidar sensors and perception software for industrial and automotive applications.
2. Optical phased array solid-state lidar and 2D lidar sensors paired with on-device perception software.
3. 3D perception, long-range object detection, and zone monitoring for autonomous mobile robots and security applications.
4. Lidar sensors and perception software sold as components and embedded software to integrators and machine builders.
5. Autonomous vehicles, smart cities, physical security, mapping, industrial automation, AGVs and AMRs.
6. Industrial automation providers, security integrators, transportation operators, and smart city developers.
7. Its sensors and software are designed into autonomous mobile robots and security systems by integrators and machine builders.
8. It uses optical phased array technology to deliver solid-state lidar with a high price-to-performance advantage and long-range outdoor capability.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It entered a SPAC merger agreement with CITIC Capital Acquisition Corp and has a business relationship with In-Position Technologies.
Organization type: A publicly traded company that went public via a SPAC merger.
Business model: Sensor hardware sales and perception software licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2012, it secured $150 million in funding in 2023 and operates mass production at a factory in Sunnyvale, California.
Geography: Headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, serving a global market.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire core focus and central mission of the organization's business.

points.name: Aeva
points.description: Sensor technology company building 4D LiDAR systems that detect object distance and velocity for autonomous vehicles.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops 4D lidar sensors and integrated perception software for autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics and smart infrastructure. It builds frequency-modulated continuous wave lidar-on-chip modules and custom processors that measure range and velocity simultaneously, and sells them to automakers and equipment manufacturers.
1. A sensor maker that builds 4D lidar sensors and lidar-on-chip modules with integrated perception software.
2. Frequency-modulated continuous wave lidar-on-chip technology using silicon photonics to measure range and velocity simultaneously for every point.
3. 3D perception, instant velocity detection, object categorization, localization, risk detection, real-time monitoring and road boundary recognition.
4. Sensors, custom processors and lidar-on-chip modules sold to automakers, plus licensed perception software.
5. Autonomous trucks, passenger vehicles, industrial robotics, warehouse automation, defense and smart infrastructure.
6. Automakers, autonomous truck developers, tier-one automotive suppliers, industrial robotics makers and defense agencies.
7. Its sensors and processors are designed into autonomous vehicles and robotic systems by OEMs.
8. Its frequency-modulated continuous wave technology provides direct velocity measurement and immunity to sunlight and multi-sensor interference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Daimler Truck, Torc Robotics, LG Innotek and Ouster.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Sensor and component hardware sales, plus software licensing.
Scale and maturity: A public company selected as a tier-one supplier for a major truck maker, with automotive-grade sensors in advanced sample stages moving toward series production.
Geography: Based in Mountain View, California, operating in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI perception is the sole focus of its operations.

points.name: Hesai
points.description: Chinese LiDAR manufacturer producing automotive-grade sensors that provide 3D perception for autonomous vehicles and robotics.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that designs and manufactures automotive-grade lidar for autonomous vehicles, robots, and industrial automation, supplying the 3D perception hardware that downstream developers integrate into complete autonomous platforms.
1. A sensor maker that builds lidar sensors and integrated sensing kits, sold as hardware components to automakers and robot makers.
2. Mechanical, solid-state, and hybrid solid-state lidar systems powered by proprietary ASIC and SPAD system-on-chip technology that fire laser pulses to generate 3D point clouds, fusing spatial and color data.
3. 3D perception, long-range object detection, blind-spot monitoring, high-resolution environmental mapping, and spatial intelligence for embodied intelligence training.
4. Lidar sensors and integrated sensing kits sold as hardware components, delivered as modules designed into vehicles and robots by device makers.
5. Robotaxis, autonomous trucks, passenger vehicles, delivery vehicles, mobile robots, humanoid robots, lawn-mowing robots, smart ports, and 3D digitalization.
6. Automakers, autonomous vehicle companies, robotaxi operators, autonomous trucking firms, and robotics manufacturers.
7. Its sensors are designed into autonomous vehicles and robots by automotive OEMs and robot makers.
8. Vertical integration of in-house ASIC chip design and domestic VCSEL fabrication enables mass production at sub-$200 unit costs, driving rapid product iteration and high-volume deliveries.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Nvidia, Zoox, Waabi, Kodiak, Nuro, Baidu, Pony.ai, Motional, WeRide, Li Auto, BYD, Xiaomi, Toyota, Unitree, and Meituan.
Organization type: A publicly traded company listed on Nasdaq and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Business model: Hardware sales of lidar sensors and integrated sensing components.
Scale and maturity: The world's largest automotive lidar supplier with over 2.4 million cumulative deliveries, commanding 37% of the global market.
Geography: Headquartered in Shanghai, China, with operations spanning over 70 cities across 30 countries and regions.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play technology provider whose entire operational focus is dedicated to the development and mass production of lidar sensors and related perception hardware.

points.name: Cepton Technologies
points.description: Silicon Valley technology company building LiDAR sensors for real-time 3D perception in autonomous vehicles and smart infrastructure.
points.bullets:
A lidar maker that develops 3D lidar sensors and integrated perception software for automotive advanced driver assistance systems, autonomous driving, and industrial applications. The company designs compact, embeddable sensing hardware alongside edge computing and perception software that deliver real-time object detection, tracking, and classification for automakers and industrial system integrators.
1. A sensor maker that builds lidar sensors and perception software, sold as hardware components and software subsystems to automakers and industrial integrators.
2. Micro Motion Technology architecture that uses frictionless, rotation-free, and mirrorless mechanics to deliver long-range, high-resolution 3D perception, paired with edge computing and lidar perception software for real-time object detection, tracking, classification, and velocity.
3. The specific capabilities it delivers include 3D perception, long-range object detection, wide-area tracking, classification, and velocity estimation for autonomous systems.
4. Customers get it as lidar sensors, embedded hardware components, and integrated perception software subsystems.
5. The sensors and software are used in advanced driver assistance systems, autonomous vehicles, intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, road tolling, railway stations, security, crowd analytics, and industrial robotics.
6. The types of customer it sells to include automakers, autonomous vehicle operators, industrial system integrators, and smart infrastructure providers.
7. Its sensors and perception software are designed into autonomous vehicles and smart infrastructure systems by automakers and integrators.
8. Its proprietary Micro Motion Technology architecture delivers high-resolution 3D perception without rotating or mirror components, enabling a compact form factor and high-volume manufacturability at lower cost than competing lidar approaches.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable named partners include NVIDIA, Dataspeed, Kudan, May Mobility, Wideye, MechaSpin, MH Corbin, and INIT.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of lidar sensors and associated perception software subsystems.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016, the company raised $100 million in early 2024 and maintains registered offices in Germany, Canada, and the UK alongside its San Jose headquarters.
Geography: It is based in San Jose, California, USA, and operates globally with facilities in locations such as Austria.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the absolute core of the organization's mission, as its entire product portfolio is dedicated to enabling autonomous machines and systems to perceive and navigate the physical world.

points.name: LiDARit
points.description: US LiDAR digitization company supplying laser sensors that enable automated systems to detect objects and monitor environments in real time.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker and data services provider that builds laser scanning technology for precision digitization of physical environments and trains clients to use the technology across various industries.
1. A sensor maker that builds lidar scanning hardware and provides digitization services and training.
2. Laser-based lidar scanning technology used to scan environments and analyze data.
3. Sensors, digitization services, and client training delivered directly to end users.
4. A dedicated focus on precision digitization through laser scanning technology paired with client training on effective technology use.
points.profile: Geography: Based in the United States.

points.name: Seyond
points.description: US technology company manufacturing LiDAR sensors and perception software that help autonomous machines navigate physical environments.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that designs and manufactures image-grade solid-state LiDAR sensors and perception software for autonomous vehicles, robotics, smart infrastructure, and industrial automation.
1. A sensor maker that builds solid-state and scanning LiDAR sensors sold as hardware components to automakers and robotics builders.
2. Solid-state and scanning LiDAR architectures with fully digital electronic scanning, ultra-long ranges exceeding 500 meters, and wide field-of-view point cloud capture, accompanied by perception software.
3. Long-range and short-range 3D perception, precise object detection and tracking, environmental mapping, and traffic management.
4. LiDAR sensors, perception software platforms, and road user detection systems sold as hardware components and software to integrators.
5. Autonomous vehicles, intelligent transportation systems, robotics, smart infrastructure, industrial logistics, and traffic intersections.
6. Automakers, autonomous trucking developers, robotics companies, smart infrastructure operators, and industrial logistics providers.
7. Its sensors are designed into autonomous vehicles and robots by automakers and machine builders.
8. It combines automotive-grade mass production readiness with flagship long-range sensors exceeding 500 meters and deep integration into major simulation platforms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with NIO, NVIDIA, Inceptio Technology, Zhongke Xingchen, Exwayz, and Hexagon.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of LiDAR sensors and software platforms.
Scale and maturity: It has deployed over 200,000 units with a production capacity expected to exceed half a million units annually.
Geography: It is based in Sunnyvale, United States, and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is purely dedicated to advancing LiDAR sensing technology and perception services for physical automation.

points.name: HERE Technologies
points.description: US mapping and location services company providing AI-powered HD maps for autonomous vehicle navigation.
points.bullets:
A mapping and location services company that builds automotive-grade HD maps and terrestrial lidar datasets for automated vehicles and 3D modeling. It provides continuously-updating, highly-precise road network maps built using sensor data and AI, serving automakers developing software-defined vehicles.
1. A developer tools and platform company that builds HD mapping software and lidar datasets sold as cloud services and licensed data.
2. A continuously-updating mapping service that uses sensor data and AI to identify real-world changes across the road network, alongside a global library of three-dimensional terrestrial lidar.
3. Autonomous navigation support, highly-precise road network mapping, real-world 3D modeling, and automotive-grade location intelligence.
4. Cloud services, licensed mapping software, and datasets accessed via a location platform.
5. Automated vehicles and software-defined vehicles.
6. Automakers.
7. Its mapping services and datasets are integrated by automakers into their automated driving systems.
8. It uses AI to power a continuously-updating mapping platform that identifies real-world changes using sensor data from the road network.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners and investors include Audi, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Lotus, Bosch, Continental, Daimler, Intel, Pioneer, and Renovo.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses, data subscriptions, and cloud platform access.
Scale and maturity: A global provider of mapping and location services serving major automotive manufacturers.
Geography: Based in Chicago, United States, and operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: It provides general mapping, location intelligence, and navigation services for people, businesses, and cities beyond autonomous driving.

points.name: Lumina Lidar
points.description: 3D mapping service providing high-resolution spatial data for physical AI perception.
points.bullets:
A sensor and spatial data services provider that performs terrestrial, aerial, and mobile lidar scanning to generate point clouds, 3D models, and 2D floor plans for physical AI applications. It operates within the sensor and perception layer of the physical AI stack, supplying processed spatial data and digital twins necessary for AI systems to perceive and act in the physical world. The organization functions as a specialized data services provider rather than a complete physical AI system manufacturer, feeding accurate, high-fidelity spatial information into the broader robotics and automation value chain.
1. A sensor and spatial data services provider that builds 3D mapping and modeling services, sold as processed point clouds and digital twins.

It builds an end-to-end autonomy system and integrates it into electric vehicles, then operates a robotaxi fleet through ride-hailing partnerships.
