2. An end-to-end autonomy stack built around Large Driving Models that handle perception, prediction, and control, supported by over 30 sensors, onboard compute, and a cloud-based continuous learning framework for edge cases.
3. Level 4 autonomous driving, 360-degree perception, and fleet management for driverless ride-hailing and delivery.
4. A licensed autonomy stack integrated into factory-built electric vehicles and operated as a robotaxi fleet through ride-hailing platform integrations.
5. Robotaxis and autonomous delivery vehicles in urban ride-hailing and food delivery.
6. Ride-hailing platforms, delivery platforms, and passengers.
7. It licenses its autonomy stack to its own fleet of factory-built vehicles and operates the resulting robotaxis through third-party ride-hailing apps.
8. It vertically integrates an end-to-end, AI-first autonomy stack with factory-built automotive-grade vehicles and operates the fleet itself rather than only supplying software to automakers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv are parent companies; Uber and Lyft are ride-hailing partners; Hesai supplies lidar and Ambarella supplies AI processors.
Organization type: A joint venture and subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group and Aptiv.
Business model: Ride-hailing and delivery fees, and fleet operations.
Scale and maturity: An established joint venture founded in 2013 that has completed over 130,000 autonomous rides and holds permits for fully driverless testing on California public roads.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, with robotaxi operations in Las Vegas and planned expansion to Los Angeles.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and autonomous mobility are the company's entire focus.

points.name: Li Auto
points.description: Chinese automotive manufacturer building proprietary autonomous driving chips for in-vehicle perception and decision-making.
points.bullets:
An automaker and robot maker that designs and manufactures premium smart electric vehicles and develops autonomous driving systems and silicon in-house, while branching into wheeled and bipedal robots for consumers.
1. A vehicle and robot maker that builds and sells electric cars and developing bipedal and wheeled robots, alongside proprietary autonomous driving silicon.
2. Vision-language-action driver models, custom autonomous driving systems-on-chip with network-on-chip interconnects, and integrated spatial-behavioral intelligence architectures.
3. On-vehicle perception, real-time autonomous driving decision-making, and high-compute edge AI inference for physical automation.
4. Complete vehicles integrated with proprietary silicon and autonomy stacks, with planned future delivery of complete robots.
5. Premium electric vehicles, autonomous driving systems, and humanoid robots.
6. Consumers in the automotive market.
7. It designs and manufactures complete vehicles and robots, integrating its proprietary silicon and autonomy software directly into its own machines.
8. Complete vertical integration of autonomous driving capabilities, developing custom silicon architectures in-house rather than relying on third-party autonomy stacks.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses lidar from Hesai, network-on-chip IP from Arteris, Snapdragon Elite automotive platforms, and batteries from CATL, with backing from Matrix Partners China.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of premium electric vehicles.
Scale and maturity: A well-established manufacturer producing and deploying advanced intelligent vehicles with significant planned R&D investment in AI and robotics.
Geography: It is based in China and focuses its manufacturing, development, and sales operations within the domestic Chinese market.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's core business encompasses the design and manufacturing of premium extended-range and battery electric vehicles.

points.name: Changan
points.description: Chinese automotive manufacturer integrating LiDAR into vehicles and developing humanoid robot prototypes.
points.bullets:
An automaker and robot maker that designs and manufactures vehicles and has developed a humanoid robot prototype. It partners with sensor suppliers for automotive autonomy programs and builds physical machines for the consumer mobility and robotics markets.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that builds automobiles and humanoid robot prototypes.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Hesai Technology.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Geography: Based in China.

points.name: Geely
points.description: Chinese automotive manufacturer producing purpose-built vehicle platforms for commercial robotaxi deployment.
points.bullets:
A vehicle maker that builds purpose-built electric vehicle platforms and complete cars designed for integration with autonomous driving systems, supplying them to robotaxi operators. It manufactures modular electric vehicle architectures specifically engineered for autonomous ride-hailing rather than retrofitting consumer cars, providing the foundational automotive hardware onto which separate partners stack inference silicon, sensors and autonomy software. The organization also invests in robotics and mobility companies and operates a broader global automotive business.
1. A vehicle maker that designs and sells complete electric cars and modular vehicle platforms for autonomous ride-hailing fleets.
2. A modular electric vehicle architecture called Sustainable Experience Architecture, including a variant engineered as a purpose-built robotaxi platform with the structural and electrical interfaces needed for autonomous driving system integration.
3. Level 4-capable vehicle platforms with the chassis, passenger packaging, drive-by-wire controls and telematics connectivity required for driverless ride-hailing operation.
4. Complete electric vehicles and bare vehicle platforms delivered to autonomous driving system integrators and robotaxi operators.
5. Robotaxis and autonomous ride-hailing fleets.
6. Autonomous ride-hailing operators and autonomous driving system developers.
7. Its vehicle platforms are purchased by autonomy software developers and fleet operators that integrate their own sensors, compute and driving stacks onto the base vehicles.
8. It produces purpose-built electric vehicle platforms engineered from the ground up for autonomous ride-hailing, using a modular electric architecture to lower per-unit robotaxi cost compared to retrofitted consumer cars.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Waymo, NVIDIA, Hesai Technology, Baidu, Black Sesame Technologies, Unitree Robotics, Volocopter and Arm China.
Organization type: A publicly traded automotive conglomerate.
Business model: Vehicle and platform sales to autonomous fleet operators and automakers, plus equity investments in robotics and mobility companies.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale global manufacturer producing vehicle platforms at a volume scaling toward tens of thousands of units annually for commercial deployment.
Geography: Based in China, with manufacturing in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, and engineering operations in Gothenburg, Sweden, shipping platforms to the United States for final integration.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization designs, manufactures and sells consumer and commercial electric vehicles through multiple automotive brands globally.

points.name: Chery
points.description: Chinese automaker manufacturing humanoid robots and robotic dogs using automotive-grade perception and motion control technologies.
points.bullets:
An automaker and robot maker that designs and sells complete humanoid robots, leveraging automotive-grade manufacturing and supply chains to build bipedal and quadruped robots for consumer, retail and public-service applications.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete humanoid and quadruped robots, and an automaker that builds and sells passenger vehicles.
2. Complete deployed robotic systems integrating on-device sensors such as 3D lidar and depth cameras with perception, motion control and remote VR operation capabilities.
3. Multilingual vehicle presentations, customer service, traffic management, public safety monitoring and in-home companionship.
4. Complete robots sold directly to consumers through e-commerce platforms and distributed through a global automotive dealer network.
5. Humanoids, homes, retail showrooms, public service settings, healthcare facilities and connected passenger vehicles.
6. Consumers, public safety agencies, healthcare facilities and retail operators.
7. Its robots are sold directly to end users through e-commerce and its parent company's global dealer network.
8. It translates automotive-grade supply chain and quality control processes into embodied robotic products and is among the first automakers to sell humanoid robots directly to consumers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Hesai Technology and Baidu.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a major publicly traded automaker operating as a distinct robotics entity.
Business model: Robot hardware sales and passenger vehicle sales.
Scale and maturity: Launched in early 2025, it has delivered over 3,000 robots globally and secured agreements for thousands of additional public service units.
Geography: Based in China, it operates in more than 60 countries and regions with a significant overseas deployment footprint.
Beyond physical AI: The overarching parent organization is a major automotive manufacturer that also builds connected passenger vehicles.

points.name: Zeekr
points.description: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer building purpose-built robotaxi platforms for autonomous ride-hailing deployments.
points.bullets:
An automaker that designs and manufactures electric vehicle platforms and purpose-built chassis for autonomous ride-hailing applications, selling base vehicles to autonomous fleet operators for upfitting with self-driving systems.
1. An automaker that builds and sells electric vehicles and purpose-built robotaxi platforms for mobility operators.
2. Electric vehicle architectures with specialized features for driverless operations, such as low step-in heights and flat flooring.
3. Vehicle platforms designed to be upfitted with autonomous driving hardware and sensors.
4. Complete base vehicles exported for autonomous system integration at upfitting facilities.
5. Robotaxis and autonomous ride-hailing fleets, as well as consumer electric vehicles.
6. Autonomous vehicle operators and mobility fleets.
7. Its base vehicles are purchased by autonomous driving companies and upfitted with their own self-driving hardware at integration facilities.
8. It designs purpose-built robotaxi platforms with features for driverless operations rather than retrofitting traditional passenger vehicles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Waymo, Hesai Technology, UBTECH Robotics, RoboSense, Geely.
Organization type: Privately held automotive manufacturer and subsidiary of Geely.
Business model: Vehicle sales to autonomous fleet operators and consumers.
Scale and maturity: Has been actively supplying its autonomous fleet partner since 2021 and manufactures at scale in China.
Geography: Based in China and manufactures vehicles there, exporting platforms for integration in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The company's broader business focuses on manufacturing premium electric vehicles for the consumer market.

points.name: SAIC-GM
points.description: Chinese automotive manufacturer deploying wheeled humanoid robots for battery assembly tasks.
points.bullets:
An automaker and manufacturing operator that builds passenger vehicles and deploys wheeled and bipedal humanoid robots on its battery assembly lines, co-developing the robots with robotics makers and validating them in its own factories.
1. A vehicle maker that builds and sells automobiles and operates physical automation in its own factories.
2. Humanoid robots with on-device perception, dual-arm coordination, and force-controlled manipulation for autonomous grasping and loading on mass-production lines.
3. Real-world industrial validation of embodied AI, battery cell grasping and loading, and autonomous path planning without fixed pre-programmed instructions.
4. Integration of humanoid robots and advanced driver-assistance systems into its own mass-production facilities and vehicle models.
5. Automotive manufacturing facilities, battery assembly lines, and electric vehicles.
6. Internal mass-production operations for its own vehicles.
7. It buys and co-develops robots from makers and operates them in its own factories.
8. It deploys wheeled humanoid robots that occupy less than 15% of the footprint of traditional automated workstations while autonomously planning grasping paths.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Joint venture between SAIC Motor and General Motors, partnered with AgiBot, Fourier Intelligence, Zhiyuan Robotics, Kepler, Momenta, and Hesai Technology.
Organization type: A corporate automotive manufacturer and joint venture with an industrial investment arm.
Business model: Passenger vehicle sales, supported by manufacturing automation and industrial investment in robotics.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale industrial manufacturer that has validated dozens of robotic scenarios, tested robots across factory sites, and invested over 800 million yuan in the humanoid robotics sector.
Geography: Based in China and operating mass-production facilities domestically.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI initiatives, the organization's foundational business is the large-scale manufacturing and sale of passenger vehicles.

points.name: Dreame
points.description: Chinese robotics company building autonomous vacuum cleaners with SLAM navigation and AI perception for home environments.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and manufactures autonomous home appliances and service robots, integrating sensors, motors and on-device inference into complete consumer products for the global retail market.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous robotic appliances and smart home devices.
2. The core technology combines proprietary high-speed digital motors, lidar and RGBD spatial perception sensors, and on-device AI control algorithms for physical environment navigation.
3. The robots deliver autonomous navigation, spatial perception, and automated cleaning for home environments.
4. Customers receive fully assembled, complete robotic appliances and smart devices.
5. The products are used in homes for vacuuming, lawn-mowing, and other domestic automation tasks.
6. The company sells to consumers and retail partners.
7. The organization is a vertically integrated robot original equipment manufacturer that designs its own components and algorithms and assembles them into finished consumer goods.
8. The approach is distinguished by a reusable technology platform based on high-speed motors, spatial perception algorithms, and AI-driven control systems adaptable across over 100 product categories.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company uses lidar from Hesai in its lawn-mowing and other robotic products.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held technology hardware company.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of its robotic appliances and smart home devices.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, the mature company operates at massive global scale, generating an estimated USD 1.2 billion in revenue in 2024 with over 45% year-over-year growth and holding the largest worldwide market share for robotic vacuums.
Geography: The company is based in China and distributes its products to consumers and retail partners across more than 80 countries globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, robotics, and physical automation are the sole focus of the organization, which has no other business outside consumer smart appliances and home service robotics.

points.name: Rivian Automotive
points.description: Electric automaker developing custom silicon and AI software for on-device autonomous driving.
points.bullets:
A vehicle maker that designs and builds autonomous electric vehicles and the custom inference silicon and self-driving software that run in them for ride-hailing and consumer markets.
1. An automaker that builds and sells autonomous electric vehicles and designs its own self-driving chips and software stacks.
2. Vertically integrated Level 4 self-driving stacks running on custom 5-nanometer inference processors paired with camera, radar, and lidar sensor suites.
3. Autonomous navigation, on-device inference at approximately 1600 TOPS, sensor fusion, and Level 4 robotaxi operation.
4. Complete vehicles and licensed autonomy hardware and software delivered to mobility platforms.
5. Robotaxis, consumer electric SUVs, ride-hailing, and delivery.
6. Ride-hailing platforms, fleet operators, and consumers.
7. Its autonomous vehicles and integrated silicon are operated by ride-hailing platforms and sold to consumers.
8. Full vertical integration of custom silicon, multi-sensor autonomy hardware, and the complete vehicle in a single program.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Uber Technologies, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, and a Chinese lidar supplier.
Organization type: A publicly traded automaker.
Business model: Vehicle sales and autonomous ride-hailing fleet deployment fees.
Scale and maturity: A well-capitalized manufacturer investing hundreds of millions of dollars in a custom chip program, planning robotaxi deployments of up to 50,000 vehicles.
Geography: Based in Irvine, California, USA, focusing manufacturing and deployment domestically.
Beyond physical AI: The company designs, manufactures, and sells consumer and commercial electric vehicles.

points.name: Teradar
points.description: Boston-based startup developing high-resolution terahertz vision sensors for autonomous vehicles that see through fog, rain, and snow.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops solid-state terahertz imaging sensors for autonomous vehicles, providing high-resolution perception in adverse weather. It builds chip-based sensor modules for automakers and defense contractors to integrate into their machines.
1. A sensor maker that builds automotive terahertz imaging sensors.
2. Solid-state terahertz-band phased array sensors built on a custom silicon fabrication process that detect objects at long range using electromagnetic radiation.
3. Long-range, high-resolution three-dimensional perception and all-weather vision through rain, snow, fog and glare.
4. Sensor chips and modular engines sold to automotive manufacturers and defense integrators.
5. Autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems and military robotic combat vehicles.
6. Automakers, Tier 1 automotive suppliers and defense contractors.
7. Its sensors are designed into autonomous vehicle platforms and defense systems by OEMs.
8. It combines the resolution of lidar with the robustness of radar at a lower cost using solid-state silicon chips with no moving parts.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control and various automakers serve as development partners, while VXI Capital, Lockheed Martin Ventures, IBEX Investors, Capricorn Investment Group and MIT Engine Ventures are investors.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Sensor hardware sales and paid development programs.
Scale and maturity: Five years old, having raised $150 million in Series B funding, with sensor integration targeted for 2028 vehicle production.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, with active development operations across the United States and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Developing advanced perception technology for physical AI applications constitutes the entire focus of this pure-play enterprise.

points.name: Voyant Photonics
points.description: Photonics technology company building compact LiDAR sensors that provide autonomous machines with real-time depth and velocity perception.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops silicon photonics-based chip-scale 4D FMCW LiDAR sensors and modules for physical AI, robotics, and autonomous systems.
1. A sensor maker that builds solid-state FMCW LiDAR sensors and modules.
2. Silicon photonics technology integrates optical components onto a single die to produce frequency-modulated continuous-wave LiDAR.
3. Delivers high-resolution 4D point clouds with simultaneous depth and velocity data for every point without moving parts.
4. Sold as solid-state LiDAR sensors and modules.
5. Used in autonomous vehicles, mobile robots, industrial automation, drones, smart infrastructure, mining, agriculture, and logistics.
6. Sells to robot makers, autonomous vehicle developers, industrial automation developers, and edge AI developers.
7. Its sensors are designed into autonomous machines and integrated into simulation platforms by developers to validate autonomous systems.
8. Delivers simultaneous depth and velocity data without moving parts, ambient-light interference, or additional compute requirements, using datacom-grade photonic foundries for semiconductor-level scalability.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partnered with NVIDIA.
Organization type: Privately held startup spun out of Columbia University.
Business model: Hardware sales of LiDAR sensors and modules.
Scale and maturity: Raised $15.4 million in Series A funding.
Geography: Based in New York, NY, USA.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play provider focused entirely on advancing silicon photonics and solid-state LiDAR perception technology.

points.name: MicroVision
points.description: LiDAR sensor manufacturer building solid-state perception systems for autonomous vehicles and robotics.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that designs and manufactures solid-state lidar sensors and develops edge perception software for automotive, industrial, and security and defense markets, selling integrated hardware-software sensing subsystems rather than complete machines.
1. A sensor maker that builds solid-state lidar sensors and perception software, sold as modular hardware and integrated sensing subsystems to vehicle and robot makers.
2. Solid-state lidar sensors that output streaming 3D point clouds and edge perception software that processes the data into an ultra-high-resolution image of the driving scene.
3. Long-range 3D perception and real-time 3D mapping for autonomous navigation and collision avoidance in low-light or GNSS-denied environments.
4. Lidar sensors, integrated hardware-software sensing modules, and licensed edge perception software provided to vehicle and platform manufacturers.
5. Advanced driver assistance systems, autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, unmanned aerial vehicles, and security and defense platforms.
6. Automotive original equipment manufacturers, industrial robotics developers, and defense and security system integrators.
7. Its lidar sensors and perception software are designed into autonomous vehicles and unmanned platforms by original equipment manufacturers.
8. It targets sub-$200 sensor pricing for mainstream ADAS integration by using proven automotive-grade materials to build a cost-effective solid-state architecture that avoids exotic technologies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It works with OEM partners to enable their product roadmaps and has acquired technologies from Ibeo Automotive Systems, Scantinel, and Luminar.
Organization type: A publicly traded commercial technology company operating within the automotive and robotics supply chain.
Business model: Hardware sales of lidar sensors and software licenses for edge perception.
Scale and maturity: It operates globally within the automotive supply chain and targets mass-market integration into Level 2+ advanced driver assistance systems.
Geography: It operates globally, developing solutions for the worldwide automotive, industrial, and defense supply chains.
Beyond physical AI: It is a pure-play provider focused entirely on the design, manufacture, and software integration of solid-state lidar perception systems for physical automation.

points.name: Valeo
points.description: French automotive supplier manufacturing sensors and embedded AI software for autonomous driving systems.
points.bullets:
An automotive supplier that builds ADAS sensors, embedded perception software and digital twin simulation tools for automakers developing driver-assistance and autonomous driving systems.
1. A sensor maker and Tier-1 automotive supplier that builds lidar, radar and camera sensors, plus embedded autonomy software, sold as components and integrated subsystems to vehicle manufacturers.
2. Solid-state and scanning lidar, 77 GHz long-range radar, multi-sensor fusion, and embedded AI software for perception in automotive drive systems.
3. 3D perception, sensor fusion, adaptive cruise control, lane-centering, automated parking, and digital twin simulation for ADAS sensor validation.
4. Sensors, sensor suites, embedded software and simulation tools supplied as Tier-1 components and subsystems to automakers.
5. Advanced driver-assistance systems, level 3 autonomous driving and mass-market passenger vehicles.
6. Global automakers and electric vehicle manufacturers.
7. Its sensors and software are designed into driver-assistance and autonomous driving systems by vehicle manufacturers.
8. It delivers integrated subsystem solutions combining hardware, on-device inference software and simulation tools rather than standalone sensors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Mercedes, NVIDIA, Applied Intuition, Denso, Cathay Innovation Fund.
Organization type: Publicly traded Tier-1 automotive supplier.
Business model: Component and subsystem sales to automakers.
Scale and maturity: A large mature company with over 100,000 employees and roughly 21.5 billion euros in revenue in 2024.
Geography: Based in France and operates globally across 28 countries.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the broader business is a comprehensive automotive supplier whose products encompass electrification, interior experience and lighting systems.

points.name: AEye
points.description: LiDAR technology company developing software-defined sensors with on-device AI compute to help autonomous vehicles perceive and navigate physical environments.
points.bullets:
A lidar sensor maker that develops software-defined, long-range lidar sensors and full-stack perception subsystems for autonomous vehicles and physical AI applications. The company designs MOEMS-based solid-state lidar hardware paired with on-device AI compute runtimes, selling to automakers, Tier-1 manufacturers, and smart infrastructure operators. It acts as a specialized component and subsystem supplier within the physical AI value chain.
1. A sensor maker that builds software-defined, long-range solid-state lidar sensors and full-stack perception subsystems.
2. MOEMS-based solid-state lidar operating at 1550nm to detect objects at distances of up to 1.5 kilometers, combined with on-device AI compute and sensor fusion runtimes.
3. Ultra-long-range 3D perception, real-time object detection, pre-fused lidar and video capture, and edge AI intelligence generation for physical AI systems.
4. Lidar sensors, integrated perception modules, and full-stack solutions delivered to automakers and infrastructure operators.
5. Autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, smart infrastructure, rail, logistics, and aviation.
6. Automotive OEMs, Tier-1 automotive manufacturers, intelligent transportation operators, and aerospace companies.
7. Its lidar sensors are integrated into autonomous vehicle platforms and smart infrastructure by Tier-1 manufacturers and OEMs.
8. A software-defined architecture packs long-range, solid-state sensing into a compact, power-efficient form factor optimized for behind-the-windshield vehicle integration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Continental, NVIDIA, and the University of Toronto, with investments from Intel, Airbus, and R7 Partners.
Organization type: A publicly traded company operating as a commercial technology and sensor developer.
Business model: Component and sensor hardware sales, software-defined subsystem licensing, and major OEM contracts.
Scale and maturity: A California-based startup with major OEM contracts potentially worth tens of millions of dollars, operating a capital-light manufacturing model capable of scaling to tens of thousands of units annually.
Geography: Headquartered in Pleasanton, California, actively serving global transportation and robotics markets.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play provider of intelligent vision and perception technologies, focusing its entire commercial strategy on advancing hardware and software solutions for physical AI.

points.name: Baraja
points.description: LiDAR technology company building spectrum-based sensors that let autonomous vehicles see and navigate physical environments.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops lidar hardware for autonomous vehicles, supplying the perception components that capture spatial data for on-device processing in self-driving systems.
1. A sensor maker that builds automotive lidar sensors.
2. The core technology is a reinvented lidar system that captures high-fidelity spatial data for physical environment perception.
3. The sensors deliver high-accuracy 3D perception and spatial data for autonomous navigation.
4. Customers get the technology as sensor hardware and subsystem components.
5. The hardware is used in autonomous vehicles and self-driving cars.
6. The company sells to the autonomous vehicle industry and automotive sector.
7. Its sensors are designed into autonomous driving systems by vehicle makers.
8. The approach reinvents traditional lidar hardware to act as highly accurate perception systems for self-driving cars.
points.profile:
Geography: The organization operates globally within the international autonomous vehicle market.
Beyond physical AI: Reinventing lidar hardware for autonomous navigation represents the company's entire focus and core business activity.

points.name: Uhnder
points.description: Austin automotive radar startup developing digital imaging radar-on-chip sensors for autonomous vehicles.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops fully software-defined digital radar-on-chip solutions and sensor modules for advanced driver assistance systems, autonomous vehicles, and logistics automation. The organization integrates 77 GHz radar sensors with on-chip ARM CPUs and DSPs to enable edge computing and on-device algorithm execution for safety-critical perception.
1. A sensor maker that designs automotive-qualified radar-on-chip sensors and modules for 4D imaging perception.
2. The core technology is a single-chip radar solution built on a 28nm RF process using Digital Code Modulation MIMO and integrated DSPs and Arm cores to provide high-resolution 4D imaging radar.
3. It delivers digital perception capable of detecting and tracking thousands of objects in height, speed, and distance at 50+ fps with high angular resolution and interference immunity.
4. Customers get radar-on-chip sensors and modules supplied to automotive manufacturers and Tier 1 suppliers for integration.
5. The sensors are used in autonomous vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, and logistics automation systems.
6. The company sells to automotive manufacturers and Tier 1 automotive suppliers.
7. Its radar chips and modules are designed into digital radar products and vehicles by Tier 1 suppliers and automakers.
8. It differentiates through cost-effective Digital Code Modulation radar-on-chip designs that provide superior angular resolution and contrast at a fraction of the cost of LiDAR systems while mitigating mutual radar interference.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Magna for its ICON Digital Radar product, Fisker for the Ocean vehicle, and Spartan for software application development.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held technology company.
Business model: The company makes money through supplying radar-on-chip sensors and modules to Tier 1 suppliers and automakers.
Scale and maturity: Having secured Series C funding, the company has completed production part approval processes with leading Tier 1 customers and is actively transitioning its technology into mass production.
Geography: Based in Austin, Texas, the company operates within the global automotive and mobility supply chain.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play entity, it focuses its entire business strategy and product portfolio exclusively on the development of advanced radar perception technology.

points.name: Arbe
points.description: Israeli automotive radar startup developing ultra-high-resolution 4D imaging radar chipsets for on-device autonomous vehicle perception.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops high-resolution 4D imaging radar chipsets and perception software for autonomous vehicles and industrial machines. It supplies radar system-on-chip components and integrated software to tier-1 suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. Its technology processes dense sensor data at the edge to provide AI-ready inputs for central compute and sensor fusion systems.
1. A sensor maker that builds radar chipsets and software for autonomous driving and industrial autonomy, sold to automotive suppliers and OEMs.
2. 4D imaging radar system-on-chip components utilizing digital beamforming and high-density virtual channel arrays to generate ultra-high-resolution point clouds.
3. High-resolution 3D perception, long-range object detection and dense point-cloud generation in adverse weather and low-light conditions.
4. Radar chipsets, software tools and sensor integration toolboxes sold to tier-1 suppliers and industrial OEMs.
5. Advanced driver-assist systems, autonomous vehicles, off-highway industrial hauling, agriculture and mining.
6. Tier-1 automotive suppliers, vehicle original equipment manufacturers and industrial machine builders.
7. Its radar chipsets are integrated by tier-1 suppliers into sensor modules for automotive and industrial OEMs.
8. Its sensor resolution provides 100 times more detail than conventional automotive radars, producing dense detections without overloading central compute systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its radar technology is integrated into the NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion platform and used by tier-1 supplier Sensrad.
Organization type: A publicly traded company listed on NASDAQ and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
Business model: Chipset sales and support and maintenance agreements with automotive and industrial suppliers.
Scale and maturity: A publicly traded company targeting a global automotive radar market projected to reach $11 billion, with offices in China, Germany, the United States and Israel.
Geography: Based in Tel Aviv, Israel with offices in China, Germany and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and edge perception hardware and software for autonomous systems is its entire focus.

points.name: NOVELIC
points.description: Automotive technology company building mmWave radar sensors for in-cabin monitoring and surround perception systems.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops mmWave radar sensing platforms and embedded perception systems for on-device processing in automotive applications, delivering integrated radio frequency hardware, digital signal processing software, and machine learning models to Tier 1 suppliers and vehicle manufacturers.
1. A sensor maker that builds mmWave radar sensors and radar software development platforms sold as hardware modules, custom sensor subsystems, and licensed software to automakers and their suppliers.
2. Millimeter-wave radar sensing platforms with planar antenna intellectual property, radar digital signal processing libraries, and deep learning algorithms for multimodal sensor fusion.
3. Child presence detection, seat occupancy monitoring, intrusion and proximity alerts, blind spot detection, lane change assist, collision warning, cross-traffic alerts, 360-degree surround awareness, park assist, and human presence detection.
4. Hardware sensors, custom radar subsystems, and licensed radar software libraries delivered to vehicle manufacturers and their Tier 1 suppliers.
5. Passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, two- and three-wheeled vehicles, truck coupling assistance, and smart lighting control.
6. Tier 1 automotive suppliers, original equipment manufacturers, and industrial lighting companies.
7. Its radar sensors and custom subsystems are designed into vehicles and driver-assist products by automotive manufacturers and their suppliers.
8. It differentiates through proprietary planar antenna intellectual property, AUTOSAR compliance, functional safety support, and deep expertise in multimodal sensor fusion.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborated with Firefly on a mmWave radar-based human presence detection solution and designed custom 79 GHz radar sensor technology for VBG Coupling's truck coupling assistance product.
Organization type: A privately held technology company with a subsidiary established for international market expansion.
Business model: Hardware sensor sales, custom engineering services, and licensed software platforms.
Scale and maturity: An established provider with an expanding geographic footprint, evidenced by its recent international subsidiary expansion into the Indian market.
Geography: Headquartered in Europe with an expanding global presence and operations in India through a subsidiary.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on automotive radar and embedded sensing technology, encompassing complete hardware design, software frameworks, and AI-based annotation.

points.name: Arbe Robotics
points.description: Israeli automotive radar startup developing high-resolution 4D imaging radar chips that process sensor data on-device for autonomous vehicles.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops ultra-high-resolution 4D imaging radar chipsets and perception solutions for autonomous vehicles and industrial machines. The organization builds a complete radar stack including proprietary radio frequency chips, radar processing chips, and high-density antennas that generate detailed point clouds for environmental mapping. It supplies these components to automotive manufacturers, Tier-1 suppliers, and industrial OEMs for integration into autonomous driving and off-highway systems.
1. A sensor maker that builds 4D imaging radar chipsets and radar processing chips sold to automotive manufacturers and Tier-1 suppliers.
2. Massive MIMO radio frequency technology with ultra-high virtual channel counts and a dedicated radar processing chip that generates dense point clouds at high frame rates.
3. Ultra-high-resolution 4D perception, detailed object classification, road geometry mapping, false-alarm elimination, and 360-degree environmental awareness in adverse weather.

points.name: RadSee Technologies

points.description: Semiconductor company designing CMOS image sensors and AI processors for on-device visual perception.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that develops CMOS image sensors, neuromorphic event sensors, and ultra-low-power AI video processors for edge and physical AI applications. It supplies the perception silicon, including ASICs with integrated neural processing units, that machine makers build into their autonomous systems. Its components target automotive driver monitoring, machine vision, robotics, and other perception-driven markets.
1. A chip company that designs image sensors and embedded AI video processors, sold as semiconductor components to device makers.
2. CMOS and hybrid event-based image sensors, alongside neural processing units integrated into automotive application-specific integrated circuits for on-device inference.
3. High-resolution image capture, global shutter perception, microsecond-accuracy event detection, and on-device deep learning inference for eye gaze and eye tracking.
4. Chips, sensors, and processors delivered to systems integrators and device manufacturers for integration into camera modules and autonomous machines.
5. Advanced driver assistance systems, driver and occupant monitoring systems, robotics, drones, industrial machine vision, and mobile devices.
6. Automotive systems integrators, robot makers, machine vision equipment manufacturers, and consumer electronics device makers.
7. Its chips and sensors are designed into camera modules and autonomous systems by downstream device manufacturers.
8. It combines standard CMOS imaging with acquired neuromorphic event sensor technology and integrated AI processing to deliver full-stack perception silicon.

Organization type: Subsidiary of a publicly traded semiconductor company.
Business model: Semiconductor component sales.

Geography: A globally operating company that ships hardware worldwide and develops automotive imaging standards.

points.name: iBionext
points.description: Venture studio financing and incubating startups building on-device processing and bio-inspired physical automation systems.

A venture studio that finances and incubates startups building edge inference silicon, neuromorphic perception sensors, and on-device intelligence for healthcare and industrial innovators.
1. A venture capital firm and startup studio that founds, incubates, and funds physical AI and edge silicon companies.
2. The portfolio companies develop bio-inspired edge inference processors and neuromorphic event-based perception sensors.
3. The funded companies deliver low-power on-device inference and energy-efficient neuromorphic perception for physical automation.
4. The organization provides venture capital funding, early-stage incubation, and operational support to hardware and robotics startups.
5. The funded technologies are used in healthcare applications and energy-efficient industrial automation.
6. The organization backs healthcare innovators and industrial technology startups.

points.name: 360 Capital

A venture capital firm that invests in early-stage technology companies, with its physical AI exposure coming from backing neuromorphic vision sensor makers that supply components for robotic perception. It provides funding to startup founders and technology companies rather than developing technology directly.

2. It provides capital to startups, and its portfolio companies supply sensors to robot and device makers.

points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: It earns returns through venture capital fund management and equity investments in startups.

points.name: Aramco

A corporate venture capital firm that funds edge and physical AI startups, backing software for edge orchestration, neurosymbolic AI, and runtime security, as well as robotics, mobility, and deep-tech companies, to modernize industrial operations for its energy-conglomerate parent.

2. Edge orchestration, neurosymbolic AI, and runtime security for industrial deployments.
3. It funds startups and connects them to industrial deployment opportunities within its parent company's global energy operations.
4. It leverages a vast global energy operational footprint to provide portfolio companies direct pathways to pilot, deploy, and scale technologies in real-world industrial environments.

Organization type: A corporate venture capital arm and growth fund under a publicly traded global energy conglomerate.

points.name: Bosch Ventures

A corporate venture capital firm that invests in deep-tech startups developing edge AI, automation software, sensors, and electric motion components, providing growth capital and co-innovation access for its portfolio companies.

points.name: Thales

points.name: University of Zurich
points.description: Swiss research institution developing event-based vision algorithms and on-device perception for autonomous drones and robots.

A university research lab that develops neuromorphic perception algorithms, event-camera datasets, drone control frameworks, and neuromorphic processors for edge and physical AI, serving the academic and industrial robotics ecosystem.

3. High-speed obstacle detection, event-based SLAM, 4D dynamic scene reconstruction, visual-inertial odometry, low-latency drone navigation, and neuromorphic on-device inference.

5. Autonomous vehicles, aerial drones, quadruped robots, and wearable assistive devices.
6. Academic researchers, robotics engineers, and autonomous systems developers.

Organization type: A public university research lab.

points.name: CIS
points.description: Technology company providing IoT and robotics software solutions for general digital transformation.

A technology company that co-develops structured-light 3D sensing evaluation kits using event-based vision sensors and embedded AI processing, while primarily operating as a general software development and IT consultancy vendor.

2. Structured light 3D sensing and point cloud generation using event-based vision sensors paired with embedded AI processing platforms.

5. The organization serves clients seeking general digital transformation, business software services, and embedded sensing evaluation.

points.name: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
points.description: Saudi research institution developing autonomous robotic systems and testing real-time physical AI in dedicated facilities.
aliases: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
points.bullets:
A research university that develops neuromorphic computing hardware and event-based vision sensors, and operates a robotics research facility for physical AI and autonomous systems. It builds memristor-based circuit systems for encoding and processing asynchronous event camera data, and provides testing infrastructure for multi-agent robotics and advanced air mobility research. Its work serves national digital transformation agendas in sectors including autonomous mobility, smart cities, logistics, agriculture, inspection, and defense.
1. A university research lab that builds neuromorphic memristor circuits and event-based vision processing hardware, and provides a robotics testing facility for researchers and industry partners.
2. Memristor-based reservoir circuits utilizing memristor arrays as non-linear dynamic nodes for feature extraction from event streams, combining spiking neural network and reservoir computing principles.
3. Energy-efficient asynchronous event camera data encoding and processing, and platform-level testing infrastructure including motion-capture systems, indoor positioning, and flight zones for multi-agent experiments.
4. Research outputs and specialized testing facilities provided through academic collaborations and partnerships with national stakeholders.
5. Autonomous mobility, smart cities, advanced infrastructure, logistics, agriculture, inspection, defense, and advanced air mobility testbeds.

8. It bridges theoretical research and real-world application through interdisciplinary collaboration and a purpose-built facility aligning with national economic diversification goals.

points.name: University of Pennsylvania General Robotics, Automation, Sensing and Perception (GRASP) Lab

points.name: XELA

A sensor maker that develops tactile sensing systems and processing software that give robots a sense of touch for adaptable automation. points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware and software system sales combined with service and know-how.

points.name: National Instruments
points.description: Software and hardware company providing test, measurement, and control platforms for physical automation and robotics.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that provides graphical programming environments, modular hardware, and machine vision software for engineers to build, test, and deploy physical control and robotic systems.
1. A developer tools company that builds graphical programming, machine vision, and test automation software, sold as licensed software suites and embedded hardware modules.
2. A graphical programming environment with libraries for image acquisition, sensor fusion, deep learning model imports, and drivers for sensors and actuators deployed on real-time and FPGA hardware.
3. Machine vision development, multi-sensor fusion, test automation, robotic system design, and embedded control for physical hardware.
4. Licensed software suites, development modules, and embedded microprocessor hardware.
5. Industrial automation, robotic prototyping, exoskeletons, and laboratory or factory test systems.
6. Industrial automation teams, hardware validation engineers, and academic robotics researchers.
7. Its software and hardware platforms are used by engineers and researchers to build and deploy their own physical control systems and robots.
8. It combines a graphical programming environment for sensor and actuator integration with a domain-specific large language model trained on decades of test and measurement expertise for context-aware code generation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Emerson Electric acquired the organization, and it co-developed an exoskeleton platform with Fourier and the University of Melbourne.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Software licenses and hardware module sales.
Scale and maturity: A well-established enterprise with decades of operational history, acquired in an $8.2 billion transaction.
Geography: Based in the USA and operates globally across industrial, academic, and field deployment contexts.
Beyond physical AI: Its core business encompasses broad test, measurement, and validation software systems used throughout global industrial manufacturing.

points.name: Optotune
points.description: Optical technology company building electrically tunable lenses and beam steering systems for robotic vision and physical automation.
points.bullets:
A sensor and optical component maker that develops electrically tunable liquid lenses, fast steering mirrors, and current controllers for machine vision systems, selling to automation equipment manufacturers and robotics builders.
1. An optical component supplier that builds tunable liquid lenses and beam steering mirrors sold as modules and components.
2. Electromagnetically actuated fluid lenses and voice-coil-driven mirrors that adjust focal length or beam direction in milliseconds without mechanical moving parts.
3. Millisecond autofocus, large working-distance range adjustments, high-speed beam deflection, and image stabilization for dynamic vision systems.
4. Optical components, mounted lens modules, and current controllers sold to original equipment manufacturers.
5. Machine vision systems, robotic perception, handheld vision systems, factory automation, and medical devices.
6. Automation equipment manufacturers, robotics builders, camera makers, and original design manufacturers.
7. Its optical components are integrated into machine vision cameras and robotic perception systems built by device manufacturers.
8. Liquid lens technology enables millisecond autofocus and billions of focus cycles with no mechanical wear, reducing size, weight, and power consumption compared to traditional mechanical focusing systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its tunable lenses integrate with cameras from Basler and serve customers including Cognex, Qisda, and Frey Medical.
Organization type: A privately held optical components manufacturer.
Business model: Component and module sales, plus customized optical solutions for high-volume manufacturing.
Scale and maturity: A mature, high-volume manufacturing enterprise that has shipped over two million units globally and holds over 200 patents.
Geography: Based globally with an in-house manufacturing footprint, supplying international robotics, automation, and consumer electronics markets.
Beyond physical AI: Developing light control technologies and adaptive optics for machine vision and physical automation is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: SenseTime
points.description: Chinese AI company building simulation platforms and world models to train intelligent robots for physical tasks.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds embodied intelligence platforms, world models, and multimodal foundation models for physical world applications such as humanoids, quadrupeds, and autonomous vehicles. The company creates native multimodal architectures and computer vision platforms that enable environmental recognition, spatial understanding, and task-level interaction for intelligent agents. It serves the smart robotics, autonomous vehicle, and advanced perception system industries by supplying the critical software, models, and perception layers necessary for physical automation.
1. An AI model developer whose embodied intelligence platforms and multimodal foundation models run on other companies' robots and vehicles.
2. Native multimodal architectures using patch embedding, 3D rotary position encoding, and native multi-head attention to fuse vision and language deeply inside the model, alongside world models and simulation environments for generating training data.
3. Spatial understanding, task-level embodied interaction, environmental recognition, path planning, camera and lidar perception, sensor fusion, behavior prediction, HD mapping, vehicle control, and natural-language interaction.
4. Embodied intelligence platforms, foundation models, and autonomy software licensed to robot and vehicle makers, plus simulation infrastructure and computer vision modules.
5. Humanoids, quadrupeds, autonomous vehicles, and smart city infrastructure.
6. Robot makers, automakers, and entities requiring advanced physical automation and autonomous mobility.
7. Its models and perception software are integrated by robot and vehicle makers into their physical machines.
8. It uses native multimodality built directly into the model architecture rather than bolting language extensions onto existing large language models, drawing on deep roots in computer vision and autonomous driving.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SAIC IM for verifying intelligent driving world models, Softbank Vision Fund as an investor, and affiliated ventures spun out by its co-founder.
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses, platform subscriptions, and enterprise AI infrastructure services.
Scale and maturity: A massive AI company with an established footprint in the industry, showcasing next-generation platforms at major 2025 artificial intelligence conferences.
Geography: Based in China, operating primarily in China and actively showcasing platforms at regional industry conferences.
Beyond physical AI: The organization develops and integrates broad enterprise artificial intelligence infrastructure, including large-scale computing centers and multimodal foundation models for large-scale urban infrastructure and surveillance.

points.name: Mech-Mind Robotics
points.description: Chinese robotics technology company equipping industrial robotic arms with 3D vision and AI software for automated factory tasks.

A sensor maker and vision systems provider that develops 3D cameras, AI-powered vision software and integrated perception solutions to guide industrial robotic arms in factory automation.

2. Industrial 3D cameras with proprietary optical designs for ambient light resistance and highly reflective small parts, paired with self-developed AI algorithms for object recognition and task planning.
3. 3D perception, object recognition, task planning, bin picking and de-palletizing for complex industrial robotics tasks.
4. 3D cameras, software development kits, and all-in-one AI and 3D vision solutions integrated with third-party robotic arms.
5. Factories, warehouses, automotive, electronics, logistics, electric vehicle battery, metalworking, home appliance and semiconductor settings.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, and industrial automation systems integrators, including Fortune Global 500 companies.

points.name: OrCam
