1. A venture capital firm that funds sensor makers and robotics companies.
2. It provides capital to 3D sensor developers and industrial robotics makers.
3. It targets financial backing across both foundational 3D sensor technologies and deployed robotic systems.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held venture capital and private equity investment firm.
Business model: Fund management and venture capital investment returns.
Scale and maturity: An established investment firm with a history of participating in funding rounds for emerging technology companies.
Geography: Based in Hong Kong and deploying capital primarily across Asian technology developers.
Beyond physical AI: The firm maintains a broader focus on investing across various technology and enterprise sectors.

points.name: RVMC Vietnam Co., Ltd.
points.location: Thuan Thanh I Industrial Park, Bac Ninh, Vietnam
points.description: Vietnamese manufacturing subsidiary building 3D vision sensors that enable robotic perception and on-device inference.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that manufactures 3D vision sensors and smart hardware for edge AI inference, operating as a Vietnamese manufacturing subsidiary of its parent company to produce camera sensors for robotics and industrial automation providers.
1. A sensor maker that builds 3D vision sensors and structured-light cameras, sold as camera components and subsystems to robot makers.
2. Stereo cameras and structured-light cameras optimized for edge AI inference, integrated with neural processing platforms and on-device AI software for depth perception.
3. 3D perception, depth perception for transparent or reflective object detection, and spatially-aware inference for robotic manipulation and navigation.
4. Camera sensors and smart hardware components shipped to robotics companies for integration into their machines.
5. Humanoid robots, warehouse robotics, logistics automation, precision assembly, and general industrial automation.
6. Robotics companies, industrial automation providers, and manufacturers of robotic vision systems.
7. Its 3D vision sensors are designed into robots and automation systems by over 1,600 device makers globally.
8. Its sensors are integrated with edge AI inference platforms using CUDA and TensorRT acceleration and paired with on-device AI software that handles difficult depth perception challenges like transparent or reflective object detection.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Robot Vision Manufacturing Company Pte. Ltd. in Singapore, operating as a manufacturing base for Orbbec Inc. and integrated with NVIDIA Jetson Orin platforms.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary functioning as a strategic manufacturing hub for its parent company.
Business model: Hardware sales of 3D vision sensors and smart camera components to robotics and industrial automation companies.
Scale and maturity: A scaling manufacturer with a planned 100,000-square-meter facility scheduled to commence full operations in 2027 to support an annual manufacturing capacity exceeding 6 million robotic vision units.
Geography: Based in Thuan Thanh Industrial Park in Bac Ninh Province, Vietnam, operating as an overseas manufacturing base targeting global deployment.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire operational focus is dedicated to the production and advancement of robotic vision sensors and smart hardware for edge AI, robotics, and physical automation.

points.name: Olive Robotics GmbH
points.description: German deep-tech startup building embedded AI sensors and software for real-time robotic perception.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that builds AI-enabled, ROS-native sensors, actuators and embedded compute modules for robotics, delivering modular perception and motion subsystems to integrators and robot builders.
1. A component supplier that makes intelligent sensors, controllers and mobile robot bases sold as modular hardware for integration into robotic systems.
2. Embedded AI modules and sensors, including IMUs, vision cameras and connectivity hardware, built on a DDS-compliant ROS 2 architecture with on-sensor fusion.
3. On-device perception, multi-modal sensor fusion, real-time motion sensing, low-latency control and autonomous navigation for mobile platforms.
4. Modules, sensors, controllers and mobile robot bases delivered as plug-and-play components for robotic platforms.
5. Industrial automation, logistics, medical robotics, autonomous vehicles and outdoor robotic systems.
6. System integrators, original equipment manufacturers and research and development labs.
7. Its modular components are designed into robotic systems by device makers and system integrators.
8. It embeds AI-driven sensor fusion directly at the hardware level with native middleware integration, eliminating the need for software drivers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Technical University of Munich, NVIDIA Inception, Resense GmbH, Open Source Robotics Alliance and investor S&F SmartTec.
Organization type: A privately held startup and university spin-off.
Business model: Hardware and component sales.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company founded in 2022 with one million euros in pre-seed funding.
Geography: Based in Munich-Ottobrunn, Germany, operating predominantly within European robotics and industrial automation ecosystems.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation are its entire commercial focus.

points.name: Contoro Robotics
points.description: US robotics startup deploying AI-powered robots for automating trailer and container unloading in warehouses.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and deploys complete robotic unloading systems for warehouse logistics, combining its own proprietary software and end-effectors with third-party robotic arms to automate the unloading of floor-loaded trailers and shipping containers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete AI-powered trailer-unloading robots.
2. The system uses customer-specific foundation models for perception and motion planning, a proprietary two-point articulated suction end-effector, and a human-in-the-loop teleoperation platform for remote oversight of edge cases.
3. It delivers autonomous unloading of multi-SKU floor-loaded boxes, grasping of varied box sizes up to 80 pounds, and remote human teleoperation to achieve over 99% reliability.
4. Customers get the complete robotic unloading system through a pay-per-container pricing model that reduces upfront capital costs.
5. It is used in warehouses, distribution centers, and e-commerce fulfillment hubs for logistics operations.
6. It sells to logistics operators, e-commerce companies, and supply chain operations dealing with labor-intensive trailer unloading.
7. The company builds its own proprietary end-effectors and software, which it integrates with third-party industrial robotic arms to operate the complete robotic systems in customer warehouses.
8. Its patented two-point suction end-effector and human-in-the-loop AI approach enable reliable handling of varied box sizes on day one without requiring months of preliminary training.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It uses third-party industrial robotic arms from Kuka, counts Coupang and States Logistics as collaborators and investors, and is backed by the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, Doosan, IMM, SV Investment, KB Investment, Kakao Ventures, and Future Play.
Organization type: It is a privately held startup and a spinoff from Harmonic Bionics.
Business model: It makes money through a pay-per-container pricing model for its unloading services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2022, the startup has raised $22 million in total funding, including a $12 million Series A round, and has autonomously unloaded over 100 trailers.
Geography: It is based in Austin, Texas, USA, and actively deploys its robotic systems within U.S. warehouses.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is the organization's absolute core, strictly limited to warehouse automation and logistics with no presence outside this domain.

points.name: Futurail
points.description: Franco-German autonomous systems startup developing safety-certified hardware and software stacks for autonomous train operations.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds and integrates a safety-certified autonomy stack and multi-sensor hardware for autonomous trains, serving both passenger and freight rail operators.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving train stack and provides hardware integration for new and existing rail vehicles.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software and EN50155-certified multi-sensor computing units providing long-range obstacle detection, high-precision localization, and intelligent train control.
3. Fully autonomous train operations, long-range obstacle detection, high-precision localization, speed management, emergency braking, and remote monitoring.
4. Licensed autonomy software, remote operations software, and integrated multi-sensor hardware systems for new or retrofit installations.
5. Passenger and freight trains, mainline railways, branch lines, and depot operations.
6. Passenger and freight rail operators.
7. Its autonomy stacks and sensor systems are integrated into rail vehicles by train makers.
8. It differentiates through a founding team with autonomous vehicle expertise, alignment with European rail safety frameworks, and the flexibility to retrofit existing fleets or integrate into new vehicles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It counts EIT Urban Mobility as an investor, Lohr as a design partner, and provides perception technology for Parallel Systems.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses, system integration services, and hardware integration.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023, the company secured €7.5 million in early-stage funding and is expanding its workforce from 15 to 30 employees with active field trials.
Geography: The company is based in Strasbourg and Munich and operates primarily in Europe and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Developing autonomous systems for rail is the entire focus of this pure-play organization.

points.name: Andrenam
points.description: US maritime sensing startup deploying AI-powered passive acoustic buoys for real-time undersea surveillance.
points.bullets:
A defense and maritime operator and systems integrator that builds and operates distributed networks of passive acoustic sensing buoys, autonomous swarm drones, and AI signal processing software for persistent undersea domain awareness. It delivers maritime surveillance and threat detection as a managed sensing service, selling persistent coverage rather than hardware.
1. An operator and systems integrator that builds acoustic sensor buoys and autonomous underwater drones and operates them as a managed sensing service.
2. Hydrophone arrays, modular passive sonar systems, and edge AI signal processing software that detect, track, and classify surface and subsurface maritime targets.
3. Persistent passive acoustic monitoring, real-time target classification, undersea threat detection, and autonomous drone swarm coordination.
4. A contractor-owned, contractor-operated managed sensing service that provides persistent coverage rather than selling hardware outright.
5. Subsea monitoring defense networks, naval operations, port security, critical infrastructure, and commercial maritime environments.
6. Defense forces, homeland security agencies, port security operators, and commercial maritime operators.
7. It designs, builds, owns, and operates its own sensor networks and drones, selling surveillance coverage directly to end users.
8. It delivers an AI-native, lower-cost alternative to legacy sonar approaches, turning raw acoustic data into actionable intelligence for operators without specialized sonar experience.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Upfront Ventures, Valor Equity Partners, Also Capital, First Round Capital, Mines Venture Fund, the U.S. Navy, NavalX, and NW Tech Bridge.
Organization type: A privately held dual-use technology startup.
Business model: Managed sensing service contracts where customers purchase persistent maritime surveillance coverage.
Scale and maturity: A startup founded in 2024 that has built over 35 sensor units across three hardware generations, logged more than 4,500 in-water hours, and raised $30 million in total funding.
Geography: Based in Los Angeles and operating across defense and commercial maritime environments.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, maritime robotics, and physical automation represent the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Archetype AI
points.description: US physical AI startup building foundation models that interpret multimodal sensor data to help machines understand and act in the real world.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds foundation models fusing multimodal sensor data with natural language for industrial physical AI, offering the models via an edge-capable platform for enterprises.
1. An AI model developer whose physical foundation models run on enterprise edge and on-premises hardware.
2. A 2.0-billion-parameter multimodal foundation model that unifies human language and time-series sensor data using universal tokens.
3. Multimodal sensor fusion and natural-language interpretation of complex physical patterns and sensor data.
4. Cloud APIs, edge-deployable foundation models, and a no-code developer platform with APIs.
5. Manufacturing, construction, supply chain logistics, automotive, telecommunications and smart city infrastructure.
6. Industrial enterprises across construction, electronics, automotive, logistics and retail.
7. Its models and development platform are integrated by enterprises into their own physical AI solutions and sensor deployments.
8. It trains foundation models on diverse physical sensor data rather than text or vision alone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, Comcast LIFT Labs and former Google machine learning teams.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Platform and model licensing, subscriptions and APIs.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023 with 11 to 50 employees and $35 million in Series A funding.
Geography: Headquartered in San Mateo, California, operating locally with United States-based municipalities and industrial enterprises.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, robotics and physical automation are its entire focus.

points.name: StirlingX
points.description: United Kingdom autonomous systems startup building drones and sensor platforms that analyze physical environments for defense autonomy.
points.bullets:
A drone and autonomous systems maker that designs and manufactures unmanned aerial vehicles paired with AI-driven data analytics and resilient communications to capture and interpret sensor data in complex physical environments. It builds complete deployed platforms that act in the physical world, selling to organizations operating critical national infrastructure and defense settings.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that builds and sells autonomous drones and integrated intelligence platforms for defense and infrastructure customers.
2. Automated drone platforms, resilient communications, and AI-driven software that process aerial and sensor data into actionable insights through a proprietary Data Fabric.
3. Autonomous data collection, sensor data analysis, environment interpretation, and delivery of data-backed decision-support across an asset portfolio.
4. Complete drones and a unified intelligence platform sold as integrated deployed systems rather than individual components.
5. Critical national infrastructure, defense, military and civil operations, and cyber and electromagnetic battlespace.
6. Organizations operating critical infrastructure, defense forces, and state institutions.
7. It builds complete deployed platforms that act directly in the physical world rather than supplying individual components like silicon or actuators.
8. Its deep expertise in the Cyber and Electromagnetic battlespace uniquely combines physical autonomous drone platforms with electronic warfare and spectrum-control knowledge.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It was founded and incubated within GALLOS Technologies and aligns its operations with the UK's recent Strategic Defence Review.
Organization type: A privately held startup founded and based in the United Kingdom.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of drone platforms and software systems for defense and infrastructure applications.
Scale and maturity: A newly established early-stage organization founded in 2024 that began its operations in the same year.
Geography: It is based in the United Kingdom and aligns its operations there.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond its physical artificial intelligence offerings, the broader company profile encompasses data-backed decision support and specialized instruction in Cyber Electromagnetic Activities for state institutions.

points.name: Perciv AI
points.description: Dutch radar AI startup enhancing affordable radar sensors with perception software for autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds radar-first perception software for autonomous vehicles and robots. The organization processes raw radar data through AI algorithms to deliver LiDAR-like 3D perception at lower cost, licensing its stack to automakers, robot makers, and industrial system integrators.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses radar-perception and radar-camera fusion stacks to automakers and robot makers.
2. Neural networks that process raw radar data and fuse it with camera inputs on lightweight edge compute to generate 3D perception, odometry, and object tracking.
3. Ego-motion estimation, free-space detection, object classification and tracking, and radar-camera sensor fusion for all-weather, GPS-denied environmental perception.
4. Licensed software modules and preconfigured hardware kits that integrate into existing autonomous vehicle and robotics stacks.
5. Autonomous cars, delivery robots, drones, airport operations, smart traffic infrastructure, warehouse logistics, agriculture, and defense systems.
6. Automakers, industrial robotics firms, micro-mobility providers, drone manufacturers, airport operators, and defense organizations.
7. Its perception software is integrated into the autonomy stacks of vehicle and robot makers.
8. It transforms low-cost radar data into high-resolution perception that matches LiDAR accuracy while maintaining superior performance in adverse weather like rain, fog, and darkness.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Day One Capital Ventures and Keen Venture Partners participated in its seed funding round.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and hardware kit sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2023, the early-stage company employs 20 people and grew to 19 customers within a year of its seed round.
Geography: Based in the Netherlands, it deploys autonomous perception solutions across Europe and broader global markets.
Beyond physical AI: Delivering AI-driven perception platforms for autonomous systems is its entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Tycho AI Inc.
points.description: US autonomous systems startup building onboard AI hardware and software for self-navigating drones in GPS-denied environments.
points.bullets:
An autonomous systems startup that builds mission-critical autonomy software and mission-optimized compute hardware for unmanned aerial systems operating in GPS-denied and communications-contested environments. It serves defense and security sectors requiring resilient, on-device AI for intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, counter-UAS operations, and autonomous swarming.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving flight stack and supplies proprietary compute hardware integrating ASIC and FPGA processors for unmanned aerial vehicles.
2. Multi-modal sensing and advanced machine learning running on proprietary ASIC and FPGA hardware to perform sensor-fusion autonomy software without external navigation aids.
3. Real-time obstacle avoidance, precision navigation, autonomous decision-making, and on-device inference at speeds up to 200 mph in GNSS-denied environments.
4. Integrated hardware and software autonomy stacks and compute subsystems that incorporate directly into unmanned aerial vehicles.
5. Unmanned aerial systems operating in electronic warfare, contested military domains, intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, counter-UAS operations, and autonomous swarming.
6. Government customers, defense forces, and major defense contractors procuring through military innovation initiatives.
7. Its software and compute hardware are integrated into unmanned aerial vehicles by defense platform providers.
8. It delivers resilient, on-device AI inference enabling autonomous navigation, threat detection, and decision-making at speeds up to 200 mph without relying on external navigation aids or persistent connectivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: FirstMark Capital led its Series A funding, and its platform is available through the Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace for government customers.
Organization type: A privately held startup operating at the intersection of academic innovation and operational defense expertise.
Business model: Government contracts, defense procurement, and subsystem sales.
Scale and maturity: A 2022-founded company that closed a $10 million Series A funding round in October 2025 and demonstrates commercial momentum within the domestic defense ecosystem.
Geography: Based in the United States, operating within the domestic defense ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: Developing edge autonomous intelligence for unmanned aerial systems is the organization's entire focus, purpose-built to solve critical capability gaps in electronic warfare and contested military domains.

points.name: AIWaysion Inc
points.description: US edge AI startup developing local computer vision systems for real-time traffic and pedestrian safety analysis.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and edge systems company that builds edge computing sensors, analysis devices, and software for intelligent transportation. It leverages computer vision and sensor fusion to process local data in real time for traffic monitoring, road safety, and smart parking, selling hardware-software subsystems to transportation agencies.
1. A hardware-software subsystem provider that builds edge computing traffic sensors and analysis devices, sold as integrated edge systems and software platforms.
2. Computer vision and multi-sensor fusion algorithms running on localized edge servers to analyze video and road condition data independently of the cloud.
3. Real-time traffic data collection, vehicle classification and speed detection, dilemma zone and traffic conflict event detection, and road surface condition monitoring.
4. Integrated edge computing devices and sensors, alongside AI-powered data generation and analysis software platforms.
5. Smart transportation infrastructure, including intersections, rural roads, parking, and curb management.
6. State and local Departments of Transportation, municipal agencies, international road administrations, and tribal nations.
7. Its edge computing subsystems integrate deployed sensors with existing traffic management infrastructure like signal controllers and communications systems.
8. A specialized edge computing architecture enables real-time, cloud-independent traffic analysis effective in underserved rural areas with limited broadband.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company partners with the University of Washington, the City of Bellevue, the City of Tucson, the Yakama Nation, the Norwegian Public Road Administration, and NYC DOT, and has received SBIR funding from USDOT.
Organization type: A privately held startup and university spin-off.
Business model: Hardware-software subsystem sales and government grants.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2021, it is an early-stage firm with multiple federal Small Business Innovation Research awards and deployments across domestic municipalities and European corridors.
Geography: Based in the Pacific Northwest, it operates nationally across the United States and internationally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical infrastructure, it offers AI-powered transportation planning software that automates data analysis for planning decisions using transportation-standards-informed large language models.

points.name: SentiSystems
points.description: Norwegian sensor processing startup fusing real-time sensor data for on-device navigation in autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
A sensor processing and navigation subsystem provider that builds hardware and software for real-time sensor fusion and GNSS-denied localization for autonomous platforms. It sells sensor synchronization boards, navigation hubs, and associated software to integrators building robots, drones, and autonomous vehicles. Its technology provides the precise positioning and perception foundation required for advanced autonomy in contested or GPS-unavailable environments.
1. A component and software supplier that builds sensor synchronization hardware and navigation software for autonomous platforms.
2. Multi-modal sensor fusion software and hardware that achieves nano-to-microsecond time synchronization across IMU, lidar, cameras, and radar.
3. GNSS-denied navigation, precise positioning, velocity and attitude estimation, sensor health monitoring, and situational awareness.
4. Sensor synchronization boards, navigation hubs, and licensed navigation software.
5. Maritime vessels, zero-emission ferries, unmanned aerial vehicles, ground robotics, space systems, and defense platforms.
6. Autonomy integrators, maritime operators, and defense organizations.
7. Its sensor synchronization and navigation subsystems are integrated into larger autonomous platforms built by vehicle and robot makers.
8. It achieves nano-to-microsecond synchronization precision for multi-modal sensor data to enable reliable navigation when satellite signals are jammed, spoofed, or unavailable.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a development partner for autonomous ferry programs, a member of the Ocean Autonomy Cluster, and a participant in an AI startup program run by NVIDIA.
Organization type: A privately held startup spun out from a Norwegian university.
Business model: Hardware component sales and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A lean early-stage company founded in 2021 with two to ten employees and over a decade of prior university research.
Geography: Based in Norway with a focus on autonomous applications in the Baltic and Northern Europe regions.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are the entire focus and business activity of this pure-play company.

points.name: Hive Robotics
points.description: German robotics startup building modular hardware and software stacks for autonomous unmanned systems.
points.bullets:
A component supplier and autonomy software developer that builds modular command, control, and communication subsystems bundling onboard AI, perception, localization, and secure communications for unmanned systems operating in GPS-denied environments.
1. A component supplier that builds modular hardware and software subsystems for autonomous unmanned systems.
2. Integrated hardware modules and a software orchestration layer combining onboard AI, robot control, perception, localization, and secure communications compatible with existing middleware.
3. Swarm intelligence, collaborative multi-domain teaming, distributed sensor fusion, and resilient operation in GNSS-denied environments.
4. Modular hardware units and integrated software architectures sold to unmanned system makers.
5. Unmanned aerial, ground, maritime, and space vehicles in defense, disaster response, critical infrastructure monitoring, search and rescue, wildfire detection, and maritime security operations.
6. Civil and defense organizations operating mission-critical unmanned systems.
7. Its subsystems integrate into unmanned platforms alongside existing middleware to provide distributed AI and secure communications.
8. It bridges uncertified consumer systems and expensive aerospace-grade solutions with a certifiable, real-time orchestration framework for scalable robotic teaming in GPS-denied environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors include b2venture, Firedrop, Pareto, Klocke Group, and Matthias Hilpert.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware subsystem sales and software integration contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2025, early-stage with €2 million in pre-seed funding, having demonstrated over 3,000 UAV flights and support for vehicles up to 1,000 kilograms.
Geography: Headquartered in Munich, Germany, serving European and global markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire focus of the company's business profile and technology roadmap.

points.name: Humble
points.description: Namibian autonomous vehicles startup building cabless electric freight trucks driven by vision-language-action models.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vehicle maker that builds fully autonomous, cabless, battery-electric Class 8 haulers for commercial freight transportation. It operates as a full-stack deployed systems provider, integrating sensor suites, electric drivetrains, vision-language-action models, and remote operational support into a single end-to-end platform, offering comprehensive freight transport services to logistics and supply chain operators.
1. A vehicle maker that designs and builds fully autonomous, cabless, battery-electric Class 8 haulers and operates them as a full-service freight transport offering.
2. Vision-based artificial intelligence, 360-degree sensor suites, vision-language-action models, and electric drivetrains integrated into a purpose-built autonomous vehicle platform.
3. Autonomous freight transport, 360-degree perception, direct dock-to-dock unloading, and 24/7 remote operational support.
4. Complete autonomous electric vehicles paired with full-service freight transport, remote operational support, and charging.
5. Long-haul freight transport, shipping container movement, warehouses, railyards, and seaports.
6. Market leaders in the logistics and supply chain sector requiring efficient shipping container movement.
7. The company builds and operates its own purpose-built autonomous vehicles to move freight for logistics operators.
8. A purpose-built autonomous platform integrates the tractor, trailer, and driver into a single cabless entity capable of direct dock-to-dock unloading.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Seed funding was led by Eclipse Ventures with participation from Energy Impact Partners.
Organization type: A privately held startup founded in 2026.
Business model: Full-service freight transport services designed to lower per-mile operating costs in the commercial freight industry.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2026, the company recently emerged from stealth with $24 million in seed funding.
Geography: Based in and primarily operates within the United States, targeting the American truck-based freight industry.
Beyond physical AI: The company's entire focus is dedicated to providing autonomous electric freight solutions.

points.name: Society of Automotive Engineers
points.description: US standards organization defining the six levels of autonomous driving.
points.bullets:
A standards organization that develops and publishes technical frameworks for automotive technology, most notably the J3016 standard that defines the six levels of driving automation from Level 0 to Level 5 for automakers and autonomous system developers.
1. A standards body that publishes taxonomy and classification frameworks for autonomous driving systems.
2. A recommended practice framework that categorizes automotive automation into defined levels based on the allocation of driving tasks between human drivers and automated systems.
3. Standardized terminology and classification levels for autonomous driving systems.
4. Published industry standards and recommended practices.
5. Autonomous vehicles and self-driving technology development.
6. Automakers, autonomous vehicle developers, government agencies and hardware platform providers.
7. Its published standards are adopted by autonomous system developers to structure and benchmark their self-driving stacks.
8. Its driving automation taxonomy is the universally adopted industry baseline, codified into government legislation and built around by autonomous vehicle platform providers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its standards are referenced in the BUILD America 250 Act and adopted by the United States Department of Transportation and NVIDIA.
Organization type: A professional standards and engineering organization.
Business model: Membership dues and the sale of published technical standards documents.
Scale and maturity: A long-established global organization whose standards are foundational to the automotive and autonomous vehicle industries.
Geography: Based in the United States with globally adopted standards.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond autonomous driving levels, the organization develops broad engineering standards across mobility industries including aerospace, commercial vehicles and passenger cars.

points.name: Computer Vision Center
points.description: Spanish research institution developing open-source simulation environments for testing autonomous driving and robotics systems.
points.bullets:
A research institution and developer tools provider that co-develops and directs an open-source simulator for training and validating automated driving systems. It builds simulation software that provides virtual urban environments and sensor inputs for academic and industrial researchers developing autonomous vehicle algorithms.
1. A research institution and developer tools company whose open-source simulation platform robotics and autonomous driving engineers use.
2. Open-source urban simulation software that generates flexible environmental conditions, realistic scenarios, and simulated sensor inputs and control outputs for autonomous vehicles.
3. Training, testing, and validation of perception, planning, and control systems using virtual testbeds with configurable sensor suites.
4. Open-source simulation software hosted on public code repositories and integrated with middleware like the Robot Operating System.
5. Autonomous vehicles and urban driving systems.
6. Academic researchers, industrial researchers, and defense agencies developing autonomous systems.
7. Its simulation platform is used by researchers and engineers to develop and validate algorithms before real-world deployment.
8. It provides a non-profit, open-source simulator with realistic urban environments and flexible sensor configuration not always testable in the real world.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Co-developed the simulator with Intel Labs, received funding from Toyota Research Institute, and operates under a Spanish university.
Organization type: An academic research institution housed at and operating under a university.
Business model: Grant funding and research collaborations supporting open-source software development.
Scale and maturity: An established research center with institutional backing and industry partnerships dating to at least 2018.
Geography: Based in Spain with global collaborations involving international research entities and United States defense agencies.
Beyond physical AI: It advances computer vision and artificial intelligence research, with its focus dedicated to developing tools and platforms for autonomous systems.

points.name: SINTEF Digital
points.description: Norwegian research organization developing edge AI perception and sensor fusion systems for autonomous delivery vehicles.
points.bullets:
A research institute that develops integrated edge AI and autonomous systems, building full-stack perception and sensor fusion platforms for physical environments. The organization acts as an advanced systems integrator and research partner, combining sensor selection, algorithm development, and system deployment for industrial clients across demanding real-world settings.
1. A government-supported research organization that builds edge AI perception and sensor fusion platforms for autonomous systems.
2. Sensor fusion and edge AI perception algorithms integrated with selected sensor hardware for autonomous navigation.
3. Perception, sensor fusion, and autonomous navigation for deployment in low-visibility and underwater settings.
4. Applied research partnerships, systems integration, and deployed autonomous platforms.
5. Autonomous last-mile delivery, maritime robotics, industrial inspection, aquaculture, construction, healthcare, and renewable energy.
6. Industrial clients across logistics, maritime, energy, construction, and healthcare sectors.
7. The organization integrates sensors, algorithms, and hardware into deployed autonomous platforms for industrial clients.
8. Deep integration of hardware sensing with AI algorithms and extensive operational experience in demanding real-world environments like underwater or low-visibility settings.
points.profile:
Organization type: A government-supported research institute.
Scale and maturity: One of Norway's largest AI research communities, leveraging over 100 specialized laboratories and having successfully spun out commercial ventures.
Geography: Based in Norway, bridging domestic industry needs with global AI development through cross-border applied partnerships.
Beyond physical AI: The broader organization conducts wide-ranging scientific research and acts as a national technological innovation hub.

points.name: NxTech AS
points.description: Norwegian technology company developing edge AI sensor fusion platforms for autonomous last-mile delivery vehicles.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds AI-based perception and sensor fusion platforms for autonomous last-mile delivery vehicles. The company licenses a software subsystem that performs real-time edge processing and sensor fusion for on-device inference rather than manufacturing vehicles or hardware components. It serves the logistics and last-mile delivery sector for deployments in managed delivery networks and controlled traffic environments.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a perception and sensor fusion software stack to last-mile delivery operators.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software that integrates ultrasound, inertial measurement units, LiDAR, radar and cameras with real-time edge processing algorithms.
3. Autonomous navigation and real-time perception for dense urban delivery routes.
4. Licensed software and algorithmic subsystems integrated into vehicles by delivery operators.
5. Autonomous last-mile delivery vehicles in dense urban environments.
6. Logistics and last-mile delivery operators.
7. Its perception and sensor fusion software is designed into autonomous delivery vehicles by mobility operators.
8. It integrates multiple complementary sensor modalities to solve the specific navigation challenges of dense urban delivery routes with diverse traffic participants.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Norwegian research institutes with which it conducts formal research collaborations to develop and validate its perception platforms.
Organization type: An established privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses and platform development contracts.
Geography: Based in Norway with a development focus on dense urban environments.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, sensor fusion and physical automation are entirely central to the company's overall mission and business operations as a pure-play technology provider.

points.name: Breaker
points.location: Austin, Texas, USA and Sydney, Australia
points.description: Robotics AI startup equipping unmanned vehicles with onboard software for autonomous navigation and natural language control.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds platform-agnostic edge AI agents transforming unmanned systems into autonomous, self-organizing teammates controllable via natural language, primarily for defense and special operations.
1. A software company that builds platform-agnostic edge AI autonomy software and agents, sold as licensed software integrated onto existing unmanned systems.
2. On-device AI agents and a passive 3D localization pipeline that converts 2D camera detections into precise 3D world coordinates without lidar, running sub-second inference entirely onboard without cloud dependency.
3. Single-operator 1:N control of multi-domain robot teams via natural voice commands, autonomous platform coordination, context-aware decision-making, and passive 3D localization in contested environments.
4. Licensed software and edge AI agents integrated onto customers' existing unmanned platforms through standard platform APIs.
5. Air, land, and sea unmanned systems in defense, special operations, search and rescue, mining, agriculture, logistics, and manufacturing.
6. Defense forces, special operations, defense contractors, and autonomous systems manufacturers.
7. Its software is integrated onto existing unmanned platforms and command-and-control systems built by defense hardware makers.
8. It enables sub-second inference and multi-agent coordination entirely on-board without cloud dependency in communications-degraded and contested environments.

points.name: Yaanendriya

It builds MEMS-based sensing hardware, GNSS systems and embedded autonomy software for drones, ground robots, spacecraft and underwater vehicles. Its subsystems deliver state estimation and localization for mission-critical platforms operating where global navigation satellite service is unavailable.
1. A component and subsystem supplier that builds inertial sensors, navigation controllers and compute modules sold to autonomous system manufacturers.
2. MEMS accelerometers, gyroscopes, inertially aided odometry and sensor-fusion algorithms running on embedded navigation controllers.
3. Inertial sensing, GNSS-denied navigation, localization, state estimation and flight control for autonomous platforms.
4. The company delivers physical sensors, compute modules and embedded software components to machine makers.
5. Drones, ground robots, underwater vehicles, satellites, aerospace platforms and mission-critical autonomous systems.
6. Defense forces, aerospace primes, robotics manufacturers and industrial automation providers.
7. Its sensors and controllers are integrated by vehicle and robot manufacturers into their autonomous platforms.
8. Hardware-software co-design focused on operational reliability in GNSS-denied mission-critical environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ARTPARK, the Indian Institute of Science, Piper Serica, Taraba State, IQ Spacecom and the 515 Army Base Workshop.
Organization type: Privately held startup incubated at a university research park.
Business model: Hardware component sales and government non-dilutive grants.

Geography: Based in Bengaluru, India with global deployments.

points.name: Piper Serica

points.name: Autonomous Vehicles sector in Germany

A German industry sector comprising numerous companies that develop autonomous vehicle technologies and enabling subsystems for self-driving. points.name: AMI Labs

2. Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture, including vision-language variants, using self-supervised learning to predict physical environment states rather than generate tokens.

4. Models intended for integration into autonomous agentic systems.
5. Autonomous agentic systems.
6. Developers of autonomous agentic systems.
7. Its models are intended to be integrated by developers into their autonomous systems.
8. It pursues a fundamental research approach to world models based on predicting physical environment states rather than generating tokens.
