Geography: Based in the United States, with dominant market presence in North America and systems deployed globally.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play surgical robotics company where physical AI and robotic automation are its entire focus, dedicated to enhancing human surgical capabilities rather than pursuing fully autonomous operations.

points.name: Swisslog
points.description: Swiss automation company deploying warehouse robots and software for real-time inventory handling.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator that designs, builds, and installs complete warehouse, distribution, and healthcare automation systems, combining autonomous mobile robots, automated storage and retrieval systems, and software orchestration for retail, e-commerce, grocery, and pharmaceutical customers.
1. A systems integrator that builds and installs complete warehouse automation systems and robotic intralogistics solutions for retailers and logistics operators.
2. Automated guided vehicles using 2D SLAM for localization, automated storage and retrieval systems, robotic case and item picking mechanisms, and software for warehouse management and execution.
3. Goods-to-person automation, autonomous pallet transport, high bay warehousing, high-density pallet storage, and fleet orchestration of mixed automated and manual operations.
4. Integrated automation systems, complete robotic installations, and software platforms installed in customer warehouses, distribution centers, and hospitals.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers, fulfillment centers, and hospitals.
6. Retailers, e-commerce companies, grocery operators, consumer goods distributors, pharmaceutical companies, and healthcare organizations.
7. It designs and installs complete automation systems built from its own mobile robots and storage systems integrated into customer facilities.
8. It reliably orchestrates mixed fleets of both legacy and modern automation equipment at an enterprise scale.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Subsidiary of KUKA, with partnerships with Berkshire Grey and customers including Asda and Master Electronics.
Organization type: Privately held corporate subsidiary.
Business model: Integration services, hardware sales, and software licenses.
Scale and maturity: A global organization founded in 1900 with over 2,000 integrated installations across more than 50 countries and over 14,000 employees.
Geography: Based in Switzerland and operating globally across more than 50 countries.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI, robotics, and physical automation form the absolute core of the organization's mission, driving its end-to-end fulfillment systems and material handling operations.

points.name: Samsung Research
points.description: Technology company developing compact on-device inference models and edge AI processors for smart home appliances.
points.bullets:
A corporate research division of a global technology conglomerate that develops edge AI silicon, on-device inference software, and intelligent robot systems for consumer applications.
1. A corporate research division that designs edge inference silicon, on-device AI models, and complete consumer robot prototypes for a parent technology conglomerate.
2. Neural processing units, on-device inference models, and computer vision software integrated into consumer IoT devices and appliances.
3. On-device inference, computer vision, intelligent physical assistance, and environment perception for connected home devices.
4. Research outputs and prototype robots transferred to internal consumer electronics business units for commercialization.
5. Smart home appliances, mobile terminals, connected physical devices, and consumer robots for homes, factories, and offices.
6. Internal consumer electronics business units and smart home appliance divisions within the parent conglomerate.
7. Its research outputs and prototypes are transferred to internal hardware divisions that manufacture and sell consumer devices.
8. It vertically integrates efficient AI models and edge computing technologies directly into a vast ecosystem of deployed consumer appliances and IoT devices.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operates as the advanced research arm of Samsung Electronics.
Organization type: A corporate research division of a publicly traded global technology conglomerate.
Business model: Funded internally by its parent technology conglomerate to secure foundational software and hardware technologies.
Scale and maturity: An established corporate research division leveraging the massive scale, manufacturing infrastructure, and global footprint of a mature parent company.
Geography: Based in South Korea and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: It is part of a broader conglomerate whose overarching business encompasses mobile devices, home electronics, semiconductor manufacturing, and digital appliances.

points.name: Bosch Research
points.location: Stuttgart, Germany; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; San Francisco, California, USA
points.description: German research and technology company developing sensors, control systems, and industrial AI for physical automation and robotics.
points.bullets:
The research and development arm of a multinational engineering conglomerate that develops physical AI and edge computing technologies, acting as a component supplier for sensors and actuators, a software platform provider for on-device inference, and a systems integrator for automated solutions across mobility and industrial sectors.
1. A corporate research lab that develops manipulation, autonomous driving, and human-robot interaction technologies and builds foundational components, subsystems, and software platforms for internal commercialization and external partners.
2. Manipulation algorithms, autonomous driving stacks, human-robot interaction software, acoustic monitoring instruments, sensors, actuators, and on-device inference platforms designed for safe and explainable industrial AI.
3. Robotic manipulation, autonomous driving, human-robot interaction, acoustic monitoring, on-device inference, and systems integration for physical automation.
4. Components, subsystems, software platforms, and integrated automated solutions delivered to product divisions and commercial partners.
5. Industrial automation, mobility and automotive systems, space station monitoring, consumer goods, and building technologies.
6. Internal product divisions of its parent conglomerate, automotive manufacturers, industrial technology providers, and aerospace partners.
7. Its components and software are designed into products by its parent conglomerate's divisions and external manufacturers.
8. It bridges fundamental artificial intelligence research with real-world deployment through a focus on safe, secure, robust, and explainable industrial AI.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Astrobotic and its parent company Bosch.
Organization type: Corporate research lab and subsidiary of a privately held multinational engineering and technology conglomerate.
Business model: Funded internally by its parent conglomerate to develop technologies commercialized through product divisions and partnerships.
Scale and maturity: Employs approximately 82,000 research and development associates across 136 global locations.
Geography: Based in Stuttgart, Germany and Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA, with a worldwide operational footprint.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge AI and physical automation, the organization develops consumer goods, industrial technology, mobility solutions, and energy and building technologies through its parent conglomerate.

points.name: Harvest Automation
points.description: Robotics startup deploying autonomous mobile robots for plant spacing and sorting in nurseries and greenhouses.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and builds autonomous mobile robots for spacing, consolidating, and collecting container-grown plants in commercial greenhouses and nurseries, selling complete physical automation systems directly to agricultural operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots with onboard perception and simple manipulators for agricultural tasks.
2. Behavior-based autonomy software running on-device, using planar laser range sensors, failsafe algorithms, boundary tape navigation, and single-degree-of-freedom manipulators.
3. Autonomous plant spacing, consolidation, and collection in greenhouse environments.
4. Complete robots sold directly to growers.
5. Commercial greenhouses, nurseries, and emerging warehouse and fulfillment operations.
6. Commercial greenhouse operators, nurseries, and specialty crop growers.
7. Its robots are operated directly by agricultural growers in their own facilities.
8. Engineering simplicity and low operational costs by deliberately excluding expensive positioning technologies in favor of boundary tape navigation and cost-effective manipulators.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Lampin Corporation for component refinement, investors including Mousse Partners Limited, and customers including Metrolina Greenhouses and Altman Plants.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robot systems.
Scale and maturity: Having secured Series C financing, the company deployed nearly 200 robots across approximately 30 customer sites.
Geography: Based in Billerica, Maine, with commercial deployment operations entirely within the United States nursery and greenhouse sector.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are the organization's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Barrett Technology
points.description: Robotics startup manufacturing embedded motor controllers for precise physical actuation in medical robots.
points.bullets:
A component supplier and medical robot maker that develops robotic manipulators, multi-fingered hands, and miniature brushless servo controllers, and builds FDA-cleared upper-extremity rehabilitation robots for clinical use.
1. A component supplier that makes robotic arms, hands, and embedded servodrive modules, and a robot maker that builds and sells medical rehabilitation robots.
2. Gear-free cable-driven robotic arms with intrinsic whole-arm touch sensitivity, compact programmable multi-fingered graspers, and hermetically sealed brushless servo controllers with integrated 32-bit CPUs.
3. Whole-arm manipulation, dexterous grasping of varied objects, real-time adaptive physical assistance, and AI-powered posture detection during rehabilitation exercises.
4. Components and subsystems sold to other robotics developers, complete rehabilitation robots sold to clinics, and licensed manipulator technology sold to surgical robotics companies.
5. Medical rehabilitation, surgical robotics, space station robotic recovery, and articulated portable coordinate measurement.
6. Hospitals, physical rehabilitation clinics, surgical robotics developers, and space agencies.
7. Its actuation components are designed into machines built by other robotics developers, and it builds its own complete rehabilitation robots for direct clinical installation.
8. Ultra-miniature motor-level intelligence that eliminates the need for external controller cabinets combined with backdriveable gear-free cable drives for safe direct human interaction.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, NASA, the Department of Energy, DARPA, the National Institutes of Health, Spaulding Rehabilitation Hospital, and a surgical robotics company it licensed its arm technology to.
Organization type: A privately held company spun off from a university artificial intelligence laboratory.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic arms, hands, and controllers, medical device sales of rehabilitation robots, and technology licensing contracts.
Scale and maturity: A decades-old company with eleven to fifty employees and hundreds of active medical device installations worldwide.
Geography: Based in Massachusetts, USA, with global installations of its robotics hardware.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the organization's entire focus and core mission.

points.name: Veo Robotics
points.description: Industrial robotics startup developing 3D vision and safeguarding systems that let large factory robots work safely alongside humans.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and subsystem company that built intelligent safeguarding systems for industrial robotic arms, combining 3D vision sensors and edge AI software to let large robots operate safely alongside humans without safety cages.
1. A developer tools and subsystem company that builds perception and safeguarding systems for industrial robot arms, sold as integrated sensor and software subsystems.
2. Distributed computer vision hardware, lidar sensors, and edge AI algorithms that perform real-time sensor fusion and object classification within robotic workcells.
3. 3D perception, human detection, and dynamic speed and motion control that slows or stops industrial robots when humans enter a workcell.
4. Safeguarding systems comprising multiple cameras, sensors, and software integrated into existing robotic workcells.
5. Factory assembly lines, manufacturing workcells, and industrial automation settings.
6. Manufacturing engineers and systems integrators designing factory workcells for automotive, durable goods, and general industrial production.
7. Its sensor and software subsystems are integrated onto industrial robots from major arm manufacturers to upgrade them into collaborative machines.
8. Deploying distributed sensing throughout a workcell rather than relying on onboard robot vision allows large industrial robots to maintain full production speed while automatically slowing or stopping when humans approach.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its technology and assets were acquired by Symbotic, robotic arms from FANUC, KUKA, and Yaskawa were used in its workshop, and it was a portfolio company of the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund.
Organization type: Privately held startup before substantially all of its assets were acquired.
Business model: Hardware and software subsystem sales for industrial robot safeguarding.
Scale and maturity: Reached a mature stage with EU safety certifications and successful client deployments before having substantially all of its assets acquired for $8.7 million in August 2024.
Geography: Based in Waltham, Massachusetts, USA, with operations focused on industrial manufacturing automation in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization was entirely focused on its core mission of providing software-driven human-machine collaboration and intelligent safeguarding for factory automation.

points.name: Vecna Robotics
points.description: US robotics startup deploying autonomous forklifts and pallet movers to automate warehouse material handling.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile robots and orchestration software for material handling, selling to warehousing, manufacturing and fulfillment operators.
1. A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile robots and fleet orchestration software, sold as complete robots or as robots-as-a-service.
2. Autonomous mobile robots with onboard sensors and machine vision for real-time perception, integrated with multi-agent orchestration and teleoperation software.
3. Autonomous navigation, pallet lifting, heavy-load towing, case picking, dynamic task routing, and fleet orchestration.
4. Complete robots and orchestration software, offered as robots-as-a-service with infrastructure-free installation.
5. Warehouses, factories, distribution centers and fulfillment operations.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, distribution centers and automotive parts suppliers.
7. Its robots and software are operated directly by manufacturers and warehouse operators to move materials inside their facilities.
8. Infrastructure-free installation and autonomous navigation that enables dynamic rerouting without fixed pathways.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Shape Corp.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Robots-as-a-service with an annual fee, plus software and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: An established enterprise with deployments across all listed US states and Canada.
Geography: Based and operates in the United States and Canada.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play enterprise whose entire business focus is warehouse automation and robotic fulfillment.

points.name: 6 River Systems
points.description: Robotics startup deploying autonomous mobile carts that assist warehouse workers with picking and sorting tasks.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds collaborative autonomous mobile robots and integrated software for warehouse and fulfillment operations, supplying complete robotic systems directly to logistics operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots for warehouse piece picking.
2. Autonomous mobile robots that use machine learning and smart routing for navigation, integrating pick-to-light systems and zone-based orchestration software with warehouse management systems.
3. Autonomous navigation, goods-to-person picking optimization, pick-to-light guidance, fleet orchestration, and smart sorting.
4. Complete robots and integrated software sold as deployed systems directly to warehouse operators.
5. Warehouses, e-commerce fulfillment centers, and logistics operations.
6. Third-party logistics providers, retailers, and e-commerce fulfillment networks.
7. It builds and sells complete robotic systems that are deployed and operated directly within customer warehouse facilities.
8. Its collaborative systems require significantly fewer robots than competing platforms while delivering multiple productivity gains over manual cart picking and offering rapid return on investment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Ocado Group, Shopify, Menlo Ventures, DHL, XPO Logistics, Office Depot, ACT Fulfillment.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a grocery technology group, formerly a privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and associated software systems.
Scale and maturity: Founded with approximately $46 million in venture funding, acquired for $450 million, and deployed across North America and Europe.
Geography: Based in North America and operates in North America and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and warehouse robotics constitute its entire business focus, and it does not operate outside of this domain.

points.name: RightHand Robotics
points.description: US robotics startup deploying AI-powered piece-picking robots for e-commerce warehouse fulfillment.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous piece-picking systems for e-commerce order fulfillment, owning the full technology stack from soft gripper end-effectors and industrial hardware to AI pick-planning software and fleet management. It supplies complete robotic picking stations to logistics operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells piece-picking robots for warehouses.
2. Machine learning and AI for model-free picking, integrated with custom soft gripper end-effectors, industrial hardware, computing platforms, and fleet management software.
3. Autonomous model-free piece picking, grasping, selecting, and sorting handheld items, and fleet orchestration for fulfillment operations.
4. Complete robotic picking systems, including hardware, grippers, software, and fleet management, supported by service.
5. Warehouses, e-commerce order fulfillment, intralogistics, and pharmaceutical supply chains.
6. Logistics operators across electronics, apparel, pharmaceutical, and grocery supply chains.
7. It designs and builds the complete picking robot and sells the integrated system directly to warehouse operators.
8. It owns the entire deployed technology stack end-to-end, eliminating the need for customers to assemble components from multiple third-party vendors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with peer mobile robot providers for cross-platform warehouse fulfillment and holds partnerships for logistics center integration in South Korea, with backing from a venture capital firm.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware and system sales, software, and support services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, it has established deployments accumulating over a petabyte of operational fleet data.
Geography: Based in Somerville, Massachusetts, with international operations and partnerships in markets including South Korea and Sweden.
Beyond physical AI: Warehouse automation is the organization's entire focus, operating strictly as a pure-play provider of physical AI and robotic fulfillment solutions.

points.name: Sea Machines
points.description: Marine robotics startup retrofitting commercial and defense vessels with autonomous command and control systems.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer and marine robotics company that builds retrofit-ready autonomous command and control systems for commercial and defense vessels. It designs on-board ruggedized computers, perception and autonomy software that enable remote control and autonomous navigation for workboats. The organization sells its technology to commercial marine operators, surveyors and military clients seeking to automate existing vessels rather than build new ones.
1. An autonomy software developer that builds retrofit autonomous vessel systems and on-board computers sold as hardware-software packages for existing workboats.
2. On-board ruggedized computers running sensor-fusion autonomy software with computer vision perception, obstacle avoidance and mission planning.
3. Remote control within 1 km range, autonomous navigation, mission planning, collaborative following, obstacle avoidance, remote payload control and data management.
4. Retrofit hardware-software systems installed on existing vessels, integrating with existing vessel systems.
5. Workboats, survey vessels, crew-transfer vessels, search-and-rescue boats, oil spill response vessels, autonomous barges and military surface vessels.
6. Commercial workboat operators, hydrographic surveyors, offshore wind operators, search-and-rescue teams, oil spill responders, navies and defense agencies.
7. Its autonomy systems are retrofitted onto existing vessels built by boat makers and operated by marine operators.
8. Its retrofit-ready approach enables autonomous operations on existing vessels without requiring entirely new vessel builds.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The U.S. Navy selected it for the MUSV program, the Defense Innovation Unit awarded it a contract for autonomous barge prototyping, and it has partnered with a survey company, a maritime academy and a boat builder supplying the U.S. Coast Guard.
Organization type: A privately held startup founded in 2015 with 30 employees across offices in the U.S. and Europe.
Business model: Hardware-software system sales, defense contracts and prototyping agreements.
Scale and maturity: A venture-funded startup that has raised $39 million, operates an active marine test fleet and has been selected for a Navy unmanned surface vessel program.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts with offices in Hamburg, Esbjerg, dealer networks and manufacturing across North America, Europe, Singapore and the UAE.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play company where marine autonomy platforms and deployed systems constitute its entire focus.

points.name: Locus Robotics
points.description: US robotics company deploying autonomous warehouse picking robots.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile robots and mobile manipulation systems for warehouse fulfillment, selling them as a fully managed service to third-party logistics providers, retailers, and industrial brands.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds autonomous mobile robots and mobile manipulation platforms, sold primarily through a robots-as-a-service subscription model.
2. Autonomous mobile robots, mobile manipulation platforms, and fleet orchestration software using applied AI for dynamic route optimization, adaptive decision-making, and integrated grasping.
3. Autonomous navigation, piece picking, goods-to-person transport, multi-order batch picking, and fleet orchestration across end-to-end fulfillment workflows.
4. Complete robots and manipulation systems delivered as a robots-as-a-service subscription, accompanied by cloud-based orchestration software.
5. Warehouses, fulfillment centers, and distribution facilities for e-commerce, retail, and third-party logistics operations.
6. Third-party logistics providers, retail brands, healthcare distributors, and industrial manufacturers.
7. It builds its own mobile robots and manipulation platforms and supplies them directly to warehouse operators for in-facility deployment.
8. It delivers flexible, retrofit-compatible collaborative robots that work alongside human pickers without requiring facility redesign, financed through a pure subscription model.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its investors include G2 Venture Partners and Eclipse Ventures, and its customers include major logistics operators such as DHL, GEODIS, and Radial.
Organization type: A privately held company spun out of a logistics operator following an acquisition of its previous robotic systems.
Business model: Robots-as-a-service subscriptions generating recurring revenue for deployed robot fleets and orchestration software.
Scale and maturity: A mature, globally deployed organization with over 15,000 active robots across more than 350 sites, surpassing billions of total picks, with funding exceeding $400 million and a valuation over $2 billion.
Geography: Based in the United States, with extensive deployments across North America and expanding operations in Europe.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play enterprise whose entire operational and commercial focus is dedicated to physical artificial intelligence and warehouse fulfillment automation.

points.name: Ava Robotics
points.description: Robotics startup deploying autonomous telepresence robots for remote workplace navigation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous telepresence robots for enterprise video collaboration, combining physical mobility with video conferencing for commercial applications.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete autonomous mobile robots for telepresence.
2. Autonomous navigation and mapping software integrated with HD cameras, sensor perception, and enterprise cloud connectivity on a mobile platform.
3. Autonomous navigation to user-designated destinations, environmental mapping, and remote HD video conferencing with full-fidelity audio.
4. Complete telepresence robots with integrated video conferencing, sold as end-to-end deployed systems.
5. Offices, manufacturing floors, hospitals, hospitality venues, education environments, and corporate workplaces.
6. Commercial enterprises, healthcare facilities, educational institutions, and hospitality operators.
7. It designs and manufactures complete telepresence platforms that it sells as deployed systems to commercial end users.
8. Its robots move to user-designated destinations without requiring constant remote teleoperation, combining autonomous navigation with enterprise video collaboration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its telepresence robots are powered by Webex and integrated with Cisco Spark, and it won a 5G Robotics Challenge sponsored by Verizon and Ericsson.
Organization type: A privately held startup spun off from a consumer robotics company and founded by former robotics engineers.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete telepresence robot systems to commercial enterprises.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company that has raised $2.9 million in funding and introduced its first telepresence robot in 2018.
Geography: Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States, serving commercial markets across sectors including healthcare, education, and corporate environments.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus, centering entirely on developing and deploying physical telepresence robotics that enable remote workers to move around real-world locations as if they were physically present.

points.name: GelSight
points.description: Robotics startup building tactile sensors that give robotic hands the ability to feel surfaces and handle objects precisely.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops and manufactures imaging-based tactile sensors and accompanying software frameworks for robotic manipulation and precision surface inspection, providing high-resolution touch data to robots and researchers.
1. A sensor maker that builds optical tactile sensors for robotic grippers and inspection tools.
2. Vision-based tactile sensors using elastomeric 3D imaging systems to capture high-resolution spatial information about local contact geometry, deformation, and surface structure at high frame rates.
3. High-precision tactile sensing that measures surface texture, geometry, force feedback, and contact pose in real time, enabling dexterous manipulation and micron-level surface analysis.
4. Tactile sensors sold as components and handheld metrology devices, integrated directly into robotic grippers or used as standalone inspection tools.
5. Robotic manipulation in research and industrial settings, alongside surface inspection and metrology in aerospace, automotive, forensics, consumer electronics, medical, and defense.
6. Robotic research labs, industrial robotics developers, manufacturers, and organizations requiring precision quality assurance and inspection.
7. Its sensors are designed into robotic grippers and hands by robot makers and used as standalone metrology tools by industrial operators.
8. It delivers superhuman touch sensitivity that detects forces as small as one millinewton and captures omnidirectional surface deformations with micron-level precision using a flexible vision-based approach.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Meta AI, with which it partners to develop and commercially manufacture tactile sensors for research.
Organization type: A privately held MIT spin-off company.
Business model: Hardware sales of tactile sensors and metrology devices.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2011, with established products in the market and a community-driven early access research program planned for wide availability in 2025.
Geography: Based in the US, operating globally across industrial, aerospace, automotive, and advanced technology research markets.
Beyond physical AI: Developing physical artificial intelligence technology through tactile sensing and metrology solutions constitutes the organization's entire business focus.

points.name: AutoX
points.description: Chinese autonomous driving startup operating commercial robotaxi fleets using fully self-driving systems.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vehicle company that develops Level 4 and Level 5 autonomous driving systems and operates commercial driverless robotaxi fleets. It builds the full self-driving stack, including the domain controller, sensor suite, and AI driver software, and uses it to run a Mobility-as-a-Service ride-hailing platform for urban passengers.
1. An autonomous vehicle system provider and operator that develops self-driving hardware and software stacks and operates a commercial robotaxi fleet.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software combined with a multi-sensor suite of cameras, lidar, and radar, running on a self-developed domain controller built with automotive-grade GPUs, multicore CPUs, and FPGAs for high-performance on-vehicle inference.
3. Level 4 and Level 5 autonomous driving, real-time perception, decision-making, planning, and fleet operations in dense and dynamic urban traffic without safety drivers.
4. Autonomous vehicle systems integrated with automaker platforms, and commercial ride-hailing services operated directly for the public.
5. Robotaxis and autonomous vehicles in dense urban environments.
6. Urban passengers for ride-hailing services, and automakers for system integration and pilot programs.
7. It licenses and integrates its self-driving systems into vehicles built by automakers and operates the resulting robotaxi fleets itself.
8. It was an early operator of fully driverless robotaxi services without safety drivers on public roads in China.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Investors and partners include Alibaba Group, SAIC Motor, Stellantis, Honda, Dongfeng Motor, FCA, NEVS, Amap, Pengcheng Electric, SiLC, Intel, Xilinx, and NVIDIA.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Ride-hailing fares through a Mobility-as-a-Service platform, and system integration collaborations with automotive OEMs.
Scale and maturity: A unicorn startup valued at over $1 billion that has raised over $267 million and operates a fleet of over 1,000 autonomous vehicles.
Geography: Based in Shenzhen, China, with operations across major Chinese cities including Guangzhou, Shanghai, and Beijing, and a presence in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play enterprise in the self-driving sector whose entire focus is the development and operation of autonomous mobility systems.

points.name: Double Robotics
points.description: Robotics startup building telepresence robots with on-device AI for autonomous navigation and obstacle avoidance.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and manufactures autonomous telepresence robots integrating on-device artificial intelligence, sensor arrays, autonomous driving logic, and motorized camera hardware for enterprise, education, and logistics clients.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells fully integrated telepresence robots and related accessories.
2. Two-wheeled balancing robotic platforms with self-driving navigation, 3D obstacle-avoidance sensors, mixed-reality overlays, and pan-tilt-zoom camera systems operating via on-device inference.
3. Autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance, telepresence, and remote driving control.
4. Complete robots and attachable accessory kits.
5. Hybrid offices, classrooms, universities, and warehouses.
6. Enterprises, educational institutions, and logistics operators.
7. It builds and sells complete robotic platforms directly to end users.
8. A mixed-reality click-to-drive interface and autonomous obstacle avoidance operate independently of cloud-based processing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Apple is a supplier of essential iPad hardware used in earlier robot models.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and accessories.
Scale and maturity: An established company with multiple generations of deployed products and continuous over-the-air software update capabilities.
Geography: Based and operates globally with a focus on enterprise and educational markets.
Beyond physical AI: Designing and manufacturing autonomous telepresence robots is its sole business activity.

points.name: Blue River Technology
points.description: Agricultural robotics startup deploying computer vision-powered farm equipment to identify weeds and spray crops in real time.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous agricultural machinery for field-based precision farming. It designs computer vision-guided weeding and spraying robots that distinguish crops from weeds to apply herbicides with high precision. It builds these machines for agricultural producers to optimize chemical usage and increase crop yields.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous precision agriculture robots.
2. Computer vision and deep learning algorithms run on edge computing inference silicon to process real-time plant-level data and control spray actuation hardware on moving machinery.
3. Real-time crop and weed classification, targeted herbicide application and agricultural piece spraying.
4. Complete agricultural robots and machinery.
5. Farms, agriculture and outdoor field operations.
6. Farmers and agricultural producers.
7. It builds complete agricultural robots that are deployed directly by farmers in their own fields.
8. A closed-loop learning approach collects field data annually to optimize subsequent crops, reducing chemical usage by over 90 percent.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of John Deere and a former investment recipient of Monsanto Growth Ventures.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded agricultural equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of agricultural machinery.
Scale and maturity: Acquired for $305 million in 2017 and operating across millions of acres.
Geography: Based and operating primarily in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on applying robotics and artificial intelligence to optimize farming practices.

points.name: Liquid Robotics
points.description: Marine robotics startup developing autonomous ocean surface vehicles powered by wave and solar energy for persistent maritime data collection.
points.bullets:
A robot and vehicle maker that designs and manufactures uncrewed surface vehicles powered by wave and solar energy, integrating edge processing and onboard computing with configurable sensor payloads for persistent maritime monitoring. It builds complete autonomous platforms primarily for defense, scientific research, and offshore commercial customers, operating as a subsidiary of a larger aerospace conglomerate.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds autonomous uncrewed surface vehicles for maritime deployment.
2. Wave- and solar-powered autonomous surface vessels equipped with edge processing, onboard computing, and extensible sensor-hosting architectures.
3. Long-endurance persistent ocean monitoring, real-time data collection and communications, autonomous navigation, and above- and below-surface perception.
4. Complete autonomous vehicles and sensor-integrated platforms delivered to defense and commercial operators.
5. Ocean monitoring, maritime defense, offshore energy, oil spill response, and oceanographic and climate research.
6. Navies, government research agencies, offshore energy operators, and maritime defense organizations.
7. It builds complete autonomous surface vehicles that are deployed directly by maritime defense and commercial operators, and integrates third-party sensors and software onto its platforms.
8. Its vehicles achieve extreme endurance by harvesting wave and solar energy, operating for months without fossil fuel dependency or logistical support.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The Boeing Company, Bedrock Ocean Exploration, Integer, and the United States Navy.
Organization type: A wholly owned subsidiary of a publicly traded aerospace conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of autonomous surface vehicles and tailored solutions for long-endurance maritime monitoring missions.
Scale and maturity: Nearly two decades of operation with approximately 100 employees, validated by over 3 million nautical miles of real-world deployment experience across multiple platform generations.
Geography: Based in Maryland with an expanding global operational footprint that includes co-development manufacturing partnerships in India.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is dedicated to the design, manufacturing, and deployment of autonomous marine robotics and edge computing platforms.

points.name: FarmWise
points.description: Agricultural robotics startup deploying autonomous field robots with on-device computer vision to identify and remove weeds.
points.bullets:
An agricultural robot maker that builds autonomous weeding tractors with on-device computer vision and physical blade actuators to mechanically remove weeds for large-scale farms.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells autonomous farm machinery for mechanical weed control.
2. On-device computer vision models and onboard processing paired with mechanical blade actuators that snip weeds with sub-inch precision.
3. Autonomous intra-row weeding, plant detection and crop distinguishing, precision cultivation, and soil preparation or planting.

points.profile:

points.name: Built Robotics
points.description: Construction robotics startup upgrading heavy machinery with edge AI kits for autonomous excavation and grading.
points.bullets:
A construction robotics company that builds aftermarket autonomy upgrade kits transforming standard heavy construction equipment into autonomous machines. It develops proprietary edge AI models, sensors, and on-device computing stacks, and operates deployed systems for construction and infrastructure customers.
1. A construction robot maker that builds retrofit autonomy kits for heavy equipment and autonomous pile driving robots, sold as installed systems or robots-as-a-service.
2. A technical stack spanning ruggedized edge sensors, liquid-cooled on-device computing, GPS, and machine learning models for equipment autonomy, including a proprietary edge AI model for personnel detection trained on active construction sites.
3. Fully automated trenching, grading, excavation, autonomous pile driving, personnel detection, geofencing, and safety protocols for heavy equipment.
4. Aftermarket retrofit kits installed on existing machines, complete autonomous pile driving robots, and robots-as-a-service deployments.
5. Excavators, bulldozers, pile drivers, and survey robots used in utility-scale solar farms, road building, land preparation, housing, energy, and infrastructure construction.
6. Construction contractors, energy and infrastructure developers, and unions whose members operate the machines.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with xLAB on physical AI research, Silicon Valley Bank on debt financing, and unions on training and certification; investors include Tiger Global, NEA, Next47, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, and Blattner as a customer.

points.name: Bear Robotics
points.description: Service robotics startup deploying autonomous indoor serving robots for restaurants.

A robot maker that builds, deploys, and operates autonomous service robots and mobile manipulators alongside a cloud orchestration platform, primarily for restaurants and hospitality venues.

points.name: Civ Robotics
points.description: Construction robotics startup deploying autonomous surveying robots to mark site coordinates for solar and renewable energy projects.
points.bullets:
A construction robot maker that builds autonomous mobile robots for site layout and an AI-powered machine-control material distribution system for solar and general construction projects.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A major construction firm is a customer having used its robots and machine-control system on their projects.
Organization type: A privately held commercial entity operating within the industrial robotics sector.

points.name: Dexterity Robotics
points.description: Robotics startup deploying AI-powered robotic arms for complex warehouse picking and packing tasks.
points.bullets:
A robotics startup that develops a full-stack warehouse and fulfillment automation platform combining AI, computer vision, and tactile sensing to enable industrial robotic arms to perform complex manipulation tasks. It supplies this intelligent software and integrated subsystem to major logistics and supply chain operators.

2. The core technology integrates on-device perception, tactile sensing, and general machine learning models for real-time control of standard industrial robotic arms.
3. It delivers sub-400-millisecond decision speeds for complex piece picking and manipulation, having logged tens of millions of goods picked with over 100 million autonomous decisions and zero safety incidents.
4. Customers receive it as a hardware-agnostic, SaaS-based software platform and integrated subsystem running on standard industrial robotic arms and interchangeable end-effectors.
5. It is used in warehouses and fulfillment operations for piece picking and goods manipulation.
6. It sells to major logistics and supply chain operators, including parcel companies, third-party logistics providers, and consumer goods manufacturers and retailers.
7. Its software and subsystems are deployed within the broader warehouse automation value chain, supplying the intelligent manipulation layer for standard robotic arms operated by logistics providers.

points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held technology company operating as a commercial robotics and software provider.
Business model: It makes money through a SaaS-based platform model.

Geography: It is based in the United States, operating extensively in American warehouses while expanding deployments into Europe.

points.name: Nimble

points.name: Relay Robotics

points.name: Pyka
