Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Robot sales and agricultural data collection services.
Scale and maturity: Over 150 robots deployed with more than 300,000 kilometers of autonomous operation across commercial farms, over 50 employees, and founded in 2016.
Geography: Headquartered in Oslo, Norway, with operational bases in Lincoln, UK, and Paso Robles, California, serving European and American agricultural markets.
Beyond physical AI: The development and deployment of autonomous agricultural robots is the company's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Baubot
points.description: Vienna-based construction robotics startup developing semi-autonomous mobile robots that drill holes and perform repetitive tasks on building sites.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that develops mobile robotic systems for automating physically demanding tasks on construction sites. It combines industrial robot arms, safety sensors, and proprietary planning software to deliver complete construction automation solutions for the civil infrastructure sector.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells mobile construction robots integrating industrial arms and planning software.
2. Mobile robotic systems integrating industrial robotic arms, advanced safety sensors, and simulation software for BIM and CAD-based mission planning.
3. On-site drilling for handrails and cable routes, paving stone 3D printing, and automated route planning in virtual construction environments.
4. Complete mobile robotic systems and proprietary planning and simulation software.
5. Construction sites, tunnel construction, bridge construction, road development, and production halls.
6. Civil infrastructure contractors and construction companies.
7. It integrates industrial robot arms and sensors into complete mobile robotic systems deployed on construction sites.
8. It combines industrial-grade robotic hardware with specialized construction automation software, achieving a Guinness World Record for drilling thousands of aligned holes in a single day.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: KUKA supplies industrial robotics, and the fischer Group of Companies is its parent company.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary operating as an acquired startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of mobile robotic systems and software.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2017 with 11 to 50 employees that reached production-ready commercial systems by 2022.
Geography: Based in Vienna, Austria, with deployments in Austria and Germany.
Beyond physical AI: Developing mobile robotic systems for the construction industry is the pure-play and entire focus of the company.

points.name: Blue Ocean Robotics
points.description: Danish robotics venture factory developing and deploying autonomous mobile service robots with on-device AI for healthcare and hospitality.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that develops, produces and sells autonomous mobile service robots for professional applications, operating as a venture factory that commercializes robotic platforms from concept through exit. It builds complete robotic systems integrating on-device autonomy, sensors, navigation and task execution for highly regulated and professional environments.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete autonomous mobile service robots.
2. Mobile robot platforms integrating autonomous navigation, UV-C disinfection, telepresence and patient-handling mechanisms with on-device perception and task execution.
3. Autonomous navigation, UV-C disinfection, telepresence communication, safe patient handling and rehabilitation.
4. Complete robots and telepresence units.
5. Hospitals, pharmaceutical cleanrooms, hospitality, corporate facilities, agriculture and construction sites.
6. Hospitals, pharmaceutical manufacturers, facility operators, hospitality providers and agriculture businesses.
7. The company builds complete robots and sells them to end-users in professional service industries.
8. The venture-factory model develops robotic solutions from problem and design through commercialization and exit, with robots engineered for highly regulated environments such as GMP-compliant cleanrooms.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Distribution and exhibition partners include PSC Biotech and Mason Technology, with investment from A.P. Møller Holding and full ownership by 3C GROUPS.
Organization type: Privately held company operating as a robot venture factory and subsidiary.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robots and associated services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2013, it has secured over $51 million in investment and secured major contracts for hundreds of robots, including a European Commission contract for hospital deployments across EU member states.
Geography: Based in Odense, Denmark and expanding its global market presence.
Beyond physical AI: Developing and commercializing AI-driven service robots is the organization's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Starship Technologies
points.description: Estonian autonomous delivery startup deploying sidewalk robots for local last-mile goods transport.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and fleet operator that designs, builds and runs small electrically-powered sidewalk delivery robots for autonomous last-mile transport of food, groceries and parcels on behalf of retailers, delivery platforms, universities and industrial sites.
1. A robot maker that builds autonomous sidewalk delivery robots and operates its own fleet.
2. Multi-modal sensor fusion combining cameras, radar and machine learning with visual positioning systems that build 3D maps of the robot's surroundings for real-time pedestrian-speed navigation.
3. Autonomous on-device navigation, obstacle avoidance, 3D mapping, cargo unlocking via mobile app and last-mile delivery at pedestrian speeds without remote tele-operation.
4. Complete robots and delivery services operated by the company itself as a deployed fleet.
5. Sidewalk and pedestrian last-mile delivery on university campuses, city streets and industrial corporate premises.
6. Retail grocery chains, third-party food delivery platforms, university campus meal services, meal-plan providers and major German industrial corporations.
7. It designs, builds, maintains and operates its own fleet of delivery robots, selling delivery services directly to end clients rather than licensing its machines or software.
8. It achieves a 99% autonomous driving rate without relying on remote tele-operation, at massive commercial scale with millions of completed deliveries.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners include Uber Eats, Co-op, Tesco, Bolt, Grubhub, Sodexo, George Mason University, Veriff and the European Investment Bank.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Delivery fees and service contracts for autonomous last-mile transport.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2014, it has completed over 10 million autonomous deliveries with a fleet of over 2,700 robots across more than 300 global locations, backed by over $230 million in equity and €100 million in debt facilities.
Geography: Headquartered in Tallinn, Estonia with a major presence in San Francisco, California, operating across seven countries globally.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play entity whose entire business model and operational focus is strictly dedicated to autonomous physical delivery and embodied artificial intelligence.

points.name: Keybotic
points.description: Spanish inspection robotics startup deploying autonomous quadruped robots for hazardous industrial environments.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and manufactures autonomous quadruped robots for industrial inspection in hazardous environments, offering them to heavy industry through a robotics-as-a-service model.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous quadruped robots for industrial inspection.
2. Autonomous four-legged robots integrating visual, thermal and acoustic sensors with on-device edge AI algorithms for autonomous navigation, anomaly detection and task planning.
3. Autonomous navigation, gas leak and hotspot detection, instrument reading, intruder detection and real-time alarm generation in hazardous environments.
4. Complete robots offered through a robotics-as-a-service subscription model.
5. Chemical plants, oil and gas facilities, energy installations and mining operations.
6. Operators of hazardous industrial facilities in the chemical, oil and gas, energy and mining sectors.
7. It designs and manufactures its own quadruped robots and operates them for industrial customers under a service model.
8. It combines sophisticated autonomous fleet coordination with a subscription-based leasing model that lowers upfront costs while removing human workers from dangerous environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company has received funding from Helsing and a family office, and won first prize in the 2021 DARPA Robotics Challenge.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Robotics-as-a-service subscription contracts for industrial inspection.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup that has secured approximately €3 million in funding.
Geography: Based in Barcelona, Spain, with operations focused on industrial facilities across Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation represent the entirety of the organization's overall mission and business operations.

points.name: Exotec
points.description: French warehouse robotics startup deploying autonomous mobile robots for goods-to-person order fulfillment.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and builds autonomous mobile robots and integrated warehouse execution software for goods-to-person fulfillment operations in warehouses, serving major retail and e-commerce brands.
1. A robot maker and systems integrator that builds autonomous mobile robots, robotic arms, and the software to orchestrate them, sold as complete warehouse automation systems.
2. Autonomous mobile robots capable of climbing high-density storage racks, robotic picking arms, and proprietary warehouse execution software for real-time fleet orchestration.
3. Goods-to-person storage and retrieval, autonomous mobile robot navigation, automated item picking, and fleet orchestration.
4. Complete robotic systems, including robots, robotic arms, and orchestration software, installed as integrated warehouse automation, offered under a robotics-as-a-service model.
5. Warehouses and fulfillment centers.
6. Retail, logistics, and e-commerce brands, as well as systems integrators.
7. Its robots and software are designed and manufactured in-house and integrated directly into the fulfillment centers of major brands.
8. Its modular, plug-and-play architecture and vertical integration enable rapid and repeatable scaling compared to traditional bespoke warehouse automation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by Bpifrance, with named partnerships and integrations for Decathlon, Carrefour, Gap, Uniqlo, Ariat, Oxford Industries, A1 Sorter, and POSCO DX.
Organization type: A privately held scale-up company operating in the robotics sector.
Business model: Hardware and software system sales, integration services, and robotics-as-a-service contracts.
Scale and maturity: A mature global enterprise generating $1 billion in annual sales, having deployed over 10,000 robots across more than 200 sites and completed over 938 million operational cycles.
Geography: Based in Croix, France, with its North American headquarters in Atlanta, Georgia, and a global operational footprint.
Beyond physical AI: The company's entire focus is dedicated to warehouse automation and supply chain transformation.

points.name: TuSimple
points.description: Chinese autonomous trucking startup deploying self-driving heavy-duty trucks using onboard edge AI for real-time freight transportation.
points.bullets:
An autonomous trucking company that develops a Level 4 self-driving system for heavy-duty semi-trucks and operates them to haul commercial freight. It builds proprietary autonomy software and sensor suites for long-haul delivery, running real cargo routes for logistics customers before winding down its U.S. operations to shift focus to the Asia-Pacific region.
1. An autonomy software developer and fleet operator that builds a Level 4 self-driving truck stack and runs autonomous freight operations as a service.
2. A sensor-fusion autonomy stack processing continuous data streams from cameras, LiDAR, and radar through up to 100 deep learning modules on onboard edge AI inference hardware.
3. Level 4 autonomous navigation, real-time perception, construction zone detection, and dynamic routing for long-haul trucks.
4. Autonomous freight capacity delivered through a transportation-as-a-service model it operates itself.
5. Autonomous semi-trucks hauling commercial freight on limited-access highways in dry, daytime conditions.
6. Commercial freight operators, logistics companies, and postal services.
7. It integrates its proprietary self-driving system into vehicle maker partners' trucks and operates the resulting autonomous fleet itself.
8. It emphasizes fully onboard, on-device edge inference for driving decisions and has demonstrated driverless commercial freight runs on public roads.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It conducted pilots with major logistics operators and postal services and partnered with commercial vehicle makers.
Organization type: A publicly traded company that wound down its U.S. operations and rebranded.
Business model: It generated revenue by charging freight and delivery fees for operating autonomous truck routes.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, the company employed about 400 people, conducted the first driverless run on public roads, and laid off 75% of its U.S. workforce before closing its American operations.
Geography: Based in San Diego, California and Shenzhen, China, it operated primarily in Arizona before shifting strategic focus entirely to the Asia-Pacific region.
Beyond physical AI: Autonomous freight transportation constitutes its entire operational focus and corporate identity.

points.name: Tonner
points.description: French aerial vehicle startup developing warehouse logistics drones and inventory automation robots.
points.bullets:
A drone and robot maker that builds unmanned aerial vehicles and warehouse logistics robots, delivering complete integrated automation solutions for the logistics and security sectors while also operating as a holding company with venture investments.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells drones and warehouse logistics robots, and acts as a systems integrator installing complete automation solutions.
2. Unmanned aerial vehicles and warehouse robotics hardware designed for inventory management and stock control automation.
3. Autonomous aerial vehicle operation, warehouse inventory management, and stock control automation.
4. Complete integrated automation solutions, drones, and warehouse automation hardware.
5. Warehouse logistics operations and security robotics deployments.
6. Logistics operators and security sector customers.
7. It builds complete robots and drones and integrates them into deployed systems for end users.
8. It combines direct development of warehouse robotics through collaborations with major logistics partners with a broader investment strategy in the drone manufacturing ecosystem.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded holding company.
Business model: Hardware sales of drones and warehouse robots, systems integration contracts, and venture investment returns.
Scale and maturity: An established publicly traded holding entity operating primarily within the French drone and logistics sectors.
Geography: Based in Cannes, France, with operational footprint and investment activities concentrated in France.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical automation, the organization pursues diversified financial strategies including patent royalty generation and crypto-related treasury investments.

points.name: Volocopter
points.description: German aerial vehicle startup deploying autonomous electric aircraft for urban air mobility.
points.bullets:
An eVTOL aircraft maker that builds electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft for passenger urban air mobility and heavy-lift cargo logistics, integrating onboard flight control and a cloud-based fleet management platform.
1. An aircraft manufacturer that builds and sells complete electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft and cargo drones.
2. Electric multicopters with 18 rotors, fly-by-wire control systems, swappable batteries, and a cloud-based digital connective platform for fleet management.
3. Electric vertical take-off and landing, redundant stable flight control, heavy-lift cargo transport, and aerial fleet orchestration.
4. Complete passenger aircraft, cargo drones, vertiport infrastructure, and cloud-based fleet management software.
5. Urban air taxis, cargo logistics, agriculture, public services, and medical transport.
6. Urban air mobility operators, logistics providers, general aviation consumers, and public services.
7. Its aircraft and fleet management platforms are deployed by urban air mobility and logistics operators.
8. Extensive redundancy-based flight control systems that allow aircraft to maintain stable flight after multiple motor or sensor failures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partnered with Near Earth Autonomy for autonomous flight testing, acquired by Diamond Aircraft, with investors including Daimler, Geely, DB Schenker, BlackRock, and Intel Capital.
Organization type: Privately held startup acquired out of insolvency by another aircraft manufacturer.
Business model: Aircraft and hardware sales, vertiport construction, and fleet management software.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2011, raised €322 million in equity, completed over 1,000 test flights, and recently underwent insolvency and acquisition restructuring.
Geography: Based in Bruchsal, Munich, and Singapore, with international flight demonstrations in Singapore, Dubai, and Paris.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is on manufacturing autonomous electric aircraft and managing the supporting aerial infrastructure for urban air mobility ecosystems.

points.name: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
points.description: Seattle research organization developing interactive simulators to train physical AI agents in virtual environments.
points.bullets:
A research organization that develops developer tools for physical AI, building simulation platforms that procedurally generate interactive 3D scenes for training embodied AI models. It creates environments with sufficient interactivity, diversity, and rationality to support research in robot perception, navigation, and manipulation.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation platform robotics engineers and AI researchers use to train and evaluate embodied agents.
2. Procedural generation software that automatically constructs large-scale simulated scenes with rich interactivity and physical constraints, built on an interactive simulation framework.
3. Synthetic training environments, embodied AI simulation, and interactive scene generation for physical reasoning and manipulation tasks.
4. Open-source simulation platforms and codebases released for research and development use.
5. Robotics research, embodied AI, and simulation-based training for machines operating in physical environments.
6. AI researchers, robotics engineers, and academic institutions.
7. Its simulation platforms are used by researchers and engineers to train models that are later deployed on physical robots.
8. It focuses on procedural generation of massive, diverse, and interactive scene datasets rather than hand-crafted simulation environments.
points.profile:
Organization type: A research organization.
Beyond physical AI: The organization also conducts research across natural language processing, machine learning theory, knowledge representation, and computer vision.

points.name: Open Robotics
points.description: San Francisco and Singapore robotics software organization developing open-source operating systems and simulation tools for physical AI.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform organization that builds and maintains open-source robotics software, middleware, simulation tools, and fleet management systems for the robotics ecosystem.
1. A developer tools company whose middleware, simulation platforms, and fleet coordination software robotics engineers use.
2. Open-source middleware utilizing Data Distribution Service for decentralized communication, 3D physics simulation, and real-time control frameworks.
3. Robot behavior control from sensor inputs, multi-robot fleet coordination, infrastructure interoperability, and physics-based simulation.
4. Open-source software releases and distributions.
5. Mobile robots, autonomous vehicles, warehouse logistics, manufacturing, and space exploration.
6. Robotics developers, engineers, and systems integrators.
7. Its software is used by developers and integrators to build and operate robots.
8. A vendor-neutral, open-source approach maintained by a broad global community.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with NVIDIA, Intel, Canonical, Clearpath Robotics, and Google's Intrinsic.
Organization type: A nonprofit organization with over 50 employees guided by a steering committee.
Business model: Government contracts and open-source ecosystem stewardship.
Scale and maturity: An established ecosystem player with over a decade of broad industry adoption and global community support.
Geography: Based in the United States with global software distribution.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play robotics software organization whose entire focus is providing foundational tools for the physical AI and robotics ecosystem.

points.name: Army Research Laboratory (ARL)
points.description: US government research agency developing autonomous ground vehicles and robotic physical autonomy for Army modernization.
points.bullets:
A government agency that conducts foundational research in edge AI and robotic autonomy for the military, developing autonomous off-road mobility, tactical behaviors for ground vehicles, and human-robot interaction. It operates as a primary research and development hub, executing intramural and extramural research and collaborating with academic and industry partners to advance physical autonomy solutions.
1. A government agency that funds and conducts foundational robotics and autonomy research for defense applications.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software, simultaneous localization and mapping, and generative artificial intelligence integrated with robotics for natural language command execution.
3. Autonomous navigation in adversarial terrain, human-guided machine learning, tactical behaviors for ground vehicles, and battle damage assessment.
4. Research programs, collaborative partnerships, and funded research proposals administered through broad agency announcements.
5. Defense forces, ground vehicles, quadruped robots, and wheeled robots executing real-world military missions.
6. Militaries and defense modernization programs.
7. Its research is transitioned to defense forces and integrated into military ground vehicles and robotic platforms.
8. It integrates generative artificial intelligence with robotics to enable natural language command execution during battle damage assessment operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with university robotics labs and administers research associateship programs through the Oak Ridge Associated Universities.
Organization type: A government agency that serves as a military research laboratory.
Business model: Federally funded research and development programs and administered research grants.
Scale and maturity: An established national laboratory with mature research programs, collaborative campuses, distributed virtual proving grounds, and restricted airspace.
Geography: Headquartered in Adelphi, Maryland, USA, operating collaborative research facilities domestically.
Beyond physical AI: The organization serves as the broader foundational research arm for the United States Army, advancing general scientific and engineering priorities across diverse fields.

points.name: Naval Research Laboratory (NRL)
points.description: US government research agency developing edge AI systems and autonomous physical platforms for naval defense.
points.bullets:
A government research laboratory that develops autonomous physical platforms, including unmanned underwater, aerial, and ground vehicles, alongside edge AI systems and sensor networks, primarily for the U.S. Navy and Department of Defense. It functions as a systems integrator and foundational research institution, translating theoretical advances into deployable prototypes and demonstration systems rather than commercializing individual components.
1. A government research institution that designs and builds complete autonomous platform prototypes, sensors, and AI algorithms for defense applications.
2. Autonomous unmanned vehicles, marine robotics, sensor networks, human-robot interaction systems, and artificial intelligence algorithms integrated into physical platforms.
3. Autonomous underwater and aerial navigation, manipulation, autonomous testing of robotics, and edge AI perception and control for military systems.
4. Deployable prototype systems, demonstration platforms, and contracted research services delivered to the military.
5. Defense platforms including unmanned underwater vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles, autonomous firefighting robots, and military sensor networks.
6. The U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, and the Department of Defense.
7. It develops and integrates complete autonomous platforms and AI systems directly for military end-users rather than supplying commercial components.
8. It leverages specialized multidisciplinary research teams and unique simulated environmental testing facilities to conduct long-term basic research free from commercial pressures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The Office of Naval Research, the Navy and Marine Corps, and the Industrial Acoustics Company.
Organization type: A government laboratory and scientific command operating under the United States Navy.
Business model: Federally funded research and contracted development serving military interests.
Scale and maturity: A mature, large-scale scientific enterprise with an artificial intelligence center established in 1981 and a 50,000-square-foot testing facility opened in 2012.
Geography: Based in Washington, D.C., United States, operating dedicated research facilities to serve American naval and defense interests globally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond artificial intelligence, the institution conducts broader scientific research responsible for historical breakthroughs such as GPS, deep ocean searches, radar, and friend-or-foe identification systems.

points.name: Air Force Research Laboratory
points.description: US government agency developing edge AI software and autonomous hardware for military systems.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and directs research, development, and integration of edge artificial intelligence, autonomous unmanned vehicles, and physical automation for military systems. It operates across the technology stack, sponsoring programs in neuromorphic computing, multi-spectral sensor fusion, and swarming autonomy, and contracts commercial vendors and academic institutions to build and transition these technologies into defense platforms.
1. A government agency that funds and oversees R&D contracts for autonomous systems and edge computing hardware and software.
2. Neuromorphic processors for radar signal processing, multi-spectral sensor fusion algorithms, and software for collaborative autonomous swarming and electronic warfare.
3. On-device inference for contested electromagnetic environments, collaborative swarming, autonomous defensive electronic warfare, and unmanned aerial vehicle payload release.
4. Contract awards, cooperative research agreements, and government programs that integrate commercial hardware and software into military platforms.
5. Unmanned aerial vehicles, attritable aircraft, defense platforms, and military aircraft maintenance operations.
6. The Department of the Air Force and other U.S. defense forces.
7. It contracts commercial technology developers and academic institutions to build and integrate components and systems into deployed military platforms.
8. It combines multi-domain defense mission needs with direct funding and oversight of foundational edge AI and neuromorphic hardware research.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: DARPA, GA-ASI, BrainChip, BAE Systems, Sarcos, Concurrent Technologies Corporation, NREC, Yaskawa Motoman, CapSen Robotics, and AFIT.
Organization type: A government research and development agency.
Business model: Government appropriations and contract awards.
Scale and maturity: A highly established organization with over 11,500 personnel across more than 40 locations that recently awarded over $340 million in swarm-defense AI R&D contracts.
Geography: Based and operates within the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it conducts comprehensive aerospace, space, and cyberspace research to advance air and space power.

points.name: NASA Ames Laboratory
points.description: US government research agency developing autonomous systems and robotic technologies for spacecraft and planetary exploration.
points.bullets:
A government research agency that develops autonomy software and control algorithms for space robotics, autonomous unmanned ground vehicles, autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles, self-assembling structures, computer vision, and human robot interaction to reduce astronaut workload and extend mission capabilities for the aerospace sector.
1. A government research agency that develops autonomy software and control algorithms for robotic systems.
2. On-device autonomy software, control algorithms and computer vision designed to handle communication latency, system complexity and crew workload management.
3. Autonomous navigation, free-flying space robotics, self-assembly, human robot interaction and on-board decision making.
4. Research outputs and autonomy software developed for aerospace missions.
5. Spacecraft, free-flying space robots, autonomous aerial vehicles, autonomous ground vehicles and space missions.
6. Aerospace sector organizations, space missions and government programs.
7. Its autonomy software is integrated into robotic platforms operated by space programs rather than sold as commercial products.
8. It addresses critical challenges such as communication latency, cost reduction, crew workload management and system complexity in domains where commercial robotics companies have less operational experience.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Operated under the broader umbrella of a national civilian space program with a strategic partnership to establish a generative AI laboratory.
Organization type: Government research agency.
Business model: Government-funded research programs.
Scale and maturity: A highly established, foundational contributor with over 400 personnel and a track record of historic deployments dating back to the 1990s.
Geography: Based in Sunnyvale, California, focusing on remote scientific discovery and inspection capabilities for space missions.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it focuses on broader scientific discovery and engineering research, including evaluating new technologies using publicly accessible datasets.

points.name: Bain Capital Ventures
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage autonomous consumer robotics startups.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that invests in early- and growth-stage companies across edge and physical AI, backing robot makers, autonomy software developers and AI inference silicon companies, alongside broader B2B software.
1. A venture capital firm that funds startups building robots, autonomy software, developer tools and AI inference chips.
2. Capital deployed across wheeled general-purpose robots, warehouse autonomy software, AI inference accelerators and robotic simulation platforms.
3. Portfolio investments target warehouse piece picking, autonomous mobile robot navigation, on-device inference acceleration and robotic machine design.
4. Funding provided through early and growth-stage equity rounds, including Series A and Series B investments.
5. Investments span warehouse automation, robotic hardware design, AI silicon and broader enterprise software infrastructure.
6. The portfolio companies it sells its capital to include robot makers, AI model developers, chip designers and developer tool builders.
7. The firm holds minority equity stakes in startups that design robots, build autonomy software and manufacture inference silicon for downstream industrial and enterprise users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Part of the larger Bain Capital organization; portfolio companies include Kiva Systems, Sunday Robotics, Vention, Gather AI, Mind Robotics, Etched and TerraFirma.
Organization type: A multi-stage venture capital firm and a subsidiary of the broader Bain Capital asset management organization.
Business model: Fund management generating returns through carried interest and management fees on raised capital across multiple investment funds.
Scale and maturity: A firm that recently raised $1.9 billion in new funds, with a portfolio spanning from early-stage startups to acquired robotics companies.
Geography: Based in the United States, deploying capital into American and global startups.
Beyond physical AI: The firm maintains a broad B2B software and fintech investment practice outside of its edge and physical AI portfolio.

points.name: Conviction
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage AI and robotics startups.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that funds early-stage companies building edge and physical AI hardware, including home robots and inference silicon.
1. A venture capital firm.
2. It provides equity funding to startups that build robots and AI hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Benchmark.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: Fund management and venture capital returns.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage AI fund.
Geography: Based and operates in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: It invests broadly in artificial intelligence startups beyond the physical AI ecosystem.

points.name: Greenoaks
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage physical AI and robotics startups.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that provides funding to early-stage physical automation and AI startups, acting as a financial investor rather than building silicon, sensors or deployed systems directly, for technology entrepreneurs.
1. A venture capital firm that funds early-stage robotics and AI companies.
2. The organization delivers capital investment to startups.
3. The firm serves technology entrepreneurs and early-stage companies operating within the robotics, broader software and fintech markets.
4. It acts as a capital provider within the broader technology value chain rather than operating as a robotics OEM or component supplier.
5. A distinguishing characteristic of this firm is its broad technology investment portfolio, which features a specialized but small allocation specifically dedicated to robotics companies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Neil Mehta leads the firm, which funded The Bot Company and co-led Anthropic's Series H.
Organization type: The entity is a privately held venture capital firm that manages investment funds on behalf of its limited partners.
Business model: The firm makes money through fund management.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2012, the mature investment firm has grown to manage approximately seven billion dollars in assets under management.
Geography: The venture capital firm is based in the United States and deploys capital into technology companies globally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond its niche investments in physical automation, the broader organization focuses heavily on funding enterprise software, financial technology and e-commerce businesses.

points.name: Eclipse
points.description: Venture capital firm funding early-stage physical AI and general-purpose robotics startups.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that funds and incubates startups building physical AI, robotics, and autonomous systems for the physical economy. It backs companies developing foundational AI models, simulation platforms, and complete deployed robotic systems, while explicitly excluding humanoid robotics in favor of task-specific industrial applications. The firm targets the upper layers of the physical automation stack rather than lower-level silicon or components.
1. A venture capital firm that raises early-stage and growth funds to invest in physical-world startups.
2. Financial capital and strategic support directed toward startups building foundational models, physics simulation platforms, and deployed robotic systems.
3. Funding, incubation, and board-level governance for robotics, physical AI, and autonomous vehicle startups.
4. Equity investments and incubation services provided through early-stage and growth-stage venture funds.
5. Warehouses, construction, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, autonomous vehicles, and laboratory automation.
6. Early-stage and growth-stage robotics, physical AI, and automation startups.
7. It acts as an investor that builds and curates a portfolio of robotics, sensor, and physical automation companies across various deployment contexts.
8. Its exclusive focus on the physical world and its strategic avoidance of humanoid robotics in favor of immediate, task-specific industrial applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Portfolio companies include Genesis AI, The Bot Company, Capstan Medical, Bedrock Robotics, Simbe Robotics, Humble Robotics, Wayve, Cerebras, and Foxglove.
Organization type: Privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: Fund management and venture capital returns through equity investments in physical-world startups.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015 with approximately $10 billion in regulatory assets under management, including a recent $1.3 billion fund for physical AI startups.
Geography: It operates by funding startups within the global robotics and physical automation markets.
Beyond physical AI: Venture capital investment in the physical world is its entire and exclusive focus, with no other business activities.

points.name: Rivian
points.description: California automaker developing an on-device AI compute platform to power autonomous electric vehicles.
points.bullets:
A vertically integrated electric vehicle maker that builds complete cars and trucks along with the full autonomous driving stack to run them, including custom inference silicon, sensor suites, autonomy software and driving models, manufacturing the vehicles it will deploy as robotaxis for ride-hailing networks and commercial delivery.
1. An automaker that designs and manufactures electric vehicles and develops the full self-driving stack to run on them.
2. A custom 5nm AI processor delivering 1,600 TOPS, an 11-camera, five-radar, one-lidar sensor platform, and a large driving model trained for Level 4 autonomous driving.
3. Hands-free highway driving assistance and Level 4 fully autonomous driving for robotaxi deployment.
4. Complete electric vehicles sold to consumers and autonomous vehicles supplied to ride-hailing fleets.
5. Robotaxis, autonomous commercial delivery trucks, consumer electric pickup trucks and SUVs.
6. Ride-hailing platforms, e-commerce logistics operators and consumers.
7. It designs and manufactures complete vehicles and the autonomy stacks inside them, supplying robotaxis to a ride-hailing operator.
8. It vertically integrates custom inference silicon, multi-sensor hardware, autonomy software and vehicle manufacturing in-house.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It has a $1.25 billion robotaxi deal with Uber, supplies autonomous delivery trucks to Amazon, and spun out the robotics venture Mind Robotics.

Key partners and customers: Thistle Systems serves as its official UK integration partner, and MotionTech partners to scale deployments across Europe.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Robot and system hardware sales and robots-as-a-service agreements.
Scale and maturity: An established commercial entity with more than 250 employees and hundreds of robots already deployed in active production environments.
Geography: Headquartered near Cincinnati, Ohio, operating extensively across the United States and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: Warehouse automation and physical AI represent the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Magazino
points.description: German warehouse robotics company building autonomous mobile robots that perform AI-driven shelf picking of standardized items.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile manipulation robots for warehouse picking and transport, integrating on-device perception, control software and physical hardware into complete systems for logistics operations.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells mobile warehouse robots with manipulation arms.
2. Autonomous mobile robot platforms combining on-device perception, control algorithms, navigation systems and physical manipulation arms.
3. Autonomous navigation, mobile manipulation, piece picking of rectangular and irregularly shaped objects, and internal transport.
4. Complete robots and mobile manipulation platforms.
5. Warehouses and intralogistics operations.
6. Logistics operators and warehouse automation customers.
7. It designs and builds complete robots that are integrated into warehouse operations by its parent intralogistics enterprise.
8. It solves both transport and picking problems in order fulfillment, whereas many competitors address only mobile transport.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its parent company is a European intralogistics enterprise.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded intralogistics company.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robotic systems.
Scale and maturity: It employs over 160 experts and operates as an integrated subsidiary following its acquisition in August 2023.
Geography: It is based in Munich, Germany, and operates within the European warehouse automation market.
Beyond physical AI: Warehouse robotics and mobile manipulation represent the entire focus of the business.

points.name: Attabotics
points.description: Canadian warehouse robotics company deploying 3D cube storage and retrieval systems for automated order fulfillment.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells three-dimensional robotic cube storage and retrieval systems for goods-to-person warehouse fulfillment, combining proprietary robotic shuttles, modular grid structures, and control software for logistics operators.
1. A robotics company that builds and sells automated storage and retrieval systems and proprietary robotic shuttles for warehouse fulfillment.
2. Robotic shuttles that navigate horizontally and vertically within a high-density three-dimensional grid structure to retrieve inventory and deliver it to human pick stations.
3. High-density goods-to-person storage and retrieval, enabling access to any SKU in a single move and pick initiation in under sixty seconds while reducing warehouse footprint by up to 85%.
4. Complete automated storage and retrieval systems, including proprietary robots, modular storage infrastructure, and control software, installed directly or through integration partners.
5. Warehouses, e-fulfillment centers, and logistics supply chain operations.
6. E-fulfillment and logistics operators, major retailers, and systems integrators.
7. Its robotic storage systems are integrated by partners into end-to-end warehouse automation systems or sold directly to fulfillment operators.
8. It replaces traditional warehouse rows and aisles with a three-dimensional cubic structure that provides immediate direct access to any inventory location without pre-stacking or advance digging.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is part of LaFayette Systems, counts Honeywell Ventures as a strategic investor, and partners with integrators including SAVOYE North America and Extolla.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a privately owned material handling automation conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware and system sales of storage infrastructure and proprietary robots, along with associated software and support services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016 with 201-500 employees, having raised CAD $200M before being acquired and relaunched in 2025 after financial collapse.
Geography: Based in Calgary, Alberta, Canada, with manufacturing in Kentucky and operations serving the North American market and Australia.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is dedicated to warehouse automation and physical robotics.

points.name: Daifuku Co., Ltd.
points.description: Japanese warehouse automation company deploying AGVs, mobile robots, and AI-enabled storage systems for intralogistics and material handling.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator and robotics OEM that builds comprehensive warehouse and intralogistics automation solutions incorporating AI-enabled robotics, automated storage and retrieval systems, autonomous forklifts, mobile robots, conveyors, and truck loading systems for distribution centers and manufacturing environments.
1. A systems integrator and robotics OEM that designs, manufactures, and installs complete material handling automation systems, including autonomous forklifts, mobile robots, and automated storage and retrieval systems.
2. Material handling automation systems incorporating on-device intelligence, IoT, digital twins, and AI-enabled robotics for autonomous palletizing, truck loading, storage, retrieval, and goods movement.
3. Autonomous navigation for forklifts and mobile robots, automated storage and retrieval, piece picking, palletizing, truck loading, and fleet orchestration of integrated warehouse automation.
4. Complete automation systems, robots, and material handling equipment installed directly into customer warehouses, distribution centers, and factories as integrated end-to-end solutions.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers, factories, and manufacturing facilities across e-commerce, grocery, pharmaceuticals, retail, and home improvement sectors.
6. Logistics operators, retailers, e-commerce companies, grocers, pharmaceutical distributors, and manufacturers operating distribution centers and production facilities.
7. It designs and manufactures its own robots and material handling equipment and integrates them into end-to-end automation systems installed in customer facilities.
8. It delivers comprehensive integrated solutions combining multiple automation technologies with an explicit strategic commitment to physical AI as a core driver of autonomous material handling capabilities.
points.profile:
Organization type: A publicly traded global corporation and material handling equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and material handling equipment, combined with systems integration services and contracts for installed automation.
Scale and maturity: An established global enterprise operating worldwide with multiple R&D facilities in Japan and the United States, recently opening a Tokyo R&D hub staffed initially by 30 personnel with plans to expand to 50.
Geography: Based in Japan and operating globally, with R&D facilities in Tokyo, Kyoto, and Shiga, Japan, and an Intralogistics Innovation Center in Bolingbrook, Illinois.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the entirety of its business, focused entirely on intralogistics and material handling solutions.

points.name: GreyOrange
points.description: US robotics company deploying AI-driven autonomous mobile robots and orchestration software to automate warehouse fulfillment operations.
points.bullets:
A warehouse robotics company that builds autonomous mobile robots and a vendor-agnostic orchestration platform to automate fulfillment operations for retailers and third-party logistics providers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots paired with a multi-agent orchestration platform and warehouse design simulation tools.
2. Autonomous mobile robots for goods-to-person fulfillment integrated with a cloud-based multi-agent AI orchestration platform that uses real-time inventory and operations data for dynamic task allocation and fleet coordination.
3. Real-time warehouse orchestration, multi-robot fleet coordination, goods-to-person sorting, dynamic order fulfillment, inventory slotting, and high-fidelity warehouse flow simulation.
4. Complete robots, licensed orchestration software, warehouse design simulation tools, and integration services delivered through systems integrator partners.
5. Retail fulfillment centers, e-commerce warehouses, store inventory management, and omnichannel logistics operations.
6. Third-party logistics providers, retailers, e-commerce companies, and systems integrators.
7. It builds its own robots and licenses its orchestration software directly to warehouse operators while coordinating multi-vendor deployments through a network of integration partners.
8. A vendor-agnostic orchestration platform integrates mixed fleets of third-party robotic hardware alongside its own robots, avoiding proprietary hardware lock-in.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Google Cloud, Bailey Equipment & Intralogistics, Active Ants, Exol, H&M Group, Dorman, Anthelion.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Robot hardware sales, licensed software subscriptions, and robotics-as-a-service deployments.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2012, it has raised over $500 million in funding, including a $135 million Series D round, and operates deployments across more than 100 enterprise sites globally.
Geography: Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, with offices and deployment operations across the Americas, Europe, and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the absolute core of the organization's overall mission as a pure-play provider of advanced fulfillment technologies.

points.name: Dematic
points.description: US warehouse automation company deploying AI-driven robotics and software systems for supply chain fulfillment.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator that designs, builds, and installs end-to-end warehouse automation and fulfillment solutions, combining autonomous mobile robots, conveyors, sortation systems, and control software for supply chain operators.
1. A systems integrator that builds and deploys integrated warehouse automation systems combining mobile robots, fixed conveyors, and execution software for logistics facilities.
2. The core technology consists of autonomous mobile robots for goods-to-person and point-to-point transport, integrated with warehouse execution software and digital twin-based AI control towers built on Omniverse and cloud AI platforms.
3. The specific capabilities it delivers include goods-to-person piece picking, pallet and shelf transport, sortation, fleet orchestration, and supply chain analytics.
4. Customers get it as integrated automation systems, software suites, and lifecycle services installed in their facilities.
5. The systems are used in warehouses, distribution centers, and manufacturing facilities for eCommerce, omnichannel fulfillment, grocery, apparel, and general merchandise logistics.
6. The types of customer it sells to are logistics operators, retailers, manufacturers, wholesalers, and third-party logistics providers.
7. Its position in the value chain is as an integrator that combines mobile robots from other makers and its own fixed automation and software into complete deployed systems for end customers.
8. Its approach is distinguished by combining mobile robots with fixed conveyors and warehouse execution software in a software-driven intelligence architecture, validated by customers in an integration facility before deployment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include KION Group as parent company, Google Cloud for AI and ML technologies, NVIDIA for Omniverse digital twin platforms, and Dexterity for robotic arm integration.
Organization type: The organization is a subsidiary of a publicly traded industrial truck and supply chain company.
Business model: It makes money through system integration contracts, hardware sales, software licenses, and lifecycle service and spare parts agreements.
Scale and maturity: The organization has over 11,000 employees and operates in more than 35 countries.
Geography: It is based in Atlanta, Georgia, USA, with a Solution Center in Grand Rapids, Michigan, and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire focus and core mission of the organization.

points.name: Geek+ Robotics
points.description: Global robotics company deploying AI-driven picking and sorting robots to automate warehouse logistics.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that builds autonomous mobile robots, autonomous forklifts and robotic arms, along with fleet management and simulation software, to automate warehousing and factory operations for global enterprises.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells autonomous mobile robots, robotic arms and forklifts, alongside integrated software platforms.
2. On-device AI robotics, unified fleet management software and 3D simulation tools that coordinate transport, picking and sorting hardware.
3. Autonomous navigation, piece picking, sorting, pallet transport and scalable fleet orchestration without major infrastructural changes.
4. Complete robots and vehicles, alongside licensed management software, deployed directly into end-user facilities.
5. Warehouses, factories and intralogistics supply chain facilities.
6. Manufacturing and electrical distribution enterprises operating factory and warehouse facilities.
7. The organization builds its own robots and software and installs them as integrated automation systems directly for end-user facility operators.
8. End-to-end automation that combines picking, sorting, transport and forklift operations under a single platform with 99.99% movement accuracy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Major international clients in the manufacturing and electrical distribution sectors.
Organization type: A publicly traded company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and vehicles alongside software licenses.
Scale and maturity: The world's first publicly listed autonomous mobile robot warehouse robotics company, with deployments across over 770 client facilities globally.
Geography: Based globally with deployments across international client facilities, including notable installations in Shanghai and the United Kingdom.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play robotics and automation provider entirely dedicated to physical AI, intralogistics and smart supply chain technologies.

points.name: Yamaha Robotics
points.description: Japanese robotics company manufacturing high-speed industrial assembly and vision-integrated inspection robots.
points.bullets:
An industrial robot maker that builds SCARA, Cartesian, and pick-and-place robots, along with AI-driven vision cameras and control software for assembly, packaging, and surface-mount manufacturing. The company serves industrial and warehouse customers, supplying robotic hardware and vision subsystems rather than manufacturing its own inference silicon. It has recently expanded its automation footprint into precision agriculture for orchard and vineyard operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells industrial robotic arms and vision cameras for factory automation.
2. SCARA, single-axis, and 2-axis pick-and-place robotic actuators integrated with shared vision cameras for real-time conveyor tracking and automated inspection library generation.
3. High-speed pick and place, conveyor tracking, vision-guided packaging, surface-mount and through-hole part handling, and automated inspection programming.
4. Complete robotic arms, vision cameras, and control software sold to industrial manufacturers.
5. Factories, warehouses, assembly lines, surface-mount electronics manufacturing, and precision agriculture.
6. Industrial manufacturers, warehouse operators, and orchard and vineyard operators.
7. Its robotic arms, vision sensors, and control software are integrated into assembly and packaging lines by industrial manufacturers.
8. It achieves high-speed vision coordination by sharing a single camera across up to four robots, enabling 225 picks per minute on moving conveyors, and provides AI tools that automatically generate inspection libraries to reduce manual programming.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: YRG, Inc. supports customers with the company's robotics solutions and expertise.
Organization type: A privately held corporate division operating under a larger, established parent conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic arms, vision cameras, and control software.
Scale and maturity: A mature market player with over 40 years of experience dating back to 1976, strengthened by recent acquisitions to expand its automation footprint.
Geography: Based in Japan, operating globally within established industrial control ecosystems with recent physical expansion into the agricultural sector.
Beyond physical AI: It is part of a vast, diversified global conglomerate historically known for manufacturing motorcycles, marine equipment, and musical instruments.

points.name: Toshiba
points.description: Japanese industrial technology company developing autonomous mobile robots for mail sorting and warehouse automation.
points.bullets:
A multinational industrial technology conglomerate that builds and deploys autonomous mobile robot solutions and goods-to-person warehouse automation systems for postal and logistics operators. It combines its own mobile robot hardware, navigation software, lithium-ion batteries, and workflow management into complete deployed automation platforms, and also sells rugged barcode, printing, and cloud tracking systems for industrial environments.
1. A robot maker and systems integrator that builds autonomous mobile robots and goods-to-person systems and installs them as complete deployed automation platforms for logistics customers.
2. Autonomous mobile robot hardware using 2D barcode navigation, conveyor-based mail sorting mechanisms, fast-charging lithium-ion batteries, and goods-to-person shelf-moving algorithms integrated with cloud-based task routing and asset tracking software.
3. Autonomous mobile robot navigation in warehouse environments, mail sorting, goods-to-person item retrieval, asset and inventory tracking, and document workflow digitization.
4. Complete mobile robots, integrated goods-to-person systems, and cloud-enabled workflow software installed directly into customer facilities.
5. Postal sorting facilities, warehouses, factory floors, and logistics distribution centers.
6. National postal operators, logistics distribution centers, and manufacturing teams.
7. It builds its own mobile robots and batteries and integrates them into complete automation systems installed inside customer facilities.
8. Over sixty years of postal system expertise and the ability to customize mobile robot sorting solutions for regional postal requirements distinguish its deployments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It collaborates with Azerpost and Kazpost on automation deployments and is a client of Standard Robots.
Organization type: A publicly traded multinational conglomerate operating through an automation and security systems division.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales, integrated system installations, and cloud software solutions for industrial operations.
Scale and maturity: A large established entity with active international deployments and proof-of-concept projects in Central Asia and Japan.
Geography: Based in Japan, it operates internationally with notable market presence and deployments in Central Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, the broader conglomerate provides digital workflow solutions including document digitization, rugged printers, multifunction devices, real-time asset tracking, and custom operational dashboards for manufacturing and logistics teams.

points.name: IAM Robotics
points.description: US warehouse robotics company deploying autonomous mobile robots for order fulfillment and material transport.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds autonomous mobile picking robots for warehouse fulfillment, combining mobile bases, manipulator arms, suction grippers, and scanning stations. It supplies complete mobile manipulation robots to logistics operators and distributors to automate piece picking and material handling.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile picking robots for warehouse fulfillment.
2. Wheeled mobile bases paired with industrial manipulator arms and suction grippers, guided by pre-scanned product databases, computer vision, and autonomous navigation software.
3. Autonomous warehouse navigation, piece picking at human-level speeds, 3D product scanning, and mobile manipulation for order fulfillment.
4. Complete robots and accompanying scanning hardware.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers, and order fulfillment operations.
6. Logistics operators, distributors, retailers, and healthcare supply chain companies.
7. It sells complete mobile manipulation robots to warehouse operators that deploy them directly in their facilities.
8. It uses pre-scanned product databases and pre-computed grasp strategies with suction grippers to achieve exceptionally fast picking speeds.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It integrates industrial arms from a robot OEM and counts major retailers and robotics integrators among its partners.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and scanning equipment.
Scale and maturity: A mature startup founded in 2012 with commercial pilots and deployments supporting customers worldwide.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating primarily within the logistics and distribution market.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play company whose entire focus is dedicated to the development and deployment of warehouse automation technologies.

points.name: Churchill Capital Corp XI
points.description: Blank-check acquisition company taking humanoid robotics firms public through SPAC mergers.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded special purpose acquisition company that merged with a humanoid robotics company to take it public, functioning as a financial vehicle rather than a provider of physical AI technology.
1. A publicly traded blank check company formed for the purpose of effecting a merger or business combination.

Key partners and customers: It is merging with Agility Robotics and counts Humanoid Global as a minority investor.
Organization type: A publicly traded special purpose acquisition company.
Business model: It makes money through capital raised in its initial public offering and held in trust to fund a merger target, generating returns to sponsors and shareholders from the combined entity.
Scale and maturity: It is a publicly traded entity on NASDAQ that facilitated a merger valued at approximately $2.5 billion.
Geography: It is based in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Its activities consist entirely of corporate finance and identifying merger targets, with no operational role outside the transaction.

points.name: Vishay Precision Group
points.description: Pennsylvania sensor manufacturer engineering custom miniature force and torque sensing solutions for humanoid robotic joints and fingertips.
points.bullets:
A sensor manufacturer that designs precision sensors, sensor-based measurement systems, special resistors, and strain gauges for physical automation systems. It supplies co-engineered force and torque sensing components that enable humanoid robots to perceive force, torque, and pressure at every joint. The organization serves humanoid robotics developers that require customized sensing capabilities adapted to exact space, load, and performance constraints.
1. A component supplier that makes custom strain gauges and force-torque sensors sold into humanoid robots.
2. Strain gauge-based force and torque sensing technologies engineered for high sensitivity, wide temperature stability, and minimal drift.
3. Tactile and proprioceptive sensing that provides real-time feedback of force, torque, and pressure at every robot joint.
4. Precision sensors and strain gauges delivered as components with comprehensive integration support from concept through production calibration.
5. Humanoid robots.
6. Humanoid robotics developers.
7. Its sensors are designed into the joints of robots built by humanoid makers.
8. It provides highly customized, co-engineered sensors rather than off-the-shelf components, leveraging aerospace-grade expertise.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its sensors supply the robots of Agility Robotics.
Organization type: A specialized technology enterprise operating through a dedicated precision sensors division.
Scale and maturity: A mature enterprise with six decades of expertise that booked $1.0M in humanoid robotics orders in a single quarter.
Geography: Based in Malvern, Pennsylvania, USA, operating within the global humanoid robotics and advanced precision sensor markets.
Beyond physical AI: Its physical AI and advanced robotics focus centers entirely on applying decades of specialized force and strain gauge expertise to physical automation.

points.name: Isuzu
points.description: Japanese automaker developing Level 4 autonomous buses for driverless public transit.
points.bullets:
A commercial vehicle maker that develops Level 4 autonomous buses by integrating on-device AI compute, perception software and sensors into its electric and diesel vehicle platforms for the public transportation sector.
1. A vehicle maker that builds and sells commercial buses and trucks, now integrating autonomous driving stacks into complete self-driving vehicles.
2. Autonomous bus systems built by combining production commercial vehicle hardware with external edge AI system-on-a-chip compute and open-source autonomy software.
3. Level 4 autonomous navigation for commercial transit, fail-operational self-driving and high-capacity public mobility.
4. Complete autonomous vehicles built from production chassis and integrated third-party edge AI silicon and software stacks.
5. Autonomous buses and commercial transit vehicles.
6. Public transportation operators and municipal transit agencies.
7. It builds its own commercial vehicle chassis and integrates external compute and software stacks into them to create complete autonomous vehicles.
8. It combines robust commercial vehicle hardware with strategic partnerships in edge AI silicon and open-source autonomous software to deliver scalable transit solutions.

Key partners and customers: TIER IV, NVIDIA and Gatik.ai.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.

points.name: Nissan
points.description: Japanese automotive company developing Level 4 autonomous vehicles using NVIDIA's edge AI compute platform.
points.bullets:
A global automaker that designs and builds passenger and commercial vehicles while integrating third-party inference silicon, lidar sensors, and autonomy software to develop Level 4 autonomous vehicles and driver-assistance systems for the personal mobility and ride-hailing markets.

2. AI-enhanced radar for scene understanding and lane-keeping, combined with autonomous vehicle compute platforms and end-to-end driving models integrated into electric and internal combustion vehicles.
3. Hands-free highway driving, obstacle detection, and Level 4 autonomous navigation for robotaxi deployments.
4. Complete passenger cars and electric vehicles equipped with advanced driver-assistance systems, supplied to ride-hailing networks and consumers.

6. Consumers, ride-hailing operators, and autonomous driving software companies using its vehicles as testbeds.
7. The company builds complete vehicles and acts as an integrator, buying inference silicon, simulation tools, and autonomy software to embed in its own cars.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Wayve, Luminar, Uber, Applied Intuition, and Amazon Web Services.
Organization type: A publicly traded global automaker.

Geography: Based in Japan, it operates globally with autonomous pilots in Tokyo and manufacturing facilities in Smyrna.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI and autonomous driving, the organization designs, manufactures, and sells traditional passenger cars and commercial vehicles.

points.name: PROCEPT BioRobotics
points.description: Surgical robotics company deploying AI-enabled ultrasound systems to plan and execute personalized waterjet prostate treatments.
points.bullets:
A surgical robotics company that develops and manufactures complete robotic systems for performing waterjet ablation therapy in urology, integrating real-time ultrasound imaging, on-device AI treatment planning, and robotic actuators. It builds and sells these robotic platforms to hospitals to enable minimally invasive prostate resection for treating benign prostatic hyperplasia.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete surgical robotic systems for urological procedures.
2. The core technology combines heat-free waterjet ablation, real-time ultrasound imaging, and on-device AI models for image-guided treatment planning and autonomous tissue removal within surgeon-defined parameters.
3. It delivers Level 3 autonomous robotic prostate resection, ultrasound-guided tissue ablation, and AI-interpreted surgical planning.
4. Hospitals receive complete surgical robotic systems.
5. The machines and procedures are used in hospitals for urological surgery and prostate resection.
6. The company sells to hospitals and urological surgeons.
7. It builds complete surgical robots and installs them in hospital operating rooms.
8. Its approach uses heat-free waterjet ablation rather than thermal energy, minimizing tissue damage to preserve sexual function and continence.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its systems are installed in McKenzie-Willamette Medical Center and over 350 hospitals worldwide.
Organization type: It is a publicly traded company listed on Nasdaq.
Business model: It makes money through surgical robotic system sales.
Scale and maturity: It went public in 2021 and has deployed systems in over 350 hospitals globally.
Geography: The company is based in San Jose, California, and operates globally with an established domestic presence and planned expansion into the United Kingdom.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization manages an extensive clinical evidence pipeline with over 250 peer-reviewed publications and established Medicare reimbursement codes.

points.name: Stryker

A medical device company that builds and sells robotic-arm-assisted surgical platforms for orthopedic procedures, integrating on-device inference, proprietary sensors, and haptic actuators for hospitals and surgeons.

2. Robotic arms with haptic feedback boundaries, 3D CT-based preoperative planning, real-time bone modeling, and proprietary high-speed cameras for intraoperative guidance.
3. Sub-millimeter bone cutting accuracy, intraoperative planning, active adjustment, and robotic-assisted joint replacement.
4. Complete robotic surgical systems, handheld robotic tools, and compatible implants sold to healthcare facilities.
5. Orthopedic surgeries including total knee, partial knee, total hip, and spinal procedures in hospitals.
6. Hospitals, surgeons, and healthcare systems.
7. Its complete robotic systems are deployed in operating rooms by healthcare providers for surgical procedures.
8. It tightly integrates 3D CT-based preoperative planning with real-time active adjustment and haptic feedback to enforce sub-millimeter cutting accuracy.

Key partners and customers: IRCAD North America for surgical training and Memorial Healthcare for clinical deployments.

points.name: Emerson

An industrial automation technology company that makes controllers, drives, instruments, software, and ruggedized industrial PCs for factories and process plants. It provides edge computing hardware for physical AI workloads and a cloud operations platform for industrial autonomy. Its automation solutions are sold to industrial manufacturers to optimize operations.

2. Ruggedized industrial PCs with AI-accelerated computing power designed for harsh environments, combined with cloud operations platforms and industrial controllers.

points.name: Nova
points.description: Machine vision provider enabling edge AI systems to process camera streams efficiently.

It provides software and encoding formats that compress video data and enable selective region-of-interest access before inference, serving robotics, IoT, and industrial automation applications where power, bandwidth, and latency are constrained.
1. A developer tools company whose video compression and machine vision software optimizes visual data feeds for edge inference.
2. Hierarchical video formats and encoding standards that allow selective access to specific regions of interest in a video feed without requiring full video decoding.
3. Low-latency visual data optimization, video compression, and efficient processing of camera streams for edge devices.
4. Licensed software and encoding standards integrated into edge AI systems by device makers.
5. Robotics, IoT, and industrial automation systems where power, bandwidth, and latency constraints are critical.
6. Device makers and engineers building robotics, IoT, and industrial automation systems.
7. Its software and encoding standards are designed into edge AI systems and robotic platforms by device makers.
8. Selective access to specific regions of interest in a video feed without requiring full video decoding, enabling lower-latency edge inference.

Geography: Based in London, United Kingdom, and operating within the global technology and media standards ecosystem.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's broader focus includes high-performance video compression, streaming, and remote visualization technologies.

points.name: Honeywell Intelligrated

A systems integrator and warehouse automation provider that designs, installs and operates end-to-end logistics ecosystems combining robotics, material handling hardware and warehouse execution software for distribution centers.

4. Complete integrated warehouse systems comprising hardware, licensed warehouse execution software, lifecycle services and maintenance.
