points.name: Serve Robotics
points.description: US service robotics company deploying autonomous sidewalk delivery robots for urban last-mile logistics.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and operator that designs, builds, and runs a fleet of Level 4 autonomous sidewalk delivery robots, and recently expanded into indoor hospital robotics through acquisition.
1. A robot maker and operator that builds autonomous sidewalk delivery robots and runs the fleet itself for last-mile logistics.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software running on NVIDIA Jetson Orin inference processors, using lidar and cameras for real-time outdoor navigation and path planning.
3. Level 4 autonomous navigation, last-mile delivery, pedestrian-safe sidewalk traversal, and fleet orchestration.
4. Complete robots and vehicles it operates itself as a delivery service, alongside licensed software and technology to a contract manufacturer.
5. Sidewalks, urban last-mile logistics, food and grocery delivery, and hospitals.
6. Food delivery platforms, quick-service restaurants, convenience stores, and healthcare facilities.
7. It builds and operates its own robots, and licenses its technology to a contract manufacturer that builds the robots for it.
8. It achieves reliable Level 4 autonomy in unpredictable public sidewalk environments using continuous learning from roughly one million miles of monthly operational data.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Magna, NVIDIA, Ouster, Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, 7-Eleven, Shake Shack, White Castle, Wing Aviation, and Diligent Robotics.
Organization type: Publicly traded company, spun off from Uber in 2021.
Business model: Delivery fees and service contracts from operating its autonomous fleet, plus software licensing and technology agreements.
Scale and maturity: Operates over 2,000 robots across 44 cities and 14 states, with over 100,000 completed deliveries since its founding in 2017.
Geography: Based in Los Angeles, California, operating in major U.S. cities.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the entire core focus and central mission of the organization's business model.

points.name: AeroVironment
points.description: Defense contractor building AI-powered unmanned aerial vehicles and autonomous loitering munitions.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and defense contractor that develops uncrewed aerial, ground, and maritime robots for government and military use, integrating edge computing, computer vision, and autonomy software into complete deployed platforms rather than individual components.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that designs and sells unmanned aircraft, loitering munitions, and ground robots for defense applications.
2. The core technology comprises fully integrated unmanned platforms combining electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, loitering munitions, modular autopilot interfaces, and onboard computer vision software for detection and tracking.
3. It delivers autonomous navigation, intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, precision strike, counter-unmanned aircraft systems, and multi-vehicle fleet orchestration.
4. Customers receive complete unmanned aircraft systems, loitering munitions, and ground robots alongside proprietary command and control software and autonomy retrofit kits.
5. Its platforms are used in defense, military, and government operations across aerial, ground, and maritime domains.
6. It sells primarily to government agencies, defense ministries, and military forces.
7. The organization operates as a prime defense contractor, designing and manufacturing complete robotic platforms and integrating its own autonomy software directly into its vehicles.
8. Its approach combines field-tested physical hardware with resilient, on-device artificial intelligence designed to operate in communications-contested environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company holds contracts with the U.S. Army and U.S. Department of Defense, collaborates with Red Cat Holdings, and acquired BlueHalo, Tomahawk Robotics, and ESAero.
Organization type: It is a publicly traded defense contractor.
Business model: The organization generates revenue through government and military contracts for unmanned systems, hardware sales, and defense procurement programs.
Scale and maturity: An established entity, it has achieved over 50,000 unmanned system deployments across more than 55 countries.
Geography: Based in the United States, it operates globally with a focus on allied defense ministries and government agencies.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the central, defining mission of the organization, driving its primary product development and market strategy for military applications.

points.name: Kratos
points.description: US defense contractor building autonomous jet-powered tactical drones for reconnaissance and strike missions with minimal human intervention.
points.bullets:
A defense contractor that designs, builds, and integrates unmanned aerial, ground, and maritime vehicles for the U.S. Department of Defense and allied militaries.
1. A defense robot and vehicle maker that builds uncrewed tactical aircraft and maritime platforms for government and military customers.
2. Jet-powered unmanned aircraft, hybrid eVTOL platforms, and autonomy-software integration for high-speed, runway-independent reconnaissance and strike missions.
3. High-speed tactical flight, runway-independent launch and recovery, reconnaissance and surveillance, and mission execution with minimal human intervention.
4. Complete uncrewed vehicles and aerial platforms integrated with command and control systems.
5. Defense, national security, tactical military operations, and autonomous delivery.
6. The U.S. Department of Defense and allied military forces.
7. As a prime contractor, it designs complete unmanned systems and integrates third-party autonomy software and mission systems onto its platforms.
8. It rapidly integrates third-party autonomous AI pilot software onto its unmanned aircraft in under 180 days and productizes affordable tactical aircraft at a sub-$500,000 price point.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Boeing, Airbus, the Crucis Companies, and a hybrid eVTOL operator named Chaparral.
Organization type: A publicly traded defense contractor.
Business model: Government and military contracts for complete uncrewed platforms and integrated systems.
Scale and maturity: An established defense prime that produces high-performance aerial target systems and tactical UAVs in limited production for deployed national security missions.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates across domestic and allied international defense markets.
Beyond physical AI: Its broader portfolio also encompasses propulsion systems, hypersonics, space domain awareness, satellite communications, and command and control systems.

points.name: Roboteon
points.description: US software provider building AI orchestration platforms that coordinate multi-vendor robotic systems across warehouse and manufacturing environments.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds a vendor-agnostic software platform to integrate, orchestrate and optimize mixed fleets of robots from different vendors in warehousing and manufacturing operations for logistics operators and manufacturers.
1. A developer tools company whose multiagent orchestration and simulation platform logistics engineers and operators use on robots they do not make.
2. AI-driven orchestration software, an execution engine, and simulation tools that connect disparate robotic hardware to warehouse and enterprise management systems.
3. Vendor-agnostic fleet orchestration, multirobot task assignment, real-time material flow optimization, and warehouse process simulation.
4. Licensed software or SaaS and integration services.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers, and manufacturing facilities.
6. Logistics operators, manufacturers, robot OEMs, and systems integrators.
7. Its software sits above individual robotic hardware to manage fleet execution, integrating robots from multiple OEMs into enterprise resource and warehouse management systems.
8. It prevents vendor lock-in by enabling seamless interoperability and intelligent task assignment across mixed fleets of automation equipment from different brands.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It has certified integration with SAP EWM and Microsoft Dynamics 365, and works with robot OEMs and systems integrators as complementary partners.
Organization type: A privately held software company.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions and integration services.
Scale and maturity: An emerging company exhibiting at automation trade shows to showcase its robotics platform and software capabilities.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating primarily within the global warehouse automation and manufacturing markets.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play software provider whose entire focus is on robotics fulfillment applications, simulation tools, and integration capabilities for physical automation.

points.name: Superior Communications
points.description: Tennessee mobile accessories distributor deploying autonomous mobile robots for high-speed warehouse order fulfillment.
points.bullets:
A logistics operator that deploys AI-powered autonomous mobile robots to automate order fulfillment workflows within its own warehouses, serving major wireless carriers, retailers and OEMs. It procures robots through a robotics-as-a-service model and runs them in its distribution centers to optimize internal logistics. Its core business remains the distribution of mobile accessories and telecommunications equipment, using physical AI to reduce fulfillment costs.
1. An operator that runs robotic picking fleets in its own warehouses, buying robots-as-a-service rather than building them.
2. It operates fully integrated robots equipped with onboard edge AI processing, 3D vision, LiDAR sensors and robotic actuators.
3. It delivers automated piece picking and order fulfillment, achieving high pick rates with minimal human labor.
4. It gets its automation through a robotics-as-a-service model, operating the robots inside its own facilities.
5. It uses the robots in distribution centers and warehouse fulfillment operations.
6. Its customers are major wireless carriers, original equipment manufacturers and big-box retailers.
7. It buys robots from OEMs and runs them in its own warehouses.
8. It achieves up to 3,500 picks per hour with only a few warehouse associates per shift, replacing legacy conveyor-based systems.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held commercial enterprise operating as a distributor.
Scale and maturity: A mature distribution business scaling its robotic fleet from 37 to 50 units in a single facility.
Geography: It is based and operates entirely within North America, specifically in Tennessee.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, the company distributes screen protectors, phone cases and other telecommunications equipment.

points.name: Global Robotics Services
points.description: UK technology firm providing robotics-as-a-service for warehouse automation.
points.bullets:
A UK-based robot maker and systems provider that builds autonomous mobile robots and edge AI systems for warehouse logistics, offering them through a robotics-as-a-service model with flexible lease terms for commercial businesses seeking to automate intralogistics and fulfillment operations.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots and integrated sorting systems for warehouse automation.
2. Autonomous mobile robots integrating onboard sensors, inference compute, and robotic actuators, paired with AI-powered sorting tools and warehouse execution system software.
3. Parcel sorting and sequencing automation, material handling, and warehouse fulfillment operations.
4. Complete robots and integrated systems delivered as robotics-as-a-service with flexible lease terms and lower upfront investment.
5. Warehouses, logistics fulfillment centers, and parcel sorting operations.
6. Commercial businesses and logistics operators seeking to automate intralogistics and material handling.
7. The company builds and deploys its own robots and edge AI systems directly into warehouse operators' facilities.
8. A robotics-as-a-service business model that lets clients deploy automation without heavy upfront capital expenditures.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: UniUni is a named partner that implemented the company's warehouse sorting and sequencing automation across its North American warehouses.
Organization type: A privately held technology firm.
Business model: Robotics-as-a-service with flexible lease terms and lower upfront investment fees.
Scale and maturity: An active market participant competing against established, well-funded players in the logistics automation space.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom, operating in the broader regional or global logistics automation market including North America.
Beyond physical AI: Warehouse robotics deployment constitutes the entirety of the company's commercial business model and overall mission.

points.name: Comau
points.description: Italian automation and robotics manufacturer building vision-based piece-picking systems and collaborative robots for smart manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that builds industrial robots, collaborative robots and wearable exoskeletons and installs complete factory automation systems for heavy industry.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells industrial and collaborative robots, exoskeletons and integration services.
2. Six-axis articulated robots, high-payload collaborative robots with collision-avoidance sensors, mechanically powered exoskeletons and AI-enabled vision-based piece-picking systems.
3. High-payload articulated manipulation, collaborative human-robot operation, overhead and lower-back worker assistance and automated bin picking of heterogeneous objects.
4. Complete robots, wearable robotics, proprietary robot control software and fully integrated production cells and logistics systems.
5. Automotive factories, general manufacturing, warehouses, assembly lines and worker assistance in strenuous tasks.
6. Automakers, aerospace manufacturers, battery manufacturers, food and beverage producers, logistics operators and shipbuilders.
7. Its robots and exoskeletons are sold directly to manufacturers and it also designs and installs complete automation systems built from its own and other companies' machines.
8. It combines high-payload industrial robotics with collaborative and wearable human-centric technologies and AI-driven adaptability for agile manufacturing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Stellantis working with Intrinsic, Rockwell Automation, Automha and IUVO.
Organization type: Privately held industrial automation company and subsidiary.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and exoskeletons, systems integration contracts and asset optimization services.
Scale and maturity: A global enterprise founded in 1973 with $1.2 billion in annual revenue, 3,700 employees, 12 manufacturing plants and 5 innovation centers across 13 countries.
Geography: Headquartered in Turin, Italy, with manufacturing plants, innovation centers and digital hubs operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Industrial robotics, edge AI and physical automation constitute its entire business focus.

points.name: Epson
points.description: Japanese electronics and robotics company manufacturing industrial robotic arms with built-in controllers and vision guidance for factory automation.
points.bullets:
An industrial robot maker that builds and sells SCARA and 6-axis robots with embedded controllers, force sensing and vision guidance for factory automation.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells industrial robotic arms and their controllers.
2. Electromechanical arms with ballscrew-based Z-axis configurations, battery-less encoders, proprietary vibration reduction, PC-based programming software and integrated force-torque sensing.
3. High-speed planar pick-and-place, vertical insertion, precision assembly, labeling, packaging and vision-guided manipulation.
4. Complete robots, controllers and integrated workcells sold to manufacturers and integrators.
5. Automotive, electronics, semiconductor, medical device, pharmaceutical, aerospace, food processing and consumer products factories.
6. Manufacturers and systems integrators.
7. Its robots and controllers are installed in factories by manufacturers and integrated into workcells by automation integrators.
8. It is the largest SCARA robot manufacturer in the world, differentiating through high precision, low total cost of ownership via battery-less encoders and no-recurring-license software.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its controllers integrate with vision systems from sensor makers and are built into workcells by systems integrators.
Organization type: A corporate division operating within a publicly traded global technology conglomerate.
Business model: Robot and controller hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A mature manufacturer founded in 1942 that has deployed over 150,000 robotic units globally across hundreds of models.
Geography: Based in Japan with international operations and a strong presence across North and South America.
Beyond physical AI: Its broader parent company encompasses semiconductor and electronic component manufacturing, printing and visual communications.

points.name: Kawasaki
points.description: Japanese industrial manufacturer deploying AI-enabled robot arms and collaborative robots for autonomous factory tasks.
points.bullets:
An industrial robot maker that builds and sells robotic arms, collaborative robots, and integrated automation hardware for manufacturing and logistics. It also develops AI vision systems for robotic picking and partners with external AI software developers to pair its hardware platforms with advanced perception and control stacks.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells industrial robot arms, dual-arm SCARA cobots, and AI vision systems.
2. Industrial robotic arms, dual-arm SCARA cobots, and AI vision systems that combine 2D and 3D information with AI inference for masterless recognition of overlapping workpieces.
3. Vision-guided robotic picking, depalletization, and industrial automation based on open control APIs that integrate with external AI software and ROS environments.
4. Complete robots and automation hardware, alongside AI vision systems and open control APIs for external integration.
5. Factories, warehouses, life sciences labs, electronics production, and food production.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, packing and transportation firms, and systems integrators.
7. Its robots are bought as off-the-shelf hardware by systems integrators and orchestrated by external autonomy software platforms.
8. A technology-agnostic partnership model pairs decades of manufacturing reliability with open control APIs for external AI integration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Unimation, KEYENCE, NEURA Robotics, Fujitsu, Mujin, NVIDIA, Gritt, and Matsuura Packing & Transportation.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and automation systems.
Scale and maturity: A highly mature company founded in 1896, with over 160,000 robots installed worldwide and $1.3 billion in annual revenue.
Geography: Based in Japan, operating globally with deployments across international factory and warehouse environments.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire focus of the organization's robotics division, operating alongside its broader motorcycle, engine, and aerospace businesses.

points.name: Stäubli
points.description: Swiss industrial robotics manufacturer deploying six-axis robots, collaborative arms, and AMRs integrated with vision-guided AI systems for manufacturing automation.
points.bullets:
An industrial robot maker that builds and sells 6-axis, SCARA, and collaborative robotic arms for high-precision manufacturing, integrating edge AI vision systems into its hardware for on-device decision-making.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete industrial robotic arms, cobots, and control systems.
2. Six-axis and selective compliance assembly robot arm kinematics paired with collaborative safety features like millisecond contact reaction, integrated with third-party edge AI and perception systems.
3. High-speed and high-precision assembly, dexterous multi-orientation manipulation, machining, and contact-safe human-robot collaboration.
4. Complete robots, controllers, and integrated software suites sold to manufacturing operations.
5. Factories, metal processing facilities, automotive plants, and life sciences manufacturing lines.
6. Industrial manufacturers, metal processors, automotive companies, and medical device producers.
7. Its robotic arms are deployed in manufacturing facilities and integrated with external edge AI vision systems.
8. It differentiates through ultra-short cycle times, enclosed compact form factors, and full lifecycle software for predictive maintenance and virtual commissioning.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It provides robotic solutions to Palcan Group and partners with external vision system developers.
Organization type: A privately held industrial robotics manufacturer and subsidiary of a broader manufacturing conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and controllers, software licenses, and full lifecycle support services.
Scale and maturity: A mature company founded in 1892 with an annual turnover around $1.2 billion, operating in 28 countries.
Geography: Based in Horgen, Switzerland, with a global operational footprint.
Beyond physical AI: Its parent entity historically encompasses broader industrial engineering, textile machinery, and quick-connect coupling businesses.

points.name: RoboDK
points.description: Canadian robotics software company providing simulation and offline programming tools for industrial robot deployment across multiple manufacturers.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds brand-agnostic simulation and offline programming software for industrial robot arms, used by manufacturers to create, validate and deploy robot programs without interrupting production.
1. A developer tools company whose simulation and offline programming platform robotics engineers and integrators use to program and validate industrial robot arms.
2. Brand-agnostic simulation software with post processors that convert CAD files and universal API code into native robot controller programs, featuring collision-checking, motion planning and digital twin generation.
3. Offline robot programming, 3D simulation, collision-free motion planning, CAM integration for machining cells and automated program generation for over 1400 robot models.
4. Licensed software, an API and a free training academy.
5. Industrial robot arms in factories, machining cells and manufacturing automation.
6. Manufacturers, integrators and industrial robot users.
7. Its software sits between CAD design files and physical robot controllers, generating programs deployed onto robots made by major industrial arm manufacturers.
8. The platform is hardware-agnostic across a vast library of robot brands and models, offering a graphical interface that requires no proprietary coding skills.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its platform supports and integrates with robot arms from ABB, Fanuc, KUKA, Yaskawa, Universal Robots and Mecademic.
Organization type: A privately held company spun off from a university robotics laboratory.
Business model: Software licenses sold starting from a few thousand dollars per license.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, serving over 5,000 customers through 90 distributors with tens of thousands of robot deployments globally.
Geography: Headquartered in Montreal, Canada, operating worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: Industrial robotics simulation, digital twin creation and offline robot program generation represent the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Unimation
points.description: US industrial robotics company pioneering programmable robotic arms for factory automation.
points.bullets:
An industrial robot maker that designed and built the first commercially available programmable robotic arms for factory automation. It sold complete robotic hardware systems to heavy industrial manufacturers, performing physically demanding and hazardous tasks on assembly lines.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells industrial robotic arms.
2. Hydraulically and electrically actuated programmable manipulators designed for repetitive industrial tasks.
3. Programmable material handling, die-casting, spot welding, and heavy parts stacking.
4. Complete industrial robots sold as factory equipment.
5. Automotive factories and heavy industrial manufacturing.
6. Automotive manufacturers and heavy industrial companies.
7. Its robots are installed directly on factory floors by manufacturers.
8. Originated the commercial industrial robotics market with the first programmable robotic arm.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: General Motors, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, GKN, Stäubli, Westinghouse.
Organization type: Privately held commercial enterprise that was later acquired.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robotic systems and international technology licensing.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 1956, achieving decades of operation with deployments in major automotive plants.
Geography: Based in the United States with international manufacturing expansion through licensing in Japan and England.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and industrial robotics were the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Techman Robot
points.description: Taiwanese collaborative robotics company building robots with native AI vision systems and inference engines.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells collaborative robots with natively integrated vision systems and AI inference for industrial automation, serving manufacturers and electronics and semiconductor producers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells collaborative robotic arms with integrated AI vision and a humanoid robot.
2. 6-axis robotic arms with built-in vision systems, direct-mounted inspection cameras, NVIDIA GPUs for cloud-based inference and training, and proprietary flow and AI software.
3. Defect detection, visual positioning, object detection, barcode reading, smart sorting, pick-and-place, and safe human-robot collaboration.
4. Complete robots and associated proprietary software, sold through a strategic partner's global distribution network and directly to industry.
5. Factories, electronics manufacturing, semiconductor production, and automotive assembly.
6. Manufacturers, electronics and semiconductor firms, automotive companies, and small to large enterprises.
7. Its robots are distributed and integrated into factory automation by industrial partners and used directly by manufacturers.
8. Native integration of vision, AI inference, and hardware directly on the robotic arm reduces integration costs and simplifies deployment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Quanta Group, Omron, Siemens, NVIDIA, and Tesollo.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a larger hardware manufacturing group.
Business model: Hardware sales of robotic arms and associated software.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015 with 388 employees, holding an estimated 3.9 percent of the global collaborative robot market and operating worldwide.
Geography: Headquartered in Taiwan with global hubs in Shanghai, Busan, Europe, and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The company is a pure-play physical AI technology company focused entirely on the integration of artificial intelligence, vision systems, and robotic hardware.

points.name: igus
points.description: German robotics manufacturer building low-cost, maintenance-free cobots with plastic gearboxes for edge manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and component supplier that builds collaborative robotic arms, gantry robots, and a humanoid robot using proprietary dry-running plastic components, alongside strain wave gearboxes and modular robotic joints sold separately to other builders, primarily for small-to-medium enterprise manufacturers.
1. A robot maker and component supplier that designs and sells complete collaborative robots, gantry robots and a humanoid robot, plus strain wave gearboxes and modular robotic joints sold as components.
2. Lightweight, lubrication-free polymeric motion components, strain wave gearboxes and modular joints engineered for low-wear, maintenance-free operation.
3. Low-cost automation, robotic manipulation, gantry positioning, and modular joint articulation for factory automation.
4. Complete robots and cobots, mechanical components and gearboxes, free control software, and fixed-price online integration consulting.
5. Factory assembly, quality inspection, industrial production, service environments and internal transport.
6. Small-to-medium enterprise manufacturers and developers seeking low-cost automation.
7. Its components are designed into its own robots and into machines built by other automation builders.
8. Lubrication-free plastic components and strain wave gearboxes enable maintenance-free, lightweight and affordable robotic arms.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and components, plus digital consulting services and a component marketplace.
Scale and maturity: Mature global manufacturer operating a digital consulting footprint across 21 countries.
Geography: Headquartered in Germany with a global online marketplace.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and factory automation are the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: U.S. Department of Commerce
points.description: US government agency coordinating policy, investment, and supply chain initiatives to advance domestic robotics and physical AI manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A U.S. government agency that regulates physical AI technology and funds domestic manufacturing ecosystems, operating as a federal policy actor rather than a commercial provider. It administers export controls on advanced semiconductors and AI model weights, provides grants for silicon and robotics R&D, and coordinates national manufacturing networks to scale automation adoption for U.S. industry.
1. A government agency that sets export control policy and administers federal funding grants for semiconductor and robotics manufacturing.
2. Export control frameworks, federal grant programs, and domestic manufacturing extension networks are its core mechanisms.
3. It delivers regulation of dual-use AI and robotics technology, enforcement of semiconductor trade restrictions, and federal funding for domestic manufacturing.
4. Federal policy notices, export control lists, and direct grant funding are delivered to compliant industries and foreign entities.
5. Its policies apply to inference silicon, advanced computing chips, AI models, and robotics manufacturing supply chains.
6. Chip companies, robot makers, manufacturers, and foreign governments subject to U.S. trade regulations are its targets.
7. It controls the flow of edge and physical AI technology across borders and seeds domestic manufacturing capability through federal grants.
8. Its dual capacity to set international technical standards through NIST while simultaneously acting as the primary enforcer of U.S. export controls on advanced AI technology distinguishes its role.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It oversees NIST, the Bureau of Industry and Security, and the Manufacturing Extension Partnership, and engages with organizations like AUVSI.
Organization type: A cabinet-level department of the United States federal government.
Business model: It operates through federal appropriations, administering grant programs and enforcing trade regulations.
Scale and maturity: It is an established federal institution managing billions in manufacturing incentives and overseeing national trade policy.
Geography: It is based and operates within the United States, coordinating a national network across all 50 states.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, it manages broad economic policy, international trade enforcement, supply chain resilience, and weather and census bureau operations.

points.name: HIWIN Technologies
points.description: Taiwanese precision engineering firm manufacturing robotic arms and actuators for AI-powered warehouse automation.
points.bullets:
A component supplier and precision engineering manufacturer that builds motion-control systems, actuators and robotic arms for AI-driven industrial automation. It collaborates with AI software developers to produce lightweight, dual-arm robotic systems for warehouse operations and enterprise deployments.
1. A component supplier that makes precision actuators, gearboxes, linear guideways and robotic arms sold to automation developers and industrial manufacturers.
2. Precision motion control and mechanical components including linear guideways, ball screws, strain wave gear reducers, torque motor rotary tables and multi-axis robotic arms.
3. Lightweight multi-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulation with optimized strength-to-weight ratios enabling lifting of loads up to 60 kilograms in confined spaces.
4. Precision components and complete robotic arm subsystems delivered to AI software developers and industrial automation builders.
5. Warehouse operations, parcel logistics, e-commerce, retail, semiconductor manufacturing, machine tools, precision machinery and medical applications.
6. AI software developers, enterprise logistics operators, retailers, e-commerce companies and industrial automation manufacturers.
7. Its robotic arms and motion-control components are integrated by AI software developers into complete robotic platforms for warehouse deployment.
8. It optimizes the strength-to-weight ratio of its robotic arms to enable deployment in confined warehouse spaces while maintaining heavy-load lifting capacity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Strategic manufacturing and engineering partnership with Dexterity to produce robotic arms for the Mech platform.
Organization type: A publicly traded precision engineering and manufacturing company founded in 1989.
Business model: Component and hardware sales through precision engineering manufacturing contracts and industrial automation partnerships.
Scale and maturity: A global manufacturer founded in 1989 with established production scale preparing for mass production of advanced dual-arm robotic platforms.
Geography: Based in Taichung, Taiwan, with established operations across North America, Asia and Europe.
Beyond physical AI: The company's broader business revolves around providing precision motion-control systems and manufacturing expertise for industrial automation across semiconductor, machine tool, precision machinery and medical sectors.

points.name: Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory
points.description: Maryland defense research organization developing autonomous robotic teams and AI agents for complex physical environments.
points.bullets:
A university-affiliated research center and applied research facility that integrates generative AI and large language models into physical robotic systems for defense and national security applications. It functions as a systems integrator and testing center, translating frontier embodied AI research into mission-critical autonomous systems and validating them for operational deployment in complex environments.
1. A research laboratory and systems integrator that builds and validates autonomous robotic systems and advanced manufacturing capabilities for government sponsors.
2. AI reasoning engines integrating large language models and generative AI with robotic hardware for perception, planning, and task execution.
3. Autonomous perception, planning, task execution, and advanced maritime repair and manufacturing using robotic arms.
4. Mission-critical autonomous systems, validated robotic platforms, and applied research delivered through government contracts and collaborative programs.
5. Tactical military operations, disaster response, maritime industrial repair, and advanced manufacturing.
6. Defense agencies, national security sectors, the Navy, and government military organizations.
7. It translates fundamental AI research into integrated robotic platforms and validates them for deployment by government sponsors.
8. It combines fundamental research in embodied AI frameworks with a testing center that validates systems for demanding and potentially dangerous operational scenarios.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: DARPA, Microsoft, and the Navy.
Organization type: A university-affiliated research center and government-affiliated applied research facility.
Business model: Government contracts and federally funded research and development programs.
Scale and maturity: A well-established, large-scale research institution with dedicated laboratories and specialized testing facilities.
Geography: Based in Laurel, Maryland, USA, focusing research and operational efforts on supporting American defense and national security objectives.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond robotics, it explores how generative AI can accelerate materials science research, including the discovery of superconductors, and contributes to broader scientific and technological initiatives.

points.name: CATL
points.description: Chinese battery manufacturer supplying smart power management systems and energy storage for physical AI applications.
points.bullets:
A battery manufacturer that supplies lithium-ion cells, energy storage systems and skateboard chassis for electric vehicles and robots, and operates its own factory floors where it deploys humanoid, mobile and heavy-duty robots for assembly and logistics.
1. A component supplier that makes lithium-ion battery packs and cells, sold to automakers and robot makers.
2. Lithium-ion battery chemistries, including lithium iron phosphate and M3P cells, integrated with battery management systems for fast charging and thermal control.
3. High-density energy storage, fast-charging battery packs and integrated skateboard chassis for electric vehicles and robots.
4. Battery cells and packs, energy storage systems and chassis platforms sold to automakers and robot makers.
5. Electric vehicles, humanoids, factory assembly lines, stationary energy storage and urban logistics trucks.
6. Automakers, robot makers and energy utilities.
7. Its batteries are designed into electric vehicles and robots by machine makers, and it operates robots from other makers on its own production lines.
8. Vertical integration of battery materials, cell chemistry and structural chassis platforms at massive manufacturing scale.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Tesla, Unitree, BMW, Ford, Stellantis, Valmet Automotive, VinFast, Pony.ai, Baidu, Galbot, Spirit AI and Galaxy Universal Robot.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Component and hardware sales, joint-venture manufacturing and equity investments in robotics and autonomy companies.
Scale and maturity: The world's largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer, operating over twenty global manufacturing bases.
Geography: Based in China, with manufacturing and partnerships across Europe, North America and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's primary business is developing battery chemistries, manufacturing lithium-ion cells and packs, and operating large-scale energy storage and recycling facilities.

points.name: RoboStrategy
points.description: Publicly traded investment fund acquiring long-term equity stakes in pre-IPO robotics and physical AI startups.
points.bullets:
A publicly traded closed-end investment fund that deploys capital into private, pre-IPO and public robotics and physical AI companies, giving public market investors access to a concentrated portfolio of category-defining physical automation firms.
1. A venture capital firm that acquires equity stakes in private and public robotics and physical AI companies and sells publicly traded shares of the fund on a stock exchange.
2. Capital deployment and active portfolio management across the physical AI value chain.
3. Publicly traded fund shares and direct venture investments.

5. Factories, warehouses, automotive production lines, and facilities handling food, electronics, and life sciences products.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, and systems integrators.
7. Its robots and open control APIs are integrated by systems integrators and AI software developers into deployed factory and warehouse automation.
8. It combines decades of industrial robot engineering with open real-time control APIs specifically designed for external physical AI orchestration and 8-axis dexterous manipulation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with Dexterity, NEURA Robotics, Mech Mind, Coherix, and Fives DyAG.
Organization type: A corporate subsidiary of a heavy industrial manufacturing conglomerate.
Business model: Robot and controller hardware sales, automation system integration, and after-sales customer support.

Geography: Headquartered in Wixom, Michigan, USA, with sales and service offices across North and South America and a parent division based in Japan.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and industrial robotics are its entire focus.

points.name: Reeman
points.description: Robotics company building autonomous forklifts and modular AMR chassis for warehouse and factory automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous forklifts, mobile robots, and modular chassis for industrial and warehouse automation, integrating on-device AI for navigation and safety.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots, forklifts, and robot chassis.
2. Laser SLAM, 3D vision, ultrasonic radar, and neural processing units in modular compute designs for autonomous navigation and obstacle detection.
3. Autonomous navigation, multi-stop delivery, precise sub-centimeter positioning, latent transport, elevator integration, and collision prevention.
4. Complete robots, forklifts, and chassis sold with open SDKs for integration into warehouse systems.
5. Warehouses, factories, and industrial material handling operations.
6. E-commerce, third-party logistics, and manufacturing sectors.
7. Its robots are deployed directly into warehouse and factory operations by logistics and manufacturing enterprises.
8. It offers an open, plug-and-play modular architecture combined with edge computing, avoiding reliance on magnetic strips or QR codes for navigation.

Key partners and customers: Integrates with WMS and RCS systems and is compatible with ROS, Unity, and MATLAB platforms.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and chassis.
Scale and maturity: An established enterprise with over a decade of experience, holding over 200 patents, and having deployed more than 10,000 robots globally.
Geography: Based globally, deploying automation solutions across various international industrial markets.
Beyond physical AI: Designing intelligent physical automation systems and supporting software frameworks constitutes the entire focus of this organization.

points.name: AutoGuide
points.description: Robotics company deploying high-payload autonomous mobile robots for warehouse and manufacturing automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds high-payload autonomous mobile robots and automated guided vehicles for industrial material handling, integrating perception, navigation, and autonomous control into complete deployed systems for logistics and manufacturing operations.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots and automated guided vehicles.
2. Lidar-based natural features navigation and magnetic tape guidance systems integrated into mobile robotic platforms with autonomous control and real-time path planning.
3. Autonomous navigation, heavy-load transport, pallet handling, tugger operations, and conveyor deck movement in dynamic industrial environments.
4. Complete robots and vehicles, including mobile robot platforms and automated guided vehicles, sold as integrated hardware systems.
5. Warehouses, factories, manufacturing facilities, distribution centers, and healthcare logistics operations.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, distribution companies, and healthcare facilities.
7. Its mobile robots are deployed as complete systems by manufacturing and logistics operators in their facilities.
8. Heavy-load autonomous mobile robots capable of transporting up to 10,000 pounds in dynamic environments without requiring infrastructure modifications, featuring modular designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A unit of a publicly traded robotics conglomerate, merged with Mobile Industrial Robots under the MiR brand following its acquisition by Teradyne.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of mobile robots and automated guided vehicles.
Scale and maturity: Part of a combined entity employing 450 people with over 7,000 robots deployed across more than 60 countries.
Geography: Based in the United States with research and development in Massachusetts and manufacturing in Kentucky.

points.name: Hai Robotics
points.description: Chinese robotics manufacturer deploying autonomous warehouse robots that retrieve totes and cartons from tall storage racks.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and warehouse automation integrator that designs autonomous case-handling mobile robots for high-density storage and retrieval. It builds complete goods-to-person systems comprising robotic mobile bases with vertical lift mechanisms, workstations, and proprietary fleet management and warehouse execution software for logistics operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous case-handling mobile robots and complete warehouse automation systems.
2. Autonomous mobile robots equipped with vertical lift mechanisms, telescopic forks, and onboard navigation sensors integrated with a proprietary edge intelligence software platform for fleet coordination and warehouse execution without cloud dependency.
3. Autonomous case handling, high-density storage and retrieval of totes and cartons from tall racking, multi-tote transport, goods-to-person order fulfillment, fleet orchestration, and warehouse execution.
4. Complete robots, workstations, and integrated automation systems sold alongside licensed software platforms.
5. Warehouses and distribution centers handling e-commerce, retail, apparel, consumer electronics, and pharmaceutical goods.
6. Third-party logistics providers, e-commerce companies, retailers, and manufacturers.
7. It designs and builds its own robots and software, integrating them into end-to-end goods-to-person systems deployed directly within customer warehouses.
8. It extracts individual bins and cartons from standard racking using mobile robots without fixed infrastructure, enabling rapid deployment and easy reconfiguration in two to eight weeks compared to traditional automated storage and retrieval systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named partners and customers include Vanderlande, iFactory, GXO, Alibaba, and JD.com.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and workstations combined with software licenses and system integration services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016 with over 1,500 projects deployed across more than 30 countries and unicorn valuation led by 5Y Capital.
Geography: Based in Shenzhen, China with offices and operations across the United States, Europe, Japan, South Korea, Southeast Asia, and Australia.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is physical-world warehouse robotics and automation.

points.name: ASI
points.description: Industrial vehicle automation provider converting existing heavy equipment into autonomous fleets using on-device AI orchestration.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer and systems integrator that retrofits existing industrial vehicles with brand-agnostic autonomous hardware kits and licenses an industrial fleet management platform for off-road environments.
1. An autonomy software developer and integrator that builds retrofit hardware kits for industrial vehicles and sells the Mobius fleet management platform licensed to enterprise operators.
2. The platform's core technology includes edge AI inference modules for path planning and collision avoidance combined with a centralized command-and-control architecture that supports universal vehicle command, teleoperation, mapping, and path-building capabilities.
3. The system delivers autonomous navigation, remote teleoperation, multi-vehicle fleet orchestration, collision avoidance, and site-wide path planning for mixed manned and unmanned fleets.
4. Customers receive OEM-agnostic hardware kits that integrate with existing industrial vehicles, paired with licensed autonomy and fleet management software.
5. The technology is used in mining, agriculture, construction, civil infrastructure, landscaping, waste management, and law enforcement operations.
6. Enterprise customers include mining companies, construction contractors, agricultural operators, logistics operators, and law enforcement agencies.
7. The organization acts as a systems integrator and software provider, retrofitting vehicles from multiple industrial OEMs with its own hardware kits and managing them through its orchestration platform.
8. Its OEM-agnostic platform allows a single operator to command and control hundreds of mixed-brand vehicles simultaneously, integrating both autonomous and human-operated workflows without requiring vehicle replacement.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Liebherr is a vehicle partner.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: The organization generates revenue through software licenses, hardware kit sales, and systems integration services.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2000, the company employs 130 people and has deployed over 1,000 autonomous vehicles across multiple continents.
Geography: Based in Salt Lake City, the organization operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire focus of the business.

points.name: Intuitive
points.description: US medical robotics manufacturer deploying minimally invasive surgical systems with on-device vision and instrument control.
points.bullets:
A medical robot maker that designs and manufactures complete robotic surgical systems for minimally invasive procedures, integrating physical robotics, advanced sensing, endoscopic vision and on-device AI into its surgical platforms for the healthcare sector.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete surgical robotics systems.
2. Surgeon-in-the-loop robotic surgical platforms equipped with advanced vision technologies, energy systems, stapling, instruments, force feedback and on-device AI that processes real-time kinematic movement patterns and surgical video.
3. Minimally invasive surgery, peripheral lung biopsies, high-precision surgical control, force feedback and on-device generation of objective performance assessments.
4. Complete surgical robots and platforms.
5. Hospitals and operating rooms.
6. Healthcare providers and trained physicians.
7. Its surgical robots are operated by trained physicians in operating rooms.
8. On-device AI processes real-time kinematic movement patterns and surgical video directly on the system to generate objective performance assessments.
points.profile:
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Capital equipment sales of robotic surgical platforms.
Scale and maturity: A mature, established enterprise with systems used in millions of procedures since the late 1990s.
Geography: Based in Sunnyvale, California, USA, with robotic systems deployed in operating rooms globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation for high-stakes medical applications represent the organization's entire focus as a pure-play medical robotics business.

points.name: Dandy
points.description: New York dental robotics company automating the manufacturing of personalized dental restorations using AI and 3D printing.
points.bullets:
An operator that runs a vertically integrated dental manufacturing network using custom robotics, intraoral scanners, AI-assisted design, 3D printing, and robotic finishing to produce custom dental prosthetics at scale for dental practices.
1. An operator that runs digital dental factories and supplies intraoral scanners and chairside software, delivering custom-manufactured dental prosthetics.
2. The core technology combines intraoral scanning, AI-assisted design, additive and subtractive manufacturing, and industrial robots for automated shade matching and surface finishing.
3. It delivers on-device computer vision inference for chairside scanning, robotic finishing operations, and automated optical inspection.
4. It provides intraoral scanners and chairside software to dental practices, runs owned factories for production, and ships finished dental prosthetics via delivery carriers.
5. The machines and operations are used in dental practices for scanning and in owned digital factories for automated dental manufacturing.
6. The organization sells to dental practices and dentists across the United States.
7. The company operates its own manufacturing facilities, buys 3D printing systems from component makers, and runs them alongside custom robotics to produce dental appliances for dental practices.
8. It uses a vertically integrated approach to mass customization, applying industrial robotics and proprietary vision systems to automate manual dental lab tasks like shade matching and finishing.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization partners with Carbon, EnvisionTEC, Stratasys, and 3D Systems for 3D printing hardware, and utilizes UPS and FedEx for delivery.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: The organization makes money by selling custom-manufactured dental prosthetics and providing intraoral scanners to dental practices.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2020, the company has secured over $170 million in funding, surpassed $100 million in revenue in its first two years, and serves over 6,000 dentists.
Geography: It is based in New York, New York, operates owned factories in Utah and Texas, and serves customers across the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization functions as a comprehensive dental laboratory that manufactures crowns, bridges, dentures, night guards, implants, veneers, and clear aligners.

points.name: AutoStore
points.description: Norwegian warehouse robotics company deploying autonomous grid robots for high-density storage and order fulfillment.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and manufactures cube-based automated storage and retrieval systems, combining grid infrastructure, bin-handling robots, workstations and routing software for retail, healthcare and third-party logistics operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous grid-navigating warehouse robots and complete cube-storage goods-to-person systems.
2. Grid-based automated storage and retrieval systems in which small battery-powered robots travel across a dense aluminum grid to retrieve and redistribute bins, coordinated by routing and orchestration software.
3. High-density storage, goods-to-person bin retrieval, fleet routing, order fulfillment, piece picking, congestion optimization and throughput management.
4. Complete systems including robots, storage grids, modular workstations and proprietary software, sold through a network of system integrators.
5. Warehouses, e-commerce fulfillment centers, third-party logistics operations and pharmaceutical distribution.
6. Retailers, healthcare providers, third-party logistics operators and smaller businesses.
7. Its robotic systems are installed and integrated by qualified system integrators for end-user warehouse operators.
8. Cube-storage architecture that maximizes storage density by stacking bins in a grid with no aisles, paired with modular robot lines and hot-swappable batteries.

points.name: Piaggio Fast Forward
points.description: Boston-based robotics company deploying autonomous mobile robots for following people and transporting goods using on-device computer vision.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots for person-following and goods transport in human environments, along with a standalone following module it licenses to other equipment makers. Its mobile carriers carry up to 40 pounds and run hybrid navigation entirely on edge hardware. It serves both consumers and enterprises across manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, retail, delivery, and real estate.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile cargo-carrying following robots and licenses a standalone following module to other equipment makers.
2. Hybrid navigation technology that combines deterministic algorithmic control with on-device AI models, trained on a proprietary multi-agent 3D kinematic dataset of human motion, social negotiation, and object handling.
3. Dynamic person-following, edge-based local decision-making, cargo transport up to 40 pounds, and cloud-based fleet orchestration, reporting, and maintenance supervision.
4. Complete robots sold to consumers and businesses, a standalone following module licensed to third-party equipment makers, and cloud-based fleet-management software.
5. Pedestrian environments, workplaces, manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, retail, construction, food delivery, real estate, and travel.
6. Everyday consumers and enterprise clients across manufacturing, logistics, hospitality, retail, construction, food delivery, and real estate.
7. Its robots are deployed directly by consumers and enterprises, and its following module is integrated by third-party equipment makers into their own machines.
8. Its hybrid navigation framework combines deterministic algorithmic control with AI models that run entirely on edge hardware without cloud dependency, trained on one of the world's largest high-fidelity multi-person motion datasets.

Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of the Piaggio Group, the Italian manufacturer behind the Vespa scooter.
Organization type: A privately held corporate subsidiary operating within a larger publicly traded automotive conglomerate.

Beyond physical AI: Physical robotics and mobile goods transport represent the organization's entire operational focus and commercial product line.

points.name: MORSE Corp
points.description: US defense technology firm developing edge AI algorithms and autonomous systems for military vehicles.
points.bullets:
A defense technology contractor and systems integrator that develops autonomous systems software, AI/ML capabilities, and airdrop mission-planning tools for the U.S. military. It builds algorithms and runtimes for edge AI applications on manned and unmanned aerial vehicles, and provides rigorous test and evaluation services to translate AI research into validated military platforms.
1. A defense services contractor and systems integrator that builds autonomy algorithms and software for edge AI, sold as government contracts and specialized technology services.
2. Autonomous decision-making algorithms and runtimes for unmanned aerial vehicles, alongside web-based mission planning software for airdrop systems.
3. Edge AI inference for autonomous systems, AI/ML algorithm test and evaluation, and operational airdrop mission planning.
4. Government contracts delivering software integration, algorithm development, and test and evaluation services.
5. Manned and unmanned aerial vehicles, military airdrop systems, and defense platforms.
6. The United States Department of Defense, including the Army, Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy, and Special Operations Command.
7. It develops and integrates software layers on top of military hardware platforms built by defense prime contractors.
8. It uses a user-centered development approach with field testing in operationally representative conditions to translate academic AI research into soldier-facing systems.

Organization type: An employee-owned small business operating within the defense industrial base.
Business model: Government services contracts for AI/ML testing, algorithm development, data modernization, and airdrop systems.
Scale and maturity: An established contractor holding multi-year contracts valued up to $241 million and employing between 201 and 500 personnel.
Geography: Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with offices in Arlington, Virginia, and Seattle, Washington, operating across the United States.

points.name: General Dynamics Mission Systems
points.description: Defense contractor building autonomous underwater vehicles with embedded intelligence for on-device decision-making.
points.bullets:
A vehicle maker that designs and builds autonomous unmanned underwater vehicles for defense, commercial and scientific clients, providing complete deployed undersea systems with embedded intelligence, integrated sensors and command-and-control infrastructure.
1. A vehicle maker that designs and builds autonomous underwater vehicles and complete deployed undersea systems for naval applications.
2. Autonomous underwater vehicles with embedded intelligence, modular payloads, integrated inertial navigation, dead reckoning and Doppler velocity log technologies for GPS-denied navigation.
3. Autonomous undersea navigation, deep-sea reconnaissance, mine countermeasures, unexploded ordnance detection and undersea surveillance.
4. Complete autonomous underwater vehicles, expendable UUV mining systems, optional turnkey survey packages and engineering services.
5. Unmanned underwater vehicles, maritime and deep-sea reconnaissance, submarine-launched mining systems and naval mine countermeasures.
6. Defense customers, navies, allied naval forces, commercial clients and scientific clients.
7. Its vehicles are delivered as complete platforms to defense primes and directly to naval forces.
8. Its approach maintains autonomous navigation accuracy to 0.1% of distance traveled in denied GPS environments using integrated inertial navigation, dead reckoning and Doppler velocity logs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Thales, the U.S. Navy and the Royal Australian Navy.
Organization type: A business unit of a large, publicly traded aerospace and defense conglomerate.
Business model: Vehicle sales, prototype contracts and engineering services.

points.name: SVT Robotics
points.description: Norfolk-based automation software company connecting factory robots and IoT devices through a tech-agnostic integration platform.

A developer tools company that builds a technology-agnostic integration platform for deploying robots, automation and IoT devices in warehouses and factories. It sits at the platform level of the automation stack, establishing standard communication protocols rather than manufacturing physical components.

2. Middleware software that provides a plug-and-play foundation for facilitating communication between diverse robotic hardware, sensors and software systems.
3. Automation integration, monitoring and scalability for heterogeneous robot fleets and IoT devices.

points.name: University of Texas at Austin

A university lab that develops real-time adaptive neural network systems for IoT devices and conducts humanoid robotics research, from which a humanoid robot maker spun out.

2. Variable bit-width deep neural networks that adapt precision in real time to match fluctuating IoT device resources.

points.name: Armstrong Robotics
points.description: Hospitality robotics company deploying AI-powered dishwashing robot arms in commercial kitchens.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds multi-armed robotic dishwashing systems for commercial restaurant kitchens and operates them under a subscription model.
1. A robot maker that builds and deploys complete multi-arm robotic dishwashing systems.

5. The systems are used in commercial kitchens and full-service restaurants.
6. The customers are full-service restaurant chains facing persistent labor shortages.
7. The organization builds its own robots and operates them directly within restaurant kitchens.
8. The approach is distinguished by a perception-driven autonomy stack that autonomously selects from a library of custom gripper fingers to handle greasy and chaotic kitchen environments.

Key partners and customers: Investors include Lerer Hippeau, Bloomberg Beta, Next Play Ventures, Transmedia Capital, and West Wave Capital.

points.name: Flytrex
points.description: US drone delivery startup deploying autonomous drones using edge AI for safe suburban last-mile food and retail deliveries.
points.bullets:
A drone delivery company that builds and operates a fleet of autonomous delivery drones and a cloud flight-management platform for on-demand food and retail delivery in suburban neighborhoods. 1. A drone operator that builds its own autonomous delivery drones and cloud platform and sells drone delivery as a service to restaurants, retailers and delivery platforms.
2. Autonomous fixed-wing-transition delivery drones with onboard edge processing for navigation, flown from central nest and mall-parking-lot hubs, managed by a cloud platform that accounts for topography, man-made objects and weather and coordinates routes through airspace traffic management.
3. Fully autonomous last-mile delivery from order placement through pickup to customer yards within roughly five minutes over about five-mile round trips, including automated flight management and route conflict coordination.
4. It delivers packages itself as a drone delivery service operated through its own fleet and cloud platform.
5. Used in suburban last-mile food and retail delivery, carrying pizzas, sandwiches, ice cream and family meals to residential backyards in the United States.
6. Its customers are quick-service restaurant chains, national food brands, delivery platforms and consumers ordering food and retail goods.
7. It builds and operates its own drones and flight platform, delivering directly for restaurant chains and marketplace delivery platforms.
8. It operates its own FAA-certified drone system at commercial scale with over 200,000 completed deliveries, using purpose-built hardware such as a pizza-holding system that reduces drag and generates lift, and one of the world's largest drone-flight black-box datasets.

Business model: It makes money from fees for drone delivery services performed for restaurant chains and delivery platforms.

points.name: Navifra

points.name: Flo Mobility

points.name: Mela Ventures

It evaluates ventures on domain depth, proprietary data, and regulatory compliance rather than software growth metrics, providing capital for extended R&D and hardware development.

points.name: Vicarious Surgical
points.description: Surgical robotics startup building single-port surgical robots that perform minimally invasive abdominal procedures through tiny incisions.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that developed a complete single-port surgical robotic system for minimally invasive abdominal procedures. It built the entire platform, integrating miniaturized robotic actuators, a 3D visualization camera, and proprietary control software, aiming to sell the deployed systems to hospitals. The organization ultimately dissolved before achieving commercial authorization.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete surgical robotics systems for hospitals.
2. The core technology is a single-incision surgical robot combining miniaturized nine-degree-of-freedom articulated arms and a high-definition camera that operate entirely inside the patient, driven by a surgeon console with hand controllers and proprietary software.
3. The system delivers minimally invasive abdominal surgery through a single micro-incision, providing 3D visualization and human-inspired motion control for procedures such as ventral hernia repair.
4. The organization delivers complete surgical robotic systems, including the patient cart and surgeon console.
5. The machines are used in hospitals for minimally invasive abdominal surgical procedures.
6. The organization sells to surgeons and hospitals.
7. It operates as a complete robot original equipment manufacturer that designs and builds its own surgical systems rather than supplying components.
8. Its approach places two highly articulated arms and a camera entirely inside the patient through a single port to eliminate external collision risks and shrink the surgeon's presence.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company's investors include Bill Gates, Khosla Ventures, Innovation Endeavors, E15 VC, and BD, and it merged with D8 Holdings Corp.
Organization type: It was a publicly traded medical device company before its dissolution.

Beyond physical AI: The organization was a pure-play medical robotics developer with no other business activities.

A surgical robot maker that builds and sells a complete robotic system for minimally invasive abdominal procedures, integrating human-like robotic arms with embedded perception and on-device vision and motion control, for hospitals.

2. Vertically integrated hardware and software encompassing robotic arms with 28 sensors per arm for embedded perception and on-device vision and motion control systems.

points.name: Emerson Electric Co
points.description: Industrial technology company embedding machine learning chips into industrial PCs for real-time factory floor anomaly detection and predictive maintenance.

An industrial automation and component company that builds edge AI hardware, sensors and actuators, alongside process management software, for industrial operators. It combines rugged industrial PCs with embedded machine learning SoCs and smart sensors to enable autonomous operations through on-device intelligence. The organization serves industrial sectors needing air-gapped, extreme-environment control without cloud dependency.

2. The core technology includes rugged industrial PCs with embedded machine learning System-on-Chip technology, advanced smart sensors, and motion control technologies for actuator systems.
3. It delivers on-device AI inference, automated control, edge intelligence, and autonomous operations for industrial environments.
4. Customers receive industrial components such as sensors and actuators, edge computing hardware, and enterprise software platforms.
5. Its technology is used in smart factories, chemical plants, life sciences facilities, oil and gas operations, semiconductor manufacturing, and power and water utilities.
6. The organization sells to manufacturers, industrial operators, and utility companies across diverse industrial sectors.
7. Its hardware components and sensors are designed into factory automation systems by industrial operators, and its software platforms are deployed directly in process management environments.
8. It provides a unified, end-to-end technology stack that delivers air-gapped security, extreme environmental resilience, and autonomous operations without cloud dependency.

points.name: Microbot Medical Inc.
points.description: Medical device company building single-use robotic systems for remotely navigating endovascular procedures.
points.bullets:
A medical robot maker that builds and sells a single-use, remotely operated endovascular robotic system for peripheral vascular procedures. The company designs and manufactures a complete miniature robotic system integrating a bedside drive, an articulated arm, and a handheld remote controller for catheter navigation. 3. Remote-controlled navigation, precision delivery, and manipulation of catheters within peripheral vasculature.
4. Complete single-use robotic medical devices sold to healthcare facilities.
5. Peripheral endovascular procedures in hospitals and academic medical centers.
6. Hospitals, academic medical centers, and interventional physicians.

Organization type: A commercial-stage, publicly traded medical device company.
Business model: Sales of single-use robotic medical devices and procedural systems to healthcare providers.

points.name: Otto

An autonomy software developer that builds self-learning agentic AI driving systems for assisted and autonomous driving and partners with fleet operators to launch robotaxi services.
