2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software for trucks integrated into the operator's fleet infrastructure and terminal operations.
3. Autonomous freight transportation and long-haul navigation paired with human-driven logistics management.
4. Freight hauling services and logistics management using a fleet it operates itself that is augmented with licensed autonomous driving technology.
5. Long-haul trucking, freight transportation, and logistics operations.
6. Freight shippers and logistics customers requiring long-haul transportation capacity.
7. It buys autonomous trucking technology from external developers and operates it within its own logistics and trucking fleet.
8. A hybrid operational model that combines professional human drivers for complex routes with autonomous systems for monotonous, long-distance highway segments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners with Aurora to deploy the Aurora Driver in its freight hauling ecosystem.
Organization type: A publicly traded transportation and logistics conglomerate.
Business model: Freight hauling fees, logistics management services, and transportation contracts.
Scale and maturity: A large, mature enterprise generating billions in annual revenue, employing over 13,500 associates, and managing an extensive modern fleet.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates autonomous freight pilots primarily along southern routes connecting Texas, Arizona, and Florida.
Beyond physical AI: A comprehensive freight transportation and logistics services company that manages a vast network of traditional trucking, intermodal transport, and logistics operations.

points.name: Mars Auto
points.description: South Korean autonomous trucking company deploying camera-based AI driving systems for long-haul freight transport.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer and freight operator that builds camera-based end-to-end autonomous driving systems for heavy-duty trucks and runs paid transport services on fixed routes. It retrofits standard trucks with its hardware and software, and operates subsidiaries that haul freight commercially for logistics companies in Korea and the US.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack for trucks and an operator that runs autonomous freight routes itself.
2. A vision-based end-to-end AI system that uses a single neural network to map seven camera inputs directly to vehicle control, trained on millions of kilometers of real-world driving data and avoiding reliance on lidar or high-definition maps.
3. Level 2 and Level 4 autonomous navigation for heavy-duty trucks, including highway and general-road driving without HD maps, plus fleet data acquisition from retrofitted trucks.
4. The autonomy system is installed on standard trucks within a day as licensed software and retrofitted hardware, and the company also operates its own commercial freight hauling services.
5. Autonomous long-haul and mid-mile freight trucks, transcontinental logistics routes, postal freight, and military logistics.
6. Commercial logistics operators, postal agencies, militaries, and shippers that use its freight services or retrofit their trucks.
7. Its autonomous driving stack is installed on standard trucks and it operates those trucks through its own logistics subsidiaries.
8. A camera-only end-to-end architecture that retrofits onto standard trucks in a day at low cost without lidar or HD maps, while the company also operates its own freight routes.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Logistics partners include LX Pantos, Hyundai Glovis, Lotte Global Logistics, CJ Logistics, Logisquare, Postal Logistics Agency, Army Logistics Command, T map Mobility, and Hyundai Mobis; SK Telecom provides 5G networks; Nvidia provides Blackwell GPUs for training; investors include Kakao Ventures, Kakao Mobility, and Y Combinator.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software subscriptions, per-vehicle system installations, and paid freight transport fees from its logistics operations.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017 with 11-50 employees, ranked the #2 autonomous truck startup by Seedtable, having collected over 10 million kilometers of driving data and operating commercial routes in Korea and the US.
Geography: Headquartered in Seoul, South Korea with a US base in Round Rock, Texas, operating freight routes domestically and expanding transcontinental operations between Korea and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is strictly dedicated to physical AI and autonomous trucking, with no business operations outside of autonomous driving and freight transport.

points.name: Kodiak Robotics
points.description: Autonomous vehicle developer deploying driverless AI systems for Class 8 trucks.
points.bullets:
An autonomous trucking company that develops a self-driving system for Class 8 tractors and operates driverless freight routes, hauling cargo for logistics providers and the military.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack to fleet operators and runs driverless trucks on hub-to-hub routes.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software running real-time perception and driving models on AI SoCs, integrated with modular hardware featuring redundant braking, steering and power systems.
3. Driverless highway navigation, autonomous freight hauling and field-swappable sensor modules designed for harsh environments.
4. Licensed autonomy software installed on customer-owned trucks and a driverless truck platform operated as a freight service.
5. Class 8 highway tractors, logistics fleets and military vehicles.
6. Logistics providers, commercial fleets, industrial shippers and militaries.
7. Its self-driving system is integrated into customer-owned and partner trucks that it operates to haul freight.
8. A modular hardware approach with swappable sensor modules allows driverless operation on customer-owned trucks in harsh environments like the Permian Basin.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include Ambarella, Bosch, Atlas Energy Solutions, Applied Intuition, Ryder System, Pilot Co., Maersk, C.R. England, Werner, SK Inc., IKEA and the U.S. Air Force.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Freight hauling fees and licensing its autonomous driving system to carriers and fleet operators.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018, operating driverless freight routes with a sixth-generation truck platform and reaching a milestone of 20 driverless trucks.
Geography: Based in Mountain View, California, operating routes in Texas and Oklahoma with planned expansion into Asia-Pacific markets.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play autonomous vehicle company entirely focused on developing and deploying driverless trucking systems for commercial freight and defense applications.

points.name: Gatik
points.description: Autonomous vehicle developer deploying driverless box trucks for fixed-route middle-mile logistics using on-device perception and sensor fusion.
points.bullets:
An autonomous trucking company that develops and operates self-driving Class 3-6 box trucks for middle-mile logistics, running driverless routes between distribution centers and retail stores for major retailers and grocers.
1. An autonomous vehicle operator that runs a fleet of driverless box trucks as a commercial freight service.
2. Level 4 autonomous driving systems integrating camera and lidar sensor fusion for real-time perception, object detection and behavioral prediction on fixed, pre-mapped routes.
3. Driverless operation on structured, repeatable short-haul surface streets and highways in light rain and snow.
4. Autonomous freight delivery as a service operated by the company itself.
5. Middle-mile logistics, supply chain transportation and retail delivery operations.
6. Fortune 500 retailers, grocers, food and beverage companies and logistics operators.
7. It buys trucks from OEMs, equips them with autonomy and operates the fleet itself for retail customers.
8. It pursues a structured autonomy approach on fixed, repeatable short-haul routes rather than complex long-haul driving, enabling profitable fully driverless operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its customers and partners include Walmart, Loblaw, Kroger, Tyson Foods, PepsiCo, Georgia-Pacific, Pitney Bowes and Ryder System; it buys trucks from Isuzu Motors and lidar from Velodyne, and has joined the NVIDIA Halos AI Systems Inspection Lab.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Revenue from per-delivery or contract-based autonomous freight and logistics service fees.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2017, it has raised about $500 million including a $200 million Series D, and operates dozens of trucks with over half a million driverless deliveries completed.
Geography: Based in Palo Alto, California, it operates driverless routes in Arkansas, Ontario, Canada, and Texas.
Beyond physical AI: Autonomous middle-mile logistics is its entire focus.

points.name: Plus
points.description: Santa Clara autonomous vehicle developer building AI software for self-driving commercial trucks.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds and licenses Level 4 self-driving stacks and driver-assist systems for commercial freight trucks. The company creates sensor-fusion, perception, prediction, and planning software that runs on vehicle computers, supplying its autonomous driving technology to truck OEMs and fleet operators.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack and hardware reference designs to automakers and fleet operators.
2. The core technology is a transformer-based perception stack and multimodal sensor fusion using lidar, radar, and cameras, processed by end-to-end deep neural networks running on-device inference.
3. It delivers SAE Level 4 driverless operation, Level 2 advanced driver assistance on highways, simultaneous localization and mapping, and deep perception with a detection range over 1,600 meters.
4. Customers get it through licensed software, autonomy stacks integrated into factory-built trucks, hardware reference designs for redundant sensor and compute setups, and retrofitted autonomous systems for existing fleets.
5. Its technology is used in commercial freight trucks, driverless Class 8 semi-trucks, and hydrogen fuel cell electric trucks.
6. It sells to truck manufacturers, commercial fleet operators, logistics companies, and retailers.
7. Its software and reference designs are integrated into commercial trucks built by OEMs and retrofitted into existing delivery fleets.
8. It distinguishes itself by replacing traditional hand-coded logic with an AI-native software architecture using deep learning models, supported by proprietary auto-labeling and model distillation techniques.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include truck makers Traton Group, Hyundai, IVECO, Nikola, and FAW, fleet operators Amazon and DSV, and technology suppliers Nvidia, Ambarella, and Bosch.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through software licensing, per-vehicle royalties, system sales, and retrofit contracts.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016, the company has accumulated over six million miles of real-world driving and is advancing toward mass-market commercialization.
Geography: It is headquartered in Silicon Valley, California, and operates in the United States, Europe, Australia, and China.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Einride
points.description: Swedish autonomous vehicle developer deploying cabless electric trucks managed by an AI fleet operating system.
points.bullets:
An autonomous trucking company that builds and operates cabless electric autonomous trucks and a freight mobility operating system to transport goods for industrial shippers.
1. A vehicle maker and operator that designs cabless autonomous trucks and sells autonomous freight transport as a managed service.
2. Purpose-built cabless Level 4 autonomous electric trucks integrated with an AI-powered operating system, remote operator oversight, and supporting charging infrastructure.
3. Autonomous freight transport on public roads and private industrial sites, fleet orchestration, remote operation, and electric vehicle charge management.
4. Complete autonomous trucks operated as a freight mobility service, alongside licensed fleet management software and smartcharger stations.
5. Autonomous trucking, logistics hubs, industrial sites, ports, and public road freight corridors.
6. Industrial shippers, retailers, logistics operators, and carriers.
7. It builds its own autonomous trucks and operates them alongside human-driven electric trucks within customer supply chains.
8. It takes a ground-up approach that combines purpose-built cabless hardware, proprietary operating software, and dedicated charging infrastructure into a single freight ecosystem.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Notable partners include GE Appliances and Maersk.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Autonomous freight transport services and licensed software platforms.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2016 with commercial deployments operational across Europe and the United States, including U.S. regulatory approval for public road operation secured in 2022.
Geography: Based in Sweden and operating throughout Europe and the United States, with presence in the South Korean market.
Beyond physical AI: Autonomous physical AI and electric vehicle automation represent the entirety of its business model and value proposition.

points.name: Forterra
points.description: Defense technology company building vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving systems for military ground vehicles.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator and deployed-system provider that delivers complete autonomous driving and mission systems for on-road and off-road vehicles. It integrates sensor-fusion autonomy software, communications, and hardware into military and commercial vehicles, providing an end-to-end operating stack for defense and logistics customers.
1. A systems integrator that installs and delivers complete autonomous vehicle solutions and autonomy stacks for existing heavy-duty machines.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software, low-bandwidth vehicle communications, and integrated hardware appliques that enable vehicle- and use-case agnostic autonomous driving in mixed traffic and off-road environments.
3. Autonomous navigation, driver-assist functionality, GPS-denied navigation, and distributed warfare mission orchestration.
4. Complete autonomous vehicle solutions delivered as integrated systems, licensed autonomy stacks, and retrofitted hardware appliques.
5. Military ground vehicles, heavy-duty transit buses, terminal tractors, and off-road logistics platforms.
6. Militaries, government agencies, and commercial vehicle OEMs.
7. It buys vehicle platforms from OEMs and integrates its autonomous systems into them for end-use deployment.
8. Combat-proven, field-deployed off-road autonomy and specialized expertise in GPS-denied navigation originally developed for military mine-clearing operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include BAE Systems, New Flyer, Gillig, and Polaris, using Ouster lidar sensors, with funding led by SoftBank.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Government and military contracts, commercial vehicle OEM partnerships, and autonomous systems integration.
Scale and maturity: Shipped over 100 vehicles accumulating 400,000 miles across military programs in ten countries, selected for four active defense programs.
Geography: Based in Maryland, USA, operating globally with recent combat deployments in Ukraine.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are entirely central to the organization's overall mission, driving its core technology stack and overarching business model.

points.name: Locomation
points.description: US autonomous vehicle developer linking paired trucks in convoys where one driver leads and the other rests while the follower truck drives itself.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that built a human-guided truck convoy system for the long-haul freight industry, creating an electronic tethering system that allows a driverless truck to follow a human-driven lead truck before shutting down in 2023.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving convoy stack to trucking fleets.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software with integrated sensors, computers, and steering systems for on-device perception and control of Class 8 trucks.
3. Autonomous following and platooning for heavy-duty trucks, enabling electronic tethering and autonomous relay convoys with periodic lead-follower swapping.
4. Complete autonomous following kits integrated into existing Class 8 freight trucks.
5. Class 8 long-haul freight trucks and commercial highway trucking operations.
6. Commercial freight carriers and long-haul trucking fleets.
7. Its autonomous convoy stack is integrated into Class 8 trucks operated by commercial freight carriers.
8. A human-guided autonomy approach requires an active driver in the lead truck rather than fully driverless operation, focusing on near-term regulatory compliance through hours-of-service management.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Wilson Logistics, PGT Trucking, Stevens Trucking, Boundless Impact Research & Analytics, Carnegie Mellon University National Robotics Engineering Center.
Organization type: A privately held startup that ceased operations in February 2023.
Business model: Contracts and commercial operations with freight carriers for autonomous convoy technology deployments.
Scale and maturity: A startup founded in 2018 that completed real-world testing pilots and shut down in 2023 before full commercial deployment.
Geography: Based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA, conducting testing and planned operations within the domestic American freight market.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play entity whose entire focus was on developing and commercializing autonomous relay convoy technology for the commercial freight sector.

points.name: Schneider
points.description: US trucking and logistics provider testing autonomous trucks in pilot programs.
points.bullets:
A trucking and logistics operator that runs freight hauls and participates in autonomous trucking pilots using self-driving stacks from technology developers, and a strategic investor in robot foundation model developers.
1. A logistics operator that runs trucking fleets and a venture investor that funds robotics and AI model developers.
2. It operates trucking fleets itself and deploys autonomous trucking services in pilot programs, and provides capital to robotics companies.
3. Long-haul trucking, logistics operations and warehouse production environments.
4. Shippers needing freight transport and, as an investor, robotics and AI companies seeking funding.
5. It buys or leases trucks and buys autonomous driving services from software developers to run freight operations, and takes equity stakes in AI and robotics developers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Torc, Aurora, Skild AI and JAKA.
Organization type: A publicly traded logistics operator and multinational energy management and automation company.
Business model: Freight hauling and logistics fees, and venture capital investment.

points.name: C.R. England

A trucking and logistics operator that runs a fleet of freight trucks and is conducting pilot programs with autonomous truck developers to test self-driving technology in its operations.

points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Kodiak Robotics and Torc Robotics.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Freight hauling and logistics services.
Scale and maturity: A top truckload carrier ranked among the largest North American for-hire carriers.
Geography: Based and operating in the USA.
Beyond physical AI: A traditional trucking and third-party logistics provider whose core business is freight transport, now engaging with autonomous technology through fleet testing partnerships.

points.name: LM White Consulting
points.description: US consulting firm advising logistics companies on autonomous trucking adoption and deployment.

A consulting and advisory firm that facilitates the adoption, deployment, and scaling of autonomous trucking within the logistics and freight transportation sector. It acts as a strategic advisor and systems integrator bridging the gap between autonomous vehicle technology developers and traditional commercial fleet operators. The firm provides strategic planning and operational integration services rather than manufacturing hardware or developing software.
1. A consulting firm that provides strategic advisory services for integrating autonomous trucks into commercial fleets, delivered as professional consulting engagements.
2. Strategic advisory frameworks and operational integration methodologies for deploying autonomous freight networks.
3. Autonomous trucking adoption planning, commercial fleet integration, and autonomous freight network scaling.
4. Professional consulting engagements and integration services.
5. Autonomous long-haul trucking, freight transportation, and logistics supply chains.
6. Traditional trucking companies and freight operators.
7. It operates as an integrator and strategic advisor between autonomous vehicle technology developers and traditional fleet operators.
8. The organization differentiates itself through operational credibility derived from successfully commercializing a working autonomous freight network rather than providing theoretical advice.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The firm is led by a former executive with over thirty-five years of experience at a major global logistics corporation.
Organization type: A privately held, specialized consulting firm.
Business model: Consulting contracts and strategic advisory fees.
Scale and maturity: The organization has demonstrated operational maturity by building an autonomous trucking freight network to multi-million dollar annual revenue with hundreds of weekly loads.
Geography: Based in the United States, focusing on domestic long-haul, highway-based operations along high-density freight routes.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond autonomous trucking, the firm situates its advisory work within the broader context of supply chain automation, referencing warehouse robotics and automated material handling.

points.name: Polymath Robotics
points.description: US autonomous vehicle developer building navigation software for industrial off-highway vehicles.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds a vehicle-agnostic autonomy stack for industrial off-highway vehicles, providing retrofit kits and a SaaS platform for path planning, navigation, and obstacle avoidance in controlled off-road environments for industrial operators and OEMs.

2. Modular autonomous navigation software bundling AI, machine learning, controls, and ROS, with mature vehicle dynamics, a built-in safety layer, and low network bandwidth overhead.
3. Autonomous navigation, path planning, obstacle detection and avoidance, vehicle-following, and auto-stop safety.
4. Plug-in retrofit autonomy kits and a software-as-a-service platform accessible via a REST API.
5. Off-highway vehicles, haul trucks, bulldozers, and heavy equipment in agriculture, mining, forestry, construction, and ground support logistics.
6. Industrial vehicle operators and original equipment manufacturers in the agriculture, mining, forestry, construction, and logistics sectors.
7. Its autonomy stack is integrated onto existing heavy equipment and vehicles retrofitted by industrial operators and OEMs.
8. The platform is vehicle-agnostic, easily installed on legacy equipment with minimal field service, and uses detailed data visualization tools to provide superior customer transparency into vehicle safety and decision-making.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ConGlobal and Foxglove.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software-as-a-service subscriptions and retrofit autonomy kit sales.

points.name: Pronto

An autonomy software developer and robotic systems integrator that builds and deploys camera-based autonomous haulage systems for existing off-road heavy equipment in mining and quarrying. It provides retrofit automation solutions integrating on-device AI, sensor-fusion perception, and drive-by-wire control for small quarry operators and large-scale mining companies.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack and provides it as a retrofit system for existing industrial vehicles.
2. Camera-based, on-device AI stacks integrating sensors, perception algorithms, and drive-by-wire control for autonomous navigation.

7. Its autonomy technology is integrated into off-highway trucks built by heavy equipment manufacturers and operated by industrial customers.
8. It uses a physics-first philosophy selecting sensors and perception algorithms for specific operational dynamics to achieve a low total cost of ownership without requiring new trucks or site modifications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Komatsu, Bell Trucks America, and Anthony Levandowski.
Organization type: A privately held startup acquired by Atoms.

Geography: Based in Silicon Valley and operating in mining and quarrying sectors across North America.

points.name: FedEx

A logistics operator that deploys robots, autonomous trucks, and drones in its own delivery and hub operations, and an investor that funds robotics and AI startups whose technology it integrates into its network. It runs package sortation, trailer unloading, linehaul freight, and last-mile delivery, deploying automation from other makers alongside its own initiatives. It also acquires autonomous delivery startups to build out its last-mile robotics capabilities.
1. A logistics operator that runs robots, autonomous trucks, and drones bought from or built by other companies in its own warehouses, hub facilities, and delivery network, and an investor that funds robotics and autonomous-vehicle startups.
2. Autonomy software, robotic manipulation systems, autonomous driving stacks, cargo drones, and computer vision damage-detection systems integrated into its physical operations.
3. Autonomous truck linehaul, autonomous last-mile delivery, drone package delivery, robotic trailer unloading and case handling, robotic bulk truck loading, and computer-vision-based parcel damage detection.
4. Logistics and transportation services run in its own operations, using robots and vehicles acquired from automation makers, drone delivery services operated with partners, and integration of licensed autonomy software into its fleet.
5. Warehouses, package sortation hubs, long-haul trucking routes, last-mile delivery, and home delivery.
6. Consumers, e-commerce businesses, and commercial shippers that use its transportation and fulfillment services.
7. It buys robots, drones, and autonomous-driving stacks from OEMs and runs them in its own logistics and delivery operations.
8. It combines early adoption and direct integration of third-party robotics with its own physical logistics network, using its operations as a deployment ground for the automation it funds and buys.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Aurora, PACCAR, Wing, Nimble, Dexterity, Elroy Air, Nuro, Asylon, Cobalt AI, and Aegis Sortation.
Organization type: A publicly traded global logistics and transportation company.
Business model: Transportation, e-commerce, and business services, augmented by venture investments in robotics startups.
Scale and maturity: A Fortune 500 global company with $92 billion in annual revenue and large-scale pilot deployments of autonomous trucks and warehouse robots across its network.
Geography: Headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee, USA, with operations and drone delivery pilots spanning global markets including Asia and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: It provides global transportation, courier delivery, and supply-chain management services, using its network to develop and deploy automation for logistics efficiency.

points.name: Daimler Truck

A commercial vehicle manufacturer that builds autonomous-ready heavy-duty trucks and develops Level 4 autonomous driving systems for long-haul freight through a subsidiary.

6. Freight carriers, logistics operators and commercial fleets.
7. It builds the redundant truck platforms designed to carry autonomous driving systems and operates the subsidiary that develops the virtual driver.
8. Hardware-software co-design between the OEM truck chassis and the subsidiary-developed autonomy stack, producing purpose-built autonomous trucks rather than third-party retrofits.

Geography: Headquartered in Germany, with testing and operations in the United States, Canada and Germany.

An autonomy software developer that built a full-stack SAE Level 4 self-driving system comprising integrated software, hardware, HD maps, and cloud-support infrastructure to enable driverless ridesharing and delivery services for automakers and commercial operators.

points.name: Starsky Robotics

An autonomous vehicle developer that builds complete unmanned delivery vehicles and autonomous ride-hailing cars, designing its own driving intelligence and operating the vehicles it deploys for goods delivery and mobility platforms.

8. It uses an AI-first architecture rather than traditional rule-based logic to power universal autonomy across all roads and all rides.

A logistics operator that deploys third-party autonomous yard operations systems in its distribution centers as an end-user of physical AI.

2. Safety-certified software runtimes for autonomous systems, high-fidelity simulators for AI training, and deployed autonomous driving software.
3. On-device autonomy, safety-critical system validation, and autonomous driving.
4. Strategic capital investments and operational collaboration with its parent company's manufacturing and fleet networks.
5. Autonomous long-haul trucking, commercial transportation, and automotive systems.
6. Early-to-late-stage autonomous software, chip, and sensor startups, and robot and vehicle OEMs.
7. It invests in startups building the software, silicon, and subsystem layers that are integrated into commercial vehicles and autonomous machines.

points.name: Kroger

4. Autonomous machines and automation services operated in its own stores and supply chain, sourced from external providers.

points.name: DEXA

points.name: DoorDash

Scale and maturity: Founded in 2003, it is an established national organization that hosts major industry conferences with over 400 participants and maintains a broad membership spanning the Canadian autonomous systems sector.
Geography: It is based in Canada and operates nationally, maintaining direct engagement with national transportation authorities and international aviation bodies.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond autonomous drones, the association actively promotes environmental sustainability, Indigenous innovation, and the advancement of women in the broader aviation and unmanned systems sectors.

points.name: EDR Coalition and Annual Summit
points.description: Industry event convening energy operators and robotics makers to showcase drones and physical automation for energy operations.
points.bullets:
An industry coalition and event platform that aggregates and showcases third-party unmanned systems, edge AI, and physical automation technologies for energy operations rather than manufacturing its own hardware. It connects unmanned systems innovators and service providers with asset owners in oil and gas, power, maritime, and renewable energy. The organization acts as a marketplace and knowledge-sharing hub within the value chain, linking component and subsystem makers with end-user energy companies.
1. An industry coalition and convening body that runs a flagship annual summit and platform for third-party unmanned systems, edge AI, and robotics technologies.
2. It facilitates the adoption of unmanned systems, edge AI, and physical automation for energy operations.
3. Customers get it through attendance and participation in annual conferences and knowledge-sharing events.
4. The machines, operations, and settings it focuses on include drones, robotics, and automation in oil and gas, power, maritime, and renewable energy operations.
5. The types of participants it serves are unmanned systems innovators, service providers, component and subsystem makers, and energy asset owners.
6. It sits between component and subsystem makers and end-user energy companies by acting as a marketplace and knowledge-sharing hub.
7. Its exclusive dedication to the business and technology of unmanned systems in energy operations makes it the world's largest event platform of its kind.
points.profile:
Organization type: It is an industry coalition and convening body.
Business model: It makes money through hosting industry events and conferences.
Scale and maturity: Having hosted its flagship annual summit for eleven iterations, the organization draws over 1,500 global participants to its co-located conferences.
Geography: It is based globally and brings together international participants across the energy and industrial spectrum.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, its entire focus is acting as the primary networking and educational hub for drone, robotics, and industrial digital reality technologies.

points.name: Sky Elements
points.description: Drone light show company deploying large-scale aerial displays that capture national attention.
points.bullets:
A drone light show company that designs, produces and operates choreographed outdoor aerial displays using swarms of coordinated drones for entertainment and event clients.
1. An operator that runs large-scale drone light shows as a performed service.
2. Multi-drone swarm choreography executed by coordinated unmanned aerial vehicles in outdoor airspace.
3. Synchronized formation flight and aerial light animation across dozens or hundreds of drones.
4. Complete aerial light shows performed on behalf of clients at event sites.
5. Entertainment spectacles, public events and aerial displays.
6. Event organizers, municipalities and entertainment brands.
7. It buys drones from hardware makers and operates them as aerial display performances.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: UVify is a hardware partner supplying drones for the shows.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Performance and production fees for drone light shows.
Scale and maturity: A prominent drone show operator that has executed nationally publicized displays.
Geography: Based in the United States and operates shows domestically.
Beyond physical AI: It is a pure-play physical AI operator focused entirely on drone show performances.

points.name: DRONERESPONDERS
points.description: Non-profit organization supporting public safety agencies deploying emergency response drones.
points.bullets:
A non-profit program that supports public safety and emergency management professionals in adopting and maximizing unmanned aircraft systems. It provides education, standards development, and operational guidance for deploying drones in first responder roles, rather than manufacturing hardware or software itself.
1. A non-profit organization that builds and operates a community, education and standards program for public safety drone operations, delivered as membership and training resources.
2. Drone-as-first-responder program guidance, standards development, UAS program management courses, and operational best practices.
3. The organization delivers its support through conferences, forums, training courses, and guidance resources.
4. Public safety and emergency response operations, including law enforcement, fire service, emergency medical services, search and rescue, and emergency management.
5. Public safety professionals, law enforcement agencies, fire departments, emergency medical services, and emergency management agencies.
6. It operates at the deployed system and community ecosystem level, helping end operators integrate unmanned aircraft systems manufactured by other companies.
7. It is the largest unified community organization specifically dedicated to public safety unmanned aircraft system operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Administered by the non-profit organization AIRT, Inc.
Organization type: A 501(c)(3) non-profit program.
Business model: Grants, donations, and program fees.
Scale and maturity: An established advocacy and educational initiative in the public safety sector.
Geography: Based and operating primarily within the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire existence is dedicated to public safety advocacy, community building, and the professionalization of emergency response drone operations.

points.name: OnPoynt
points.description: US educational supplier providing drone kits and aerial robotics programs for schools and universities.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator and specialized supplier that packages drone kits and custom aerial robotics solutions with educational curriculum, guidance, and operational best practices for educational organizations.
1. A systems integrator and supplier that sources drone hardware and packages it into educational kits for schools and STEM programs.
2. It delivers turnkey STEM drone aerial robotics programs, custom hardware solutions, and advisory services on safe and legal drone operation.
3. Customers get complete drone kits, custom integrated solutions, and advisory services.
4. It is used in schools, universities, educational nonprofits, and municipal STEM programs.
5. It sells to educators, school administrators, university faculty, non-profit after-school program directors, and public entities.
6. It sources drone hardware and packages it with educational scaffolding and advisory services for institutional buyers.
7. It is distinguished by its veteran ownership, a team of FAA-certified drone pilots with diverse aviation backgrounds, and customized turnkey solutions for educational buyers.
points.profile:
Organization type: It is a privately held, veteran-owned business.
Scale and maturity: Established in 2012, the organization possesses over 13 years of domain expertise as a drone technology supplier.
Geography: It is based in and operates within the United States, serving the national educational sector and local municipal markets.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond providing physical hardware, the organization produces educational content channels to share aviation knowledge, STEM learning scenarios, and operational best practices.

points.name: Causey Aviation Unmanned
points.description: US drone logistics provider operating long-range autonomous delivery flights.
points.bullets:
A drone logistics operator that runs commercial Beyond Visual Line of Sight package deliveries using autonomous aircraft it does not manufacture, holding regulatory certification to operate on-demand aerial delivery networks for retail, restaurant, and healthcare customers.
1. An operator that runs on-demand commercial drone delivery flights using aircraft supplied by a drone maker, rather than building its own hardware.
2. Long-range BVLOS drone delivery operations, autonomous package logistics, obstacle avoidance, and regulatory compliance for commercial aerial transport.
3. Operates a drone delivery fleet itself under its own air carrier certificate, integrating aircraft from its hardware partner.
4. Drones used for commercial delivery in logistics, retail, restaurants, and healthcare.
5. Retailers, restaurants, and healthcare industries requiring on-demand package delivery.
6. It operates drones from OEMs and runs them as a certified commercial air carrier in its own delivery network.
7. It holds an unrestricted FAA Standard Part 135 air carrier certificate, one of very few granted to drone operators in the United States.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Flytrex is its drone platform partner, and it holds its Part 135 air carrier certification from the FAA.
Organization type: A privately held aviation and logistics company.
Business model: Commercial drone delivery fees and logistics operations.
Scale and maturity: An established operator holding one of only a small number of FAA Part 135 air carrier certificates awarded to drone operators, with prior delivery operations across five cities.
Geography: Based and operating entirely within the United States, specifically Texas and North Carolina.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI logistics, its core focus is managing complex aviation regulatory compliance and certification processes.

points.name: Apian
points.description: United Kingdom drone logistics partner deploying autonomous aerial and ground delivery networks to transport medical supplies between hospitals.
points.bullets:
A healthcare logistics operator that coordinates autonomous drone delivery networks and last-yard ground robots for hospital systems, providing the on-demand automated transport of clinical samples and supplies within the NHS.
1. A logistics operator that runs autonomous drone and ground robot delivery networks, provided as an operated service for healthcare providers.
2. An orchestration and software framework that aggregates aerial drones and ground robots from hardware partners into an integrated delivery network.
3. Fleet orchestration, autonomous last-yard transport, and hands-free movement of physical items between delivery drones and clinical teams.
4. An operated drone and ground robot delivery service deployed within hospital environments.
5. Hospitals and pathology networks.
6. Healthcare providers and pathology laboratories.
7. It buys drones from manufacturers and operates the automated delivery service within hospital networks.
8. It acts as an orchestration layer aggregating partner hardware to achieve major transport time reductions for medical samples.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Matternet, Wing, Great Ormond Street Hospital, SYNLAB, the UK Civil Aviation Authority, and NATS.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Delivery and logistics service contracts.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage enterprise with live deployments at major central London hospitals and regulatory approvals extending through early 2027.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom, with deployments and operations entirely within British hospital networks.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Sierra Nevada
points.description: US defense contractor integrating command-and-control platforms and AI autonomy systems into tactical military edge devices.
points.bullets:
A defense contractor and systems integrator that embeds AI at the tactical edge by delivering autonomous aerial platforms, autonomous ground vehicles, and command-and-control software for military customers.
1. A systems integrator that builds and operates autonomous VTOL cargo aerial platforms and command-and-control software for defense forces.
2. Open-architecture command-and-control software with API plug-ins that integrates real-time data across land, air, sea, space, and cyber domains, alongside vertical takeoff and landing cargo aircraft.
3. Tactical edge processing, multi-domain command-and-control, autonomous cargo delivery, and real-time system integration.
4. Integrated defense systems, autonomous aerial platforms, and command-and-control software networks installed for military operations.
5. Defense forces, coast guard operations, and multi-domain military logistics.
6. United States and international defense forces and militaries.
7. It acquires, develops, and integrates complete autonomous platforms and command networks directly for military end-users.
8. An open-architecture software platform integrating real-time data across land, air, sea, space, and cyber domains using over a hundred API plug-ins distinguishes its approach.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The European Union and United States defense forces are named partners for active programs and coast guard operations.
Organization type: A privately held defense and aerospace contractor.
Business model: Defense contracts for delivering rapidly deployable, combat-ready autonomous platforms and integrated command networks.
Scale and maturity: A large-scale, established enterprise connecting over one million systems on its command-and-control network with active international deployments.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating internationally.
Beyond physical AI: The organization develops broad defense technologies including intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance systems, and expeditionary area air defense systems.

points.name: Alphabet Wing
points.description: US drone operator deploying autonomous AI-powered delivery aircraft for residential and commercial logistics.
points.bullets:
An operator that runs a commercial drone delivery service, integrating its own autonomous aircraft, traffic management software and automated loading and docking infrastructure into a distributed logistics network for businesses and consumers.
1. A drone operator that builds and operates autonomous delivery aircraft and the ground infrastructure it flies them from.
2. Edge AI and autonomous flight control running on custom-built unmanned aircraft and coordinated through unmanned traffic management software.
3. Autonomous aerial navigation, in-flight edge decision-making, drone-to-ground-infrastructure handoffs and fleet orchestration.
4. Delivery fees from a drone delivery network it operates itself.
5. Drones used for last-mile delivery to homes, yards and medical facilities.
6. Food delivery marketplaces, pharmacies, grocers, healthcare providers and general e-commerce businesses.
7. It operates its own drones and ground infrastructure to deliver parcels for businesses and consumers.
8. A distributed infrastructure model using geographically dispersed landing pads and multi-modal autonomy with robot-to-drone order handoffs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: DoorDash is a delivery partner.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary of a publicly traded technology conglomerate.
Business model: Delivery fees from operating its drone delivery network.

Geography: It is based in the United States and operates in North America, Australia and the United Kingdom.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, autonomous robotics and physical automation constitute the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Blue Water Autonomy
points.description: US defense startup building large autonomous unmanned surface vessels for naval intelligence and logistics missions.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vessel maker that builds ship-sized unmanned surface vehicles for the U.S. Navy and allied forces, integrating edge AI navigation, situational awareness, and mission planning software with steel marine hardware for extended open-ocean operations.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous unmanned surface vessels for naval defense.
2. Steel-hulled, ship-sized unmanned surface vessels integrating AI navigation, situational awareness, mission planning, and marine diesel propulsion for autonomous ocean operation.
3. Autonomous open-ocean navigation, intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, logistical mission execution, and deep ocean survey operations.
4. Complete autonomous vessels delivered to naval defense forces.
5. Uncrewed naval ships for defense, maritime surveillance, and deep ocean survey missions.
6. The U.S. Navy and allied naval forces.
7. It designs complete autonomous vessels and integrates marine diesel engines and other specialized components sourced from defense suppliers into the ships it builds.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Google Ventures, the U.S. Navy through PMS 406, Conrad Shipyard, Caterpillar Defense, Precise Power Systems, Valstad, and Tulip.
Organization type: A privately held defense technology startup.
Business model: Defense procurement contracts for the design and delivery of autonomous ships.
Scale and maturity: A 40-person company founded in 2024 with a 145-ton prototype vessel testing outside Boston and a 190-foot vessel under construction.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, USA, with distributed manufacturing across roughly 40 domestic shipyards.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus as a pure-play deep tech company.

points.name: Epirus
points.description: US defense startup deploying high-power microwave systems to disable drone swarms.
points.bullets:
A defense technology company that builds and integrates autonomous directed-energy weapons and counter-drone platforms for militaries. It combines high-power microwave hardware, AI-driven sensing software, and vehicle integration to physically disable unmanned aerial systems and drone swarms. It operates as a systems integrator and original equipment manufacturer delivering complete counter-unmanned aerial system kill chains.
1. A defense systems integrator and original equipment manufacturer that builds directed-energy weapons and autonomous counter-drone platforms sold as complete systems to militaries.
2. Solid-state, long-pulse high-power microwave systems built on gallium nitride electronics, combined with AI-driven sensing software and autonomous vehicle integration.
3. Counter-drone and drone-swarm defeat, air defense, electronic warfare, and non-kinetic neutralization of unmanned aerial systems.
4. Complete directed-energy systems, autonomous ground vehicles, and integrated counter-unmanned aerial system kill chains delivered under military contracts.
5. Counter-drone and drone-swarm protection, air defense, electronic warfare, convoy security, de-mining, and special operations.
6. Militaries, including the United States Navy, Army, and Marine Corps.
7. Its directed-energy subsystems and complete platforms are integrated into military vehicles and defense ecosystems by government customers and partner contractors.
8. Solid-state, long-pulse electromagnetic interference neutralizes entire drone swarms simultaneously rather than targeting individual threats one at a time.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partnered with General Dynamics Land Systems and Kodiak AI on an autonomous counter-drone truck, DroneShield on interoperable defeat capabilities, Palantir on engineering automation, and DFT on counter-UAS kill-chain integration.
Organization type: Privately held high-growth technology company.
Business model: Defense contracts for prototype and production systems, including a $66 million prototype contract in 2024.
Scale and maturity: Secured a $66 million prototype contract in 2024 and is advancing toward becoming an official Pentagon program of record by 2027.
Geography: Based in Los Angeles, California, USA, and primarily operates within the United States, focusing testing and deployment on domestic military installations.
Beyond physical AI: The organization also develops big-data-powered perception capabilities and software automation tools designed to accelerate engineering delivery.

points.name: Firestorm
points.description: Defense startup 3D printing modular drone airframes and replacement parts directly in the field using containerized micro-factories.
points.bullets:
A drone maker and expeditionary manufacturing company that builds 3D-printed unmanned aerial systems and containerized microfactories for defense applications. It produces complete modular drones and the field-deployable additive manufacturing platforms to print and assemble them at the point of need, serving military customers with platforms for ISR, electronic warfare and strike missions.
1. A drone maker that designs and sells complete unmanned aerial systems and containerized 3D-printing microfactories.
2. Additive manufacturing platforms and modular airframes for unmanned aerial vehicles, including containerized edge production cells and multi-mission drone designs.
3. Point-of-need production and assembly of modular drones, distributed manufacturing, intelligence surveillance reconnaissance, electronic warfare and strike operations.
4. Complete drones and mobile 3D-printing units delivered as hardware platforms.
5. Drones, front lines, defense and battlefield operations.
6. Militaries and defense agencies.
7. Its drones and microfactories are deployed directly by defense forces at the edge of the battlefield.
8. Containerized 3D-printing microfactories enable rapid, on-site production and assembly of modular drones, reducing reliance on centralized supply chains.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Orqa, the U.S. Air Force, AFWERX, Air Combat Command, Air Force Special Operations Command, Lockheed Martin Ventures, Booz Allen Ventures, NEA, Decisive Point, Washington Harbour Partners and J.P. Morgan.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales and defense contracts.
Scale and maturity: A 2022 startup that has raised $47 million in Series A funding and secured a $100 million IDIQ contract with the U.S. Air Force.
Geography: Based in San Diego, California, USA, operating primarily within the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus as a pure-play defense technology manufacturer dedicated to expeditionary drone production.

points.name: Vannevar Labs
points.description: Defense startup developing on-device language models and AI infrastructure for tactical edge deployment.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and AI model developer that builds edge AI systems, fine-tuned language models and agentic orchestration infrastructure for defense autonomy and tactical edge deployments.
1. An AI model and software developer that builds on-device inference models and agent infrastructure for defense organizations.
2. Fine-tuned language models and model-agnostic agentic orchestration software optimized for on-device inference at the tactical edge.
3. On-device inference, sentiment analysis, geospatial reasoning and counter-misinformation capabilities.
4. Licensed software, edge-deployable models and integration services.
5. Defense missions, maritime vigilance, misinformation disruption and nontraditional intelligence collection.
6. United States Department of Defense branches, military units, combatant commands, federal civilian agencies and defense contractors.
7. Its models and agent infrastructure are integrated by defense organizations into their own operational platforms.
8. A services model that embeds mission experts on-site to adapt AI agents is paired with a petabyte of rare adversarial data that compresses multi-day analytical tasks into minutes.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Databricks Mosaic AI.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses, subscriptions and defense contracts.
Scale and maturity: A mature startup with 125 deployments across every branch of the military.

Beyond physical AI: Developing artificial intelligence capabilities for defense applications is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: Joby

A vertically integrated autonomous aircraft maker that builds complete vertical takeoff and landing aircraft with on-device flight autonomy stacks, serving defense customers and commercial urban air mobility markets.

5. Autonomous military logistics aircraft and commercial electric air taxis.

7. It designs and manufactures complete autonomous aircraft and delivers them directly to defense customers and aviation operators.
8. It is differentiated by vertical integration of airframe design, autonomous flight software, hybrid-electric propulsion, and manufacturing capability.

Key partners and customers: The company is partnered with Skyports for air taxi services and with Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority to launch an air taxi service.

points.name: Reliable Robotics
points.description: Defense startup developing autonomous flight systems for crewed and uncrewed aircraft.
points.bullets:
An autonomous flight systems integrator that develops certifiable automation subsystems for retrofitting existing manned and uncrewed aircraft, providing remote operation and autonomy for commercial and defense aviation.

2. A rules-based, high-redundancy autonomy system combining proprietary air-to-air radar for detect-and-avoid with software runtimes that automate taxi, takeoff, navigation and landing without relying on artificial intelligence.
3. Fully automated flight through all phases of operation, remote piloting, detect-and-avoid and intra-theater military logistics.
4. Drop-in automation subsystems retrofitted onto existing aircraft and autonomy systems developed under government contract.
5. Commercial regional cargo aircraft and military transport planes operating in civilian airspace and contested logistics scenarios.
6. The United States Air Force, government agencies and regional cargo operators.
7. Its automation systems are integrated into existing type-certified aircraft rather than built into newly manufactured airframes.
8. It pursues a regulation-first strategy by retrofitting highly redundant, certifiable, non-AI automation onto existing general aviation aircraft instead of developing purpose-built drones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The United States Air Force, the Federal Aviation Administration, AFWERX and Boeing's investment arm.

points.name: Boeing

An aerospace and defense prime contractor that designs and manufactures commercial aircraft, combat aircraft, spacecraft, satellites, and autonomous unmanned aerial and maritime vehicles, executing physical AI programs as a principal investigator and operator for militaries and government agencies.
1. A defense and aerospace vehicle maker that builds and sells complete manned and unmanned aircraft, spacecraft, and submarines, and develops modular autonomy and safety software for mobile robots.

3. Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle swarming, command and control for collaborative combat aircraft, modular dynamic safety guarding for mobile robots, and persistent autonomous maritime navigation.
4. Complete autonomous aircraft, spacecraft, and unmanned surface vehicles, alongside government contracts for integrated defense systems and dynamic safety software modules.
5. Combat aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicles, spacecraft, unmanned surface vehicles, satellite communications, and collaborative mobile robot safety.
6. Militaries, government agencies, aerospace prime contractors, and commercial airlines.
7. Its unmanned vehicles and aircraft are designed and operated as complete platforms for defense forces, while its safety software is integrated into mobile cobots by other developers.

Key partners and customers: NASA, the FAA, the US Army, Anduril, Archer Aviation, Kratos, iRobot, and SparkCognition.

points.name: U.S. Army DEVCOM
points.description: US government research agency developing autonomous ground and aerial systems with on-device AI for disconnected combat environments.
points.bullets:
A government agency that conducts foundational research and development to advance on-device artificial intelligence and autonomous systems for military applications. It develops both foundational algorithms and integrated autonomous capabilities at the subsystem and platform levels, spanning sensors, perception technologies, and complete robotic platforms. The organization serves the United States military by providing advanced technological capabilities for complex battlefield operations.
1. A government research laboratory that develops edge AI algorithms, perception technologies, and complete robotic platforms for the military.
2. Foundational on-device AI algorithms, sensor technologies, and integrated robotic subsystems designed to operate in denied, degraded, intermittent, or limited network environments without cloud connectivity.
3. On-device inference, autonomous perception, and integrated robotic platform operations for complex battlefield environments.
4. Cooperative research agreements, foundational technologies, and certified autonomous platforms delivered to military and research partners.
5. Military battlefield operations, surveillance, human-machine teaming, and unmanned aerial vehicles.
6. United States military branches, defense research centers, and academic institutions.
7. Its research and technologies are matured through cooperative agreements and integrated into defense platforms by public, private, and academic partners.
8. It enables robotic platforms to operate effectively in denied, degraded, intermittent, or limited network environments without relying on cloud connectivity.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Perseus Defense, Applied Research Laboratory, Aviation and Missile Center, Armaments Center, High Performance Computing Modernization Program, and Skyfish.
Organization type: A government agency operating under a broader military development command.
Business model: Government-funded research, development, and certification programs.
Scale and maturity: An established governmental command operating dedicated research facilities and maintaining a robust ecosystem of cooperative research agreements.

points.name: Simtoo

points.name: ARM Institute

A government-funded Manufacturing Innovation Institute that accelerates the adoption of robotics, autonomy, and physical AI for U.S. manufacturers by funding collaborative projects, providing integration assessments, and developing workforce training programs across a consortium of industry, academia, and government members.
1. A government agency that funds and coordinates robotics integration and workforce development programs for manufacturers.
2. Applied robotics and physical AI deployment frameworks integrated through consortium-driven project management and automation assessments.
3. Robotics and AI integration planning, manufacturing workforce competency development, and automation risk assessment.
4. Project funding, customized automation assessments, workforce training resources, and physical manufacturing demonstration hubs.
5. Factories, defense industrial base facilities, foundries, shipyards, and semiconductor manufacturing plants.
6. Manufacturers, defense facilities, academic institutions, and robotics technology developers.

8. It operates as a neutral, public-private consortium broker that lowers the risk of robotics adoption for manufacturers through guided assessments and funded collaborative projects.

points.name: 3Laws Robotics

A robotics safety software company that develops a dynamic safety layer for autonomy stacks, providing collision avoidance, geofencing, stabilization, and fault management for robotic and autonomous systems in defense and manufacturing.

2. Control Barrier Functions that monitor signals from existing autonomy software and modulate them to ensure dynamic, deterministic safety.
3. Collision avoidance, geofencing, stabilization, fault management, and trajectory modulation.
4. Licensed software and a free community tier that integrate into existing ROS-based systems and custom control architectures.
5. Industrial mobile robots, autonomous vehicles, last-mile delivery, drones, articulated robot arms, quadrupeds, humanoid robots, and military aviation platforms.
6. Defense forces, manufacturers, logistics operators, and robotics developers.
7. Its software is integrated into autonomy stacks by robot and vehicle makers.
8. It uses Control Barrier Functions to actively deflect robots away from obstacles while maintaining forward progress, providing deterministic safety guarantees without the unnecessary stoppages of traditional safety-rated hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ARM Institute, U.S. Air Force, Open Navigation, Yaskawa, TenOneTen, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Caltech.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions.

Geography: Based in Pasadena, California, USA, and focused on deployments in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play company focused entirely on safety software for physical AI and autonomous systems.

points.name: The Boeing Company

A robot maker that builds autonomous uncrewed surface vehicles and edge AI systems for long-duration maritime operations, acting as a platform OEM and systems integrator for naval defense forces, offshore wind operators, and environmental monitoring organizations.

Key partners and customers: Partners include Elistair, Safran, KNDS France, Rheinmetall, the German Army, the Belgian Navy, the Royal Netherlands Navy, Oceaneering, Naval Group, and parent company Exail Technologies.
Organization type: A privately held subsidiary of a family-owned industrial group.
Business model: Hardware sales of vehicles, sensors, and navigation systems, alongside integrated system contracts and software suites.
Scale and maturity: Formed in 2022, employing over 2,200 people across 30 sites worldwide, with a track record of over 150,000 hours of operations at sea in more than 19 countries and business in over 80 countries.
Geography: Based in France, operating globally with training facilities in Ostende and business across over 80 countries.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge AI and physical automation, the organization has no other business activities, as it focuses exclusively on robotics, navigation, and autonomous systems that act in the physical world.

points.name: Nearthlab
points.description: South Korean defense technology startup deploying autonomous AI drones for military operations and industrial inspection.
points.bullets:
A drone maker that builds autonomous drone systems and counter-drone hard-kill platforms with integrated edge AI for defense and industrial inspection. The company supplies complete aerial robots and cloud-based analytics platforms to defense forces and industrial operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous drones and counter-drone systems, paired with cloud-based analytics software.
2. Computer vision, AI algorithms, and autonomous flight control software integrated directly into deployed aerial systems.
3. Autonomous navigation, aerial inspection, counter-UAS hard-kill interception, and swarm strike operations with one operator controlling multiple units.
4. Complete drones, autonomous inspection solutions, and counter-drone subsystems, along with a cloud-based analytics platform.
5. Defense operations, wind turbine inspections, public safety, and counter-drone missions.
6. Defense ministries, militaries, and global wind turbine OEMs.
7. Its drones and counter-drone subsystems are deployed by defense forces and industrial operators.
8. It operates as a full-stack platform integrating AI, navigation, and flight control into deployed aerial systems with a portfolio of 126 patent filings.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: LIG D&A, Red Cat Futures Initiative, Siemens Gamesa, Vestas, GE, SoftBank, FuturePlay.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales, defense contracts, and industrial inspection service contracts.

Geography: Based in South Korea with subsidiaries in the United States and Germany, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are the company's entire operational focus as a pure-play defense technology and robotics provider.

points.name: Rheinmetall
points.description: German defense contractor building AI-powered collaborative robots and autonomous ground vehicles for extreme environments.
points.bullets:
A defense prime contractor that builds autonomous unmanned ground vehicles and anti-drone laser systems, integrates autonomy software and sensors into military platforms, and invests in robotics and AI startups for armed forces.
1. A defense contractor and vehicle maker that builds autonomous ground vehicles and air-defense systems for militaries.
2. Autonomous ground vehicle platforms, high-energy laser systems, and integrated autonomy stacks built on open software architectures and third-party AI operating systems.
3. Autonomous reconnaissance, logistics transport, medical evacuation, fire support, communications relay, and counter-unmanned aerial system interception.
4. Complete autonomous vehicles, integrated weapons platforms, and defense contracting services for military customers.
5. Ground combat, air defense, logistics, military reconnaissance, and rugged unstructured outdoor environments.
6. Militaries, defense ministries, and armed forces.
7. It builds complete military vehicles and defense systems, integrating subsystems and software from suppliers and running them in deployed military operations.
8. It combines a legacy defense industrial base with an open architecture approach, jointly developing homogeneous operating systems with autonomy software partners and taking equity stakes in them.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with Kraken Technology Group, Auterion, Anduril, Helsing, Breaker Industries, Vantor, Exail, Spleenlab, and the Canadian Space Agency.
Organization type: A publicly traded defense and technology conglomerate.
Business model: Defense contracting, military vehicle and weapons sales, and strategic venture investments.
Scale and maturity: A large established international systems provider founded in 1889, deploying systems like the Skyranger HEL with the German Bundeswehr.
Geography: Based in Germany, operating across European defense programs and expanding into the United States.
Beyond physical AI: It is a major international systems provider for the defense industry that is also active in civilian industrial markets.

points.name: Expeditions
points.description: European venture capital firm funding defense and physical AI startups.
points.bullets:
A venture capital firm that invests in early-stage European defense startups at the intersection of security and deep tech, including those developing edge AI, robotics, autonomy, and physical automation technologies.
1. A venture capital firm that funds early-stage defense and deep-tech startups developing autonomy, AI, robotics, and physical systems.
2. The firm serves the European defense sector and sovereign security markets by funding startups that address capability gaps.
3. The organization operates as an independent venture investor and as a strategic extension of major defense contractors' innovation pipelines.
4. A dual structure provides portfolio founders with direct access to major defense customers while allowing prime contractor backers to monitor fast-moving innovators.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backers include BAE Systems as a limited partner and the NATO Innovation Fund.
Organization type: A privately held venture capital fund manager established in 2021.
Business model: Fund management, deploying capital into early-stage startups.
Scale and maturity: The firm has closed an oversubscribed €197 million investment fund and backed nearly thirty percent of the most well-funded European defense startups.
Geography: Based in Warsaw, Poland, the organization focuses its investment operations exclusively across the European continent.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization is entirely focused on funding dual-use deep technologies such as cybersecurity, quantum computing, space systems, and intelligence.

points.name: Disruptive
points.description: Investment firm funding physical AI and defense technology ventures.
points.bullets:
An investment firm that provides capital to companies operating in the edge and physical AI sector, including developers of defense autonomy software and robot foundation models, without manufacturing hardware or software itself.
1. A venture capital firm that funds physical AI and robotics companies in exchange for equity.
2. It invests capital into companies across the physical AI technology stack, from AI model developers to defense autonomy software providers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It participated as an investor in funding rounds for a defense autonomy software developer and a robot foundation model developer.
Organization type: A privately held investment firm.
Business model: It makes money through fund management and returns on venture capital investments.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and robotics are the central focus of its current investment thesis, and available material describes no other activities.

points.name: Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives
points.description: US growth equity investment division funding physical AI and robotics companies that deploy intelligent machines to automate real-world operations.

A growth equity investor that deploys capital into physical AI and robotics ventures, funding deployed systems that fuse advanced computing with physical hardware like sensors, actuators, and processors for enterprise automation and last-mile retail logistics providers.

points.name: Prima Materia
points.description: Investment firm funding defense autonomy startups that build on-device AI systems for military applications.
points.bullets:
An investment firm that finances defense autonomy and edge AI systems, acting as a capital provider rather than a direct developer of physical automation technologies.
1. A venture capital firm that funds companies building deployed physical AI systems including autonomous drones, electronic warfare software, and underwater vehicles.
2. The organization deploys capital through equity investments in defense technology startups.

5. It occupies a financial position in the technology stack, funding deployed physical AI systems developed by other companies.

points.name: Grob Aircraft
points.description: German defense subsidiary manufacturing autonomous combat aircraft integrated with on-device AI for collaborative flight missions.

An aircraft manufacturer and subsidiary that develops, manufactures, and tests an autonomous unmanned combat aerial vehicle for defense forces, integrating airframe production with on-device AI developed by its parent company.
1. A drone maker that builds and manufactures autonomous unmanned combat aerial vehicles.
2. High-subsonic uncrewed combat aircraft designed for swarming operations, utilizing scalable manufacturing infrastructure for prototyping and production.

Organization type: A subsidiary of a privately held defense AI company.

points.name: KONGSBERG
points.description: Norwegian defense company building autonomous underwater vehicles for deep-sea intelligence and mine countermeasure missions.

A defense contractor and industrial technology group that builds autonomous underwater and surface vehicles, sensors, and weapon systems for navies and maritime operators. It acts as a complete systems integrator, combining proprietary platforms, hydroacoustic sensors, and control software into operational autonomous solutions for high-consequence defense and maritime missions.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that builds autonomous underwater vehicles, uncrewed surface vessels, and defense platforms sold as complete systems.
2. Autonomous underwater vehicles with optimized hydrodynamics, high navigational accuracy, and multiple mapping and imaging sensors, alongside integrated control systems, hydroacoustic sensors, and weapon stations.
3. Autonomous navigation, subsea and seabed warfare, mine countermeasures, intelligence surveillance and reconnaissance, and remote vessel monitoring and control.
4. Complete autonomous vehicles, sensors, weapon stations, and cloud-based monitoring platforms delivered as integrated defense systems.
5. Undersea operations, seabed warfare, mine countermeasures, critical undersea infrastructure inspection, uncrewed surface vessel missions, and ground vehicle weapon stations.

points.name: Saab

A defense contractor that builds military aircraft, naval vessels and autonomous systems, and integrates third-party AI software into its fighter jets and maritime platforms for militaries.

points.name: European Union

A supranational government body that funds and coordinates collaborative research and innovation in edge AI, robotics, and physical automation across European member states, while enacting legally binding regulations for autonomous systems and AI.

2. Public funding frameworks, public-private partnerships, and regulatory frameworks that govern AI risk, data sharing, and machinery safety.
3. Research grant allocation, cross-border consortium coordination, and legally binding governance for AI and automated decision-making systems.
4. Research grants, regulatory frameworks, and direct assistance packages.

6. Academic institutions, small and medium-sized enterprises, industrial manufacturers, defense companies, and member state governments.

points.profile:

points.name: Trident Group
points.description: Ukrainian defense technology startup building onboard AI navigation and targeting modules for unmanned aerial vehicles.

A defense technology company that develops onboard autonomy modules providing computer vision-powered navigation and targeting for unmanned aerial vehicles. points.name: Frost Works
points.description: Ukrainian defense startup building edge AI sensors to detect low-flying drones.

A sensor maker that builds UAV detection systems combining acoustic and radar sensors with edge AI processing for defense stakeholders. It designs and supplies subsystem components for broader air defense ecosystems, focusing on low-altitude aerial threats that evade traditional radar. The organization serves military stakeholders requiring distributed detection of terrain-following drones.

4. Detection systems delivered as subsystem components for integration into broader defense stacks.
5. Defense airspace monitoring and protection against low-altitude aerial threats.
6. Military stakeholders and defense sectors that require distributed detection of terrain-following drones.
7. Its detection components are designed into broader air defense ecosystems by defense system integrators.
8. It maintains passive, real-time threat detection by applying machine learning to drone acoustic signatures, enabling it to spot aircraft that exploit low-altitude flight paths or modify their noise profiles.

A component supplier that builds onboard protective modules for reconnaissance drones, performing on-device inference to detect and neutralize threats from interceptor drones for the defense sector.

A drone maker that manufactures fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles with on-device artificial intelligence for autonomous strike and logistics missions, sold to military operators navigating electronic warfare and GPS-denied battlefield conditions.

A counter-drone defense system maker that builds a unified, AI-powered short-range air defense platform combining a multi-sensor turret with an autonomous interceptor drone for military end-users confronting unmanned aerial threats.

points.description: German defense subsidiary integrating AI-driven detection and autonomous interception technologies into counter-drone systems.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator and manufacturing partner that develops autonomous drone defense systems, combining autonomous unmanned ground vehicles and counter-drone technologies for defense and critical infrastructure protection.
1. A systems integrator that builds and assembles autonomous defense systems and unmanned ground vehicles for counter-drone missions.
