Beyond physical AI: Edge artificial intelligence, robotics and physical automation represent the entirety of its strategic focus and investment mandate.

points.name: Booz Allen Hamilton
points.description: US defense contractor deploying AI systems for national security and military operations.
points.bullets:
A defense contractor and systems integrator that delivers AI, cyber, and autonomous systems for America's defense, civil, and national security priorities, operating much of the software development and AI operations for the Pentagon and intelligence agencies.
1. A defense contractor and systems integrator that builds and operates AI and machine learning platforms and integrates autonomous vehicles and counter-drone systems for government clients.
2. AI and machine learning operations platforms, predictive analytics, and military-grade compute systems running AI workloads in deployed environments.
3. AI/ML operations, predictive analytics for defense intelligence, maritime autonomous mission integration, and non-kinetic counter-UAS technology evaluation.
4. Government contracts, integration services, and operated platforms for defense and intelligence agencies.
5. Defense, national security, maritime missions, and military counter-UAS environments.
6. Militaries, defense intelligence agencies, and civilian government bodies.
7. It buys and integrates autonomous platforms and sensors from OEMs and operates AI workloads on military compute systems for government agencies.
8. It derives nearly all of its revenue from government contracts and operates the software development and AI operations for the Pentagon and intelligence agencies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Andreessen Horowitz, Ulysses, Carnegie Robotics, D-Fend Solutions, Firestorm Labs, and Booz Ventures.
Organization type: A publicly traded defense contractor and advanced technology company.
Business model: Government contracts and integration services.

3. High-precision torque and position control with minimal backlash, IP66-sealed durability for demanding environments, and legged locomotion for inspection robots.
4. Components sold as modules and complete robotic platforms delivered to research and industry customers.
5. Humanoids, exoskeletons, service robots, urban air mobility, and inspection of underground water and sewage infrastructure.

points.name: Lin Engineering

points.bullets:
A food processing and packaging manufacturer that operates as an end user integrating humanoid robotics and on-device AI perception into its internal warehouse logistics for spare parts inspection.
1. An operator that runs humanoid robots and enterprise middleware in its own warehouses to automate inbound logistics processes.
2. Humanoid robotics hardware integrated with on-device AI perception and enterprise warehouse management software.
3. Automated verification of received items and packing processes within physical warehouse operations.
4. Internal integration of external robotics and enterprise software into its own logistics facilities.
5. Warehouses and inbound logistics facilities.
6. The organization uses the automation internally to support its own manufacturing operations.
7. It buys robots from OEMs and operates them in its own warehouses.
8. It transitions embodied AI from proof-of-concept to production warehouse environments at an enterprise scale.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A humanoid robot maker and an enterprise software provider.
Organization type: A privately held multinational corporation.
Business model: It makes money selling food processing and packaging systems to manufacturers.
Scale and maturity: A mature enterprise operating for several decades with a massive global manufacturing footprint.
Geography: Based globally, operating manufacturing and processing facilities across numerous countries worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, its core business encompasses the design, production, and servicing of food processing and packaging systems.

points.name: Arçelik-LG
points.description: Manufacturing joint venture deploying humanoid robots for autonomous warehouse processing guided by real-time enterprise software integration.
points.bullets:
A manufacturing joint venture that operates as an enterprise customer and deployment site for physical AI, integrating humanoid robots and fleet management software into its own inbound logistics workflows to address storage placement errors.
1. A logistics operator that deploys humanoid robots and enterprise warehouse management software in its own facilities.
2. Integration services using complete robots and licensed software operated in its own warehouses.
3. Warehouses and inbound logistics operations in manufacturing supply chains.
4. The organization is its own primary customer, deploying the systems internally.
5. It buys robots from OEMs and fleet management software from vendors and runs them in its own warehouses.
6. Early-stage proof-of-concept adoption of production-deployed embodied AI for inbound logistics in a sector where humanoid robotics remains nascent.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SAP and FairConsult 24|7 for enterprise warehouse management and fleet orchestration, and Unitree for humanoid robots.
Organization type: A global manufacturing joint venture.
Business model: The organization makes money through manufactured goods and logistics operations, deploying physical AI internally to reduce operational errors.
Scale and maturity: An ongoing proof-of-concept phase rather than full-scale production.
Geography: Based and operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI initiatives, the organization operates broadly as a global manufacturer and logistics operator.

points.name: FairConsult 24|7
points.description: Global robotics enablement company orchestrating warehouse robot fleets through enterprise software integration.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and systems integration company that provides fleet management software and integration services to coordinate heterogeneous robotic fleets in enterprise warehouses and logistics operations. The organization sits at the middleware layer, bridging enterprise resource planning systems with on-device edge decision-making and physical robot execution for manufacturing and logistics customers.
1. A systems integrator and platform provider that builds fleet management software and robotics enablement services for enterprise warehouse automation, sold as licensed software and integration services.
2. Context-enriched business logic and middleware software that bridges enterprise resource planning systems with edge robotic execution to route tasks to diverse robotic fleets.
3. Fleet orchestration of heterogeneous robotic fleets, enterprise-connected warehouse execution, and task routing across diverse robots.
4. Licensed software and integration services.
5. Warehouses, factories, automotive plants, food processing facilities and industrial manufacturing operations.
6. Manufacturing and logistics operators, including automotive, food processing and industrial manufacturing companies.
7. Its software and integration services connect enterprise software systems to robots manufactured by robotics OEMs and deployed in enterprise facilities.
8. The company applies context-enriched business logic and deep enterprise integration expertise to route tasks to diverse robots rather than competing on hardware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company partners with SAP and over a dozen robotics manufacturers, with deployments at Arçelik-LG.
Organization type: A privately held enterprise software and integration company.
Business model: Software licenses and integration services.
Scale and maturity: An established enablement partner with documented global deployments across automotive, food processing and industrial manufacturing customers.
Geography: The company operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: The company focuses entirely on providing software middleware and integration services for enterprise resource planning and logistics management.

points.name: Cyberwave
points.description: Robotics software startup building AI platforms that enable rapid training and deployment of adaptive autonomous robots in dynamic warehouse environments.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds software for training, fine-tuning, and deploying autonomous robots in variable warehouse environments. It bridges enterprise logistics software to physical robots and digital twins without manufacturing its own hardware, serving enterprise logistics operators.
1. A software platform provider that builds orchestration and model-training tools for autonomous robots, sold as a software platform.
2. Vision-language-action and reinforcement learning models fine-tuned from demonstration data to adapt robots to real-world variability.
3. Robot training, fine-tuning, deployment, and dynamic task reassignment for high-variability packing and logistics tasks.
4. Licensed software platform integrated with enterprise logistics management systems.
5. Warehouses and logistics environments.
6. Enterprise logistics operators.
7. Its software is integrated onto robots from other makers and connected to enterprise business software systems.
8. It reduces robot training cycles from weeks to hours using vision-language-action and reinforcement learning models.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SAP.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses and platform subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: An emerging startup with production-scale deployments demonstrated globally and active operations in Germany.
Geography: Based globally with a notable presence and active deployments in Germany.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus, dedicated to solving the adaptability bottleneck in dynamic warehouse environments.

points.name: BITZER
points.description: Global refrigeration manufacturer deploying cognitive humanoid robots for autonomous warehouse picking.
points.bullets:
An industrial manufacturer of refrigeration and air conditioning systems that operates as an end user and integration testbed for humanoid robots and embodied AI in its own warehouse logistics. The company integrates cognitive robotics hardware and cloud-based enterprise software directly into its operational workflows to automate temperature-controlled logistics.
1. An operator and systems integrator that deploys and runs automation built from other companies' machines in its own facilities.
2. Humanoid robotics integrated with cloud-based enterprise warehouse management systems and embodied AI to execute autonomous picking tasks.
3. Autonomous piece picking, real-time task responsiveness, 24/7 warehouse utilization, and direct integration of cognitive robots with enterprise business logic.
4. Integration services and internally operated automation workflows deployed within its own warehouses.
5. Warehouses, factories, cold-chain logistics, and temperature-controlled environments.
6. The organization is an end user that serves its own internal logistics operations and the broader market through its refrigeration products.
7. It buys robots and AI software from developers and runs them in its own warehouses as an operational end user and testbed.
8. It provides a mature industrial operational environment as a proof-of-concept testbed for direct integration of cognitive robots with enterprise business logic without custom middleware.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborates with SAP and NEURA Robotics.
Organization type: A privately held global industrial company.
Business model: It makes money manufacturing and selling refrigeration, air conditioning, and heat pump technology, while operating its warehouses as an internal deployment site.
Scale and maturity: A globally established industrial enterprise serving healthcare, hospitality, and supermarket sectors, running pilot deployments in Rottenburg, Germany.
Geography: Based and operating in Rottenburg, Germany, with a global footprint.
Beyond physical AI: A manufacturer of refrigeration, air conditioning, and heat pump technology that maintains temperature-controlled environments for industrial cold chains.

points.name: Sartorius
points.type: life sciences and laboratory equipment manufacturer
points.description: German laboratory equipment manufacturer integrating cognitive robots into warehouse operations.
points.bullets:
An operator and systems integrator that installs cognitive robots from external makers into its own warehouse operations to support manual workstations. It deploys externally sourced humanoid robots trained on its own products as part of an enterprise embodied AI proof of concept. It is a global manufacturer of life sciences and laboratory equipment integrating adaptive physical automation into its internal supply chain.
1. An operator that runs cognitive robots in its own warehouse facilities and a systems integrator that installs those machines into its operational workflows.
2. Dynamic adaptive warehouse automation and human-robot collaboration at manual workstations.
3. Integration services and internally operated robotic deployments.
4. Warehouses and manual workstations in life sciences manufacturing.
5. Internal operations supporting its own life sciences supply chain.
6. It buys robots from OEMs and operates them in its own warehouse facilities.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SAP and a cognitive robot maker are partners on an enterprise embodied AI proof of concept.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of laboratory equipment and screening systems.
Scale and maturity: A global enterprise demonstrating early robotic integrations at major industry events.
Geography: Based and operating globally, with robotic integration demonstrations in Berlin.
Beyond physical AI: Its core business is manufacturing life sciences and laboratory equipment, including high-throughput screening systems.

points.name: KINEXON
points.description: Global robotics orchestration company coordinating diverse fleets of autonomous mobile robots across manufacturing and warehouse facilities.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds a vendor-agnostic fleet management and orchestration platform for heterogeneous autonomous mobile robots, automated guided vehicles, and manual vehicles in intralogistics and manufacturing. The organization provides AI-driven scheduling, real-time diagnostics, and IoT-based localization that connects physical automation to enterprise resource planning systems for logistics operators and manufacturers.
1. A developer tools and platform company whose fleet management and orchestration software logistics engineers and operators use to control heterogeneous robot fleets.
2. A fleet orchestration engine that uses machine learning and constraint-aware scheduling for task assignment, supplemented by IoT hardware for real-time localization and an AI assistant for operational analytics.
3. Fleet orchestration, task assignment and route optimization, real-time diagnostics, vehicle downtime prevention, and digital asset tracking.
4. Licensed software and accompanying IoT hardware, integrated with enterprise resource planning and manufacturing execution systems.
5. Warehouses, factories, intralogistics, and manufacturing operations, particularly in the automotive, aerospace, and high-tech industries.
6. Logistics operators, manufacturers, and industrial enterprises running mixed fleets of autonomous mobile robots and automated guided vehicles.
7. Its software sits between enterprise resource planning systems and individual robots, integrating diverse hardware from multiple manufacturers into a centralized management layer.
8. A vendor-agnostic approach that centralizes control of heterogeneous fleets, combining AI-driven scheduling with IoT-based real-time localization and business-driven agentic reasoning from enterprise system integration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SAP, major industrial robot providers, and leading enterprise software platforms.
Organization type: A privately held technology company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions, IoT hardware sales, and enterprise integration contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established enterprise technology provider operating globally, with deployments across European industrial markets and international equipment vendors.
Geography: Based in Europe, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is dedicated to physical automation, digital asset tracking, and the orchestration of warehouse and manufacturing operations.

points.name: LG CNS
points.description: South Korean IT services company deploying multi-vendor warehouse robots and integrating them with business software for logistics automation.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and IT services company that builds robot orchestration and training platforms, integrating physical AI and multi-vendor robot control into enterprise software environments for logistics operators.
1. A developer tools company whose multi-vendor robot orchestration and training platform runs across third-party logistics automation, combined with enterprise IT integration services.
2. Multi-vendor robot orchestration software integrated with enterprise resource planning systems to drive AI-driven automation and optimization.
3. Multi-vendor robot orchestration, physical AI training, and the generation of robotics data from deployed automation.
4. Integration services and a robot orchestration software platform.
5. Logistics centers and warehouse automation.
6. Logistics operators and enterprise businesses undergoing digital transformation.
7. It installs and orchestrates third-party robots and logistics automation within enterprise customer facilities.
8. It combines multi-vendor robot orchestration with enterprise resource planning system integration to align physical AI with business context.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: SAP and LX Pantos.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a large conglomerate.
Business model: IT services contracts and enterprise software integration.
Scale and maturity: An established enterprise IT services provider with deployments across Asia.
Geography: Based in South Korea and operating across Asia.
Beyond physical AI: The organization provides broader IT services, digital transformation, and enterprise system integration outside of physical AI.

points.name: CSP Maintenance
points.description: Singapore cleaning company deploying autonomous floor-scrubbing robots with on-device navigation across commercial buildings.
points.bullets:
A commercial cleaning services company that operates autonomous mobile robots for floor-scrubbing in commercial properties, integrating robots sourced from robot makers with fleet middleware and building management systems rather than building its own hardware or software.
1. A cleaning operator that runs autonomous mobile robots it integrates and deploys in its own facility-management contracts.
2. Autonomous floor-scrubbing, on-device perception and navigation, and robotic fleet orchestration across multi-tower commercial properties.
3. Robotic cleaning services performed by the organization in commercial properties under its facility-management contracts.
4. Commercial buildings, business parks and multi-tower office properties.
5. Property owners and facility-management operators at large commercial properties.
6. It buys autonomous mobile robots from robot makers and operates them in its own cleaning contracts, integrating them with middleware and building infrastructure.
7. Early-mover advantage in local robotics middleware deployment, combining deep facility-management expertise with locally embedded engineering and change-management support.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: MPACT, LionsBot and HOPE Technik.
Organization type: A privately held commercial cleaning services company.
Business model: Facility-management and cleaning service contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established cleaning business recently expanded to autonomous robotics deployments at a large multi-tower commercial property in Singapore.
Geography: Based in Singapore and operates its robotics deployments within the country.
Beyond physical AI: Its traditional and primary business is providing manual commercial cleaning and facility-management services.

points.name: HOPE Technik
points.description: Singaporean technology provider building industrial and defense robots for factory automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that builds custom-engineered robotic systems and unmanned vehicles for defense, industrial, and commercial applications, and provides middleware integration services for multi-robot building environments. The company delivers complete physical platforms alongside Robotics Middleware Framework-based integration, programming, and digital mapping for facility deployments, serving military, industrial, and property management clients.
1. A robot maker and systems integrator that builds custom-engineered unmanned vehicles and specialized mobile robots, and sells them as complete physical systems alongside integration services.
2. Mechatronic platforms with on-device control systems, including unmanned firefighting vehicles, multifunction robots, and drones, combined with Robotics Middleware Framework-based software that bridges communication between applications and building infrastructure.
3. Autonomous navigation in challenging environments, remote firefighting and ordnance disposal operations, and multi-robot fleet coordination through building systems like lifts and turnstiles.
4. Complete robots, unmanned vehicles, and middleware integration services including digital mapping, programming, troubleshooting, and change management workshops.
5. Defense and military operations, firefighting, healthcare, industrial facilities, and commercial properties with cleaning, surveillance, and last-mile delivery functions.
6. Militaries, civil defense forces, industrial operators, property managers, and government agencies.
7. It builds and supplies complete robotic platforms to end operators and integrates middleware services into building infrastructure for multi-robot facility deployments.
8. A hands-on engineering approach rooted in motorsports and high-risk military robotics delivers flexible physical platforms with a high level of on-device sophistication for challenging environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: MPACT, Mapletree Business City, Singapore Civil Defence Force, CSP Maintenance, AIRBUS Group, DELPHI, and its wholly-owned subsidiary SESTO Robotics.
Organization type: A privately held engineering and robotics firm.
Business model: Hardware sales of custom robotic systems, unmanned vehicles, and integration services contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established engineering firm that transitioned from military robotics to commercial and industrial automation with global clients and facility-scale deployments.
Geography: Based in Singapore, operating in global robotics markets and participating in Singapore's Smart Nation initiative.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation constitute the entire focus and core mission of the organization.

points.name: LionsBot
points.description: Singaporean robotics provider deploying autonomous cleaning robots for commercial facilities.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs and manufactures autonomous mobile robots for commercial floor cleaning, integrating on-device perception and navigation to perform scrubbing, mopping, and vacuuming tasks without human supervision. It supplies complete, self-sufficient cleaning machines to the commercial cleaning sector for deployment in high-traffic indoor and outdoor environments.
1. A robot maker that designs and manufactures autonomous mobile cleaning robots.
2. Autonomous mobile robots built with 3D lidar, multi-sensor fusion, and on-device AI inference using NVIDIA silicon for navigation and cleaning operations.
3. Autonomous floor scrubbing, mopping, and vacuuming, independent lift operation, multi-floor navigation, and obstacle avoidance in tight corridors.
4. Complete robots sold or leased to cleaning operators and facility managers, supported by integration services through third-party integrators.
5. Commercial real estate, healthcare facilities, airports, hospitality venues, retail spaces, train stations, and public hawker centres.
6. Commercial cleaning operators, facility management firms, transportation hubs, and robotics integrators.
7. It builds complete robots and sells or leases them to facility operators and integrators that deploy them in end-user environments.
8. It builds cleaning robots certified for data protection, privacy, and sustainability, with a rental-based business model and lift-operation capability.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It sources vision technology from Orbbec and sells robots through the integrator RobotLAB.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through robot sales and a robots-as-a-service rental model with monthly fees.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018, it has deployed thousands of robots across 30 countries.
Geography: It is headquartered in Singapore and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and autonomous cleaning robotics represent its entire focus.

points.name: Tata Motors
points.description: Indian automaker integrating Level 2+ autonomous driving features and NVIDIA-powered systems into its passenger vehicles.
points.bullets:
An automaker that builds electric buses and passenger vehicles and is integrating autonomous driving technology into its cars. The company manufactures complete electric vehicles while relying on external suppliers for critical EV components such as battery cells, power electronics and motors, and partners with AI platform providers for autonomous vehicle software. It serves the passenger and commercial vehicle market.
1. A vehicle maker that builds and sells electric passenger cars and buses.
2. Electric vehicle drivetrains incorporating externally sourced lithium-ion battery cells, power electronics and motors, with Level 2+ driver-assistance features being integrated through a collaboration with an AI compute platform provider.
3. Electric mobility and Level 2+ assisted driving in passenger vehicles.
4. Complete electric passenger vehicles and commercial buses.
5. Passenger vehicles and electric buses.
6. Consumers and commercial fleet operators.
7. The company designs and sells complete vehicles, buying battery cells, power electronics and motors from component suppliers and autonomous driving software from AI platform providers.
8. The company is a major domestic electric vehicle and bus manufacturer sourcing key electric drivetrain technology from Chinese suppliers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA.
Organization type: A publicly traded automotive manufacturer.
Business model: Vehicle sales.
Scale and maturity: A major established automotive manufacturer and top electric bus maker in India.
Geography: Based in India and serving the Indian market.
Beyond physical AI: The company produces internal combustion engine vehicles alongside its electric vehicle and bus lines.

points.name: Rockwell
points.description: US industrial automation company deploying autonomous mobile robots and edge AI computing systems for smart factory operations.
points.bullets:
An industrial automation company and systems integrator that designs and installs factory automation combining edge compute, machine vision, digital twin simulation, and robotic systems for manufacturers and logistics operators.
1. A systems integrator that installs factory and warehouse automation built from its own industrial control platforms and acquired robotic systems.
2. Industrial control software, edge computing infrastructure, machine vision, and digital twin simulation integrated with autonomous mobile robots.
3. Factory automation, predictive operations, autonomous material handling, and sim-to-real robotics training.
4. Integration services, industrial control systems, and autonomous mobile robots installed as complete deployed architectures.
5. Factories and warehouses.
6. Manufacturers and logistics operators.
7. It integrates industrial control systems and autonomous mobile robots into complete deployed architectures for factories.
8. It acts as a platform orchestrator combining proprietary automation software, acquired robotic systems, and external cloud APIs into predictive factory operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It integrates industrial systems with autonomous mobile robots from an acquired robot maker.
Organization type: A publicly traded conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales, software licenses, and integration services.
Scale and maturity: A large, mature enterprise described as the world's largest dedicated industrial automation firm, operating globally.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating globally, with installations in Indian factories and a Robotics Center of Excellence in Waterloo, Ontario.
Beyond physical AI: Industrial automation is the organization's entire focus.

points.name: ModelMill
points.description: AI software platform automating training of logic-based neural networks for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that operates an automated machine learning platform for edge AI, training logic-based networks optimized for resource-constrained microcontrollers. The platform takes in raw data and outputs self-contained C code software development kits for embedded inference without machine learning framework dependencies or cloud connectivity. It serves developers and manufacturers needing on-device intelligence for ultra-constrained hardware.
1. A developer tools company whose automated machine learning platform generates logic-based models for embedded deployment.
2. Logic-based networks that use bitwise operations on integers rather than floating-point matrix multiplication, produced by automated model architecture search optimized for specific hardware profiles.
3. Automated machine learning, hardware-agnostic code generation, and on-device inference on 32-bit microcontrollers without GPUs, NPUs, or floating-point units.
4. Self-contained C software development kits and cloud-based automated machine learning platform access.
5. Hearing aids, vision-based quality inspection, predictive maintenance, and battery-operated IoT sensors.
6. Developers and manufacturers needing on-device intelligence for embedded systems.
7. Its generated C code is deployed on edge AI chips from multiple semiconductor manufacturers and integrated by device makers into embedded systems.
8. It generates deterministic models that run on any 32-bit processor without floating-point units, GPUs, or NPUs, achieving 52× greater energy efficiency than neural network equivalents.
points.profile:
Organization type: A technology company operating a specialized software platform developed by a separate corporate entity.
Business model: Software platform access or licenses.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on automating the machine learning pipeline from data ingestion through model training, testing, and portable code generation for edge AI.

points.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
points.description: US technology company providing ruggedized edge servers for AI inference in industrial and manufacturing environments.
points.bullets:
A systems manufacturer that builds ruggedized edge computing servers and converged infrastructure for industrial AI workloads and harsh physical environments, packaging GPU acceleration for customers that need to run inference and data processing on-site.
1. A systems manufacturer that designs edge computing servers and hyperconverged infrastructure sold as hardware and as consumption-based cloud services.
2. Industry-standard rack and tower servers, ruggedized edge systems with extended temperature and vibration tolerance, and hyperconverged infrastructure with silicon root-of-trust security and AI-driven operational monitoring.
3. On-site AI inference, real-time data processing, GPU acceleration for edge workloads, and AI-driven infrastructure monitoring and resolution.
4. Hardware servers, ruggedized edge systems, and hyperconverged infrastructure sold directly or through a consumption-based subscription model.
5. Factory floors, remote industrial environments, telecommunications, and space-based computing systems.
6. Manufacturers, retailers, telecommunications operators, public sector agencies, and aerospace organizations.
7. Its server and edge systems are deployed by industrial operators and integrators to run AI workloads directly at the point of data creation.
8. Its enterprise-grade silicon root-of-trust architecture and ruggedized hardware deliver consistent manageability and operational continuity from data centers to harsh physical edge environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its systems incorporate GPUs and processors from NVIDIA, Intel, and Qualcomm, and it is acquiring Juniper Networks for intelligent edge networking.
Organization type: A publicly traded enterprise technology conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales and consumption-based infrastructure subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: A multinational corporation with over USD 30 billion in annual revenue that has deployed systems aboard the International Space Station.
Geography: Based in Spring, Texas, USA, with global operations.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the broader organization provides enterprise IT products, hybrid cloud solutions, and comprehensive networking infrastructure.

points.name: Rockchip
points.description: Chinese semiconductor company producing system-on-chips with integrated NPUs for edge device inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs system-on-chips with integrated neural processing units for on-device inference, targeting cost-sensitive edge AI devices and robotics.
1. A chip company that designs system-on-chips with integrated neural processing units for on-device inference.
2. 8nm octa-core system-on-chips combining quad-core Cortex-A76 and quad-core Cortex-A55 CPUs, Mali-G610 MP4 GPUs and 6 TOPS neural processing units, alongside an SDK for converting and running models on its NPUs.
3. On-device inference, real-time object detection and video processing for edge gateways and smart devices.
4. Chips or modules designed into single-board computers, industrial Android boards, edge computing boxes and smart devices by embedded systems manufacturers.
5. Service robots, quadruped robots, humanoid robots, digital signage, smart home hubs and edge gateways.
6. Embedded systems manufacturers, industrial computing brands and single-board computer makers.
7. Its chips are designed into edge computing systems and smart devices by original equipment manufacturers.
8. It targets the cost-effective, power-efficient intermediate layer between low-level control and high-level reasoning in robotics, rather than high-performance mobile-class silicon.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its processors are used in systems by Advantech, ADLINK, Avalue Technology and Khadas.
Organization type: Privately held fabless semiconductor company.
Business model: Chip sales and related software toolkits.
Scale and maturity: An established chip supplier with a flagship processor deployed across numerous industrial computing platforms and robot forms.
Geography: Based in Shanghai, China, with chips utilized globally by various embedded systems brands.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI are central to its mission, as its flagship processors are specifically engineered to deliver low-latency, on-device inference for autonomous navigation and real-time control.

points.name: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking
points.description: European government funding agency financing supercomputing infrastructure and AI Factories to support AI development across Europe.
points.bullets:
A government initiative that funds edge AI silicon development and operates supercomputing infrastructure for AI training and inference across Europe.
1. A government agency that funds AI hardware development and provides supercomputing facilities as a shared infrastructure resource.
2. Publicly funded high-performance computing systems and grant programs supporting RISC-V-based AI acceleration chiplet development.
3. Supercomputing capacity and GPU resources for developing AI models, along with grant funding for edge AI chiplet hardware development.
4. Government grants awarded to silicon developers and pay-per-use or free access to computing infrastructure for startups and researchers.
5. AI factories, supercomputing centers, and edge AI acceleration platforms used across scientific, industrial, and startup environments.
6. AI startups, small and medium-sized enterprises, researchers, and scientific communities.
7. It acts as a funding and infrastructure provider that pools resources to support the AI ecosystem rather than directly manufacturing hardware or models.
8. It provides digitally sovereign, EU-compliant computing infrastructure to protect European interests in sensitive applications.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: BDVA is a private member of the joint undertaking, and Axelera AI received a 61.6 million euro grant for RISC-V-based AI acceleration platforms.
Organization type: A public joint undertaking of the European Union and participating countries.
Business model: Public funding through grants and state-funded computing infrastructure provision.
Scale and maturity: It manages 12 procured supercomputers and 19 AI factories across Europe, including an exascale system, with a planned 10 billion euro expansion for AI gigafactories.
Geography: It is based in and operates exclusively across Europe, distributing resources among member states.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it operates Europe's quantum computing infrastructure and funds research across the entire supercomputing supply chain.

points.name: Aetina
points.description: Taiwanese embedded systems provider building computing hardware and platforms to run artificial intelligence directly on physical devices.
points.bullets:
An embedded systems provider that designs and builds industrial edge computing platforms and GPU servers for on-device inference and on-premises AI training, serving robotics and industrial automation developers.
1. A hardware company that builds edge AI computers, inference modules, and GPU servers, sold as embedded systems and computing appliances to machine builders and integrators.
2. Fanless, rugged edge computing systems powered by low-power system-on-modules and discrete GPUs, featuring modular AI accelerator card slots.
3. On-device inference for 3D perception, agentic AI, and defect detection, alongside on-premises edge AI model training and fine-tuning.
4. Edge AI computers, inference modules, and GPU servers sold as embedded hardware to device makers and as on-premises appliances to enterprises.
5. Robotic arms, industrial defect inspection, automated wiring and cable assembly, and smart city or transportation systems.
6. Robotics companies, industrial automation integrators, and enterprise AI developers.
7. Its edge computers and servers are designed into physical machines and on-premises deployments by device makers and automation partners.
8. Modular hardware designs that allow flexible AI accelerator selection without system redesign, paired with industrial-grade rugged construction.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Rockchip, TrueFlaw, and Stereolabs.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of embedded computing systems and edge servers.
Scale and maturity: A mature embedded computing provider with a multi-tiered product portfolio and global operations.
Geography: Based in Taiwan, serving global markets.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire business is dedicated to developing and deploying edge AI hardware and computing infrastructure.

points.name: Fibocom
points.description: Chinese wireless communications module vendor equipping smart mowing robots with on-device processing for autonomous navigation without cloud reliance.
points.bullets:
A wireless communications module vendor that builds intelligent modules enabling on-device computation for autonomous robotic systems like smart mowers, integrating edge AI silicon from chip partners into ready-to-deploy robotic solutions for device makers.
1. A wireless communications module vendor that designs intelligent wireless modules for on-device inference, sold as embedded modules to robotics and device manufacturers.
2. Wireless communication and intelligent compute modules integrating system-on-chips for on-device environment mapping, obstacle avoidance, and boundary recognition without cloud reliance.
3. The module delivers on-device computation, autonomous decision-making, environment mapping, obstacle detection, and boundary recognition for robotic systems.
4. The company provides its technology as embedded intelligent modules integrated into robotic systems by device manufacturers.
5. The intelligent modules are used in autonomous robotic systems such as smart mowing robots.
6. The modules are sold to robotics manufacturers and device makers building autonomous machines.
7. Its intelligent modules are designed into autonomous robotic systems by device manufacturers using edge AI silicon from chip companies.
8. It combines wireless communications with intelligent compute modules to enable fully autonomous, cloud-independent robotic operation in a single embedded component.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Qualcomm provides the intelligent module for its robotic solutions.
Organization type: The organization is a publicly traded company.
Business model: The company makes money through the sale of wireless communication and intelligent embedded modules.
Scale and maturity: The China-based vendor demonstrated its robotic solution at Embedded World 2024.
Geography: The company is based in China and operates domestically.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the company focuses on wireless communications modules for cellular IoT, broadband, and connected device markets.

points.name: Thundercomm
points.description: US IoT joint venture delivering edge AI computing stations for industrial video analytics and on-device inference.
points.bullets:
An IoT edge device maker that builds turnkey edge computing appliances combining third-party inference silicon with proprietary software for on-device AI and video analytics, sold to enterprises for industrial and commercial deployments.
1. An edge device maker that builds and sells edge AI gateways and computing stations built around third-party SoCs.
2. Fanless edge computing hardware integrating Qualcomm SoCs for INT8 inference with a proprietary operating system providing microservices and cloud connectivity.
3. On-device AI model execution, real-time video decoding across multiple channels, and human detection and tracking.
4. Complete edge computing appliances with embedded operating system software.
5. Smart manufacturing, smart retail, smart city, video collaboration, security monitoring, and traffic management.

3. Automated assembly of complex mechanical systems, precision fastening operations and battery pack assembly.
4. Complete deployed modular robotic cells, contract manufacturing services and integration services.

6. Defense sector customers, energy storage manufacturers and dual-use industrial hardware developers.

points.name: House Science, Space and Technology Committee
points.description: US congressional committee overseeing edge AI and robotics policy through legislative hearings and industry assessments.
points.bullets:
A government body that conducts legislative oversight and develops federal policy for the edge and physical AI ecosystem, examining the intersection of autonomy software and robotic hardware without directly producing commercial products.
1. A government agency that sets science and technology policy for physical AI industries.
2. Legislative analysis of the full edge AI technology stack, evaluating computer vision, reinforcement learning, and physical robotic hardware systems.
3. Identification of critical policy gaps in physical AI, noting that hardware development and system integration remain underfunded relative to software.
4. Federal policy recommendations and legislative hearings evaluating technological competitiveness.
5. Manufacturing, agriculture, elder care facilities, and emerging physical AI sectors across the United States.
6. Federal legislators, national policy makers, and domestic physical AI industries.
7. Acts as a policy regulator and strategic evaluator rather than a direct participant in the manufacturing or deployment of physical AI systems.
8. Distinguishes its approach by identifying that while AI software receives significant investment, physical hardware development and system integration remain critically underfunded.

Key partners and customers: Engages with industry leaders and trade associations to assess robotics development across multiple sectors.
Organization type: A congressional committee of the United States federal government.

points.name: Tulsa Innovation Lab
points.description: Oklahoma-based innovation hub advancing regional ecosystems and deploying autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
A regional innovation hub that develops the autonomous systems ecosystem and supports advanced air mobility deployment in Tulsa, working with federal partners on airspace safety initiatives.
1. An innovation organization that operates an ecosystem development hub and funds or coordinates regional autonomous systems initiatives.
2. Ecosystem coordination and airspace safety frameworks facilitate the integration of unmanned aircraft into national airspace.
3. Advanced air mobility ecosystem development, drone delivery support and autonomous systems airspace safety coordination.
4. Partnership programs, government initiatives and ecosystem coordination services.
5. Advanced air mobility, drone delivery and autonomous systems.

Organization type: A regional innovation organization and government-adjacent ecosystem hub.

A government committee that legislates the regulatory framework for autonomous commercial motor vehicles, establishing national standards for the safe testing and operation of autonomous trucks using on-device AI for the freight logistics sector.
1. A government body that drafts and advances federal legislation governing autonomous commercial vehicle operations on surface transportation networks.
2. Federal legislative frameworks and surface transportation reauthorization bills that define operational requirements for autonomous commercial motor vehicles.
3. Regulatory oversight, national operational standards, and legal guidelines enabling the deployment of autonomous freight systems on public infrastructure.
4. Federal legislation and statutory frameworks implemented by federal motor carrier safety administrations.

6. Commercial trucking operators, freight logistics companies, and autonomous vehicle technology developers.

Key partners and customers: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration is responsible for implementing its operational requirements.
Organization type: A congressional committee within the United States House of Representatives.

A government legislative committee that drafts and advances federal policy and regulatory frameworks governing the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles and physical AI systems. points.name: Ukraine's Defense Ministry
points.description: Ukrainian government agency deploying autonomous ground robots for frontline logistics and casualty evacuation.

A government defense ministry that procures and operates unmanned ground vehicles for frontline military logistics, evacuation and strike missions. It runs a mass-deployment robotics modernization initiative to field tens of thousands of ground robots and substitute a portion of frontline infantry with autonomous systems. It acts as an end operator and systems integrator, approving domestic robotic platforms and coordinating production across hundreds of manufacturers.
1. A government agency that procures unmanned ground vehicles from private manufacturers and operates them in its own military forces.
2. Unmanned ground vehicles equipped with on-device AI for autonomous navigation and real-time decision-making in GPS-denied battlefield environments.
3. Autonomous frontline logistics, ammunition transport, mine clearance and casualty evacuation.
4. Complete robots and vehicles procured through contracts and a digital procurement system, operated by the military itself.
5. Active frontline combat zones and domestic defense production facilities.
6. National armed forces and frontline military units.

8. Rapid scaling of physical AI for combat backed by large-scale frontline operational experience and a surge in domestic manufacturing.

Organization type: A government ministry functioning as a wartime defense agency.
Business model: Government procurement through defense contracts.

points.name: Brave1
points.description: Ukrainian government defense program funding AI-enabled autonomous systems and robotic platforms for battlefield deployment.

5. Defense technology, combat drones, ground robots, and unmanned systems.
6. Defense technology developers, domestic and international manufacturers, and military stakeholders.
7. It funds and integrates technology from robotics developers and manufacturers into military operations and defense procurement.
8. It facilitates rapid iteration cycles measured in weeks rather than years by providing direct real-time feedback from combat conditions alongside traditional financial backing.

points.name: Hadrian Automation
points.description: US aerospace manufacturing startup operating software-driven, automated factories to produce precision components.

A systems integrator that designs, builds and operates automated, software-driven factory cells that produce precision-machined components for aerospace and defense hardware, embedding the production lines inside client facilities under a factory-as-a-service model.

4. Turnkey production cells and factory software delivered as an embedded, factory-as-a-service operation inside client facilities.
5. Aerospace and defense manufacturing facilities, including missile and fire control plants.
6. Aerospace and defense prime contractors and autonomous defense system makers.
7. It installs and operates its own automated production cells inside the facilities of defense primes.

points.name: Nominal
points.description: Cloud platform startup building data infrastructure and testing software for AI-integrated hardware systems.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides a cloud and edge data and testing platform for hardware engineering, enabling the validation of autonomous physical systems. It builds software that connects, manages, and analyzes real-time test data for engineers building AI-driven machines, selling this platform to commercial hardware developers and government defense programs.
1. A developer tools company whose data and AI validation platform robotics and aerospace engineers use to test physical systems.
2. Cloud-based databases and edge-native control applications that ingest, synchronize, and analyze real-time hardware test data for automated verification.

points.name: AI Rapid Capabilities Cell
points.description: US government agency accelerating deployment of uncrewed and autonomous systems for defense applications through rapid experimentation and pilot funding.

A government agency that accelerates the adoption and integration of commercial uncrewed systems, physical automation, and edge AI technologies for military use cases by procuring and orchestrating subsystems into complete operational systems.

points.name: Foundation Future Industries
points.description: California robotics startup developing industrial humanoid robots with camera-based perception and language model reasoning for human-scale physical labor tasks.

A humanoid robot maker that builds and sells industrial and defense humanoid robots, leasing them to commercial customers and supplying them to government entities for hazardous workflows. 1. A government agency that funds robotics R&D, establishes industry clusters, and procures robots to stimulate national market demand.
2. Legislation, funding programs, and industrial policy targeting self-sufficiency in core robotics hardware and autonomous operation software.
3. Strategic investment, regulatory frameworks, robotics education mandates, and coordination of national humanoid platform development.
4. R&D grants, physical industry clusters, subsidized procurement programs, and public-sector deployments.
5. Manufacturing, agriculture, defense, and public facilities.
6. Domestic robot makers, component suppliers, public institutions, and private automation companies.
7. Its funding and policies drive hardware and software development across the entire domestic robotics value chain.
8. A holistic approach to industrial independence targets raising domestic production of critical robot parts from 44 percent to 80 percent by 2030.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Engages domestic conglomerates through the K-Humanoid Alliance and deepens technology-sharing alliances with the United States.
Organization type: A national government entity operating under the Intelligent Robots Development and Promotion Act of 2008.
Business model: State budget allocations, public-private investment matching, and government procurement.
Scale and maturity: A mature apparatus that has committed over $3 billion historically and is coordinating $2.24 billion through 2030, achieving a robot density of 932 robots per 10,000 workers by 2023.
Geography: Based in and entirely focused on advancing the domestic ecosystem within South Korea.
Beyond physical AI: Functions as the state's overarching economic and technological policy engine, utilizing targeted legislation to guide broader industrial growth and national security alliances.

points.name: China
points.description: National government accelerating domestic robotics production and edge AI adoption to dominate global high-tech manufacturing.
points.bullets:
A government that funds, regulates and coordinates a national ecosystem for robotics, autonomous systems and edge AI, using subsidies, procurement preferences, state-backed venture capital funds and multi-year strategic plans to build domestic manufacturing scale and self-reliance across the full technology stack for domestic and global markets.
1. A government agency that directs and funds national robotics, autonomous-system and semiconductor programs through policy, subsidies and procurement preferences.
2. State-directed industrial strategy spanning inference silicon, sensors, actuators, robots and autonomy algorithms, including classified algorithms for autonomous drone swarms and programs for military underwater robots.
3. National-scale robot manufacturing, deployment density and supply-chain control across industrial, humanoid, autonomous-vehicle and military autonomous platforms.
4. Government subsidies, procurement preferences, equity guidance funds and classified research and procurement programs that drive domestic production and deployment.
5. Industrial robots in factories and warehouses, humanoid robots, autonomous vehicles, military drone swarms, underwater robots and aerospace composites.
6. Domestic manufacturers, robot makers, automakers, militaries and state-backed enterprises receiving subsidies, procurement contracts or strategic guidance.
7. Its subsidies and procurement preferences shape domestic design and manufacturing of robots, chips and components, while its export controls on rare earths and procurement policy influence global machine makers.
8. Unified state mobilization combining long-term policy, subsidies, procurement and supply-chain control to capture manufacturing scale and global market share in physical AI.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Named collaborators include Boeing and Hexcel in an aerospace composite materials joint venture, and component supply to Russian drone programs.
Organization type: A national government and its agencies, including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and a state-backed venture capital fund.
Business model: State expenditure through subsidies, procurement and equity guidance funds, supplemented by export licensing of rare earths.
Scale and maturity: A mature national strategy launched in 2015, accounting for the majority of global robotic deployments and roughly three-quarters of the humanoid and autonomous vehicle markets, with a robotics industry generating nearly 240 billion yuan in revenue in 2024.
Geography: Based in China, operating domestically while heavily influencing and controlling critical nodes of the worldwide technology supply chain.
Beyond physical AI: It directs national policy across advanced industrial sectors including electric vehicles, lithium batteries, innovative pharmaceuticals, nuclear power and aerospace, with robotics and physical AI as foundational to a broader goal of high-tech self-reliance and global industrial supremacy.

points.name: United Kingdom
points.description: National government driving physical AI growth through strategic policy frameworks and ecosystem investment.
points.bullets:
A national government body that funds and regulates the edge and physical AI ecosystem, establishing regulatory sandboxes and investing in research infrastructure across the entire stack from foundational research to deployed autonomous systems for public and private sectors.
1. A government agency that funds robotics programs and establishes outcome-based regulations for physical AI technologies.
2. Regulatory frameworks, regulatory sandboxes, and targeted research and development funding programs spanning inference silicon, sensors, robots, vehicles, drones, autonomy software, and robot models.
3. Regulatory authorization for autonomous systems like drone delivery, controlled testing environments for physical AI, and ecosystem coordination across manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, energy, defense, and environmental monitoring.
4. Government grants, research funding, and regulatory pathways delivered to organizations developing or deploying physical AI.
5. Autonomous vehicles, drone delivery, warehouse automation, manufacturing, agriculture, healthcare, infrastructure, energy, defense, and environmental monitoring.
6. Research councils, private industry developers, logistics operators, manufacturers, healthcare providers, defense forces, and technology startups.
7. It sits above the physical AI value chain, funding foundational research and deployment while regulating the organizations that build and operate physical AI systems.
8. It uses adaptive, outcome-based regulations focused on safety performance with technical flexibility and regulatory sandboxes to overcome domestic fragmentation and foster ecosystem growth.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Expert partnerships and research councils with private industry.
Organization type: A national government agency.
Business model: Taxpayer-funded research and development grants, regulatory oversight, and strategic national investments.

Geography: Based in the United Kingdom, focusing investments and regulatory initiatives entirely within the domestic national ecosystem.

points.name: United States
points.description: National government funding breakthrough research in autonomous systems and on-device AI for national security.
points.bullets:
A government defense agency that funds and conducts fundamental research and development in edge AI, robotics, and autonomous systems to build and transition high-risk prototypes for national security.
1. A government agency that funds research programs developing sensors, actuators, autonomy software, and unmanned platforms for the military.
2. Advanced unmanned systems, actuators, sensor architectures, and physical AI prototypes developed through managed research programs and technical challenges.
3. Autonomous navigation, target recognition, dexterous manipulation, and unmanned vehicle operation under military operational conditions.
4. Government contracts and funded research programs that deliver prototype hardware, software, and integrated unmanned platforms.
5. Defense, military ground vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles, spacecraft, and government research operations.
6. Military branches, defense organizations, nontraditional defense contractors, and technology startups.
7. It funds research that develops components, software, and platforms for other defense contractors and military operators to integrate.
8. It explicitly pursues high-risk, high-gain technological breakthroughs beyond immediate military requirements by running open technical challenges and funding nontraditional performers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The Department of Defense, NASA, research universities, and technology startups.
Organization type: A government agency operating as an independent research and development arm within the federal defense apparatus.
Business model: Government funding and contracts for research and development programs.

points.name: HD Hyundai Robotics
points.description: South Korean robotics manufacturer deploying sensor-equipped collaborative robots and AI safety controllers for factory automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells industrial robots, collaborative robots and complete factory automation systems integrated with physical AI, serving heavy-equipment, automotive, shipbuilding and logistics manufacturers.

points.name: Airobotics
points.description: Israeli drone manufacturer deploying fully autonomous drone-in-a-box systems for continuous aerial missions.
points.bullets:
A drone maker that builds fully autonomous drone-in-a-box systems and counter-unmanned aerial vehicle platforms for government, industrial, and commercial sectors. It develops the complete integrated stack, including the custom aircraft, automated base stations, and AI-driven autonomy software, to deliver continuous, automated aerial missions.

8. Full-stack engineering control over the entire platform combined with deep regulatory compliance expertise enables civil airspace approvals for automated flight.

Organization type: A wholly owned subsidiary of a publicly traded holding company.

points.name: Elbit Systems
points.description: Israeli defense contractor developing autonomous AI systems for unmanned military drones and ground vehicles.

A defense electronics company and robot maker that builds and operates unmanned aerial systems, unmanned ground vehicles, and advanced sensors with integrated AI for military and security applications.

A robotic software and vision system developer that builds AI-powered controllers, force feedback software, and 3D cameras for high-accuracy and high-agility manipulation in industrial automation. points.name: Platform Industry 4.0

points.name: Economic Development Board (EDB)
points.description: Singapore government agency funding robotics R&D, subsidizing business automation adoption, and driving AI transformation across industries.
points.bullets:
A government agency that plans and executes national economic strategy, administering a multi-hundred-million-dollar national robotics program that funds R&D, provides automation adoption incentives, and supports workforce training rather than building hardware or software.
1. A government agency that funds robotics programs, administers grants for automation, and orchestrates the physical AI ecosystem for research institutions and enterprises.
2. The agency delivers funding for R&D, automation adoption incentives, workforce training programs, and regulatory frameworks for real-world robotics testbeds.
3. It sits at the top of the value stack as an ecosystem orchestrator, driving the deployment of autonomous systems through funding and regulatory agility rather than manufacturing components.
4. The organization leverages the country's compact geography and regulatory speed to serve as a competitive real-world testbed and a gateway for robotics companies entering the broader ASEAN market.
points.profile:
Organization type: A well-established government agency responsible for economic planning.
Business model: Grants, funding programs, and strategic national investments.
Scale and maturity: A mature entity administering a $635 million national robotics initiative.
Geography: Based in Singapore, focusing on establishing the nation as a critical gateway for robotics companies entering the ASEAN market.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, the organization drives broad enterprise-wide digital transformation, supports large-scale industrial infrastructure projects, and co-leads national solar PV deployment programs.

points.name: A*STAR
points.description: Singapore government agency accelerating robotics adoption and coordinating research for physical AI systems.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and conducts research and development in robotics, physical AI, and advanced manufacturing, and operates testbed factories and data platforms to transfer automation technologies to industry. It bridges fundamental robotics research and commercial adoption by developing AI tools for human-robot interaction, teleoperation, and manufacturing automation, and deploying robotic systems in collaboration with enterprises.
1. A government agency that funds and operates robotics research programs, experimental manufacturing testbeds, and data-sharing platforms for researchers, manufacturers, and public sector entities.
2. Research programs in robot perception, planning, manipulation, and human-robot interaction, combined with AI-driven digital twins, teleoperation data standards, and cross-platform policy transfer.
3. Robot learning through natural human interaction using speech and gesture recognition, manufacturing process automation, and live factory testbeds for evaluating robotic systems.
4. Government-funded research programs, shared experimental factory facilities, AI software tools, and integration support for physical systems.
5. Manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, facilities management, and aerospace maintenance and repair.
6. Public sector researchers, industrial partners, local small and medium enterprises, and international corporate stakeholders.
7. It funds and generates fundamental robotics research and integrates those technologies directly into industrial operations through testbed facilities.
8. It focuses on enabling robots to understand human intentions and learn through natural interactions rather than relying on traditional programming.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Rolls-Royce, SAESL, and the Singapore Economic Development Board.
Organization type: A publicly funded government agency.
Business model: Government funding and research contracts.
Scale and maturity: A mature national agency overseeing multi-million dollar investment programs and operating multiple dedicated research institutes.
Geography: Based in Singapore and operating domestically and internationally.

points.name: Israel Innovation Authority
points.description: Israeli government agency funding R&D and commercialization of physical AI technologies like exoskeletons and delivery drones.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds edge and physical AI development by providing matching R&D grants to private businesses and academic centers. It runs incentive programs that support collaborative research and technology commercialization in robotics and related fields. The agency reduces commercialization risk for hardware and software developers while maintaining private sector discipline.
1. A government agency that funds robotics and physical AI R&D programs through matching grants to private companies and academic centers.
2. It delivers funding for system-level AI development and collaborative research in physical AI technologies including drones and exoskeletons.
3. It provides matching grants and R&D funding to companies developing physical AI products.
4. The funded technologies are used in drones, wearable exoskeletons and other physical AI systems.
5. Private businesses, technology companies and academic research centers developing physical AI and robotics.
6. It sits at the funding layer, allocating public capital to private sector developers of physical AI systems.
7. It provides matching grants that reduce commercialization risk while requiring private sector discipline and co-investment.

Key partners and customers: It runs the MAGNET incentive program in collaboration with academic centers and has funded companies including Flytrex and ReWalk.
Organization type: A government agency of the Israeli government.
Business model: It makes money by disbursing government grants and takes no equity or revenue share.
Scale and maturity: It operates at a national level with programs targeting multi-year technology strategies through 2026.
Geography: It is based in Israel and operates domestically.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the agency funds broad technology innovation across multiple sectors of the Israeli economy.

points.name: U.S. Department of Agriculture
points.description: Government agency funding agricultural robotics research and insect-detection technologies.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds agricultural robotics research and applications to enhance food production, processing, and distribution. It awards grants through initiatives like the National Robotics Initiative and supports commercialization programs that connect researchers with agricultural technologies such as UV-light treatment.
1. A government agency that funds robotics research programs for agricultural applications.
2. Federal grant programs and research initiatives that support the development of robots for insect detection, vertical farming, and crop treatment.
3. Funding for agricultural robotics research, statistical reporting on farming demographics, and commercialization support for agricultural technologies.
4. Federal grants, coordinated funding mechanisms, and commercialization programs distributed to universities and researchers.
5. Farms, vertical farming facilities, and agricultural processing and distribution systems.
6. University research labs, robotics researchers, and agricultural technology startups.
7. Its grants fund university and startup development of agricultural robots and farm automation technologies.
8. It is the federal authority developing and executing laws and funding programs specifically for farming, forestry, rural economic development, and food.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: National Institute of Food and Agriculture and the National Robotics Initiative.
Organization type: Federal executive department and government agency.
Business model: Federal funding through grants and research programs executed by taxpayer appropriations.
Scale and maturity: A cabinet-level department that administers multi-agency programs like the nearly $883,000 National Robotics Initiative grant.
Geography: Based in the United States and operating across its agricultural sector.

points.name: National Institutes of Health
points.description: US government agency funding biomedical data initiatives and machine learning tools for clinical and assistive applications.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds research and development programs for assistive and medical robotics, on-device AI, and physical-world healthcare technologies. It finances the creation of algorithms, predictive models, and software solutions intended for deployment in medical and assistive environments, serving academic institutions, medical centers, and scientific researchers.
1. A government agency that funds robotics and AI research programs through grants.
2. It funds the development of prostheses, rehabilitation systems, surgical robotics, and assistive technologies for health intervention.
3. The organization delivers funding through federal research grants and SBIR programs to accelerate commercialization and technology development.
4. Its funded technologies are used in surgery, health intervention, prostheses, and rehabilitation.
5. It provides research funding to academic institutions, medical centers, and scientific researchers.
6. It acts as a financial and strategic backbone, enabling partner institutions to build and deploy AI and robotics solutions rather than manufacturing hardware itself.
7. It focuses on funding the generation of findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable biomedical data to drive machine learning strategies.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a partner in the National Robotics Initiative and jointly supports the NRI-3.0 program with other federal agencies.
Organization type: A United States federal government agency.
Business model: It operates by administering government research budgets and grant programs.
Scale and maturity: It is a long-established, large-scale federal entity responsible for administering vast research budgets.
Geography: It is based in the United States and primarily funds domestic academic and medical research institutions.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI and robotics, its overarching mission is to fund foundational biomedical and public health research aimed at enhancing human health and reducing disabilities.

points.name: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health
points.description: United States government agency researching the safe integration of robotics and intelligent systems into workplace environments.
aliases: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and conducts research on the safe integration of robotics and physical automation into workplaces, establishing best practices and safety guidelines for industrial sectors.
1. A government agency that funds robotics safety research and develops occupational safety guidelines for physical AI systems.
2. The agency's core work involves epidemiological research, safety standards development, and convening frameworks for evaluating human-robot interaction safety.
3. It delivers safety guidelines, recommended weight limits, and risk assessment frameworks for workers who use, wear, or work near robots.
4. Customers receive its outputs through federal funding opportunities, cooperative agreements, research publications, and public safety alliances.
5. Its research applies to manufacturing, mining, warehouses, and broad industrial settings where robots and automated machines operate.
6. Its stakeholders and grantees include robotics researchers, safety professionals, industrial operators, and miners.
7. It operates at the ecosystem and standards layer, funding external research and influencing how physical automation systems are safely designed and deployed.
8. It distinguishes itself through its statutory authority and regulatory convening power, establishing consensus safety standards rather than competing in a commercial market.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The agency partners with the National Robotics Initiative, OSHA, the Association for Advancing Automation, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Organization type: A federal government agency operating as part of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Business model: It operates on federal funding, distributing grants and cooperative agreements while conducting internal scientific research.
Scale and maturity: The organization established its Center for Occupational Robotics Research in 2017 and manages multi-agency funding opportunities awarding millions of dollars.
Geography: It is based in the United States and directs its research, funding, and safety initiatives toward domestic workplaces and industrial operations.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI and automation, the organization maintains a comprehensive mandate to conduct scientific research and provide guidance on all aspects of occupational safety and health.

points.name: Flex
points.description: Global manufacturing company building automotive-grade compute platforms and validating autonomous vehicle safety systems.

A contract manufacturer and design partner that builds automotive-grade compute platforms for autonomous vehicles and scales physical AI in manufacturing for automakers and robotics companies.

2. A compute design platform engineered to automotive-grade standards for autonomous vehicle systems.
3. High-reliability compute hardware manufacturing and design validation for autonomous driving safety ecosystems.
4. Compute design platforms and contract manufacturing services delivered to autonomous vehicle makers.

points.profile:

Geography: A global organization operating worldwide.
