points.profile:
Key partners and customers: D3 Embedded, HTEC and STMicroelectronics on interior sensing solutions.
Organization type: Publicly traded company listed on Nasdaq Stockholm.
Business model: Sensor and module sales to automotive and consumer electronics customers.
Scale and maturity: Global leader in eye tracking, publicly listed since 2015.
Geography: Based in Stockholm, Sweden, serving global automotive markets.
Beyond physical AI: The company also applies eye tracking to consumer devices, research and accessibility markets beyond automotive physical AI.

points.name: Textron Systems
points.description: United States defense contractor developing autonomous uncrewed ground vehicles for military logistics and reconnaissance.
points.bullets:
A defense contractor that designs and builds uncrewed ground vehicles, drive-by-wire systems, and weapons payload integrations for military applications, providing physical robotic platforms and subsystems to defense customers.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that designs and builds uncrewed ground vehicles and mobile robotic platforms for military use.
2. Modular open systems architecture chassis, drive-by-wire vehicle controls, and interchangeable payload integrations for uncrewed platforms.
3. Uncrewed ground mobility, reconnaissance, target acquisition, counter-unmanned aircraft systems operations, and loitering munition launch delivery.
4. Complete uncrewed ground vehicles, subsystems, and systems integration services.
5. Military ground vehicles, uncrewed air and surface platforms, and defense force operations.
6. Defense customers including the U.S. Army, the U.S. Marine Corps, and defense agencies.
7. Its uncrewed ground vehicles are operated by militaries and integrated with external autonomy software.
8. Highly modular, transportable, and Modular Open Systems Approach-compliant platforms enable rapid integration of autonomous systems across air, land, and sea domains.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Part of Textron Inc., collaborating with Howe and Howe on the RIPSAW family, with AM General on the M-MET platform, and with Shield AI on autonomy integration.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded aerospace and defense conglomerate.
Business model: Defense contracts and hardware sales for military platforms and systems integration.
Scale and maturity: A mature and established player in the defense autonomy market with decades of experience and millions of operational hours.
Geography: Based in and operates within the United States, focusing on the modernization and operational needs of the U.S. armed forces.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI, robotics, and uncrewed platforms are central to its defense mission, supported by broader multi-industry brands in aerospace and other sectors through its parent company.

points.name: Wind River
points.description: Alameda software company providing safety-critical operating systems for managing distributed on-device AI and physical automation.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds the real-time operating systems, virtualization platforms, and orchestration tools for running mission-critical on-device AI and physical automation safely and deterministically. It licenses its safety-certified software portfolio and lifecycle management tools to device makers and automakers requiring high reliability in the physical world.
1. A developer tools and platform company whose real-time operating systems, embedded Linux distributions, and fleet orchestration software run on other companies' edge devices and machines.
2. Deterministic real-time operating systems, hypervisors, and Yocto-based embedded Linux distributions designed for mixed-criticality consolidation and cloud-native DevOps across x86, Arm, and RISC-V architectures.
3. Deterministic execution of AI inference workloads, mixed-criticality workload consolidation, secure over-the-air updates, continuous integration and deployment for edge devices, and large-scale fleet telemetry and lifecycle management.
4. Licensed software, cloud platforms, and developer environments delivered to device manufacturers for integration into their own hardware.
5. Autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, factory automation, aerospace and defense systems, medical imaging, and telecommunications infrastructure.
6. Automakers, aerospace and defense manufacturers, industrial device manufacturers, and telecommunications providers.
7. Its software platforms are designed into edge servers, controllers, and autonomous machines by device makers and automotive suppliers.
8. It bridges IT and operational technology silos by providing a deterministic, safety-certified software foundation that allows diverse hardware and AI models to function safely in mission-critical environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Aptiv, it collaborates with AI chip companies SiMa.ai and DeepX, and MLOps platform developer Nota AI.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded automotive technology supplier.
Business model: Software licenses, enterprise support, maintenance subscriptions, and cloud platform services.
Scale and maturity: A mature entity with over four decades in the market powering billions of devices, operating globally across multiple industrial sectors.
Geography: Based in Alameda, California, USA, operating globally across automotive, aerospace, industrial, medical, and telecommunications markets.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and mission-critical edge intelligence are the organization's entire focus, as it provides the essential software layer that enables physical devices to sense, think, and act reliably.

points.name: Antler
points.description: Global venture capital firm funding early-stage founders building physical AI and robotics startups through residency programs.
points.bullets:
A global early-stage venture capital firm that funds and launches startups across the edge and physical AI stack, backing founders who build everything from on-device AI software and components to fully deployed physical systems like industrial automation and drones.
1. A venture capital firm that provides pre-seed to Series A funding and operates structured residency programs for founders.
2. Portfolio building across industrial automation, warehouse logistics, autonomous drones, and construction technology.
3. Pre-seed funding, structural support, and cohort programs for early-stage founders.
4. It provides capital and mentorship to startups across multiple layers, from on-device AI software and components to deployed physical systems.
5. It uses a generalist, evidence-driven approach to identify macroeconomic inflection points like shifting labor dynamics and falling component costs rather than acting as a deep-tech specialist.
points.profile:
Organization type: A privately held venture capital firm.
Business model: Fund management and equity investments in early-stage companies.
Scale and maturity: A mature firm operating across 27 cities with over 1,000 portfolio companies and a goal of backing over 20 robotics and physical AI companies.
Geography: Based and operates globally across 27 cities, including Singapore, Australia, the United Kingdom, and Japan.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the firm operates as a broad startup generator and investment vehicle backing founders across software, artificial intelligence, healthcare, SaaS, and energy.

points.name: Lucky Robots
points.description: Startup providing a virtual robotics platform that simplifies robot training for software engineers.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a robotics platform for software engineers, providing virtual robot training and enabling infrastructure that abstracts traditional robotics complexities.
1. A developer tools company whose robotics and simulation platform robotics engineers use.
2. Software infrastructure that decouples robotics development from hardware complexities to enable virtual robot training.
3. Accessible robotics development and virtual robot training.
4. A software platform accessed by developers.
5. Software engineers.
6. Its platform is used by software engineers to build and train robotics applications.
7. It decouples robotics from traditional complexities to make the field accessible to software engineers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Draper.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Platform access.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage startup.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on providing enabling infrastructure for the robotics ecosystem.

points.name: Human-Centered Robotics Lab
points.location: University of Texas at Austin, USA
points.description: University research lab developing humanoid robotics technologies that launched commercial robotics company Apptronik.
points.bullets:
A university lab that conducts research in human-centered robotics and incubated a humanoid robot maker.
1. A university lab whose robotics research produced a humanoid robot company.
points.profile: Organization type: A university lab at a public research university.

points.name: EPSRC
points.description: UK government agency funding university research and prototypes in edge intelligence and autonomous sensor systems.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds edge and physical AI research and development, financing the creation of sensor network software, real-time edge intelligence models, reconfigurable autonomy, and deployed robotic prototypes for academic institutions and industry.
1. A government agency that funds research and development programs in edge AI and autonomous robotics.
2. Government research grants supporting the development of verifiable autonomy, reconfigurable autonomy, sensor system software, and real-time edge intelligence.
3. Funded research programs that deliver reconfigurable autonomy, verifiable safety for autonomous systems, sensor network software, and real-time edge intelligence.
4. Government research grants, programme grants, and funded multi-year research partnerships distributed to academic institutions and industry.
5. Autonomy and robotics research applied in nuclear energy, offshore energy, space, defense, critical national infrastructure, and healthcare.
6. Academic research institutions, national research centres, and industry heavyweights operating in energy, defense, space, and healthcare sectors.
7. It funds universities and national centres to develop physical AI subsystems and autonomy software that are later integrated into industrial and defense systems.
8. It places a heavy emphasis on the safety, verification, and ethical reliability of autonomous systems acting in the physical world.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: UKRI, The Alan Turing Institute, Innovate UK, the University of Cambridge, Microsoft, and bilateral partnerships with the United States.
Organization type: A government agency and research council operating within UK Research and Innovation.
Business model: Government research funding and grant management.
Scale and maturity: A mature, large-scale funding operation managing a £1 billion broader AI portfolio and multi-million-pound investments in specialized physical AI research hubs.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom, fostering international collaboration including bilateral partnerships with the United States.
Beyond physical AI: It funds a broad portfolio of engineering and physical sciences research, maintaining a vast £1 billion initiative dedicated to wider artificial intelligence.

points.name: University of Southampton
points.description: British university designing and manufacturing next-generation AI chips and providing edge AI research expertise.
points.bullets:
A university laboratory and foundry services provider that designs and manufactures next-generation AI chips for edge and physical AI applications. The organization operates a multidisciplinary cleanroom complex for electronic and photonic prototyping, and contributes autonomous control systems and astronautics research to national edge AI hubs. It serves researchers and organizations developing on-device inference silicon and reconfigurable autonomy systems.
1. A university research lab and foundry services provider that designs and manufactures next-generation AI chips and provides prototyping services for edge AI hardware developers.
2. Electronic and photonic chip prototyping facilities, alongside autonomous control systems and astronautics research capabilities.
3. Chip design and manufacturing for next-generation AI silicon, photonic and electronic prototyping, and autonomous control systems research.
4. Foundry services and prototyping facilities provided through a university cleanroom complex, plus research expertise contributed to national hubs.
5. On-device inference silicon, photonic chips, and reconfigurable autonomous systems.
6. Edge AI hardware developers, national edge AI research hubs, and consortium partners developing autonomy systems.
7. Its cleanroom foundry services are used by chip designers and researchers to prototype edge AI silicon, and its research expertise feeds into national hub programs.
8. It combines a leading multidisciplinary cleanroom complex for photonic and electronic chip prototyping with deep autonomous control systems and astronautics research.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: National Edge AI Hub led by Newcastle University, NeuroSYNC consortium, and Reconfigurable Autonomy project.
Organization type: A university research institution and laboratory.
Business model: Foundry services for chip prototyping and publicly funded research programs.
Scale and maturity: A long-established UK university hosting Europe's leading multidisciplinary cleanroom complex and partnering in multiple national research hubs.
Geography: Based in Southampton, UK, contributing to UK national research programs.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the university is a broad research and teaching institution covering disciplines from astronautics to cleanroom manufacturing.

points.name: FLIR Systems, Inc.
points.description: Canadian sensor manufacturer building thermal imaging systems for defense autonomy.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker and defense unmanned systems provider that builds thermal imaging cameras, electro-optical sensors, and reconnaissance drones and ground vehicles for military and industrial customers. It supplies perception hardware that captures environmental data for automated target recognition and on-device inference, alongside complete small unmanned systems for physical world acting. The organization serves defense agencies, automakers, and industrial operators requiring advanced sensing in combat, automotive, and monitoring settings.
1. A sensor maker that builds thermal imaging cameras and electro-optical sensors, and a vehicle maker that builds reconnaissance drones and unmanned ground vehicles for defense applications.
2. Uncooled thermal imaging sensors, CMOS and CCD image sensors, and autonomous unmanned ground and aerial platforms.
3. Thermal perception, target recognition, reconnaissance, remote inspection, and automotive thermal vision development.
4. Sensors and camera modules, complete unmanned ground vehicles and drones, and automotive development kits sold to defense forces and developers.
5. Defense reconnaissance, explosive ordnance disposal, autonomous driving development, industrial monitoring, and agricultural inspection.
6. Militaries, defense agencies, automakers, and industrial operators.
7. Its sensors are integrated into defense autonomy programs and automotive development systems by vehicle makers and government agencies.
8. It is the largest commercial maker of thermal imaging cameras and sensors, deeply embedded in military reconnaissance and combat simulation programs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Acquired by Teledyne, acquired ICx Technologies and Aeryon Labs, supplied an unmanned ground vehicle to RE2 for the ACE program, and collaborated on the Ripsaw M5 project.
Organization type: Subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of sensors, cameras, drones, and unmanned ground vehicles, and defense contracts.
Scale and maturity: A global enterprise and established provider with large defense contracts, including delivery of reconnaissance systems to the French military.
Geography: Based in Richmond, BC, Canada, operating primarily within the United States defense sector and globally.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on thermal imaging, sensor systems, and unmanned defense assets.

points.name: AIUT Group
points.description: Polish industrial integrator deploying automation, robotics, and asset management systems for manufacturing facilities.
points.bullets:
A systems integrator that designs and installs robotics and industrial automation solutions for manufacturers, combining process robotization with asset management software.
1. A systems integrator that builds and installs automation and robotics systems for industrial customers.
2. Industrial engineering and robotics integration paired with enterprise asset management and computerized maintenance management systems.
3. Automation and robotization of industrial processes and management of industrial assets.
4. Integration services and installed automation systems delivered to industrial facilities.
5. Factories and industrial plants.
6. Manufacturers and industrial operators.
7. It buys robots and components from OEMs and installs them as integrated automation systems for industrial customers.
8. It pairs robotics integration with proprietary asset management software for industrial maintenance.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It operates as the parent organization of its automation subsidiary.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Contracts for integration projects and asset management software.
Scale and maturity: One of Europe's largest automation and robotics integrators with over 35 years of engineering expertise.
Geography: Based in Poland and operates internationally.
Beyond physical AI: Its focus extends to enterprise asset management and computerized maintenance management software beyond physical AI integration.

points.name: Walden Robotics
points.description: Cambridge-based startup developing partially humanoid robots for factory work and leasing them as a managed service.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and deploys general-purpose, partially humanoid robots and the embodied AI models that control them for industrial customers. The company integrates physical hardware like actuators and sensors with on-device inference software and physical AI control to perform repetitive, physically demanding tasks in factories and warehouses.
1. A robot maker that designs, builds and sells partially humanoid robots for manufacturing and warehouse work.
2. Wheeled or fixed-base humanoid torsos with arms and sensors, controlled by embodied foundation models trained with generative-AI diffusion policy methods.
3. Machine tending, tool setting, parts kitting, assembly, machinery cleaning and car parts loading.
4. Complete robots it designs, builds, deploys and maintains itself in industrial environments.
5. Factories and warehouses performing manual tasks like machine tending and parts kitting.
6. Global manufacturing corporations, including electronics and automotive manufacturers.
7. Its robots and proprietary foundation models are built and deployed directly into the industrial environments of its manufacturing customers.
8. It uses generative-AI diffusion policy to power large behavior models, enabling robots to learn new physical movements from a few human demonstrations without requiring new code.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Spun out of Toyota Research Institute, it is partnered with and backed by Toyota Motor Corporation, Deviation Capital, Nvidia and Boeing, and has tested robots at Samsung sites.
Organization type: A privately held startup spun out of a corporate research institute.
Business model: Hardware sales and deployment of robotic systems.
Scale and maturity: A well-capitalized startup backed by $300 million in funding, valued at $1.1 billion, that has moved from pilot to production in under two months.
Geography: Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, it deploys robotic systems in North America.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play physical AI company whose entire focus is on building, deploying and maintaining general-purpose robotic systems.

points.name: KIRIA
points.description: South Korean government agency funding robotics development and commercialization initiatives.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and coordinates the national robotics industry, advancing physical AI and robot commercialization through policy, standards, and financing rather than by building hardware. It allocates state funding to research, development, and deployment programs for embodied foundation models, on-device physical AI, and robotics hardware. It serves domestic robotics startups, the research community, and manufacturers developing AI-driven service robots, humanoids, and dexterous manipulation systems.
1. A government agency that funds robotics programs and administers national robotics R&D, standards, and industry support.
2. Government funding mechanisms, policy frameworks, and standards development for embodied foundation models, on-device physical AI, and robotics hardware.
3. Funding for robot distribution, manufacturing process innovation, workforce development, startup activation, and commercialization of embodied AI and physical automation.
4. Grants, matching funds, regulatory sandboxes, and national programs administered to robotics companies and researchers.
5. Service robots, bipedal and quadrupedal systems, dexterous manipulation hardware, and manufacturing automation.
6. Domestic robotics startups, the research community, and manufacturers.
7. It acts as a foundational platform and investor that catalyzes research and provides funding to physical automation companies.
8. It is the centralized state apparatus for a country with high robot density, leveraging domestic deployment to drive global market expansion.
points.profile:
Organization type: A government agency.
Business model: Government funding and state program administration.
Scale and maturity: A well-established state apparatus administering a multi-year national plan from 2023 to 2028 that allocates roughly $630 million.
Geography: Based in and operating entirely within South Korea.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's entire focus is on the strategic advancement, funding, and regulatory facilitation of the national robotics industry.

points.name: Stäubli Robotics
points.description: Swiss industrial robotics division manufacturing 4-axis and 6-axis robotic systems for factory automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells industrial robotic arms, collaborative robots, mobile platforms and automated guided vehicles for factory automation. It provides complete robotic units alongside controllers, teach pendants and programming software for manufacturers. Its systems address Industry 4.0 challenges in automotive, electronics, aerospace, life sciences and food processing.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells industrial robots, cobots, mobile robotics and automated guided vehicles.
2. Four-axis and six-axis robotic arms, collaborative robots with safety features, omnidirectional mobile platforms and associated programming and virtual commissioning software.
3. Pick-and-place, heavy-payload material handling, hygienic production, ESD-sensitive component handling, hairpin electric motor assembly and high-precision positioning.
4. Complete robots and vehicles, controllers, teach pendants, end-of-arm tooling and programming software.
5. Factories, pharmaceutical production, life sciences, food processing and automotive assembly.
6. Manufacturers in the automotive, electronics, aerospace and food and beverage industries.
7. Its robots are deployed directly into factory automation lines by manufacturers.
8. A strong reputation for engineering reliability, service support, safety and consistency distinguishes it from competitors embedding advanced on-device inference capabilities.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Oxipital AI is a preferred partner, and Schunk, VTR and sibling divisions Stäubli Electrical Connectors and Stäubli Fluid Connectors supply grippers, vision-guided feeders, connectors and tool changers.
Organization type: A privately held company operating as a division of a larger industrial conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and mobile platforms plus associated controllers, tooling and software.
Scale and maturity: An established, mature global player with a long-standing presence in the industrial robotics market and a base in Duncan, South Carolina, USA.
Geography: Based in Duncan, South Carolina, USA and operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: Industrial robotics and factory automation represent the organization's entire commercial focus.

points.name: Quanta Computer Inc.
points.description: Taiwanese electronics manufacturer building collaborative robots and edge computing servers for industrial automation.
points.bullets:
A major global electronics manufacturer that designs and deploys AI-enabled collaborative robots, edge servers and private 5G solutions for industrial robotics and factory automation, acting as a robot maker, subsystem integrator and deployed system architect.
1. A robot and subsystem maker that builds AI-enabled collaborative robots, edge servers and private 5G nodes, sold as complete hardware and integrated systems.
2. AI inference technology in robotic control systems, edge computing subsystems, private 5G infrastructure and AI-embedded robotic hardware.
3. Industrial robotics, factory automation, edge AI computing and private 5G networking for deployed systems.
4. Complete robots, edge servers, 5G nodes and integrated deployed systems.
5. Factories, warehouses and industrial automation settings.
6. Industrial robotics operators, manufacturers and factory automation sectors.
7. It builds robots, edge servers and 5G nodes that it integrates into comprehensive deployed systems for industrial operators.
8. Vertical integration combining internally developed AI cobots with edge computing and private 5G infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its robotics subsidiary is backed by the parent company, with partnerships with Ambarella for SoCs and Siemens for digital transformation platforms.
Organization type: A publicly traded global electronics manufacturer and parent company of robotics subsidiaries.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots, edge servers and 5G infrastructure, plus integrated system deployment.
Scale and maturity: A major established global manufacturing heavyweight with extensive financial and research resources conducting operations on a global scale.
Geography: Based in Taoyuan City, Taiwan, with manufacturing and technology deployment operations globally.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it is a premier global electronics manufacturer that produces computing hardware and serves as a major hardware partner for global cloud providers.

points.name: Voyage.auto
points.description: Autonomous vehicle fleet operator deploying driverless taxis and remote assistance technology in retirement communities.
points.bullets:
An autonomous vehicle fleet operator that developed and deployed self-driving taxi services in constrained environments by integrating third-party sensors and autonomy software into retrofitted vehicles for residents of retirement communities.
1. An operator that runs a robotaxi fleet and a systems integrator that retrofits passenger vehicles with autonomous driving hardware and software.
2. A self-driving system built on an autonomous vehicle operating system, lidar sensors, and high-definition maps.
3. Autonomous navigation and driverless ride-hailing in low-speed, highly mapped, and predictable environments.
4. A fleet of autonomous vehicles it operates itself as a ride-hailing service.
5. Robotaxis operating within retirement communities and on private roads.
6. Residents of retirement communities and retirement community operators.
7. It buys passenger vehicles and sensors from OEMs and operates them as a ride service in its own deployments.
8. It achieved early commercial viability by targeting low-speed, geofenced retirement communities rather than attempting to solve complex urban driving.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partners include a provider of autonomous vehicle operating systems, a lidar sensor maker, a high-definition mapping provider, a car rental company, and retirement community operators, with funding from venture capital and automotive corporate venture arms.
Organization type: A privately held startup that was acquired by a subsidiary of a major automotive manufacturer.
Business model: Ride-hailing fees from operating a driverless taxi service.
Scale and maturity: Raised $52 million in total funding and operated daily driverless ride services across multiple retirement communities before its acquisition.
Geography: Based in Palo Alto, California, and operated ride services in San Jose, California, and Central Florida.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation were the entire focus and central mission of the organization.

points.name: Motorola Solutions
points.description: US technology company integrating AI-driven drone systems and voice analytics into public safety command centers.
points.bullets:
A technology and communications company that integrates third-party drone and counter-drone systems into its command center software for public safety and defense, acting as a reseller, integrator and acquirer of physical AI technologies.
1. A systems integrator and communications company that resells third-party drone technology and builds command center software, sold as integrated software platforms and hardware to public safety agencies.
2. Command center software with AI-assisted 911 call keyword identification, mobile ad-hoc networking for autonomous systems, and RF-based counter-drone signal control.
3. Drone dispatch orchestration, AI-assisted emergency dispatch, tactical mesh networking for soldiers and autonomous systems, and detection and control of unauthorized drones.
4. Licensed command center software, smart radios, tactical networking systems, and counter-drone systems, bundled with resold drone-first responder technology.
5. Public safety command centers, emergency response, military communications, and defense counter-drone operations.
6. Public safety agencies, emergency dispatchers, police forces, and militaries.
7. It integrates third-party drone and counter-drone hardware into its own command center software and resells the combined package to public safety operators.
8. It pairs exclusive reseller rights for drone-first responder technology with its own command center software and radio ecosystem to create an end-to-end public safety workflow.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: BRINC, Silvus Technologies, D-Fend Solutions.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Software licenses and subscriptions, hardware sales, and systems integration contracts.
Scale and maturity: A large, established public company executing multi-billion-dollar acquisitions of defense electronics firms.
Geography: Based in the USA and operating primarily in North America.
Beyond physical AI: It provides mission-critical communications, video security, and analytics solutions for public safety and enterprise sectors.

points.name: Israeli Ministry of Defense
points.description: Israeli government agency deploying tactical ground robots and validating autonomous vehicle systems for defense operations.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds, tests and deploys edge and physical AI systems for defense, acquiring autonomous ground vehicles, tactical UGVs and sensor systems for military and security use.
1. A government agency that acquires, deploys and operates autonomous ground vehicles, tactical robots and sensor systems for national defense.
2. Autonomous ground vehicles, tactical unmanned ground vehicles and sensor-based contamination detection systems.
3. Algorithm development and safety validation of autonomous ground vehicles, tactical UGV deployment, and hospital contamination prevention.
4. Autonomous vehicles and robotic systems it operates itself, alongside simulation platforms and sensors acquired from suppliers.
5. Defense, security, ground vehicles, unmanned ground vehicles and hospitals.
6. Defense forces, security agencies and military operators.
7. It buys robots, sensors and simulation platforms from suppliers and operates them in its own defense and security missions.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Cognata, Vayyar and Roboteam.
Organization type: Government agency.
Business model: Government defense budgets and procurement contracts.
Scale and maturity: A national defense ministry with active Tier-1 deployments of tactical UGV systems.
Geography: Based in Israel and operating across Israeli defense and security facilities.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it is responsible for Israel's national defense, military operations and security policy.

points.name: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
points.description: German government agency funding industrial AI research and factory automation projects.
aliases: German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and sets policy for the integration of artificial intelligence and robotics into industrial manufacturing, financing the research, computing infrastructure and applied projects that connect embodied AI to factory automation and predictive maintenance for the German industrial base.
1. A government agency that funds robotics and AI programs through grants and public-private partnerships.
2. Factory automation, predictive maintenance and the translation of production, logistics and engineering data into actionable intelligence for intelligent robotic systems.
3. It funds applied research and ecosystem hubs that develop and deploy robotic systems in physical industrial settings.
4. It champions a human-centered, ethical approach to technology, positioning German embodied artificial intelligence and industrial robotics as a high-trust alternative to U.S. and Chinese market dominance.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It fosters domestic innovation hubs like Cyber Valley and funds projects under the MarTERA initiative alongside robotics companies.
Organization type: A federal government ministry responsible for economic affairs and energy.
Business model: Government funding and public-private partnerships.
Scale and maturity: A long-established governmental body that has committed up to five billion euros to implement its national artificial intelligence strategy by 2025.
Geography: Based in Germany with a strategic focus on European cooperation.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is broadly responsible for shaping national economic, industrial and energy policy to ensure technological sovereignty and sustained competitiveness.

points.name: ONBERG Autonomous Systems
points.description: German joint venture deploying autonomous drone defense systems for physical interception and aerial threat neutralization.
points.bullets:
A joint venture and systems integrator that builds integrated autonomous drone defense systems, combining development, system integration, and industrial-scale manufacturing for critical infrastructure protection.
1. A systems integrator and robotics OEM that designs, manufactures, and operates integrated autonomous counter-drone defense systems for government and security customers.
2. A multi-layered defense architecture that integrates on-device sensing, autonomous decision-making, and engagement into a unified operational framework.
3. Autonomous aerial threat detection, guidance, interception, and intelligence gathering for critical infrastructure protection.
4. Complete integrated defense architectures delivered through development, series production, and system integration services.
5. Defense and security operations protecting national security assets, borders, energy infrastructure, and transportation hubs from aerial threats.
6. Government and defense entities requiring critical infrastructure protection.
7. It integrates counter-drone and autonomous security technologies with precision mechanical engineering to produce complete defense systems.
8. It combines battle-proven autonomous systems with German precision engineering and a localized European supply chain for high-volume production.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A joint venture between Ondas and Heidelberger Druckmaschinen, combining autonomous security technologies with industrial manufacturing capabilities.
Organization type: A joint venture formed as an established industrial enterprise.
Business model: Defense systems integration and manufacturing contracts.
Scale and maturity: An established industrial enterprise positioned for high-volume production with initial deployments in Germany and Ukraine.
Geography: Based in Brandenburg an der Havel, Germany, operating across Germany and Ukraine with plans to expand across European and NATO allied markets.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play entity whose entire focus is dedicated to physical AI, robotics, and autonomous defense systems.

points.name: Ondas Autonomous Systems (OAS)
points.description: Defense technology provider deploying autonomous drones, ground robotics, and counter-drone systems for critical infrastructure security.
points.bullets:
A defense and security robotic platform provider that builds and operates a portfolio of AI-enabled autonomous aerial drones, ground robots, and counter-drone systems for defense, homeland security, and critical infrastructure protection missions.
1. A robotic platform provider that designs and sells complete autonomous drones and ground robotics for defense and security applications.
2. AI-enabled autonomous navigation, on-device computer vision, and orchestration software that transforms sensor data into operational decisions in contested environments.
3. Autonomous aerial data collection, persistent security monitoring, counter-UAS interception, and multi-domain robotic operations without relying on GPS or RF signals.
4. Complete robotic platforms and counter-drone systems deployed directly to end-users.
5. Defense missions, homeland security, public safety, and critical infrastructure protection.
6. Defense forces, homeland security agencies, public safety organizations, and critical infrastructure operators.
7. The organization builds and deploys its own autonomous robotic platforms and systems directly to government and enterprise end-users.
8. It delivers continuous, multi-function autonomous operations in complex and contested environments without relying on GPS or RF jamming.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It operates through American Robotics, Airobotics, Apeiro Motion, Roboteam Ltd., and Sentrycs, and provides technologies to the ONBERG joint venture.
Organization type: A business unit of a publicly traded parent company.
Business model: Hardware and platform sales to government and enterprise customers.
Scale and maturity: A mature-scale business unit with a globally deployed portfolio and international expansion across the Middle East, Europe, and Asia.
Geography: An American-Israeli organization operating globally with expanding operations across the Middle East, Europe, and Asia.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are the entire focus of the organization.

points.name: Ondas Capital
points.description: Investment and advisory platform funding and scaling mature unmanned systems and autonomous physical AI technologies.
points.bullets:
An investment and advisory business unit of a publicly traded parent company that funds and accelerates the deployment of unmanned systems and edge AI for physical-world applications, primarily for Allied defense and security markets. It combines strategic investment management with advisory services to scale mature, combat-proven autonomous technologies, acting as a bridge to transfer battlefield systems into the United States and Europe. The unit focuses on integrating subsystems like tactical edge AI image processing and unmanned vehicles into comprehensive defense architectures.
1. A strategic investor and systems integrator that provides funding and advisory services to scale autonomous technologies, sold as investment capital and integration services.
2. It delivers funding, operational expertise and scaling to transition mature, edge-deployed physical AI and robotic systems into broader defense architectures.
3. Customers get it through investment capital, advisory services and integration services for autonomous technologies.
4. The machines, operations and settings it is used in are unmanned battlefield technologies, tactical edge AI and unmanned vehicles in defense and security markets.
5. The types of customer it sells to are defense, security and dual-use technology markets, and Allied defense customers.
6. It invests in and integrates subsystems from other makers into comprehensive defense architectures for end use.
7. It functions as a specialized accelerator that rapidly localizes and transitions proven, edge-deployed physical AI and robotic systems rather than operating as a traditional defense contractor.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is a business unit of Ondas Holdings Inc. and has made a $14 million strategic investment in an AI landmine detection technology firm.
Organization type: It is a business unit of a publicly traded company.
Business model: It makes money through fund management of a $150 million investment program and advisory services.
Scale and maturity: It manages a $150 million investment program and has demonstrated scaling capability through notable deployments.
Geography: It is based in the United States with an expanding European headquarters, operating with an initial emphasis on Eastern Europe and the Baltic states to facilitate transfers into broader Allied markets.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation represent the entire focus of the organization's investment mission and operational strategy.

points.name: ByteDance Seed
points.description: Chinese research institution developing vision-language-action models and bi-manual robots for complex household tasks.
points.bullets:
A research division of a global technology conglomerate that develops embodied AI foundation models and builds complete bipedal mobile manipulation robots, targeting complex real-world and household physical automation.
1. An AI model developer and robot maker that builds vision-language-action foundation models and complete bi-manual mobile robots.
2. Vision-language-action models using a mixture-of-transformers architecture trained for long-horizon task execution and bi-manual deformable object manipulation, alongside physical robots with sphere wrist designs and multiple cameras.
3. Generalist robot policies with novel object generalization, long-horizon task execution, and bi-manual dexterous manipulation.
4. Generalist robot models capable of running on its own mobile robots and complete physical robotic systems it builds.
5. Household and real-world physical automation requiring complex mobile manipulation.
