It designs automated guided vehicles and autonomous mobile robots for material transport, pallet handling, and piece picking, along with smart cameras and software for warehouse management, parcel tracking, and pallet detection.
1. A robot maker and vision system provider that builds and sells industrial mobile robots and machine vision software for logistics and manufacturing.
2. Vision and laser fusion perception technology, automated guided vehicles, and smart cameras integrated with warehouse management and robot control systems.
3. Autonomous material transport, pallet handling, piece picking, under-vehicle transport, multi-face barcode reading, dynamic parcel measurement, and fleet management for mixed robot fleets.
4. Complete mobile robots, smart camera systems, and licensed warehouse management and robot control software.
5. Warehouses, fulfillment centers, manufacturing facilities, and third-party logistics operations.
6. Logistics operators, manufacturers, and third-party logistics providers.
7. Its robots and vision systems are deployed in intralogistics operations by logistics companies and manufacturers.
8. It leverages the vision technology ecosystem of its parent company to deliver industrial-grade perception and robot systems for complex environments.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: A subsidiary of Hikvision.
Organization type: Privately held subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and smart cameras, and software licenses for warehouse management and robot control.
Scale and maturity: A substantial industrial provider operating within a major global vision technology parent company.
Geography: Based in Hangzhou, China, deploying systems in industrial and logistics environments.
Beyond physical AI: Its focus is entirely on industrial mobile robots, machine vision, and warehouse automation.

points.name: ForwardX
points.description: Chinese robotics company deploying vision-guided autonomous mobile robots and forklifts for warehouse and factory automation.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds vision-navigated autonomous mobile robots and autonomous forklifts for warehouse and factory intralogistics, supplying both the physical machines and the fleet orchestration software to manufacturers and logistics operators.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots and autonomous forklifts, integrating them with its own fleet scheduling software as complete material handling systems.
2. Visual SLAM navigation using cameras and lidar for localization and mapping in dynamic environments, combined with unified cluster scheduling software for multi-robot orchestration.
3. Autonomous mobile robot navigation without floor modifications, assisted piece picking, heavy pallet movement, line-side replenishment, and fleet orchestration.
4. Complete robots and forklifts paired with integrated fleet management software, deployed as turnkey material handling systems.
5. Warehouses, factories, and logistics facilities where humans, vehicles, and robots work together.
6. Manufacturers, logistics operators, supply chain providers, and retailers.
7. It designs and builds its own mobile robots and sells them directly to end users for deployment in their facilities.
8. Pure visual SLAM navigation that requires no physical floor modifications, enabling rapid deployment with a five-to-nine-month return on investment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: JD.com, Chery Automobile, TCL, DHL Supply Chain, SF Supply Chain, and Highline Warren.
Organization type: A privately held robotics company.
Business model: Hardware sales of mobile robots and forklifts combined with software for fleet orchestration, sold as complete automation systems.
Scale and maturity: Over 5,000 autonomous mobile robots deployed across more than 250 facilities on five continents, including a single-site deployment of over 435 AMRs at an automotive factory.
Geography: Based in Beijing and Suzhou, China, with deployments across five continents including North America and the Asia-Pacific region.
Beyond physical AI: Physical automation, mobile robotics, and sensor perception constitute its entire focus and core business activity.

points.name: Hon Hai Technology Group (Foxconn)
points.description: Taiwanese manufacturing giant deploying autonomous mobile robots and swarm robotics systems to optimize production lines.
points.bullets:
A global electronics manufacturer that designs and builds autonomous mobile robots and swarm robot systems for its own production facilities and for other industrial users, operating as a hardware maker and joint-venture partner in robotics.
1. A robot maker that designs and builds autonomous mobile robots and swarm robotics systems, sold as complete robots to industrial users.
2. Autonomous mobile robot systems built on ROS 2 middleware, engineered for swarm robot coordination.
3. Fleet coordination, autonomous navigation and flexible production-line automation.
4. Complete robots and autonomous mobile robot solutions, delivered through a joint venture and used directly in its own factories.
5. Factories and production facilities.
6. Manufacturers and industrial operators, including its own internal production lines.
7. It builds and deploys autonomous mobile robots into its own manufacturing facilities and supplies them to other industrial users through a joint venture.
8. It develops swarm-intelligence robotics through a joint venture to increase the flexibility of its own manufacturing lines, leveraging its vertical integration from robot builder to factory operator.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It formed a joint venture with a robotics company to develop swarm robotics and AMR solutions.
Organization type: A publicly traded manufacturing and technology conglomerate.
Business model: Hardware sales of robots and manufacturing services, with robots deployed for its own operational efficiency.
Scale and maturity: A global manufacturing giant with extensive production facilities and established operations.
Geography: Based in Taiwan and operates manufacturing facilities globally.
Beyond physical AI: A global leader in technology services and electronics manufacturing that also invests in electric vehicles, digital health, semiconductors and next-generation communication technologies.

points.name: FORECR
points.description: Industrial hardware manufacturer building compact computing platforms for on-device AI and real-time computer vision in physical environments.
points.bullets:
A hardware company that builds rugged edge AI computing platforms, carrier boards, and industrial computers using NVIDIA Jetson modules. It supplies the physical computing foundation for on-device inference in defense, aerospace, industrial, and surveillance applications.
1. A hardware manufacturer that designs and sells ruggedized carrier boards and industrial box PCs built around NVIDIA Jetson modules.
2. Industrial-grade and military-grade edge computing hardware integrating NVIDIA Jetson SoMs for high-performance on-device AI processing in harsh environments.
3. On-device AI inference, real-time sensor and image processing, and high-speed data transfer for compute-intensive edge workloads.
4. Carrier boards, ruggedized computers, and industrial box PCs sold as hardware components to integrators and end users.
5. Unmanned aerial vehicles, defense and aerospace ISR missions, industrial automation, retail surveillance, and multi-sensor systems.
6. System integrators, aerospace and defense contractors, surveillance system providers, and industrial automation end users.
7. Its carrier boards and computers are integrated into edge devices and vehicles by system integrators and defense contractors.
8. It specializes in compact, fanless, ruggedized computing platforms that meet military standards while delivering high AI performance in a small, power-efficient footprint.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with NVIDIA for Jetson modules and software frameworks, and with Airbus Defence and Space for UAV-based ISR hardware integration.
Organization type: A privately held hardware company operating in the industrial technology sector.
Business model: Hardware sales of carrier boards and industrial computers, with additional custom design support services.
Scale and maturity: An established enterprise offering off-the-shelf industrial hardware and custom design support.
Geography: It operates globally, with hardware deployed in harsh environmental conditions across field, industrial, and defense settings.
Beyond physical AI: As a pure-play edge AI hardware company, its entire focus is designing and manufacturing computing platforms for on-device inference in physical automation.

points.name: Accelint
points.description: Defense technology platform delivering AI-enabled autonomy and sensor systems for US military operations.
points.bullets:
A defense technology platform and systems integrator that builds and installs AI-enabled autonomy, mission systems, and edge AI runtimes for the United States Department of Defense and allied militaries.
1. A systems integrator and autonomy software developer that builds modular, open-architecture mission autonomy software and edge AI systems for defense platforms.
2. Modular, open-architecture software and edge AI runtimes that connect sensors and perception to autonomous action on physical platforms.
3. Autonomous flight, robotics in contested environments, command and control integration, and tactical edge autonomy.
4. Integration services and licensed autonomy software installed on existing defense platforms.
5. Defense platforms, autonomous testbeds, and contested military operating environments.
6. The United States Department of Defense, every branch of the military, and allied international partners.
7. Its autonomy software and integrated systems are designed into existing defense platforms operated by militaries.
8. Its solutions are engineered by real-world operators to function reliably in degraded conditions and contested environments where standard systems fail.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Lockheed Martin is a core partner on the Army's Next Generation Command and Control program, and the organization operates under the Lyntris parent entity.
Organization type: A privately held, private equity-backed defense technology platform.
Business model: Defense contracts for systems integration, software licenses, and mission systems delivery.
Scale and maturity: The organization manages over 200 active defense programs and has collaborated with the Department of Defense for over 25 years.
Geography: It is based in the United States and focuses operations entirely on domestic defense programs and allied international partners.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the organization's entire focus, serving as its core mission to deliver tactical edge autonomy from national command authorities down to frontline operations.

points.name: DROPLA Tech ApS
points.description: Danish defense startup building autonomous drones and ground robots for on-device explosive threat detection and clearance.
points.bullets:
A robot and drone maker that builds complete unmanned ground vehicles and UAV swarm systems integrated with its own landmine-detection AI for demining operations. It combines remote-controlled ground machines, multi-sensor drone swarms and proprietary neural networks into deployed systems for defense and government demining organizations.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells uncrewed ground vehicles and drone swarms, integrated with proprietary AI detection software as complete systems.
2. Neural networks for landmine detection trained on proprietary datasets of labelled frames, deployed on UAVs equipped with optical, magnetic and electromagnetic sensors alongside remote-controlled ground vehicles built to withstand anti-personnel mine detonations.
3. Landmine and unexploded ordnance detection, ground preparation, vegetation clearing, safe-zone confirmation and aerial survey of up to 0.5 square kilometres per day.
4. Complete drones, uncrewed ground vehicles and sensor platforms sold as integrated deployed systems.
5. Demining operations, battlefields and defense.
6. Government demining organizations, emergency services, transport special services and defense procurement programs.
7. Its machines and AI models are operated directly by government demining and defense organizations in the field.
8. Extensive proprietary datasets and active real-world deployments in high-intensity combat zones reduce demining costs by roughly ninety percent compared to traditional methods.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Odense Robotics StartUp Fund, Danish Technological Institute, Emergency State Service of Ukraine and State Transport Special Service.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware and system sales and government defense contracts.
Scale and maturity: A pre-seed startup with €2.4 million in funding, currently scaling production and testing systems in the field.
Geography: Based in Odense, Denmark, with an operational presence and active deployments in Ukraine.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation represent the entire focus and core mission of the organization.

points.name: Hyster-Yale Materials Handling
points.description: US industrial vehicle manufacturer deploying autonomous forklifts for warehouse operations.
points.bullets:
A vehicle maker that builds and sells autonomous forklifts for materials handling operations. The organization designs complete industrial lift trucks with integrated autonomy, targeting warehouses, factories and distribution centers that need self-driving pallet movement.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that builds and sells autonomous forklifts.
2. Autonomous navigation and pallet-handling systems integrated into industrial forklift trucks.
3. Autonomous pallet movement, lift-truck navigation and materials handling within warehouses and distribution centers.
4. Complete autonomous forklift vehicles sold to industrial operations.
5. Warehouses, factories and distribution centers.
6. Logistics operators, manufacturers and industrial facilities.
7. Its autonomous forklifts are deployed directly by warehouse and factory operators as self-driving materials-handling equipment.
8. It brings autonomy to established industrial forklift designs used in heavy materials handling rather than building mobile robots from scratch.
points.profile:
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Vehicle and equipment sales.
Scale and maturity: A major established player in the autonomous forklift market.
Geography: Based in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond autonomous forklifts, the broader business manufactures conventional materials-handling equipment and lift trucks.

points.name: Mitsubishi Logisnext Co., Ltd.
points.description: French factory automation company deploying autonomous forklifts and automated guided vehicles for warehouse material handling.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and systems integrator that develops autonomous material handling equipment and integrated software for warehouse and factory intralogistics. The organization builds physical vehicles equipped with advanced sensors, machine vision, and AI-driven navigation, delivering complete warehouse automation platforms to end operators. It serves manufacturing, retail, and distribution sectors seeking scalable automation solutions.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells autonomous forklifts and material handling vehicles, sold as complete hardware platforms with integrated software.
2. The core technology combines AI-driven navigation, machine vision, and sensor fusion integrated directly into physical material handling vehicles.
3. The organization delivers autonomous navigation, material handling, and fleet orchestration for decarbonized intralogistics operations.
4. Customers receive complete automated guided vehicles and integrated software systems with installation services.
5. The machines are used in warehouses, factories, and distribution centers for intralogistics and material handling.
6. The organization sells to manufacturing, retail, and distribution operators seeking warehouse automation.
7. The organization builds complete robotic vehicles and integrates them directly into end-customer warehouse operations.
8. The organization differentiates through a mixed-fleet philosophy allowing customers to blend automated and manual operations, scaling automation incrementally without requiring fixed infrastructure.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization collaborates with Jungheinrich to advance intelligent intralogistics solutions.
Organization type: The organization is a major global corporation operating within a larger heavy industries conglomerate.
Business model: The organization makes money through hardware sales of material handling equipment and integrated automation systems.
Scale and maturity: The organization is an established, large-scale global enterprise competing directly with other major international material handling corporations.
Geography: The organization is based in Japan and maintains a strong global presence, including advanced integration services across North America.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's broader profile encompasses general logistics and materials handling equipment, with increasing focus on decarbonized physical logistics and data-driven automation solutions.

points.name: Jaguar Land Rover
points.description: UK automaker integrating Nvidia Drive tools to enhance autonomous driving capabilities.
points.bullets:
An automaker integrating advanced driver-assist features and autonomous driving capabilities into its vehicles, using external computing platforms and developing high-frequency radar systems for urban perception.
1. An automaker that designs and sells passenger vehicles with integrated advanced driver-assist and autonomous driving systems.
2. AI-based lane management, collision avoidance, high-frequency radar systems, and autonomous driving stacks built on external compute platforms.
3. Enhanced vehicle perception in urban environments, lane management and collision avoidance.
4. Complete vehicles with integrated advanced driver-assist features and autonomous driving systems.
5. Passenger vehicles operating in urban environments.
6. Consumers purchasing passenger vehicles.
7. It buys autonomous driving and compute platforms from technology suppliers and integrates them into its own vehicles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Nvidia, InMotion Ventures and Voyage Auto.
Organization type: Privately held automotive manufacturer.
Business model: Vehicle sales.
Scale and maturity: A UK-based automaker with a global customer base.
Geography: Based in the UK and sells vehicles globally.
Beyond physical AI: It is a traditional automotive manufacturer whose physical AI focus is strictly limited to integrating advanced driver-assist and autonomous driving capabilities into its passenger vehicles.

points.name: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD)
points.description: US technology company designing high-performance GPUs and software for edge AI inference and robotics.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs high-performance GPUs and software ecosystems for onboard and server-side inference and simulation in edge and physical AI, and acquires silicon photonics startups to advance co-packaged optics.
1. A chip company that designs GPUs and accelerators for inference and simulation.
2. Its core technology consists of high-performance graphics processing units and a software ecosystem for training and inference workloads, augmented by silicon photonics and photonic integrated circuits.
3. It delivers onboard and server-side inference for physical AI systems alongside simulation and training compute for robotics cloud back-ends.
4. Customers get it as chips and accelerators, plus software ecosystems for machine learning workloads.
5. Its hardware and software are used in robotics cloud back-ends and physical AI inference systems.
6. It sells to robot makers, autonomy software developers and robotics engineers.
7. Its chips are designed into edge devices and server infrastructure used by physical AI developers and device makers.
8. Its acquisition of silicon photonics startups to advance co-packaged optics distinguishes its approach to high-bandwidth AI compute.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with semiconductor foundries for chip manufacturing.
Organization type: It is a publicly traded company.
Business model: It makes money through chip and accelerator sales alongside software ecosystem development.
Scale and maturity: It is a major, established semiconductor company.
Geography: It is based in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, it is a major semiconductor company supplying high-performance compute across data centers, personal computers and gaming.

points.name: Sony Semiconductor
points.description: Japanese semiconductor company developing image sensors with embedded AI for edge computing applications.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops image sensors with embedded AI for on-device inference in edge and physical AI systems. The company builds semiconductor technology for AI and edge computing and participates in joint ventures that apply this sensing technology to physical-world domains. It supplies these AI-integrated sensors to device makers and industrial enterprises through its semiconductor business.
1. A sensor maker that builds image sensors with embedded AI processing.
2. CMOS image sensors with integrated neural processing circuits for on-device inference directly on the imaging silicon.
3. On-device image inference, visual perception and edge AI processing at the sensor level.
4. Image sensors and semiconductor components sold to device manufacturers.
5. Edge computing devices and physical-world sensing systems.
6. Device makers and industrial joint-venture partners.
7. Its image sensors are designed into edge devices and physical AI systems by device manufacturers.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Partner in the EarthBrain joint-venture.
Organization type: A subsidiary of a publicly traded company.
Geography: Based in Japan and operates as a global semiconductor supplier.
Beyond physical AI: A semiconductor business whose focus extends beyond physical AI to consumer electronics, imaging and sensor technologies.

points.name: Hirebotics
points.description: US robotics company deploying no-code cobots for metal fabrication tasks.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds collaborative robot systems for metal fabrication, integrating third-party robotic arms with its own no-code software platform to provide ready-to-run welding, cutting, and painting automation for manufacturers.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete collaborative robot cells built on third-party hardware and proprietary software.
2. A no-code software platform with click-and-teach hand-guiding for robot programming, augmented by AI algorithms that recommend welding and cutting parameters.
3. No-code robot programming, automated welding and cutting parameter recommendation, and stationary painting.
4. Complete robotic systems sold outright or leased as robots-as-a-service with optional support packages.
5. Metal fabrication shops, agricultural manufacturing, automotive manufacturing, and high-mix low-volume factories.
6. Fabricators, welders, and industrial manufacturers of all sizes.
7. It integrates third-party robotic arms and power supplies with its own software to sell complete cells directly to end users.
8. A no-code platform that lets shop-floor operators program robots via smartphones and tablets without specialized expertise.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Its systems are built on robotic arms from FANUC and Universal Robots, using power sources from Miller, ESAB, and Hypertherm.
Organization type: A privately held company.
Business model: Robot-as-a-service rent-to-own programs, complete robotic system sales, and subscription support packages.
Scale and maturity: A privately held company founded in 2015 serving the North American industrial market.
Geography: The organization is based in Nashville, Tennessee, USA and focuses its deployments within the North American industrial manufacturing market.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play enterprise entirely focused on physical automation and edge AI solutions for metal fabrication.

points.name: Genrobot
points.description: Technology company providing large-scale, multi-modal data and automated platforms to train physical robots.
points.bullets:
An embodied intelligence data solutions provider that processes multi-modal data into training sets for robot models, selling data services and a governance platform to AI and robotics developers.
1. A developer tools company whose data processing platform robotics and AI engineers use to build training datasets.
2. An automated data governance platform that converts massive collected physical-world data into high-quality training sets for embodied intelligence.
3. High-volume, multi-modal data processing, dataset curation and shortened model iteration cycles.
4. A data services offering and a software platform delivered to customers building robot models.
5. Embodied intelligence, robot intelligence and physical-world AI training.
6. Robotics and AI developers building embodied intelligence models.
7. It supplies the processed training data and data tools that AI model developers use to build robot foundation models.
8. It focuses on scaling human-skill data collection and automating the conversion of physical-world data into model-ready training sets in days rather than months.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Data services and platform subscriptions.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Génération Robots
points.description: European robot distributor supplying collaborative and humanoid robots while providing software development and integration services.
points.bullets:
A distributor and systems integrator that supplies collaborative and humanoid robots to European manufacturers and small businesses, with an in-house team that handles research and integration to deploy the machines for end users.
1. A distributor and systems integrator that sources collaborative and humanoid robots from robot makers and installs them for manufacturers and small businesses.
2. Collaborative robotic arms and humanoid robots built by other manufacturers, integrated into customer environments by an internal engineering team.
3. Sourcing, integration, and deployment of collaborative robots and humanoids for industrial and research applications.
4. Complete robots and integration services.
5. Factories, manufacturing lines, and research environments.
6. Manufacturers, small and medium-sized enterprises, and research organizations.
7. It buys complete robots from original equipment manufacturers and integrates them into production lines for end customers.
8. It combines regional distribution with an internal engineering team that performs hands-on research and integration for end users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Rethink Robotics and the HERA consortium.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales and integration services.
Scale and maturity: A European distributor with operations across France and Germany.
Geography: Based in Europe, operating in France and Germany.
Beyond physical AI: The organization's work extends to humanoid robot software development alongside its distribution and integration activities.

points.name: VSORA
points.description: French startup designing high-performance chips for fast and low-power on-device AI inference in autonomous vehicles and generative AI.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs silicon intellectual property and high-performance inference chips for on-device artificial intelligence, supplying accelerators and compilation platforms to systems integrators and original equipment manufacturers for autonomous vehicles and edge generative AI workloads.
1. A chip company that designs AI inference accelerators and digital signal processors, sold as licensed silicon IP and semiconductor chips.
2. Multicore digital signal processors and deep learning accelerators built on a patented architecture that collapses hierarchical memory into a tightly coupled memory accessed in a single clock cycle to achieve high processor utilization.
3. High-throughput, low-latency, low-power on-device inference for large language models, generative AI, and massive sensor data processing.
4. Licensed silicon intellectual property and semiconductor chips.
5. Autonomous vehicles, ADAS, and edge generative AI deployments.
6. Systems integrators and original equipment manufacturers in the automotive and AI sectors.
7. Its chips and IP are designed into edge AI systems and autonomous machines by device makers.
8. A patented memory architecture that eliminates memory bottlenecks by collapsing hierarchical memory into a single-clock-cycle tightly coupled memory, achieving up to 80% processor utilization.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Funded by venture capital firm Otium and supported by a grant from the European Innovation Council.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Silicon IP licensing and semiconductor chip sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2015, the company has raised $46 million in venture funding and secured a $13.2 million European Innovation Council grant.
Geography: Based in Meudon-La-Forêt, France.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play semiconductor provider whose entire focus is on designing algorithm-agnostic silicon for complex artificial intelligence applications.

points.name: HyperAccel
points.description: Hardware startup developing chips for generative AI inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that develops generative AI inference solutions, building hardware accelerators for on-device and edge AI inference. It targets device makers and developers needing to run large language models and other generative workloads locally on edge hardware.
1. A chip company that designs AI inference accelerators for edge and on-device generative AI.
2. Large language model inference acceleration hardware designed for low-power edge deployment.
3. On-device generative AI inference and local execution of large language models at the edge.
4. Chips and hardware solutions sold to device manufacturers and developers.
5. Edge computing devices, consumer electronics, and on-device generative AI applications.
6. Device manufacturers, hardware developers, and systems integrators building edge AI products.
7. Its chips are designed into edge devices and hardware platforms by device makers.
8. It focuses specifically on optimizing generative AI inference for edge deployment rather than general-purpose edge AI workloads.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Chip sales and hardware licensing.
Scale and maturity: An early-stage company that has raised $40 million in funding.
Geography: An Asian company.
Beyond physical AI: Generative AI inference acceleration is its entire focus.

points.name: Samsung Securities
points.description: Investment firm funding AI chip startups through major Series D rounds.
points.bullets:
An investment firm that led a funding round for a company designing inference chips for on-device AI.
1. A venture capital firm that invests in edge and physical AI companies.
points.profile:
Organization type: An investment firm.
Business model: Capital investment in edge and physical AI silicon developers.
Scale and maturity: Led a $693 million Series D funding round.
Beyond physical AI: An investment firm whose broader activities extend beyond edge and physical AI.

points.name: Recogni
points.description: Vision processing startup designing chips for AI-powered autonomous driving perception.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs power-efficient inference accelerators for edge perception sensors, building silicon that processes camera, radar, and lidar data at the edge for automotive and autonomous machine makers.
1. A chip company that designs inference accelerators for on-device sensor processing.
2. The company develops neural processing units that perform vision-based distance estimation using camera footage alone.
3. The chips deliver low-power on-device inference and camera-based 3D perception out to 300 meters.
4. Customers get the technology as semiconductor chips.
5. The silicon is used in autonomous vehicles and edge sensors.
6. The company sells to automakers and autonomous machine makers.
7. Its chips are designed into perception sensors and autonomous machines by device makers.
8. The silicon performs camera-only distance estimation without requiring direct depth sensors.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is backed by investors providing $102 million in Series C funding.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup.
Business model: The company makes money through chip sales.
Scale and maturity: The company is a Series C-stage startup that has raised $102 million.
Geography: The company operates globally within the edge sensor and autonomous vehicle markets.
Beyond physical AI: The company focuses entirely on edge and physical AI silicon.

points.name: Blumind
points.description: Canadian fabless semiconductor startup designing ultra-low-power analog chips for on-device audio and vision inference at the edge.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs ultra-low-power analog AI inference chips for on-device processing of physical signals like sound and vision at the edge. It develops semiconductors, software, and system solutions for always-on applications, preparing to ship first-generation silicon to lead customers.
1. A chip company that designs analog AI inference semiconductors for on-device edge processing.
2. Analog neural processing technology that stores values in single transistors and runs entire neural networks natively to achieve lower power consumption and latency than digital processors.
3. Always-on, low-latency on-device inference for processing physical information like sound and vision.
4. Chips and modules, offered in compact chip-scale and quad-flat no-leads packages, as well as evaluation boards.
5. Robotics, smart mobility, medical devices, wearables, and industrial systems.
6. Device makers and electronics manufacturers across robotics, mobility, medical, wearable, and industrial sectors.
7. Its chips are designed into edge devices and physical AI systems by device makers.
8. A patented all-analog architecture runs entire neural networks natively and independently, claiming up to 1000x lower power consumption than digital alternatives.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It is backed by investors including Cycle Capital, BDC Capital, Fusion Fund, Real Ventures, and Two Small Fish Ventures, and relies on GlobalFoundries as its foundry partner.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Chip sales and hardware sales.
Scale and maturity: A startup founded in 2020 that has raised $14.1 million in Series A funding and is preparing to deliver first-generation silicon.
Geography: Based in Ottawa, Canada, leveraging a global supply chain with fabrication and packaging partners.
Beyond physical AI: Developing specialized analog AI inference hardware is the organization's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Bowles Farming Company
points.description: California family farm deploying autonomous robotic weeders in cotton fields.
points.bullets:
A farm operator that runs autonomous weed control robots in its own cotton fields to evaluate robotic crews for agricultural operations.
1. An agricultural operator that runs autonomous weeding robots it has partnered with a robot maker to deploy in its own fields.
2. It operates robotic weed control crews supplied by a robot maker under a strategic partnership.
3. Pima cotton fields and agricultural row-crop weeding.
4. It is an end-user farm rather than a vendor, acting as an operator and evaluation partner for robotics technology.
5. It buys or partners to deploy robots from a maker and runs them in its own farming operations.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partners with Aigen for autonomous weed control robots.
Organization type: A privately held family farm.
Business model: It generates revenue through crop production and farming operations.
Scale and maturity: A sixth-generation family farm operating in California's Central Valley.
Geography: Based and operating in California's Central Valley, USA.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond physical AI, it is a traditional row-crop farming enterprise producing Pima cotton and other crops.

points.name: Gravis
points.description: Robotics company retrofitting heavy construction machinery with sensors and on-device inference for autonomous earthmoving.
points.bullets:
A robotics systems integrator and platform provider that retrofits legacy construction and earthmoving machinery with autonomous control systems, sensors and tablet interfaces. It upgrades existing heavy equipment into robotic machines that a single operator can supervise, and is also developing its own autonomous excavator. Its customers are commercial construction, earthmoving and industrial machinery companies.
1. A systems integrator and platform provider that builds autonomous control retrofit kits for construction machines, sold as installed upgrades to existing heavy equipment, and is developing a complete autonomous excavator.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software, on-device inference, lidar, 3D models and tablet-based control interfaces integrated with legacy heavy equipment actuators.
3. Autonomous excavation, trench digging, single-operator multi-machine supervision and job site safety enhancement.
4. Retrofit kits installed on existing construction machines and complete autonomous excavators.
5. Construction sites, earthmoving and trenching.
6. Commercial construction, earthmoving and industrial machinery professionals.
7. It integrates its retrofit systems onto legacy construction equipment already owned by operators and builds its own autonomous excavator.
8. Upgrading existing heavy machinery into autonomous robots so one operator can supervise multiple excavators through a game-like tablet interface.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Taylor Woodrow.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of retrofit kits and autonomous excavators.
Scale and maturity: An emerging startup developing an autonomous excavator for commercial testing in 2026 with trials at Manchester Airport.
Geography: Based in Europe and expanding into North America.
Beyond physical AI: A pure-play enterprise whose entire focus is on physical automation and robotics.

points.name: Superb AI, Inc.
points.description: South Korean AI company providing computer vision, synthetic data, and MLOps platforms for autonomous robots and industrial automation.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides a data and MLOps platform for building and deploying computer vision models used by autonomous robots and industrial automation systems.
1. A developer tools company whose data annotation and MLOps platform robotics and automation engineers use to build and deploy vision models.
2. A platform for computer vision model development that includes synthetic data generation and machine learning operations tooling.
