points.description: UK startup building vision-guided robotic systems that automate the sorting of recyclable materials on conveyor belts.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells AI-powered, vision-guided robotic sorting systems for automating the picking of dry mixed recyclables on conveyor belts in waste management facilities.
1. A robot maker that builds complete vision-guided picking robots and integrated sorting systems, sold as modular hardware units paired with proprietary software.
2. Two-arm robotic systems equipped with high-efficiency grippers, controlled by a proprietary computer vision system and machine learning algorithms that identify and outline target recyclable objects on moving conveyor belts.
3. Automated piece picking, contaminant removal, and object identification for sorting dry mixed recyclable materials at high speed and precision.
4. Complete robotic systems and computer imaging hardware designed as modular, plug-and-play units that retrofit into existing manual waste sorting facilities.
5. Waste sorting and recycling facilities, specifically dry mixed recyclable processing lines on conveyor belts.
6. Waste management operators, local governments, and large recycling companies seeking to automate existing manual sorting facilities.
7. It designs and manufactures its own robotic sorting hardware and software, selling and deploying the complete integrated systems directly into existing recycling facilities.
8. It builds retrofittable, plug-and-play systems that install in under one meter of conveyor space and reduce contamination rates from 50 percent to below 1 percent with a two-year return on investment.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Trialing systems with Glasgow City Council Recycling Centre, selected for the Google DeepMind Accelerator: Robotics program, developing software with EPCC, and funded by Sustainable Ventures and Old College Capital.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of durable physical robots paired with hardware-licensed AI software models.
Scale and maturity: A startup with 10 employees that has transitioned from technology development to commercial deployment, currently running trials in live industrial facilities.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and operating within the British waste management sector.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on developing specialized physical AI technology for the climate technology and circular economy sectors, with no business activities beyond edge AI and physical automation.

points.name: ROBEAUTE
points.description: French medical robotics startup developing tiny self-navigating microrobots for brain surgery and targeted drug delivery.
points.bullets:
A medical robot maker that builds microrobots for navigating brain tissue to diagnose and treat neuropathology, integrating on-device machine learning models for autonomous navigation with micro-scale mechanical components. The company serves neurosurgeons and the medical technology sector with a complete robotic tool platform for intracerebral applications.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells therapeutic microrobots for intracerebral medical applications.
2. Self-propelled microrobots with micro-scale propellers, modular sensors, and on-device machine learning models for autonomous navigation through brain tissue.
3. Autonomous navigation through dense brain tissue, multi-site access from a single entry point, and intracerebral diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring.
4. Complete robotic platforms with integrated navigation software for medical professionals.
5. Hospitals and neurosurgical settings for brain biopsies and neuropathology treatment.
6. Neurosurgeons and medical technology providers.
7. Its microrobots are operated by neurosurgeons in clinical settings for intracerebral procedures.
8. A proprietary navigation software and mechanical design enables multi-site brain access from a single entry point without damaging surrounding neurons.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Google DeepMind selected the company for its Robotics Accelerator program, Plural led its funding round, and it maintains a partnership with a Munich-based surgical software company.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware and integrated platform sales to medical professionals and institutions.
Scale and maturity: A company that has raised $28 million in Series A funding, is in the animal-testing phase, and is preparing for human clinical trials in 2026.
Geography: Based in France and expanding operations into the United States to pursue FDA approval.
Beyond physical AI: Developing medical microrobots for intracerebral applications is the company's entire focus and sole business activity.

points.name: Touchlab
points.description: British startup building ultra-thin tactile e-skin sensors that give robots a human-like sense of touch.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that builds electronic skin using nano inks to give robots a high-resolution sense of touch, operating at the component level within the physical AI stack to supply tactile interfaces for machine makers and healthcare operators.
1. A sensor maker that builds tactile e-skin sensors and a teleoperated robot equipped with its own sensors.
2. Ultra-thin electronic skin composed of force sensors utilizing nano inks, with a flagship technology capable of detecting the full 3D force vector, including normal pressure and shear forces, with high accuracy and dynamic range.
3. High-resolution tactile sensing, slip detection, object identification through touch, and the transfer of a sense of touch from a robotic hand to human operators.
4. Tactile sensor components and a complete teleoperated robot.
5. Robotic hands, teleoperated systems, hospitals, and extreme physical environments involving acid exposure, extreme temperatures, or radioactive conditions.
6. Robot makers, healthcare operators, and industries requiring operation in extreme physical environments.
7. Its tactile sensor components are designed into robotic systems by device makers and used in its own teleoperated robots.
8. It solves the complex challenge of measuring both normal pressure and shear forces with high accuracy and dynamic range, a capability often cited as the holy grail of electronic skin.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Google DeepMind, Octopus Ventures, the National Robotarium, and Laakso Hospital.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Sensor component sales and teleoperated robot sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2018, it raised $4.8 million in seed funding in 2022 and is actively undergoing pilot deployment.
Geography: Based in Edinburgh, Scotland, with pilot deployment in Helsinki, Finland.
Beyond physical AI: Developing durable, high-resolution tactile sensors for teleoperated systems and physical AI constitutes the organization's entire business focus and core operational activity.

points.name: Peer Robotics
points.description: US startup deploying collaborative mobile robots that learn industrial tasks directly from human demonstration.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots for manufacturing and warehouse environments, offering fleets that learn tasks by human demonstration.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous mobile robots for tote and pallet handling.
2. The robots use computer vision and force feedback combined with haptic sensing to learn tasks directly through human demonstration.
3. The robots deliver autonomous navigation, tote and pallet movement, and learning-by-demonstration task acquisition.
4. Customers get complete mobile robots and robotic fleets through a network of distributors and integrators.
5. The robots are used in manufacturing and warehouse environments.
6. The company sells to manufacturing and warehouse operators through distributors and integrators.
7. Its complete mobile robots are sold through distributors and integrators into industrial facilities.
8. The approach distinguishes itself by enabling autonomous mobile robots to learn tasks directly through human demonstration, bridging rigid classical automation and flexible learning-based autonomy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company participated in an interoperability demonstration with a fleet management platform and uses a sales acceleration platform, with funding led by a venture capital firm.
Organization type: The organization is a privately held startup operating within the industrial robotics sector.
Business model: The company makes money through hardware sales of its robotic fleets.
Scale and maturity: The company was spun out of a Yale-MIT collaboration in 2019, has raised $2.3m in seed funding, and is focused on scaling commercial deployment.
Geography: The company is based in the USA and operates across manufacturing and warehouse target markets.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play industrial automation provider whose entire business revolves around developing robotic solutions.

points.name: Oxipital AI
points.description: Boston technology company deploying visual AI for machine-vision-guided robotic picking and inspection.
points.bullets:
A visual AI and robotic picking provider that develops 3D machine vision and edge-deployed neural networks for product inspection and pick-and-place robotics in manufacturing.
1. An AI and vision technology company that builds end-to-end visual AI solutions and robotic picking systems for industrial automation.
2. 3D machine vision and edge-deployed neural networks optimized for high-speed product inspection and robotic picking.
3. Visual AI-guided inspection and robotic pick-and-place capabilities for manufacturing environments.
4. End-to-end AI vision solutions sold to manufacturing industries.
5. Robotic process automation, product inspection, and pick-and-place robotics in food processing, agriculture, and consumer goods production.
6. Fortune 500 manufacturing companies and industrial automation users.
7. Its visual AI solutions and picking systems are integrated directly into manufacturing production lines by consumer goods and food processors.
8. It combines soft robotic grippers with 3D machine vision to solve high-speed picking and inspection in food processing and agriculture.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: ABB is an investor and Stäubli Robotics is a preferred integration partner.
Organization type: A privately held technology company and the reformed entity of Soft Robotics Inc.
Business model: Sales of end-to-end visual AI solutions and robotic picking systems.
Scale and maturity: A funded company that has raised $86 million and counts Fortune 500 customers among its deployments.
Geography: Based in Boston, Massachusetts, United States, serving manufacturing industries.
Beyond physical AI: The company focuses entirely on visual AI technology, machine vision, and robotic picking solutions for industrial automation.

points.name: Jacobi Robotics
points.location: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
points.description: Startup building AI software for rapid robot programming and on-device motion planning in industrial automation.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds AI-driven motion planning and programming software for industrial robots, supplying a hardware-agnostic platform to system integrators and manufacturers to reduce deployment time for physical manipulation tasks.
1. A developer tools company that builds AI-powered motion planning and programming software for industrial robots, sold as licensed software or a platform.
2. AI-based motion planning algorithms and on-device inference software that abstracts simulation processes to control robotic joints and end-of-arm tooling while avoiding singularities.
3. Robot motion planning, programming time reduction, and streamlined configuration for physical manipulation tasks like palletizing, welding, and pick-and-place operations.
4. Hardware-agnostic orchestration software and platforms licensed to system integrators and manufacturing businesses.
5. Industrial robotic cells in factories and supply chain operations.
6. System integrators and manufacturing businesses.
7. Its software platform is integrated by system integrators and manufacturers into various industrial robots and peripherals.
8. It uses proprietary AI to reduce traditional engineering setup and simulation time by up to ninety-five percent, enabling new robotic cell configurations in under a single day.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Microsoft's M12 and Moxxie Ventures are investors, and it has a strategic partnership with Formic to integrate its software with robotics-as-a-service offerings.
Organization type: A privately held startup company.
Business model: Software licenses and platform subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2022, it is in its early growth stage and recently secured a five million dollar seed funding round.
Geography: Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA, it initially targets American manufacturers.
Beyond physical AI: Advanced robotics and factory automation represent the entirety of the organization's business focus.

points.name: Tetsuwan Scientific
points.description: Biotech company automating biology labs to run genetic tests tracking local pollution.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and autonomy software company whose laboratory orchestration platform runs automated biology workflows using robotic hardware.
1. A developer tools company that builds laboratory orchestration software for automated biology workflows.
2. Software that integrates mobile hardware systems to coordinate and sequence qPCR laboratory processes.
3. Workflow orchestration and task automation for environmental sample profiling.
4. Licensed software platform.
5. Automated biology laboratories and environmental monitoring stations.
6. Biotechnology research organizations and environmental monitoring programs.
7. Its orchestration software is used by laboratories to direct robotic hardware in executing biological assays.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held biotechnology company.
Geography: Based and operates in California.

points.name: Automata
points.description: Lab automation company building modular robotic workcells that integrate with software to orchestrate biological research workflows.
points.bullets:
A lab automation company and systems integrator that builds modular robotic workcells and orchestration software for biological research workflows, integrating third-party lab instruments with on-device physical automation for life sciences customers.
1. A systems integrator and platform provider that builds modular robotic lab benches and orchestration software for life sciences researchers.
2. Modular dual-access lab benches with robotic handling and transport modules are orchestrated by node-based design software and a Python SDK that integrates third-party instruments and AI agents.
3. Workcell orchestration, sample handling, instrument management, laboratory workflow automation, and intelligent instrument error handling.
4. Integrated physical workcells, lab instruments, transport modules, orchestration software, Python SDKs, and no-code design interfaces installed for laboratory customers.
5. Pharmaceutical and biotech laboratories, automated wet labs, and life sciences research workflows.
6. Life sciences researchers, pharmaceutical companies, and biotech laboratories.
7. Its workcells and software are installed in laboratories, integrating third-party instruments and AI models into connected physical automation for researchers.
8. A modular physical workcell design supports hundreds of thousands of configurable setups orchestrated by AI agents using standardized protocols.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: CellVoyant, Molecular Devices, Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, and Danaher Ventures.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales, software platform sales, and integration services.
Scale and maturity: A Series C company that announced a USD 45 million round in January 2026.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom.
Beyond physical AI: It is a pure-play provider entirely focused on laboratory automation, advancing its platform to support fully autonomous, lights-off laboratories.

points.name: Gatik.ai
points.description: Canadian company developing autonomous trucking systems for middle-mile logistics.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds a self-driving system for autonomous trucks and licenses it to commercial fleet operators and vehicle makers.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving truck stack to automakers and logistics operators.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software for autonomous urban driving and middle-mile logistics.
3. Autonomous navigation for box trucks operating on fixed, repetitive urban routes.
4. Licensed software or autonomy stacks integrated into partner vehicles.
5. Autonomous trucks and commercial logistics fleets.
6. Commercial fleet operators and automakers.
7. Its autonomy stack is integrated into trucks supplied by vehicle maker partners and operated by logistics customers.
8. It focuses on middle-mile logistics on fixed, repetitive routes rather than long-haul or passenger autonomy.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Isuzu and a named venture capital portfolio.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions and per-vehicle royalties.
Scale and maturity: A startup that launched operations in 2021.
Geography: Based in Canada and Silicon Valley, operating in Arkansas.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on autonomous driving software.

points.name: Crewline
points.description: San Francisco startup deploying autonomous retrofit kits that transform existing heavy construction machinery into self-operating units.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds autonomous retrofit kits for existing construction machinery, targeting labor shortages in soil compaction and grading workflows for excavation and road construction contractors. The company combines onboard computers, sensors, and actuators into reversible systems installed on standard equipment, operating under a robot-as-a-service model that includes 24/7 monitoring and remote operator oversight.
1. An autonomy software developer that builds autonomous retrofit kits and licenses them to contractors as a full-service automation offering.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software integrated with onboard computers, safety systems, and physical actuators that enable existing heavy machinery to drive and operate autonomously.
3. Autonomous operation for soil compaction, remote operator oversight of multiple machines, and 24/7 monitoring and support.
4. Autonomous retrofit kits installed on existing equipment within about an hour without permanent modifications, paired with field service, spare parts, and remote operations support.
5. Active construction job sites, road construction, soil compaction, excavation, and grading.
6. Excavation and grading contractors, construction firms, and equipment services companies facing labor shortages.
7. It retrofits and operates autonomy systems on heavy machinery owned by construction contractors, providing full-service support throughout deployment.
8. Its kit can be installed on existing rollers in about an hour without permanent modifications, avoiding the high costs and delays of building new robotic hardware from scratch.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Watts Services and DSS partner to test and deploy the automation solution on active construction sites.
Organization type: A privately held startup backed by venture capital funding.
Business model: Robots-as-a-service offering single-task jobs by machine, with revenue from full-service automation contracts that include monitoring, remote operations, and field support.
Scale and maturity: A recently founded company that has raised $7.1 million in seed funding and built a pipeline of over 200 potential customers.
Geography: Based in San Francisco, California, it operates deployments on active construction job sites to gather real-world data and refine its systems.
Beyond physical AI: Developing physical automation for the construction sector is the organization's entire focus and central mission.

points.name: Textron Inc.
points.description: US aerospace and defense contractor developing autonomous aircraft and unmanned systems for military and commercial markets.
points.bullets:
A diversified aerospace and defense company that builds unmanned aircraft systems and autonomous ground vehicle chassis for military and commercial customers. It leverages multi-industry businesses to produce platforms for the autonomous aircraft and defense vehicle markets, including supplying chassis integrated into autonomous ground platforms.
1. A defense contractor and aerospace company that builds unmanned aircraft systems and autonomous vehicle chassis for military customers.
2. Autonomous aircraft platforms, military unmanned aerial systems, and chassis systems for heavy autonomous ground vehicles.
3. Autonomous flight, military unmanned aerial operations, and ground vehicle chassis mobility for heavy autonomous platforms.
4. Complete aircraft, unmanned aerial systems, and vehicle chassis supplied as defense hardware.
5. Military unmanned aircraft, commercial autonomous aircraft initiatives, and defense autonomous ground vehicles.
6. Militaries, defense agencies, and defense platform integrators.
7. Its aircraft and chassis are built into defense systems and unmanned platforms operated by military forces.
8. It applies multi-industry aerospace and defense manufacturing across both autonomous aircraft and ground vehicle chassis.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Howe & Howe, Bell, Carnegie Robotics, and Textron Systems.
Organization type: Publicly traded company.
Business model: Defense and aerospace hardware sales and contracts.
Scale and maturity: A large, established global multi-industry corporation operating across aerospace, defense, industrial, and finance sectors.
Geography: Based in the USA, operating globally.
Beyond physical AI: It builds general aviation aircraft, rotorcraft, industrial products, and finance services.

points.name: MightyFly
points.description: US startup building autonomous cargo aircraft for middle-mile logistics and defense resupply.
points.bullets:
An autonomous aircraft maker and operator that builds and flies hybrid eVTOL cargo drones for middle-mile and last-mile B2B and defense logistics, integrating onboard AI for fully automated flight.
1. A robot maker that builds and operates autonomous hybrid eVTOL cargo aircraft, selling and delivering logistics services rather than licensing its platform.
2. Autonomous hybrid electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft that use onboard AI, physical actuators, and integrated autonomy software for fully automated flight operations.
3. Autonomous vertical take-off and landing, heavy-lift cargo transport of 100 to 500 pounds over 600 to 1,000 miles, and fully automated flight operations for logistics missions.
4. Complete autonomous aircraft that the organization builds, deploys, and operates itself to provide delivery services under contract.
5. Autonomous cargo drones used in middle-mile and last-mile expedited logistics, healthcare diagnostics delivery, remote resupply, and defense logistics.
6. Healthcare diagnostics providers, commercial businesses, and defense agencies requiring expedited logistics.
7. It builds its own autonomous aerial vehicles and operates them directly to fulfill logistics contracts for commercial and defense customers.
8. It is differentiated by a heavy-lift autonomous cargo drone platform capable of carrying 100 to 500 pounds over 600 to 1,000 miles.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Seed investors include At One Ventures, Draper Associates, and 500 Global.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through logistics and delivery service contracts, including a $50 million contract with a healthcare diagnostics provider.
Scale and maturity: The startup has raised a total of $15 million in funding and holds a $50 million contract for autonomous aircraft deliveries.
Geography: Based in San Francisco, California, with operations focused on commercial and defense logistics.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation are its entire focus, serving as the foundational operating system for its autonomous cargo aircraft logistics services.

points.name: Aethero
points.description: US startup building high-performance computing systems for edge processing in space and aerial operations.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds high-performance computing solutions for space and aerial operations, combining commercial hardware components with modern software for edge computing in aerospace environments.
1. A developer tools company that builds high-performance computing solutions using commercial components, sold as edge computing modules and software stacks for aerospace applications.
2. High-performance computing architectures built from commercial off-the-shelf components paired with modern software for space and aerial edge processing.
3. On-device computing and edge processing for space and aerial platforms.
4. Computing modules and software stacks sold to aerospace developers.
5. Space vehicles, aerial platforms, satellites, drones and aerospace edge computing.
6. Aerospace developers and space technology builders.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Geography: Based in the USA.

points.name: Airbound
points.description: Indian aerospace startup building ultralight autonomous aircraft for efficient drone-based delivery.
points.bullets:
A drone maker that designs and builds autonomous aircraft for drone-based delivery and logistics, aiming to reduce the cost and improve the scalability of last-mile delivery.
1. A drone maker that builds and sells autonomous aircraft.
2. Ultralight, carbon-fiber blended-wing-body aircraft.
3. Autonomous flight and last-mile delivery.
4. Complete drones and vehicles.
5. Drones, logistics and last-mile delivery.
6. Logistics operators.
7. Its drones are operated for delivery by logistics companies.
points.profile:
Geography: Based in Bengaluru, India.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Fortem Technologies, Inc.
points.description: US technology company building AI-powered interceptor drones that physically capture hostile aircraft mid-air.
points.bullets:
A drone maker that builds autonomous counter-drone interceptor drones and the radar sensors and autonomy software they use, for defense, law enforcement, and critical infrastructure protection.
1. A drone maker that designs and sells complete interceptor drones and radar sensors for counter-unmanned aerial system operations.
2. Autonomous interceptor drones, radar sensors, and on-device artificial intelligence for mid-air detection and physical net-based capture of hostile unmanned aircraft.
3. Autonomous airborne operations, beyond-line-of-sight interception, radar perception, and physical capture of small drones.
4. Complete drones, radar sensors, and integrated proprietary software sold as counter-drone systems.
5. Defense, law enforcement, critical infrastructure protection, and airborne counter-drone operations.
6. Defense forces, law enforcement agencies, and critical infrastructure operators.
7. It designs and manufactures its own interceptor drones and sensors and supplies them directly to defense and security customers.
8. It uses a reusable, non-lethal, physical net-based capture method that achieves an eighty-five percent first-shot success rate against small drones.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Selected for the United States Department of Defense Replicator initiative.
Organization type: A privately held company operating in the defense technology and national security market.
Business model: Hardware sales of drones and sensors with integrated proprietary software.
Scale and maturity: A mature operational company with established deployments and selection for the Replicator initiative.
Geography: Based in the United States, operating domestically and extending solutions to allied international partners.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire business focus is dedicated to autonomous defense technologies and physical counter-drone automation.

points.name: Archer Aviation
points.description: US aerospace company developing on-device AI for autonomous electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft.
points.bullets:
An electric aircraft company that designs and builds eVTOL aircraft and autonomous air taxis, embedding on-device edge AI compute for real-time aviation safety and operational autonomy. It operates at the deployed system level, integrating third-party AI hardware into its proprietary avionics and control software to create a unified aerospace and defense platform.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that designs and sells complete eVTOL aircraft and autonomous uncrewed aerial vehicles.
2. Electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, hybrid autonomous aircraft, and an aerospace and defense foundation model trained on nearly two million flight hours, running on embedded compute platforms for real-time environmental processing.
3. On-device inference for real-time aviation safety, vertical takeoff and landing, autonomous flight, and advanced air mobility network operations.
4. Complete aircraft, including piloted air taxis and autonomous uncrewed aerial vehicles, alongside airspace software for managing autonomous operations.
5. Air taxis, defense UAS, commercial logistics, freight, emergency operations, and urban air mobility networks.
6. Future passengers, US government and military, international defense buyers, and commercial logistics operators.
7. The company builds complete aircraft and embeds third-party AI compute platforms into its proprietary avionics and control software.
8. An aviation-grade advanced driver assistance system that processes real-time environmental data on-device to assist human pilots safely, combined with a foundation model trained on nearly two million flight hours.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Boeing, Wisk Aero, Insitu, SkyGrid, Anduril, and NVIDIA.
Organization type: A publicly traded company.
Business model: Hardware sales of aircraft, defense contracts, and airspace software revenues.
Scale and maturity: Approaching initial commercial operations with targeted launch dates in the mid-2020s, with an active defense business and ongoing US government contracts.
Geography: Based in the United States with a dedicated test bed and operational hub in Hawthorne, Los Angeles, targeting commercial operations in the Middle East and the United States.
Beyond physical AI: The organization extends its technological capabilities into aircraft manufacturing, fleet operations, and pilot training programs.

points.name: Wisk Aero
points.description: US aerospace subsidiary developing autonomous electric air taxis for passenger transportation.
points.bullets:
An autonomous passenger aircraft maker that designs, builds, and tests fully pilotless electric vertical takeoff and landing air taxis for urban air mobility. The organization acts as a complete vehicle original equipment manufacturer, integrating autonomous flight controls, sensors, and software directly into its physical aircraft.
1. An aircraft maker that builds fully autonomous eVTOL passenger air taxis and sells them as complete vehicles.
2. Tilt-rotor and winged compound electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft equipped with autonomous flight control software and a multi-vehicle supervisor system for ground-based monitoring.
3. Fully autonomous passenger flight, vertical takeoff and landing, and single-operator multi-vehicle fleet monitoring.
4. Complete autonomous aircraft and integration services.
5. Urban air taxis, passenger aviation, and military unmanned aircraft systems.
6. Commercial aviation operators, urban air mobility providers, and defense forces.
7. Its complete aircraft are operated by urban air mobility and defense operators.
8. A multi-vehicle supervisor system replaces onboard physical cockpit controls and allows a single ground operator to monitor up to three aircraft simultaneously.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Boeing and Archer Aviation.
Organization type: A corporate subsidiary absorbed by a publicly traded aerospace firm.
Business model: Aircraft sales and integration contracts.
Scale and maturity: A developer with 16 years of operation, six generations of aircraft, and more than 1,700 test flights.
Geography: Based in the United States with test operations and partnerships domestically and internationally.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI is the entire focus of the organization, which centers on achieving fully autonomous, passenger-carrying commercial flight.

points.name: SkyGrid
points.description: US subsidiary deploying edge AI for autonomous flight navigation and on-vehicle cybersecurity in unmanned aircraft.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds ground-based, aircraft-agnostic air traffic management software for integrating autonomous aircraft into shared airspace, providing the digital infrastructure for safe uncrewed flight operations.
1. A developer tools company whose air traffic management platform autonomous vehicle operators and civil aviation authorities use.
2. A software platform that uses AI-enabled dynamic traffic routing, blockchain, data analytics and cybersecurity to construct a high-fidelity common operating picture from integrated aeronautical and environmental datasets.
3. Inflight monitoring, automated route approvals, predictive maintenance, airspace surveillance and decision support for automated flight rules compliance.
4. A cloud-based software platform and third-party services delivered to operators and regulators.
5. Advanced air mobility, autonomous cargo and passenger air vehicles, drones and urban air mobility.
6. Urban air mobility operators, civil aviation authorities and autonomous vehicle developers.
7. Its software platform integrates into the airspace infrastructure layer used by autonomous aircraft operators.
8. It is aircraft-agnostic and designed to support emerging FAA Automated Flight Rules, distinguishing it from vehicle-specific autopilot stacks.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Boeing, SparkCognition, EUROCONTROL, Archer and Wisk.
Organization type: A subsidiary that originated as a joint venture and was absorbed by an aerospace company.
Business model: Software platform services, government task orders and contracts for airspace integration.
Scale and maturity: A strategically backed entity operating at a deployed commercial scale with active international collaborations, founded in 2018.
Geography: Based in Austin, Texas, with operational engagements across North America, Europe and the Middle East.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics and physical automation represent the entirety of its mission, focused exclusively on enabling scalable self-flying air transportation.

points.name: Windracers
points.description: UK startup deploying autonomous cargo aircraft to deliver goods to remote areas.
points.bullets:
A drone maker that builds heavy-lift autonomous cargo aircraft and is working to operate them as a cargo service in remote regions, having flown missions in active conflict zones. The organization designs complete uncrewed aircraft for carrying goods to areas with limited logistics infrastructure, for commercial and defense customers.
1. A drone maker that builds and sells heavy-lift autonomous cargo aircraft and is developing an air cargo service it would operate itself.
2. The company builds fixed-wing unmanned aircraft designed to carry heavy cargo loads over long distances without a pilot on board.
3. The aircraft deliver autonomous heavy-lift cargo transport and uncrewed flight operations in remote and austere environments.
4. The organization provides complete autonomous cargo aircraft and is working to operate air cargo drone services itself.
5. The machines are used in autonomous air cargo logistics, flying missions in remote regions and defense supply operations.
6. The company sells to logistics operators, defense forces and regional transport authorities.
7. Its aircraft are built in-house and operated by the organization or its partners to run cargo services in remote regions.
8. The firm is developing a self-operated cargo drone service specifically for remote and hard-to-reach areas and has flown autonomous missions in an active conflict zone.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Highland and Islands Transport Partnership to deploy drone operations in remote UK regions.
Organization type: The company is a privately held startup.
Business model: The organization makes money through drone sales and is working to generate revenue from operating autonomous air cargo services.
Scale and maturity: A startup that has active aircraft flying autonomous cargo missions in remote regions and in Ukraine.
Geography: The organization is based in the UK and operates in remote regions of Scotland and Ukraine.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play physical AI company focused entirely on autonomous cargo aircraft and drone logistics operations.

points.name: SOFWERX
points.description: United States innovation hub accelerating prototyping and industry collaboration for defense autonomous systems.
points.bullets:
An innovation hub that facilitates industry engagement and rapid prototyping for unmanned and autonomous systems in defense, partnering with government stakeholders and operating on behalf of special operations forces.
1. A government-affiliated innovation hub that runs collaborative programs, ideation events and rapid prototyping to source and assess autonomous systems solutions for defense customers.
2. The organization delivers rapid prototyping, solution assessments and collaborative events for the defense community.
3. Its activities are used in defense and special operations settings.
4. The organization serves special operations forces, government stakeholders, defense industry contractors, national labs and academia.
5. It acts as an intermediary between defense operators and technology developers to source, assess and prototype autonomous systems.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The organization partners with the United States Special Operations Command and is part of the DEFENSEWERX innovation hubs.
Organization type: The organization is a government-affiliated innovation hub.
Business model: The entity operates on government partnerships and defense program funding to facilitate rapid prototyping and solution assessments.
Scale and maturity: It is an established innovation hub within the United States defense ecosystem.
Geography: It is based and operates in the United States.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the organization addresses a broader range of challenging defense and warfighter problems through collaboration and ideation.

points.name: Apeiro Motion
points.description: Robotics subsidiary deploying AI-driven ground robots and tethered drones for industrial surveillance.
points.bullets:
A robotics platform provider and systems integrator that develops advanced ground robots and tethered unmanned aerial vehicles for defense and security applications. It integrates edge AI hardware, proprietary navigation tools, and AI-driven electro-optical sensing modules into its deployed robotic systems. The organization serves as the ground mobility and tethered surveillance layer within a broader autonomous defense ecosystem.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells ground robots and tethered unmanned aerial vehicles.

points.name: EVE Energy
points.description: Chinese battery company developing solid-state batteries for robotics.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that develops and manufactures batteries for robotics, advancing solid-state battery technology for humanoid robots and other machines in the physical AI ecosystem.
1. A battery company that builds solid-state batteries and other power cells for robotics applications.
2. Solid-state battery cells and advanced power storage engineered for the energy density and safety demands of robotics.
3. High-density power storage and delivery for humanoid robots and other physical AI machines.
4. Battery components and cells sold to robot makers for integration into their machines.
5. Humanoid robotics and other robotic systems operating in the physical world.
6. Robot makers and humanoid robotics manufacturers.
7. Its battery cells are designed into robots by device makers.
points.profile:
Geography: Based in China and advancing in the Chinese humanoid robotics market.
Beyond physical AI: The organization focuses entirely on battery technology and power storage solutions.

points.name: Muddy Machines
points.description: UK startup deploying autonomous physical robots with on-device AI to harvest asparagus.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds and sells autonomous agricultural robots for harvesting labor-intensive crops, integrating the complete physical machine, on-device perception and field-management software for commercial growers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells complete electric harvesting robots.
2. Deep learning computer vision paired with custom mechanical actuators on a lightweight electric vehicle frame to identify and sever mature crops in real time.
3. On-device visual crop detection, selective harvesting of curved and irregular vegetables, and in-field coordination of multiple robotic units through a farmer-facing application.
4. Complete harvesting robots delivered directly to farms as deployed systems.
5. Agricultural fields and commercial farming operations, specifically the harvesting of asparagus and other labor-intensive crops.
6. Commercial agricultural growers and farming enterprises.
7. Its complete robots are operated by agricultural growers in their own fields to automate harvesting tasks.
8. Specialized end-effectors and visual processing enable the delicate harvesting of curved and irregularly shaped vegetables without crop damage.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Collaborated with the nation's largest asparagus grower for on-farm testing and is backed by a named venture capital firm.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of complete robotic systems to agricultural enterprises.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2020 and transitioning from prototype testing to manufacturing its next hundred robots.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom, where it operates and maintains commercial deployments.
Beyond physical AI: Edge AI, robotics, and physical automation represent the entire focus and core mission of the company.

points.name: DexRobot
points.description: Chinese robotics startup building five-finger dexterous robotic hands that mimic human hand strength and mobility.
points.bullets:
A component supplier that develops five-finger dexterous robotic hands that mimic human hand strength and mobility for robot makers.
1. A component supplier that builds dexterous hands for humanoid and industrial robots.
2. The core technology is tendon drive mechanisms that replicate human hand strength and mobility in a five-finger format.
3. It delivers dexterous manipulation capabilities for robotic platforms.
4. Customers get it as mechanical components integrated into their own robotic systems.
5. The hands are used in humanoids and robotic manipulation systems.
6. It sells to robot makers building humanoid or industrial robotic platforms.
7. Its components are designed into robots by device makers that need human-like manipulation.
8. It operates as a full-stack self-developer of dexterous hand technology rather than integrating third-party designs.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: The company is backed by CICC Capital.
Organization type: It is a privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through component sales of dexterous hands.
Scale and maturity: It is an early-stage startup that raised investment in May 2025.
Geography: The company is based in China.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Artisense
points.description: Software company providing spatial mapping software that helps machines navigate physical spaces autonomously.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds SLAM and sensor fusion positioning software for machines that need to localize and navigate in physical space. A spin-out from a university technical institute, the company develops computer vision and sensor fusion systems that integrate with robot operating environments for developers and machine builders.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses SLAM and sensor fusion positioning software.
2. The core technology is simultaneous localization and mapping software that fuses computer vision and sensor data to calculate position.
3. It delivers precise localization, spatial mapping and sensor fusion for autonomous navigation.
4. Customers get it as licensed software with support for robot operating system frameworks.
5. It is used in robots, drones and autonomous vehicles that require vision-based positioning.
6. It sells to robotics developers and machine builders integrating autonomy into their products.
7. Its software is integrated by machine makers into their autonomous platforms.
8. It originated as a university spin-out focused on accelerating SLAM development.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It joined the Kudan group to accelerate SLAM development.
Organization type: It is a privately held company that originated as a university technical institute spin-out.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is on SLAM and sensor fusion positioning software for physical AI.

points.name: Nordbo Robotics
points.description: Robotics software company developing no-code programming platforms that let operators easily teach industrial robots tasks like painting and sanding through demonstration and 3D scanning.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds no-code programming and AI software for industrial robots, focused on surface finishing and visual inspection. It makes teach-by-demonstration platforms, adaptive process control software, and edge-deployed vision models for manufacturers and integrators using six-axis arms.
1. A developer tools company whose no-code robot programming and inspection software runs on industrial robots and edge devices.
2. Lead-through teach-by-demonstration software, 3D scanning-based process adaptation, and image-annotation defect detection models deployed to edge computing hardware.
3. Robot path capture by demonstration, adaptive sanding and painting path generation, and automated visual defect detection.
4. Licensed software platforms and edge devices deployed on existing industrial robot arms.
5. Surface finishing operations including painting, powder coating, sanding, grinding, polishing, deburring, dispensing, and visual quality inspection.
6. Manufacturers and factory automation integrators.
7. Its software is installed on industrial robot arms purchased from robot makers to program and control surface finishing and inspection tasks.
8. It enables robot programming by demonstration and image annotation without coding, lowering the skill barrier for complex surface finishing and inspection tasks.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and edge device sales.
Beyond physical AI: The company is also associated with six-axis force torque sensing technology.

points.name: Meili Robots
points.description: Software company building cloud-based fleet management systems to coordinate and route mobile robots.
points.bullets:
A developer tools and platform company that builds a universal fleet management system for mobile robots, providing mission management, traffic control, and route planning to logistics operators and manufacturers running mixed fleets of automated guided vehicles.
1. A developer tools company whose fleet management software robotics engineers and operators use to coordinate mobile robots, sold as a cloud-based SaaS platform.
2. A cloud-based fleet management system that supports ROS1, ROS2, and VDA5050 to orchestrate mission management, traffic control, and route planning across mobile robots.
3. It delivers fleet orchestration, mission management, traffic control, and route planning for mobile robots.
4. Customers get it as a cloud-based software platform or SaaS.
5. It is used in warehouses, factories, and logistics operations running automated guided vehicles and mobile robots.
6. It sells to logistics operators, manufacturers, and robotics engineers managing fleets of mobile robots.
7. Its software is integrated by operators and integrators to orchestrate mobile robots built by various robot makers.
points.profile:
Organization type: It is a privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through software licenses or SaaS subscriptions.
Scale and maturity: Founded in April 2019, it develops a universal fleet management system for the mobile robot sector.
Geography: It is based in Europe and operates in the global mobile robot market.
Beyond physical AI: Beyond edge and physical AI, the company has no other focus.

points.name: Otto Fleet Manager
points.description: Fleet management software company providing task assignment and health monitoring for autonomous mobile robots.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds fleet management software for assigning individual tasks to autonomous mobile robots and monitoring fleet health, sold to operators and integrators of warehouse automation.
1. A developer tools company whose fleet management platform robotics engineers and integrators use.
2. Fleet management software with standard APIs for task assignment and AMR health monitoring.
3. Individual task assignment to robots and fleet health monitoring.
4. Licensed software integrated via standard APIs.
5. Warehouses and factories running autonomous mobile robots.
6. Systems integrators and factory automation operators.
7. Its software is integrated into factory and warehouse deployments by automation integrators.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions.

points.name: Avassa
points.description: Software company managing containerized AI applications across distributed robot fleets.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides an edge computing platform for robotics teams to deploy and manage distributed software across robot fleets. The platform supports declarative deployments, edge-native monitoring, distributed security, and application autonomy for managing containerized AI models.
1. A developer tools company whose edge orchestration platform robotics engineers use.
2. Containerized AI model management with declarative deployments, edge-native monitoring, and distributed security for distributed edge devices.
3. Edge-native orchestration, monitoring, security, and application autonomy for fleet-wide software deployment.
4. Licensed software or platform tools used by robotics teams on their own machines.
5. Robot fleets and distributed edge computing systems.
6. Robotics teams and developers managing distributed software across fleets.
7. Its platform is used by robotics teams to deploy and manage software on robots built by other makers.
8. It specializes in edge-native orchestration and distributed security for managing containerized AI models across robot fleets.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions for its edge orchestration platform.

points.name: ReductStore
points.description: Software company providing high-throughput time-series storage for unstructured robotics data on edge devices.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that builds a time-series data storage system for robotics and edge AI workloads. It provides high-throughput storage for sensor and robotics data on edge devices and in the cloud, serving engineers who need to retain and replay recorded machine data.
1. A developer tools company whose storage software robotics engineers use to manage edge data.
2. A time-series database with volume-based FIFO retention and conditional replication accessible through a unified API.
3. High-throughput data storage, volume-based retention, conditional replication, and integration with visualization and robotics middleware tools.
4. Licensed software that runs on edge devices and cloud infrastructure.
5. Robotics deployments, edge devices, and sensor data systems.
6. Robotics engineers and developers building edge-heavy machine deployments.
7. Its software is deployed by developers into their own edge devices and robotics systems.
8. It focuses on high-throughput time-series storage with volume-based retention rather than general-purpose databases, though it lacks native ROS integration and built-in visualization.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with Grafana for dashboards and Foxglove for MCAP file visualization.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Heex
points.description: Software company recording only relevant autonomous system data triggered by specific events to reduce storage needs.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides an event-driven data capture platform for autonomous systems and production fleets. It records only specific moments triggered by events or anomalies to reduce bandwidth and storage needs, and integrates with standard visualization formats for data review.
1. A developer tools company that builds an event-driven data capture platform for autonomous systems, sold as software.
2. Event-driven data recording software that triggers data capture based on specific events or anomalies and integrates with MCAP and open-source visualization tools.
3. Selective data collection that reduces storage and bandwidth requirements by recording only relevant operational moments.
4. Licensed software or a data review dashboard with integrated open-source visualization tools.
5. Autonomous systems and production fleets.
6. Developers and operators of autonomous systems.
7. Its data capture software is integrated into the data pipelines of autonomous system developers and fleet operators.
8. It reduces data storage by over 90 percent by recording only event-triggered moments rather than continuous streams.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Integrates with Foxglove and MCAP.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses or subscriptions.
Beyond physical AI: Its focus is entirely on data management and review tools for autonomous systems.

points.name: Slamcore
points.description: Software company providing spatial intelligence software that helps robots and drones map environments and track their locations.
points.bullets:
A developer tools company that provides a software platform and SDK for creating, integrating, and deploying SLAM systems for autonomous robots, drones, and manually driven vehicles. It builds spatial intelligence software that enables machines to localize themselves, map unfamiliar surroundings, and navigate reliably, serving robotics engineers and developers who need real-time perception and mapping capabilities.
1. A developer tools company whose SLAM software development kit and hardware-software bundle robotics engineers use for spatial localization and mapping.
2. Simultaneous Localization and Mapping software combining visual-inertial sensing with real-time mapping algorithms to estimate position and build environment maps.
3. Real-time localization, environmental mapping, spatial visualization, and consistent navigation in unfamiliar surroundings.
4. Licensed software development kits and integrated hardware-software bundles.
5. Autonomous robots, high-end drones, and manually driven industrial vehicles.
6. Robotics developers, drone manufacturers, and industrial vehicle builders.
7. Its software is integrated by robot and drone makers into their machines for navigation and perception.
8. It pairs its SLAM SDK with industrial-grade hardware to bring robot-like localization to manually driven vehicles.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Software licenses and hardware-software product sales.

points.name: AIDIN ROBOTICS
points.description: South Korean sensor manufacturer building high-precision force torque sensors for humanoid robots.
points.bullets:
A component supplier and robot hand maker that builds force-torque sensors, tactile sensors, and humanoid robot hands, sold as components to robot makers and as integrated picking and finishing systems to manufacturers and logistics operators.
1. A component supplier that makes force-torque sensors, tactile sensors, and humanoid robot hands, and also builds integrated robotic finishing and picking systems.
2. Capacitance-based six-axis force-torque sensors, capacitive tactile sensors, and linkage-driven robot hands with sixteen degrees of freedom.
3. Six-axis force and torque measurement, contact location and force distribution sensing, delicate touch, power and pinch gripping, and force-aware polishing and picking.
4. Sensors and grippers sold as components, humanoid hands for research, and complete robotic finishing and picking systems.
5. Humanoid robots, collaborative robots, factory automation, surface finishing, logistics picking, warehouses, and manufacturing.
6. Robot makers, industrial robot companies, logistics operators, and manufacturers.
7. Its sensors and hands are designed into robots by robot makers, and its own integrated systems are deployed in factory and warehouse operations.
8. A proprietary electrostatic capacitance measurement method for high-durability sensors combined with a vertically integrated force-aware robotics portfolio.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: CJ Logistics, Amazon Robotics, and Zivid.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Component sales, robot hand sales, and integrated system sales.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2019, exporting components and systems to the United States and Australia.
Geography: Based in South Korea, operating internationally.
Beyond physical AI: The organization is a pure-play physical AI and robotics company.

points.name: Sonardyne
points.description: British technology company developing underwater navigation instruments for autonomous marine robots.
points.bullets:
A sensor maker that develops underwater navigation instruments combining inertial navigation, Doppler velocity logs, and acoustic aiding for marine robotics, offshore energy, defense, and science applications.
1. A sensor maker that builds underwater navigation instruments and sells them as pre-calibrated units.
2. Tightly integrated inertial navigation systems and Doppler velocity logs with sensor fusion, acoustic aiding, and SLAM calibration in a single unit.
3. Subsea positioning, true north seeking heading, free-inertial navigation, and SLAM calibration for underwater vehicles.
4. The company sells sensors and navigation instruments as hardware units, alongside supporting survey software.
5. Autonomous underwater vehicles, subsea survey operations, offshore energy, defense, and marine science.
6. AUV developers, survey companies, defense forces, and offshore energy operators.
7. Its sensors are integrated into underwater vehicles and survey platforms by vehicle makers and service providers.
8. It combines inertial navigation, Doppler velocity log, and acoustic aiding in a single pre-calibrated unit with free-inertial capability.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: AUV developer ecoSUB Robotics and survey company Sulmara use its navigation instruments.
Organization type: Privately held technology company.
Business model: Hardware sales of navigation instruments and software.
Scale and maturity: An established provider of underwater navigation instruments with multiple product variants deployed across subsea applications.
Geography: Based in the United Kingdom and operating in global offshore, defense, and marine markets.
Beyond physical AI: The company also supplies subsea positioning and acoustic communication systems beyond physical AI.

points.name: Weston Robot
points.description: Singapore robotics integrator deploying autonomous inspection platforms, custom mobile robots, and unmanned maritime systems.
points.bullets:
A robotics integrator and robot maker that resells quadruped robots and manufactures custom autonomous mobile robot platforms and unmanned maritime systems, delivering them through a robots-as-a-service model for inspection and operational applications.
1. A robotics integrator that resells third-party quadruped robots and manufactures custom autonomous mobile robots and unmanned maritime systems, offered as integrated solutions and robots-as-a-service.
2. Customers get it through robots-as-a-service arrangements and integrated robotic platforms.
3. It is used in autonomous inspection, mobile robotics operations, and unmanned maritime systems.
4. It sells to industrial and commercial operators requiring autonomous inspection and robotic mobility solutions.
5. It resells robots from OEMs and integrates them with edge AI computing into complete inspection platforms it operates or deploys for end users.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: It partnered with Avnet to launch an autonomous inspection platform.
Organization type: It is a privately held company.
Business model: It makes money through robots-as-a-service fees and sales of integrated robotic platforms.
Geography: It is based in Singapore.
Beyond physical AI: Edge and physical AI is its entire focus.

points.name: Hypershell
points.description: Chinese robotics company building AI-powered wearable exoskeletons that learn user gaits in real time to augment human movement.
points.bullets:
A wearable robot maker that designs and sells AI-powered consumer exoskeletons for outdoor activities. It builds complete systems that combine physical actuators and motion hardware with on-device inference software to augment human movement, reduce physical exertion, and increase endurance for outdoor consumers.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells complete wearable exoskeletons.
2. A fully integrated wearable system that uses on-device sensors and on-device inference to learn a user's walking gait in real time and adjust actuator torque accordingly.
3. The wearable system learns a user's gait and provides mechanical motor-assisted support to reduce fatigue and augment movement on climbs and uneven terrain.
4. It sells complete wearable robotic systems as finished consumer hardware.
5. The exoskeletons are used in outdoor activities, hiking, travel, mountainous exploration, and general mobility.
6. It sells to individual consumers engaging in outdoor recreation and long-distance walking.
7. It designs and builds the complete wearable robotic system and sells it directly to end users, with exclusive distribution in Korea handled by a domestic partner.
8. Its approach uses on-device AI to learn a user's walking gait in real time to provide a mechanical boost that reduces fatigue on steep inclines.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: VD Robotics holds exclusive domestic distribution rights for its products in Korea.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: It makes money through hardware sales of consumer exoskeletons.
Scale and maturity: A company founded in 2021 that has commercially available products and won the Best Innovation Award in the Robotics category at CES 2025.
Geography: Based in China with real-world product validation in the mountains of Wales.
Beyond physical AI: Physical AI and wearable robotic systems are its entire focus.

points.name: Ottobock
points.description: German med-tech company building prosthetics and industrial exoskeletons to reduce physical strain.
points.bullets:
A med-tech company and component supplier that builds prosthetics, orthotics, and industrial exoskeletons for medical and industrial applications.
1. A component supplier that makes prosthetic hands, microprocessor-controlled knee joints, and passive industrial exoskeletons.
2. Microprocessor-controlled prosthetic joints and mechanical, ergonomic support structures.
3. Mobility restoration for amputees and musculoskeletal strain reduction for industrial workers.
4. Complete wearable devices and orthotic components.
5. Prosthetics, orthotics, medical rehabilitation, industrial manufacturing.
6. Amputees, clinical patients, and industrial workers.
7. Its prosthetic and exoskeleton devices are fitted directly to individuals or deployed by employers to support workers.
8. A medical device heritage focused on biomechanical rehabilitation applied to industrial workplace strain reduction.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of prosthetic devices and exoskeletons.
Scale and maturity: A global organization operating in over 35 countries.
Geography: Based in Germany, operating worldwide.
Beyond physical AI: The company also provides orthotic treatment and clinical services for patient rehabilitation.

points.name: B-Temia
points.description: Canadian company developing wearable robotic exoskeletons that enhance human mobility for physical rehabilitation.
points.bullets:
A wearable robot maker that builds powered exoskeletons integrating with human biomechanics to enhance mobility for individuals with physical challenges, sold into rehabilitation settings.
1. A robot maker that designs and sells wearable dermoskeleton exoskeletons for human mobility assistance.
2. Dermoskeleton technology that integrates powered mechanical assistance with human biomechanics.
3. Mobility enhancement and gait assistance for individuals with walking impairments.
4. Complete wearable robotic exoskeletons sold through distribution partners.
5. Rehabilitation clinics, medical therapy, and personal mobility assistance.
6. Rehabilitation providers, healthcare facilities, and individuals with mobility challenges.
7. Its exoskeletons are marketed and sold through exclusive medical technology distributors.
8. Its Dermoskeletics technology is designed to integrate directly with human biomechanics for mobility restoration.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Wistron Medical Technology and DIH, which holds exclusive distribution rights for North America.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Hardware sales of wearable exoskeletons through distribution partnerships.
Scale and maturity: A major exoskeleton market player with a global presence.
Geography: Based in Canada, with distribution across Canada, the United States, and Mexico.
Beyond physical AI: The company focuses entirely on robotic mobility enhancement and has no significant operations outside physical AI.

points.name: DNSYS
points.description: Robotics manufacturer building edge AI exoskeletons that use on-device sensors and processors to assist human movement in real time.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds consumer-grade hip and knee exoskeletons integrating edge AI inference, motion sensors, and motor actuators into complete wearable robotics for human mobility augmentation. The organization designs and sells finished assistive exoskeleton hardware that uses on-device neural networks to interpret user movement intentions and adjust motor torque in real time. It markets these wearable robots directly to outdoor enthusiasts and individuals with mobility limitations through crowdfunding and direct online sales.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells consumer exoskeletons integrating AI software, sensors, and actuators into complete wearable devices.
2. Artificial neural networks running on-device interpret motion sensor data to predict muscle activation and drive motorized actuation within 0.01 seconds.
3. On-device inference for real-time intention prediction, motor torque assistance for standing and walking, and muscle fatigue reduction for human locomotion.
4. Complete wearable exoskeletons and modular hip and knee components sold through direct online retail and crowdfunding.
5. Consumer hiking, outdoor all-terrain mobility, and assistive wearable support for aging populations and individuals with movement disorders.
6. Outdoor enthusiasts, hikers, aging populations, and individuals with mobility limitations.
7. It designs and integrates its own proprietary hardware and deep learning algorithms into finished consumer products sold directly to end users.
8. It embeds a proprietary deep learning algorithm that predicts muscle activation and adjusts motor torque within 0.01 seconds for consumer-grade mobility augmentation.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Founded by robotics experts from DJI, Segway, and Xiaomi.
Organization type: A privately held startup.
Business model: Direct hardware sales of finished exoskeletons and modular components.
Scale and maturity: Founded in 2021, it has raised over $820,000 through crowdfunding for its flagship devices.
Geography: Based in China and markets its products to a global consumer audience.
Beyond physical AI: It is a pure-play physical AI company entirely focused on practical, AI-driven human augmentation through wearable robotics.

points.name: Reshape Biotech
points.description: Danish startup automating routine laboratory microbiology tasks using robotic imaging platforms.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that builds automated imaging and incubation platforms for microbiology R&D laboratories, automating routine microbiological tasks for researchers.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells laboratory automation platforms for microbiological incubation and imaging.
2. Robotic platforms integrating automated imaging sensors and incubation hardware for data-driven microbiology.
3. Automated imaging, incubation, and execution of routine microbiological tasks for data-driven decision making.
4. Complete laboratory automation systems sold to microbiology R&D labs.
5. Microbiology R&D laboratories.
6. Microbiology research and development laboratories.
7. Its laboratory automation platforms are installed and operated directly by microbiology R&D labs.
8. It combines robotic imaging and incubation into a single scalable platform designed for data-driven microbiology.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Backed by investors including Y Combinator and ACME.
Organization type: Privately held startup.
Business model: Hardware sales of laboratory automation platforms.
Scale and maturity: A startup based in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark.
Geography: Based in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark.
Beyond physical AI: Its entire focus is laboratory automation for microbiology.

points.name: SANY
points.description: Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer deploying autonomous electric mining trucks and smart mining platforms.
points.bullets:
A heavy equipment manufacturer that builds and sells cabless autonomous electric mining trucks and integrated smart mining systems for open-pit mine operators.
1. A vehicle maker that builds autonomous electric haul trucks and integrated mining systems.
2. Multi-sensor fusion perception systems using lidar, millimeter-wave radar and cameras combined with electric drivetrains and cloud-based dispatching for autonomous navigation in mines.
3. Autonomous driving, multi-sensor 3D perception, vehicle-grid energy management and remote fleet dispatching in complex mining terrains.
4. Complete vehicles and integrated energy-plus-automation ecosystems delivered directly to mining operations.
5. Large open-pit mines and heavy haulage operations.
6. Large mining operators.
7. It designs and builds the vehicles and software it sells to mining operators.
8. It integrates pure-electric cabless autonomous haul trucks with grid, load and storage energy management into a one-stop mining ecosystem.
points.profile:
Organization type: Privately held heavy equipment manufacturer.
Business model: Hardware sales of mining trucks and heavy machinery, plus integrated energy and lifecycle services.
Scale and maturity: It holds over 35% of the global market for large-tonnage electric mining trucks and has deployed intelligent machines across a fleet of over 5,000 vehicles in more than 20 large mines worldwide.
Geography: Based in China and operates globally.
Beyond physical AI: The company is a broad heavy equipment manufacturer that builds traditional industrial and construction machinery.

points.name: Vale
points.description: Brazilian mining company operating iron ore mines and deploying autonomous haul trucks.
points.bullets:
A mining operator that runs iron ore mines and deploys autonomous haul trucks in its own operations. It buys autonomous haul trucks and MineStar Command technology from a heavy equipment manufacturer through a local dealer to automate material transport in its open-pit mines.
1. A mining operator that runs autonomous haul trucks in its own mines.
2. Autonomous haul trucks and MineStar Command technology supplied by a heavy equipment manufacturer.
3. Autonomous hauling and mine site automation.
4. A fleet of autonomous haul trucks it operates itself in its own mines.
5. Iron ore mines, specifically the Northern System in the Carajás region.
6. It is an end operator rather than a seller.
7. It buys autonomous haul trucks from an OEM and runs them in its own mines.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Caterpillar and Sotreq.
Organization type: Privately held mining company.
Business model: Mining revenues from iron ore extraction.
Scale and maturity: Large-scale iron ore operations in the Carajás region with an expanded autonomous haul truck fleet.
Geography: Based and operating in Brazil, specifically the Carajás region.
Beyond physical AI: A major iron ore mining company beyond its physical AI deployments.

points.name: Fortescue
points.description: Australian mining company deploying autonomous electric haul trucks and building heavy-duty fast chargers.
points.bullets:
A mining operator that runs autonomous and battery-electric haul trucks in its own iron ore mines, co-developing the machines, autonomy systems and charging infrastructure with equipment manufacturers.
1. A mine operator that runs autonomous haulage fleets and builds battery systems and fast chargers for its own mining vehicles.
2. Battery-electric powertrays for mining haul trucks, high-power DC fast chargers and autonomous haulage software integrated through joint programs with equipment manufacturers.
3. Autonomous haulage, fleet electrification and high-power charging of mining vehicles.
4. A haul truck fleet and charging infrastructure it operates itself in its own mines.
5. Iron ore mines and mining haul fleets.
6. Its own mining operations.
7. It buys haul trucks and support vehicles from OEMs and runs them in its own mines, while co-developing battery and charging hardware.
8. It co-develops battery-electric powertrays and autonomous haulage solutions directly with truck OEMs rather than buying off-the-shelf machines.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Caterpillar for MineStar Command autonomous haulage, Liebherr for T 264 haul trucks and autonomous haulage development, XCMG for battery-electric support vehicles and KUKA for robotic charging arms.
Organization type: A publicly traded mining company.
Business model: Mining operations and iron ore sales, with capital investment in its own electrification and autonomy infrastructure.
Scale and maturity: A large iron ore miner operating across multiple sites in Western Australia with a multibillion-dollar equipment fleet.
Geography: Based and operating in the Pilbara region of Western Australia.
Beyond physical AI: An iron ore mining company engaged in large-scale mining and resource extraction.

points.name: Liebherr
points.description: US heavy equipment manufacturer building autonomous battery-electric haul trucks for mining operations.
points.bullets:
A heavy-equipment manufacturer that builds large mining haul trucks and integrates them with an autonomy platform, partnering with a mining operator to electrify and automate its vehicles for surface mining operations.
1. A vehicle maker that designs and sells ultra-class mining haul trucks, offered as autonomous battery-electric machines.
2. Battery-electric powertrains and automated route-control software integrated into heavy-duty mechanical truck architectures.
3. Autonomous haulage, battery-electric propulsion and automated route control for ultra-class mining trucks.
4. Complete vehicles sold to mining operators under large supply contracts.
5. Surface mines and bulk-material handling operations.
6. Mining operators and mining companies.
7. Its trucks are operated by mining companies in their own mine sites.
8. It combines ultra-class haul-truck engineering with an autonomy and battery-electric powertrain developed jointly with a mining-operator partner.
points.profile:
Key partners and customers: Fortescue.
Organization type: Privately held company.
Business model: Vehicle and equipment sales under large supply contracts.
Scale and maturity: A large established manufacturer operating under a multi-billion-dollar supply deal.
Geography: Based in Newport News, Virginia, USA, with a global manufacturing and market footprint.
Beyond physical AI: The company also manufactures a broad range of heavy equipment beyond autonomous mining trucks, including cranes, excavators, dozers and container-handling machines.

points.name: Hanwha Vision
points.description: South Korean security company building edge AI cameras for real-time on-device video analytics.
points.bullets:

points.name: Google — Gemini Nano
points.description: Google's family of small on-device multimodal language models (Gemini Nano, Gemma) embedded in phones, buds and browsers for offline translation, accessibility and assistant features.

An AI model developer and technology company that builds compact, multimodal language models designed for on-device inference at the edge. points.name: Google DeepMind — Gemini Robotics
points.description: Vision-language-action foundation model family that gives robots perception, reasoning and whole-body motor control, licensed to humanoid and industrial robot makers.

points.name: Google DeepMind — World Models
points.description: Generative world-modeling research line (Genie, SIMA) that creates interactive virtual environments used to train and test embodied and autonomous-driving agents.
points.bullets:
An AI research laboratory that develops generative world models which create interactive virtual environments used to train and test embodied and autonomous-driving agents.
