points.name: Google DeepMind — Gemma
points.description: Open-weight family of small, edge-optimized language and multimodal models aimed at on-device and resource-constrained AI deployments.

points.name: Fourier Intelligence — GR Humanoid Robots

points.name: Fourier Intelligence — Rehabilitation Robotics

points.name: UBTech — Walker

points.name: DARPA — Robotics Challenge

points.name: Northrop Grumman — Satellite Servicing

The organization serves robot makers, autonomous vehicle operators, and automotive engineers developing software-defined machines.
1. A chip company that designs scalable, energy-efficient CPU architectures and compute platforms for robotics, autonomous vehicles, and edge devices, licensed to semiconductor and device makers.
2. Its core technology consists of central processing units and compute subsystems designed for functional-safety processes, computational efficiency, and scalable performance in low-power edge systems.
3. It delivers foundational compute performance, functional safety, and architectural standardization for on-device inference, autonomous driving stacks, and robot task execution.
4. Its technology reaches customers through licensed intellectual property and compute platform packages that semiconductor and device makers integrate into their own silicon and systems.
5. Its architectures are used in autonomous mobile robots, autonomous-driving vehicles, software-defined automotive systems, smartphones, and data centers.
6. Its customers include robot makers, autonomous vehicle operators, automakers, and semiconductor companies that design chips based on its architectures.
7. Its intellectual property is designed into silicon and compute platforms by semiconductor and device makers building robots and vehicles.
8. It distinguishes itself as a fabless designer of the underlying compute architecture rather than a chip manufacturer, supplying the foundational technology that others build upon.

points.name: Arm — AGI CPU
points.description: Arm's own manufactured silicon product line, a purpose-built CPU targeting AI data centers and agentic AI workloads, marking its entry beyond pure IP licensing.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company and semiconductor IP licensor that designs energy-efficient processor architectures and has recently begun manufacturing its own purpose-built CPUs for AI data centers and agentic workloads, providing the compute foundation for edge devices, robots, and vehicles.
1. A chip company that designs and licenses semiconductor IP and instruction set architectures, and now manufactures its own data-center CPUs.
2. Energy-efficient compute architectures and purpose-built central processing units designed for AI data centers and agentic AI workloads.
3. Scalable compute foundations for on-device inference, edge computing, and agentic AI processing.
4. Licensed semiconductor IP, instruction set architectures, and manufactured data-center silicon chips.
5. Data centers, edge devices, robots, vehicles, and drones.
6. Chip designers, device makers, and data-center operators.
7. Its semiconductor IP is designed into chips by device makers, and its manufactured CPUs are sold directly for data-center compute.
8. It transitions a decades-long pure IP licensing model into direct silicon manufacturing for agentic AI workloads.

points.name: Mercedes-Benz — DRIVE PILOT
points.description: Mercedes-Benz's SAE Level 3 conditional automated driving system for consumer passenger vehicles.
points.bullets:
A premium automaker that designs and sells passenger vehicles equipped with a certified SAE Level 3 conditional automated driving system, integrating third-party autonomy software and redundant sensor arrays into its production cars for consumer use.
1. A vehicle maker that builds and sells complete passenger cars, offered as integrated hardware-software systems to consumers.
2. Redundant sensor arrays including 4D imaging radar combined with third-party GPU-based drive AV software for conditional automated driving.
3. Conditional highway autonomy and hands-free automated driving under specific operational constraints.
4. Complete production vehicles sold to consumers, featuring integrated third-party autonomy stacks and embedded sensor hardware.
5. Consumer passenger vehicles, highway driving, and robotaxi fleets.
6. Consumers purchasing premium passenger vehicles and ride-hailing platforms operating robotaxi fleets.
7. It buys autonomy software and sensors from suppliers and integrates them into the complete vehicles it designs and manufactures.
8. It was among the first automakers to achieve regulatory certification and deploy an SAE Level 3 conditional automated driving system in production consumer vehicles.

points.name: Mercedes-Benz — MO360
points.description: Mercedes-Benz's digital production/factory AI platform integrating LLM tools, chatbots, and automation software into manufacturing operations.
points.bullets:
An automaker that operates its own manufacturing plants and integrates AI tools, vision systems and humanoid robots into its factory production lines. It runs an internal digital factory software platform that embeds LLM tools, chatbots and vision-AI into assembly workflows for task guidance and defect detection. It also develops vehicle platform software for over-the-air updates and centralized compute in its cars.
1. An automaker that builds and sells cars and operates its own factories, deploying third-party vision-AI tools and humanoid robots on its assembly lines.
2. A digital factory platform combining LLM chatbots, automation software and vision-AI agents for real-time task guidance and deviation detection, alongside a Linux and QNX hybrid vehicle software stack.
3. Factory-floor workflow assistance, real-time task guidance, defect detection and deviation validation in precision assembly and logistics automation.
4. It operates the software and automation in its own manufacturing facilities and sells vehicles to consumers.
5. Automotive assembly lines, electric axial-flux motor production and vehicle platforms.
6. Consumers for its vehicles, and its own manufacturing operations for its internal factory software.
7. It operates AI tools and humanoid robots in its own factories and sells complete vehicles to consumers.
8. It unifies a digital factory software stack with humanoid robot pilots and vision-AI tools on a single campus to validate manufacturing processes for itself.

points.name: John Deere — Autonomy Kit
points.description: A GPS- and sensor-based autonomous-driving platform retrofitted onto tractors and other farm machinery for hands-free fieldwork.
points.bullets:
An agricultural machinery manufacturer that builds autonomous tractors and retrofit autonomy kits for hands-free farming. It develops GPS- and sensor-based driving platforms for existing farm equipment and produces fully driverless tractors for large-scale agricultural operations. The company serves farmers and agricultural enterprises seeking precision-agriculture automation.
1. A vehicle maker that builds autonomous tractors and retrofit autonomy kits for farm machinery, sold as complete machines or add-on platforms.
2. GPS-guided autonomy software paired with sensor-based perception systems for autonomous navigation in farm fields.
3. Hands-free fieldwork, autonomous tractor operation, precision agriculture navigation, and remote monitoring.
4. Complete autonomous vehicles and retrofit autonomy kits integrated onto tractors and other farm machinery.
5. Farms, orchards, and agricultural fields.
6. Farmers and agricultural enterprises.
7. Its autonomous tractors and kits are operated by farmers in their own agricultural operations.
8. It leverages deep roots in precision agriculture and heavy machinery to retrofit existing equipment with autonomy and build fully driverless tractors.

points.name: John Deere — See & Spray
points.description: A machine-vision and AI-driven precision spraying system that identifies crops versus weeds to cut herbicide use.
points.bullets:
An agricultural machinery manufacturer that builds autonomous tractors and precision spraying systems integrating cameras, sensors and machine learning to identify crops versus weeds for farmers.
1. A robot and vehicle maker that builds autonomous tractors and machine-vision precision spraying systems sold as integrated agricultural equipment.
2. Machine-vision and AI-driven precision spraying systems using cameras, sensors and machine learning to differentiate crops from weeds.
3. Targeted weed identification and herbicide application that reduces non-residual herbicide use by up to two-thirds, alongside autonomous tractor navigation.
4. Complete agricultural vehicles and bundled precision spraying systems integrated into tractors sold as farm equipment.
5. Farms, specifically cotton, soybean and corn fields.
6. Farmers and agricultural operators.
7. Its agricultural vehicles and precision systems are operated directly by farmers in crop fields.
8. Bundling AI-driven see-and-spray technology with autonomous tractors in large-scale product launches to reduce chemical inputs.

points.name: Meta — Llama
points.description: Meta's open-source Llama family of large and small language models, paired with on-device runtimes like ExecuTorch and PyTorch Mobile, targets edge and mobile AI deployment for developers.
points.bullets:
A technology conglomerate that develops open-source large and small language models and edge inference runtimes for mobile and device deployment. It produces small-parameter language and vision models purpose-built for edge devices, along with the frameworks to run them on mobile and embedded hardware. The organization licenses these models and tools to developers and hardware makers for on-device AI applications.
1. An AI model developer and tools company that builds open-source language and vision models and edge inference runtimes, released as open-source weights and software frameworks.
2. Transformer-based large language models with Group Query Attention and pre-layer normalization, alongside PyTorch Mobile and ExecuTorch inference runtimes for deploying models on mobile and edge hardware.
3. On-device language and vision inference, model safety red-teaming, content guardrails, and efficient deployment of AI models on mobile and embedded devices.
4. Open-source model weights and software frameworks that developers and hardware makers integrate into their own edge devices and applications.
5. Mobile devices, XR headsets, UAVs, and edge devices used in consumer and research applications.
6. Developers, hardware makers, and researchers building on-device AI applications.
7. Its models and runtimes are integrated by device makers and developers into edge hardware and consumer applications.
8. It releases its models and inference runtimes as open-source, enabling broad third-party compression, quantization, and deployment across diverse edge hardware.

points.name: Meta — Ray-Ban smart glasses
points.description: Meta's consumer wearable hardware line pairs camera/mic-equipped smart glasses and emerging AI pendants with its Meta AI assistant for hands-free queries, translation, and capture.
points.bullets:
A consumer wearable device maker that builds camera-equipped smart glasses and AI pendants paired with a cloud-based AI assistant for hands-free queries, translation, and real-world content capture. The organization designs and sells complete hardware devices in partnership with an eyewear manufacturer, embedding its own AI models for visual and audio interaction. It operates as a hardware maker for consumers while also developing the underlying AI models that run on its wearables.
1. A consumer electronics maker that builds smart glasses and AI pendants with embedded cameras, microphones and speakers, sold as complete wearable devices.
2. Camera and microphone-equipped wearable hardware paired with cloud-based large language models and vision models for visual queries and real-time translation.
3. Hands-free visual queries, real-time translation, audio capture, music playback, and real-world content capture.
4. Complete consumer wearable devices sold through retail partnerships, integrated with cloud-based AI assistant software.
5. Consumer smart glasses, AI pendants, and workplace wearable devices.
6. Consumers and enterprise users.
7. Its wearable devices are sold directly to consumers through an eyewear manufacturing partner.
8. It pairs mainstream eyewear form factors from a major fashion brand with a deeply integrated cloud AI assistant at massive consumer scale.

points.name: Meta — MTIA
points.description: Meta's in-house Meta Training and Inference Accelerator chip program, developed with partners like Broadcom and via the Rivos acquisition, builds custom AI silicon to reduce reliance on Nvidia.
points.bullets:
A hyperscaler and technology company that designs custom AI silicon for its internal data center workloads, building training and inference accelerators to reduce its reliance on third-party GPUs.
1. A chip company that designs custom AI accelerator ASICs for internal data center use.
2. Custom AI accelerator ASICs based on the RISC-V instruction set architecture, developed to handle recommendation and ranking workloads alongside co-developed Arm-based data center CPUs.
3. Accelerated AI training and inference for large-scale recommendation systems, advertising ranking and generative models.
4. Custom silicon deployed internally within its own data centers.
5. Hyperscale data centers running social media feeds, ad ranking and generative AI infrastructure.
6. Internal corporate operations and data center infrastructure teams.
7. Its custom chips are designed and deployed internally to power its own hyperscale computing infrastructure.
8. It vertically integrates custom data center silicon development to reduce capital expenditures and decrease dependence on external AI chip suppliers.

points.name: Xiaomi — CyberOne
points.description: Xiaomi's humanoid robot platform used as a hardware-AI showcase and piloted in industrial settings rather than sold as a commercial product.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics company that builds humanoid and quadruped robot platforms to showcase its AI-hardware ecosystem, piloting them in its own EV factories rather than commercializing them as standalone products. Its robotics division operates as a subsidiary developing full-size humanoids and open-source quadruped robots, serving primarily as a strategic technology demonstration rather than a material revenue stream. The organization extends its AIoT expertise into physical AI through prototype humanoid and quadruped platforms deployed in industrial settings.
1. A robot maker that builds full-size humanoid and quadruped robots used as hardware-AI showcases and industrial pilots.
2. Bipedal and quadruped locomotion platforms integrating vision-language-action models, active liquid cooling, 3D spatial perception, and open-source robotics world models.
3. 3D space perception, individual recognition, bimanual manipulation for self-tapping nut installation, and legged locomotion in both humanoid and quadruped form factors.
4. Complete prototype robots deployed in its own EV factory die-casting workshops and an open-source quadruped platform released to developers.
5. Humanoid robots in automotive die-casting workshops and battery production lines, with quadruped robots targeting consumer and developer ecosystems.
6. Internal manufacturing operations for industrial pilots and developer communities for its open-source quadruped platform.
7. Its robots are built and piloted internally within its own EV factories, while its quadruped platform is open-sourced for external developers.
8. Operates its humanoid program as a strategic AI-hardware ecosystem showcase rather than a commercial product line, leveraging internal EV factories as captive pilot environments.

points.name: Xiaomi — CyberDog
points.description: A quadruped robotics platform aimed at inspection, patrol, and R&D use cases distinct from the humanoid line.
points.bullets:
A consumer electronics company that builds quadruped and humanoid robots for inspection, patrol, and R&D environments, extending its hardware manufacturing and AIoT expertise into physical AI through an open-source robotics platform.
1. A robot maker that builds and sells quadruped and humanoid robots.

3. Indoor patrol, predictive maintenance inspection, and custom research workflows.

5. Indoor patrols, R&D environments, and humanoid robotics.
6. Research institutions and developers.
7. Its robots are operated directly by users in research and inspection settings.

points.name: Xiaomi — Smart Manufacturing
points.description: Xiaomi's AI-driven automated factory program spanning its smartphone and EV production lines.
points.bullets:
An operator that runs AI-driven, fully autonomous manufacturing plants for its own smartphone and electric vehicle production lines. It builds and operates automated factories where AI-driven machines handle the entire manufacturing process from assembly to testing, rather than selling the machines themselves.
1. An operator that runs automated factories for its own products, integrating AI-driven machines for assembly and testing.

points.name: Alibaba — Qwen
points.description: Alibaba's family of large and small language models, spanning cloud-scale flagships down to compact variants built to run on mobile and edge hardware.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer and cloud company that builds large, small and edge-optimized language models, and designs inference chips, for industrial, cloud and device makers.

2. Parameter-scaled multilingual language models ranging from cloud-scale flagships to compact variants running under 2GB of VRAM, and neural inference chips.

6. Device manufacturers, industrial operators, satellite operators, and enterprise cloud users.
7. Its models are embedded by device makers into edge hardware and its chips are designed into domestic cloud and edge systems.
8. It vertically integrates proprietary AI chips with a full stack of large and small language models tailored for constrained edge environments.

points.name: Alibaba — RynnBrain
points.description: Alibaba's embodied-AI program applying its Tongyi Qianwen/Qwen research to vision-language-action models that power humanoid and industrial robots.
points.bullets:
An AI model developer that builds vision-language-action models for humanoid and industrial robots, extending a large language model family into embodied AI. The organization applies its foundation-model research to robot control, creating models designed to run on robots built by other manufacturers. It pursues an open-source strategy for its AI models while leveraging its broader cloud and e-commerce infrastructure.
1. An AI model developer whose robot foundation models run on other companies' robots, built on an existing large language model family and released under an open-source strategy.
2. Vision-language-action models built on a large language model architecture, trained to translate visual perception and natural-language commands into robotic actions.

4. AI models released as open-source software and model weights that customers integrate into their own robot hardware.
5. Humanoid robots and industrial robots.
6. Robot makers and developers integrating foundation models into physical machines.
7. Its models are integrated by humanoid and industrial robot makers into their robots.

points.name: Doosan Robotics — Collaborative Robot Arms
points.description: Core cobot hardware business making and selling collaborative robot arms to industrial customers worldwide.
points.bullets:
A robot maker that designs, builds, and sells collaborative robot arms, developing its own core components and motion-control algorithms for industrial and service applications worldwide.

2. Collaborative robotic arms equipped with torque sensors in all six joints, integrated with proprietary force/torque sensors, tactile sensors, actuators, and motion-control algorithms.

points.name: Doosan Robotics — Agentic Robot OS
points.description: AI software/operating-system platform co-developed with NVIDIA for physical AI and AI-factory robotics infrastructure.
points.bullets:
A robot maker and industrial conglomerate that builds industrial robotic arms and develops an agentic robot operating system integrated with an on-device AI stack, serving manufacturers and industrial automation users.

points.name: Doosan Robotics — Intelligent Robot Solutions
points.description: AI-powered vertical automation solutions for logistics and industrial processing tasks, distinct from general cobot arm sales.

A robot maker that builds collaborative robot arms and is developing humanoid robots, increasingly packaging them with AI-integrated software for logistics and industrial processing tasks. points.name: UC Berkeley — Robot Learning Lab
points.description: Academic research group developing generalist robot-learning algorithms and vision-language-action policies, released as open-source models and datasets for the broader robotics research and startup community.

A university research lab that develops generalist robot-learning algorithms and vision-language-action policies, releasing them as open-source models and datasets for the robotics research and startup community.

points.name: UC Berkeley — Healthcare Robotics Research
points.description: Research program applying robotics and foundation-model work to surgical and clinical robotics, via simulation frameworks, datasets, and industry partnerships.
points.bullets:
A university research program that develops simulation frameworks, datasets, and foundation models for surgical and clinical robotics, working through industry partnerships.

points.name: Anduril — Ghost Shark
points.description: Extra-large autonomous underwater vehicle program built for navies, developed with Australia and manufactured via a dedicated Sydney factory and the acquired Dive Technologies line.

A defense technology company that designs, builds and manufactures autonomous unmanned vehicles, including extra-large autonomous underwater vehicles, autonomous surface vessels and loitering munition drones, for militaries.

points.name: Anduril — Sentry Towers
points.description: Autonomous Surveillance Tower product line providing AI-powered persistent detection for border and coastal security customers like CBP, a distinct market from military combat systems.

A defense technology company that designs and manufactures autonomous surveillance systems and AI software for border security, force protection, and electromagnetic warfare. 4. Complete surveillance towers deployed in the field and an integrated software platform.
5. Border security, coastal surveillance, force protection, and electromagnetic warfare.
6. Government border security and national defense agencies.
7. Its surveillance systems are deployed by government security agencies along borders and coastal areas.

points.name: Anduril — Fury
points.description: Autonomous fighter-type aircraft program (YFQ-44A Fury) built for the US Air Force's Collaborative Combat Aircraft market, grown via the Blue Force Technologies acquisition.

A defense technology company that builds autonomous military aircraft and the autonomy software that runs them for militaries. points.name: Shield AI — Hivemind
points.description: Shield AI's AI-pilot autonomy software stack, licensed and integrated into Shield AI's own aircraft and third-party platforms across the defense industry.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that builds and licenses an AI-pilot autonomy stack for unmanned aircraft and third-party defense platforms. points.name: Shield AI — V-BAT

A defense technology company that builds autonomous unmanned aircraft and AI pilot software for military operations. points.name: Shield AI — X-BAT
points.description: Shield AI's jet-powered, VTOL-capable autonomous combat aircraft targeting the collaborative combat aircraft (fighter-adjacent) market.

A defense robot and vehicle maker that builds jet-powered autonomous combat aircraft and the AI pilot software that flies them. It develops vertical-takeoff-and-landing unmanned jets designed for strike missions alongside an autonomy software stack for defense aviation. The organization sells complete uncrewed aerial systems and their associated AI software to militaries and defense agencies.

6. Militaries, defense agencies and government research institutes.

8. It builds jet-powered vertical-takeoff-and-landing aircraft specifically designed for strike and collaborative combat missions rather than reconnaissance.

points.name: Pony.ai — Robotaxi

points.name: Pony.ai — Robotruck

8. It runs autonomous trucking as a distinct business unit separate from robotaxis, tailored specifically to the Chinese logistics market with a new L4 light-duty electric truck.

points.name: Pony.ai — POV
points.description: Licenses autonomous driving technology to personally owned vehicle makers/owners, separate from operating company-run robotaxi or truck fleets.
points.bullets:
An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack to automakers and vehicle owners, separate from operating its own robotaxi and robotruck fleets. It builds proprietary world models and virtual driver technology that apply deep learning and sensor fusion to perception, prediction, planning, and control for passenger transportation and freight.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses a self-driving stack to automakers and personally owned vehicle owners.
2. A sensor-fusion autonomy stack built on a proprietary world model and virtual driver technology that uses deep learning for localization, perception, prediction, planning, and control.
3. Autonomous navigation and driving for level-4 passenger vehicles and light trucks.
4. Licensed autonomy stacks to automakers and vehicle owners.
5. Robotaxis, autonomous trucks, and personally owned vehicles.
6. Automakers and personally owned vehicle owners.
7. Its licensed autonomy stacks are integrated into vehicles built by automakers and personally owned vehicle owners.
8. It licenses its autonomous driving stack as a distinct revenue stream separate from operating its own robotaxi and robotruck fleets.

points.name: Helsing — Centaur
points.description: AI air-combat agent that Helsing integrates into partner-owned manned fighter jets rather than building its own aircraft.
points.bullets:
A defense AI company that develops autonomy software and AI agents for existing manned fighter jets, and also builds strike drones and loitering munitions. For partner air forces and defense ministries, it integrates software-only air-combat agents into partner-owned aircraft and manufactures its own autonomous munitions at scale.
1. An autonomy software developer that licenses combat AI agents for integration into existing manned fighter jets, alongside operating its own loitering munitions manufacturing.
2. Autonomy software and AI agents for air-to-air combat, plus GPS-independent strike drones and battlefield operating systems.
3. Autonomous air-combat, long-range air-to-air engagements, and GPS-independent strike.
4. Licensed software integrated into partner-owned aircraft, and manufactured loitering munitions.
5. Manned fighter jets, loitering munitions, and battlefield operations.
6. Air forces, defense ministries, and military aircraft manufacturers.
7. Its combat AI agents are integrated into fighter jets built by aircraft manufacturers, and its loitering munitions are produced in its own facilities for direct military use.
8. It integrates software-only AI agents into existing manned platforms rather than building its own fighter aircraft.

points.name: Helsing — HX-2
points.description: Helsing's loitering-munition / strike-drone product line manufactured at scale for battlefield use.
points.bullets:
A defense technology company that develops and manufactures autonomous military drones and battlefield AI software for democratic governments. It builds GPS-independent loitering munitions, uncrewed combat aircraft, and subsurface gliders, paired with AI software for electronic warfare and air combat. The organization acts as both an autonomous vehicle maker and an autonomy software developer serving defense forces.
1. A defense drone and vehicle maker that designs and manufactures autonomous strike drones, uncrewed combat aircraft, and underwater gliders, and develops the autonomy and electronic-warfare software that runs on them.
2. Artificial intelligence software for electronic warfare, air combat, and drone operations, integrated into GPS-independent loitering munitions and autonomous platforms.
3. GPS-independent autonomous navigation, aerial strike, underwater surveillance, and electronic warfare.
4. Complete military drones, uncrewed combat aircraft, and licensed battlefield AI software.
5. Battlefield operations, aerial warfare, and subsurface surveillance.
6. Defense forces and democratic governments.
7. Its autonomous vehicles and AI software are deployed directly by defense forces in military operations.
8. It manufactures its own autonomous strike drones at high volume alongside proprietary battlefield AI software, rather than licensing software to other vehicle makers.

points.name: Helsing — SG-1 Fathom
points.description: Subsurface autonomous glider program extending Helsing's autonomy work into underwater surveillance.
points.bullets:
A defense technology company that develops AI software for electronic warfare, air combat and drone operations, and designs autonomous military platforms including loitering munitions, uncrewed combat aerial vehicles and subsurface gliders for democratic governments.
1. A defense prime contractor that develops autonomy software and builds and sells autonomous military strike drones and underwater surveillance gliders.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software for electronic warfare and drone operations, integrated into aerial and subsurface unmanned platforms.
3. Electronic warfare support, air combat autonomy, underwater surveillance, and autonomous strike and loitering mission execution.
4. Licensed software and autonomy stacks, complete uncrewed aerial vehicles, loitering munitions and underwater gliders.
5. Aerial warfare, undersea surveillance and defense.
6. Democratic governments and militaries.
7. Its software and unmanned platforms are deployed directly by defense forces.
8. It pledges to sell exclusively to democratic governments and builds both the AI software stack and the complete military platforms.

points.name: Helsing — CA-1 Europa
points.description: Helsing's own uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) program targeting 2029 service entry.
points.bullets:
A defense technology company that develops AI software and autonomous platforms for aerial and subsurface warfare. It builds strike drones, underwater surveillance gliders, and AI-enabled uncrewed combat aircraft, and it acquires manufacturing capabilities to produce them.
1. A defense prime contractor that builds uncrewed combat aircraft, strike drones, and underwater gliders, sold as complete defense platforms to militaries.
2. Artificial intelligence software for autonomous military platforms, encompassing aerial warfare algorithms, uncrewed combat air vehicle systems, and subsurface navigation.
3. Autonomous strike, aerial warfare, underwater surveillance, and uncrewed vehicle autonomy for combat missions.
4. Complete uncrewed combat aircraft, strike drones, and underwater gliders delivered as military defense platforms.
5. Aerial warfare, underwater surveillance, and next-generation autonomous combat missions.
6. Militaries and defense ministries of democratic governments.
7. It designs and builds complete autonomous defense platforms in-house, integrating proprietary AI software with acquired aircraft manufacturing capabilities.
8. It combines AI software development with aircraft manufacturing to produce autonomous combat platforms distinct from AI-integration upgrades to existing partner aircraft.

points.name: Airbus — Autonomous flight
points.description: Airbus develops onboard autonomy and computer-vision systems to enable self-flying aircraft, drones and air-taxi airspace integration.
points.bullets:
An aerospace corporation that builds and sells commercial aircraft, helicopters, and defense and space systems, and develops onboard autonomy, computer-vision, and airspace-integration technology for self-flying aircraft and drones.
1. An aircraft and rotorcraft maker that builds and sells complete aerial vehicles and develops autonomous-flight software and UTM systems for its own products and broader airspace integration.
2. Onboard autonomy and computer-vision systems for self-flying aircraft, demonstrator platforms for autonomous flight, and unmanned traffic management systems for lower-airspace integration.
3. Autonomous flight, computer-vision landing, detect-and-avoid, and unmanned traffic management for drone and air-taxi airspace integration.
4. Complete aircraft and helicopters, plus autonomy software and UTM systems developed through demonstrators and subsidiary programs.
5. Commercial aircraft, helicopters, drones, air taxis, defense, and space systems.
6. Commercial airlines, helicopter operators, defense ministries, space agencies, and urban air-mobility operators.
7. Its autonomy software is integrated into its own aircraft and rotorcraft, and its UTM systems coordinate third-party drones and air taxis in shared airspace.
8. It develops autonomous-flight technology as a major aerospace OEM with aircraft manufacturing and certification capability, rather than as a software-only startup.

points.name: Airbus — Wingman
points.description: Airbus co-develops AI-piloted combat drone and loyal-wingman systems for European air forces with partners like Helsing, Kratos and Quantum Systems.
points.bullets:
A drone maker and aerospace company that co-develops AI-piloted combat drone and loyal-wingman systems for European air forces, integrating autonomy software and sensors into unmanned aircraft designed to fly alongside manned fighters.
1. A drone maker that builds and sells unmanned combat aircraft and loyal-wingman systems.
2. AI-piloted unmanned combat air vehicles and drone swarms using onboard edge AI and sensor-fusion navigation.
3. Autonomous flight for combat drones, coordinated swarm operations, and loyal-wingman integration with manned fighter aircraft.
4. Complete unmanned aerial vehicles and integrated drone systems sold to air forces.
5. Combat drones, loyal-wingman aircraft, drone swarms, and fighter-jet electronic warfare systems.
6. European air forces and defense ministries.
7. Its drones are co-developed with AI software partners and sold directly to military customers.
8. Its wingman drones are designed to add mass and dilute risk at roughly one-third the cost of a modern fighter jet.

points.name: Airbus — Walker S2
points.description: Airbus is deploying UBTech's Walker S2 humanoid robots into aircraft manufacturing and assembly lines.
points.bullets:
An aerospace manufacturer that operates as an early adopter and integrator of humanoid robots in its aircraft assembly plants. The organization purchases complete humanoid robots from robot makers and deploys them into its own aviation manufacturing lines as part of concept testing. It acts as the end user and operator of physical AI within its production facilities.
1. An aircraft manufacturer that buys complete humanoid robots and deploys them in its own factories.
2. Humanoid robots designed for industrial assembly and manufacturing tasks.
3. Aircraft manufacturing and assembly line operations using humanoid labor.
4. Complete humanoid robots purchased from a robot maker for direct deployment in its own facilities.
5. Aviation manufacturing and aircraft assembly plants.
6. Internal manufacturing and assembly operations.
7. It buys complete robots from OEMs and operates them in its own manufacturing facilities.

points.name: U.S. Navy — Hybrid Fleet
points.description: Navy program fielding AI-enabled unmanned and crewed surface vessels (MUSV, LUSV, USVRON squadrons) to expand the fleet with autonomous ships.
points.bullets:
A government agency and military service that acquires and fields AI-enabled unmanned surface vessels and autonomous ships to expand its fleet, running programs that buy autonomous maritime platforms and autonomy software from defense and marine companies and integrating them into operational squadrons and task forces.
1. A government agency that funds and procures autonomous surface vessels and maritime autonomy systems for its own naval operations.
2. Unmanned surface vessels in medium and large classes with autonomous navigation and control software, organized into dedicated unmanned vessel squadrons and integrated with crewed ships in a hybrid fleet.
3. Autonomous maritime navigation, unmanned surface operations, fleet integration of crewed and autonomous ships, and at-sea testing and evaluation of emerging autonomy systems.
4. Autonomous vessels and autonomy systems acquired through production contracts, studies contracts and other transaction authority agreements, and operated in its own squadrons and task forces.
5. Naval warfare, maritime surveillance and surface operations in contested zones, Pacific deployments and Arabian Gulf operations.
6. Buys from autonomy software developers, shipbuilders and unmanned vessel makers rather than selling to external customers.
7. A military end customer at the top of the defense acquisition chain, buying unmanned vessels and autonomy stacks from commercial developers and fielding them in its own operations.
8. Operates a dedicated task force and standing unmanned vessel squadrons to rapidly integrate commercial autonomy technology into fleet operations, treating ship acquisition like technology products.

points.name: U.S. Navy — Unmanned Undersea Vehicles
points.description: Navy program (incl. PMS 394) developing and fielding autonomous underwater vehicles for undersea surveillance, mine/UXO clearance, and Arctic operations.
points.bullets:
A government agency that develops, procures, fields and operates unmanned undersea vehicles and their autonomy software for undersea surveillance, mine clearance and Arctic operations.
1. A military operator and program office that develops, buys, deploys and operates autonomous underwater vehicles for defense missions.
2. Torpedo-shaped and extra-large autonomous underwater vehicles equipped with sonar, navigation and autonomy software for undersea perception and mine countermeasures.
3. Undersea surveillance, autonomous navigation, mine and unexploded ordnance clearance and Arctic under-ice operations.
4. Complete autonomous underwater vehicles it buys from defense contractors and operates itself in naval exercises and missions.
5. Defense undersea warfare, mine countermeasures and Arctic operations.
6. The naval warfare branch of the United States Armed Forces.
7. It buys complete underwater vehicles and autonomy systems from manufacturers and operates them in its own fleet and exercises.
8. It maintains a dedicated program office and manufacturing center for unmanned undersea vehicles and runs under-ice exercises to test and field them.

points.name: U.S. Navy — Shipyard Robotics
points.description: Navy effort bringing robotics and AI into shipyards for construction, inspection and maintenance of ships to improve fleet readiness.
points.bullets:
A government agency that funds and commissions robotics and AI integration into naval shipyards for ship construction, inspection and maintenance.
1. A government agency that runs robotics programs and awards contracts to robot and inspection companies for shipyard automation.
2. Shipyard grinding, blasting, painting, and AI-driven asset inspection for ship construction and maintenance.
3. Performance-based agreements and contracts let to robotics and automation companies.
4. Naval shipyards building and maintaining aircraft carriers, submarines and destroyers.
5. Prime shipbuilders and robotics companies contracted to perform the work.
6. It funds and directs the integration of third-party robotics into its own shipyard maintenance and production operations.
7. It ties robotics adoption directly to fleet readiness targets and multi-billion-dollar naval shipbuilding programs.

points.name: U.S. Navy — Project Overmatch
points.description: Navy's edge AI and networked-fleet initiative connecting sensors, data and autonomy across the force for mission-critical decision-making.
points.bullets:
A military organization that runs an edge AI and networked-fleet initiative connecting sensors, data and autonomy across its forces for mission-critical decision-making. It funds and operates distributed edge computing and advanced network management for defense environments. It collaborates with technology providers under cooperative research agreements to develop and deploy edge AI capabilities for its fleet.
1. A government agency that funds and operates edge AI and networked-fleet programs for its military forces.
2. Networked edge computing, sensor fusion and autonomy software for distributed naval forces.
3. Mission-critical decision-making, fleet networking and edge AI deployment across naval operations.
4. Defense programs and cooperative research agreements that integrate edge computing and network management into military operations.
5. Defense forces, naval vessels and distributed military sensor networks.
6. Military forces and defense technology providers.
7. It funds and operates programs that integrate technology from commercial providers into its own naval forces.
8. It connects sensors, data and autonomy across a distributed naval force for mission-critical edge AI.

points.name: Bosch — Robotics and Automation
points.description: A cross-industry robotics and humanoid-robot technology effort supplying sensor platforms, software, and manufacturing expertise to industrial and humanoid robot makers.
points.bullets:
A global industrial and technology company that supplies sensor platforms, actuation and energy-conversion technology, software, and contract manufacturing for industrial and humanoid robot makers, and also builds its own agricultural robots.
1. A component supplier and contract manufacturer that builds robot sensor platforms, actuation technology and manufacturing services for robot makers, and also makes complete agricultural robots.
2. Sensor platforms for robot movement, electrical energy conversion into motion, and design-for-manufacturability frameworks for hardware production.
3. Robot movement control, hardware design, production and supply chain operations, and weed identification and eradication.
4. Components, sensors and licensed software to robot makers, contract manufacturing of complete humanoid robots, and complete robots it builds for agriculture.
5. Humanoid robots, warehouse automation and farming.
6. Humanoid robot makers, warehouse automation providers, and farmers.
7. Its sensors, actuators and manufacturing services are integrated into humanoid robots built by other companies, and it builds its own farm robots.
8. It combines component supply with large-scale contract manufacturing capacity for humanoid robots under a design-for-manufacturability framework.

points.name: Bosch — ADAS Components
points.description: Bosch's Tier-1 automotive hardware business supplying radar, imaging, and sensor chips for driver-assistance systems sold to passenger-vehicle OEMs.
points.bullets:
A tier-one automotive supplier that builds ADAS hardware, including radar sensors and cockpit computers, for passenger-vehicle OEMs and robotaxi builders. It manufactures components like long-range and short-range radar, imaging radar, and in-vehicle networking modules that integrate into broader vehicle architectures. It is a major consumer of high-end FPGAs and collaborates with semiconductor and platform partners on cockpit and ADAS systems.
1. A sensor and component supplier that builds automotive radar sensors and cockpit computers sold to automakers.
2. 77 GHz long-range and short-range radar, AI-integrated imaging radar, FMCW-based 4D imaging radar, and FPGA-based in-vehicle networking modules.
3. Object recognition, real-time processing, precise tracking of moving objects in adverse weather conditions, and in-vehicle networking.
4. Sensors and components integrated into vehicle architectures by automakers.
5. Passenger vehicles, robotaxis, autonomous cars, and electric powertrains.
6. Passenger-vehicle OEMs and autonomous-vehicle builders.
7. Its radar and components are designed into vehicle architectures by automakers across multiple manufacturers.
8. It holds an estimated 15-20% market share in automotive radar and has published 64 LiDAR patents.

points.name: Bosch — Autonomous Trucking
points.description: A dedicated commercial-vehicle automation program pairing Bosch's integrated steering systems with partners like Plus for Level 2+ trucking automation.
points.bullets:
An automotive component supplier that builds integrated steering systems for commercial-vehicle automation, pairing its hardware with autonomy software partners to deliver Level 2+ trucking automation for truck makers and fleet operators.
1. A component supplier that makes integrated steering systems for commercial vehicles, sold as automotive components to truck makers and autonomy software developers.
2. Integrated steering systems engineered for commercial vehicles, designed to interface with external Level 2+ autonomy software for automated lane changes and highway platooning.
3. Steering actuation for Level 2 partial automation, highway truck platooning and automated lane changes in commercial vehicles.
4. Automotive steering components integrated into commercial trucks in collaboration with autonomy software partners.
5. Autonomous trucks and commercial vehicles operating on highways for hub-to-hub transport.
6. Truck makers, commercial-vehicle manufacturers and autonomy software developers.
7. Its steering components are integrated into commercial trucks by vehicle makers alongside autonomy software from its partners.
8. It combines automotive-grade steering hardware with external autonomy software partners to deliver integrated Level 2+ trucking systems.

points.name: Bosch — Automated Driving
points.description: Bosch's software and systems push toward Level 3/4 self-driving and robotaxi deployment, anchored by the Five AI acquisition and OEM partnerships.
points.bullets:
An automotive supplier and mobility provider that develops and licenses Level 3 and Level 4 autonomous driving software and automated valet parking systems for automakers, integrating capabilities from acquired AI software firms.
1. An automotive supplier and autonomy software developer that builds self-driving stacks and automated parking software licensed to automakers.
2. Sensor-fusion autonomy software and Data Distribution Service middleware for automated driving and valet parking systems.
3. Level 3 and Level 4 autonomous driving and automated valet parking.
4. Licensed software and autonomy stacks integrated by automakers.
5. Robotaxis and passenger vehicles.
6. Automakers.
7. Its autonomy stacks are integrated into vehicles by automakers.
8. Combines its own automotive sensor and systems engineering with acquired AI software teams to build a European-made self-driving stack.

points.name: Tsinghua University — Brain-Inspired Computing
points.description: A dedicated research centre that designs neuromorphic and vision chips for low-power, brain-like edge perception.
points.bullets:
A university research center that designs neuromorphic and vision chips for low-power, brain-like edge perception in robotics. It develops specialized inference silicon that supports both spiking and non-spiking neural models for fast, efficient on-device machine perception.
1. A chip developer that designs neuromorphic vision processors and licenses or transfers the resulting silicon architectures to device makers.
2. Neuromorphic computing chip architectures that support spiking and non-spiking neural networks alongside event-camera and human-eye-like vision processing.
3. Low-power, brain-like edge perception and fast object detection optimized for robotic vision.
4. Designed silicon and chip architectures transferred to or prototyped for device makers.
5. Robotics and machine vision systems requiring fast, low-power perception.
6. Robotics researchers and device makers adopting neuromorphic silicon.
7. Its chip designs are prototyped and transferred into robotic vision systems by device makers and researchers.
8. It develops distinct, named silicon architectures that unify spiking and non-spiking neural models for human-eye-like machine perception.

points.name: Tsinghua University — Integrated Circuit Design
points.description: A chip-design and EDA research institute and lab that studies hardware-software co-design for edge AI accelerator chips.
points.bullets:
A university research lab that studies hardware-software co-design for edge AI accelerator chips, advancing inference silicon architecture through academic research and seminars for the chip-design community.
1. A university lab that researches edge AI accelerator chip architecture and shares findings through academic publications and seminars.
2. Hardware-software co-design methodologies for edge AI inference accelerator chip architectures.
3. An academic research approach to accelerator architecture distinct from commercial neuromorphic or vision chip product lines.

points.name: Microchip Technology — VectorBlox Accelerator
points.description: An FPGA-based neural-network acceleration design flow, built on PolarFire FPGAs/SoCs and enhanced through the Neuronix AI Labs acquisition, aimed at embedded/industrial hardware designers building edge AI into custom logic.
points.bullets:
A broadline semiconductor company that designs and manufactures microcontrollers, microprocessors, and FPGAs, providing a full-stack edge AI toolchain for embedded hardware designers.
1. A chip company that designs MCUs, MPUs, and FPGAs, plus the software design flows and IP cores for on-device inference.
2. Low-power mid-range FPGAs and SoCs paired with a neural-network acceleration design flow, neural network IP cores, and a machine learning development suite.
3. Low-power, secure on-device inference and neural network acceleration for embedded machine learning.
4. Chips, IP cores, compilers, and software development kits.
5. Industrial, automotive, consumer, aerospace and defense, communications, and computing systems.
6. Industrial, automotive, consumer, aerospace and defense, and communications hardware designers.
7. Its chips and design tools are used by embedded hardware designers to build edge AI into custom logic and electronic systems.
8. It integrates neural-network acceleration design flows directly into a full-stack embedded control portfolio to position low-power FPGAs as secure platforms for edge machine learning.

points.name: Microchip Technology — PolarFire Space
points.description: A radiation-hardened FPGA and compute line for satellite and spacecraft edge AI, serving the aerospace/defense market rather than terrestrial embedded design.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that supplies radiation-hardened FPGAs, SoCs and space-qualified components for edge AI and compute on satellites and spacecraft, serving the aerospace and defense market.
1. A chip company that designs radiation-hardened FPGAs, SoCs, microcontrollers and space-qualified components for on-device inference and compute in orbit.
2. Radiation-hardened field-programmable gate arrays and RISC-V-based SoCs designed to run neural networks and process sensor data in the space environment.
3. Onboard spacecraft AI vision, edge inference, sensor bridging and precision timing for satellite systems.
4. Chips, SoCs, atomic clocks and sensor bridges sold as space-qualified components to aerospace and defense integrators.
5. Satellites, spacecraft, orbital data centers and spaceflight processors.
6. Aerospace and defense contractors, space agencies and spacecraft integrators.
7. Its radiation-hardened semiconductors are designed into satellites and orbital systems by aerospace integrators.
8. It dominates the radiation-hardened FPGA niche for space and defense with a family of FPGAs and SoCs built to survive and compute in the radiation environment of orbit.

points.name: Microchip Technology — PIC64GX RISC-V MCUs
points.description: A RISC-V-based microcontroller product line with licensed NPU IP, targeting power-efficient edge AI for IoT and industrial devices distinct from the FPGA and space businesses.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that builds microcontrollers with licensed neural processing units for power-efficient on-device inference in industrial and robotics applications. It designs RISC-V-based MCUs and licenses NPU IP to embed AI capabilities across its microcontroller product families for IoT and industrial device makers.
1. A chip company that designs RISC-V microcontrollers with embedded NPUs for on-device inference.
2. 64-bit RISC-V processing subsystems paired with licensed neural processing unit IP for power-efficient local AI computation.
3. Low-power on-device inference and secure edge compute for mission-critical industrial and robotics applications.
4. Chips and microcontrollers sold to device makers.
5. Industrial IoT devices, robotics systems, and aerospace applications.
6. Industrial device manufacturers, IoT device builders, and robotics engineers.
7. Its microcontrollers are designed into industrial and robotics devices by embedded system developers.
8. It pairs 64-bit RISC-V subsystems with licensed NPU IP to bring on-device AI to low-power microcontrollers rather than application-class processors.

points.name: MediaTek — Genio
points.description: MediaTek's edge AI/IoT SoC platform line aimed at embedded, robotics, industrial, and smart-retail customers rather than smartphones.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs edge AI and IoT system-on-chips for embedded, robotics, industrial, and smart-retail customers. Its processor line integrates neural processing units and multimedia engines for on-device inference and vision workloads in edge computing devices. The organization supplies these silicon platforms to embedded computing and robotics designers rather than building end-user machines itself.
1. A fabless chip company that designs edge AI and IoT system-on-chips with embedded NPUs for on-device inference.
2. System-on-chip platforms integrating Arm CPUs, neural processing units, multimedia accelerators, and connectivity for edge AI inference and computer vision.
3. Low-power on-device generative AI inference, edge computer vision, multimedia processing, and IoT connectivity for embedded systems.
4. Chips and reference designs sold to embedded device makers, robotics integrators, and industrial computing vendors.
5. Robotics compute, industrial edge computing, smart retail, embedded AI vision, and IoT devices.
6. Embedded computing board vendors, robotics designers, industrial automation companies, and smart-retail device makers.
7. Its chips are designed into embedded computing boards and robotic systems by device makers and integration partners.
8. It scales smartphone-grade multimedia and connectivity silicon architecture down into low-power edge IoT and robotics platforms with integrated neural processing.

points.name: MediaTek — Dimensity
points.description: MediaTek's mobile SoC line that integrates an on-device APU/NPU for smartphone AI workloads, including LLM and vision-language-action inference.
points.bullets:
A fabless chip company that designs mobile SoCs with integrated neural processing units for on-device AI inference, targeting smartphone and mobile device makers.
1. A chip company that designs mobile SoCs with integrated NPUs for on-device inference.
2. Neural processing units embedded in low-power mobile SoCs, optimized for INT8 quantization and multimodal AI workloads.
3. On-device inference for large language models and vision-language-action models on mobile devices.
4. Chips sold to mobile device manufacturers, accompanied by a software development kit for model deployment.
5. Smartphones and mobile devices.
6. Smartphone and mobile device makers.
7. Its chips are designed into smartphones and mobile devices by device makers.
8. It is the second-largest mobile SoC designer, delivering high NPU TOPS within smartphone power constraints.

points.name: Walmart — Advanced Systems and Robotics
points.description: Walmart's warehouse and distribution-center automation program that deploys third-party robotics (ASRS, AMRs, forklifts, shelf-scanners) to automate fulfillment.
points.bullets:
A retail operator that deploys third-party robotics and automation systems across its warehouses, distribution centers, and stores for fulfillment and inventory management.
1. A logistics operator that runs third-party autonomous robots and automated storage systems in its own facilities.
2. Autonomous mobile robots, automated storage and retrieval systems, autonomous electric forklifts, and autonomous shelf-scanning robots integrated into its supply chain.
3. Goods-to-person order picking, inventory management, automated sortation, and autonomous pallet movement.
4. Internally operated robots-as-a-service and integrated automation systems deployed within its own facilities.
5. Warehouses, distribution centers, and retail grocery stores.
6. Its own internal supply chain, logistics, and retail store operations.
7. It buys robots and automation systems from OEMs and runs them in its own warehouses and stores.
8. It acts as a primary deployment partner and anchor customer for robotics OEMs, driving large-scale adoption across its global retail footprint while funding those automation suppliers directly.

points.name: Walmart — Autonomous Trucking
points.description: Walmart's middle-mile and last-mile autonomous ground-vehicle delivery program using self-driving trucks and electric delivery vans.
points.bullets:
An operator that runs autonomous truck and van delivery services for its retail logistics network, deploying self-driving vehicles from technology partners to move goods across middle-mile and last-mile routes.
1. An operator that runs autonomous vehicles it purchases or contracts from self-driving technology suppliers.
2. Autonomous box trucks and electric delivery vans integrated into retail logistics operations.
3. Driver-out commercial delivery, autonomous middle-mile and last-mile transportation, and automated retail logistics.
4. Logistics services operated within its own supply chain using third-party autonomous vehicles.
5. Autonomous delivery trucks, electric delivery vans, and retail logistics operations.
6. Retail customers receiving delivered goods.
7. It buys or contracts autonomous vehicles from self-driving technology suppliers and operates them in its own logistics network.

points.name: Broadcom — AI XPUs
points.description: Co-designs custom AI accelerator chips (XPUs) for hyperscalers and AI labs rather than selling a branded chip line.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that co-designs custom AI accelerator chips (XPUs) and ASICs for hyperscalers and AI labs rather than selling a branded off-the-shelf chip line. It builds bespoke inference and training silicon, plus switching and connectivity solutions, for the largest cloud and AI operators.
1. A chip company that designs custom AI accelerators and XPUs for hyperscalers, sold as co-designed semiconductor silicon manufactured by foundries.
2. Custom AI ASICs and XPUs built on advanced foundry process nodes, combined with switching and networking solutions for large-scale AI infrastructure.
3. High-throughput AI inference and training acceleration, networking, and storage connectivity for hyperscale data centers.
4. Custom-designed semiconductor chips delivered through foundry manufacturing partnerships to specific hyperscaler and AI lab customers.
5. Hyperscale data centers and cloud AI accelerator systems.
6. Hyperscalers, AI labs, and large technology platform operators.
7. Its custom silicon is designed directly into the large-scale AI infrastructure and data centers of its hyperscaler clients.
8. It dominates the custom AI ASIC design market by co-designing silicon to customer specifications, enabling hyperscalers to reduce their reliance on merchant GPU vendors.

points.name: Broadcom — AI Networking
points.description: Supplies Ethernet switching and optical interconnect silicon (e.g. Tomahawk) for AI data center scale-up/scale-out, separate from its custom-chip design business.
points.bullets:
A semiconductor company that supplies Ethernet switching and optical interconnect silicon for AI data center scale-up and scale-out networks. It builds networking chips and optical-attach silicon used to connect AI accelerators across large compute clusters. Its custom-chip and networking components are designed for hyperscale data center operators building AI infrastructure.
1. A chip company that designs Ethernet switching silicon and optical interconnect components for AI data center fabrics.
2. Ethernet switching ASICs, optical DSPs and optical-attach silicon built for high-bandwidth scale-up and scale-out AI cluster networking.
3. High-bandwidth, low-latency interconnect for linking AI accelerators across multi-rack data center fabrics.
4. Chips and optical modules sold to hyperscale data center operators and network equipment manufacturers.
5. AI data center compute clusters and accelerator fabrics.
6. Hyperscale cloud operators and network equipment manufacturers.
7. Its networking chips are designed into AI data center switches and optical modules built by equipment makers.
8. It pitches Ethernet-based interconnect technology as a scalable rival to custom networking fabrics for both scale-up and scale-out AI clusters.

points.name: Broadcom — Broadband and Wi-Fi
points.description: Edge connectivity silicon for ISP and consumer broadband gear (Wi-Fi, PON gateways, set-top boxes) with on-device AI/ML features.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs connectivity and broadband system-on-chips with integrated on-device machine learning processing for network edge devices. It builds silicon for broadband gateways, set-top boxes and fixed wireless access equipment, embedding AI inference directly into network infrastructure hardware for consumer and internet service providers.
1. A chip company that designs broadband and Wi-Fi system-on-chips with embedded machine learning accelerators for edge devices.
2. System-on-chips integrating Wi-Fi, passive optical network and fixed wireless access networking with on-device machine learning processing.

points.name: Broadcom — Automotive Ethernet
points.description: Automotive-grade networking and chip partnerships serving connected and autonomous vehicle makers, distinct from its data-center and broadband businesses.

A semiconductor company that supplies automotive-grade Ethernet switches and chips for connected and autonomous vehicles, and integrates virtualization platforms for automotive manufacturing.
1. A chip company that designs automotive-grade Ethernet switches and networking silicon, sold as components to vehicle makers and manufacturing partners.
2. Automotive-grade Ethernet switches and networking semiconductors enable high-bandwidth, low-latency in-vehicle data routing for connected and autonomous systems.

points.name: Ambarella — Automotive ADAS
points.description: Ambarella's automotive business designs vision-based domain-controller SoCs and software stacks for ADAS and autonomous driving, sold to automakers, truck makers, and tier-1 suppliers.

A fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power system-on-chips and software stacks for edge AI perception, specializing in vision-based automotive domain controllers and AI image processing for cameras and radar. It builds chips and autonomy software for automakers, truck makers, tier-1 suppliers, and robotics developers to enable on-device inference and sensor fusion for autonomous machines.
1. A chip company that designs low-power system-on-chips and AI domain controllers for on-device inference, sold as semiconductors and licensed software stacks.
2. Low-power system-on-chips built on a computer vision architecture that perform high-resolution video compression, image and radar processing, and deep neural network processing, alongside adaptive AI radar software.
3. On-device inference, computer vision perception, 3D perception, sensor fusion, and planning for vehicle autonomy.
4. Chips, semiconductors, and licensed software stacks delivered to device makers and integrators.

points.name: Ambarella — Video Security
points.description: Ambarella's core vision-SoC line (CV5/CV7, CVflow) sold into video security, surveillance, and smart-camera markets distinct from automotive and robotics customers.

A fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power vision system-on-chips for edge AI perception, video compression, and deep neural network processing. It builds and sells embedded vision processors for device makers in the security, automotive, and robotics markets, enabling on-device inference and multi-sensor perception in cameras, drones, and autonomous machines.

3. On-device vision inference, multi-sensor perception, high-resolution video processing, and deep neural network execution for edge devices.
4. Chips and systems-on-chip sold to original equipment manufacturers, alongside a full stack of supporting software and services.

7. Its vision processors are designed into smart cameras, autonomous vehicles, and robots by original equipment manufacturers.

points.name: Ambarella — Robotics
points.description: A dedicated robotics product line (CV7x/N1x SoCs) targeting cobots, industrial AMRs, outdoor robots, and humanoid robot perception.
points.bullets:
A fabless semiconductor company that designs low-power edge AI systems-on-chip for computer vision and robotics, supplying perception processing for cobots, industrial AMRs, outdoor robots and humanoid robots.

2. Low-power systems-on-chip engineered for multimodal sensor fusion, high-resolution video compression and image processing.

points.name: Sony — IMX Image Sensors
points.description: Sony Semiconductor Solutions' CMOS and event-based vision sensor family (IMX series) that embeds edge AI processing for robotics, automotive, industrial and drone machine-vision customers.
points.bullets:

points.name: Sony — Aibo
points.description: Sony's consumer entertainment robot dog platform, a standalone companion-robotics product line distinct from its industrial sensor business.

A consumer robot maker that designs and sells companion quadruped robots for the home. points.name: Honda — ASIMO
points.description: Honda's long-running humanoid robotics research program that produced the ASIMO biped and continues in new humanoid robot development.

A humanoid robot maker and automaker that developed the ASIMO bipedal humanoid robot and continues to build next-generation humanoid robots and disaster-response avatars. points.name: Honda — SENSING
points.description: Honda's driver-assistance and autonomous-driving technology stack spanning radar perception, Level 3 automation and robotaxi trials.

An automaker that develops and builds autonomous-driving technology stacks for its passenger vehicles and partners to deploy robotaxi services. It designs Level 3 highway automation systems, radar-based perception, and AI-enhanced scene understanding for its cars, and co-develops inference silicon for next-generation vehicles.

points.name: Lockheed Martin — Autonomous Wingmen
points.description: Program developing uncrewed combat aircraft and manned-unmanned teaming technology for fighter jets and next-generation air dominance.
points.bullets:
A defense contractor and drone maker developing uncrewed combat aircraft, manned-unmanned teaming technology and autonomy software for next-generation air dominance. It builds and demonstrates autonomous systems and multi-domain command-and-control for the U.S. military and allies.

points.name: Lockheed Martin — MATRIX Autonomy
points.description: Sikorsky's autonomy flight-control system enabling uncrewed and reduced-crew operation of helicopters and VTOL aircraft.

An autonomy software developer and defense prime whose subsidiary builds flight-control autonomy software for uncrewed and reduced-crew operation of helicopters and VTOL aircraft, primarily for military operators.

points.name: Lockheed Martin — AI Factory
points.description: Internal AI/ML development and testing platform, including MLOps tooling and the AI Fight Club simulation environment, used to build and validate AI across defense programs.

points.name: NASA — Commercial Lunar Payload Services
points.description: NASA's program contracting commercial companies to deliver landers, rovers, and navigation/surface hardware to the Moon.

points.name: NASA — Mars Exploration Program
points.description: NASA's sustained effort to build AI-driven autonomy into Mars rovers for navigation and science planning.

points.name: NASA — High Performance Spaceflight Computing
points.description: NASA's research push into radiation-tolerant edge AI chips and processors for onboard spacecraft computing.

points.name: NASA — Advanced Air Mobility
points.description: NASA's initiative developing autonomous air traffic management and airspace-safety technology for drones and urban air vehicles.

points.name: Uber — Robotaxi Network

points.name: Uber — Freight

points.name: RoboSense — Smart LiDAR Sensor Systems

points.name: Ford — Factory AI

points.name: General Motors — Super Cruise
points.description: GM's hands-free advanced driver-assistance system for personal vehicles, expanding from highway-only Super Cruise toward broader-roads Ultra Cruise and robotaxi-capable autonomy.

points.name: General Motors — Industrial Robotics

points.name: General Motors — OnStar Virtual Assistant

An automaker that builds connected vehicles and develops in-vehicle conversational AI and autonomous driving assist features for consumers.

points.name: Magna International — ADAS

points.name: Magna International — Robotics Contract Manufacturing

points.name: BYD — Xiao Di

points.name: BYD — God's Eye

An automaker that builds and sells complete vehicles, integrating Level 4-ready autonomous driving systems and advanced driver-assistance features into its consumer and commercial vehicle lineup.

points.name: ETH Zurich — Robotics and Perception Group
points.description: A perception and vision research group studying event-based cameras and embodied-AI navigation for autonomous robots.

points.name: ETH Zurich — PULP Platform
points.description: An open-source ultra-low-power RISC-V processor architecture research program aimed at enabling AI inference on tiny, power-constrained edge chips.

An academic research program that develops open-source, ultra-low-power RISC-V processor architectures for AI inference on tiny, power-constrained edge chips. points.name: XPeng — IRON Humanoid Robot

points.name: XPeng — Robotaxi

points.name: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory — Robotic Mobility and Manipulation
